reviews.comment: Momtaz was a nice guy in all my interactions but the class organization was a mess. It always felt like I got the concepts then had another 3+ hours of work to do. At one point the instructions straight up said to copy-paste 80% of the code from the instructions. Whats the point of the assignment then??

Great class ruined by the convoluted group projects and bad CSE department policies. Almost failed the class when I took it because I was really sick and missed a step assignment. Got a -100 and it tanked my grade. The professor wasn't nice when approached about it. You will learn a lot in this course and it's essential, but needs some work.
Dr. Momtaz is incredibly undestanding and very easy to approach.

Momtaz is a very understanding and patient professor, but the structure of 335 limits his ability to make the class not suck.  Lectures are entertaining, but all materials are online.  Group projects are simply a nightmare, with awful organization.  Solo projects were demanding and confusing.  Good prof, and I learned a lot, but the work is absurd.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The way this class was designed is messy and not organized well. The professor is MIA and only 2 TA's were actually helpful. There is so much content to go over and more guidance could be given. The projects take a long time and if you have a bad group, you are screwed. No exams. Hybrid class but meet with group outside class during projects.

Nothing against Prof. Momtaz but this class is a mess. The group projects are incredibly stressful and an obscene amount of work to handle in just a few weeks. Requiring 3-4 out of class meetings a week is unreasonable. Assignment instructions are all over the place,and responses from TAs are unhelpful at best and outright misleading at worse.

This guy is inaccessible, the TAs are shit, they do not know anything, he doesn't know anything, together they run a zoo where the animals are the students. He is the worst professor I have ever taken, not accessible, and rarely replies to emails, he should be reported.

Worst class and worst prof I've had at MSU. Took it during summer and he was completely unhelpful. The course basically was “study past tests or you will fail” none of the actual course work mattered, and he just blamed you if you struggled. Exams were opennote but one bad exam and you fail. just take it during fall/spriong and avoid this prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you go to his office hours or talk to him 1 on 1 he is very great to talk to and is very reasonable. However I need to give a 4 not 5 because until he makes the group projects reasonable and not a 3 week anxiety attack mixed with anger and awful structure/rules he does not deserve more. That project does not resemble an actual swe group work.

Dr. Momtaz should handling group issues and protecting victims' grades in this group-project-based course. While his role is vital, his help is limited to stern warning emails and the inconsistent guidance from TAs is ignored. Fair course for most, but if you're stuck with bad teammates after the drop deadline, be ready to do all the work yourself.

Do not believe these reviews!! Dr. TerBush is genuinely one of the best professors I ever had at MSU. His class is extremely challenging and he expects a lot from his students, but he is always happy to help. He has office hours everyday, any hour unless he is teaching. He is hard on his students, but in a way to promote growth and excellence.
I asked him a question during office hours and he gave very short replies, not really caring if I understood or not.
Dr. Terbush's feedback is not constructive. He is very short when answering your questions. He does not appear to care about students.

Worst prof I ever had in my life, I am a good student that puts extra time into their work. No matter what this teacher will not help you, doesn't care for you and wants you to fail seriously. It's like he finds enjoyment on failing his students. I spent countless hours reading articles and notes, and watching all these lecture videos. for nothing!
Really bad teaching and she seems to not know what is going on either. Pointless assignments.
Really inconsiderate and tough grader and doesn't seem to know what she's doing

Really really tough grader who doesn't make things clear for assignments that take hours. Been trying to wrap my head around what exactly I learned in this class and I can't figure it out. Genuinely a professor who doesn't want to help students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Highly recommend. One of the most straight-forward classes I have taken at MSU. Professor Allen taught asynchronous, but I never felt confused or lost on what to do. 1 lecture video a week that is 30 minutes max, then a quiz and assignment. Honestly, even if you really care about your work, this class should take no more than 2-3 hours per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I never saw her in person due to the course being online, but Jeana-Dee's CAS 110 had enough put into it to make it up. things were visually appealing, informative and beautifully organized. This class was very lightweight (apart from the midterm interviews) and, while things can be vague, she's a very generous grader! Great way to add 3 credits.
This is the most annoying class ever. Everything you do is so pointless it is painful to waste time doing it. The lectures are so weird as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: JeanaDean is a great prof. She really cares about success and the material is really fun if you get into it. The lecture videos can be a little tedious but totally worth it.

Professor Allen seems to genuinely enjoy what she's teaching and is nice enough. With very lenient grading, multiple attempts on every test, and few assignments this might be one of the easiest classes you can take.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof is very nice & the rubrics are clear, but the class is frustrating. 30 min lecture videos sound like they think this is life changing information (it's not). It takes so many hours each week which is ridiculous for a 100-level required class. A big thing to note is that you'll get docked a lot of points for being even 10 words under word count
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Allen is an amazing professor. I took this class as a Summer class and it was extremely easy and at the same time fun and educational. There is lots of writing, almost excessive word counts, but nothing to not take the class over. If you put forth minimal effort you will get an A+. Insane extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Allen is great, but the CAS 110 course is less so. The workload is unnecessarily large with most assignments having unreasonably high word counts that will result in having to type up lots of fluff. TONS of extra credit opportunities though.

The class is definitely what you make of it. There is a lot of flexibility in terms of the content that you create throughout the course, but I wouldn't say that it was a particularly fun class. Professor seems very nice, but the hybrid format meant you didn't have much interaction. What you learn is worthwhile even if it is confusing sometimes.

Projects must be started early. Some range from close to 1500-2000 words and 500-1000. Meet every friday, mostly online, do not miss lectures, interview assignment (interview 3 people you do not know). Quizzes are all based on lectures. easy grader but do not take workload for granted. Do not take as elective, not very fun.

Yes, this class has a heavy workload, but it's easy work and it doesn't take that much time when you just sit down and do it. As long as you follow the rubrics and just do the work, you'll 4.0 in this class no question. Prof is laid back and friendly. Gives us a lot of leeway to get the grade we want.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very easy class, don't know what everyone else is talking about here. Doesn't take much time at all per week, and is all online. Prof is super sweet and nice too

So I am that student that sits down 1 time a week and does all my homework on that day. This prof took maybe 30 minutes a week. Just a lot of homework that is opinionated. It is nothing hard, just takes a little bit of time. Her class is an easy 4.0 and 3 credits if you can do simple tasks. Very EASY.

Had this class online so didn't have too much interaction with the prof. She seemed nice but the coursework was heavier than it needed to be. Multiple weekly assignments many of which were in big project formats that were so time consuming. She does offer lots of chances for extra credit though, which should bring me to a 4.0 in the end
I really think this class would have benefitted by being in-person. Allen is a really good, fun professor, but the class itself can feel boring and draining since it's mostly online.

I took this class asynchronously and had to drop it a week in. The professor is nice but the class itself is a nightmare. There is way too much posted to still have to figure everything out on your own. Just a headache, do not take.

I took this class asynchronously, so Im not sure what Allen is like as a professor as I didnt have much communication with her. Its a very easy class but there is just SO MUCH WORK. An excessive amount to basically teach common sense. CAS110 is very tedious and not kind to procrastinators. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are of professional quality. She really cares about how you do and tries to be flexible with lessons. Although the homework can seems kinda tedious and irrelevant, it's laid out so specifically for you. She really tries to make it as interesting as can be. I wasn't a huge fan of the class, but she was a good and kind professor

Welcome to the world of a thousand words with one useful piece of information. In every weekly assignment, you will learn something that the average person already knew and then have to write a reflection about why this unit changed your entire way of thinking and how useful it was.

Yes this class is easy, but the class itself is so boring. The lecture is 3 hours long for a class that only needs to be an hour, it's ridiculous. The professor is not very good at keeping things interesting. If you want something easy, take this class. Also prepare to hear her say Y'ALL for 3 hours.

Dr Golden is an OK musical instructor for an athletic band, but her attitude comes off as rude more often than not. She has a tendency to make callous remarks towards students especially when asking questions. Also, the repertoire for games is heavily skewed towards a small subset of all the large body of songs we learn.
Dr. Golden is a great professor. As long as you come prepared and know your parts you will never have a problem. If you want to get to know her better ask her about rock music :)

literally one of my favorite directors i've ever had. tbh if you think she's mean, that means you didn't prepare your parts.
also! her conducting class conducted our band and she gave them feedback for it in front of us and the feedback was never degrading or mean. don't go to music school if you can't take criticism
Dr. Golden is amazing. The Spartan Marching Band is the best band in the country, and she deserves tons of credit as the Associate Director. Go State, Go SMB

Dr. Golden is a great instructor and I enjoyed this semester in concert band with her. She expects a lot out of all of us and makes us work for excellence. If you want to be a successful band director or conductor, her class will help you immensely.

I have never been scared to go to class until this one. I have never cried because of a class until this one, twice. Conducting is such a vulnerable act and I felt that her criticisms turned conducting from a passion to a fear. Even on mundane things like scheduling, she would phrase them as attacks. Be careful and prepared for the gauntlet.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Golden is disorganized, untimely, passive aggressive and always defensive. It's unfortunate that the conducting faculty at MSU thought she was fit for the job. She doesn't utilize proper tools, doesn't offer regular office hours and worst of all doesn't teach. I hope she can progress to at least an acceptable professional performance level.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Dorr was my writing professor at James Madison College more than 40 years ago.  He was tough but fair and always interesting.  When a family member died shortly before finals, Dr. Dorr was kind and compassionate.  I completed my project during the summer session, and he called me in to see how I was doing.  Dr. Dorr is my fave MSU professor.

He needs to actually retire already. He could be my grandpa and it seems like he enjoys teaching but his class was miserable. Hated all my papers no matter how much work I put into them. Forced unnecessary class participation. Not fun to chat with at all. Way too much reading, and the homework had almost no connection to writing sometimes. not good
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor is the best teacher here at James Madison. As one of the founders, he is extremely passionate about teaching, especially freshman, which is hard to come by. Take his course if you want to become a better writer. My papers only improved. I appreciate all the time and effort he put into the course to help the students get the most out it.

Professor Dorr is an eccentric old man that is very passionate about writing which makes the class enjoyable. However, it is very hard to do well in the class due to his extreme pickiness when grading papers. He will humiliate you participating in class but it is worth it. Unless you have PERFECT grammar, don't expect more than a 3.5 in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Great professor, very insightful and wise however he is a VERY tough grader on papers. Make sure you go to office hours and participate in class discussions, although you dont get marked for absences, it will seriously hurt you if you don't show up.

Although once a great professor, in recent years Dorr has been overcome with sentimentality. Inappropriate morality lessons and Bible quotes in class, scattered dry discussion and overall not a lot of progress. Grades based on level brown-nosing done in class, not quality of writing. Overall a major disappointment.

One of the better English professors at James Madison if you are looking to better your writing. He grades tough, and takes no B.S. He expects you to attend most classes and if you do not he will call you out on it. Also make sure you have the readings done because he does active discussions.

Probably one of the hardest profs I've ever had, but he's taught me so much about writing. He's amazingly smart and his classes often run over because we have such good discussions. He grades really tough, but it's worth taking the class.

i knew i would like him. and then i did. it was great. serious, smart, passionate about his work. everything you could hope for. hard grader, which angered those used to grade inflation. earning a b? who has ever heard of such a thing!
No Comments
JMC lost one of the best profs ever with Dorr's retirement. Perhaps, though, he will yet live out his dream of being reincarnated as a Hutterite woman...
No Comments
No Comments
Although Dorr certainly is one smart cookie, his class is only benefical to those who go to office hours regualarly, which I didn't.
very hard, but an amazing prof
Very good professor and my favorite at my time with the university. Made lectures very fun and the subject more manageable, also very accessible and understanding outside of class. Would take again.

Dr. Bazgir without a doubt is the best orgo prof I have ever had. Organic chemistry is hard but he managed to make it fun and manageable. he taught us how to approach complex reactions step by step. The extra credits and homeworks were great and he also pastes many practice problems. please please  take orgo with him!
He wants you to 4.0 and will do what he can. #livelaughloveayoob

He is a great teacher, cares about his students' learning. Organic chemistry is difficult, but he makes it manageable. It's very possible to get a 4.0, which is great for this class. He offers lots of extra credit, so even exam averages in the 60s can still earn a 4.0. Homework is easy with multiple attempts, and the 4 quizzes can be retaken.
Deserves all the hype
Once again, an incredible teacher. Lots of opportunities to succeed, put in the work and study hard. His lectures are amazing, all posted online as well. one of the best professors out there.

Bazgir made the class way too easy with the amount of extra credit he handed out. But it's hard to learn from him since he just gives the answers to everything rather than actually teaching. Also skipped spectroscopy completely last semester (just emailed everyone and said "study it on your own").

No feedback on exams (makes it impossible to tell what did you get wrong since you can't even access the blank exam afterwards). Posts some video lectures the day before the exam. Midterm 2 is a cumulative exam which makes no sense. Lots of extra credit so people tend to like him.

The best chemistry professor I have had in my 4 years here. Lecture isn't required but I would recommend still going because he explains things in ways that make it so much easier to understand. Quizzes and exams are open note/you get a cheat sheet and it's basically impossible to fail this class.

Bazgir is an amazing professor, and is truly the only reason I did so well in Orgo. With every lecture, he made them entertaining and engaged with the class, always making sure that you understand the material before moving on. If you have the chance, take Ayoob Bazgir!
Very interesting class. Professor is chill and relaxed, and content material is very easy. Would definitely recommend!
Great professor! explains organic chemistry in a simple way that allows everyone to understand! gives a lot of extra credit!

He makes chemistry so easy with his comparisons to real-world analysis. He truly wants all his students to see how complex concepts can be broken down in simple ways. He allows students to engage during lectures free of shame. He makes funny jokes and does call-and-responses so we all stay engaged. 10% EC boost to your grade. Everyone loves him

I would go to war for him
- gives a lot of extra credit
- extra tries on the hw if you ask
- he will help on quizzes and tests
- he wants you to pass

Great prof, lots of opportunities for extra credits, I got a OK Exams and quizzes but bcs I did all the hws and extra credits, which you got tons of time for btw, and I got a 4.0. If you miss his lectures, the video lecture are still great and they are not too long. Most lectures he also lets you leave early which is great. great prof, good man.

Professor Bazgir is very knowledgeable and offers many resources to for you to succeed in his class. Although I would still recommend studying with peers outside of class often. His grading is forgiving, since he allows retakes for many quizzes and takes your highest grade out of the two attempts.

Dr. Bazgir is an excellent professor. His lectures are very engaging and full of examples to help solidify content understanding. Apart from his office hours, he is also always happy to accommodate if you have questions or want to meet in-person. Lots of opportunities for extra credit. Overall, a great experience.

He is very kind and curves grades/gives extra credit based off of the class's needs. I had around a 75% in the class but ended up with a 100% because of how much extra credit he gave out. His lectures are engaging and he provides the lectures online as well. The subject itself is hard but Dr. Bazgir helped me understand a lot about orgo chem.

I was super scared to take orgo, but Ayoob made it so easy. He explains everything clearly and reviews past content at the beginning of lectures. 8am lectures with attendance not required, but I still went.  Activ takes a while to get the hang of, but there's also 10% (or more) extra credit offered. Needed 24% on the final to 4.0. Highly recommend!
Incredible

He explained things really well and made it so easy to be able to learn from. If you miss a lecture he has them all recorded and posted on D2L so you don't miss anything. He gives so much practice and help, especially with recitations as well. You also get extra credit options! Super helpful professor and good at teaching.

He's the goat, lecture is worth going to even though the slides are posted. There are so many resources available to practice and the class is structured to be very forgiving with make up quizzes and EC, will be taking him again for Orgo 2

Prof. Bazgir is a great professor and clearly wants his students to succeed. While his accent at times makes it difficult to understand lectures, he is always happy to take questions during lecture and even helps during quizzes. I am not a good chemistry student so the multiple extra credit opportunities and easy homework was a grade-saver.

Prof. Bazgir is a great professor and clearly knows the material and wants to see his students succeed. The homework and extra credit assignments saved my grades. I am not a good chemistry student and I was very surprised at the amount of care Bazgir puts into answering students' questions, even during quizzes or after exams.
Lecture can be a bit fast but he posts video lectures online so you can go over it. Overall if you try somewhat the class is very manageable.
Very good lectures and professor. If you attend class and try to understand, you will do good.

He is very lecture heavy, go to the lectures and make sure you understand, as while he moves on quickly, he will go over it as many times as you need during class if you have questions. He also has recorded lectures available, but I don't find them to be as helpful as going to class. He is always very engaging and truly wants you to succeed!
Best teacher to take for orgo makes the class feel like a breeze and teaches it perfectly also makes it very clear what will be on the exam and gives you materials for it.

Dr Bazgir is the best professor at MSU, hands down! He gives his class amiable opportunities to succeed by offering a ton of extra credit and quiz retakes. Even if Dr. Bazgir gave us 0 extra credit and no quiz retakes, it would still be easy to 4.0 the class due to the engaging way he teaches the class. It is semi-impossible to do bad in his class.

one of the best teachers i have had at MSU. I had Dr. Bazgir for both Orgo1 and orgo 2 and struggled a lot in the beginning but he was always very patient and didnt mind re-explaining things 30 different times lol. i am not the best in chem but i remember so much from his classes ! if you put in the work, his classes are an easy 4.0 and he gives ec
Amazing teacher for orgo. His lectures and slides makes organic chemistry much easier to understand. Would highly recommend taking him if you can.

Ayoob is a great professor and his lectures are always interesting; I always came even though attendance wasn't mandatory. There is lots of extra credit, making it fairly easy to 4.0 if you don't do well on exams. He always reviews content at the beginning of lecture before starting new material which I found very helpful.

Ayoob is hands down the best professor at MSU. 4.0'd both Orgo I and II because of him. He offers tons of extra credit, gives engaging and fun lectures, and truly wants you to do well. You have to put the effort forth, but you will do well if you do. I wouldn't take orgo with anyone else!

AYOOB IS MY MAN. I 4.0d easily in orgo 1&2 bc of this blessing of a man. He's my favorite professor I've ever had. Very loved by his students. Offers so much extra credit I had to get a 20% on the final to 4.0. Lectures are funny and engaging. Requires effort but that is normal, the bad reviewers are the people who expect to 4.0 without any effort.

Prof. Bazgir was one of the best professors I've had here. He made orgo 2 so easy with all of the extra credit he offered and his great lectures. I took orgo 1 online and was nervous about taking 2 in person but it was the best choice I could've made.

I LOVE AYOOB!!! SO much EC offered because he simply wants you to do well in this course. Lectures are posted online so if you miss a class you can get caught up (or never go to class if you want to). Always posts practices before the exams as well as videos. Learn the different reactions and you should do great!

I had Dr. Bazgir for orgo 1 and 2. I absolutely would recommend him to anyone! He taught the material is a very straightforward manner, reviewed content during the lecture before the exam, answered all my questions during office hours, and offered tons of extra credit. He absolutely wants his students to succeed. 10/10 recommend!!

Take Ayoob for orgo, and nobody else. his 8am lectures both semesters are the only 8am classes I've ever taken, only because I actually loved the class. Orgo is notoriously a weeder class but NOT Ayoobs class. You will learn the material so well and enjoy it. This might be a hot take but general chem was harder than his classes. Take his class!
Great lectures, lots of in-class examples on the chalkboard, much extra credit, great at explaining complex concepts simply, and overall a chill dude.

He genuinely wants his students to succeed. He gives so many opportunities for extra credit and ways to boost your grade. If you don't understand a topic talk to him and he will take the time to explain until it makes sense.

Bazgir is a great Prof. If you can get him for organic chem, do it. Helped me 4.0, available outside of class and always willing to re-explain concepts. Made material feel easy. Straight forward with concepts so they were easy to get. Lots of extra credit and online assessments.

This guy is one of the best professors I've ever had. Breaks down Orgo very well and provides plenty of resources to learn inside and outside of class. Very funny and plenty of extra credit opportunities which make the class lower stress. Genuinely sad that the class is over. The Persian Prince is the professor to take Orgo I and II with.

WORTH TAKING THE 8AM FOR! He offers lots of extra credit as the class is only a few hw grades, 4 quizzes, the 2 midterms and final. His class is all lectures (with slides posted) and he posts recorded lectures online. He is very funny and tries to keep the students engaged during class. I would highly recommend, ONE OF THE BEST PROFS AT MSU.

WORTH TAKING THE 8AM FOR! Ayoob loves to teach and is very funny during lectures, but he also posts them online so you don't even need to go. There is SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT, no one should pass with less than a 4.0 imo. He wants everyone to do good and he makes it very easy to; I would highly recommend him for Orgo 1 and 2. He is a great caring prof!
Organic chemistry goat. TAKE HIM IF YOU NEED TO TAKE ORGO.

Beware of his accent for some people that can be a game changer. He likes to move on from information fast without much context other than writing it on the board only to erase it 2 minutes later. If the material was taught different with more consideration for the students I feel like I would've done better.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
This professor truly wants everyone to succeed. Homework is what you see on quizzes, quizzes are almost exactly what you see on the exams. overall a really good professor. Do the homework, learn how to do it the other ways (where the answer becomes the question). Learn that, you'll be just fine. 
(for reference, I failed CEM 141)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is literally the GOAT, make sure you take him for orgo!

You are making a mistake by taking any other orgo prof. This guy made orgo genuinely an enjoyable class. He is super funny, makes things really easy to understand (his accent is thick but easy to understand after a lecture or two), super accessible and you cant get any bettwe grading in any other class. 4.0 is extremely achievable. TAKE HIS CLASS!

One of the best professors I've ever had. Funny, but watch out for small details on quizzes and exams! Neither class nor recitation is mandatory (and he posts shortened lectures online), but I highly recommend going. Recitations are also bonus points for attending. All my extra credit meant I only needed 45% on the final instead of 87% for a 4.0!

Dr. Bazgir is a fantastic professor and extremely likable. Makes lectures extremely enjoyable and understandable. Orgo is hard no matter what professor you have but he tries his hardest to make sure everyone understands the content. Very easy to 4.0 as well since he gives out so much extra credit.

There aren't many grades that he puts in, just tests and quizzes. However, he hands out extra credit like it's candy. He also records lectures, which is helpful when you don't want to drag yourself to the 8 a.m. lecture. Overall, he is good at teaching the concepts.

Great Professor. He makes the class lighthearted and fun, and gives a LOT of extra credit, making a difficult subject more manageable. His accent is a bit thick, so it may be a challenge if you struggle with that, but it's honestly easy to get used to. Definitely taking him again for orgo 2!
THIS MAN IS A HERO! Please take him when you take organic chemistry, you will be glad you did!

I enjoyed your lectures a lot, it was easy and understandable to follow along. I know that I skipped one of the lectures, but I'm glad you posted it online, if we couldn't make it to class, because personally for me I would get stressed out if I didn't know what we are covering. I utilized the office hours you held (thanks to one of my friends)!

The Michael Jordan of Organic Chemistry at MSU. Dr. Bazgir is an amazing guy, hilarious lecturer, constantly available outside class and makes Organic digestible and understandable. The only knock on him is that he gave out so much extra credit it almost led me not to learn the material, but if you study out of class it's just more of a boost.

Professor Bazgir is by far the best prof I have ever had. Orgo is hard, but he makes it as easy and understandable, and as a plus, he is hilarious. He offers plenty of extra credit and wants you to do well - always available outside of class. Looking forward to 252 with him, I would only take this class with him if at all possible.

My glorious Persian king, my all-time goat, I cannot stress how much I recommend taking 251 with Dr. Bazgir. As other reviews have mentioned, he provides plenty of extra credit in his class. Additionally, he is super accessible outside of lectures and generally responds to emails within an hour or less in my experience.

My persian prince. He is literally the best orgo professor you can have. Do not listen to the 1/5 person, clearly they did not gaf about their grades because if they actually took the time to listen they wouldn't even need the extra credit. He lets you leave for the quizzes and their online. ASK HIM QUESTIONS ON EXAMS!!

Dr. Bazgir is a really good professor and his lectures are really concise and easy to follow. He gives out lots of extra credit (+1 for every recitation attended, +50 for practice problems) and is very easy to reach outside of class despite having hundreds of students. Highly recommend taking this class, he makes Orgo easy and understandable.

Dr. Bazgir is a really funny professor, and he takes time to explain everything in depth. His accent is a little heavy, however, it's understandable enough to get a great grade in the class. He provided so much extra credit during the class time that it literally could've "erased" a bombed midterm from your grades.
Best professor at MSU. Truly loves his job and is freaking hilarious. Makes Orgo easy. So much extra credit and exams are easy. GOAT.

Honestly, best prof I've had here, I'm even taking him again next semester for 252. Posts all lectures online so you don't technically have to go to class, and offers a ton of EC. He is very funny in lecture and is always available to help. Homework is graded on accuracy, but you have 3-6 attempts/question depending on the assignment.

BEST PROF EVER. love this man. I was so scared for organic chemistry but he makes it so easy. I genuinely understand everything from his lectures and the homework was not bad at all. 20 questions for each chapter and there is 50 points EC. He's also hilarious and made me laugh in my 8 am lecture. Don't take this class unless he is your professor.

This is the best professor at msu. Organic is such a hard class, but this professor is funny and so smart. He has an accent, but you get used to it very fast. The material is hard but there is so much extra credit that makes a huge difference in your grade. I cannot explain how good of a professor he is and can't wait to take him again. #Ayoobontop

Bazgir is very knowledgeable and he is just a great professor. Some people complain about his accent, but it's actually pretty easy to understand him. Just show up to lecture and you can easily get a 3.5 or above since he gives out lots of extra credit. Not too much homework, just 4 quizzes and a few tests. He also has a good sense of humor. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor ever
He gave a lot of extra credit and had very good detailed lectures, he also was helpful and accomodating.

Ayoob is the best. Chemistry really isn't my forte and I was scared out of my wits about taking orgo, but Ayoob really makes it easy to understand. He really wants you to succeed in his class. Gives out extra credit no problem. Makes sure to poll the class for questions, if any, after he explains a part of the topic being covered. He's also funny.
Chemistry is hard but Bazgir will go out of his way to help! He is absolutely the best prof!

Professor Bazgir is great! Recorded lectures, lecture slides, practice problems, & exam reviews are all on D2L. The grade is 4 quizzes, 2 midterms, final exam, & Aktiv homework. He is very accommodating to students & offers many extra credit opportunities. Although there is a lot of difficult material in orgo, he does not try to "trick" students.

Very easy professor but leads me to not remember the material or even learn it. Gave around 11% of the total grade as extra credit for CEM 252 and rounded by CEM 251 grade by like 5% with a lot of extra credit on top of that.

Professor Bazgir is your best bet at understanding organic chemistry. A professor can only lead you so far, but Bazgir is understanding and is always willing to reexplain topics and gives good examples during office hours. Orgo is difficult, especially as a first-gen student where you lack a lot of connections and experience. In short; TAKE HIM.

Had him for two semesters and I think he is a gift to chemistry. Makes lectures available online, in case if you want to sleep in (I have the 8m). Funny guy who makes me want to come to lecture and learn. 100/10.

I love Professor Bazgir! I was intimidated taking Orgo 1 at first but he takes the time to answer questions, re-explain topics, gives many examples, and gives many practice problems. I have also heard his office hours were very helpful which I regret not taking advantage of. I am taking him again for Orgo 2!

I loved Prof. Bazgir. His lectures were well organized and his quizzes accurately tested the material. Prof. is caring and easy to communicate with. He responds to emails quickly and is understanding.

I took CEM 251 with him and am not in 252 with him as well. He covers what we need to know and does so in a concise manner. He (and his TA's) is/are accessible outside of class to help students. Go to office hours if you need it and you will be able to succeed. One of my favorite classes and had great instruction!
This professor really does care about getting us through the class. Lots of opportunities for extra credit which was great. Overall very nice and caring.

Professor Bazgir was good. You can tell that he cares greatly for his students and genuinely wants you to succeed. However, orgo itself is difficult so go to class!! He does have a thick accent, but if you pay attention, you can understand what is going on. I'd also reccommend that you buy the orgo for dummies book; it pairs well with this class.

Did it in-person. If possible, do it online (all their assessments are online).Our quizzes were accessible online but the midterm and final were in person. Based off of the original syllabus few people were on track to 4.0, but last 2 weeks he decided to: drop 2 instead of 1 quiz, give retakes, 20 extra credit hw, 10 point final curve + cheat sheet

I personally loved ayyob. he was incredibly kind, if you send him an email he responds quickly. he allowed me to make up a quiz i missed and clearly wants students to succeed. orgo 1 is a lot of content and fast paced, and ayoob has a thick accent and is not tech savvy at all. offers extra credit and is overall a great guy
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lots of extra credit opportunities that arent listed in the syllabus. gives great feedback for honours projects
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He honestly isn't a terrible professor. Content moves very quickly, and there's a lot to cover in a short period of time, but when he isn't rushing, he does break things down in a way that is mostly understandable. I did have to YouTube a lot of the content to truly understand it though. He did offer extra credit to help grading.

Lectures are boring and a bit of a struggle to focus with just going from slides to slides. He was very kind to his students and understanding and gave retakes and extra credit he does not want his students to fail. Although his accent can be difficult from time to time and unclear what he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would recommend not taking organic chemistry with Ayoob. This class caused so much stress for no reason as the language barrier and thick accent meant that I could not fully follow his lectures. Additionally he would state things such as "just don't fail" or post a pdf with every student's midterm score.

This class was hard but Dr. Bazgir was a good professor who wanted everyone to succeed. He records his lectures and posts it with the slides, he offered a lot of extra credit, offers retakes, and drops a lot of grades. The lecture slides can be a little confusing and there is not a lot of practice so I recommend reading the textbook.

Dr. Bazgir is very knowledgeable, but can be hard to approach. Few things are graded; chapter HWs (8), 4 out of 6 quizzes, midterm, and final. Extra credit was given towards the end of the course to boost grades. He can be hard to understand at times, but usually repeats himself in lecture. Lots of studying on your own, not much to practice with.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ayoooooooooooooooooob!!!!!!! Great slides, he also posts online lectures and gives extra credit.
Professor Bazgir is a great guy, and very responsive. Lectures are good and answer questions you are confused about. drops 2 lowest quizzes, homework is worth points

I give all the props to Dr. Bazgir as he tried to make the class understandable, however I found myself constantly lost with nowhere to turn to. He was nice at rescheduling a few quizzes that took place during a test for another class. However, the homework is not like the tests and the midterm + final is worth 55% of your final grade.

Dr. Bazgir is definitely a knowledgeable professor. He responds back to emails relatively quickly and his helpful answering questions. Lectures are extremely long and heavy and his slides/notes are quite disorganized. His explanations are also quite short and he moves through notes very quickly. Dedicate lots of time to this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hes my sweet prince. Made Orgo the easiest class ever, IDEK how. If you have to take orgo, take it with Ayoob or don't take it all. WE LOVE AYOOB!!!!!!!!!!!

Dr. Bazgir is an amazing professor. He is extremely kind, caring and fair. He gives out a ton of extra credit to help relieve the stress of the class. He explains the concepts very well in lecture, but also has super helpful Office hours where he will help with anything. The lectures are not mandatory, but I highly recommend going!!

Whenever i emailed him about a quiz question i didn't understand why i got wrong, he emailed me back almost always within an hour, with an explanation and images to help me. He was very good in lecture and would even demonstrate stereochemistry to us with molecules. he even would say funny things during class and even get the class to laugh at 8am

Dr. Bazgir breaks down confusing topics into more understandable material. However, good luck if you have any questions because he does not understand how to answer them. Exams are heavily weighted and there's only 2 of them!! Get ready to put time into this class.

Super clear and concise teaching and makes sure to go over things many times so you understand. Graded on 2 exams, 4/6 of the quizzes, and 20 homework questions every other week or so. Recitation is optional and they provide the questions from that for practice. He did provide extra credit at the end of the semester. Final is cumulative

Dr. Bazgir was one of my favorite professors. Warning, he does have an accent that makes it difficult to understand him at times but you get used to it. He is amazing at explaining concepts and tries his best to help you pass.

Ayoob has a heavy accent and is not tech savvy. There are only 2 exams and are heavily weighted. They are also not like the hw or quizzes. He will add more slides to the lecture and not say anything and you will scramble to find it. He does not take questions often and be ready to receive sass. He is funny, but the lectures are draining and a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Bazgir's class is straightforward. If you just show up to lectures you should be able to get a B. Some concepts can be unclear but if you go to office hours he will explain until you understand. Quiz retakes and Extra credit are offered but they aren't mentioned in the syllabus. He is very knowledgeable and actually cares about your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: heavy accent and fast lectures makes it harder to understand but if you ask questions he goes step by step until you get it. Go to office hours he will make sure you get hw correct

He has a very thick accent which makes it hard to understand his lectures. you will end up teaching yourself from the textbook. The grading is odd and there are only quizzes and few homework sets. He speeds very fast over important topics but his slides break them down to an easier level.

Go to his office hours(OH) & ask questions! He will help you with the homework problems at OH until you get it right, he cares a lot and is willing to help you. He simplifies hard topics very well. He tends to go fast in lectures and has an accent but he records lectures from the online class so you can watch those! Very kind, funny, and easygoing
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lectures are very fast and confusing. The exams are harder than any of the reviews and quizzes. You are better off self teaching the materials than going to any lecture. To his credit though, I do believe that Prof Bagzir understands this and provides a very lenient grading scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Breezes over very complex and difficult topics too quickly. Doesn't explain very well. Heavy accent doesn't help either. If he slowed down it might be better. He posts the lectures which helps if you didn't pick something up in lecture. Orgo is hard no matter what but with this prof you will prob be watching a lot of youtube vids for help.

Organic chemistry is naturally going to be hard. The professor does have a thick accent and when you space out, it can be easy to miss the things he's saying. However, his explanations are good and digestible when you focus in lecture. Lectures for his online section are also recorded and uploaded, making it easy to find anything you miss.

He is quite hard to understand which wouldn't be a problem if he didn't speak so fast. He goes through very advanced topics too fast and to brief to for anyone to understand. 90% of your learning in this class will be through the text book or youtube. He is a good guy and he isn't bad. Just not very effective in lectures.

Horrible. You can NOT understand a thing he is saying. He has a very heavy accent, which makes it very difficult when trying to learn complex chemistry concepts. He does not care about learning. When students tried to ask question, he would ignore them. He is not tech savvy. He did not understand how to correctly post content online.

At first attending his lectures I had no idea what he was saying because of his accent but he really cares about his students. I asked him to record his lectures and that helped a TON. He can make very complex things become simplified and he even helped me gain some researchers when I asked him for help. Also go to his office hours I swear it helps

Literally, just pay attention. I get the feeling a lot of students may not pay attention because of his accent. If you pay attention, you will realize his explanations are very easy to understand. It's organic chemistry so obviously expect to put in some time outside of lecture as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: this man... oh god. in addition to being difficult to understand surface level, the man never explains ANYTHING. there is also no T.A.s like im sorry WHAT. a girl tried to ask a question and he signaled her to lower her hand because he doesnt take questions... save yourself.

This professor has the ability to simplify complex topics so students can understand and truly cares about the success of students. The practice problems and quizzes matched perfectly with the exams, and there were never any surprises. I took this class accelerated in 6 weeks instead of 16 and it was an easy 4.0.

Coming from someone not in business or economics, this class was very difficult. I studied more for this subject than CEM 141. DO THE PRACTICE PROBLEMS some of them are on exams. Exams are rough but you do get a drop and 3 homework drops. Go to every class you can. You get a little bit of extra credit if you only miss class a few times.

Didn't cancel class in -10. Office hours are posted but doesn't show. He ignores emails for days and is rude when he finally replies. Lectures are truly just him reading slides; TAs provide zero help. He pretends to care right before surveys, but it's an act. Grading is harsh—even with perfect attendance and 100% on HW, a 4.0 is not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You don't need the textbook, and Ackermann focuses more on being funny than actually teaching. Lock in for exams with the practice questions and youre fine.

Overall I enjoy him as a professor. I thought there was quite a bit of content and the exams really reflected them. My only dislike is the fact that the exams take 70-75% of your grade, some people just aren't the best test takers and ruin there grade because of how dependent the class is on them.

Ackermann is just not a good professor at all, even in person from what I have heard from peers. If you are not a math or business major like me, I heavily recommend taking this class in person. I would also recommend outside tutoring, and heavy studying. His exam questions are extremely hard and don't reflect what you learn in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will study for hours and take the exams and only some of you learned will be on it

Wish I had Dr. Ackermann in person he seems like a genuine guy. If u take this class make sure to do the practice exams and homework because Exam questions are often on those. Definitely would have performed better if this class was in person.

Genuinely the GOAT. I took him in-person for both EC201 and EC202 and he was great in both. His lectures are informative and easy to understand with funny examples. The homework is tough, but he lets you drop 3. Also, tests have easier questions than the homework, so if you do well on the homework, you'll succeed on the tests. Lastly, 89% is an 4.0

His lecture videos are good and informing, homework is just a weekly exercise wtih a small quiz, and overall super easy class if your taking him online. The questions on the practice problems are decently hard, but don't worry because questions on the exam are a lot easier. Akermann just a happy fella whose always smiling in his lecture videos.

Ackerman is a really nice guy and you can tell he loves the subject but he is not a good professor. He explains things in a very confusing way and the way that homework assignments and exams are written are just bad. My dad is also an econ professor and even he said that the questions made no sense. I'd recommend going to tutoring outside of class.

Professor Ackermann tries his best to make class engaging for students, and oftentimes succeeds. However, the large lecture setting makes getting feedback on the homework difficult, and it can be hard to course correct due to this. Attending every lecture is important if you want to understand the material!

Do not sign up for this class... His exams are insanely hard. I did all the practice questions before the first exam and still received a poor score. The homework quizzes on D2L are also easier than the exams and do not prepare you. Overall, the course is set up fine, but the exams are 70% of your grade and very challenging, not worth it.

Ackerman tries to make class fun. If you care about your grade, show up, and put in the effort outside of class, you will pass. He will never cancel a class, even if the weather is really, really bad.

You genuinely have to put in effort if you want a good grade. If economics is not your strong suit, you might want to go to office hours and the help room to get better. The professor is really nice and helpful, but only if you ask for help. The grade range of a 4.0 is larger than the stereotypical 90-100%, but it can still be challenging.
He makes the class entertaining and interesting, I recommend for EC201/202.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: THE GOAT.🐐LeBron James in the lectures should say it all. He is also the GREATEST 3rd grade girls soccer and basketball coach to never win a game! (Please include me in your syllabus week lecture)
On the first day of class, he will talk about the similarities between himself and Lebron James. This is Ackermann teaching students that he is, in fact, the GOAT.
if you're not a business major, i highly recommend you take this class in person. very difficult concepts that are hard to grasp and the exams are very math-based, which can be a struggle.

I truly do not understand the complaints about Dr. Ackermann or his class. His lectures were entertaining and actually explained the material rather than rushing through it. The tests were very similar to the homework and practice tests, sometimes having identical questions. An 88 is an A and the lowest three homeworks and lowest test are dropped.

Ackermann is a funny and nice guy, clearly loves what he does. His lectures are good, nothing amazing, but the weekly homework assignments are lengthy. His 3 midterm exams and final exam were difficult, but doing the large amounts of practice questions definitely helped. I did bad on the final, and still ended with a 3.5.

Recorded lectures weren't great, most of the time it felt like he was phoning it in. Frequent typos and errors. Wording of questions bad on homework and worse on exams. The only reason I managed to get the grade I did was because I got tutoring twice a week and they were able to basically teach me instead. Also, no notes allowed for exams is insane

Wrong answers on practice assignments. Conflicting info between textbook/Connect/lectures. Connect hw was torture, sometimes you'd answer 100+ questions (2 hrs) for one chapter. Then go do his hw assignment & realize it's different. Tanked the final despite studying for 6 hrs for it bc the wording was confusing (also he was really noisy during it?)

Jeff is funny. The textbook that he assigns sucks though, and asks horrible questions, teaches nothing, costs more than its worth (which should be $0), and finally was broken for a good two months on Firefox. Class was overall worth it and iClicker for attendance only (not graded on correctness) is great. Cutoff for a 4.0 is an 88, not hard.

Don't listen to the negative reviews. He's genuinely a really good professor, his lectures were educational and he posts them all on D2L later. While there is a lot of weekly homework, and the tests are decently hard, he is a fair grader and lets you drop your 3 lowest homework assignments and lowest test. Also you only need a 88% for a 4.0, so...
Don't take, his videos are poor and not helpful. Use practice exams to study. Overall not a good teacher.

I took this course over the summer for a major requirement. About what you can expect from an Econ teacher, however the class wasn't the most boring thing I've ever taken, I just don't have a passion for Econ. Micro was harder than macro in my opinion. Teacher was always available outside of class when i emailed for help.
Not fair, other EC201 get cheatsheets and calculators and online courses with him don't it is so hard to understand.
It is hard to imagine that in our planetary system, there could exist a professor of economics who is both skilled and humorous to such an extent. Always the number 1 choice.
Being a tenure professor goes a long way. Your TA's do all of your work for you while you sit back and watch students struggle!

He was good teacher. He was extremely helpful if you go to office hours. Top hats are included as attendance as completion not accuracy so that was amazing. He was really easy to talk to, fun and helpful. The practice test was almost exactly like the actual test. Make sure that's your main source of study material for 201.

DON'T TAKE MACRO FIRST! THIS WAS A MISTAKE! Ackermann always made the class fun and interesting, making me want to come to class every day. But man, he could NOT teach. He hardly goes over the content, often going on side tangents about family or the news. Be prepared to teach yourself and get yelled at if you email him if you're confused
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very outgoing personality. His classes in-person vs online are basically the same (i took in-person but i have a friend who took it online), i would say his class in-person was easier because participation grade is easy credit (just show up for iclickers). I probably studied a combined 3 hours outside of lecture for the exams and still got 4.0.

His class wasn't difficult per se. However, Professor Ackermann fought my RCPD coordinator on midterm extensions. I had life saving surgery, and only received a two-day extension for the first midterm. The work is definitely manageable, but his schedule is incredibly strict. Also, in-person exams for an online course are brutal. (EC 201 & 202)

This class was extremely difficult. The professor is nice, but doesn't teach well, and I felt like I had to teach myself everything for the exams. The exams were very hard, and there were not many assignments to help balance your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: With little to no choice for an economics class, you will most likely get stuck with Ackermann. If this happens, I hope you are good at teaching yourself the entirety of microeconomics. Even with the video lectures, much is up to interpretation during the exams when you have to study eight different units for a single exam. Would not take again.

not a lot of homework, you watch lecture videos then have a few assignments each week. 4 exams and one is dropped. chill class but it's hard because you basically teach yourself. I've heard he isn't easy to go to for help though I never did. just stay on top of everything since there isn't much to be graded on or turn your grade around.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ackermann is a hilarious guy and tries to keep up with the trends. Although his class is incredibly hard, you can't hate the guy because he is so funny and caring.

Honestly it's a whatever class, I can't claim bias or anything, but like I showed up, 3rd row to front, quiet, attentively. But its like every interaction is lol why do you like hate me. Like I just take it personal sometimes and couldn't help but feel like rip me. Like idk I think he's rude and bald sorry.

Prof. Ackermann was great! I highly recommend taking his classes; he is super chill & funny and teaches great. 4 exams, including the final, with one drop(all MCQ). Not very homework heavy and he usually extends the deadlines. Good Luck!
I found success in this class by completing the homework and attending help rooms. The resources are there for success, highly recommend taking advantage of them!

Typical tenure professor -- recycles the same video lectures, wants you emailing his TA instead of him, etc. Beware that he has a history of changing course cutoffs at the END of the course to make his teaching skills seem more impactful.

i love ackermann he's so silly. i have him online and even though online classes aren't usually ideal for me, i would rather have him online than a different professor in person. the lectures actually make sense, and he provides good resources like fill in the blank notes, along with accessible office hours. everybody loves this man for a reason!

Great guy, very well spoken, lectures are clear and concise. Grading criteria and homework are very simple and clear. If you go to his office hours every so often he is a lot of help. Office hours and practice problems in his classes are the key to an easy 4.0!

One of my favorite professors, was very funny and made lectures fun. Online questions were given during class so make sure to show up for easy points. Homework was pretty easy as long as you had the notes. Exams were easy as long as you actually did the notes and homework. Homework questions were very similar to exam questions.

Ackermann is a very funny, smart guy. I took him online but it seems he knows how to engage his students with his examples and in class questions. Warning: Do Not Buy Textbook. There is no reading for the class and it is very expensive. There's also a good shot that his already generous online grading curve may be lowered again, but still study up.

His online course was not my favorite, so I would suggest taking him in person since I've heard great things about him. The online course just lacked a personal connection which made it easier to get boring. He dropped 3/4 homework and even an exam so that helped my grade since the material can be hard to grasp over videos/slides.

For an online class it was fine. I already took AP Macro in hs but didn't get the credit so I had to take it again. I wouldn't take this class until you take EC201 since most of the first and second units are based off that content as review. Exams were ok. You get an exam drop out of the three exams plus the final so I skipped out on the final.
I didn't like this class, would not recommend it

I liked the class however I will never take an online Econ class ever again, I did not learn anything and I still got a 4.0. Definitely recommend in person lectures if you Wanna learn about your major.

Professor Ackermann was hand-down the funniest professor I've ever had. My top highlight was when he asked an open-ended negative externalities question about the worth thing our roommate has ever done. After submitting my response, my roommate chased me out of class, which ultimately resulted in me being able to finally switch roommates.
It was a good class but the exams were harder, though.

Was entertaining and made lectures more fun. Uses TopHat during class so make sure to show up for easy points. The exams were difficult, but he has a lot of materials including the homework that can help you study for them, and a lot of the practice questions are similar to the actual exam.

His class is test-heavy, and the tests are hard. The average test score is never more than 75%. He is good when he does his lectures, but he is not easy to work with, and, most of the time, won't help you if you need any help. unfortunate for sure.

Ackerman was a funny guy who made lectures pretty fun to be at. He dumbs down economics and makes it easy for non-econ people. tophat is required and so is macmillon achieve. Homework wasnt hard but tests have majority of the weight for your final grade.

Enthusiastic about econ, teaches concepts well and makes them fun. Fill in the blank notes are provided too. Homework took about 20 minutes per week, and that is the only work i did for this class besides attending classes and studying. Exams were a little difficult, but very manageable. You also get drops which helps a ton.

The way he teaches the material is fine, not particularly outstanding. Video lectures were simply old zoom recordings. Worst part is how inconsist the video and sound quality of lectures is. Few were high quality, some were ok, many terrible.

For an A:
1. Ignore Lectures
2. Watch Jacob Clifford Economics
3. Go by each section of the textbook

I had Ackerman for EC 202 online last semester and EC 201 in person this semester. I recommend taking it in person and attending lectures if you struggle with time management in online courses. To succeed on exams you must understand the content you are learning and it is almost impossible to do well by cramming since the study guide is different.

Ackermann is a good prof who knows what he's talking about but you need to be able to learn on your own to be successful in the class. You can't just wing exams but go to the helprooms they're more helpful than anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You can drop 1/4 exams. Study hard and you can get the grade you want. A couple of homework assignments each week and a few hours of video lectures. You can drop 3 homework assignments. Prof was nice and lectures made sense.
Overall a hard class, but help room, lecture videos, and textbook work can help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ackerman is a really cool guy, he cares about his students and wants his students to succeed. He tries to have interesting lectures to keep you entertained and teaches in a very comprehensive way. I am planning on taking his 202 class because of how well he taught the curriculum.

Ackermann acts nice in lecture, but is pretty rude if you try and go to him for help. He explains things in a way that feels belittling, and. I never felt comfortable asking him a question. For homeworks and exams, he writes the questions, and they are not easy. It is hard to study for exams outside of the stuff he gives you. Beware of the tutors

I'm not sure if the course work was just hard to grasp or if it was just hard to learn.There are recorded lectures and then homework assignment(s) due every Wednesday. Exams are pretty similar to the HW. You are only graded on homework and exams.The homeworks are basically quizzes bc you only get one attempt and some of the questions are confusing.
Great professor. Homework and exams are not bad. You can tell he cares a lot about the course.

Good professor. Posts slides online, and multiple prep materials for each exam (questions on prep were extremely similar to exams). Any difficulties I had were from the content, and not the professor. Would recommend for sure.

Terrible. Expect one-word, vague, and unhelpful responses to questions. He is immature, rude, and does not respect his students. It's an unpleasant experience to attend his in-person lectures and encounter him face to face. He cares more about inflating his ego than helping students learn; I recommend taking EC 202 online if he is your professor.

I think that he is a good professor it was just hard to focus on the course since I took it online. The practice problems just weren't like the tests. I also took macro before micro so I don't know if that made a difference. Overall I think he is a good professor you just need to watch the lectures, spread the coursework out, and study.

This class is HARD. I needed it as a prerequisite for my minor and I wish I didn't. It brought down my GPA because you are only graded on quizzes and tests and the tests are extremely difficult compared to the quizzes. Some questions are easy give aways, but then random topics get tossed in and make you fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took asynchronous EC 202, and I enjoyed it more than in-person, and will be doing 201 online as well. I found the online version very helpful in that you can work at your own pace, have 1 assignment due at the same time every week, and take the tests from your room. The policies are generous and fair, and expectations are laid out.

His lectures were really awesome, he explains problems is very helpful. The textbook is also really great, it follows the lecture almost 1:1 and it has you fill in some information. There are a ton of resources like practice problems with explanations and videos. If you show up, do the practice problems, and review what you missed you will pass.

Do not take this class unless it is your only option. Extremely difficult with no help from either the Prof or TA. I got nothing from this class and it was honestly a waste of time and money. He adjusted the schedule due to the events at MSU but still didn't do as much as other professors.

Very difficult if you aren't interested in economics. Lots of regularly scheduled homework but manageable. There's a workbook that he recommends you buy but I handwrote notes and managed a 3.0. Hardest part of class is motivating yourself to go to a lecture that he makes feel like a high school environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Last economics class I had a lot of trouble getting ahold of the TA. So when a problem arose in this class and it was about an assignment due in a day, I decided to reach out to Jeff directly so I could turn it in on time instead of waiting days for a TA. Jeff responded with a paragraph telling me to contact the TA instead of him with no answer.

You can tell he's passionate, but doesn't do a great job at explaining and tries to be in college again... WELL anyways you probably can't avoid him... so do the homework and try to understand those, as it's the same type of questions on exams. Oh you can also drop one (if you do well enough on the first three). but try to go to class.

Jeff is an awesome professor, but because I did the course online I didn't really have the chance to connect with him. The coursework is honestly kind of difficult, even with the lectures and the homework assignments. Because you can't really ask questions with classmates or the professor, you really struggle to get the concepts.

Professor Ackermann is a seemingly funny and nice guy, but I'd never take his class again. Nobody knows what he's talking about. The clicker questions show that based on the fact that the answers are always all over the place. Often overcomplicates the material to the max, both in class and on exams. I hope he shows this rating to his lectures

This is the only review you really need. The homework and tophat during class take up 40% of your grade. you can drop one test. tests are identical to the homework so review those. funny but could be a little better at explaining. Would recommend. Hard to fail this clas. get 100 on everything youll 4.0 with a E on Exam 3 and can skip the last exam
Do not take Ackermann online if you want to understand the content and actually learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Lectures were fun and he uses TopHat to track attendance
Homework assignments are easy as long as you pay a bit of attention in class 
Tests are just like the homework, if you can review your homework you are almost guaranteed a good grade
Talks a lot in lectures, gets off topic really fast. Do the homework if you want to do well. Exams are heavy, make sure you do well on the first two so you can drop the final exam.

I did ECO 201 online, and at the beginning of the semester Ackermann threw all his notes and powerpoints on D2L, and that was the end of his teaching for the semester. You will be required to learn it all on your own with no lectures or Zoom meetings. Hands down worst professor I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams were lockdown and the questions were all worded funky. He offered office hours but it was hard to get questoins answered. I would have liked to not take it but it was nice that if you did well on both midterms that you could just drop the final. Just buy the book through Macmillan and not the school bookstore. Might like it more in person

Professor Ackermann is a funny guy but when it comes down to success in this class I think he falls a little short. There are 3 30-question tests, two of which count towards your final grade weighted at 70%. If you're a bad test taker I strongly recommend staying away. He makes lectures somewhat relatable to things that apply in today's world.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is not very available outside of class, and when you do meet with him he rushes you out of his office. His grading policy is extremely tight, and says in the syllabus that even if you have a 81.99 he won't round you up. Very unreasonable and not a very compassionate person. When he describes concepts to you, he just pulls up the slide show.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class overall sucked, the exams were nothing like the practice sheets or the lectures, this teacher is hard to reach, because if you have a question, they will just email back look at the syllabus. Homework is 100% as long as you do it. There is still a good chance you will pass, but not with a great score.

Professor Ackermann is a passionate professor that cares about his job and students. However, he oversimplifies and under-explains material. I felt that I was always lacking the "why." Furthermore, his meta-level approach to economics undercuts the actualities of the world around us.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He uses clear and relatable examples in class and really as long as you pay attention, attend, and participate, you should be fine. He gives 2-3 problem sets per week/two weeks, and pulls some exam questions from those sets. If you're confused on some of the questions, he wont give you the answer, but he will explain them really well! 

GREAT PROF!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His class was relatively okay, it was lecture heavy and we had top hat in class participation points but it was just for completion, we had problem sets for each chapter but they arent terrible. 3 exams, and he drops the lowest one, funny prof which made his 9am not terrible

This is the best micro professor at MSU, no doubt about it. Tests are easy if you take the problem sets seriously and do the practice exam. Lectures were engaging and extremely concise, almost zero bloat in the course. Homework outside class was minimal, no more than an hour a week on non-exam weeks.
if you can take econ with any prof choose Ackerman! he explains difficult concepts in such an easy way his lectures are amazing never zoned out the entire semester

Exceptionally nice person, and genuinely tried to get to know the students who made the effort to show up, despite that it was a huge lecture hall. Course wasn't super super easy (he did not pull his punches on the exams) but if you show up to the lectures and take notes you'll be just fine.
good guy, would recommend
loved him!!! very difficult exams, but fair
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ackermann is a weird dude but he is good at explaining concepts. You can tell he really enjoys his job. He says the textbook is needed but you really just need access to the online homework. The course is pretty straightforward and as long as you do some practice problems before the exams they end up being pretty easy.
Great professor! Material is not easy but he is a good teacher. Do the practice problems and go to class and you'll do well.

I took an asynchronous class with Ackermann and he was sometimes difficult to communicate with. The circumstances definitely didn't help, but sometimes it didn't seem like he prioritized his online students. The class itself is very homework heavy and is partially graded on correctness. Exams are pretty standard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Ackermann is a good guy, EC201 and 202 aren't hard and he's really upfront with what you need to know for homework/tests so as long as you keep up with the homework you'll do fine in the class. He makes an effort to be fun and relatable so going to lecture is a good plan too, if you're able.
Never watched any lecture videos and I did fine. Do the online exercises and google what you don't know. Lowest exam is dropped, which is a big bonus.

For all the classes taken at MSU, both Ec 201 and 202 were the best classes I have ever taken. There are a ton of resources that are given within the class and if you put in the effort it will pay off. You'll learn a lot and have a lot of fun doing it. The goodbye song was the best by far and I was always excited to come to class.

He never got back to emails. Very unorganized. There were 3 exams and a final, lowest exam grade drops so if you are ok with your grade before the final, you dont have to take the final. Lectures are not easy to understand.

One of my favorite professors this semester. He may have had heavy lectures, but they were easy to follow. He also gave quite a big amount of hw, but it was manageable. Plus, he understood all our circumstances and a month into the semester, he dropped more assignments, and let us bring cheat sheets into exams. Gives good review packets for exams.

Jeff is a gem. Econ can be very boring but he tries his best, even in the lecture I felt like he cared for me and my grade. He is very good at explaining things, so if you are confused GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. I wouldn't choose another prof over him.

Some love him, some hate him. I think he has a good personality to match the entry-level content. If his lectures confuse you, look back at the textbook definitions and you'll probably be fine. He stays after class for a few minutes so it is easy to ask questions from the hw and get a deeper explanation.

Easy 4.0 class. Professor Ackermann's lectures were simple and easy to understand. Show up to class because he uses iClicker questions for attendance. Lots of homework but he gives you plenty of time to do it. I would definitely take him again.

Professor Ackermann is a really good choice for EC 201 compared to any other economics teacher at MSU from what I have heard. He makes his lectures very interesting and provides you the right resources to succeed on exams. He posts practice problems that are very reflective of the exams. Homework can be a bit too much but its still manageable.

The midterms will hit hard but it's a manageable grading scale and he was very generous with giving extra credit opportunities at the end of the semester as long as you have put in the work prior in the semester.

Professor Ackermann is a really fun professor, especially for a subject that can be boring. He does give out lots of homework at some points, but it's not very hard and is easy to get done. He's very friendly and wants everyone to pass, so I would absolutely take any of his classes if you can!
A great professor. Keeps class interesting and engaging. Never asks too much and anyone can do well.

Professor Ackermann was one of my only professors that was able to make online learning really interesting. He was always available to help outside of class, but do keep in mind that there are 2000+ students just in macro, and he also teaches micro. If you need to take an econ class be sure to have Ackermann as a professor!

I liked Econ with Prof. Ackermann. I think he explains concepts in a good way and cares about his students. He uses tophat to ensure you're attending class, but they're participation- based so it's a good way to get some free points. I thought the final was a bit difficult, but overall I enjoyed class and would take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ackermann is a really funny and caring professor. He tries his hardest to make his lectures interesting and funny and likes to interact with the class (even online classes). That being said, he gets off topic quite often, making it difficult to follow the lecture. He also does not go into much detail on the topic covered in class. Teach yourself!

Awesome guy. Funny, accessible outside of class, and really wants you to succeed. For a class of 400+ students you really feel like you know him well.
