reviews.comment: I had friends who had her last year who loved her, so naturally I was excited to take her theater history class. Were they in a different dimension? Bullying students, harshly graded papers, and the most boring readings of all time added up to my most headache-inducing semester yet. Parrot her ideas back to her and you'll pass.

Dr. White diminished my appreciation for theatre as she made experiencing productions feel like a chore. Not being allowed to actually watch the show did not make for a pleasurable class. On top of that, many of the questions on the exams were not covered in the lectures nor reading.

she knows her stuff, but her behavior is completely inappropriate. i watched her slam a kid's computer shut and berate them for eating crackers, which was incredibly uncalled for. i genuinely don't know what makes her think it's okay to put her hands on other people's belongings or speak to students like that. it creates a really hostile classroom
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unless you're okay paying $1500 to be treated like a child, avoid her at all costs. You can barely use a computer in her class without being under constant surveillance. She will stop the class and call you out by name, then raise her voice. Takes points away if she thinks you're not "paying attention" which could literally mean anything.

Absolutely loved her as a professor, super friendly and nice to talk to. The class can be difficult with all the readings required throughout the semester but as long as you actually read everything the rest of the class is pretty smooth.

If you can take any of her classes, you 100% should! Her recitations are fun; the quizzes are extremely easy; however, be warned, the midterm and final are worth quite a chunk of your grade. It's a very fun class, and it has a lot of reading, but Ann is great!

Dr. White is one of the coolest professors in the department. I had her for play analysis freshman year and theatre history this year and she is really smart and knows what she is talking about. She does make you take a lot of quizzes so definitely make sure you do the readings. She also directed Men on Boats which was a pretty dope show.

I failed my first STT200 class with a 26% and no motivation to learn it. This semester, I passed the class with an 80% (3.0) and with an understanding of Stats completely. Professor Fairbourn makes sure that you understand the material and is happy to go over it with you as many times as needed. She's very understanding and loves to help you learn!

Sweetest prof. ever, poor teaching style. Made many mistakes, not tech-savvy, wasted time. Wanted us to succeed, helpful 1-on-1 but should be teaching a smaller class. Content shouldn't have seemed so dificult to understand, I didn't like the way she overcomplicated things/underexplained things. She deserves to teach a subject she's better at

Lectures and recitations were quite confusing. I thought that the lectures were a bit all over the place, and it was hard for me to follow what we were learning. She is really nice, but I do not think that she is the best teacher and I found the course difficult due to her teaching style.

Professor Fairbourn genuinely made me like a math class! She is so kind and answers any questions! One homework assignment per week, 2.5% added to your final grade if you do all the EC, my TA was amazing and helped me understand the content. The Stats Learning Center is such an amazing resource if you're struggling, I highly recommend utilizing it!

Very kind professor, uses great comparisons to get the lesson across. Attendance is a grade but you can always get at least half points and it is not weighed too heavily on your final grade. The final exam is cumulative, but the midterms are okay. Stats overall is hard so thats the main thing.

Her lectures are always confusing and her TA's are no help and make everything more difficult to understand, I would not take her class if your not the best at math because of the way she attempts to teach the material

I would try to take another professor. She makes the lectures very confusing, and most of the time, you are just doing examples and not actually learning the content, which made me have to learn it outside of class. Attendance is mandatory, but she offers make-up attendance questions at the beginning of the week. I wouldn't retake it.
Teacher didnt give me a 3.5 by 0.07% and would not round up. Other then that very boring lectures, and tests are heavily graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is fine, class material is just hard. Starts off very easy and then quickly becomes impossible

Was definitely my toughest class of the semester, but I was still able to get the 4.0. Tophat and WebWork every single week, so make sure you do that. Taking notes is crucial and her lectures were good enough to where I could follow along, although I definitely got confused at some points. Use the very usuful practice tests and study for exams!

Prof Fairborn seems like a sweet woman but it almost felt like she knew too much for a base level stats class, it got confusing at times. She goes through slides fast and it was hard to keep up during lectures. If you feel confident about math you'll be fine. If you struggle with math, then you may want to make sure you can find outside help.

Fairbourn is by far the best stats prof. She is very caring and if you put in the work, you will get a good grade. Also, if you are having problems I would recommend going to the SLC. They walk through everything with you until you fully understand.

Super easy class, lectures are pretty easy to follow, only three exams; all very easy if you do the practice exams and study guides, don't necessarily need to go to class but you would need to do the top questions online if you want to get the points, definitely would recommend to anyone who has to take STT 200

Pretty easy 4.0 if you go to class, do the webwork, and do the study guides. Webwork and TopHat are required, along with a course pack. She was a great professor and I understood every lecture. Going to class is so important because she has TopHat questions for participation points! Overall would recommend
Great teacher for STT200, the lectures were valuable and the practice tests made the real test super easy.

Easily one of the best math professors I've ever had! She made statistics so easy to understand and was so nice. Grade was based on attendance (she usually gave us extra points or ways to gain back the points we missed) via Tophat, homework, recitation attendance, and 3 exams. All the exams were exactly like the study guides and practice exams!

This is the average STT class that colleges provide. It wasn't very hard, however, it could take time to get the concepts down. It wasn't extremely enjoyable but that isn't the fault of the professor for the most part. There is Tophat and Webwork due every week, so be prepared for that. Exams can vary in difficulty but they aren't very tough.

Fairly easy course and she tells you all the shortcuts possible. Course is not very difficult and she tries very hard to make your time enjoyable. She does well at not talking at you and talking to you instead. Very kind and compassionate lady.
I love camille. She is very sweet. Lectures can be confusing but if you go up to ask a question she affectively re-explains it.

Camille Fairborn is a good professor, but her lectures are hard to understand. She goes pretty fast through the slides and does not give a lot of time with required attendance top hats. Her tests are easy though as long as you do the practice exam and the study guide. Going to the lectures is very important if you want a good grade!! Shes good tho!

I liked Professor Fairbourn, but her lectures weren't great,so go to helprooms. Her tests are pretty easy as long as you understand how to do the practice exams she gives you, they are basically the same exact thing just different numbers. Attendance is graded on tophat and if you miss any lectures she has makeup questions you can do every Monday.

She does TopHat in class for attendance, however, she goes quite fast and gives us limited time to figure out the answer. She also goes a little fast in the lectures so you have to pay attention. But, Prof. Fairbourn has been great at answering questions and emailing back quickly as well as making the class fun on Thursdays with TopHat questions.

She is terrible, and when I say terrible, I mean it. By far the WORST math teacher I've ever had; not only does she have horrible lecture slides and fails to articulate what she means, she flat out completely fails her students as she cannot grasp the idea of how to teach math. I've had plenty of not-so-great math teachers, but she takes the cake.
Professor speaks and lectures but does not being concept to the main topic. Very hard to understand have to relearn everything in recitation.

Professor Fairbourn was awesome! She cares about her students and tries to remember names even though there's 300+ students in her class. Exams are easy if you regularly attend lecture and complete your WebWork. Have access to a TI-84 calculator because the majority of the course is just memorizing how to use the different functions on it.
Very organized slides. She knows her stuff as she is the course administrator for the class. You will need a TopHat account for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fairbourn is super sweet and does a lot of interactive parts during class. TopHat questions will count for attendance so you could get away with skipping if you're paying attention to the classroom, but the content moves fast. Each class goes through roughly 10 pages of the course pack. Stay till the end for Thursday fun questions.
The lectures actually make sense and the whole course is clear and organized. The tests are just like the study guides and the homework is relevant. Overall such a good class!

Professor Fairbourn is the sweetest professor ever. If you got to the lectures and put in the effort you will do fine. She always asks for feedback and adapts to the class to make sure everyone is on the same page. The schedule of due dates and everything is super clear. She is super caring and will help you with anything if you ask.
Lectures were amazing. If you actually listen in her lectures you will understand the whole course.

I took this class online so I never interacted with her. But, from her lectures, I could tell how passionate she was about stats. The large homework load in this class is painful and tedious. I now hate stats but that's not Camille's fault lol her lectures taught the material clearly and concisely.

Although I did four point the class, the class required LOTS of homework and studying if you weren't the best at math. Had her for an online stats class and the homework would sometimes have questions that she never went over so sometimes it was difficult. She seemed nice though.

Prof Fairbourns' lectures and notes were incredibly helpful in being successful in this class. Watching them is a MUST! Hybrid-flex class made balancing the workload in this class manageable. Content is difficult at times, but the notes prepare you well for homework/exams. I enjoyed how the class was setup. Attendance was mandatory for recitation.

I took the flex-hybrid course and it was really manageable and easy. There was a lot of practice work and extra credit that helped me prepare for exams. Also, the videos were easy to follow and no longer than usually 15 minutes. Professor Fairbourn is a great person and lecturer and she's great at explaining things.

Professor Fairbourn is amazing! We were given the option to either go in-person or do the class asynchronously. I did the class asynchronously and had no issues at all! Each lecture video never exceeded 15 minutes so they were super manageable. I recommend printing the lecture notes as it made note taking so much easier.

I love this woman. I am awful at math and barely passed all of my other required courses, but her lectures make it so easy to understand! She breaks down her lectures into manageable videos and puts helpful references and tools in between the videos! She also uses great examples :)
Professor Fairbourn is great, be sure to do the homework, don't be afraid to ask questions, you've got this!

This class was strictly online but was performed perfectly by Professor Fairbourn. The course was extremely well organized, easy to follow, and she broke down hard to understand concepts very well. Watching all of the lectures is key as well as doing the homework every week, if you do that, you're bound to get a 4.0!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I never talked to this professor as the class was online, but these are the most straightforward and easy to understand lectures Ive ever had. There are many many opportunities to do well in this class, and the lectures outline everything in perfect detail. If youre ever confused, the team of professors responds to emails quickly.

I had Professor Fairbourn during a COVID year so our stats class was completely online and I never had an actual one-on-one conversation with her, however, her lecture videos were really good and I think she is a good teacher, especially for a tougher class like statistics.
Professor Fairbourn was very thorough with her lectures and explained each concept in great detail. Pay attention to the lectures and the class will be a breeze.

Not a bad intro to stats class, took it online asynchronous and it was easy to do well in and to get help. Her lectures are nice, lots of examples and easy to understand even if you've never taken stats before. Very lenient with technical issues this semester too, gave extensions for that sort of thing. Overall good class and I usually hate math

I took STT200 all online asynchronous. I really liked the way prof Fairbourn set up the material on D2L. It was very clear to follow and hard to miss anything. I liked how she split up all of the lecture videos into short 4-10 minute videos that go by section. The detailed lectures follow the notes packet so you never get lost.

A solid instructor for an intro stats course. She explains things in a way that you can understand. Sometimes it is still hard to keep track of everything you're learning but she does her best to keep it manageable. One of the better classes I've taken for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: best math teacher i have ever had. very easy going & she explains everything. i was scared to take a math class during a pandemic but her set up was by far the best of any of my profs. she made things super easy & made it asynchronous so i can do it on my time. wonderful teacher, really cares about her students. take her classes !!!!!
Really great lectures which made the course a lot more enjoyable.

She probably never learned that you learn the best from your mistakes. The dumbest part of this class was the practice exams. You could complete them up to 10 times but you never got to know what you got wrong. How am I supposed to learn from my mistakes if I don't know what mistakes I made? so I ended up doing bad on the exams. Also, no late work.

Professor fairborn is a great teacher! Her lectures are easy to understand, and the class itself is nothing too difficult. She gives great examples, and I was able to learn very well from her. I highly recommend her.

I took this class online and LOVED professor Fairbourn. She posted video modules for each week, breaking them into smaller submodules. She was very thorough with her teaching and used relatable topics to help you understand the material. Take advantage of the workbook because it is a fantastic reference as long as you followed along.

I never met her once because there were 1,800 other students taking this class this semester, but from her lectures she seems like a nice lady. She explains things easily, but I benefitted from putting the recorded videos on 1.5x speed.

First, I'm an undergraduate student and got special permission to take this graduate course. I did realize that the grad students were better prepared, but I would take it again. The course design and approach to a difficult subject were excellent. Prof Sly is a master of this approach and gave us scaffolded work that built in complexity. Superb!

I took a variety of classes with Sly over my time at MSU. He is an ineffective professor for a lot of people. Seems to enjoy intimidating the students and is one of those professors that takes your performance in his classes personally. He hasn't updated his teaching style seemingly in several centuries and I'm not sure he knows what a computer is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (cont'd) I think the course was fabulous. I'm not a theorist, I'm a choral conductor. I don't need analytical tools; I need a *musical* approach to analysis, and that's just what Dr Sly offers. His analyses are off-the-charts brilliant. I won't get there. But I don't need to. It's the approach that matters, and what I learned will help my career.

It's fascinating to read the comments here. They probably reflect the wide range of student expectation in a school the size of MSU. I took this course because it's "common knowledge" that it isn't to be missed! Every student in the graduate conducting programs takes this course. Profs Rayl and Snow rave about it. Sedatole, it seems, mandates it.

Sly is a great prof but his course design could use some work. All of the homework is located within the course pack, and is not outlined that well in the syllabus. He mentions it in class but if you miss a day you have no way of knowing if anything was assigned. Definitely knows his stuff, and is great at answering questions. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was a very fun straightforward and humorous professor.

Dr. Sly is incredibly knowledgeable and eager to teach. Sometimes, however, his knowledge gets in the way of understanding what it was like to learn this material for the first time. If you think you're too smart or musical to go to office hours or schedule meetings, you're wrong. You'll get out of the class what you put in.

Wow...I sure learned a lot! All of the information is so beneficial to being a musician. I think Sly really cares about getting his students to master what he is teaching. **However, be very careful with this professor: His temper is unpredictable.
What a fabulous class and teacher. Sly has changed the way i look at music in one week. Best course and teacher I've ever had.
I love Dr. Sly! He is brilliant and such a fantastic teacher. I will never be able to see what he sees in a piece of music, but I'm aiming for 10%:)

We're just a third of the way through, but it's been a great semester so far. The course is challenging, but not as hard as Dr. Sly's reputation. I think he's getting nicer. He knows so much about this stuff, it's crazy. But his explanations are very clear, and I understand what's going on!!! Thank you, Dr. Sly! Theory is my biggest fear.
If you are one of those people taking the path-of-least-resistance approach to life, be very, very afraid of this man. But if you want to make an effort, Sly's class can be a high point of your life.
Several prima donna 9-year-olds in the class, who slowed things down and made life a little uncomfortable occasionally, but Sly dealt with them. Fabulous class. Sly knows his stuff! Super teacher!
Very difficult class.
Fabulous teacher. Knows his stuff. Loves it. You can't beat that combination. Best prof I've had.
He is such a wonderful teacher
Extremely intense class.
No Comments
No Comments

Toughest prof and class, but the highest pay-off. Sly is an exceptional theory guru, truly helpful to those who seek learning, and rewards hard work, growth, and genuine interest. An Apollo of a teacher.

Dr. Sly is really tough, but if you do the work, you're guaranteed to learn A LOT.  He's one of the biggest 'theory geeks' out there, but he's fun, intelligent, patient, and is just a really cool guy.

He was a great guy and cared very deeply about the subject and the students. Made me interested in number theory and higher level math in general. Can be slightly fast in lectures, but I personally didn't mind it much. Would take him again.

I took his class last spring. He was very caring and very knowledgeable, one of the best professors I have ever had. I thought the class was very difficult and put in many hours to get the grade I got, but I felt like it was very fulfilling.

Goes very fast during lecture, but extremely caring and understanding. Responds outside of class, and overall a pretty good professor. Calculus 3 just kind of sucks, and I didn't really understand concepts too well until I watched either Ryan Maccombs or other online resources, but nonetheless teaches quite well and make sure to asl questions!!

Prof Gakhar is probably the best prof I have had at MSU. He knows the material he teaches very well and he actually cares about his students doing well. He makes sure to check up on students individually and help them if they are struggling. I would def take his class again if I could.

Dr. Gakhar is very knowledgeable on the material, and presents topics very well. He is very caring and gives extensions frequently, but still leaves a LOT of work to do for his classes. Grading is very tough, but fair. Overall great professor.

Professor Nagys online lectures are not good. Every single one runs over the 50 minute allocation and most the time is spent deriving where equations come from and going out of order on the steps of the problem. I think he'd be amazing if he just solved problems in their entirety in one go instead of jumping around.

Genuinely so many quizzes. My main gripe with this teacher was that he had a quiz every single week and they were all lock down browser with content that was from previous exams too. The only upside for this course is the extra credit offered and the fact that the general math is pretty easy.

This professor was alright. He really didn't do anything extraordinary but he taught pretty well. The class has about 2.5% extra credit (i think) added to your final grade. The recitations kinda carry.

Lecture videos were honestly really bad and made it way harder to learn. Just goes over tons of stuff that doesn't matter as well. Other than that, course was run well. Everything in D2l is well organized and there are tons of resources. Offer a few extra credit opportunities throughout semester. Quizzes every week are really annoying.

As course coordinator, I thought his weekly quizzes were rough since they have the same number of questions as the exams, and the exams also cover old material which was annoying (exam 3 covers material from exams 1 and 2). The quizzes caused so much un-necessary stress, and prioritized short term memorization over actual learning

Took online Fall 25 w/ in-person recitation. Excellent lecturer, explains things extremely clearly, obviously passionate about math and responds to Piazza questions/emails quickly. Didn't like how some units felt physics-heavy. Exams are pretty easy. Offers 4% extra credit, optional recitation. WW is heavy but it's the same across all sections.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Handwriting is a little tough to read and accent can be a bit distracting. Quizzes and midterms are cumulative, which is strange. Weekly quizzes were overly difficultly formatted. Textbook is written by him and is a free PDF, which is cool. Accepts late webworks for 90% credit until the end of the semester! Recitation is extra credit.

The professor himself is nice however the teaching is kind fof bad. He basically records his hand written notes (not like MacCombs he actually handwrites them) and all the videos are an hour long. But it takes you 2-3 hours PER video (3 times a week) to actually even write it down not understand it because he prefills and then reads right off it.

I took the online version and his recorded lectures weren't bad. He doesn't provide structure for the notes he just writes it all down on a blank page which makes it hard to take notes for at times. His handwriting can be hard to read, but you get used to it. He seemed nice enough. The class it hard, but I think he was a decent professor.
difficult to be difficult

Do not take for MTH 235. For a 3 credit course I found myself spending more time on webwork doing homeworks during the week versus previous Calc classes. All midterms are cumulutive and most quizzes often covered material from a couple chapters in the past. He makes the class require too much effort for a 3 credit math class supposed to be "easier"

the most boring class ive ever taken. pretty good lecturer though, it's just a lot of boring dull content as opposed to difficult content imo and the hardest part is getting through the lectures w/o falling asleep. posting on piazza feels like bracing to be patronized. easy exams reflective of lectures and quizzes, ww is way harder for some reason
Good lectures sometimes a little dull
lecture not very helpful and heavy on self-teaching

While he was very organized and never missed a single lecture, his teaching style is like an AI chatbot. He only describes the same basic overviews of course topics over and over again and rarely shows the class how to solve problems that may appear on exams and WebWork. He is way too broad in his explanation of things and expects a lot.

This professor has a thick accent but you'll get used to it fast. This class is very self-taught, your expected to watch video lecture and complete accompanying lecture notes before attending the actual lecture, which is quick review. It's not ideal for this kind of class.

If you are coming in as a freshman and did not do any math over the summer do not take this class. He does have an accent but which can make it hard to understand him sometimes but if you focus you can understand him decently but the main problem is that he does not explain things well at all, he just does the math and kinda moved on right away

Professor Nagy was great given the circumstances. Lectures broke things down into simple steps. VERY exam/quiz heavy class, and lots of homework. The class focuses heavily on "concept" understanding and not actual problems, which makes it difficult to know what to study. However, my TA was wonderful and probably the reason I did so well.

terrible class, terrible professor. not one person i knew did well in the class. hard to understand- topics from lecture and recitation do not match. no feedback on any test. TA's were clueless as well
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Could be very snarky when students asked questions about the course setup. Used a lockdown browser unfortunately. 3 lectures a week and a quiz or midterm every week. At least two webwork assignments every week. Generally just a lot of work for the course. Unfair quizzes with written response questions each worth 20% of quiz/midterm grade.

Expect LOTS of time to be spent on this class. the class is passable as long as you know where to look for help. piazza response times are quick which is nice to ask questions. most of the homework problems have a solved example problem in the textbook when lecture notes don't help. it's as difficult as you would expect a 200 math class to be.

Class is doable if you expect minimal help and can learn by yourself via outside resources. Prof wrote the textbook for the class so that sucks. He will respond to piazza posts, but it will probably be a rude or snarky comment, nothing of actual use or helpfulness. Doesn't really seem to care if students pass, but did end up curving final grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nagy was always quick to answer questions and I thought his class as a whole was very fair. His lectures were pretty boring but it's differential equations so you can't expect much. If you do the homework and look at the textbook for examples, you will be fine in the class. Quizzes and exams were pretty easy to predict and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just a lot of material is covered. Study a week in advance for quizzes and exams

Absolutely wonderful class. I was in the honors section and loved how interesting our deep dives were, especially the last one on quantum mechanics. Differential equations is not my preferred mathematical poison, but the course was fun and not too hard. Many chances to score bonus or extra points. You don't need to go to class, just read the book.

His lectures were near impossible to figure out, no matter what I did I didn't seem to be able to dig myself out of this class, would absolutely recommend going with another professor for 235. No hate to Nagy as an individual he seemed like a cool guy, but just nit my favorite teacher.

Nagy makes the online lectures, and the videos can be difficult to understand and are often an hour or longer. The class itself is hard because it is Calc 4. Lots of homework every week through Webwork and the usual weekly quiz like most math classes at MSU. Not my favorite professor but not my least favorite professor.

Nagy was a good professor. Super quick response time on piazza and email. Nice grading structure. Lectures can be a bit boring, but not too bad. He is a nice genuine person. Most of the quizzes and exams were very fair. Overall a good professor that I would recommend.

This class was very well organized and all of the lectures are put on D2L so you don't actually have to attend any lectures. I thought he was really good at explaining the concepts but most of it can be self-taught. Tests and quizzes can be tough but they are based on the homework and lecture quizzes so if you do well on those they aren't bad.

Not the best at pure teaching but otherwise pretty great.
- Well organized class
- Reasonable Exams, quizzes and grading
- Was possible to self teach using the internet and the homework

Not that bad of a choice if you don't care for lectures and would rather teach yourself the material.

Textbook was a PDF written by the professor that kinda sucks

this class is hard and the prof is semi-helpful. Lectures are pretty clear but they move fast and prof is passive aggressive if you need help on homework. Quizzes every week and exams are HARD so prep yourself to cry

Professor Nagy is mediocre in my view. Lectures were lackluster and the tests were tougher than they needed to be (though not horrible). On the other hand, we were given a 2% extra credit opportunity which was very generous and the course is very well organized. If I had to take the class over again I wouldn't take it with him if possible.

The class and content is difficult. I was able to do well by watching all of the lectures, and never used any outside additional help. By only watching the lectures I obtained a 4.0 and asked him for a favor once and he provided it. For those reasons I think he is a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nagy, Oh professor... The lecture videos were extremely dull and long, making it almost impossible to pay attention. He also was very rude to the students making it seem like he definitely didn't want to help them. Many students did not make it through the semester, as he tests HEAVY on things we barely covered/learned right before exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nagy always was able to answer your question in the class forum. It doesn't mean that he was nice about it. There was usually a "you're dumb" tone to his responses. To be fair he usually gave useful feedback. If he cares about how his class does he does not do a great job of showing it.

I emailed him about an exam problem and how I don't remember covering it and asked him what unit it was so I could study, and he almost cussed me out because "he's tired of people" I apologized to him. Then he kept emailing me till I agreed with him it was a fair problem
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nagy was always answering my questions on piazza within a reasonable time and he will answer follow up/ clarification questions as well. His lectures are pretty straight forward, I highly recommend printing out his notes and following along with his lecture.

I have taken this class online with this professor and all I can say is that this professor has proven over and over again to be outwardly rude and arrogant to students asking for help, as well as making attempts to embarrass them. The course itself has a heavy workload with multiple video quizzes weekly as well as section quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took his DiffEq class, was it hard? Yes. Did I have to work hard for my grade? Yes. Is he a great professor? YES! Prof Nagy has a propensity to explaining complex topics in an elegant way, simply put, if you pay attention during lectures and do the homework, you'll be fine.
Nagy is the best math professor I've had at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy. Replies to emails quick and always willing to help. Definitely a lot of homework and quizzes but that is expected for a math class and it would be really difficult to understand if you werent forced to practice. Lectures are all you really need for the homework assignments but the book (he wrote it and its FREE) has some extra examples

Notes are very proof based. Could definitely make his own notes but basically copies word for word from the textbook. Class itself isnt too bad but with online format, and video quizzes (mini assessments after watching lectures), the class becomes a little longer. His videos also become longer ad you get into the semester. Should be a 4 credit clas
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course is not difficult. The course was very consistent throughout the semester. The practice exams and quizzes were pretty similar to regular exams, with many opportunities to improve your grade if needed. It's not necessary to watch the videos, instead just use his electronic notes, much easier and takes less time.

Gave an obscene amount of assignments, including four quizzes every week. Made TAs do most of the work and often refused to help students or respond to emails. Lectures consisted mainly proofs with a few examples. Didn't really seem interested helloing anyone succeed

I stopped attending class and hired a tutor. He is in charge of webwork so everything is done on webwork. If I did not have a tutor, I would not have passed this class. The MLC did not have any tutors that could help me in this class. Unfortunately he is probably better at teaching this class than any other professor at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The AMOUNT of school work we have to do throughout the week is unbelievable. TOO much work for a 3 credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: No, just no. Very mediocre, does NOT care about your grade and success. Dont take the class online, he doesnt do anything and he just makes his TAs do all the work for him.

This professor is mediocre at best. The lectures will contain almost entirely proof and sometimes during lectures when students have asked questions, he refused to answer at the time. The exams are very tough especially because the multiple-choice will be like "Choose all that Apply" with no partial credit which was unfair for a test quesiton.

Textbook was only used for honors projects, but he also supplied it as a PDF for free, which was GREAT. Class is tough, and you definitely don't want to skip. His lectures were dull, but very well organized and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy. His lectures are kind of dull but are good. This class is very doable but has lots of webwork to do. My one complaint is that he didn't finish the practice test until the day before the midterm both times, which was annoying for everyone who didn't want to wait until the last minute to study.

Very intelligent and its clear he knows what he is talking about. Has an accent but still easy to understand. Lectures are boring and can be difficult to sit through. Still can learn a lot from his lectures though. So much webwork. If his lectures improved, he'd be an easy 5 star.

He reads directly from the book that he wrote. There are a significant amount of quizzes on webwork, that you get to take up to 3 times. While his lectures are not good, you are given enough homework and assignments to pass. All of your exams are done AT LEAST 50% on webwork. The final is 100% on webwork. Do you webwork and you will pass
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He just reads off the notes
He was excellent at explaining topics! Best math professor ever!

Very intelligent but lectures are very boring. Has an accent, but he is very easy to understand. All of the material is found online and you can learn it that way much easier. Overall, my TA was fantastic, so that helped a lot as well. Quizzes are easy, exams are a bit harder.
When proving something goes wrong.... "and then your toast" Really enjoyed his class :)
great guy
Hard to understand. Smart guy but not much help when it comes to learning. Better learn how to teach yourself.

Recktenwald was a really good proffesor, but the class is just very difficult. He offers a couple opportunities to get points back He is generally accesible to reach but sometimes responses can take a while. I would reccomened taking the class elsewhere if worried about gpa, but if your most worried about learning the content I would take it at msu

Dr. Recktenwald is an excellent prof. He is really passionate about mechanics, and all of his lectures are engaging and interesting. Grading is super tough (be prepared for low exam scores towards the beginning), but really fair and manageable overall. Very accessible with office hours and online forums, cares for your success as long as you try.

Recktenwald's score on here does not do him justice. Although i didn't receive the grade i would've liked this class would've been even worse without his teaching. He genuinely cares about us as students and wants us to truly learn the material rather than drift through our degree not retaining anything. He is the best professor for this class.

If you're a CE major or struggled in statics DO NOT take this course at MSU. Has 4 exams + final, each with an A and B version given in b2b weeks. Great lecturer and challenges you to think. However, his graders show no remorse with extremely little to 0 partial credit given for likely the most difficult CE course you will take.

He decided that even if you get 90% of the problem right, and only make a minor error, you get 0 points total on the question for the exams that determine your grade, and while there is the ability for corrections, it is only if he gives you the very rare partial credit on the problem. Take this class at a community college instead
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Recktenwald is knowledgeable and fair and provides many opportunities for success. Lectures are well structured, but the pace is fast and problems can be long. The class is test heavy, so consistent practice is required. Grading is reasonable if setup and logic are correct. Stay on top of the material! Solid professor overall.

Genuinely one of the greatest classes I have taken at MSU so far, it's clear that this class takes a lot of work very early on, but the professor really does help guide you through if you put in the effort. Office hours are great and recommend going. It's hard but fair and honestly, I believe every ME proff should look to emulate Proff Recktenwald.

Loved him for ME222, ME370 was not the same at all. Exams and quizzes take forever to be graded. Project directions are vague and unclear at times. Lecture slides are often screenshots of the textbook. The homework is long and accounts for virtually none of your grade. It feels impossible to do well in the class even if you understand the content.

Took him for 370 after having him for 222 and 361. 370 seems to be a secondary priority, grades are ridiculously late, syllabus is a copy of 222 practically. Not tons of examples compared to the other classes. Material is very much off slides. Homework is long and nothing like test. If you care about your grade, take someone else.
The GOAT. Hard class but he taught well :D
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Recktenwald is an amazing professor who cares very much about his students. His lectures are straightforward and he explains things very well. Go to his office hours, he is a nice guy and is passionate about what he does.
Definition of mediocre.
The GOAT. Class is hard but if you do practice exams its not horrible

Recktenwald is the best. ME 222 is hard material, but he lectures very well and is structured well. He truly cares about how the class retains the info. The class is very test heavy, but with 2 parts, superscoring, and exam appeals, it's not that bad. lecture attendance HIGHLY reccommended.

Very engaging lectures. There was lots of homework but if you stayed on top of it it was easy. Clearly cares about teaching, he is very energetic. Exams were a big part of grade, but if you studied and payed attention in class it was easy. I would give him a 5 if he was not a eugenicist.

Gabe's teaches a great class. He really cares about all his students. He gives lots of opportunities to achieve the highest grade possible regardless of exam score. Although he says attendance isn't mandatory, it is very necessary to come to class as a good portion of the grade comes from in class work and pop quizzes.

Gabe is such a fun guy and makes class interesting but at the cost of your free time. The amount of homework for an ISB is a lot more compared to other classes, and the exams arent the easiest. However, I learned so much from his class and truly enjoyed his unwavering charisma during lectures and office hours.

Gabe is the most passionate professor I've ever had. He makes an effort to learn every students name and to make his lectures enjoyable. As long as you show up to class you'll do fine in this course. He also made cookies for the entire class

Gabe is one of the most passionate professors and genuinely makes an effort to connect with the content as well as the students. The course was a bit unorganized and harder than anticipated for a standard ISB, but he is very straight forward about what is going to be on the exams. He made the course more enjoyable, and if you show up you'll do well

one of the most genuine professors, who cares about his students and the class he teaches, however so unorganized and heavy workload not worth it for an isb class unless your also passionate about the topic.

I love Gabe so much and he is so passionate about what he teaches, but this class is so hard. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you miss a single class it will affect your grade like crazy. the exams are also very difficult, overall just a bit too difficult for a mandatory college course in my opinion
He is fun.

The class average for the second exam multiple-choice was 63%. I ended this class with a 2.5. For a basic-level ISB, ridiculous is an understatement. Gabe is genuinely a nice guy but no ISB test average should be 63. Lots of hw, lecture heavy, no grades posted all year, and attendance heavy. The worst grade I've ever gotten. No curve. Ridiculous.

Gabe is nice, but such a harsh grader. All of my friends said this class was an easy 4.0, but had a different prof. This was the hardest class I've taken so far at MSU. Tests are hard, especially multiple choice sections, and are nothing like the study guide. Did not know my grades the entire semester. Would never take a class taught by him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Gabe is a great guy but not a great professor. Lots of homework, typically 2-3 reading checks and then 1 assignment with a 400-500 word count, twice a week due before class. grades are NEVER posted on D2L. Exams are half multiple choice half open response but you only get your multiple choice scantron back. Way more difficult than needed.

You can tell Gabe is very passionate about what he teaches. Great guy, but would not take again. Anyone who says this was an easy 4.0 is lying. Exams are nothing like the "study guide." Way too much work for an ISB to even do okay in the class. Attendence HEAVY, tough exams, no posted grades the ENTIRE semester, lot's of hw, and time consuming.

Gabe is a genuine guy who really cares for his students. He's a nice guy, but he's not a great prof. Exams are tough and so many hand-written questions, lot's of hw, no grades on D2L, and super attendance heavy. This is seriously my most time-consuming class, and worst grade of this semester. Really too much work for an ISB.
This professor made this class go from an easy 4.0 to genuinely my worst grade of the semester. Way too many assignments, way too many quizzes, way too much weight on attendance in class.

I can't say enough good things about this professor. If you show up to class and do the homework you will do very well. The homework load can be excessive sometimes but it is not hard. To those who say grades are not on D2L they are correct but you can literally ask one of the TA's at anytime and they will tell you your grade.

I LOVE Gabe as a prof, but his class is a lot of work! He is so nice and rly tries to get to know everyone. You have to go to class if u wanna pass, and there's multiple HW assignments a week. He also doesn't post grades, which is a little frustrating. It can get annoying since this class is outside my major but if u pay attention, u can do well.

Gabe himself is super nice, but I do not have access to my grade outside of office hours which is difficult. I also am always doing homework or reading for this class and it is far outside my major which is very frustrating. I spend so much time on this course and it drives me crazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures were long, but easy to follow along, however throughout the entirety of the course grades were never posted until the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gabe is a genuine human being. If you are having a tough time, do not hesitate to reach out to him because he will help you all he can. His lectures are engaging, and he really helps you learn the material. If you pay attention in class, you will succeed.

The professor was great at the start of the semester, but as the semester went on became agonizing. You must attend class every day, due lots of homework, you need to attend office hours to see grades because he does not post them, things in February were not graded until the final day, and lies about the amount of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The kind of guy great for campfires, but not for teaching. Strict grader, 400-500 word homework twice weekly, plus surprise quizzes. Miss a class, miss a quiz. No grades on D2L, a major letdown. Tests full of handwritten questions, low-class averages on tests and he admitted to it openly. You will only excel if deeply interested; overrated teacher.

Most overrated prof at MSU. Very unorganized as there are no grades posted on D2L and homework has required word count and have to cite sources with quizzes based on homework in almost every lecture. He creates a class that is harder than any other ISB general class

This has been my favorite lecture that I have taken at MSU so far! Gabe is so entertaining and really wants you to understand and succeed. There's a fair amount of homework (but it's really easy) and there is always some form of attendance taken every lecture, normally as a group quiz on the reading from that week. Take this class! (easy 4.0)

There is consistent homework due before every lecture but it is very doable and never difficult. There are so many grades throughout this course you don't have to do well on every quiz. Gabe is very chill and fun and has interactive lectures. The quizzes are always reflective of things we learned.

Gabes was a nice proffesor. You could tell he was passionate about his class and tried to make the lectures as interesting as possible. I'm gonna be honest though I got lost about halfway through the semester and still got a 4.0. Make sure you do all the homework and come to every class. Quizzes are open friend but exams are tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Gabe is awesome! Super funny and engaging professor. Lectures are interesting, easy to follow and there's a lot of group participation.
Attendance IS mandatory if you want to perform well. Exam content is based on lecture material. There are no online slides, two hw assignments a week, but numerous extra credit opportunities. Would take Gabe again!

Gabe is a really nice person, and he cares a lot about his students. But make sure you are in class or you are going to miss a lot. His exams are way harder than they need to be and he gives an unnecessary amount of homework as well. Make sure you are in class to get some extra points. Really great guy, not a great professor.

Very unorganized. Grades not posted on D2L - have to stay after class or go to office hours to see grades. Group quizzes every single class. Powerpoints don't make sense unless you attend lectures. Lots of homework and reading. Required word count on homework. Final exam is cumulative. If you miss a few classes it impacts your grade a lot.

Gabe has a great sense of humor and makes lectures interesting, but he is the WORST at grading. Will not use D2L to post grades and instead makes you go to office hours or come early/stay late after class to ask about your grade. He also takes 3-5 weeks to grade exams. Extremely frustrating, especially when the end of the semester nears.

If you want to do well in this course YA GOTTA GO TO CLASS, in class assignments are a big part of this class and there is a pre-class quiz and assignment before almost every class, he makes this class kind of harder than it needs to be but he has a very fun lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Best prof ever! He takes time to get to know his students and cares for them, despite it being a large lecture. He is also hilarious and makes the lectures/materials super entertaining. There IS a lot of homework, and you DO need to attend every class, but if you put forth effort, it's 10/10. I love Gabe

As much as Gabe is a great guy, he made his class far more difficult than it needed to be. Be prepared to do lots of homework, show up to every class, and put in the work to study for the exams. I wish I knew what he expected ahead of time so I knew exactly how much effort I would need to put in in order to succeed in the class.

Great professor full of energy but in no world should an ISB course be this hard. 4 assignments each week + an in-class quiz. Attendance is mandatory! I love Gabe but the class is hard for no reason, other ISB classes are easy 4s I had to work myself to death just for a 3.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Gabe is an awesome teacher and I really like him as a person. However, this class requires a lot of participation and if you want to pass YOU NEED TO COME TO EVERY CLASS! Gabe has group quizzes and Half sheet assignments that make it easier to study. All exams are in person closed book ,closed note and there are also essay questions.

This guy will fool you with his great personality and being a good dude but this course is way overcomplicated and too difficult. He is difficult to talk with and meet if you won't come to his office and office hours, won't respond to emails, etc. Attendance is 80% of this class and if you miss more than 2 than your SOL.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gabe was an incredible teacher but the workload was way too much for this class especially it being an gen ed requirment. Love the professor though
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Please do yourself a favor and never take one of this Professors classes. He assigns a ridiculous amount of homework, gives quizzes almost every single class, and asks that you call him uncle Gabe. His class was such and odd and terrible experience that I will not miss.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Keeps class entertaining and makes you want to come to lecture. There are so many assignments that he encourages students to collaborate and its almost impossible to fail his class because of how many extra credit opportunities are available . His homework can sometimes be a lot of work but its never too difficult. Gabe is my absolute favorite prof

Amazing teacher. He's super fun and makes lectures entertaining! There are in class activities and group quizzes for points so attendance is important. A handful of extra credit opportunities. Homework is not hard. I genuinely learned a lot from this class, it was my favorite this semester. I highly recommend taking any class Gabe teaches. 100/10

Gabe is a fun professor who is up to date on whats going on in the world. In class he goes over slides which are posted online. It's hard to know what to write in your notes. There are in class quizzes (for attendence) that do not match the content on the exams. Exams are online short answer and long. SO MUCH out of class homework and quizzes.

I don't know, he's an incredible person and all, but teacher, I don't know. He's got something that most teacher's don't and that's personality. He puts so much pride in doing his work and gives a smile to everyone. He is the best person to be around. As a teacher, I don't know, his work methods don't really work for some people.

Nice teacher,
Slightly biased but not in any distracting or harmful way. Genuinely likes the material he teaches. Coursework is large but not very challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gabe wants all of his students to succeed and enjoy their time at MSU. I would recommend for everyone to take one of his classes at least once.

Overall good, interesting professor that is passionate about the material. However, A LOT of work outside of class. Weekly essay assignments, readings, and quizzes. Also attendance is very important because missing out on some in-class quizzes will tank your grade. Material itself is fairly straightforward.
Professor Ording has easily been one of my favorite profs here at Michigan State. The class was easy if you do the work and was also very engaging and interesting.

Gabe is such a good professor. He always made sure what he was lecturing on was important for the class. None of the quizzes or exams where unexpected. He made sure that whatever was on the exam, he had covered in lecture. He's a very friendly prof and knew most of his students by name, which was crazy because the class was huge. Best prof so far.

Loved this class and with it being online, it wasnt that bad. He would try his best to make class interesting despite the circumstances of online classes. There is a bit of busy work, but nothing too difficult.

He gives so much extra work and makes everything way harder than it needs to be. The class isn't difficult material but because there's constantly readings, long homework assignments, and quizzes in class it feels like I'm drowning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Gabe is very funny and kind but he gives lots of readings and homework. Also, the readings he gives for homework will sometimes be on the exams and the study guides don't really help much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Gabe is a very down to Earth professor. He gives a ton of extra credit possibilities, along with recycling previous years exam questions. Gives you all the information you need to pass and has no trick questions on the exam, many are in fact exactly off the study guide. Going to class every day would help as there is no textbook for this class.

He understands most people taking this class don't care about science and tries to make the class as enjoyable as possible. He forces you to go to office hours to get to know you and gives you answers to tests and reveals questions early if you go to office hours. Posts notes but have to go to class to get so many points and understand the concept.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gabe is really funny and nice but his tests were ridiculously hard. If you don't read or pay attention to lecture you will not pass his tests. There are other professors who teach this same class but demand a lot less, I would go for them. Overall, he is a nice dude but avoid him if you don't want to deal with a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gabe is one my favorite professors I've had at MSU! He is so kind and funny. His lectures are always great and I actually looked forward to class. He often related the class to social issues, and is very passionate about what he teaches. There is homework, but you get points just for completing it. If you show up and study you will do great!

Gabe is the best professor at MSU. He genuinely cares about the success of the students. With that said, the tests are quite difficult. Make sure to study and go to his review sessions. He is very considerate of personal issues. Go to his office hours and get to know him. He is there to help.

Gabe is an amazing professor. He makes the lectures interesting and truly takes the time to get to know his students. This class is not an easy A, but it is absolutely worth it. Truly a pivotal person in my life.

Gabe is hands down the best professor I have ever had at MSU. He's super funny, and is extremely engaging when he teaches. He's the reason I added on an entomology minor! Lots of reading and frequent pop quizzes, but if you pay attention and do the assigned homework, it should not be an issue.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: best prof I've had at MSU. There is little emphasis on bugs and more on the environment. There is homework almost every day but it is mostly completion points and can be done fairly fast. It helps a lot with understanding the material and makes studying easier. The class feels hard but really is just a lot of points. I came out with a 4 no problem.

Gabe is by far the coolest professor that I have ever had. He makes lectures fun and very informative. The homework is not really that bad, but I would recommend keeping up with all the assigned readings. He offers a lot of extra credit opportunities and is just a caring guy. Highly recommend him.
NOT A EASY A. You must work for a 4.0. I got a 4.0 in the class and was constantly scared for my grade. Daily pop quiz, homework everyday.

Gabe Ording was literally the best teacher I've ever had. If you are at all concerned or interested about the environment, this is the class to take and the professor to have.  I was excited to go to his class twice a week, his lectures are phenomenal.  He strongly encourages and forces participation and engagement, not that you wouldn't want to.

Best professor at MSU, hands down. Funny, personable guy who truly cares about students and his class. He makes sure to know your name within a couple days. You do have to study quite a bit and really know the content, but it turns out to be so interesting that it's not a problem. Show up, take notes, go to study sessions, and you'll be fine

This guy is an explosion of energy.. Don't hesitate to ask questions in his class and he loves global warming and the process of evolution.. Class doesn't cover bugs too much! He tries to trick you on exams..

AMAZING Teacher! You will love his class. He is very clear and more than willing to help with everything. Super nice and super approachable. Take any class he teaches and it will make you a better student and an enlightened individual. One of the BEST teachers I have ever had, hands down.

Gabe is the best professor I've had at MSU.  I despise all things science related, however, this class was very interesting.  If you show up to class and write down a few notes here and there, the class is a piece of cake.  Gabe repeats everything so often, you can't help but not remember it.  He gives lots of easy points, and is VERY fair.

Gabe is fantastic. Sit in the first few rows and he'll know your name within two days. Very funny and personable, he even helped me begin to get over my fear of bugs. Pay attention to lecture, as he has some very interesting things to say. DEFINITELY read the online stuff. Don't buy the textbook, it's useless. Best required class I've ever taken.

Gabe is an awesome prof. I don't even like science and this was easily my favorite class of the semester. Don't bother buying the textbook-you won't need it, but do the online readings and go to class and you'll be fine. Overall awesome class.
really funny, engaging for sure
Great guy fun class!
Engaging, has a sense of humor. Type of Prof who is always in a good mood, you'd never know if he was having a bad day.
Gabe is awesome. One of the best profs MSU has to offer. If you don't understand things he is more than willing to help. Plenty of extra credit if you're not a good test taker.

Gabe is awesome. Science is NOT my thing and that is an understatement. His explanations are completely clear. His tests are fair, but if you aren't a good test taker there are still ample opportunities for extra credit. Periodic quizzes for attendance. Keep your old tests to study for the final and be sure to do the readings!

Gabe is awesome. If you have him for this honors class though, he won't be your only prof, but will be the main one. He makes everything easy to learn, and I always find his lectures easy to study over. His tests make you think, but if you put a lot of time into studying you can do well.

He's an awesome professor. If I were more interested in science I'd take him in a heartbeat. He makes the material fun, interesting and easy to learn. He gives out tons of group quizzes, and has a lot of opportunities for extra credit. You will not regret taking his class.

Prof Ording is one of the best professors at MSU, he's very useful, always available during office hours, before and after class. If you need to take any ENT class, sign for a class that he teaches, you'll definitely pull off with at least a 3.0+
No Comments
No Comments

Gabe was amazing. I hated science and let loved his class. He really takes an interest in his students and their actually taking something away from his class. I take another class with him if I could.

GT was a great professor! While the class is a lot of work, it prepares you well for future courses. She has great insight into child development, and I feel that she really cares about what she's doing. Her feedback really helps you understand which aspects of an assignment need improvement.
She's not very tech savvy for it being an online class -  but she clearly cares about what she's talking about. As long as you do the work and put in effort you'll do great!

She was very strict about her grades.  She wasn't really good with technology either, so if something goes wrong it takes so much longer then it should.  Half the time you can't hear or see the videos either.

I usually don't write, but I had to this time. When someone asked for feedback, she said it was too much work. When I asked to make up a quiz the next week, she said yes, but when the it came she ignored all my chats and emails. When someone asked how to get graded, she put it in the chat for everyone to see. Grading is also bad.

Her grading makes no sense. She will grade you a 50% one week and a 200% the next. So slow at putting the grades in, a quiz every week, so much homework and writing assignments. The lecture is so boring and I never knew what she was talking about. You probably have no choice of another professor, so good luck.

Her grading system is ridiculous, she barely gives out extra credit even though on D2L there are lots of extra credit opportunities listed, and the lectures are so long me and several of my classmates fell asleep.

If you want to pass this class, here is a tip. when answering the field assignments, write essay length answers (or a large paragraph).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst professor at MSU. She will give you points to act like "you're earning points" until the final test comes around, you get a terrible grade for no reason. I don't understand her thought process when she grades. I think she just wants to give people a bad score for fun. Thought about switching my major a couple times, if that says anything!!

Terrible communicator. I emailed her so many times over the semester begging to get assignments graded that I completed on time, it took her months. She constantly posted wrong dates on D2L and never corrected them, leaving everyone so stressed. The class was very boring, she just reads the slides and then ends class with a NEVER ENDING WORKLOAD.
The lectures were pretty boring, but the class in general wasn't too hard. She provides a lot of extra credit opportunities, and the exams aren't too difficult.

She had the dates on the quizzes wrong and I could not take them. She took a month to fix it and I had to take all the past quizzes in one day. She is a super harsh grader and does not explain why she took off points. She assigned about 15 pages of reading each week along with about 3 assignments a week plus a quiz. A 95% is 4.0 and a 70% is a 1.0.
She wasn't that bad. Seems like a nice enough person but very tough grader. She does offer EC assignments, so look out for those.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I loved Professor GT. I was really struggling in the beginning of the semester and I met with her to talk about it. She helped me feel so much better. Going to her office hours makes a huge difference as well. It is a heavy course load but that's partly due to the fact that they are preparing future teachers. I would take this class again!
Super sweet professor! Ended the class with over 100% because she gave several EC opportunities. Assignments went with the course and weren't super hard, quizzes were short and eas

I am shocked by her reviews, but my personal experience was very different. She offered several extra credit opportunities, and she gave us access to the assignment guidelines very early on, giving us plenty of time. The assignments weren't hard but also weren't just busy work. She was always sweet and encouraging in lecture, I really liked her!

I was confused by the bad reviews at first because my first couple assignments went great. Until recently, I think this is targeted towards the TA, Sylvia Lin, it took forever to get grades in.
