Thank you, Imen, for your great effort in prompting me to leave this university! Not to even mention her horrible TAs. Can't solve your questions but at the same time will berate you over a small single mistake.

Difficult because it is an online class that needs lectures. You don't see professor Zaabar often. The TA's teach the lab and they are ok. Videos are boring. 

Grades: the class is 30% projects (very difficult and you get 1-2 weeks per project), 60% exams (all coding, not to bad), 5% homework assignments (easy), and 5% quizzes (easy).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Do not come to this school if you want to study CSE. Please just leave. I am actually losing hair over this class. There is a special place in hell for Imen and I'm not just saying that. She is horrible and deserves the worst. This class is uncompletable. Look up the grade distribution for this class.

Very unkind to new learners, very tough grader, lots of tough assignments, and so unfortunate to be around. MSU needs to revise this class and not make it so hard for a beginner class. Turns many off of coding as a whole.

This is my second time taking this class (because i failed it the first time), and things need to be changed drastically. The professor was okay I suppose, but there is no reason for there to be a lot of homework/projects just for the majority of it to not matter because the exams will either make you or break you, even if you do well on hw/projs

The WORST class of MSU. I have over two years of coding experience and yet this class was equivalent to climbing mount everest. the professors aren't teaching at all, and the TAs are useful only in the helproom hours. tbh you cannot score in this class and do not bring your morale down or change your major if you're barely passing this class.

very nice if you talk in office hours. class is hard just because learning computer languages is a new topic to lots of people. The way the professor teaches isnt the problem, its the way the grading is set up. Sometimes the written questions feel like an all or nothing kind of point system. start projects on time and get help when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Advice for anyone taking CSE 231: start the projects early and study for exams. You'll be fine if you can learn quick.

Had no python experience and struggled all the way through. I spent all of my free time in the help room, where every TA knows me by name. I understood the material, but the quizzes and exams (totaling 70% of grade) were all or nothing, ruining my grade. She should be more interested in improving the curriculum instead of researching pavement.
I'm a 4.0 senior Physics major, and this class just ruined my GPA. It also ruined my hair. Thanks.

CSE 231 is NOT A CLASS FOR BEGINNERS. I took 2 years of computer science in hs and am still struggling to get an 80. Prof. Zaabar is however a very kind professor. I have had issues arise from unclear instructions in regards to coding projects, but she is very quick to respond to emails, and help in person if needed.
If you want to 4.0 this class, you either need 2+ years of previous coding experience or you either need to sell your soul.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Sands and her both make the TA's "teach" all the classes, even though the TA's explicitly said they wouldn't teach the material. The lecture videos only explain the bare minimum and don't help. This class has a lot of homework even though exams are 60% of your final grade. Save yourself and take this class anywhere else. Worst class at MSU.
I don't think this professor wanted many students pass this class, because most people I know, who picked this class all failed in the coding exam.
Wasn't too bad. If you pay attention and do projects her course shouldn't be hard

she was a very good professor always responded to my emails, and consider my requests it was a easy class 
for me and if you study hard it will be easy to you.
i went bald

She's a really tough professor and doesn't offer much extra credit or help. She's never really around except during the last 10 minutes of class during the weekly quizzes and at that point doesn't help much at all. She is also a harsh person in general.

When I initially saw the rating for Dr. Zaabar, I was scared for this course. However, I feel like it is super possible to do well in this class, you just can't be afraid of work! Leaving this class I genuinely have a much better handle on Python and found Dr. Zaabar very helpful on Piazza, when she was around in class, or on her hosted reviews!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I have taken in my academic career. my MSU advisor even told me not to take it. Only saw the professor one time, the TA's run her class. The exams are graded so harshly and are weighted at 60%. when the projects are a measly 25%. Do not take this class. Take it at a community college, I wish I listened to my advisor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: shes bad. unhelpful, condescending, and makes the class unreasonably hard. for the amount of effort the projects take, they should really be more than 4% of the grade for 12 hours of work.

Imen Zaabar was the worst professor I have ever had. She doesn't teach students at all, TAs do. The worst thing about the class is the unfair grading. Quizzes and tests are all or nothing. You can go from 100% to 0% based on a grammar mistake. This is not an Intro class, it's more about exams than actually learning. Codeo doesn't even let you debug
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is such a sweetheart and a kind person. Some people may think that she is rough or mean, but in my experience this is tough love rather than her being rude. Her class was alot of work, but she was supportive, office hours she was always helping students, as well as going to help-rooms and responding to Piazza quickly and respectfully.

I understand this is a weeder class but there should be no reason an intro level CS class should be designed so poorly. The content is completely self taught and mostly online. The weighting is very unnecessary and the professor herself only does review sessions and comes to some labs, and most of the content is taught by TAs.

Ever wanted to take an intro class that required absolute perfection? No actual grading (or very very minimal) is done on the exams/quizzes, that would require the profs/TA's to actually do something, so it's all auto-graded and must match the instructor results PERFECTLY. A grammar mistake or missing word can take you from a 100% to 0% quiz grade.
womp womp, drop this class

She's one of the most beloved people on the MSU campus. Her empathy, resourcefulness, and helpfulness have changed my perspective on life. I beg each and every one of you to take her class. Witness her greatness in person! You'll be left in tears for sure.

Zaabar has shown up to a couple of my labs. However, she has not actually participated in any of the course content. 

The review videos are hard to grasp and dragged out, the textbook is absurdly expensive and underutilized, and the quizzes and tests are excessively difficult for the course content taught. The HW projects can take 20+ hours to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zaabar is the most inspiring person I've ever met. I mean it. No one has inspired me more to jump off a cliff and kill myself in a slow, antagonising, brutal way than she has. Her unnecessary in-lab quizzes and exam-heavy policy is prob the reason 90% of my class will eat batteries for breakfast, dinner, and lunch. Mission accomplished?

She doesn't give partial credit at all. If your code does everything except print a space wrong or something like that and fails the check, you will get no credit at all. My exam grade dropped off a cliff because I couldn't get it to perfectly do the checks. Not to mention that you have so little time that you have to rush through the exam.

By far the worst class I have ever taken. I had no knowledge about coding and took the class because I was interested, but the amount of tears and hours spent on this class not even a month in has not been worth it. Maybe the in person sections are a bit better, but good luck if you have never coded before.

Only 3 weeks in, and I already regret it. I read that this was an intro to coding class and thought that this class couldn't be too bad. I was wrong. There are so many assignments with so many tears, I am very new to coding and have received very little help. The only people that teach are the TAs and you receive no feedback from the professor.

It's hard to evaluate Dr. Zaabar because this class is primarily run by the TAs, and most of the content made by professors no longer involved with the course. For an "introduction" class, the exams are unnecessarily difficult and brutal. Be prepared to grind on the projects to absorb the damage from exams. Be sure to pirate the $120 textbook.

It is truly an impressive feat that the professors for CSE 231, including Dr. Zaabar, have accomplished: taking an easy-to-learn concept (Python) and making it a struggle. If you want to do well in this course, you must read the textbook and take thorough notes. You will not do well if you don't understand the concepts taught by the textbook.

As a student finishing the summer semester, and taking it for the second time, it was much better the second time. Weekly review videos and exam review videos were helpful, but will not be enough to pass. Zaabar responded to questions quick at the beginning of the semester, but that did not last for long. If you fail one exam, pray for help.

As a CS major, I would rather touch grass than retake this class. When I asked her about getting credit for one of the mistakes in the exam she told me that her "mistake" wasn't a mistake as there were better academic ways to "trick" us and told me how I should have known the intention behind the question.

The class structure is absolutely horrible, because how is it that everytime there is an exam there's no project that week but for the final exam which is the heaviest and most important one, there is a project due and a penalty added at the last minute. This is ridiculous
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Every week I need to do four assignments. Pre-lab, lab, exercise, and project. Each project spends almost 2 or days and worth almost about 60 credits, and if you lose 100 credits, you will get 3.5, lose for the second 50 credits you will get 3.0 and go on. That means if you want to get a good grade need to finish all the projects and get full score

Capable of teaching just chooses not to it feels like, no lectures, just crappy textbook and videos. Also course policies are hyper unreasonable for an introductory class, 1 hour to code four problems on an exam, you have so many projects that your grades in other classes slip and you are still struggling to get a c in this one. 0/5 if I could.

Weekly programs are quite tough, and sometimes I feel like they are trying to give us headaches purposely. Atleast lecture every week could fix this everything, and I would definitely not miss those lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exams are AWFUL. 50 mins to code 4 separate questions, despite the lab (where you take the exam) going for 2 hrs, and often several definitions in those blocks. Wildly unhelpful, was told to "think about it" after asking a question about a project. Some projects taking more than 30 hrs a week to complete despite me having lots of coding experience

To me it was an easy class. There was a recap of the material that should have been studied before class. There was an in person lab every week with a chunk of code due at the end. Exercises due every Saturday. Project based off of lab concepts that were upscaled due every Monday night.

If you already know ANY coding language, you'll be fine. If not, prepare for hard (but manageable!) work. Tips on how to succeed: 1) start your weekly projects early 2) ask questions 3) form a study group. There are plenty of resources provided (old exam questions, online videos, extra credit...), you just have to be resourceful and use them.

There are projects due every week. It's not unmanageable if you put in the work needed and start it couple days before the due date. Tests are not difficult, as long as you study the past projects/labs. You can bring in 1-page cheat sheet, which will be a lot of help. No previous coding experience needed, if you put in 5-10hrs of work each week.

If you have never taken a coding class before this will be difficult, but manageable. The prof isn't the best, but you will only be dealing with TA's anyways. The profs don't want you to fail so they give many help and review sessions. The class is tough but if you put in effort you will pass.

Dr. Imen always responded fast to emails and piazza posts. I took this over the summer so it was a lot of work per week, but her videos and my previous experience with python helped me through. The exams were easy because she lets you put whatever you want on your cheat sheet.

Dr. Zabaar teaches CSE 231 with Dr. Enbody. To be exact, Enbody has the most control over the class structure, so I don't blame Zabaar for the dismal quality of CSE 231. Zabaar hosted weekly hour-long review sessions which helped somewhat for the exam. She did her best to answer them. It will be a lot better if Enbody was not there in CSE 231.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: don't take this course asynchronously. if you have no other choice, start learning python right now or else you're going to struggle A LOT. the weekly review sessions help but most of the time you're left to fend for yourself. i'm literally begging all future students to reconsider this course, it's genuinely so hard.

Dr. Zabaar teaches CSE 231 alongside Dr. Enbody. As far as I can tell, Enbody has the most control over the class structure, so I don't blame Zabaar for the dismal quality of CSE 231. Zabaar hosted weekly hour-long review sessions which helped somewhat with the difficulty of the class. She was patient with questions and did her best to answer them.
Super sweet and genuinely cares about his students

DO NOT take this professor. His explanations make little sense, all material he teaches is his handwritten notes which are very poorly written and in cursive. None of the class had any idea what was going on most of the time, class average ended as a 1.8 even though the average for the class university wide is a 2.7. 1/3rd of the class got a 0.

Mr. Smith is definitely the best 103 teacher, but the class is hard itself. With lectures being short he doesn't have that much time to go over everything and not a lot of explanation because of that. The 3 exams are hard so be sure to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams are very hard but I think Mr.Smith is the best professor for MTH 103

Don't take this professor if you value your free time. He explains concepts quickly and poorly, writes in cursive, and even when the class average on an exam was failing, he refused to grade on a curve. I barely passed after spending all of my free time supplementing my learning.

His lectures are unfortunately not long enough to go very in depth, so studying and teaching yourself are skills you must learn, which will be needed in your other classes anyway. He drops 1 of 3 exams and 2 of 7 quizzes, so you have breathing room if you bomb something. Very nice person! Writes exclusively in cursive and goes a little fast.

His lectures drag on and on, and he skips over a lot of things, just assuming we know how to do it already. He doesn't really go into detail with a lot of the concepts, which can get tricky when it comes to reviewing for quizzes or exams.

I have never been good at math, and this class made me feel even worse. He's a solid teacher and explains everything well, but there was way too much content for the semester. I would end up re-teaching everything to myself because he would skip around and skim through lessons. He writes in cursive, too, which doesn't help.

I hate math, and this class didn't make me feel any better about it. He's not a bad teacher, his lectures are just boring and everytime he tries to engage with the class only one person answers. This class is way too test dependent. A bunch of quizzes and 3 exams. Lot's of HW but it barely counts for anything.
lots of homework but it only counts for a very little grade percentage. I do like the drop policy for the 2 quizzes and 1 exam.

This professor is caring yeah but ready to not be able to read his writing or keep up with anything. You might as well teach yourself everything outside of class. He doesn't go as in depth with the notes and doesn't cover everything that the quiz and tests are actually on.

I had this class for trigonometry. Joseph is very sweet and cares about students success if you ask for help, and will make accommodations for you. This class is hard based on the way it's set up with weekly quizzes and exams. My one complaint were that the exams were way to long with not enough time to complete. prepare to study a lot.

Was a very good teacher. Took good notes and explained things clearly. he was very easy to work with and talk to. He was super nice, and was always willing to repeat things or explain them differently.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Although I struggled in this class somewhat, Mr. Smith did such a wonderful job encouraging me, and was more than willing to meet with me even outside of his office hours. He's very kind, and you can tell that he enjoyed what he does.

While Professor Smith is a nice person, I would not recommend him as a professor. He often goes at a pace which no students can keep up with. When you attend office hours with questions, he will not give explanations or answers to your questions. Instead, he will counter with a question. DON'T TAKE MATH 103!!!

Writes in cursive, hard to read his work. Often times skips over important problems in the notes, sometimes full pages even if there is an exam that week on the content in the notes. Doesn't go super in depth and quizzes/exams are more complex than the other math 103 professors after comparing quizzes with classmates with other professors.

Smith is a solid professor, but his handwriting is hard to read, making it difficult to follow along in lectures. His tests also seem much harder than the ones given to some of my friends who have other professors for the same class. Overall, just be prepared to put in a lot of effort outside of class studying for the tests/quizzes.
If you want to learn cursive at the same time as learning, I would not take this class. Awful tests, and overall this class is not worth it take it at a community college.

He puts a lot of time and effort into making sure all of his students understand the materials. Recitation can be a little iffy- but for the most part it's pretty easy to follow along. If you show up to office hours, he will go over things as many times as you need to understand.

Solid professor. Lectures were easy to follow, the expectations were super clear, this class is honestly not hard but a lot of people just aren't ready for a college level class. The second exam was a bit challenging so be prepared for that one but a 4.0 is very attainable.

He is a good professor, he just talks and teaches SO fast. He makes it hard to understand how to do algebra. But he is a nice, genuine guy, gives you lots of opportunities to ask questions. He just moves on very quick.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took his online course for MTH103 B. Honestly, one of the nicest professors I have taken thus far. He is very willing to meet outside of class and even let me skip 2 quizzes due to religious reasons. His lectures are simple and easy to understand despite being online. Would take again.

He often didn't go into depth and would skip over the smaller details when doing problems. He writes in all cursive, which can be hard to read at times, especially if you sit further back. I had 3 TAs in a single semester, and they were too stressed out about their own classes and struggled to review the material properly before quizzes/exams.
This is the greatest professor I have ever had at MSU!!! If you take anyone else, you're doing it wrong.

Math is not my strong suit, but Mr. Smith does a pretty good job at explaining each concept considering it is a massive lecture (I think mine had over 300). I utilized the printable guided notes that are provided with the course to help me with note taking during lecture. His office hours are very helpful. Homework is done on inquisitive ($75).

Joesph Smith is nice, but he doesn't have a ton of interaction with the online sections. The lectures weren't usually of him, but recorded videos from other mathematics professors from the previous 1-3 years. The recitation class every week was ran by the ULA, and all of the grading was done by the ULA as well. In-Person is probably better!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: MTH 103 is definitely a hard math class to start with. The content moves very fast, which he does mention at the beginning of the semester, but he is not kidding. Professor Smith is smart but sometimes forgets to go into detail. ULA's grade all exams and quizzes and personally mine did not seem to really understand what she was teaching us.

Math 103 is hard in general. If you want to 4.0 you will need to do a lot of studying outside of class. Exams make up 60% of the grade. Quizzes are 20% and homework is 20%. There is a quiz or exam every Friday and lots of homework. You do not need to go to the lectures. The prof is nice but you really just need to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, if you take this class, make sure to STUDY the basics. The class moves fast, and there are quizzes every week on topics covered in class. In my opinion, Mr. Smith is a great teacher and is available if you have any further questions about the topics, but again you can't pass without studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Smiths lectures are pretty chill he's very wholesome, attendance isn't mandatory so if you miss a class just watch the online lecture. I would recommend him, unfortunately its a math class so its not gonna be that in interesting so this is a good option.

He was a nice guy but not a good teacher. We had a test or a quiz every week and we had lots of homework. The class itself is hard, but he talked so fast, and it was very hard to follow. If you take this class, be prepared to study for 2 hours a day every day.

Very very test heavy, quiz or exam every week of the semester. Homework due dates are provided on the syllabus, but change quite a bit over the semester, so beware. I submitted all of my homework and attended lecture and office hours, but I still didn't grasp the material.

This is a hard class. The lectures are good, and there are many resources to help you. However, the lectures are different from the homework, quizzes, and tests. He is not helpful when it comes to answering questions, and I found him to be lacking. Everything is different so it is hard to know what the tests are like or what is on them.

Attendance was encouraged but not mandatory. He was very accommodating if you needed to miss class or had questions on quizzes. He is easy to reach out to after class, always answers his emails, and has office hours twice a week. Overall, he is a great teacher. I totally recommend him.

Very difficult. Lost my quiz first week of class, and was going to make me take a zero until I fought for it and said I was going to contact math department. Joe is not helpful at all. Lectures are very fast, and nothing really makes sense. Expects you to know stuff from high school, and doesn't give you any help. Good luck!

Extremely difficult professor, his lectures move too fast and he expects us to remember from high school. Homework doesn't match up with the lectures and too many quizzes every single Friday. Had to drop the class, would not recommend this professor.

Professor Smith is one of the best math professors I have ever had. He explains the material thoroughly and clearly, always taking time to ask if we have questions. While there are weekly quizzes or exams it is fairly graded with two dropped quizzes and a dropped exam. There are many resources provided to help struggling students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mth103 shouldn't be this difficult. Far too fast far too much content and weekly quizzes will hurt you if you are not good at math. Save yourself some stress by taking Math 103a, this is not a course that should be taken in one single semester if you aren't good at math. They go through the questions expecting you to already know everything.
Nice guy but this class is so hard for no reason and he does not really do a good job actually helping. He doesn't even go through the lecture notes fully so I basically taught myself all semester

I am absolutely awful at math. I have never been good at it and Mr. Smith seemed to always understand that. I went to a lot of his office hours and he would sit down with me and try to find a way to help me understand the material. Now, I may not have done very well in the class but thanks to Mr. Smith, I was at least able to pass.

I'm not good at nor like Algebra, and this class was partially hard for me. But Mr. Smith made the content easy for my brain to comprehend, which isn't easy. Grades are based on Webwork homework and quizzes and exams done in recitations, there are quizzes or an exam every week. Mr. Smith provides practice exams which helped me a lot! Very grateful.

Once again, you're graded based only on quiz performance, which means if you do bad you do bad. He explains concepts in a way that is much easier to comprehend, and did not make me feel afraid to ask questions! Does a mix of lecture-based teaching and then lets students solve problems on their own while he wanders around the room to help others.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Smith is really nice he actually makes sure you understand what your being taught. Just pay attention in class and make sure to do the work for exams and quizzes.

I took 103B, but he is a great professor. He makes things as easy as he can, but he understands that the course is difficult. Doesn't make you feel bad or stupid. Gives gradescopes (basically free points if you take notes) and is very accessible outside of class. Really good at explaining things if they don't make sense. Just overall a good guy.

This class was online but everything was really easy to get a hang of. If I needed help on any of the subjects, I went to his office hours and he was always willing to help and explain the material to me. Super helpful and wants you to do well!

He provided guided notes for the whole semester, which made following along very easy. Learning was very easy with his style of teaching. I would 100% recommend. Taking his class sets you up for success as long as you put in the effort. Used webwork, and was never that tricky.
Doesn't even teach lectures to us

Prof. Smith is great with students, and is accessible in and out of class. His lectures are pretty chill, he just goes over the material and engages with the class. Participation every now and then matters, be ready to watch some videos every now and then for clarification in case he's not available after class. 10/10

Prof.Smith was the best professor I have ever had. His lectures are amazing and he explains everything so well. He is a very good communicator, and advocates for his students. Homework is through Webwork which is super annoying, but easy to work through once you get the hang of it. If I could have Smith for every class in the future I would.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was an awesome math teacher and genuinely wants all his students to succeed.
He is one of my favorite math professors ever. He gives you so many resources to get help and will gladly make time for you if you need his help.
Great Professor. Is very helpful with questions related to the homework and quizes and is very informative relating to key dates such as when homework is due or when quizes are.
Genuinely a good professor who wants the best for everyone. Would recommend his class to everyone.

Im a freshman at msu currently taking math 103A online with professor smith, Smith is a very nice guy, he answers emails very quickly, and is easy to find outside class. He is a younger guy so its sometimes easier to relate to him, I'm not very math savvy and the content lately has been hard for me but Smith teaches it very well and cares.
clear expectations, planning to take his 103B course next semester !
Good
Easy to get along with and is always answering questions, tries to explain in different ways so everyone can understand. Likeable guy and is helpful on office hours. TA's are good too!

Janet is a great teacher. She is passionate about what she teaches and is a very nice lady. You can tell she cares about her students. I took 2 classes with her and felt well supported through both of them. I would recommend.

5 stars. Janet was the best teacher that I have had yet. she gives awesome lectures, and I would take her class one thousand times over.  I hope that Janet will keep teaching and giving help to students that need it. Janet is the best teacher I could ask for, and I hope to see her on campus again.
Great professor who cares about the students. Shares real life experiences to help make topics relatable. She is very understanding with absences and make ups.

The most flexible professor ive ever had. She is super chill when it comes to missing class or late assignments/exams. She gives amazing exam reviews and basically tells you exactly what to study. She canceled class a ton but I didnt mind that. Not the best at responding to emails, so just go up to her after class. Overall super nice women
She was very easy going when it came to accidentally missing an assignment or doing bad on an exam (offered retakes). Very understanding

Professor Hauck is super nice and very accommodating. She is passionate about what she teaches making it easy to understand and sets you up to succeed for every test/quiz. She is one of the best professors Ive had at MSU!
Dr. Hauck clearly outlines what will be on exams and is very passionate while lecturing. If you're pursuing OT/PT/PA, DR. Hauck will prepare you for your future career.

Janet Hauck has to be one of the best kinesiology professor at MSU. She was very caring and made learning fun! Attendance is sorta mandatory because there are quizzes on specific weeks but you don't know what day it will be so just go to class. Overall, great professor!!

Dr.Hauck is an amazing professor who cares truly for her students! Her class is interesting, and structured nicely. She only has 3 assignments throughout the semester that are not time consuming at all, and 3 exams which she will go over with you in class what questions to expect. They take a bit of studying, but are not hard. Highly recommend her!
LOVE HER! she really cares about students and wants you to do well! also very passionate about what she teaches

Dr. Hauck was amazing! She is so passionate about this class, and it shows in her lectures. She gives so many real-life examples of her experiences working with children with disabilities. The exams are not hard, but you do have to study a few hours for each one to learn some material. Show up and listen in class and you'll do great.

This might sound like some sort of joke, but I literally genuinely have a hand built shrine in my apartment to Jeemin Kim and his Kin 440 class, where I bow down and pay my respects to the important and useful information taught in this class everyday. All hail Kin 440, and its achievements toward eventually achieving world peace.

I love, LOVE Jeemin. He is my only friend, and sometimes I think back to his class and cry real actual tears, from remembering his beautiful haircut, which too inspired me to use an entire bottle of gel every morning. I often have dreams about his class while reminiscing what once was, whispering to myself, "I'll never forget you Jeemin"

Semester long project, I had multiple meetings with him abt my sources bc was hard finding ones that met the criteria. Found one, sent to him, said it was good, took points off because it wasn't good enough. Final presentation, sent him my slides, he said there were too many words, I made it bullet points, he took points off for not enough words.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The material was engaging, but Dr. Kim makes the class unnecessarily stressful. Office hours are limited, and communication—including emails and assessment feedback—can be rude or insulting. Assessment instructions are unclear, grading inconsistent, and most of the grade is crammed into the last weeks. Unnecessarily frustrating for a KIN cognate.

Dr. Krans is honestly the most caring professor I have ever had. She truly cares about students and is a great teacher.

Professor Henson is one of the best professors I have had, he is very passionate about what he teaches and is always there to help if you have any questions. Dr. Henson seems to really enjoy his job, which makes a huge difference because he is really passionate about teaching and students' learning. teaches well
Honestly love this course and the material, especially when lectured by Dr. Henson. Great guy and great class.

She is honestly super sweet and likes to engage with her class. there is a-lot of bust work to prepare before class and you are expected to know it for the in class activity and quizzes that are every day. I learned a-lot overall though! do not skip class

She is sweet but I HATE how this class is a flipped course. Honestly believe if it was like a regular lecture, many would know what the heck is going on in class. She knows what shes doing.

I LOVED Dr. Krueger for BS161! Professor Krueger is such a sweet heart. She is super helpful in class and will make sure you understand the iClicker if you ask her. The class is a hard class so be sure to do the online lectures. Her help rooms and very helpful and she is more than happy to help you.

Lots of resources for this class which can students if they choose to use them. Professor Krueger is very understanding and she gets to know all her students. This class you do have to stay on top of the work since the class is not a traditional lecture class.

Great

Just started taking this class and already know it's gonna be good

The expectations are clear from the start and he constantly gives away exam answers. If you pay attention and take notes you'll have a 4.0 before even taking the final.

Prof. Kang sets clear, basic expectations with TopHat quizzes and homework. Each exam has a review session where he literally spells out what questions will be on the exam. He literally tells you the questions and answers them... It can still be a challenging class, obviously, but that's the content. Don't hate the player, hate the game.
A good professor overall. Can be a little difficult to hear/read his handwriting sometimes, but not too bad. He did a good job of teaching most of the content, but he relies heavily on TopHat.

I absolutely loved Professor Kang. If you are willing to pay attention, I can assure you will actually retain the concepts. Really take the review sessions serious, they are beyond helpful. His office hours truly made me succeed in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The exams are a lot like the practice tests that he gives you, as a lot of the answers are the same. As long as you take notes and do the participation points, and homework you should be fine. I really liked him as a person too.

Genuinely don't know how he's still allowed to teach at MSU. Only cares about 15% of class getting 4.0. Grades on a curve instead of curving the exams themselves. Doesn't teach, just clicks through slides fast and does confusing examples. Class is way harder then it needs to be. Everything is online, even exams. You're better off taking online.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Teaches at an extremely fast pace and is very difficult to understand. Exams are very lecture heavy and attendance is required.

Professor Kang is a simple professor who expects the students to understand the material taught in the lectures and then apply the knowledge on the exams. If you pay attention in his class it's not that difficult of material being taught. He is difficult to understand at times and his handwriting isn't the best. Take good notes and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take Econ201 with Kiwon. Very difficult to follow due to his monotone voice, fast-paced content and horrible handwriting. Class avg my semester was below a 60% on exams and progressively dropped with each exam. Attendance is very important as he has live questions online that are directly related to content that is projected on the screen.

Kiwon Kang is by far the worst professor I've ever had the misfortune of having. His lectures are dull and his voice exceedingly monotone. A majority of my fellow students in this course are boasting 50 percents or lower, with the class average even being below 50%. Homework usually consists of over 40 questions every night. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kang knows his stuff, but he goes really fast in his lectures because he covers a lot of things, especially on exam reviews! Attendance isn't mandatory but he always has pop quizzes in class which are graded. Overall he's an ok teacher if you're good at econ and focus really hard and pay attention. The 3 exams are major parts of the grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Take EC 201 with ANYONE else. I have never in my life failed a class, let alone one that I did every homework question and attended every lecture. The exams are impossible and the TopHat is extremely hard to study. He said that even though he had HUNDREDS of emails asking for extra credit, there was nothing he could do.

Literally the worst professor I have had at MSU. I can get past his accent, as most of my professors have thick accents, but he is so monotone when talking about an already boring topic. He also has a very low score average, making 65%s curve up to 80%s. If you can take a different econ professor, I highly encourage it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Goes at fast pace, gives pop up quizzes on things that his lecture doesn't really target.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kang is a good professor who has a lot of office hours. In large classroom settings, it can be hard to hear and understand him in the back so you will need to sit closer to the front.
Tests are very difficult, but he will work with you to help you improve your grade if you reach out for help. One chapter of reading assigned per class. Very nice guy.

I cannot pass this class and I'm usually good at econ. The tests are impossible, with the class average being 50% on both exams. I currently have a 47% in the class, but he never made it clear where i would end up after the curve. I wouldnt recommend him to anyone, and I wish someone warned me not to take his class. My GPA is going to plummet!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are insane with class averages below 55%. So much content with barely anytime to comprehend it. Just regurgitates the text book for an hour and 20. You can not pay attention even if you enjoy the subject matter
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is miserable to listen to. You cannot pay attention if you tried. Tests are curved but whole does so poorly it doesn't change anything. Grade scale is by class percentage not by points so your will be a surprise . Tests are hard and not enough to buffer any bad grades.
How does one pass this class without needing to cheat this bro aint teaching nothing

He lectures two chapters ahead of the weekly homework's and moves through the lecture so fast that it's nearly impossible to take notes. The tests are incredibly difficult and your score is pretty much irrelevant, all that matters is the curve. Also be familiar with TopHat because that's all he uses.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him this semester and this is the hardest class I've ever taken. Tests are very hard and make up most of your grade. Homework and popup quizzes will help your grade. You have to teach yourself and honestly pray you do well. Final grade is curved, based on percentile of the class. This class makes me wanna cry ngl. Lucky if I finish with a 2.5.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Cannot read the room to save his life, and blamed the students for not understanding a concept that he spent less than 5 minutes on. His teaching style is probably fine for some but it wasn't for me. Really important to listen in lectures but prepare to teach yourself out of the textbook.
But it's an econ class so it wasn't hard
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kang seems like a humble, sweet guy, but his class was just not for me. He is available outside of class and is often flexible with make-ups. If you don't read the textbook or actively pay attention in class, you will do horrible. Even if you do pay attention, its very possible that you won't do as well as you would hope. I think we all struggled

Professor Kang really cares about his students and wants to make sure you succeed. Overall the class is tough and you will definitely need to put in the work to do well. You have to attend the zooms because he does attendance questions, and you will also want to make sure you take good notes to do well on the exams. I would definitely recommend him
Grades on a curve, also he let me redo the final so he's very flexible. Good man.

He is a great professor and cares about his students. He allows extensions and gives help during his office hours. Quizzes are given during class, so going to class is mandatory. The exams make up most of your grade and are hard, so you need to study hard. He curves your grade at the end of the year. You need to take lots of notes in class.

Kang cares about his students and makes himself available for extra guidance. Everything is based on TopHat, so you don't technically have to be in class to get credit, but I would recommend it. The exams are tough but your GPA is based on a curve, so even though I got a B in the class I still finished with a 4.0. Overall, a solid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was fine, but Professor Kang is hard to understand sometimes. It's nice that your exam grades can be balanced out by homework and attendance points. He's always willing to help and is accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This man changed my life in the world of Micro Economics, he is an amazing lecturer as well as a respected faculty member, 11/10 would recommend.
His lectures always contain humor. As long as you do ok on the midterms, he gives a pretty generous curve.
being not a business major, this class got very repetitive and boring. just go to class and read the notes and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Kang tries really hard to make sure everyone understands his lectures, but microeconomics is just a tough class. Make sure to take the quizzes on TopHat seriously, because those will affect your grade and they help prepare you for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I can tell he's good at what he does, but some people may find it hard to understand him. Therefore some may find the class to be difficult. Overall he's a decent professor.

Prof. Kang has a very thick accent and if you have trouble with accents I'd recommend finding a different professor. Attendance is necessary for lecture notes. Exams are graded on a curve, a total of two midterms and a final exam. Homework is done through Pearson MyEconLab with a total of 22 assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Greatest teacher I ever had.
Do not need to show up to class Cant understand him Nice person Big curve Need your book and do the online hw

Good teacher, at times hard to understand, but text is clear, and easy to understand. Generous curve. Recommended if your motivated and interested, if not  his accent may make the class difficult for you.

This class was extreamly difficult to stay focused in becasue Kang is not so easy to follow in his venacular. But on the up side she is very helpful and intellegent. You have to keep up on readings becasue he is hard to understand at times. He basis he tests of his lectures so although attendences isn't required I would still go to class.

The best professor I have had yet at MSU.  I hate econ, but he actually made it tolerably.  He knows a lot, and if you go to his office hours he makes it easy to understand.  His teaching style was highly effective for me, so I recommend taking this class with him.
Speaks good english but sometimes I had a hard time understanding him, he was very helpful to those who asked and paid attention
He will take points off your grade if you submit an assignment in PDF form and he can't figure out how to download it himself. Very unfair grader.

I didn't think this class was that hard, and it was nice to be able to have a cheat sheet on the exams, but the exams themselves were really hard and worth about 70% of our grade. No one shows up for his class because he is such a slow lecturer and goes on long tangents (making it more confusing). You may as well teach yourself most of the content.

I made a Rate My Professor account just to leave this review. Avoid if possible. Take-home online exams sound great, but each one takes around 10 hours. Lecture slides are not posted, making studying much harder. He also complained about attention in class and banned phones/laptops. Only take if you absolutely need the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Leonidas Murembya, was an amazing teacher and has a really good way of getting you to understand the content in such a big class. The homework is graded by completion which really helps so you don't feel scared to get something wrong. The exams are so easy to prepare for. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: went so fast and couldn't understand

reviews.comment: Overall, the class (macroeconomics) was not difficult, albeit the lectures were rather dull. Better to teach the material to yourself through just doing the homework. Went faster that way than his lectures, anyhow
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very hard class (Macro) already, but he made it more difficult with hard-to-follow lectures and a lot of information that he does not give examples about. On the exams, he does not test on what he teached nor the info from the book. He does have a very generous curve to the whole class tho.

This class was relatively easy. Grading scale was great (81=4.0) and you were able to use a cheat sheet for every exam. Lectures were just very dense and boring, and he can be difficult to understand. Overall, easy but extremely tedious.

The lectures are painful to sit through, you have to buy books that I didn't open once and the walking to that class everyday felt awful. He goes over definitions rather than actually teaching how to put it to use. DONT TAKE

I lowkey think economics comes easy to me so while I may not have struggled my friends in the class did. He is a horrible teacher and I gained nothing from showing up to class since it is incredibly difficult to understand him, he is a nice guy though.

if you actually pay attention in his class and take the time to read the textbook and do assignments, this class is a breeze. the one downside is the textbook was over $100 and required. mr leo was very kind and helpful, as well as the TA.
He teaching style is awful and is constantly asking everyone for the answers but HE is supposed to be the one teaching.
Dr Leo keeps saying to do practice problems but then there are things on the exam that were never covered.

Someone that and I quote "failed Economics my first time taking it" shouldn't be teaching this course. Dr Leo also has a strong accent and a studder so it was really hard to understand him. I ended up having to teach myself most of the topics. We got cheat sheets on exams but even with all the key ideas on my cheat sheet it wasn't much help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is 30% homework grade which makes for a really easy 100% on that category. The rest of your grade is made up of 3 exams worth a total 70% or 23.33% each. The 4.0 cutoff is an overall 81% in the class. Do good on the exams and you'll do well in the class. Overall good EC202 class and teacher.
This guy blows
you know.. im about to take the final. I am praying with the peers next to me.

Absolutely loved attending every lecture. Doctor Leo is a great professor. He is great at preparing students for homework and exams, and keeps them engaged with humor. Class was late, but often ended early. The exams are not very difficult as long as you dedicate time to studying. You must spend $125 on an online textbook to do any work.

Be prepared to do a lot of studying and learning outside of class. Lectures are difficult to pay attention to, but if you study you will pass the class. Leo is nice and emails back fast but went over material very quickly.

Not a horrible professor in my opinion, other reviews scared me at first but overall the material in this class is not that diffficult and if you put in a decent amount of effort you should be fine, just be ready to sit through some boring lectures
He doesn't explain anything well. The tests are weighted very heavy, and the grading calculator he has is very unclear.

He's a funny guy and makes jokes to keeps students engaged. Attendance and weekly homework/ quizzes may seem minor but largely contribute to your overall grade. The reviews scared me at first but it turned out to be a good class. Allows cheat sheets on exams and lectures pretty fast but he'll explain a topic if you don't understand.
Tough to understand, will give very poor grades over small mistakes, and unwilling to negotiate on any grade given.

This class make me want to put my fist though a wall every time I show up. He rushes through lectures and it makes it impossible to be engaged in what he has to say. This is definitely the worst class I have ever taken and I wish that I dropped it. Don't take if you have any self respect. You will be teaching yourself the whole semester.
It's impossible to communicate with him.
He is a very nice guy, however, he is really hard to understand, and his exams had nothing to do with what you learned during his lectures.

writing  while in his class right now, ive been in here for 47 minutes and I've already dropped it. He's a very kind soul from what I can tell but the other reviews are already correct, I can tell this will make me want to slam my head into the nearest wall, $124 for a textbook is crazy, I have $56 to my name after paying for college. Don't do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you do the homework each week you should be fine. 3 exams throughout the semester but does not connect with the students. However you are allowed a cheat sheet for the exams.

You will be fine if you attend lectures and pay attention. The ratings here make you second-guess the class, but you will be fine if you read the book and pay attention. Many students don't attend lectures and, therefore, don't know what's going on. All it takes in this class is a little studying and paying attention. Don't let the reviews scare.

At first, he seemed like a super nice guy, but the more lectures you attend, the more you want to drop out of college. The lectures were impossible to pay attention and the exams were extremely difficult. Even with a cheat sheet, the average exam grade was almost failing. I would not recommend this class to anyone unless it is the only class open.

The lectures are extremely boring. He doesn't use a microphone, and it is hard to hear and understand the lecture. The lectures are very unclear, and although you can use a cheatsheet the exams are still incredibly difficult. You can study so much and still not do well.  The class average is so low. Do not take this class.

every time I had to go to his godawful macro class I would try to get run over on my way there. I have never been more bored in my life listening to him lecture.he barely teaches anything you have to rely on the online textbook that is so expensive. there is an attendance clicker every class that needs your location. don't take him you'll wanna die

One of my worst MSU classes ever. The tests are tricky, even with cheat sheets, and the material doesn't match what we learn. The teacher isn't clear and often goes off-topic. I studied hard but still struggled on tests. The class average was almost failing. Too many boring quizzes and the teacher isn't helpful at all and is bad at email.

As a person, he is amazing! Super nice & always willing to help. His lectures were just very unstructured & I don't think I retained much. I'd take quizzes/exams & there would be material on there I have never heard of, & I attended every single class. When it came to exams, I seriously didn't know what to focus on.

Overall this course was terrible, I often found myself not wanting to go to his lectures halfway into the semester. He is a very nice professor, but he is not a good teacher. He will spend so much of your time on useless tangents and all he does is move the information slides extremely quickly, you will NOT be able to write down the slides in time.

This class was difficult due to the little communication that happened. Professor Murembya is a very smart person, but not good at talking about the topics he exceeds in. He grades 70% of your grade on 3 tests that cover the content broadly with everything else coming from a textbook that you have to buy. Please avoid this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are the most boring thing in the entire world that I just use it to catch up on other classes homework. Heavy accent so very hard to understand and keep engaged. I would not recommend this course with him at all, and I think that the university should have stricter teaching standards.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most boring class I've ever been to. Very hard to engage and stay engaged. Many people either leave during class or don't come at all until exam days.
Really long lectures that are not at all engaging. A lot of people leave the class it's so boring. Not a lot of people in class until exam days. Exams count for 70% of final grade.

He seems nice and passionate about his job.  However, lectures are so boring and the slides have basically no pictures or diagrams to keep us engaged. Expect to see the class to be empty during lectures and only full during test days.

One of the worst professors I have had. Terrible lectures. So boring and only teaches to the front two rows in a 500 person class. Everyone leaves the class because of how bad it is. Exams are hard and all 3 count towards your final grade and are almost all of your grade. No extra credit. Doesn't reply to emails. Nice guy just not a good teacher.

Very nice, but long lectures that aren't interactive. Has made comments toward us regarding our social class, stating we're here because of our "parents money," and that we "probably come from wealthy families," which isn't true for myself and others. Homework levels are an okay amount.

In the first lecture he mentioned how all of us were here with "your parent's money", so we needed to be grateful of being here. This is not only a hot button for many college students but also untrue in many cases, i.e. student loans that will last a lifetime. Decent prof material-wise but very tone-deaf sometimes. Overall 2 maybe 2.5 out of five.

The lectures are so long and boring. Teacher does nothing during them to keep you engaged. There are no in class activites or quizzes to help you apply what you learned. He just reads the notes that he later posts online. Homework is easy, tests are hard. He's a nice guy, I just don't think he's a fantastic teacher.
Awesome teacher

great asynch class with very organized d2l that made it really easy to keep track of work. decent amount of work due every week and a half, but its manageble. my only complaint is some of the "tech tasks" and "investigations" were so unnecessarily long and arduous it got really annoying.

great professor! very organized d2l page that is easy to access and check off. it can be a lot considering the amount of videos and other assignments for the week like webwork ($50-55 for the semester), snapshots, and projects, but everything is set up monday and due the next wednesday which is great and lets me work on other things! no final exam!

GREAT PROFESSOR! This course was online and organized well. Everything was super easy to locate in D2L and help was easily accessible outside of class. You're given ample time to complete assignments, but I personally used an assignment tracker spreadsheet to help. Easy to excel in this class if you follow the guidance and manage your time well!

This class reminded me so much of the same way a high school class was like where the teacher actually helped you understand. But overall, the professor was very involved even though it was an online class they always provided office hours, so they did want you to succeed and pass but still understand the material that was being taught.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Lund assigned many group projects. The groups changed all the time so each week or so you got to text strangers asking for their feedback on your work. Usually they wouldnt respond but sometimes they did. It was great.
Professor Lund was fantastic. The class was really easy and she made things easy to understand, I didn't feel stressed by her class at all.

She is crazy organized, and it makes the class so much easier!! Clear planner for every week with hyperlinks and amount of points each assignment is worth. The TAs and her are kind of picky graders, but it's not difficult to do well; you just have to try.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Class was super easy! All the assignments were easy and able to be completed with little trouble. The feedback always made sense and the grader was also forgiving. Would 100% take again.
LOVED this course. Professor Lund made everything easy to understand and answered my questions right away. Not a very overwhelming amount of work if you keep up with the due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She was great! There were many little tasks to complete, but there was a large emphasis on success. Her lecture videos were always clear, and the class was much easier as a result. I would absolutely take a course taught by her again.

Rachael is a very kind and understanding professor. The class is entirely asynchronous but she provides excellent lecture videos and is available and offers so much help for her students. She really cares for everyone and wants everyone to do well.

Loved this prof!! Super helpful, always available if needed. The lectures were engaging in my opinion, and the due dates are clear. At the end of the course she dropped the 3 lowest grades from every section. As long as you submit assignments on time, you'll do good in the class

Dr Lund was so amazing I was hesitant to take an online math class because math is not my strongest subject, but she made it so manageable. The class relates heavily to everyday math as well as graphs. Dr Lund was always there for any questions you had and would answer within 24hrs. She was amazing and made me confident in math again!

such an easy and organized online class. professor really cares about students success and makes learning the material easy. responds timely to emails, no exams, clear layout of work due each week, webwork subscription needed but overall extremely light workload and easy A

I took this course asynchronously with Professor Lund and although everything was remote, it was clear she was a very sweet woman and was very passionate about teaching the material. This class was very organized with a module to do every week that consisted of vidoes/notes, webwork, a snapshot, and a project, along with a weekly survey!
She is very sweet and this class was super organized and easy. Def would take her if you need to

Amazing prof! The class is very easy and can be as hands on/hands off as you need/want. Lund really cares about student's success, but is aware the course is meant to be a very easy math course. The most well-organized I've ever seen an online course page be, it's very easy to keep track of what you need to do. If you need a math credit, I'd recc.

Professor Lund is extremely caring, she was one of the few professors that actually wanted to sit down with me, one on one, to discuss my disability accommodations and how I could be better serviced in the course. She sends out emails often telling the student how they are doing and makes them personally tailored to each student.

She is a great professor and explains things well. I feel like I learned something from this class and at no point was I confused. Her D2L page layout is easy to use and it is easy to see when to turn things in.
She is a great professor and very easy to get a hold of for help.
The course was straightforward/simple. Content was not especially engaging. The video lectures were low quality. A course this easy is not university level.

If you dont have to take MTH 101 or 102 absolutely do not. They are painfully easy. Not worth their cost in tuition. Prof. Lund may be organized but her judgement is questionable and has resulted in trauma being inflicted on students.

I took MTH 101 and it was fairly easy. As long as you do the work you should pass with no problems. We had the same things due every module and she gave us more than a week to work on it. I recommend this teacher for this class because of how clear she was. She would provide an exact checklist with links for each module that was assigned.

this class was literally so easy and well organized. shes usually pretty available if you need help but all of the lectures & assignments were very clear. just put in 1-2 hours of effort a week for this class & youll effortlessly receive a 4.0

Prof was exceptionally good. Not much of a character, but made an effort to check in with us. Even gave us a little break mid semester to refresh. Material is easy, but I was annoyed when we had to pay $50 for a web tool that could have been done on D2L.

not much homework, group projects that were pretty pointless because they were so easy. honestly didnt learn anything. there was no midterm but a final that i didnt do well on. i think math is hard to learn online and she isnt a bad teacher. wasnt very organized online, she changed some things around but it was still confusing.
Pretty easy class, laid back and super helpful TAs

Rachael is a great professor. She always always always tries to set her students up for success as much as possible with exams/projects/labs. If it wasn't for attendance points then I would have never gone to class tbh, but overall, she's an awesome person and professor.

Professor was pretty decent but TA was horrible and that makes all the difference. There were weekly homework assignments on webwork. Recitation attendance was mandatory, there you work in groups on labs, and take snapshots/tests once a week. Midterm and Final aren't too bad as long as you study. One big project which is easy. Lectures are helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Lund is awesome! She does a great job of explaining the concepts covered in depth so that I can understand them. She loves answering questions and helping her students understand better. I really appreciated how accessible she is outside of class. She cares about her students.
Conveys material clearly and truly cares about her students.

Rachael was the kind of prof that told you exactly what you needed to know, why you needed to know it, and how to remember it. She didn't go through every proof, but she explained the ones that would help us understand the material. A++++ loved the class and the occasional stories that she told to break up the lectures.

This was my second time taking calc 2 and if I did not have Professor Lund I definitely would have failed again. She is the BEST calc 2 professor at MSU. Do yourself a favor and take her class, don't waste your time with any other calc 2 professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Rachael is really nice. She makes everything clear and she really cares about students success in this course. The most important-she is very positive-always have a smile on her face.

Rachael Lund is a great professor.  The calculus program at MSU is super difficult and the exams sometimes seem nearly impossible.  Rachael makes everything very clear and doesn't move on until everyone seems to understand the material.  I am not even a math person and I could follow everything going on.

Laura Perensen is a great teacher. Explains concepts well and goes into the 'why' behind it. Helped me learn a whole lot better and excel in this class. Very knowledgeable and kind. Quizzes every week, recitation activities, Webwork homework, and exams make up grade. Sometimes extra credit. Final isn't cumulative. Practice before exams and easy A.

Professor Perensen was great! Good lectures, breaks everything down, and answer questions. This is a college math class so prepare to go fast, but recitations help out a lot (shoutout Alaina). Almost weekly quizzes, webwork, and 4 exams. I suggest going to lectures as they are not mandatory, unlike recitations which are.

Very nice professor. The lectures are not mandatory but recitations are with two drops. You also get two drops for quizzes. You can do really good on the quizzes and not so great on the exams and still pass the class. Print out the worksheets before class so you don't have to write each thing down. Had Muzammil as a TA and he was amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was one of the easiest classes ive taken at MSU. I was familiar with the content when starting but not confident. Laura explains everything in a way that is easily digestable and understandable. Lots of homework, but the exam questions are almost identical to the recitation activity (take the section with Muzammil, hes awesome too!)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher! Lectures are easy and well organized. She's always willing to help you when you have questions. As long as you show up to the class and complete the assignments on time you'll be fine on the quizzes and exam.

Professor Perensen is a very good math professor at MSU. She helped me understand certain parts of algebra I had trouble with in high school. Now, I had taken precalc, but this class does more than teach you algebra. She also teaches you concepts that will be taught in Calc 1 to better prepare you for that class.

I loved this professor, he made class interesting. Although online synchronous class, a great professor who answered all questions and made expectations clear. During the online class, we went through the case studies which connected back to the online lectures - the structure of the class is great.

I was really excited to take this class, but also worried that we would have a professor that wouldn't meet the expectations of excitement of everyone taking this course. Dr. Nichols is a great lecturer, always takes time to answer questions and go back over things, always stays after class, and is really quite funny. Come to class, put effort into learning the material, you will do great. One of my new favorite professors!

Dr. Nichols was an amazing professor! He's very knowledgable, kind, reasonable, and funny. Solid class

pretty good.
