Highly recommend to have a fit faculty to this position. ICRC is the WORST i met

WORST professor in CSE I currently a senior.The exams do not test your understanding of the material instead,they feel more like reading comprehension exercises with poorly aligned questions More concerning is that the exam questions seems AIgenerated,Many cases,the wording is confusing,don't trust the rate here it seems she rating herself here.

Professor Onsay is the best CSE professor that you can take. She prepares you for the real world by giving out questions interviewers would use. Her lectures are fun, she really loves engaging with her students and making everyone feel welcome. The exams are laid out by section on d2l where she gives you each slide and project you need to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Onsay is the bestest professor I have ever experienced!! She is always very supportive to her students to keep track of the progress we have done and she generally is very appreciative of my eagerness towards learning CSE 331 as well as suggesting me to go to review sessions for exams to clear up all the concepts leading to difficultly
Actually cares about her students, probably one of the most caring professors you can have.
bro w professor bro fr

This course feels very repetitive among all the assignments, with everything being fully taught atleast twice for the most part. While DSA is very important for CS, the amount of work for this class definitely felt like atleast 4 or 5 credits worth. Otherwise, if you study and apply yourself in the coursework, you will be successful in this course.

Onsay is my favorite professor by far, and I have spent 2 years at MSU. She is sweet, caring, respecting, and does everything she can to help us understand the material and do well in the class. She does give a decent bit of easy homework, but all of it is HEAVILY related to the material and WILL HELP YOU and your grade - DO THEM. I will miss her.

Passionate and caring professor, calls us all "colleagues" and has us build our "backpack" of knowledge to apply to future projects, interviews, and jobs. There is a lot of content to learn, but class is paced reasonably. Only critique is many things are redundant (lectures, videos, Zybooks all teach the same thing) and d2l is hard to navigate.

Dr. Onsay is an engaging lecturer, which made the content easy to understand intuitively. The course load is very heavy, so it does take time to get used to, and you should give yourself at least a few hours a week on CCs and Projects. She doesn't penalize for AI, but it's hard to do well on exams if you rely on it entirely to code for you.

Onsay is by far one of the best professors i've had. She really cares for the students and structures the course for our long term career benefit. The exams are very easy to study for, the textbook and assignments give you everything to get at least a 3.0 in the class if you study. Theres a good amount of work required but it comes on the exams.

Bro she a GOAT. The course is chill, a lot of working but if you just see her videos and then go to lecture you'll be fine. She understands you got stuff going. She chill and tbh you can really vibe with her if you enjoy DSA like she does. Also she always looking for TAs so if you wanna be one just participate and make yourself known

You can tell she loves to teach and is good at it. If you put in the work, you will get a good grade. Lots of homework in this class but its good because it reinforces the material you are going to be tested. Class material is useful for future success as well. Great class in general, she is very caring. D2L is a mess lol

The workload is that of a 3 course class but the amount of repetition between the lectures, the lecture videos, and the online book makes it feel like a 4 course class. She really cares for her students and their success. The exam content is very fair for the most part but going back through content to study takes a lot of time.

Very poorly structured & disorganized course. Too much material: unnecessarily repetitive with videos, zybooks, lectures covering the same content. Took WAY more time than my other classes combined. D2L is a mess, with content all over the place. Each project is 1% & each exam is 17% of your grade. Def NOT a 3 credit workload, more like 5 credits.

The professor is great, and you can tell she cares about the students. My only complaint is that the class has tons of material, and she does a terrible job of organizing things on D2L. It is such a mess and hard to study for an exam. The concepts are fairly easy but she tends to overcomplicate them when explaining in class.

Onsay is a good professor and cares about students. However, the course itself is poorly organized and sometimes burdensome for no reason. The flipped classroom introduces repetitive work, which ends up being very time-consuming without significantly improving learning outcomes. Students are flooded with a jumbled collection of course material.

It's easily the biggest relief of a professor at MSU for CSE. Onsay deeply cares about her students and wants them to succeed. There is a lot of work within the course, don't get me wrong, but because of that, It requires little studying because the content is drilled into your head. I would rework a class schedule to be in her class personally.
It is a crying shame that Prof Onsay teaches but one computer science course.

I really liked this class. It was painful and stressful, but that comes with the computer science territory. The online textbook & D2L page have plenty of material, and ChatGPT is semi-allowed. Not to write a whole project, but great as a debugger. Just make sure you know the content by heart before exam night though!

Dr. Onsay will \provide you with support and care about your learning if you participate in class and put in effort. Although this class is not easy, she makes a great learning environment for all of her students. Make sure to utilize helprooms when taking this class as the TA's provide lots to offer as well.

She's definitely my favorite professor I have had within the MSU computer science department. She really seemed to care about her students and her lectures were actually engaging. She tells you exactly how it is, even if it's not what you would want to hear which I really respect in a professor. She was great in preparing us for a future in CS!

Professor Onsay is probably the best professor I've had here. She is passionate about what she teaches and genuinely cares about her students. The workload for this class is heavy, but if you run into problems, the helprooms are well run and worth it. Most of the content follows alongside zybooks. Overall an amazing professor.

Unexpectedly, the professor suggested I switch from my computer science major, despite her reputation for excellence based on positive reviews. The course, biased towards stronger students, missed practical elements and was excessively fast-paced, culminating in a disheartening experience.

Class was poorly structured with project quizzes usually happening 1-2 weeks after the project was due and quiz questions being generally confusing. But it wasn't that difficult, so it's fine. I don't appreciate the exams being outside of scheduled lecture times.

Def go to all the lectures and do Zybooks. There are weekly projects and a lot of the info is contained within both of those. She's excited about the content and I learned a lot about efficient code. Has a temper so don't make her mad. Don't expect her to round your grade up, despite how close you are to the next grade. I was 0.05% away.

Onsay was an incredible professor. After taking 232 with Nahum the bar was set extremely low, but Onsay was outstanding. She really cares about teaching and providing all the necessary material for us to succeed. Super nice and friendly. Overall great professor. Best in the CSE department. 10/10

Onsay was good. You can tell she cared about students doing well in the course and would always give side notes on what's expected in interviews and in your internships/jobs. The flipped-learning style of this class was not the best and there are far too many lectures with most lectures being insanely long. Overall, a very useful class.

Onsay was one of if not the best professor I have had during my time at MSU. She was passionate about what she taught and made it interesting. She was honest with us and wanted us to succeed. Has experience in the industry and offered very helpful and realistic advice about job searching and technical interviewing in the computer science field.
Overall, amazing prof.

One of the nicest professors I have had, very helpful and knowledgeable. Not a good teacher though, lectures are hard to sit through and lecture slides are 100+ slides long every day making it almost impossible to study them or use them for projects.
Professor Ovenhouse is a fantastic teacher of which its clear he wants to make sure that you actually learn.

One of the best math professors I've had. His lectures are very clear and simple making them not hard to follow along. His office hours were the main reason I got A's on the tests so I highly recommend going to them if you ever need help on the content or just for review before a test. He is always very kind and helpful whenever you talk to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was good at explaining tough concepts. I didn't get the best grade because I missed some lectures towards the end but every time I attended I was able to understand the concepts, very nice guy.
He is really good and the class in really exam heavy but as long as you come to lecture and understand the material the class is light.

Calc 3 is one of the hardest classes I've taken at Michigan State, but the main difference I vastly prefer it over Calc 2 is because of Professor Ovenhouse. His lectures were always super detailed and he always went over good examples, which prepared you really well for homework and exams. 10/10.
He's really nice and approachable, and easy to understand when he lectures. He's super smart but can teach at a understandable level. Also really helpful in office hours.

Nick is a great teacher. He obviously loves his subject and wants his students to do well. He's very organized and will answer any questions you have in a manner that benefits you as a student. He'll go over homework assignments to make sure you can complete them. The only downside is Lab Day - you'll have to work in groups on a large worksheet.
Great overall person, easy to talk to, teaches great, and he has a manly ass beard
Rather disrespectful and not very good with technology, which as an online professor is very concerning. Gives out zeros with one small mistake. Would not recommend.

She is VERY picky when it comes to grading. Post-reading assignments will most likely be the lower grades you get in the class, because if you don't answer the questions in the way she wants, she will dock points. Somewhat recommend? It's not an easy 4.0, but if it fits your schedule, then why not.
Seems like a nice person, but I find the class to be mind-numbing. Expect to learn the material on your own time because the whole class time is taken up reviewing the homework from the day before.
Worst professor I've had at MSU. Do not take any courses with her, I'm taking an online IAH course right now and she is so harsh with grading.
Do not take a class with this professor. She is a tough grader for a class that should be easy. I do not recommend.

DO.NOT.TAKE.HER. Has no clear instructions and its a teach your own class. This is based off of homework and says it is based off completion when it is truly based on correctness.  She says you get three excused absences, but only marks participation as grading, so basically you can not miss a single class. I advise you drop the class if signed up

Very direct and can have an attitude. Classes consist of mostly answering HW questions, which wasn't helpful as little time was left for lecture slides. Grading is REALLY tough and instructions can be unclear. However, HW is a big part of your grade which can cover up a bad exam. Very accessible outside class and helpful feedback.

This professor does not help you learn anything. She instead uses her time to send multiple emails out to students accusing them of using AI. Multiple people have now dropped the course due to fears of them receiving an academic dishonesty report, even if they didn't use AI... Adding to that, her D2L is not set up correctly. Do NOT TAKE HER !!!!!!!

This professor is terrible. Grading is impossible to understand, and there's no guidance on how to do better. I reached out multiple times but never got clear answers. The course materials were confusing, and her explanations only made things harder. It's frustrating to feel stuck with no support or direction.

FIRE HER! Worst professor ever hard grader who never gives helpful feedback. The textbook was useless. She said to ask for help, but her replies were unclear and confusing, leaving me more lost. I'm a native speaker, so it's not a language issue. She just doesn't help students improve or understand.

Carmen grades your essays as if you are already a native speaker, and will accuse you of using google translate with no good reason, to the point where i had to purposely put mistakes in my essay just so she doesn't accuse me for it. The grade boundaries are extremely high, and she will not curve it no matter how bad the class is doing.

I was terrified to take her summer SPN202 course after reading the reviews. Her character is blunt and to the point — I believe this is where majority of the bad reviews are coming from. She is, however, an incredible teacher with effective curricula. Her class was challenging, but was the one I improved in most out of the four SPN classes I took.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A year ago I was reading the reviews thinking "she can't be that bad." I was wrong. She has accused me of using google translate when I did not with no evidence. Does not take criticism but instead makes excuses. I truly dreaded each class not because the coursework was difficult but simply because I didn't want to deal with her attitude. Avoid.

As a native speaker this class was SO hard. They DON'T round. A 4.0 is a 94% so make sure to remember that. You have to do lessons before the class (another prof teaches the content) and they are time consuming but extremely important. Your grade relies on participation (2 pts for every lecture). Be sure to do all work & do well on tests/exams.

Profe Carmen was my favorite professor this semester. She is funny and caring. Participation in class is big for your grade so try not to miss classes. But she helps make sure everyone participates. SPN 310 has a pretty big workload since lectures, homework, and quizzes are all outside of class, but she helps clear things up in class.

Carmen was scary at first because of her high expectations and advanced language use in class. LOTS of hw but is the same for all SPN 310 classes and participation in class is required for a grade. She comes off strong but is very willing to help after class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She really cares that every student is on the same page & is very approachable if you need any help. I was always excited to go to her class because she's very funny. She fosters a great environment in class as she's always making jokes in class. She gets to know each of her students and it's clear she puts time into her lectures. Take her class!

Very brute and unapproachable, if you dont do things her way (even if they contradict the syllabus) you wont succeed in her class. She hones in on struggling students and made several cry and made some even abandon the language/minor all together. So bad with technology and communication

Overall, she is a nice lady. She responded to my emails very quickly and you can tell she is passionate about what she teaches. My only complaint is that the grading criteria/syllabus was not very clear at the beginning of this semester (new to the course), but got better as we progressed. She is also not flexible with late assignments at all.

Professor Octavio was pretty good. She is from Spain so she has a Spanish accent. She also hates technology with a burning passion. I took SPN 310 with her. None of the professors for that course give very clear feedback, and you do all the lectures by yourself. The textbook was pretty much useless except for when it was required for homework.

I had her for 201and 202 a year apart; her teaching improved (clearly as she's taken on more classes since). When you have a good group for class she is very entertaining and always joking with students. She really cares that her students are understanding and adjusts her teaching methods accordingly. Her classes are hard but appropriately so.

incredibly rude to all students in class and even picked on a specific person in my section, poor explanations of core concepts and would often not answer questions asked. heavy homework load that doesn't really benefit you in class. mandatory attendance, tough grader in class on both oral and written assignments. just take my word for it and avoid

She is amazing. I've had 2 SPN classes with her. She really cares about whether or not students are learning from her and her teaching methods. I've had private conversations with her and she cares for her student's well-being and success so much. She is so accommodating to personal issues. I would strongly recommend her as a professor.

Profesora Octavio is short-tempered, unreasonable, and difficult to work with. Directions and criteria for assignments are often unclear. She is not tech savvy, she becomes very upset when students make technology related mistakes or have poor connection, but then expects grace when she does the same. Do yourself a favor and avoid her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Octavio requires you to spend a minimum of 70$ on books/conversations if you want to pass. She assigns an abundance of online work/TalkAbroad transcriptions that you are unable to receive any credit for if submitted late, no matter the reason. Attendance is mandatory due to in class activities everyday that receive a 0 if not present
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was one of the best professors I've had since coming to MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: SPN330 is okay, but Octavio is the worst professor I have had. She is condescending, short-tempered, and has no patience when answering valid student questions. You might feel bad for not already knowing it all. She asks for our understanding with her life and technical difficulties but is unwilling to accommodate or be flexible with her students.

In all four years of undergrad, Octavio was by far my least favorite professor. She grades so tough if it were up to her she would fail almost everybody. She also picks on struggling students and makes it impossible to want or receive her help. She even made a student cry once. I'd pick a new language before I'd pick her class.

Worst professor I ever had. Her classroom felt toxic and unsafe, everyday I could sense that everyone else was uncomfortable too. She would snap at students for no reason, name call, use profanity. Her excuse for this behavior is that people in Spain are blunt and that Americans want to be coddled. No, we just want to feel safe and respected.

Do not take this prof if you can avoid it. She is often unclear about directions or expectations, and students are too afraid to ask her to clarify because she's rude when people don't understand. She also doesn't help students when they're struggling with what they're trying to say and instead ridicules them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not, I mean never ever ever ever ever take her section of SPN. She is horrible, she is condescending and creates a toxic learning environment. She wants heavy participation but does not offer help to students that are struggling with phrasing sentences. Worst professor I have had in my three year of university.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super smart guy and you can tell. Knows everything about what he talks about. Lecture heavy so its lowkey hard to keep up with all the info. Not too much work. Literally failed the first two out of three quizzes and I'm still somehow in the game. Had a early class but would show up every day because I loved the professor.

Super easy class & 4.0. A bunch of assignments, but he pretty much grades them for completion, & they take like 5-10 minutes to do. Daily in-class activities that are usually 1-3 questions & completion points - just look at the slides for them, you don't have to show up. And 3 in-class quizzes, 10-points each that don't affect your grade much.
The TAs teach the course. I've never even met the main professor. If you get a good TA, then you will get a good grade. Luckily, mine was amazing!
Very chill, easy 4.0.
rg34g45g34g435g
Very nice and kind, easy class, very involved and passionate about content.

Such a nice professor!!! You also can tell how much he loves teaching this. Made class interesting enough for people who don't like science. Group projects that weren't awful although some days were more boring than others. Mandatory attendance but he usually lets us go early.
Lectures are tough to sit through but I was able to do other homework. Prelab and postlab due before every class which are easy. I think the class in general is boring but overall easy.

Professor is really passionate about rivers and you can tell based off of the lectures. This was a pretty simple course and I would recommend to anyone who needs the ISP credit. The exams were online and there was weekly homework that wasn't too bad!

In class assignments you can do from home, lectures are SO hard to sit through. three exams that were all taken online outside of class, not proctored. I would recommend to others for integrative studies requirement. very easy coursework that takes less than 10 mins. not a lot of homework at all
Homework is extremely light and take about 10 minutes to complete. Exams are a bit weird and lectures are average. Still an amazing professor who cares about his students and the material he teaches

Lectures were boring as I'm not passionate about the environment, but Ozzy is a caring professor and an interesting person. Attendance is based on short questions you have to turn in online after class, and exams were online for the winter/spring '25 semester. He understands outside circumstances and will be lenient as long as you have reason.
His lecture is great. Homework and class assignments aren't too hard. There are three exams.

Very little workload, and he tried his best to make lectures more interesting. There is an in-class assignment due at the end of each class, but they were super easy. The quizzes (4), coursework (10) and homework (4) were all easy and took less than 30 minutes to complete. Easy grader, just a long lecture to get through. Everything is open note.

This class was easy and the only required work was occasionally homework and In Class Activities for attendance (but those can be done outside of class during the class period). Prof. Hernandez was nice, but canceled class a few times. No tests or finals, only open note quizzes.

This was a super chill class, he canceled lectures a lot so check your email before heading to class. There wasn't a lot of homework or assignments that went along with the class. Overall, super easy ISP credit and Osvaldo is a great guy.

Ozzy was a cool professor ti have this semester. Although he did cancel a lot, the assignments and tests were not that difficult and was easy to complete. ULA was also very accessible when needed. Recommend taking this class as it is very interesting, you just have to like lectures as it is very lecture heavy material.

I loved Ozzy last year when I had him for 203A but in a lab setting he's kinda tough. Like all labs, attendance is mandatory which is expected. One thing I hated is he would keep us in lab even when we didn't need to stay the whole time. 2 assignments due at the start of every lab, pre and post lab. Boring and one huge final project at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: very easy credit for isp. hernandez is a very interesting person but unfortunately his lectures are boring. attendance is technically mandatory because of daily assignments you have to turn in, but you totally can turn them in online without stepping foot in the lecture hall.

He is an easy professor for an ISP requirement. He does have easy homework once a week and four easy online quizzes. He uses an in-class activity for attendance (but can drop 3), posts lecture slides, and cares about his students.
Light work

He is a great professor and thoroughly explains topics. Uses picture-heavy slides and counts participation through in-class assignments that can easily be done outside of class but are due at the end of class. Overall, homework and coursework are easy (look at a graph and interpret or watch a documentary), as are tests which are online open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did not appreciate how many days he took off along with how he announced quizzes. He would hardly announce them and made the final due at a different time than the rest of the quizzes. I went to his class more times than I can count, and he didn't have class. he also didn't respond to emails. Other than his miscommunication, he was nice.

The class was canceled a lot, which made it hard to do some of the quizzes. Quizzes are not worth a lot, HW is easy but, with documentaries, and Coursework is easy. In-class assignments can be done outside of class and lectures are long. I did learn a lot about water and climate change that has stuck with me!

class was cancelled often due to personal reasons but the work he would assign (if any) was always easy. attendance is taken through in-class activities and 6 are dropped at the end of the semester. lectures get boring, but if you show up some of the information gets through and the exams are 15-question quizzes on d2l
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Hernandez is a nice person, but his execution of teaching kind of fell flat. He canceled class a lot, meaning we had less time to learn things that he would still keep on the quizzes. The courseworks are easy, but the homeworks often require watching lengthy videos. I don't think attendance is mandatory, just go through the lecture slides.

He's a great guy who is very passionate about what he teaches. He cancelled class a number of times, and the class has a low work load with relatively easy quizzes and coursework each week. No exams. Only bad thing is lectures can get boring sometimes.
Great professor and an easy grader. Not many assignments to complete and no exams, only a few at home quizzes throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All around great professor. Grade is mainly based on very short homework assignments and in class activities. Classes can get boring at times but that is heavily due to the content and not his teaching. Class was cancelled a lot but that was due to personal reasons, and he still made sure everything we needed was accessible online. Easy 4.0.

Professor Hernandez was great this semester. He canceled class a lot due to personal reasons but he always provided lecture videos or homework assignments in place of the canceled classes. There are very few quizzes or tests in this class; your grade consists mostly of homework and in class activities. Both of these were very easy to complete.

He was a great professor and he was very understanding for our course. The only thing that people probably don't like is that he dos in class activities which you have to be in class to get credit for. But don't let that discourage you from taking him because he is a great professor.

His lectures were very boring and hard to understand at times, as he did not thoroughly explain the material. He also cancelled class several times throughout the semester; however, he did give freebies. The material in the lectures, were not always what is covered in the quizzes. Be sure to complete all assignments so quiz scores wont affect grade

Really chill professor. You can tell he loves what he teaches. He had us do in-class, paper assignments every day. He also frequently canceled lecture. Even with taking a previous environmental science class, still recommend paying attention in lecture, a lot of what he says will be mentioned on the quizzes.

Not only was Professor Os super sweet and funny, but his class was also super easy. You really don't need to take notes, you just have to do the simple in-class activities every lecture. The majority of this course is super interesting and inspiring. He is super passionate and he is flexible if you just communicate with him.

One of the best classes for your ISP requirement. Overall an easy 4.0. Attendance matters but lecture slides are always posted so at least missing class wouldn't put you behind for tests or assignments. HW was weekly, but easy and not time consuming. Few tests which were all online, and no midterm or final, which made the class a lot less stressful

He was okay! Very easy going professor the only thing that would that annoyed me was the fact that he didn't answer his emails and get in real contact with him I had to stay after class and literally chase him down. He was specific on attendance. Had him during the winter semester and even when we had a really bad snowstorm he didn't cancel.

Prof. Hernandez is a super easy grader and gives out a few assignments. You have to do a short in-class activity and then 5 homework assignments and 5 quizzes for the whole semester. Definitely would recommend to fulfill your ISP requirement.

Professor H is a gem. We only had 5 homework assignments and 5 quizzes the whole semester and they were all easy. Nicest guy you will ever meet, cancelled lecture a few times. Super cool guy, almost threw us a zoom pizza party.

Dr. H is such a cool prof! Although he is a tad disorganized, it doesn't take away from his passion for teaching. The class covers very basic high school-level earth science, and he makes even that interesting to learn about. He also applies the concepts to environmental issues in our society, making the course material be helpful in the long run.

Prof. Hernandez is clearly passionate about what he teaches, but I did not find the material or the way in which he presented it to be accessible. Gave in-class coursework and the slides are not much help to look at without showing up to lecture, so go up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Hernandez is a difficult prof to deal with. Does not make accommodations for legitimate reasons and is extremely difficult to get in touch with. Says attendance isn't mandatory but as 20% of your grade is in-class assignments (that he won't allow make ups) your grade will suffer. His tests are very difficult and study guides unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hernandez is very passionate about this class and makes learning about bugs and the environment fun for people who may not have any interest in it. Attendance isn't necessarily mandatory, but most class points are based on the labs we do in class. He makes it very easy to be successful in this class and he's also super funny!!
Awesome, caring guy that truly gives students all the resources they need to do well in his courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I had a great pleasure taking an online course with Mr. Hernandez! The course was very organized and if I did have any questions, would get back to me the same day!! Awesome instructor and would advise to take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is passionate about the subjects he covers in class, but his slides are extremely confusing, so you have to go to class and pay attention because there is almost never actual writing on them, just diagrams and graphs. He is a nice guy, but I have never struggled this much in a university requirement. Extremely hard and brought my GPA down a lot.

You think that you understand the material, you study the study guides he gives you, then you get the exam and are mind blown because it is nothing like you expected! Super hard exams that is for sure. Really boring lectures, too. Randomly gives in class work for credit so you should definitely go to lecture.
lectures are really easy, posts slides online, attendance not mandatory but sometimes there is in-class activities that we hand in, exams are really easy
He was a cool professor. The lectures could get kind of long and boring, but he was passionate about it which helped. His exams were kind of hard, but he always curved them.

He's really a cool dude. If you show up and pay attention you'll not only pass the class but learn a ton about the course. This class provides some real analysis of the real problems we face and he does a great job at addressing them.

Hernandez is a great lecturer who is really knowledgable about the topic and very passionate about what he teaches.  He gives difficult tests but if you thoroughly prepare you shouldn't have a problem- just make sure you remember specifics and be aware that he likes to trick people on exams.  If you want an easy class take someone else, though!

Prof. Hernandez is a nice guy and he's enthusiastic enough about material, but his tests are pretty challenging. That being said, he provides study guides for them, so it's up to you to prepare yourself. Also, during most lectures he has you turn in something to give participation points, so attend lecture! No textbook, which is a plus!

There's no textbook; all the power points were online. With that said, you still had to drag yourself to class and listen to his hour and a half lecture because about 2/3s of the time he'll have an in class assignment (basically attendance points). The material itself isn't hard, just a boring class to go to and felt like it wasted a lot of time.
Was helpful and really wants student participation. Puts PowerPoints online but goes through them too fast in class.

Good professor and interesting course. There was no textbook because the class was new, readings posted online. Good about questions but very limited office hours, go to TA for help on assignments. Attendance is checked by turning in answers to questions from lecture, so make sure you show up because it's random.

took her for M&A class, she is amazing.

My jaw dropped to the ground when I saw his rating above a 0! At this point, I should have just gone to a community college like him. Why did MSU make the mistake of hiring him? They must have listened with no ears. Why screw students over? Why make them suffer to the point they had to make an appointment through MSU CAPS?

I mean I don't even know why this class is a requirement for my major if someone like Spranger is the only option for this GOD AWFUL CLASS. I wasted my time going over the content that Helen wrote and made a bunch of mistakes on. The class was unbearably long I started to question who I was as an individual in the pre-med field. PLS HIRE A NEW PROF

NEWSFLASH SPRANGER!!! SOME PEOPLE HAVE LIVES OUTSIDE OF YOUR PHYSIO CLASS!!!! Stop giving us stupid connects. Honestly stop teaching please. Just do everyone including yourself a favor and give up on teaching you are not good at it and it's time to accept that.

This class was a storm no one asked to survive, A place where hope goes to die while deadlines thrive.
The “teaching” felt hollow, like words tossed in air. Explanations so empty it was almost unfair. Only people with no life could keep up with this strain. We traded our weekends, our sleep, and our peace, Yet somehow the chaos refused to decrease.

This class left me drained and questioning why a course this consistently demoralizing hasn't been redesigned or reassigned. I don't understand how students are still expected to go through this experience with no alternative instructor. The teaching approach felt cold, unsupportive, and discouraging at every step. IMPOSSIBLE TO SUCCEED.

Honestly just a horrible human and an even worse professor. How can someone keep a job with such a horrible personality and ability to teach. He makes MSU look like a joke. We should donate him back to Wayne State.

This class made me dread opening my books and seriously question whether I should stay at this school. No matter how hard I worked, it felt like nothing was enough. The professor's attitude was cold, unhelpful, and exhausting, creating one of the most demoralizing academic experiences I've ever had. I cannot believe he has not gotten fired yet.

I went to every office hour, every TA session, and spent entire weekends studying, yet this class still wrecked my GPA. The level of difficulty felt unreasonable, and despite constant effort, I'm now forced to retake it. This course was exhausting and deeply discouraging. I dont understand why a professor likes to see us fail???????????????

This class was so overwhelming that if I ever had to retake it, I'd honestly rather drop out or change my major. The workload and stress were unreal, and it drained every bit of enjoyment I had for the subject. Easily the most discouraging class I've taken.

This course was brutally unrealistic. Unless you're naturally gifted, it feels impossible to succeed. I poured in endless hours for minimal payoff. The workload was excessive, the expectations unreasonable, and the class left me stressed, defeated, and questioning why it was designed this way.

Taking this class means giving up your life outside school. You can't have a job, hobbies, or free time, and the workload will drain you to the point of feeling depressed. It took over my entire semester and left me exhausted. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.

The workload was overwhelming, expectations felt unrealistic, and the constant stress took a serious toll on my mental health and performance in other classes. If you care about your mental health or maintaining any kind of balance in your life, I would not recommend taking him. This class made my entire semester miserable.

I am genuinely surprised this man still has a job.I heard nothing but horror stories going into this class and every single one was true.He covers so much material in one sitting and is so rude when students ask a question and look confused still once he has answered.He preaches how with hard work you will get good grades.WRONG!His class proves it.

Honestly, Spranger does a great job teaching. It is nearly impossible to get through the physiology of the entire human body in 1 semester, but he does it. He gives out extra credit, but this class honestly just takes A TON of work outside. Take this on an easy courseload or you won't succeed. Offers an INSANE amount of help rooms though.

I wanted to like Spranger. He does have many office hours and review sessions. He says he wants you to do well. This all means nothing. He expects a disgusting amount of work to be done. I should not have to re-listen to his entire lecture after just getting out of the 2 hour class that I just listened too.

The professor makes people feel scared and uncomfortable. He has a passion for the content, but not for his students. I think I would have enjoyed this class with a different professor teaching it. Very disappointed to say the least.

Ironic that a course so fundamental to pre-health careers is taught by someone so fundamentally disconnected from effective teaching. Interesting content ruined by a terrible professor. Do better, Matry...and don't email students asking for good reviews again, it's inappropriate and will not save the poor reputation you created.

Disgusted by his arrogance, dismissiveness, lack of empathy, & world outlook. Class is unbearable as he disregards students' struggles & other responsibilities & creates an uncomfortable & discouraging environment. Pre-health students deserve an instructor who respects and cares for them. Do not expect support during unpredictable emergencies :)

Literally so egotistical. Maybe not ask people to write reviews for you. Average of 600 students is like 67% then blames students when it's his fault. Mabe make your class where students actually want to learn. Also understand we have other classes on top of yours!!!!!!!

reviews.comment: I went into this class scared based on the reviews on here. I do think the exams are fair and could only blame myself If I didn't study enough. He offers a lot of extra credit, which I assume is due to the 68% exam average. Overall, he's not terrible but can be egotistical. Just go in wanting to learn and dedicate lotss of time and you'll be fine.

On the first day, he talked about how he had to work hard and isn't naturally smart which I really resonated with. Disappointed how empathy lacking and egotistical this professor ended up being. Doesn't respect RCPD accommodations (which literally isn't allowed) and singles students out in a 300 ppl lecture Content is clinical and interesting tho.

Ok, so realistically the amount of 5 star reviews here are skewed because he allegedly told a bunch of student to give him a good review, but he's also not a 1 quality and 5 difficulty either. I took the class 3 years ago, and I'm here to give an accurate review and say he actually is a solid teacher, but the class is extraordinarily difficult.

Do not take this class if you are taking a lot of classes. This class would be perfectly reasonable if you took it by itself, but when mixed with other challenging courses, it is hard to find a balance as this class required almost all of your free time.
so much work and so much content
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is truly a great professor. I'm not even doing that well in the class, but it is all fault of my own. He posts the video lectures online, answers questions, and offers many modes of support: study skills sessions, office hours, and content review sessions. There is a lot of content and tricky material, but his exams are very straightforward.

Marty is a very passionate professor and really cares about his students success. Most of the people on here are just mad because they didn't study and blame him for it. Is his class hard? Yes, but that is what you can expect for a pre-med class. He is trying to teach the next generation of healthcare workers!

His lectures are 2 hours full of content-heavy material, fancy vocab, and a 5 min break if you're lucky. The wording for his exams is tricky and the average score is usually around 60%. He has a lot of help room hours and gives free extra credit, but overall it is just an unreasonable "intro class" to take as a full time student.

It is a very difficult class on two parts: your own sacrifice to learn the material and the undertones of animosity behind the professor. The course is very detailed and review is extremely necessary to pass the class and if you're not willing to do that, you shouldn't be taking it. It has however helped me prepare for future classes.

So much energy and enthusiasm in lecture about wanting his students to learn. His class is hard and takes a time commitment, but if you're trying to pursue medicine, his class is key. It taught me about 15-20% of the content on the MCAT and he helped me achieve my best score on the bio section. I couldn't have asked for a better prof!!
Unaccommodating and egotistical. Blames students when 65% avg

reviews.comment: I took this class twice and both times was baffled by how disconnected the exams were from the rest of the content. Professor was rude and condescending, his ego needs to be put in check. Class would have been enjoyable if taught by someone who doesn't need to ask students to write them positive reviews. Don't take it unless you absolutely have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The material and lectures in Spranger's course provided a strong foundation in physiology, needed in any medical field. In Spranger's lectures he was engaged with the content as well as students, all while finishing lecture on time or early. Outside of class were many helpful resources including content review and note taking review sessions.

Professor Spranger is one of the most passionate and supportive instructors I've had. His class is tough but incredibly rewarding. If you put in the effort and use the resources he provides, you'll not only succeed, you'll leave truly prepared for your future. He genuinely cares and goes above and beyond for his students.

Professor was not any more accessible than any other professor but touted the fact he had open times to meet. Class was bearable when studying with people and the TAs helped a lot. I would not take this class if you do not need it for requirements, as I ended up studying physiology more on my own for the MCAT making this course a waste of money

This professor often created an uncomfortable environment with his rude and condescending behavior and with this insensitive comments toward others.

reviews.comment: This professor does not care for you outside of the classroom. He has an unmeasurable ego and he is not that caring. He often created a hostile environment in the classroom.

I have learned and remembered the most information in this class in comparison to any other course I have taken. However, you have to be ready to schedule out a LOT of time for this course. It takes time and energy, but is very rewarding. The content was very interesting.

honestly the course isn't the worst ive taken at msu. a lot of it does require more work than the regular class. although, I agree that its a bit shameful to write your own reviews to increase ratings. take the class though if you need for prehealth since it helps a lot. but expect to put in about 3-4 hours a day to review it

reviews.comment: Look, Professor Spranger's class is tough and you'll EARN that grade, but it's worth it. The material sticks with you and helps in future courses. And no, he doesn't write his own reviews—he's just that good. Take it seriously and you'll grow from it. (PS: Go to SSHS!)

He makes use of this website to boost himself. He sent an email out questioning why he did not receive any direct words of appreciation for giving out some points. Real work of a course load, averages of any exam do not pass 70% at most. I'd suggest taking this at a community college or elsewhere for your own sake.

This class is not easy. But with that being said, I have never learned more for a course at MSU. Professor Spranger was a very interactive and caring professor. He wants us to do well. He holds review sessions and study skills sessions that are alot of help. Work hard, its rewarding. This material will be beneficial as a pre-health major.

Made me feel uneasy. Lots of ramblings and rants about the disgruntles with other classmates of mine. I personally do not have an issue, but it makes me question the academic integrity of the course. Otherwise, I found the class to be okay if you have some background in anatomy.
Yeah this is very skewed. He sent an email to all students to give him a rating and mass reports negative reviews.

Look, his class is very challenging and you will have to WORK for that 4.0, but the information I learned in the class has really helped me with future health courses. I recommend taking his class with a lighter course load so you can dedicate the true time needed, but study hard and shoot high, the info you learn is very valuable (PS: Go to SSHS!)

He explains tough concepts by using real world examples that makes it easier to understand. If you don't pay attention in his class it is very easy to get lost and behind but he has scheduled study groups where you can go to try and catch back up or understand a concept better.

theres some form of discrepancy occurring behind the scenes. i wont be surprised if the ombuds get involved soon and discover something. just know the professor has his favorites, and puts down the others that aren't. thanks for making physiology unenjoyable!

Take this class. It is lecture heavy and there is a ton of information: follow the study skills. You can tell he truly cares about not only the subject matter but all 600 students in lecture.

This class is a lot, but the way I saw it was an introduction to what as a pre-health professional I will be learning in just a few years. He gives all the resources needed to succeed in this class, and he makes the lectures interesting. Study hard (and smart) and you will be rewarded. Best class I've taken at MSU.( P.S. go to SSHS u wont regret)

It's a 600 person class and you can't give everyone an A. Dr. Spranger cares about his students and gives you resources to do well. I could've gotten a better grade if I showed up to his review sessions. People that give bad reviews are unfortunately part of the crowd that believes their performance in a class relies entirely on their professor.

Dr.Spranger is very big on all students being able to be successful in his class and I would agree that that is true-- everything is there for you to get that 4.0 but rest assured that you'll have to work VERY hard for it. I highly recommend taking his course bc its very comprehensive and highly beneficial if you're pursuing anything pre-health.

Dr. Spranger teaches challenging courses, but is extremely passionate about the physiology that he teaches. He is a great mentor for those pursuing careers in medicine. Dr. Spranger teaches all students how to study efficiently and truly understand material. He has high expectations and wants the best for his students. I would highly recommend.

PSL310 was my most difficult class, but Spranger did well to prepare us. His study strategy involves rewatching lecture videos, writing your own notes out, and doing the AQs at the end, and it worked great. This class is manageable if you put in the work. Overall Spranger taught us well for this class and future classes as well.

PSL 310 is an amazing course that remains one of my favorites. There's a lot of content but w/ enough effort & (if needed) the use of the numerous help sessions that run throughout the semester, it's an easy A. Spranger's passion for physiology + the interesting information present in each lecture make the course enjoyable & fun to learn.
Just overall a terrible professor… didn't care if we actually learned but more of if HE thought us something …

One of the best professors I've had at MSU! PSL 310 is challenging, but he truly wants his students to succeed. He teaches you the material AND how to study effectively. Highly recommend!
botted his reviews, just know his lectures line up somewhat with the assignments given out; but the exams have little to no correlation. pretty condescending as a professor as well, but oh well

Dr. Spranger was the best instructor I've had the pleasure of learning from during my four years at MSU. I remember more from this course than any other

The hardest class I've taken but I enjoyed the course. You'll need to attend lecture + rewatch lecture videos + do AQs. Anything covered in lecture is testable! Expect to study ~10hrs a week but the professor is easily accesible and office hours are very informative. Easy to comprehend lectures but extremely dense in content. Gives plenty resources

Pretty sure Spranger wrote most of these, the wording and sentence structure are almost identical to his emails. Anyways, the class itself is great, but the instructor is awful. Marty, I hope you don't get that promotion

reviews.comment:
By nature, PSL 310 is very content heavy, but I found Dr. Spranger's lectures to be informative, clear, and engaging. Also, the exams were exclusively based on content covered in lecture. 
I put a lot into this class, and I know the study habits I built and the information I learned will serve me in my future studies. MSU is lucky to have Spranger!

PSL 310 is a difficult class, but if you put the time and effort in, you can succeed. The class is lecture heavy and requires plenty of time, but that is something disclosed to you on day one. Dr. Spranger is a great professor and is always looking to help his students succeed!

Look. You either love Spranger or don't. I personally think he's a good guy but his style of teaching is to be desired. Hour 50 lectures, tests are entirely based on that. Don't take any other hard courses while taking PSL310. Definitely need that study time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: PSL 310 is very lecture heavy and you have to spend a lot of time outside of class re-watching the lecture. Professor Spranger does an amazing job of explaining information and will often say what is or isn't on the exam. If your taking this class, your looking to do something in the medical field and this course prepares you very well.

Dr. Spranger genuinely cares about his students. He not only helped me succeed in the class, but also helped me find direction in my academic and professional goals. An amazing professor, mentor, and human being—MSU is lucky to have him!

He's rigorous and holds students to a high standard, which pushed me to grow. When I was confused, he explained concepts clearly and patiently. I loved his class so much that I sat in on future lectures just to learn from him again. MSU is lucky to have a professor like him.

if ur reading these 5 star rating, he sent out an email begging students to submit those and he writes his own reviews. 
Hi Marty, do better than begging for a good review.

Dr. Spranger is the best professor I've had at MSU. I was a chemistry major who felt disconnected from my studies, but his class changed everything. I enjoyed it so much I switched my major to Physiology. His energy, clarity, and passion made two-hour lectures feel like 20 minutes.

Dr. Spranger is able to make lectures extremely engaging with connections to almost every healthcare field (dentistry, pharmacy, medical, nursing, physician assistant...). He is engaged in the material and rather than reading off slides, he lectures his own experiences and thoughts. His slides are not word-heavy so you can sit back and listen.

The content itself is pretty complicated, however, Professor Spranger gives you all of the tools and resources that you may need in order to do well in the class. Tools, resources, and study methods I intend to apply to many of my other classes. This class, specifically the professor and his style, made me a better student.

Many may think Spranger's class was very hard, and don't get me wrong, physiology is a heavy course. But the way Spranger designs the course not only prepares you to do well in the exams, but in the rest of your pre-health classes. His study skills are very clear and effective, and if you follow them, you will do well in the course.

Dr. Spranger is an amazing professor.  He appreciates hard work, what you put in is what you will get out. Use his study skills... I can confidently say those are what got me through the rest of my degree at msu. Still to this day, I am in graduate school and use those same skills. So glad I got to learn from him.

Professor Spranger is very passionate about physiology. He is great at explaining complex topics. He goes the extra mile for his students and tries his best to make sure anyone who wishes to excel in his class is able to.

I had Dr. Spranger in Fall 2021, and he is one of the best professors I've ever had. Is the material tough, yes, but he is an effective teacher and I still remember the material taught today. This helped me immensely with my MCAT prep. In addition, Dr. Spranger is a joy to speak with outside of class and is interested in your success.
One of my favorite professors and courses I took at MSU!

I took PSL310 with Spranger my Junior year at MSU and reflecting back after graduating I can confidently say it was the most enjoyable, beneficial, and interesting courses I ever took in all of undergrad.This class is HUGE for preparing you for the bio/biochem portion of the MCAT, carriers over into key higher level course content. I love Spranger!

Spranger is an AMAZING professor. His love for physiology is apparent, and he genuinely wants his students to succeed. The course itself has plenty of opportunities for students to receive help outside classroom time, including his personal help room hours. I recommend this class to everyone, it has been my favorite class throughout college.

Professor Spranger genuinely wants his students to succeed. He's always available, takes time to explain things clearly, and makes learning feel meaningful. If you're willing to put in the work, he'll go above and beyond to help you understand and do well.

This class is one of those that you get out what you put into it. Spranger might come off as 'scary', but he is one of the most inspiring professors that wants you to actually learn. You will not do well in this class if you simply just memorize facts for the exam. Spranger is a down to earth professor that wants to see students succeed.

Spranger provides more student support than ANY other professor I had at MSU. He offers extensive office hours, study skill reviews, content review sessions, and a complete guide on how to study for the course. At first he will seem intimidating, but speak to him and you will quickly see that he cares about every student's individual success.

reviews.comment: Spranger is an amazing professor and it is very evident he cares about his students and their future. This class can be difficult due to the content, but Spranger offers many study sessions that are very helpful if you are struggling. As long as you stay on top of studying and take advantage of the resources he provides you can do very well.
Professor Spranger genuinely cares about his students success and offers all the resources one could need to succeed in the classroom.

Dr. Spranger is an amazing professor! He truly cares about his students. He takes the time to support and connect with everyone in his class. His lectures are always engaging and very interesting. Overall, he makes learning both enjoyable and meaningful.

Dr. Spranger showed little concern for students beyond academics and often came across as arrogant and dismissive. He frequently called out students in ways that felt unnecessary and uncomfortable, creating a tense learning environment that made it hard to stay engaged.

Spranger was a great teacher! Yes it is true, his exams are hard, but you know what else is hard? College, life, life after college. His course was one of the few that I appreciated how much knowledge I gained after walking out of lecture. 

Overall, his course prepared me more more medical school and the MCATs than any other offered at MSU.

Does a great job of explaining topics, providing effective ways to remember complex psychological systems. Exam questions are specific, but he does a great job of preparing you for the type of questions, content, and emphasizes active recall (useful for further studies). Lectures are content-heavy, but he does a great job of keeping you engaged.

reviews.comment: Yes, this class can be hard. But Spranger makes it less of a “have to” and more of a “get to”. He cares so much about his student's forward progress and provides so many opportunities for them to succeed. While the lectures are long and intensive, he breaks them up with fun anecdotes that do help with the length and extra credit opportunities.
I hope you get that promotion!!

The class is hard because the content is inherently hard. Studying consistently and managing your time is key to doing well. Even if you don't align with his personality, it is clear to see that Spranger cares about the success of his students. He offers resources online and in-person that will help you succeed if you take advantage of them.

Professor Spranger is one of the most down to earth professors at Michigan State University. At first he can seem strict or unapproachable. After meeting him during office hours he is the most caring and personable person around. He truly cares about education of his students. I encourage every student to meet with him when taking his course.

He has 600 students every semester, he won't remember who you are or what you did. Use that to your advantage! Remind him of your improvements and he'll see your dedication. Don't tell him how bad you did on a test, tell him how much better you did compared to the last! He cares more to see you working hard, not just being a perfect student

This class is hard, probably the hardest class I've ever taken. However, it contains good info for aspiring medical professionals. Dr. Spranger is tough but he outlines everything you need in order to do well in his class. He provides lots of out of lecture opportunities for extra help and extra credit and truly wants his students to do well.

Reach out to him if you're struggling, he will make time to meet with you. Yes it's an incredibly hard class, but you will do great if you lock in from the start and do his study skills! I have ADHD and have always struggled with school, and I'm so shocked with how well I did even if it wasn't a 4.0. Pay attention, ask questions, and good luck!

Professor Spranger genuinely cares about student success. The class is tough but absolutely worth it. His study strategies work, and the skills I gained helped shape my academic journey and future success. If you're willing to put in the effort, this class will leave a lasting impact.

Dr. Spranger is a good professor and this course is very interesting. The content can be challenging, but the professor outlines all the strategies needed to succeed, rewatch lectures and do the application questions! Exams are very fair. Overall, it is a really great class and you will learn so much.

This is a tough class made for students who want medical careers, so I feel that's a given. Although the material can be a lot to digest at times, Spranger was always willing to help if you put the effort in. He offered ~20 points of extra credit throughout the semester, and was willing to work around students' schedules to meet and review content.

Professor Spranger taught through a lecture-exam format and showed genuine interest in teaching. While the content was clearly taught, and high grades are achievable, expect a very significant investment in time to effectively recall the accelerated material. Spranger offered many helpful resources, such as his office hours or peer-led tutoring.

Expectations, resources, and helpful study skills are clearly outlined on the first day of class. While the content seems challenging to learn initially, the grade you get is proportional to the time and effort you invest in mastering it. The class material was helpful as a foundation for later undergrad classes and even graduate level education.

As a current PA student and prior PSL 310 student, it's a great class to help get you prepared with foundational knowledge!
This class was never easy, but it was always fair. If you work hard and study efficiently, you will do well! Reach out to Spranger if you're struggling, he's tough but caring and very willing to help!

The content covered in this course provided me with so much beneficial knowledge academically and professionally. I recently took my MCAT and I barely had to study extra biology material because of this class. Aside from the content itself though, Professor Spranger did a great job with bringing enthusiasm to his lectures and supporting students.

By far the best professor I have had in my three years. Dr. Spranger is passionate incomparable to any other professor I have had. His lectures are amazing, but definitely require you to rewatch outside of class as the slides are content heavy. Dr. Spranger has an amazing sense of humor which made going to lecture exciting. 10/10 class, I loved it.

Prof Spranger and his TAs go above and beyond to help students succeed. Attend the study skills and follow the guide he gives you, you can earn 4.0

I'm incredibly grateful I took this class and put in the effort to do it right. I got the outcome I had hoped for, and it was worth it.

Put in the work, and this class will give it back to you tenfold
