reviews.comment: Okay, I have a lot of things to say, but to keep it short and sweet, all I can say is that if you don't have enough time on your hands, DO NOT take his section. He knows what he'/ talking about and is passionate, but there's a lot of work to put in and a lot of information he covers. And it was hard to balance this with my other activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is a lot to take on if you don't know what you're getting into. I left this class understanding physiology very well but had very little time to even breathe all semester. You have to want to learn the material or else you'll just drown. It's a ton of work but anything you'll be tested on is in the lecture (which he records).

Insanely tough prof. My semester was already hard, so this class on top of it all made it impossible to pass. Test averages were extremely low (50-60%). If you wanna do good, be prepared to study 3-5 hrs every night (which nobody has time for). Nice guy with low BS tolerance but avoid him. You WILL fail if your life isn't dedicated to the class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Marty whata guy; he once bought the whole class brownies. Really likes to hear himself talk (be prepared to spend the whole hour in office hours) but has really interesting things to say. REALLY hard exams but he curved all of our exams& gave a lot of extra credit. Take immaculate notes &you'll be fine. Offers lots of ways for students to succeed.

Although he is a decent professor and very passionate about this class, the class is very tough. He purposely makes his exams extremely hard because he wants you to learn the material that he briefly covers in class in great depth. Also he expects you to do 8 hours of homework or studying per lecture which is not even possible to accomplish.

Honestly I don't know why he has such bad reviews. This class is not impossible. I study the night before each exam and I am going to most likely 3.5 or 4.0. I put in minimal work this semester. Marty is a GREAT professor, one of the best I have had. You can tell he really loves what he is talking about and it's scary how smart he is.

He's very smart and I love listening to his lectures because I have learned so much. It's just hard to juggle everything because his exams are tough. He tries to help though and posts the lectures and recordings online. He's a cool guy, it's just a lot of info all at once. I'm glad I got to take the class still.

Easily one of the worst classes I have ever taken. I came into the class the first day and he seemed like a cool professor, turns out he was terrible. He makes the tests almost impossible to pass, and in class he just reads the powerpoint without explaining the concepts. Would never take one of his classes ever again.

Terrible. hardest class you will take, not due to the material but due to his goal to fail his students. HE stated he was happy w/ the performance of our class after a 58% class average. The man designs the exams for you to fail, he admits he puts little thought into his tests which is why only he would be able to answer the question correctly.

I love biology so I thought this class would be easy. I was wrong. I was taking 3 other classes and working 2 jobs and I didn't have extra time for this. He gives quizzes on days when you don't have class, regardless of your schedule. His tests are impossible - I studied three weeks for every minute I wasn't occupied and I only scored a 70%.

I am taking 15 credits, working, and also volunteering. I do not have time to spend 3 hours a night studying for this class. He says his exams aren't hard but then makes them incredibly difficult. Class averages are about 50%. His extra credit he gives for attendance to make his averages look good is the only thing keeping me afloat.

This class is hard as hell but hear me out. He makes you understand the material to do well. I got a 67% on the first exam and then I did what he said and got an 86% on the next one. You will have put a ridiculous amount of work in to do well but its possible. Take easier classes the semester  you take this, you will not have time for other classes

First, during the lecture the professor goes off on tangents much too frequently, and then will breeze over slides to try and make up for lost time. Secondly, his exams are poorly written. For the first exam he told us that he wrote the exam the night before. Thirdly, you will not get a study guide until the night before the exam. Prepare to study.

I thought I was smart, then I took a class taught by this guy. Unless you have three hours a night to spend studying for his class don't take it. Seriously, I'm an honors college student and I'll be lucky to get a 3.0 in this class. Emphasis on LUCKY. Do yourself a solid and avoid this professor.

I liked his take not crap attitude.  He would call out students that are disrupting the class.  He explained everything well and was easy to follow along with.  He was always available to students if they needed help.  However his exams were incredible hard.  He would test us on the smallest of topics that he barley covered.  Expect to study a lot.

Well the exams are incredibly difficult, even after spending countless hours reading and UNDERSTANDING the concepts. I took this while also taking organic chemistry and the orgo was easier. He adds points to everybody's exam, which sounds great but it fluffs up the average so that he looks like he's a really good instructor, but he isn't.

His tests are ridiculously hard and the questions always have more than one right answer. Even after relistening to levitates and rewriting notes, I found that the exams usually cover stuff that isn't emphasised in class. He also claims that he'll never test you on something that isn't mentioned in class or on a PowerPoint - it's a lie.
Hard class. He does not have a pleasant attitude at times.

Talks very fast and the tests are extremely hard. I took three years of biology in high school and struggled to get a 3.5 in this class. He really does know what he's talking about and he mostly tells you what will be on the test.

easy and super interesting class that only meets once a week. Just gotta go to class and raise your hand 6 times in a semester for full participation so easy again. Readings are through perusall which is annoying but again if you can't read 20 pages once a week you probably should not be in college. a few easy cooking assignments, great prof.

Loved Dr. Qu! I'm honestly not sure why these reviews are so bad… her class is extremely easy. I got stuck with this class because it was the only IAH that fit into my schedule, however, I really enjoyed it. Class was only once a week and I actually found the lectures to be pretty interesting. Easy homework (quizzes) and midterm/final assignments.

There is a weekly quiz on a movie and/or a reading every week which can be annoying. There are participation stickers and you need 10 to get 100%. Attendance is mandatory with two unexcused. Quizzes are not lock down. Has a midterm paper and final online presentation. Nice teacher, didn't have any problems.
Save yourself the trouble and take another class.

Read the weekly course material and participate in class- the course is easy. People love to complain about everything. If you put effort into the essay portion of quiz you'll earn extra credit; I had no problems. 

I recommend this class to anyone genuinely interested in East Asia, b/c I enjoyed the material she provided. The lectures are boring.
Many reviews don't like her but I think the quizzes were not hard and you only had to do projects instead of exams. Also really easy to talk to for help.

Weekly quizzes are hard, and her grading of the "short" answer is strict. A reading or movie/series every week for the quiz that is usually unavailable unless you want to search for a free version for hours or paying. Mandatory attendance but class is only once a week, You need to participate. She also grades very slowly even with little students.
Just save yourself the trouble, pick a different class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is impossible. Quizzes are impossible and she picks readings and movies that nobody has ever heard of. She's more concerned picking things that people can't look up rather than picking content relative to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The quizzes are weird and imposossible. I went to class and some of the questions on the quizzes she never goes over, you can't look them up, and quizzes are most of your grade. I hated my life on the days I had this class.

The class literally isn't that hard. Some of these reviews are just overreacting. That being said, I wouldn't take the class if you aren't into East Asia, which I feel like is pretty obvious already. There is only one lecture every week and one quiz every week with some projects and you need to participate 10 total times in class for the whole sem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I have ever taken. Her lectures are boring and don't make a ton of sense and neither do her slides. The amount of outside reading and movies she gives to watch is crazy. The quizzes are impossible and barely anything on her slides helps. Overall, it is an insanely difficult class and not at all worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Wouldn't recommend. No variety in activity, yet participation was crucial to your grade. Her system for participation points was poor, as we only had so many weeks in the semester. Tough grader and low class quiz averages. Her teaching styles are definitely not for everyone, to a point where class wasn't very enjoyable. Nice person, hard professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Qu was speedy with email responses and super accommodating when it came to my VISA. I would not take this class if you are looking for an easy 4.0, I would only take it if you are REALLY into EA history or need it to graduate. the lectures were alright, although monotone, the content was interesting. lots and lots of reading at home tho :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: BEST TEACHER I EVER HAD! She is very concise and has a very clear passion for teaching. I loved her sticker system for participation and how she knew her presentations without reading off the board. I came into the class with no interest in the course and was surprised by the engaging material. If you pay attention, this class is sooooooo easy.

Extremely boring class. Would not recommend it to anyone. Class averages for quizzes are around 75% and don't seem to phase her. Class participation is your attendance grade but doesn't give many opportunities to participate in class.

The professor is ok. I would not recommend this class if you want an easy IAH. I am a big reader, but the readings and lectures were quite long most of the time even for me. The only assignments that are graded is the quiz every week, which she grades harshly. Many of my classmates have emailed her about issues and it was 50/50 for her to solve it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: well I did get a 4.0, this class was incredibly hard compared to other classes u can take instead. Professor also grades very hard and there is a ton of work. Every single quiz has short answer questions that are graded hard and you have to do a 15+ min presentation by yourself at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Monotone and incredibly boring lectures. Not clear with any concepts or instructions. Poor at explaining and very tough at grading. Expects a lot from students but does not give back in return.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: So many lectures and so many reading it was so hard to keep up. It also depends on the graduate student who does recitation because I believe she is who graded and I wrote paragraphs and spent way over the estimated time on the quizzes and never have got over an 80%. I would not recommend this class ):
Very boring lectures, too much reading for a single week's work, random drawing required for projects that don't relate. This isn't an art class, it's history.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you can take her for Russian, do! She's a great professor and is very generous. It's Russian, so you're going to have to work, but as long as you keep up you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lessons cover a lot of the class prep activities relating to the shows watched in class this semester. Very flexible with submitting late work and she if she doesn't allow corrections on summary activities (tests), they're usually given a bit of a curve anyway. Я люблю Жанну :)

Shannon is very kind and understanding, very flexible with late work as well, which is good considering the heavy workload for Russian. She's also pretty funny. Love hearing about the babushka lore. Lessons follow the Mezdhu Nami workbook until it's finished, then they go onto prep for the spring semester of 200 level RUS

The professor is nice, but this class is so boring. You have online prep videos, reading assignments, and a reading quiz all twice a week. We had two creative writing assignments and a final. Stories are originally in Russian and translated, so they don't make much sense and are very long and boring. Take another class if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class was easy, just a lot of homework involved. Teacher is nice and have had no grading issues either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you can. There is lots of reading every week and the stories are boring. I took this class because of the easy schedule but wish I hadn't.

If you have any other options, do not take this class. There is pre class work for every class, a reading assignment with questions, a quiz, and an online prep. It sounds easy but it's very time consuming. She will give pre class work the same days we have projects or writing assignments due. The lectures are very boring and just all her opinions.
She assigns way too much homework! I would not take this class if you do not want the heavy and boring work load.  Class is mandatory and she is not understanding. Expects A LOT!! Just the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Let Professor Quan know if you use or plan to use AI, or your grade will be affected. The material was a bit outdated and relied heavily on articles and external sources, followed by multiple small quizzes, a discussion, and an exam. While reading-heavy, it was an easy A (exams are heavily based on the external sources and articles).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is very cautious about plaigarism/ChatGPT so be careful. However the class itself was super easy. You just have to read quite a bit and write discussion posts and take some small quizzes. Thats really it though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: As this class is an online class, I can't say much about the professor but more on the course. I really enjoyed this class and was really interested that I actually want this class to be made in person as well. The downside is that there are a lot of reading to do and wish that it could be summarized down a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took ANP 429 and it was a very enjoyable and memorable experience. Class is friendly to beginner ethnographers and the professor is caring towards your progress. The readings are not overwhelming by any means and the class structures you well for the final project. Amazing professor with a lot of experience and knowledge in the field.

Prof Quan has interesting material however there is so much reading and additional articles that it was unrealistic for me to actually process the content even though I was genuinely interested and wanted to learn. If he cut out the excess requirements I would have had a much deeper understanding of everything we covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took ANP 200 in an online asynchronous format over the summer as an elective. I don't remember much from the course other than the materials were super easy and the class required minimal work. If you do the assignments you will have no issues in this course.

I feel bad giving her a lower rating because she is very sweet and kind to all of her students. But her lectures are long, boring, and tough to understand at times due to her strong accent. The midterm was randomly thrown onto us two days before the due date, in which the wrong time was told. Subpar lectures and unclear instructions define this.

(I had Qing for 201, not 202, but it wasn't an option) 

Professor Qing is an exceptional, extremely caring professor. If you want to 4.0 the class, go to her office hours and do her honors option! She gives extra credit (unlike other JMC professors) and show your appreciation for her. Nevertheless, try your best and your work will be recognized.

Professor Qing is one of the sweetest and most understanding professors I have ever had, and she is very knowledgable on a variety of political science and IR topics. Her class is somewhat disorganized and instructions for essays and assignments can be somewhat unclear, but she is usually more than willing to answer any questions you have.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love her so much. Super intelligent and understanding that life happens.

I appreciated that Professor Qing took the time to make sure we understood her lectures (she recognises that her accent is hard to understand). My biggest problem is that her guidelines for assignments are incredibly vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Qing! I really enjoyed her MC 201 course. She was very accessible outside of class and got to know us as people in addition to students. Her research is very interesting. She was a fair grader and attending office hours was really helpful. She is very sweet and I'm so glad to have developed a relationship with her. 100% recommend!
She's an amazing teacher, my favorite at James Madison College.

I LOVED Professor Qing! She is a little hard to understand sometimes but has no problem repeating herself for you if needed. She does not take attendance but I would obviously recommend attending class as much as you can. I enjoyed her so much for MC220 that I am taking MC318 with her this semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Qing is very bright. While she is hard to understand, she adds valuable insight into class discussions that you don't get from many professors. MC201 is heavily discussion based. The classes would consist of a student-led ppt, a class discussion, and then Qing would end it all up with how our discussion relates to the reading.

She is a really nice, and intelligent teacher who cares about you being able to understand her and the material. Easy grader. She doesn't post a rubric and you don't really know what she wants you to do in your writings. 70% of the grades happen at the end, so it gets stressful. Class schedule gets wonky, and she isn't good with online stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Qing is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've had at MSU; Her profound understanding of the Sino-US partnership is rare. She possesses a plethora of experience reading, writing, and teaching about Chinese foreign policy and ways to pacify Sino-U.S. relations. She is both competent and caring!
Absolutely wonderful and brilliant professor, she knows a lot and always wants what's best for her students. I've taken 2 of her classes and I would take anything she teaches.

Prof Qing is a wonderful lady. She can be difficult to understand but she knows this. She recognizes the language barrier and will help you to understand. She laughs regarding her troubles with English at times. Not really a tough grader and pretty open with due dates. She is not a very good grader and does take some time to submit. 4/5.

I graduated in 2004.  Dr. Qing is the most compassionate, enthusiastic, fair, and honest professor I've had. I am now a teacher and her spirit in the classroom inspires and informs my work.  I tried to take as many of her classes as were offered and I studied abroad with her in Beijing.   Go to office hours. Be passionate and informed--you'll learn

Excellent Prof.  Encourages Debate and provides good guide lines for understanding the reading.  Accent is a small barrier.  Don't ever underestimate her, she is very smart, and always paying attention.

While Professor Qing's accent may make it hard for some students to learn, she really wants students to understand the material and engage in discussion.  She is more than willing to go over things during office hours and her enthusiasm for the subject shows.  If you study what's on her slides for the exams then you should do fine.

Generally nice-clearly intelligent;somewhat haphazard in teaching style; accent and English as a second language pose a barrier between her and the class. Grading either w/0 rhyme/reason or aiming to hit arbitrary 2.5 bell curve. Many assignments I received had 'excellent work' coupled w/ mediocre grades. Two words: Knuckle Sandwich.
good professor, hard to understand most of the time but very interesting and intelligent.
I agree...  not a good professor.  She basically just wants you to debate in class instead of going over the readings.  Then, by the time you get to the midterm or exam, you get screwed over.
Don't take this professor.  It will be the end of your GPA.
Very nice, and pretty easy, even though grading can be a bit inconsistant and hard to predict. Be careful, or she might give you a "knuckle sandwich!"

I generally enjoyed this class and felt that Dr. Richards kept lectures entertaining. The final, however, was a nightmare. Even though it was a non-cumulative final, the material was inaccessible because he hadn't finished writing the chapters in his own textbook yet. I missed one class the whole semester and wasn't able to catch up due to that.

There are only 3 exams (2 online); the final isn't cumulative but he makes the final in person rather than online. His exams are all fill-in-the-blank or short-answer, with no multiple-choice. Provides us with an incomplete textbook, and it isn't finished for the material on the final so I had to teach myself and there was material about physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found this course difficult due to its grading structure and heavy workload. The syllabus categories made it hard to track my standing, and missing grades in a section impacted my GPA. I reached out for help over 2.5 weeks but didn't get the guidance I needed. Stay proactive and clarify expectations early.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The content is not the easiest to understand but he does a great job at making it digestible and tailors his lectures to the students that are attending class so he can really help you with the things you struggle with. Very high energy and does a great job at keeping people engaged.

One of the hardest class I have had. He is nice, but the class is not easy at all. DONT SKIP CLASS. 4 exams in total, 3 outside of class, Final is cumulative and in person. Assignments twice per week (pick 3 questions from exercise you want to talk about in class, and what are some questions you want to ask him). Ask him if you have any question.
90% of the class is exams, but 60% were take home midterms, so not that bad. attendance isn't mandatory and he has video lectures on d2l, so i never had to go to class.

If you don't like soccer, do not take this class. Lots of readings and lectures, and a lot of papers as well. No finals and no quizzes or exams, which is nice, but the ending assignment is a 5-page paper about the class. The grading scale is weird; you can get 100% on everything but miss 4 lectures, and you end with a 3.0 or worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Richards is an entertaining and talented lecturer and genuinely a really nice and understanding guy. I have no interest in soccer, but Dr. Richards is really good at still making his lectures engaging and applying the concepts outside of soccer too. If you put in effort, it's an easy 4.0.

Dr. Richards is an amazing and entertaining lecturer.  I would say the grading was a bit unfair. It is tier-based, so if you understand the class and consistently earn perfect grades on all homework and essays, you can still receive a poor grade for attendance, reading questions, or something else.  Please do not take if not interested in soccer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really easy class. Lectures can get kind of boring but when attendance is done at the beginning you can leave early. Reading question homework assignments a few times a week that are super easy and one paper like once every other friday thats only 600 words. You can tell Dr. Richards enjoys his job and a 4.0 is attainable with some work.

He is a great professor, he cares about what he teaches, and he can make lectures exciting. The essays are only 300-500 words each, and you can do revisions. It can be hard to get a 4.0, but if you show up and put in a tiny bit of effort, it's attainable. Good professor, easy class.
He is such a chill professor, always ends class early because he doesn't want to be there either.

This dude is seriously great, couple 1 paragraph papers due every other day, read about 4 books, no tests, no quizzes, actually cares about what he teaches. If you listen to him, you lowkey get inspired, this guy is amazing on everything. Class gets cancelled sometimes last minute, but who cares, seriously. Love this dude take him
Legendary professor who actually teaches interesting topics. With the homework load being light to non-existent, would recommend.

Great guy and easy class. Lots of reading from 4 books, and attendance is required. No quizzes or exams, just several short (1-page) essays that aren't too hard. He rarely answers emails and sometimes cancels class last minute, so communication can be a bit frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is very caring to students and passionate about philosophy! If you go to most lectures and complete group work, the exams were pretty straight forward. Only complaint I have is that there is no homework, so your grade is fully based on quizzes and tests along with group work. Overall, would recommend!

The professor doesn't grade the papers his TA does. His grading system is so flawed your grade is the lowest section score: If you have a 4.0 GPA in everything else  (readings, essays, etc) but miss 7 days of attendance, you're getting a 2.5. The D2L page is unusable for the students. You can miss 5 min of class and miss attendance
Awesome. Take him.

A philosophy class disguised as a soccer class, that's probably the only reason he agreed to teach this course anyways.

Important philosophical topics like the ship of Theseus, the absence of objective morality, and other stuff, but most of it goes over people's heads.

I pay less attention to the soccer and more to his oratory skills. He is a pretty good public speaker, if you try to learn from his oratory skills and pick apart what he does its like two classes in one. 

I don't like his system of grading, and other iahs are easier if your looking for that.

Topic is kinda boring, pick another class
Worst professor at MSU

I don't recommend this professor. He leaves grading to TAs and is unresponsive to emails. My grade dropped unfairly despite following rubrics. Weekly readings from 4 hard-to-find football books add extra cost. He often cancels class last-minute but mandates attendance. This course had far more work compared to other IAH 2xx classes.

I honestly had a good time in this class at the start of the semester, but when I received my 1.5 gpa after going to every lecture and getting an 100 on each essay but missing out on a couple reading questions, I now view Dr. Richards grading system to be just a tad wonky and would never allow myself personally to take one of his classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr Richard's was very engaging and fun in his lectures, all you need to do is 2 reading questions a week which takes 20 min and an essay every other week which are super easy, you just have to show up to lectures and do the questions and you will 4.0.

Honestly Dr. Richards was great he is very passionate about his teaching, during lecture you do have to go because he does take attendance. You didn't have to pay attention in lecture at all. His TAs did all the grading, one of them graded very harshly and it made its of kids struggle. the homework is very easy it just is time consuming.

His quizzes due on Saturday night because nobody is busy on Saturday night. Held class the day before Thanksgiving and expected students to be there when some people live across the country, also wouldnt give an excused absence with my plane ticket lol. I bet he's a very successful author though so teaching most likely comes second.

Professor Richards is really knowledgeable when it comes to PHL. His lectures are engaging and keeps you interested the entire time. The graded material was pretty easy if you took good class notes and read the assigned readings. If you do not go to class you will not do as good though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Richards was by far my favorite professor of the year. Attendance is not mandatory but the lectures he gives are crucial and they are super interesting and engaging. There are quizzes each week but super easy if you pay attention. Exams are also easy and he prepares you a lot for them. Overall great course to take if you need the credit!

Class is graded on a quiz after each topic (10 pt), every week a group worksheet (2 pt), and an exam (100 pt) after a few topics. The work is all on your computer so you are able to use notes for everything. But you need to attend lecture consistently to know what is going on and make sense of the notes. Very fun lectures and a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hes a very nice guy and always checked in with us to make sure we understood the material. All the lectures were over zoom and we also did group work once a week. Gives a good, broad introduction to a lot of philosophers. The class is centered on epistemology and metaphysics so be prepared.

He is a great professor! Class requires you to pay attention, luckily no textbook because he wrote his own book that is super easy to read and has good information in it. Was online but zooms were fun and fast. He is a great person and truly cares about his students. Definitely recommend this class!! Exams aren't too hard but you have to read!!

REALLY TOUGH GRADER. His rubrics are just for decoration. You gotta listen to his 2-hour-long ramble, and if you miss the 2 mins that he actually talks about the requirements that are NOT covered in the rubric, ur screwed. I know only a few got As on their projects, so be aware.
UGHHH! UGHH! DO NOT TAKE

He would grade not really based off of the rubrics, and take off lots of points if you didn't follow it. He would ramble on quite a bit in lectures and not really talk about what was important. Pretty hard class for a 101

He rambled about the most random things and then would tell us the stuff he provided for examples aren't 100% correct. It would just piss me off, but he was really kind just not a good teacher, the man needs to retire.

He's a sweet guy, but he definitely rambles on, and I would fall asleep during Zooms. I was so bored. The project guidelines were difficult to understand, and he deducted points for minor details that were not specified. Will take off attendance points if you don't want to talk. The class was difficult, even though it was a 101 class.

Rambles most of the class which is hard to listen to at 8 am twice a week. Dosent give clear feedback and the class heavily relies on participation. He typically marked you as absent if you didn't respond to him when called on.

Rambles for the whole two hours, usually repeating the same phrase. Some variation of "If you don't take these projects seriously you will fail". Exponentially more success would be achieved if he spent half as much time actually talking about the content and expectations instead of how some of us aren't taking it seriously enough.
Do not recommend this class! No solid feedback, tough grader, guidelines for projects instructions are not clear, and does not offer helpful information.
would not recommend
He just talks the whole class even if it is not related to the material. He is a really tough grader and his grading criteria is unclear.

Rushed towards the end of the semester when things started to get more difficult and was not the best at answering questions, but was a good professor overall.

Dr. Taylor cares deeply about her students, and she definitely tailors the class to encourage non-science majors to use their disciplines to find interest in environmental science. She is understanding, genuine, and truly kind.

Solid professor. Attendance required w/ in class activities every class. Pretty boring lectures though and hope you have a solid group for the class because you will do a project with them. Otherwise would recommend for a easy class to take for gen ed.

Dr. Taylor is an amazing professor. She not only provides a lot of feedback, but she is very encouraging and really works to make sure her students understand the material. She has all of the work broken up in weeks for lab, and her D2L is very organized. Professor Taylor will always find a way to meet you in the middle, and she is very fun.

reviews.comment: Nothing bad to say about Dr. Taylor. She is so passionate about what she does, but she takes into account that not everyone shares that passion. She helped me so much with my other class. If you show up, you're gonna do fine.

This class changed my opinion of science classes entirely for the better. Dr. Taylor was tentative to the needs of each and every one of her students, and was encouraging of participation and active learning in the classroom. The midterm was very balanced with content, and the final was online. In-class activities every day, so show up!

Extremely sweet professor and cares about all students who step into her classroom. She provides structured, thought-out feedback and provides interactive lectures that teaches you lessons about everyday life. As an "unmotivated" student, I'd always look forwards to class. If I could retake any class at MSU, it 100% would be this one.

Her lectures are really fun and easy to relate with in real life scenarios and she also addresses present day issues. Grading isn't too strict but will give useful comments to improve on, a lot of group work. If she sees potential, she helps give resources and references how to succeed and do more outside of class. Took the class for fun, worth it!
Really nice to talk to, helps students a lot and if you have issues with grades she loves helping students with where they can earn more points. Also very funny and lectures are fun and interactive

Dr Taylor is very passionate about her class, and she's very caring of all her students. Some of the assignments are a little annoying but she tries to make them fun. She's one of the sweetest people ever, and I would recommend going to her office hours. The only 2 big gradings in the class is the midterm (notecard allowed) and group project.
Sweetest professor ever.

She is very kind and caring and actually cares about her students. Attendance is strict and lectures can be boring but she jumps around a lot which makes it engaging. I wasn't a fan of the topic but she quickly made it my favorite course. Do the in class activities and as long as your group for the final is decent it's easy.

Dr. Taylor is a kind and caring professor. She would always say in class "this is not a building block course and we are going to be jumping around" which is 100% true. There usually always an in-class assignment so make sure to pay attention to the lectures.

Professor Taylor was an average professor. She had some boring lectures/ annoying homework assignments, but was fair in her grading. Group project/ midterm exam make up the bulk of the grade. Final group project was annoying to complete.

She is so nice. I have a 98% in this class its very easy. Just do the work and you're good. She offers extra credit and grades work super fast. I emailed her about an issue and she responded within minutes and fixed the issue. I love her, she's so sweet I'd do anything for her. Please take this class and show her love.

Literally one of the kindest professors I've ever had. Always receiving and listening to feedback, knows all her students and you can tell she loves her job. Weekly homework but it's never difficult and no exam, just a group presentation.

Dr. Taylor is just an alright professor. She explains things very clearly but she can sometimes talk to you like a baby, and other times talk too fast. The homework is pretty easy as long as you pay attention, and the midterm exam wasn't the worst. A lot of guest speakers and their content will be on the exam. No readings though which is good.

She is such a sweet teacher; you can tell she loves her job and teaching this subject. I really like her classes and hearing her talk. She takes your answers from the homework and incorporates them into the next lecture. She's very open to feedback and will adjust her class and teaching format to keep her students happy. I enjoy her class.

Dr. Taylor is my pride and joy. Had her for 202 and 208L, amazing experience in both would take a million times over. So kind, helpful, understanding, funny, smart, everything you want in a professor. learn to use excel beforehand and the class is much easier. If you have the chance to take her, do it! Praise Dr. Taylor, she deserves the world.

Although she overcomplicates the class a bit and is very nit-picky eith grading, she is incredibly nice and understanding. I didn't mind the group work, but having to show up every day or getting a 0 for the in class activities kinda suck. One midterm with cheat sheets, weekly homework and a final presentation/paper. Interesting class

Dr. Taylor is the best professor I've ever had. She truly cares about her students and will help you with anything you need. There's a regular amount of work but it's not too difficult just can be time consuming. Just show up to class and participate.
It is unbelievable how hard she tries to make this class way harder than it needs to be.

The class was setup in groups and almost everything is done with your group. The final is a semester long project which you present and work on in groups it's a good chunk of the grade. There is a textbook but she provides it. There's only one test and it's the midterm which if you don't do well can drop your grade a decent amount.

I so grateful for how this course is set up. you never feel like your wastin your time bc the lectures, readings, hw, quizzes, exam are all related and you feel prepared. she also offers a cheatsheet and it counts towards your hw grade which is a free grade !
Dr. Taylor is an incredibly supportive professor. She provides valuable insights during group projects, ensuring that we meet all the requirements and achieve the grades we desire.

Dr. Taylor makes every class activity feel engaging and exciting. Whether it's a workshop or lecture, she always incorporates interactive elements that keep us engaged while making the learning experience enjoyable and productive.

I really appreciate how Dr. Taylor encourages us during group projects. She's always available for questions, offers constructive feedback, and ensures we stay on track to meet the expectations for the project.

Working on group projects with Dr. Taylor is such a positive experience. She encourages collaboration and offers helpful suggestions to ensure we all contribute and meet the project's goals. Her support makes a huge difference in the outcome.

Dr. Taylor is incredibly supportive during group projects. She goes above and beyond to ensure that we meet the expectations and achieve the grades we want through her constructive feedback. Her guidance helps us stay on track, and she's always available to help when needed.

I really appreciate how Professor Taylor creates a positive learning environment. She always encourages her students to ask questions and gives thoughtful feedback that helps us grow and do well in her course
I love how organized and well-prepared Professor Taylor is for each class. She makes every topic easy to follow and provides helpful examples from real life that deepen my understanding.
I'm so grateful to have had Professor Taylor as an instructor. She is insightful, approachable, and truly cares about her students' growth and success. I always feel supported in her class.

She is a knowledgeable and approachable professor who creates a welcoming environment for all students. Professor taylor provides clear explanations and is always happy to offer assistance when needed during her office hours or after class

Professor taylor is one of the best professors I've had. She genuinely cares about her students' success and goes out of her way to make sure we understand the material by offering workshops and in class activities. Her feedback is always helpful and encouraging.

I have learned so much in Professor Taylor's class. She is patient, approachable, and has an amazing ability to break down difficult material. Her passion for teaching really shines through because of how well organized and constructed the course is. You can tell so much work is put into it to ensure her student's success

Professor taylor is a fantastic instructor who makes every class engaging and enjoyable. She explains complex topics in a way that is easy to understand, and she's always there to help when you need it.

Professor taylor consistently goes above and beyond to create an engaging and informative learning experience. Their enthusiasm for the subject is contagious, and their clear explanations help students feel successful and confident in their work.

professor taylor is both knowledgeable and approachable, making it easy to engage with the content. They offer constructive feedback and make sure every student has the support they need. I feel more confident in my academic abilities after taking this class.

I feel incredibly fortunate to have had Professor taylor as an instructor. They create a classroom atmosphere that encourages collaboration and critical thinking. They always make time for students and offer valuable insights into the material as well as clear up any confusion on any topic.

Professor taylor is an excellent communicator who truly knows how to make learning enjoyable. Their passion for the subject and dedication to students shines through in every lesson. I've gained confidence and a deeper appreciation for the topic.

I am so grateful for Professor taylor's teaching. They are approachable, patient, and always willing to help. I have gained a deeper understanding of the subject thanks to their clear and effective teaching methods.

Professor taylor brings enthusiasm and energy to every lecture. They explain complicated topics in a way that is both clear and engaging. I look forward to their class each week as well as the interesting in class activities that we do

What stands out about Professor Taylor is their genuine care for their students' success. They go above and beyond to ensure we grasp the material and are always willing to answer questions. I feel encouraged and supported throughout the course which i rarely find that with other professors.

Dr. Taylor is one of the best professors I've had!!! She has an incredible ability to make the subject interesting and accessible. I've learned so much from their clear explanations and thoughtful feedback. She puts so much work and effort into her course and honestly, you can see that being reflected in the course!

Dr. Taylor presents material in an organized and approachable way, and they are always available to offer guidance. I feel motivated and confident in my learning because of their teaching style and support

since we have a final project as our final, she is very understanding and supportive if we had group members who are not contributing or delaying the group's progress, and instead, grades your individual work and is very fair.

Dr. Taylor an outstanding instructor who always creates an engaging and supportive learning environment. Their passion for the subject is infectious, making complex concepts easier to understand. I truly appreciate their dedication to helping students succeed.

her lectures are always interesting and makes you more aware about your environment. I really liked the group project because it targets regions in the world that need environmental attention, which puts the spotlight on places of where people are struggling but the media doesn't highlight that.

something i like is that on the midterm, the workshops &in class activites are really a preperation for your midterm so thats why she provides so much detailed and good feedback on them (which is why many people say shes a tough grader)

What I like is that the reading &lectures go hand in hand which is amazing bc the lectures explain things that i might not understood in the readings. shes available and willing to meet with you for office hours to help you on areas where you are struggling as well as offer extra credit to help your grade. She also has a lot of drops in the course!

She is very observant and notices her hard working students and gives out stickers and thanks them for doing so well in the course which is very rare that any professor hardly even recognizes ur face. She also support you so much bc she provides the textbook for you and everything you need for free!

Dr. Taylor is very supportive and is willing to help you to make sure you do you best in her course. She puts so much time and effort into grading and giving constructive feedback. Some people say shes a tough grader, but really, she just wants you to do excellent on the midterm bc everything you do in class is preparing you for it.

Talked during every work time so we never could work in class during the time she had set aside. Class activities often have no meaning or impact. Topics are easy but assignments are often tedious and take a lot of time.
Very caring teacher, just a lot of time wasted in class

Very kind and will like you if you participate and try. Attendance is taken and she is a VERY tough grader but does not take off high amounts of points. Low points taken off but very easy to loose points. Overall great teacher for a mandatory class.

The entire class is group projects, it's awful. She is a REALLY tough grader and if you make even one tiny mistake or you don't explain something enough, you'll fail the assignment completely. She also barely gives feedback, so you usually don't know what you did wrong. The assignments are easy but there's so many each week. She's super nice tho

Taylor's lecture's aren't the *most* engaging, but she is very kind, smart and posts the lectures online if you need to review. There is only one person midterm exam and the final is a group project that you work on throughout the semester. If you put just a little bit of effort in, you should get a 4.0.

Dr. Taylor is super nice, I just was not interested in the class topics at all. If you miss a class you lose a lot of points so you need to  go to  every single  lecture. It was hard to pay attention but if you really like the Earth and the environment then this is a good fit because Dr. Taylor is a great  person.

Dr. Taylor is super nice and very passionate about her studies. Lectures were okay. She gives a lot of in class and outside of class activities/homework. Only one exam, which is the midterm. There is a big group project at the end.

Great professor, only one exam the midterm. Even if you flunk midterm you're still able to get a good grade in class. Lots of group work- the final is a group project. Talking to her helps build a good relationship.

I loved Dr. Taylor's class! She is so much fun and, outside of some of the videos she shows, the lectures are really enjoyable! In-class assignments are worth more of your grade than you think so don't miss class! Slightly challenging mid-term but she does let you have a cheat sheet. Everything is graded to the absolute letter of her rubrics.

Dr. Taylor is a nice and somewhat understanding professor. Most of your grade in that class will consist of your attendance, the in-class learning activities, and the labs she gives to you the night before. If you show up to class and do your work, then you should be perfectly fine.

I loved Dr. Taylor. In a class of over 200, she was somehow able to know my name. Course consists of weekly homework's (Quiz and Discussion Post) which are both take home and fairly easy. Show up to class, take notes, and it is literally the easiest 4.0. After the midterm, there is no need to take notes. Final is a CAP project presentation.
Great professor, homework is very easy. A lot of it is group based activities. Exams are kind of hard, but Dr. Taylor is an accommodating professor who cares for her students success.

Dr. Taylor was one of my favorite professors during the fall. She is super caring and wants all of her students succeed. Her grading criteria is very clear. If you ever have any questions she is always open to ask and provides very good feedback. If you have to opportunity to take any of her classes, do it!
This professor cares about your success and gives you many resources to help you succeed in the class. It's very flexible when it comes to assignments and homework. I recommend this professor!

Dr. Taylor was a solid professor until she started enforcing word counts on discussion posts. She will mark you down even if you are a 20 words shy, with solid content, and then still mark you down when you meet the word count using filler content and dragging it out. She needs to learn to pick one, quantity or quality. You can't have both.

Overall Dr. Taylor is a great professor. You can tell she wants you to do well in the class, and she will work with you when possible. The only reason I am not giving her a 5 is because she does weekly discussions posts, and is a stickler about minimum word counts. Remove the word count minimums and I would easily give her a 5.

Dr. Taylor genuinely cares about her students and how well they are doing in her class. She also adjusted certain aspects of the class based on feedback from us. This class is very lecture heavy but they are all very applicable in our everyday lives. We also are assigned groups at the very beginning of the semester to work in throughout the class.
She really knows what she is doing and had interesting lectures. She has a quick pace, which might not be the best for everybody.

Professor Ustunol is very personable as a professor, and is clearly passionate about the chemistry and processing of food. This class welcomes and encourages worldly perspectives that you can share through the platform PackBack for response assignments related to lectures. Occasional quizzes are very easy and taken at home, un-proctored.

As a freshman, this was an amazing class for my first semester.  Dr. U clearly cares a lot about her students, and really does want you to do well in her course. Her class is very organized and straightforward. Her lectures can be a little long sometimes, but she explains her material very well, and is clearly very educated on the topic. Love her!

I'm not fond of STEM but Dr. Ustunol made FSC super interesting. If you aren't a good test taker she has tons of other assignments to boost your grade. You do have to study a bit for the exams but nothing too challenging and the material was fun to learn about.

Dr. U is a great professor and clearly knows her stuff, she has a ton of real world experience and provides great advice. Super easy homework and discussion board assignments. Only complaint is that lectures are quite boring and at 8:30am. Attendance is required, but exams are mostly based off of lecture material so make sure to show up.

Class is easy but lectures are very boring. She is big on attendance and your attendance grade counts for 10% of the final grade in the end which sucks. Course material was easy to locate but confusing at points because deadlines were always changing.

Her lectures were impossible to attend due to her boring lectures and monotone voices. I had her at 8:30 am... I would wake up, join for attendance, answer the for credit top hat multiple choice questions and leave. The quizzes were so hard even though I used the lectures religiously. I was super surprised when I 4.0

Professor Ustunol is professional and intelligent in her field, but the lectures were a bit dry and monotone. There was 10 short quizzes (no cumulative exams) and a Packback assignment each week. 5 easy homework assignments spread out over the semester. Just put in a bit of effort and you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: Ustonol is probably one of the best professors in the MSU food science department. As long as you pay attention and put in a little bit of work you should do fine. She has neat little antidotes that relate to class material and i personally enjoyed! 10/10 would recommend!

reviews.comment: She's an ok professor, but the lectures are quite dull at times, and she didn't take attendance consistently but still factors it into your grade. The tests are intimidating at first but once you get used to it they're pretty easy, and despite attendance being mandatory its only worth 5% so you can afford to miss if you understand the material.
The quizzes are a bit intimidating at first, but they are easy if you come to class and pay attention. She grades the quizzes and exam rather harshly. Easy group project at the end of the semester.

reviews.comment: Lab reports are long and graded extremely hard. Each lab report can take excess of 5-6 hours to make and is over  10 pages at times (never shorter than 3). Basically you will be writing an essay a week.  The lab class itself is not hard, but the reports are. Expect to communicate with you TA about any issues and grading not Ustunol herself.

Her lectures can not be downloaded. You must have an internet connection to view them. The sound of her voice is incredibly irritating to the point of being almost unbearable. I dread every lecture I have to listen to from her.  Wish the class was in an overall different format to make it more user friendly (i.e. downloadable power points)

Dr. Umucu cares about student success. His goal is to make sure you are developing as a professional. reviews.comment: Comedy and culture class.
I emailed him asking for some help on a film and he told me to look at my notes. I'm pretty sure if I had the information needed in my notes I wouldn't email him.
Crude.

I'm a very diligent student. Mr. Urish is not the greatest trip I've taken. He's "fair." Everything outlined in his syllabus is EXACTLY, word-for-word, what he'll hold you accountable... But as far as being a friendly, approachable man, he's a bit intimidating. Treat him with respect still. Otherwise he'll only salivate all over your face screaming

i have no idea where to start. the class is interesting however he is nuts. he is a huge jerk, if you ever need help (which you WILL) he'll completely brush you off-repeatedly. he expects you to memorize every word and fact from the book, every word that comes out of his mouth.honestly dont take this if you care about your GPA.=]
didnt care about us, just hurried through things nad was never really interested in us!! oh and so boring
This dude is an A #1 A**hole! In my entire time at MSU, I have never had a prof. be more of a d**k than this guy. His rules are pathetic and ridiculous.

this teacher is just an jerk, if you're enrolled in his class just drop it. makes the biggest case out of everything. it would be helpful if the stuff he made a big deal about was anything important but theyre not. really just avoid at all cost.
be ware! initiallycomes off easygoing, but is really a hardass, opinionated jackass
Decent prof, just show up to class and make sure you follow EVERY rule of MLA!
Get out while you still can!!!
Very good prof, just do the work.
He's an air head. He really needs help!

Absolutely fantastic professor. His lectures are super engaging and he includes lots of fun stories in them. While there is a lot of weekly homework and test questions can be hard, he rounds up your participation/homework grades to a 100% if you get at least a 75%, which balances out the difficulty. I recommend reading the textbook to do well.

I loved this guy, but make sure you go to all lectures. I excelled because I paid attention during the lectures, but I know people that struggled because they didn't pay attention. The exams are very easy if you just pay attention and go to class.

Attendance isn't mandatory but you get iClicker points. Prof. Voit's lectures are intriguing and easy to listen to. The class is also very easy to get an A in if you read the chapters, do the practices, the homework (if you get over 75% correct you get 100% credit), and ask questions. Tests are not very complicated, just do the practice exam.

Super nice guy but if you are not interested in astronomy, do not take this class. I just needed to fill my requirement of an ISP course and this was such a hard course to do this with. If you are lost in the beginning, you are lost for good.

The lab is great; however, I recommend not taking the lecture with Professor Voit or online. His knowledge is too advanced for an introductory class, and he creates practice problems for the exams that aren't helpful, which is the issue. The work, however, isn't hard. Professor Voit is very understanding, but I had issues with his teaching style.

ISP205 was a great course because of Professor Voit! He is WAY too qualified to be teaching this course and that's what makes it so fun. Genuinely one of the easiest and most interesting classes I've ever taken. You can complete the homework fast and the lectures are enjoyable, Voit is deeply passionate about astronomy and an incredible lecturer.

Professor Voit is passionate and keen on academic honesty. I was only able to excel in this class if I did the homework, engaged with lecture material, and went to office hours. If you are interested in astronomy or possess a background in it, this course could be fun and easy. If you are looking for an easy A, this isn't it. You have to work hard.

ISP 205 was by far the most difficult class I have taken. I would suggest to take another ISP class and for sure NOT with Prof. Voit. 60% of your grade is just exams. Class averages for these exams were below a 68%. Takes a 3 week trip to California and moves the class online before one of the exams and didn't even show up for the exam. Awful prof.

ISP 205 was always really fun to go to. If you have an interest in astronomy, take this class. Voit clearly wants you to do well in this class, he does exam review on zoom at 10pm before exam days. Homework can often be trick questions so read the question. Extra credit for writing questions in emails! Take notes because it can get pretty intricate

He is one of those professors who genuinely wants his students to do well but structures his class in a way that makes it hard for them to. Readings are SO long. Exams are a majority of the grade and are only 27 questions and are extremely hard with a class average of about 50. Even studying everything on the study guide I failed nearly every exam.

Lectures are interesting/informative but not mandatory, can skip a few, 2 weekly assignment that take 1-1.5 hours total. Great prof. Caring, loves material/answering question. Funny/ engaging. No complaints for Voit. Only complaint is that for a gen ed, ISP 205 is unnecessarily difficult. If you want to get credit and leave, take an easier option.
very knowledgeable, not boring, keeps the lecture interesting by adding stories or random facts.

If I could rate a professor a 0/5 I would do so with this professor. Arbitrary test questions and he did not take advantage of lecture time. He covered way too much material for one semester and jammed it into 16 weeks. Not to mention he skipped a few weeks of class and gave us a sub that wasn't helpful - It was really unprofessional.

Professor Voit is arguably the best professor at Michigan State. He is highly respected in his field and knows what he's talking about but cares so deeply about his students. I've never seen someone so passionate about their life's work. You need to take this class.

This is a prof that really loves astronomy and wants to make his students love it as much as him. He wrote the book which is good because the examples he uses in class are in the book so it reinforces what you are learning. Great prof I'm never bored during lectures. I would recommend him and this class if you need an ISP credit
He was an amazing professor. Science is one of my worst subjects, but he made it make sense. It is very obvious he loves what he does, and he is good at it.
Really knows what he is talking about, A very smart person.
Really knows what he is talking about, A very smart person.
I was in his astronomy lab...even though he didn't teach the class, his office hours were open and was tons more helpful than any of the TA's ever were.
Okay, he's like 40 something, but he's still cute, in a nerdy sort of way. Plus he's super interesting! And he knows what he is talking about... he wrote the textbook!

Although this class was difficult and a lot of busy work, the professor was very easy to get along with. If you put in the work and show you care you will be completely fine. John Urbance is one of the best professors I've had.

Watched this man almost break a students laptop the other day. Professor was heated because the kid had asked why he was marked off when he had done it perfectly according to the rubric. Prof then checked his own rubric and the kid was right. How are you supposed to get a good grade when youre graded based on whims and mood swings?

This is the worst class I have taken at MSU. His personality is incredibly difficult to get along with. He grades based on opinions. For presentations he takes A LOT of points off because he doesn't enjoy the way things look. Incorrectly posts directions on D2L, we called him out on it, he raised his voice and shoved my lab-mates laptop away. Rude

The course itself wasn't that difficult. However, during lab periods we would often go over the end time to finish things up. He does seem to care about the students and was nice enough to offer in-person demonstrations.

reviews.comment: When I first enrolled in this course I came to this website to see what this professor was about. All the reviews said he was a jerk and a horrible professor. I very much disagree. reviews.comment: Very nice guy that knows what he's talking about. Class consisted of quizzes at the start of each class and then he demonstrated most of the procedures which was very helpful.

Dr. Urbance, for most, is a tough personality to get along with, but if you show that you are trying and working hard you will do fine. Despite his tough exterior he does care if students succeed. He gets easily irritated but ask him questions about how to get projects done correctly.

STAY AWAY. His classes are the most unorganized classes I've ever had the misfortune to take. Doesn't explain anything well, but still sends email after email repeating the same, confusing instructions. He doesn't lead recitation or any of the labs and doesn't really seem to care about his students.

This class is BY FAR the most unprofessionally led class I have ever taken at MSU. It's only worth 2 credits, but the workload definitely exceeds it. Dr. Urbance constantly emails us late at night the day before things are due and all he talks about is how perfect his work in college is and how ours has to look exactly like his or we won't pass!!!!

reviews.comment: Course not and miss. Changes happen early in week. Group presentation. Good looking man.

reviews.comment: If you go to his office hours and ask for help, he might yell at you if you don't understand a simple concept. Don't take it personally thought, that's just how he is. He's incredibly smart and knows what he's talking about, but teaching it is not his strongest suit. He's not a bad guy, but I wouldn't take a class with him again if i didnt have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Urbance is the least favorite professor I have had to date. I had him for a biology lab and he made you do a lot of busy work, such as writing over 100 pages of protocol into a lab notebook even though they are posted in a word document for you already. He is also very specific about his grading. He likes things done his way.

He's a tough grader and his personality can be hard to get by, but most of the difficulty comes from misconceptions.  He expects the best work from his students which is understandable since you're paying to take this class.  If you ask for help, it'll be there, but come to class prepared and with your work all ready and you should be fine.
SO unhelpful and rude

Besides being unable to lead an organized lecture, Urbance's condescending and rude personality made his class extremely difficult. It seems to me that he is on a serious power trip, which is unfortunate, because he has the potential to be a decent professor if he were actually down to earth and could deliver the material in a more coherent way.

This professor is HORRIBLE. No matter how much  you study it is guaranteed you will not do as well as you want or expect in this class. If you have questions, ask the TAs not him! He will think you are stupid so refrain from asking him questions at any point.
It's just a bio lab, so his involvement was minimal; however, what he has done during recitations has been pretty easy to understand, and he's been lenient for things like exams in other bio classes.
Great guy, great professor. Not too difficult and clearly presents info. Straightforward class, and the guy sounds like the dad in Finding Nemo to top it all off.
Not a very good teacher. Often times acts like a "know-it-all". He has no patience for people that aren't already geniuses in the subject he is teaching. Wouldn't take his class again.

If you are looking for a helpful professor who likes his job, Urbance is not who you want. He is grumpy and arrogant most of the time. He also makes you feel stupid if you make a mistake. The class is hard because his questions are not straight from the book, they are real world situations that you need to apply your very basic knowledge to.
His exams are extremely difficult. Good luck.

Urbance makes sport of people not able to understand material, talks about the test average of always being 61%, and lectures are disorganized, but have mandatory clicker questions. You could read the book and do the homework and still get a 75%. He refuses to curve.

I lost a bit of faith in MSU's ability to care for their student's success after taking this class. The exams were impossible but they were extremely difficult. His tests are indeed designed to trick you. Study hard and DO NOT CRAM. He expects you to "know" the material, not just have memorized the notes. Read the book and watch online lectures.

This class was pretty hard. He talks really fast and is disorganized during lecture so your notes aren't that helpful. most of his test questions were trick questions or over small details we never covered

Dr. Urbance was a horrible professor. If given the chance, take someone else. He always had an arrogant attitude and made the entire class feel stupid. His exams were unnecessarily hard and even though I studied for hours, I was only able to get above a 70 once.

When you come in on the first day of class and a professor says his exams are harder than anyone else who teaches the class, its just setting up for failure. He was often arrogant and pretentious. I encourage any future BS111 students to avoid his sections.

Dr. Urbance was extremely unhelpful and rude in his assesment of the classes ability to comprehend material. Condescending attitudes help no one learn and I would highly recommend you do not register for his section or switch as soon as possible. Exams are over subjects never covered in class.
I 4.0'ed a Microbio class the semester before this one. I failed this class. Ridiculously hard exams and expectations.

If you have the option, do not take BS 111 with him.  His exams  are really hard.  I studied a lot for them, and didn't get anything higher than a 64%.  The exam questions are over minute details that he wouldn't even talk about in class.  The majority of the class was failing for most of the semester.
Worst professor EVER!! Don't take him, whatever you do don't have Urbance!!! He had the highest number of kids fail BS111, in the history of the class! Save yourself...don't take his class
No Comments
Dr. Zhang was kind enough to write my letter of recommendation for medical school. The class was a little touhg, but very interesting. I would definitely class again if I could.

Dr. Zhang was nice, but her class was pretty disorganized. The platform for case studies was very inconvenient and hard to use. Many lab worksheets asked questions that we could not yet answer/did not learn, and the weekly quizzes were somewhat confusing. Your TA really makes or breaks this class. I highly recommend Christopher Prill, he's awesome!

This class is entirely dependent on who you get as a TA. I had Cameron and he was super amazing! Some of the quizzes are really confusing and the recitation portion of this class seems is just unnecessary busy work for more points. The actual lab is not bad and the TAs normally help with whatever you need.

CEM 255 is the most disorganized class on this campus. Students have no instruction and are simply made to figure out difficult organic chemistry procedures. TA's do not know what is going on either because she gives no guidance.The workload is incredibly insane for a 2 credit class. I would rather get hit by a CATA bus than take this class again.

I loved my TA that taught the lab portion, but I did not appreciate Dr. Zhang. You meet with her for the 1st 3 recitations and that's it. When I was confused about quizzes she gave little to poor feedback. The lab itself wasn't too bad, but make sure you don't miss lab or fall behind during lab. I had Parker as my TA and would highly recommend her

This class is mostly run by the TAs so it is somewhat dependent on who you get but the way that she laid the class out was great. The workload is not that heavy and overall it is pretty interesting material. She is very accessible but is not that involved in the day-to-day class.

I didn't really enjoy the weekly quizzes but the class itself was very fun! She works hard to make sure students enjoy what they're doing and learn. The TAs ran most of the class, but the way she organized the course was very nice.

Dr. Zhang really only runs weekly videos that have quizzes attached to them. In these videos, her accent is so crazy thick that it's hard to understand what she's saying. Then, in the attached quiz, there are questions that have nothing to do with the video, and one so far that was literally wrong. She refuses to fix any of these problems.
I didn't deal with professor Zhang very much because it was a TA who ran our lab session, but the labs were very easy and the workload was very manageable.

Do NOT take her unless you absolutely have no choice. She is the worst teacher I have had so far. Her class is confusing and videos do not align with what is being done in class. Not steps or procedures are provided and students have to figure it out themselves. She is unorganized, unfair, and is petty with her responses. She cannot take criticism

She is super interesting and knows a lot about physics (obviously). I would definitely recommend asking her all your weird physics questions as she seems to really like answering them. Try to avoid Tuesday-Thursday classes if you can though as they are pretty hard to get through, try to get a Monday-Wednesday-Friday class instead if you can.

This class is difficult within itself, but I do believe Dr. Sawtelle made the material a lot easier to understand. She genuinely cares for you and will do her best to help you succeed, making her office hours extremely available, and always present in class, engaging with all the students.

Prof. Sawtelle doesn't deserve these bad ratings. She is genuinely an awesome professor. I have no reason to glaze her; I am just saying the truth. She cares about you. She is great at office hours. Her exams were not easy, but that's cause Physics has a steep learning curve, but you can always do an exam reflection and get points back! Take her!

She is so kind, available, clear, and accommodating! She makes what is on the quizzes clear beforehand, so studying is easy! She has fun activities in class that are engaging, and waits for people's questions/writing during lecture. Her office hours are so flexible, and the class is so clear with expectations I never even needed office hours!

Graded by many things with a lot of extra credit, so the grading was easy. The class itself felt like high school and I was not a fan of the teaching style with group whiteboards to share out to the class. The entire class time is group work and the exams did not really reflect the exact material and questions covered.

Prof. Sawtelle made herself available in office hours, and occasionally took input from the students about how we would like to learn. She did care. However, this whole class felt harder than it had to be: lots of homework, disproportionately hard exams, and numerous incidents that left me way too stressed for a physics 1 class.

I can't hype enough. Dr. Sawtelle is one of the most dedicated, caring, and thoughtful professors in Lyman Briggs. The class and exams are hard, but Dr. Sawtelle is helpful and has set up the class in such a way that if you study and understand the in-class activities and labs you'll do well in the class and understand the material. Good MCAT prep!

Dr. Sawtelle knows what she's talking about, definitely. But, if you're not a physics person (as most people in Briggs are not), this class may not come easily to you. The exams are hard, and you may develop a false sense of security, since she tells you what each question will be. Study the material inside and out, it's the only way to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was really nice and caring. Class was not that difficult and became one of my favorite labs!

Dr. Viswanathan is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. You can tell it really matters to her that her students do well in class. She explains things well, and is very invested in her students' learning.

Dr.Viswanathan was clear in her expectations she has for students, the class, and the material. She was kind and was available for help for those who needed it. She was kind and would individually say goodbye when you left the lab. I would take this class again, it was fun and interesting too.

Dr. Viswanathan was so sweet and caring. Class is pretty easy to succeed in as long as you do well on quizzes and  2 lab reports. Super clear expectations/guidelines on lab activities, and you do a super fun semester-long project about oral microbiome. Recitations are underwhelming but you don't really need to be involved to succeed.

I loved this lab and Dr.P! She and the TA's are very sweet and supportive and grade very easily. Lab is actually fun and interactive while recitations are mostly I clicker questions and review for the upcoming lab.

I definitely enjoyed her as a professor. TAs were great and very attentive. However, a no absence policy with a 5% loss of grade if you are was steep. I overall thought there was a lot more work than a 1 credit class should be. In person recitation, lab, lab notebooks weekly, 2 projects, etc.

One of the sweetest profs you will have at MSU. Weekly homework quizzes based on instructional lab videos that are super easy. She made a point to introduce herself personally to everyone in my lab, and she is always available to students. I would 100% take a class with her again! She made learning fun & I retained a lot more than other courses.

Dr. Viswanathan is so sweet. I remember she personally introduced herself to everyone in my lab at the beginning of the year, which I felt like showed how much she cared about each individual person. She even asked everyone what they thought of the lab on the first day. Homework material is easy to understand and sets you up well for lab class.

Other than doing the labs, you just have to write reports and that's where a lot of your grade comes in. You're also graded on some microbio techniques in lab. Poorna is so nice and helpful!! I loved having her as a mentor and all the TAs are nice too. It's a well-guided class overall and not difficult to do well in.

Honestly this was my favorite professor at MSU so far. She is very knowledgeable/passionate about this subject and has written multiple books. She is easy to talk to and makes lectures engaging. Almost all of the class is spent taking notes, but I didn't mind. You have pop quizzes based on assigned readings but they're never hard if you did reading

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at MSU. The class is difficult, but isn't that the point of an upper-level course? Highly, highly recommend Dr Veit.
