reviews.comment: Terrible professor probably one of the worst I have had so far. Took this class without looking at his rating. Such a harsh grader for a university required class, just pick a different IAH and save yourself the trouble. Not worth it at all, does not know what he's doing and assigns a ridiculous amount of work. This class blew my 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever! Do not take his course, especially if you're just trying to fill a humanities requirement. He graded harshly, only handing out 100s if you went above and beyond the assignment requirements. Will take points off with no justification. Grading scale is crappy, with a 4.0 being a minimum of 94% overall. Group work was constant.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I had professor Ausin for SPN 440. It's not listed here so I wasn't able to choose it, but this professor is awful. The class was online asynchronous but with weekly check-ins. However, Prof Ausin felt so uninvolved and gave terrible feedback. Exams are all oral, and he gives only 18 minutes for 36-question quizzes. I felt set up for failure.

He only teaches in D2L through PowerPoints with audio. They're well made and interactive, but can be confusing sometimes. Any questions can be cleared up in class. There's always a preview quiz before the actual quiz, which was helpful to me. From my perspective with 4 years of Spanish experience, I thought his system worked fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For SPN310, lectures are online PowerPoints that are prerecorded and you are given four days to view them. There are two recitations on Wednesday and Friday with a TA and quizzes each week on D2l. This class was not bad, but just a lot of work for an intro class with almost no free time. The grading scale is also very tough (4.0=94+, 3.5=88+...)

All of the content from the course was self-taught from a powerpoint. It was very confusing for someone who is not an expert in English grammar. There is a LOT of work outside of class so beware. The exams are around 70 questions in 50 minutes so it's practically impossible. Also the threshold for a 4.0 is a 94%.

He is extremely uninvolved with the class. He does online, recorded lectures that are terrible. This is my 7th year taking Spanish, I received a 4 on the AP Spanish exam, so I already know the topics being taught. In my opinion, they're taught horribly. Along with that, the tests/quizzes set you up for failure with strange, unnecessary specifics.
His recorded lectures are fine, and the synchronous portions are taught by TA's which are good. You do not need the textbook imo, and the class is okay as long as you keep up with the work.

Taking this course online is pretty much impossible because you have to teach everything to yourself. I don't even have a good understanding of English grammar, so I don't know how I'm supposed to teach myself it in Spanish. the final was ridiculously hard with 72 questions in 50 minutes. I felt set up for failure.

Professor Ausin was great! I had him for IAH231C during COVID. He is super clear on his expectations, grading process, and is fair. The class has lots of reading but I wouldn't say it's too much. The material is actually interesting. I would highly recommend this class and professor. One of the better IAH/ISS classes I have taken at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I'm shocked Leah has a low rating. I took her for Grammar and she made everything so understandable and demonstrated expertise in the field that made me respect her as a teacher a lot. Her activities and assignments were fun and practical, and there was not a lot of homework at all (sometimes none in a week). I would recommend her for grammar.
This was the hardest online class I've ever had

LOTS OF WORK. Graded very hard, I feel like I never had enough to get 100 on anything even when I would put so much time into it. She is accessible outside of class very easily but EVERYTHING was opinion based and nothing really learned. I would shy away from this course.

Professor Addis was my lowest grade this semester. Probably the most homework I've had for a non major course with quizzes and annotations. Very opinion based grading but gave feedback to improve next time. Overall wasn't the worst but relieved to be done with the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not worth the trouble

Required gen ed but insanely hard. Wouldn't post lecture slides, recitations were brutal, assigned around 5 books, multiple midterms with 4–5 essay questions, plus random 30-second pop quizzes. Felt more like a grad seminar than a basic requirement. Way over the top and unnecessarily stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Would not take again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worst class I had at MSU
Never take this class
terrible experience
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Achebe is super passionate about this class and it's super interesting. If you don't show up to lectures you're screwed. TA's don't really know whats going on, but assignments weren't that bad as long as you follow the rubric and go to class. She gives you literally 30 seconds for pop quizzes and doesn't share her slides so take some notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super interesting lectures, Dr. Achebe is very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. She expects those who take her classes to learn a lot. Not a lot of assignments, but the assignments that do exist are big ones. Be prepared to read quite a bit and beware of random pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very invested in her classes and is very passionate about her classes, but do NOT take her if your class is online. There are constant pop quizzes that are not representative of the content of the course and they follow the format of in-person learning (i.e. 3 minutes to take and submit it). I'm sure it's great in person but online was bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is absolutely horrendous. TAs are not on the same page. The syllabus is not specific at all. They give pop quizzes and allot us only 1 minute. The syllabus is not specific at all. The teaching staff is extremely technologically challenged. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gives pop quizzes that are 60 seconds long, does not care about students grades. All she does is lecture with very few lecture slide: impossible to take notes. Projects are ridiculously long However she is very passionate about what she teaches and you will learn so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved IAH 205 with prof Achebe! She is one of the most passionate profs I've had and offers lots of extra credit. If you are willing to put in the work then the class is an easy A. She teaches from her experiences so if you don't go to lecture then you're out of luck. I'm hoping she will be teaching my ISS course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult class but great professor. Three extremely difficult papers and two blue book exams. Tough grader but very generous with extra credit. Random pop quizzes so gotta show up to class. I found that no matter how hard i worked on the papers my grade was always substandard, but the extra credit helped me earn a 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Went into this class thinking it would be super boring but it turned out being my favorite class that semester! Professor Achebe is very educated on the information presented and makes each lecture entertaining. Midterm and final questions are short answer and given beforehand! Very glad I took this course

Honestly, Achebe is probably the best professor for this course. She's so passionate about the topics that it's basically impossible to fall asleep. There's three big paper assignments throughout the entire course and six(?) pop quizzes so attendance is basically mandatory. Very hard grader though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is an amazing woman and the class an amazing course. She speaks with such dignity and strength and passion you're forced to be engaged. She teaches from her heart and has an immense amount of knowledge. The class wasn't too difficult, many projects and a lot of reading. The exams were pretty intense but weren't graded too harshly.

I respect her more than any professor Ive ever had. She is passionate and her work and life experiences are truly incredible. Ive gained love for Africa and my knowledge came from someone so close to it (shes from Nigeria). Perfect English and to the point. The projects are spread out and you get time. There is nothing wrong to say.

Not a bad class, but definitely a lot of work. Lectures aren't mandatory, but there are 5 random pop quizzes in class throughout the semester, so you kind of have to go. TAKE GOOD NOTES, you'll need it when studying for midterm and final. Mandatory recitation on Friday's, so hopefully you get a good TA. I had Janelle Edwards who was fantastic.

I also took her IAH 205 course, and totally loved her. She is passionate, brilliant, and by far  my all-time favorite professor. If you show up, do the reading, and actually participate you will do great. In her HST class we have deep discussion, amazing stories, and she promised to cook for us at the end of the semester. Take both classes!!

The class covers a very wide range of African topics including religious and traditional history, modern culture and economic system but the tests are Blue Book essay tests that ask 3 or 4 very specific questions and leave a lot of the lecture material irrelevant since the tests are not cumulative. And recitation is mandatory with group presenting.

This class is really hard. There is a lot of writting and high expectations. The exams are brutal, long essays, and map quizzes. She is very nice, funny, and passinate about what she's teaching. But sometimes too passinate, like yells into her microphone until it hurts your ears.
Excellent professor, very helpful, enjpoyed her class, learnt a lot!!!
Loved this Professor!! She seemed intimidating but when I went into her office hours she was completely down to earth and we ended up talking for two hours about non-class related things!!
Great teacher; Great clothes.  Passionate about what she teaches; cares about her students.  Hard class but you'll learn a lot

Excellent professor! She really knows her stuff. I would highy recommend any serious student to take hher class. She is one of the best professors they have in history and she is serious about her work! You will learn a great deal in her class, slackers need not apply!!

I had Dr. Acevedo last semester and she was definitely a favorite. She was very easy going, caring and the work was never anything stressful. If you face any sort of problem and just communicate she's almost always understanding. Little cornball but we love that for her :)
Beware to be accused of AI plagiarism if you are a competent writer. Beware.

This class wasn't well structured, and it wasn't all Acevedo's fault. She's very caring, kind, and energetic, but the class activities, assignments, and projects weren't the best in my opinion. Attendance is mandatory, but she's a flexible and caring professor.

Dr. Acevedo is kind and clearly cares about her students. The class is easy, with grades based only on four projects, including one group assignment. However, she often goes off on political rants and shares personal stories about past students that probably shouldn't be repeated. Different views don't feel welcomed or tolerated in her classroom.

Dr. Acevedo was extremely kind and always willing to read your essays and gives amazing feedback on what you should add or take away from your essay. Class is mandatory but she understands if something comes up. I would 100% recommend taking WRA 101 with her especially if you like to mess around. Dr Acevedo likes to keep things fun and is genuine!!

Talk about deranged. Denise had a political meltdown every other lecture. Always complaining about the administration has absolutely no respect for students who share other beliefs. Avoid her at all costs!

Love her!! It's clear she loves her job and adores her students — very flexible and willing to work with you. Highly recommend, her class was very educational while maintaining a fun, relaxed atmosphere :). Takes student feedback into consideration and actually applies it to her curricula. Highly recommend!
I absolutely loved WRA 101 with Dr. Acevedo. She cares about the success of all her students and goes above and beyond to help. Definitely one of my favorite professors at MSU.

A very nice person who cares for her students. An Hour and 50 minute lecture is way too long and it shows but a very easy grader and understanding as well. There are four projects and she gives you a lot of time to work on them. My only complaint is she isn't very clear with the projects and it's almost like she changes her mind mid way through.

Dr. Acevedo is the best. She truly cares about her students and thats reflected in her class. Assignments are easy and so is the grading but if you're stuck with a group that doesn't help then let her know and she'll try her best to help. Shes also absolutely hilarious and brought in ice cream for the class.
Taking WRA 101 with Dr. Acevedo was pretty easy. You have 4 projects throughout the semester and you get lots of time to do them. Some projects are with groups. I'd recommend taking WRA with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Acevedo is the only prof I've had that cares to get to know you. The 4 projects in this class are a little odd, but the reflective essay at the end of each one isn't hard. You definitely have to like writing to really enjoy this class tho. She talks about her own life a lot but is super funny so I like listening to her stories. Grades easy too.

Dr. Acevedo is a great professor who genuinely cares about her students and their success. The projects in this class are a little insane, but it makes it interesting. Highly recommend taking WRA 101 with her.

Prof. Acevedo is super easy to get along with, and is super fast with answering messages and questions about assignments. She's understanding and assignments are straight forward. The class isn't super hard but theres a lot of writing but she gives good feedback and will read papers before you turn them in if you ask.

Imagine every white narcissistic vain egotistical teacher you had in hs and amplify it ten times. Dr.Acevedo has no sense of her own classroom and the students in it because no one has ever walked out of her course having learned anything or smiled once. Please do not take wra with her because you will not enjoy one minute of your time

Dr. Acevedo is a really good person but her work is a little insane. This definitely wasn't treated like a 100 level course. This class did 4 different group projects and then after each project we wrote a reflective essay. So be prepared for writing a lot of essays. Her grading was pretty easy though, I got a 100% on all my essays.

The entire class is doing group projects which is a pain, and she overcomplicates things for no reason. I found her to be culturally ignorant with the latino culture as well it was quite uncomfortable. She was very nice, but if you missed a peer review she would automatically take off 30 points, and if she didn't like your peer review she dock.

I took IAH 231B with Dr. Acevedo online in the summer, and she is one of the best professors I have ever had. She actually reads and responds to each student, and her assignments are clear. You can tell she truly puts effort into her class. Would recommend :)

Absolutely loved her classes! I had her for WRA 101 as well as IAH 206 and received a 4.0 in both classes. She grades super easy, the only thing she asks of you is to attend class and participate in discussions. She is super sweet and very caring towards her students. Highly recommend taking any of her classes!
The best professor in WRA!!!
Best prof ever! Super sweet and cares about her students immensely.

That is very good professor in MSU
Best

Professor Acevedo is such a sweetheart. The best way to do well in her class is to show up in office hours a few days before a project is due, and she will honestly help you edit the entire paper as long as there isn't a line of people waiting. You will do well as long as you turn your discussion posts etc. in on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Due dates and assignment instructions are poorly formatted in a way that requires more work on your end than necessary to find them. Late work is not accepted for credit, no forgiveness if you mess up, even at the beginning. Class is listed as asynchronous yet we still had 5 required Zoom lectures. My grade did not reflect my effort at all.

I recommend her as a prof. I had her for WRA 1004 and WRA 101 and she was the best (I received an A in both courses). Participation matters in her class, but the assignments are not tough at all. She is very caring, understanding, and willing to help you out if you need it.

AWESOME professor. Class is relatively easy and she gives great feedback. Super friendly and available outside of class. I can't say enough good things about her honestly. Hearing "aha moment" all the time over the semester got kind of old but that's about the only complaint I have. I really enjoyed this class.

Dr. Acevedo is an amazing professor. She cares for her students as if they were own children. The class is beneficial as well. Participation is key to passing her class. If you need additional help, you can go to her office hours, give her a call, or just text her. I would definitely recommend to have her as a professor if you can.
One of my most favorite professors at MSU.

If you have the option to have Dr. Acevedo as a teacher, DO IT!! She's an amazing teacher! It is not hard to do well in that class if you do the reflections, go to class, and participate! Would 100% take another class with her!

I would recommend this professor to anyone and everyone. Dr. Acevedo is an AMAZING person and professor. Her class is enjoyable (as every class should be) and she keeps every lecture interesting and engaging. As long as you put forth your effort, participate and show up to class, you'll get a 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved WRA 150 with Dr. Acevedo! She's one of the only professors I've had that truly cares about their students. Participate in class, go to office hours if you need help, and if you have any questions ask!

The only professor I've had who actually seemed to give a damn about their students. She makes sure she gets to know you and you know her back. She's always there to help with whatever you need even if you're not in her class anymore. I really enjoyed her class because she makes sure you understand what to do and how to get the best grade possible.
She was sooo nice! LOVED HER! take war 150 with her! i got a 3.5 on most my essays. she was so easy and nice

Dr. Acevedo is one of the most caring educators that I have ever had in my entire educational career. She absolutely LOVES her students, and goes go out of her way to get to know them better. She is always encouraging students to come to her office hours or text/call if there is anything that they need, academically-related, or not. Very loving!

Genuinely the GOAT. I took him in-person for both EC201 and EC202 and he was great in both. His lectures are informative and easy to understand with funny examples. The homework is tough, but he lets you drop 3. Also, tests have easier questions than the homework, so if you do well on the homework, you'll succeed on the tests. Lastly, 89% is an 4.0
He is a d1 yapper. Also, the exams are more difficult than he leads them on to be. The exams ARE harder than the homework questions, despite what he says, but besides that, he's chill.

He does not allow his students to use calculators on his exams. If you know anything about economics, especially Macroeconomics, there are many calculations involved, and it seems unfair that you can't use a calculator on the exams when they have complex formulas. Other professors allow a caclulator so I suggest you take one of their courses.
Exams are tough, but Jeff is spectacular.

Professor Ackermann successfully (jokingly) catfished me into becoming an economics major. He actually made economics interesting and fun to learn, which in turn made me think the department was all like that. Boy was I wrong, almost every other Econ professor outside of him is monotone, boring, and old. I enjoyed Econ when I had him, now I don't.

I would say that this class is pretty doable as a freshman. He gives a lot of resources and I believe that the homework assignments (both completion and accuracy) and especially the study guides both give a lot of information to help when it comes to exams. This class demands a lot of effort though so make sure you're staying on track.

To succeed in this class I would review all my notes after the lecture and make my own sheet for each unit of all the really important concepts and definitions. I also constantly reviewed the homework's and practiced them as well as the practice problems and practice exams. If you study those a lot you will do good on the exams.

Very nice and funny guy. Really like his teaching and personality. In his class however, he didn't allow calculators or cheat sheets like every other professor. His 3.5 was also 4.0 in other classes. Despite him being a very good teacher, I'd rather have easier access to a 4. Recommendation is to choose a different one. Attendance is manditory.

Professor Ackerman is an incredible economics professor. If you pay attention in class, use the workbook, and actually study for the exams, you will have no problem succeeding. His comments in class are funny and do actually make sense if you are paying attention to the lecture.

Professor Ackerman was one of the BEST professors I have had at Michigan State. These comments saying this class is tough and he is a bad teacher, y'all do not know what college is. All of these comments saying this class was awful, you seriously have never taken an upper level class before.

do not skip the lectures or else you will know literally nothing. the exams are some of the hardest i've ever taken so stay on top of it. if you want a good grade you neeeedddd to do well on the tests.

Took this class online and had a great experience. The lectures are easy to understand and connect well to the homework. Provided practice problems/exams are extremely helpful and usually pop up on exams. One exam drops and the grading is more relaxed than most classes. As someone who has never taken econ I really enjoyed this class!
He is better than all the other econ professors, very difficult online and he is not very accessible. Grading is easier than most other classes.

Literally the funniest prof ever. Such an amazing guy and you can really tell that he cares abt the class and has passion for what he does. I was undecided before coming to college but after taking his class, made me want to pursue an econ degree. Funny lectures, 3 midterms and 1 final exam but only 3 exam grades count, really helpful study guides.

PROF. ACKERMAN'S CLASS WAS MY ABSOLUTE FAVORITE! I highly recommend taking his class if you are needing an Econ credit. He is super funny and his exams are respectable, considering the course criteria. The workload isn't heavy at all, and he truly wants to help students succeed.
test heavy (you get to drop one exam) so you have to do REALLY GOOD on at least one to get 4.0, this material and the horrible way he explains it gives me a headache every time I try and study

The exams are very difficult and the way Ackerman teaches the content is very difficult to understand. The exams are also a huge portion of the grade so if you do bad on them it will drop your grade significantly.

DO NOT take this class online. If you end up in it, get a good tutor to explain everything he doesn't. He gives workbook pages to follow along the videos with, which is nice, but they are vague. The actual exams are different from the practice ones, too. He also says to not reach out to him, which is strange to me, as he's literally the professor.

Its very hard to manage the workload while also trying to study and really understand the material. Ackerman is a nice guy! but the lecture topics aren't explained in a fully coherent way. It feels like every question on the exam has a double meaning and designed to trick you rather than test your knowledge.

He is one of my funniest professors, and is always energetic and excited to teach. However, you really need to do well on the exams to get a 4.0. Overall, fun guy to be around, and the class isn't terrible so long as you stay on top of things.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr. Ackerman is great! He always has a positive attitude and presents his lectures in an engaging manner. He provides very helpful guided notes for lectures and great resources for studying, especially for exams. Overall, this course is difficult, but he makes the workload manageable and definitely looks out for the student's best interest.
For the online class its tests and homework for correctness. Thats it. If you're not a good test taker, then don't bother.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I just thought it was kind of stupid that we couldnt use calculators or aa note card on the exam but in my micro class we could. idk the math is divison with big nubers and multiplication, just saves so much time when you get to use a calculator, and there are many formulas to memorize.

Don't take this class online, as a matter of fact, don't take this class if you don't have to. Its hard to figure out what to study for the finals because instead of a practice exam, there are practice questions on every single unit, like I'm not going through all those questions just for only half of them to be on the exam.

Ackermann is great, he just explains everything in very specific ways. If you take him I highly recommend you go out of your way to learn concepts in YouTube or any other way that will help you in specific!

Ackerman is a decent guy and can be entertaining, but I would not recommend taking EC 202 ONLINE. He did not keep up with posting the lecture videos and often left you hanging. Homework would often have mistakes as well. The class itself is easy, regardless, but the professor isn't the best. I would recommend it in person or not with him.

I loved learning about economics in high school. Unfortunately, this professor has now ruined the subject for me. He somehow found a way to make it a mundane, boring chore. It is extremely lecture-heavy, and I felt he explained things in an unnecessarily complicated manner. Ackerman is extremely inaccessible as well.

Typical tenure prof- all heavy lifting is done by graduate students and he doesn't even want you to email him with a question. He will say you can, but if you do he doesn't answer the question and instead directs you to contact the TAs...also has history of changing certain course cutoffs AFTER the last exam to make his "teaching" seem effective

For the online class he isn't bad you just have to actually watch the lectures and use the workbook pages to follow along. He updated almost all of his lectures so they're no longer just recordings from covid like some people said. That said, if you're a bad test taker don't take this class because they're 60% of your grade.

i took EC 201 with him asynchronously and got a 2.0, but i took EC 202 with him in person the following semester and got a 4.0. it'll suck going to class three days a week but if you want to succeed in his class i'd recommend the in person layout. his asynchronous course videos put me to sleep every night but his in person lectures kept me awake.

If youre someone that learns by teaching themselves the material you should be okay but he goes off on tangents a lot and uses lecture vids from 2020 that are to focus bc he talks so much about other things. If you can take an in person i would recommend it over this course!

Before you read. No I'm not going on a tangent because I was lazy or didn't pay attention bc I passed this class with flying colors . .However you can tell this class was structured heavily by graduate students. Insane amount of typos on the homework, lazy test questions, asynchronous students left with no chance of ec, poorly made packets.

Professor Ackermann is hands-down, the funniest professor I've ever had. My top highlight was when he asked an open-ended negative externality question on the worst thing your roommate has ever done. After submitting my response, my roommate chased me out of class which ultimately resulted in me finally being able to switch roommates.

super funny guy. enjoyed this class a lot, was a bit harder for me than my other classes and I would find myself confusing Micro and Macro a lot. Exams were simple if practice tests were done and you went to class. Final was at 8pm on a Thursday though, so that was a little irritating but great class altogether.

I took the class online asynchronous. It was fine all of the lectures are prerecorded from 2020/2021. Homework is pretty easy and the exams are fine too. Make sure you keep up everything because once you fall behind it's pretty hard to catch back up because every week there are 1 or 2 new units being taught.
This class was SUPER hard to me and prof ackerman lowkey taught things very confusing. I was online so maybe the in person was different.
In general, Ackermann is well-liked by most students. If you pay attention in class, complete all your assignments, and practice regularly, you'll be all set.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not hard at all just watch the video lectures and do the practice problems and the exams will be extremely easy as a lot of the questions are reused from the practice problems. Ackerman is a silly little guy also lots of lols to be had
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Emailed him instead of the TA because it was an urgent question and the TA can take a bit to reply. Instead of simply answering my question, he proceeded to type out a paragraph of why I should be going to the TA instead of him and did not answer my question at all. I think that's pretty petty. Also makes unfair changes to course cutoffs at the end

Do NOT take Econ with Ackerman, he was by far the worst professor I have had. He only grades by tests and homework, so not much room to improve grades, and they're both super difficult. I tried getting help from him outside of class and he told me to find friends in the class then, but it's an online class... Avoid this professor if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class online, but the lectures were very engaging where you really actually understand the material. Exams are locked down browser but if you study the practice problems it will be easy. He is a very nice professor!

Ackermann is a very funny and passionate professor. There is a textbook but you don't actually need it for the class at all so don't bother buying it. Attendance isn't mandatory either but the material can get confusing if you miss because he does to many examples in class.

worst lectures ever. so boring and dont help with the homework. quizzes are confusing and exams are hard. he is really bad at explaining things and preparing you. too many concepts he doesnt go in depth and just reads slides. don't recommend, but couldve just been that class was hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, he offers a dropped exam and there's very little work for this class. The lectures are actually enjoyable to watch too and he does a great job at explaining topics that aren't initially straightforward. Just a really nice guy overall.

Definitely don't recommend his class. Unfortunately he's the only EC 202 prof which is why I got stuck with him. His tests are very hard and there is lots of homework worksheets. Your only graded on those two things and the tests are heavily weighted. So if you do bad on the tests your grades gonna be low.

I took this course online and I shouldn't have. Powerpoints are confusing and super long. Homework is really easy, but doesn't prepare you for tests. Tests are only 30 questions and so hard. I don't think I would've passed any tests even if I had help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this course online and thought it would be easier than in person. I was wrong. The homework assignments are not that bad but the lectures are longer than an in person class. The exam questions are worded weirdly and not easy to understand. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. You are better off taking Econ 201 or Econ 202 at LCC for less money and better

Prof Ackerman was a pretty fair professor. He explained things clearly and stopped to answer questions when needed. He made lectures very interesting and really tried to connect with students individually. My main concern was with exams. Since there were only 30 questions per exam, there wasn't much room to make mistakes.

May be a friendly and fun professor but I find him to be quite an unprofessional and rude person. He has continuously been extremely uncommunicative and unsupportive on email and he seems to care more about following what is exactly in the syllabus then hearing what you have to say and at a min, recognizing it. DO NOT TAKE if comm matters to you.
Very funny, fun class, lectures were kept interesting through use of real life examples and his humor. Top 3 professors I've ever had.

You can tell that he genuinely loves teaching and tries to build a bond between him and his students. 60% of your grade is 4 exams (one dropped). He writes his own exams so you'll find that he often reuses the same questions he assigns homework give or take a few different numbers. He has helpful online lectures if you do miss class. I recommend.

Very entertaining professor. He used TopHat to incentivize coming to class (it's a small part of the grade). 70% of our grade was midterm and final, so be sure to understand the material -it's easy to stuff don't sweat it cause you will get practice with the problem sets and non-graded exam practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor that had light homework and easy to follow lectures. You need to show up to do well, if you do this class is extremely easy. Ackerman was enthusiastic about his material and wanted people to succeed, those who did poorly were those who did not attend lectures.

Lowkey don't take this class in person or online. He is not that funny. To be completely honest he doesn't explain things. Most of the students that I've taken this class have said that their exam scores did not reflect their actual knowledge in the class which is very concerning.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but his teaching is so bad. Most of the time he just reads off his PowerPoints word for word and doesn't explain. Homework assignments are graded by completion. Exams are heavily graded on and are way off from what the homework is.The study guides never match the exams.

Good guy. Can tell he really cares. Course is not that difficult you just have to be on top of things and you will succeed. It is very easy to get behind so if you procrastinate you should take the in-person version of the class.

I took the online version of this class and all the homework was due the day before tests. The homework is through an online program that recycles the same questions over and over again so they're easy to memorize the answers for. However, the homework is no help for the exams and if you want to do well you HAVE to do the practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: These other reviews must have cakewalk classes bc this was neither hard or easy. Textbook isn't required but you can find it online for free. Attendance isn't REQUIRED but you're still graded on it. 1 of 3 exams is dropped. It's not supposed to be easy. I showed up 50-75% of time and got a 3.5... A 4.0 IS ONLY 89+ do the practice problems and hw
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The asynchronous class for this was strictly video lectures and McGraw-Hill homework. Exams were most of the grades. Exams were also on lockdown browser.

This class is absolutely horrible. The tests combined are worth 75% of your grade. The exams, which he writes himself, are the hardest things. He says to look over the practice problems he provides you to study with, except they are so easy and the test questions are nothing like it. He is a nice guy, but I do not recommend his class.

The only downside of this course is that exams are worth 70% of your grade. Prof Ackerman is great, but there is a lot of material covered on each exam. As long as you pay attention during class and do all of the practice problems before the exams you'll be fine. I found this class very interesting as a non-econ major, and would recommend it.

All he gave us for lectures were his old recorded lectures from 2020. The homework assignments took hours to do and hardly had anything to do with the lectures. The exams make up 75% of your grade, were very difficult, and were not given enough time to complete.

Econ is not my major so take everything I say with a grain of salt. I thought that he cared about students, was pretty funny when it came to the overall class period, but there is not much to base your grade off. There were the exams and the homework's that were essentially quizzes, nothing else really determines your grade besides the exam.

Really hard to succeed in this class, not much accommodations made. Exams make up the majority of your grade. SO much material and really hard to understand. The concepts are applied to one example an then your supposed to just understand it. I struggled in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: you either love or hate Jeffery Ackerman, he does a great job of keeping students engaged by trying to be relatable or funny but it gets In the way of his teaching. I could tell you more about his kids and his love for Fortnite and Panera charged lemonade than I could tell you about what I learned in this class.
took online, lockdown browser and the lectures are so monotone it is hard to listen to. homework is easy but has almost no relevance to the exams.

The curriculum isn't necessarily easy, however, there are lots of resources that will help you succeed so long as you put the work in. The Econ help room, reading all of the chapters covered, watching lectures from his summer course, and doing as many practice problems as possible essentially ensures a 4.0. Ackermann is a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ackerman relied on lockdown browser and webcam for all exams, and they had mandatory time slots in which they would be taken. We took 2 exams and each exam had 7 or 8 chapters of content that were on it. His lectures posted on d2l could range from 10 minutes to over an hour. And you would have to watch 1-2 videos for each chapter.

Horrible. His lectures are boring and full of random facts about his family or pop culture references. Attendance is mandatory. Exams are so difficult, you will not pass if you don't do a significant amount of preparation. Cracked out on charged lemonade. Some say he's nice/ funny, I personally would never step foot into his lecture hall again.
funny guy, exams are difficult without studying & practice, uses iclicker for attendance, homework assignments were long but helpful to learn material, easy-ish class if you're determined enough

-lets you drop an exam and four homework assignments
-funny
-study and you will be fine
-not boring
-best econ prof

Horrible HW. For our class we had online homework through SIMnet. It was awful, the assignment would loop the same questions over and over, most assignments had around 300 questions, being the same 20 questions looped. A weeks worth of homework would take anywhere between 1-5 hours of completing the same 15 questions over and over again

Professor Ackermann is very mid at best. He tries to keep lectures relevant and up to date but the actual content is not very helpful for the class. I took him for EC 202 and exams are a huge part of the grade and very hard. Be prepared to spend countless hours doing online homework that is barely relevant to the actual class.

Funny dude, horrible professor. Lectures make no sense and just uses graphs that he only understands. Exam questions are near impossible and have nothing to do with anything we learn. The class did horrible, there is not much homework and he is a nice, laid back guy but if you truly want a good grade avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ackerman is a great professor! It's a hard class but he conveys the information well and gives lots of practice problems to help you do well. It is lecture heavy, but he uses lots of examples that make it easier to understand.
He's fine. Not the worst but not the best.

Provides lecture playlist that covers the same material as classes, so attending is optional. Online homework textbook is a mess but it is easy to get full points and he gives a few homework drops. Exam content comes from lectures, not the textbook.

This is one of the worst classes I’ve ever taken. The exam questions are nothing you can prepare for and his lectures don’t teach you anything. I showed up to class everyday, did my homework, took notes, studied and still did horrible along with other people. I’m not one to fail classes but this may be my first.
Lectures made graded material easy. I recommend the work book and really thinking about and doing the work he offers. it makes the exams much easier.

VERY DIFFICULT EXAMS that are monitored and not open note. He is so boring! The class did really bad. Do not take him. He doesnt care about the students. His lectures are too long and he doesnt clean them up when he messes up. Expect bad grades.

Jeff is the man. He makes econ as best as it could be. The course has a decent amount of homework which is much harder than the exams, so they are good preparation if you actually do them. The lectures are great, and Jeff makes an effort to know you. The lectures are perfectly paced, as he will wait a little bit after each slide for typing.

This guy is the man. One of my favorite professors at MSU. I struggle deeply with math and, by extension, Economics and Ackerman made it pretty accessible and understandable to me. He is an easy grader but is still effective in getting his material across. Plus he is a genuinely enjoyable person with a good sense of humor.

Not the best communicator. A lot of people did not finish a group of 4 assignments and he refused to give credit back partially because of the system he uses, and partially because he thinks he's not in the wrong.

Very very lecture heavy, most of the grades come from tests. Didn't offer any extra-credit opportunities, doesn't curve grades. He's pretty nice and fun during lectures, talks about his experiences, and shares any stories he has. However, he isn't that interested in getting to know students (probably because it's a super big class).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such an awesome professor! He teaches material in a very easy to understand manner and has immaculate online lectures. He makes the class stress free by relating to his students and giving life advice. I learned a ton about econ.

I'm not even an econ major and I took a second econ class so I could have this dude as prof again. The homework is super easy and it teaches you everything you need for the test so you really don't have to study much more. Jeff knows his memes and got a victory royale over the summer so he's a man of many talents.

Professor Ackerman is a really nice and accommodating instructor. His class isn't bad as long as you do the practice questions and look over Top Hat questions before the exam. People who do not take tests very well might struggle a little more. The homework is relatively easy as long as you give it some effort.

Ackerman is caring and quirky! Great human being. One of the things I wish I did more of during the semester would be to go to his office hours and dedicate more time to studying. I will say if you are NOT a good test taker like myself, you might not want to take his class. Your results from your exams and test will be your entire overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ackerman is a great guy- very nice and approachable. 75% of your grade in this class is made up of two exams. There are three total exams but he lets you drop one. The exams are very difficult. Overall, it is easy to earn points outside of the exams with the homework and in-class tophat questions, but it doesn't make up a huge part of your grade.

Spends a lot of time during lectures talking about his personal life. Also uses way to many examples to explain concepts, and often we fall behind. He also gets stumped easily by questions in class which makes me think he isn't very knowledgeable about the material.

Absolutely loved him, he's very nice and helpful. He will stop lecture and explain everything if you missed something, and if you get a chance to talk to him after/outside of class, he is super helpful and very nice. Would definitely recommend and if I could, I would have him teach all of my math courses!

Not the best professor you can have for Calc 3, but he is very good, thoroughly explains the content and goes step by step to complete complex problems. If you go to his lectures without fail and understand the concepts, you're gonna succeed in his class.
Little cousin jokes made learning calc 2 bearable

Similar to the majority of my peers, I quickly stopped attending Calculus II lectures. Instead I watched the videos/self taught. His accent, handwriting, and lecture pacing made in person lectures difficult to comprehend. Quizzes are weekly and can be difficult. MTH 133 is a rigorous course, the average final exam grade this semester was a 43% GLHF

If you don't watch the video lectures ahead of class (which I don't recall ever being told to do, I just did it because I was super lost) then the in-person lecture is useless because he does a lot of proofs. Just do the homework and you're fine.

Nice guy, makes jokes in class. I can see why some wouldn't like his fast-paced lectures, but I found them helpful because he then had time for lots of example problems. Lectures are not required and there are videos of it on D2L.

A lot of people complain about his lectures but I actually found them very useful and digestible. I understand peoples' complaints but his lecture style reflects "different strokes for different folks." He goes through the theorems and concepts very quickly, but he provides many examples after which I find more helpful. Take notes and go to lecture
All I can say is, meh.

I love Abbas, his lectures are thorough and well explained. Even if you don't like his lectures, you can always not attend lectures and instead watch videos on D2L from professor Maccombs, who is also an amazing professor. Overall the class is difficult but you have many options on how you want to approach the material.

Very bad lectures that would be a waste of my time. I never learned anything from him and had to spend many hours trying to learn to succeed in this class. Not helpful at all though he makes funny jokes.

Nice guy, but his lectures move way too fast to take notes on, much less understand. We had only three 50 minute sessions a week and yet he would speed through his notes and let us out 5-10 minutes early despite the intensity and volume of the material. I found Calc III to be easier than Calc II but I would not recommend taking it with Prof. Abbas.
The professor himself is fine. Nice, explains things well, and is very approachable. However, the class itself is just hard. No other way around it.

Great guy who cares and knows what he's talking about but has so flaws in his lectures. He can be fast with his notes and has a lot of words/explanations/theorems. Other than that, I can't blame the guy, the class is hard in general. The quizzes and exams have T/F questions that would screw me over. 100% on the written part but 60% at the end.

He was such a nice professor, and would answer any questions you brought to him, but about half way through the semester, his lectures didn't make sense. He didn't explain much to us, he just re wrote his notes for us to copy down. We normally did a couple example problems in class, but he didn't explain the steps he just did them.
Horrible Handwriting, would leave lectures without understanding anything, he proceeds really fast and its hard to grasp all the topics hes teaching

He will consistently bring up thought-provoking philosophical questions such as why people so universally conform to silly naming conventions such as "u substitution" and "p-series."  He realizes not all students will need to use Calc II in life.  So, he gives them philosophical wisdom instead.  This is what sets his lectures apart Ryan's videos.

Casim is just a huge meme between me and my friends. With his little jokes about the Stone Age to the caveman method, he got funny little jokes. He lectures quite well but his handwriting is not very easy to read at all. As a professor in any other class I would take him again, but as the professor for Calc 2 again, it depends on how you learn.
Not Casim's fault, but this class was super hard. He made the lectures almost enjoyable to attend. Ask questions, do the homework, and put in the time and you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy, so incredibly funny. His lectures were clear and useful for WebWork. Just make sure you go to recitation and take the quizzes. The exams are not bad if you study using the old exams that they provide. 10/10 recommend this guy, he's a gem

What a guy. Abbas is a German genius mathematician with a slick accent. He's always cracking little jokes, bringing a little light to a very dull and stale topic. The class is stone cold. But that's not gonna change with a different prof. Plus lectures aren't mandatory because he posts his notes online. Go to recitation for the quizzes.

I love Abbas with all my heart! Having him as a prof is like having a genius grandpa teach you math; super approachable &clearly cares for students. Explains ideas well&can offer alternative explanations. Writes down everything he says and posts online; this can be annoying in class but makes it easy to miss class, but don't skip- he's super funny!
Loved the guy. Interesting despite the topic and always cracks jokes. Easy grader and throws a huge curve at the end of the semester.
It's not an easy class, but he definitely helps. The homework problems are very similar to those on the quizzes and tests.
I love this guy, really cool!

Funny guy, really smart.  If you're naturally good at math this class won't be too bad.  I would avoid skipping as he covers about a section a lecture.  Homework is tough, but the quizzes and exams are quite easy.

Sharp guy, expects a lot from his students--sometimes I think he confuses us with his grad students. He doesn't always work out solutions to the homework problems before he assigns them, which can turn into long and grueling homework sessions. Homework took roughly ten hours a week, often more. However, it was definitely worth being in his class.
Homework due twice a week- very hard. Tests (2 exams and a final) were easier than the homework. Quizzes once a week. Difficult class, but some interesting proofs. Funny guy
This professor was terrible.
The class was hard, but not beyond what someone in an Honors math class should be able to manage. He gave up his own time for a problem session, and was helpful with office hours. Highly recommended

Very very difficult, even for an honors course. Not impossible though: a good challenge for someone looking to do well in a math career. He explains well, but the material can be so murky that it is still takes time to sift through. Gave up his own time to give us an unofficial recitation session: I highly recommend him.
Great teacher, commited to helping students understand Calculus and do well in the class.
excellent communications ability
hes hilarious, i liked the lectures
He's a really good professor and does a lot of examples to help you understand.  I would definitely recommend him.
Abbas is the****.
I like him because I understand him when he teaches me in class.
Abbas is hilarious!!!
He's not a great prof, but he's a damn genius and he's really funny.
Don't take this class unless you want to enter hell

The lectures are hard to understand and terribly organized. The quizzes are extremely confusing, but exams are better because the TA's write them. There is no homework, only quizzes and exams. The class is unnecessarily difficult and stressful.

The entire course grade is based on quizzes and two exams. It's unrealistic what you're expected to memorize. You don't get missed quiz answers back to study. The lectures teach you nothing you'll have to do most of the learning on your own. The syllabus states 1% per absence will be deducted from your final grade. Don't take unless you have to.

Much more tolerable than co-professor. Would have had much fewer issues with this class if she had taught more of the lectures. Actually graded assignments as if we were college students, rather than individuals with Ph.D's- gave clear grading criteria. Overall a caring professor; however, course lacked a central theme which overall made difficult.

Made this class tolerable for me. Much better communicator, and much better at working through content with students, than Professor Craig. Easier grader, with much better communicated expectations on the work she graded.
Very nice, caring, and a great grader with gives amazing feedback on papers.

Being only an assistant prof. she sure does the bulk of the work for this class. She's very caring and wants you to do well. Makes things easy to understand and how they grade things(even though it is EXTREMELY hard for an intro course). It is guest prof. lectures with short exam responses. She is the reason I let alone passed this, main prof. bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The main professor for this class Dr. Craig is terrible. She does the majority of the work for being an assistant professor, genuinely cares about her students and their grades. super super easy to reach and always very kind and helpful.

Dr. Bennett was great in FW181! She was very easy to contact and schedule meetings with if you were confused on the content, and helped me get a great grade on my final paper and gave awesome feedback! She is one of the best teachers I've ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is based on 4 exams, attendance, and one discussion you lead. There are no study guides, so it's hard to know what to focus on. Readings range from 3–45 pages each class. Attendance is mandatory unless you let him know days before. Exams determine your grade, and a 93% is needed for a 4.0. Wouldn't recommend unless required.

The points are unevenly distributed, no homework, graded on 4 tests(400 points), 1 presentation(30 points) and attendance(70 points). Required to read a 20-30 page article for every class and the only study materials provided are his notes. You can't take notes during most of class since it's lead by students and activity based. It's not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The points of this class are so skewed. 400/500 points are based on exams, all of which are extremely difficult and require you to basically memorize 40-page readings. He is extremely stingy with the points. There are no study guides, learning objectives, or practice exams for the 4 in-class exams throughout the semester. Every class is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gave easy weekly quizzes, three take-home essay exams, and a group project. He gave good feedback on everything, but it was hard to get a 4.0 in the class. I missed it by a few points. He's very accommodating, and caring toward his students. One of the best choices available for a Briggs HPS class.

This professor genuinely wants his students to succeed. His passion for the material makes lectures engaging, and I found his class to be one of my favorites. I would absolutely recommend this professor to others.

Easily one of my favorite professors at msu. You can tell he really cares about his students and will do everything in his power to help us. Rubrics and study guides are straight forward. He goes through every students paper and gives great feedback so you get the best grade possible. However, there are a ton a readings. Overall, great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor I've had at MSU. Genuinely cares about students + their learning, and class is structured thoughtfully. Exams are easy when you study, and Ron will do absolutely everything in his power to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ron was my fave professor this semester!! He set up the lectures and class so well, and I found it really easy to understand. It really felt like he was setting us up for success in the class. If you had any questions he was very helpful. Def take 333 with him if you have the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ron is one of my favorite professors. He is very passionate about what he teaches and is also a very kind and understanding professor. While there are exams and a paper, he gives very good lectures, study guides, and feedback on the essay, which allows you to get the best grade possible in the class. He also cares about his students a lot.

10000/10 class. I loved how this class was more of a collaborative effort rather than the traditional lecture type. There aren't any huge assignments. Optional weekly quizzes, attendance is mandatory, and lectures are fun! You work with a group for about half of the semester, get to know them, and even take the open note final exam with them.

Dr. McKim was a wonderful professor. You can tell that he's really passionate about his students and wants all of us to succeed. I would definitely take him in another class, and I recommend others take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Work with the same group throughout the semester. Every lecture has a game to help teach the topics, which I thought were fun. Easy exams, open note.

An absolutely amazing professor, passionate about what he does and talks to you like peers, rather than students. Such a manageable workload, all exams are open notes. Extremely understanding and easy to reach. Could not recommend more.
This professor was amazing, I absolutely loved his lectures. From this class you learn a lot about communication and how to be a good leader.

Professor McKim is one of the best CSUS professors I have had.  He truly cares about the students and his lectures are incredibly engaging and fun.  I looked forward to going to class and I wish I could take his class again.  There is not a lot of homework and the course is very manageable.

Professor McKim has been one of the best professors I have had at this school. He is so caring and kind to his students. His lectures are fun and engaging and he wants everyone to succeed. I would have him as a professor a million times again.

Literally the best prof I've ever had at MSU, and I'm not even a community sustainability major. He cares for his students, their success, and has the most engaging lectures I've ever had in school. I wish I could take again for him

I LOVED HAVING CLASS WITH THIS MAN!!! He literally made working out fun twice a week, SUCH a nice guy, I have no idea what all these ratings are, literally the kindest guy. There are 2 "practials" or "exams" where you have to show skills, but he will literally make you do it till you get it, and you will pass. Couldn't recommend enough.

He is very kind and supportive, always respecting the boundaries between student and teacher while still looking out for his students' well-being and safety. Joined the Taekwondo club just because his class was so much fun, and he created a very welcoming environment. I am still there to this day, even a year later!
He is 1st in the world in taekwondo
I absolutely loved this class and Southwick is a great instructor. The class is one that you have to work at, but it's worth it, and he makes it fun. Highly recommended.

Whoever is posting all these bad comments must be smoking something!  This is probably the most fun college classes I've taken.  Ron is a great professor and he treats everyone with respect.  He is aware of everyones abilities and he works with everyone on their own level.  Great class!
Ron Southwick is the kind of instructor that gives martial arts a bad name.  He disgraces MSU and their athletic department.
What did the martial arts do to deserve this?
Offensive, arrogant instructors with chips on their shoulders make this a horrible experience for all.
Best class ever! Great professor!
It's obvious this class is not something the instructors want to be doing.  There's an undercurrent of apathy and a tendency to have something going on for which most of the class remains lost.
Amazing guy!! Great teacher!!
Ron is a very knowledgeable and experienced teacher, who generally knows what he is doing
Terrible instructor.  Avoid at all costs.  Plays favorites and ruins it for everyone but his close buddies.
Tae Kwon Do deserves better than this.  Much better.
Nothing to be learned here because the instructor is always absent.  Even when he's there it's still no good.
Bad teacher.  There are many martial arts clubs and classes at MSU that treat students with respect.  This is not one of them.  Avoid this class!

I can't believe this is even a for-credit class.  It's more like a social event for instructors, in which they either don't show for class, or, give instruction to lower level belts who are inadequate instructors and simply don't care.
Great Guy!!!
The worst part of this class is the instruction.  Besides playing favorites, and a bad attitudes, the instructor is self-absorbed and everything is about him.
He doesn't even show up for most classes.  Let's his assistants teach.  Seems unfocused, burnt out on tae kwon do, and wants to be somewhere else.
No Comments
No Comments
Ron Southwick is a horrible instructor and should be avoided at all costs.  He is unfit to teach something such as the martial arts.

Ron is an excellant instructor, and overall nice guy.  He makes sure everyone understands, and is very considerate of people's different levels of physical ability.  I really enjoyed learning taekwondo with Ron, and will continue in the future.
The best out there!
Not a good instructor.  Plays favorites and is intense.
He was funny and understanding.  Show and participate for the 4.0

Seems like a nice guy, but for such a material heavy class, there is not enough effort put in. Exams are worth 25% of grade as well as research which is annoying. Also, DO NOT take at the same time as COM275 because you will have to do so much extra work
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice guy but if I am being honest he is bad teacher. Every lecture is him just reading off of slides which is fine for the first exam but when the math starts coming into play and it seems like he wouldn't even get a good grade on this final exam. When I reach out for help I either get no response or a generic "Talk to your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely worst professor I have had in class. There are three exams and like five random in person assignments that happen at the end of the year. The exams are entirely based on lectures which he does not post. He is absolutely no help outside of the classroom. Exams are extremely difficult even if you attend every lecture. Would not reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
For a class that has 75% of the final grade dedicated to your exam performance, you'd think there would be more material to actually practice for it.
The professor himself is nice, but asks WAY too much of his students.
(Depending on your major or minor, you could substitute something like STT 200 [much easier] for this class - ask your advisor.)
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ron is a great guy but probably the worst teacher I have ever had. You could know the material and study a lot and still not know the answers to the exams. In a class where exams are 75% of the grade he as a teacher seems to take pride in making his exams hard and his questions confusingly worded with multiple correct answers. Take someone else!

Ron is a great guy. He's funny, he's engaging in his lectures, and is clearly passionate about his teaching career. However, his exam's are near impossible. The answers are so incredibly similar that it will make your head spin, yes physically spin. The exams are worth 75% of your grade so each one feels like stepping onto a battlefield. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tamborini is passionate about the subject, but the class was tough. Exams are 75% of your grade and mostly (points-wise) short-answer, making them difficult. Weekly case studies are meticulously graded and don't help much. Lectures are hard to follow and don't clearly connect to assignments.

Tamborini is one of the sweetest and most caring professors I've ever had. He is knowledgable and passionate about mass communication and his lectures are packed but entertaining. He does talk a lot but the content is interesting and makes it better. LOVES his wife, HATES UMich, and always cracks dad jokes with us.

My fav professor by FAR. sweetest man you will ever meet and an amazing, clear, professor. I have 0 clue why he has any bad reviews. the class has 0 hw, and the exams are not that hard as long as you study a quizlet and look at the study guide. entertaining lectures and does not take attendance, yet somehow everyone shows up. LOVES his wife,10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is great as a person, but when it comes to the class itself be careful. Attendance isnt necessary but there are 5 pop up papers at the end of the class scattered through the semester that count as a grade. The exams are a lot of information. If you need to take this class and its your only option, do it, but if you have other options, do that.

Worst professor I have ever had. So lecture heavy he doenst post the slides which are from the 1900s btw talks like an ice age character and goes through them so quick without enough time to write everything down. No homework basically your entire grade is based off of exams with the exception of the random in class participation papers. stay away.

Professor Tamborini is a very nice guy, his lectures are boring and his class is super exam heavy. 80% of your grade is how you do on the exams and the exams are difficult, he references back to lectures on your test so attend the lectures. Also BEWARE of pop quiz writing exerts at the end of classes to count towards your attendance grade.

He is very nice but he does give out random in class papers throughout the semester and he will have you do his research projects as apart of your grade but there options to get out of it. Also attendance isn't mandatory but the lectures aren't posted at a later time

Hands down one of the most caring professors at MSU. Attendance is taken through random small writing assignments. His slides are not on D2L so attending lecture is important. He cares about his students and teaches exactly what is on the exam. Textbook is (not) required but the lectures are from the book. Would totally have a class with him again!

Tamborini is cool. Simple lectures that are helpful (he tells you what will be on the exam). Just take notes and you'll be set. This course does require in-person research participation done outside of class on 5 separate occasions which is a little annoying but it is very easy, and worth a large chunk of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tamborini is really pleasant, and his lectures were very clear and didn't have any useless information. The assignments were really reasonable, and the exams were really doable if you attended lectures and took good notes. I would absolutely take more classes from him.

I loved Dr. Tamborini! He's great at lecturing I never read the book except for skimming through it while studying for the exams. If you show up to the lectures and take notes, you'll be fine. I'd suggest making friends in the class to get notes from if you have to miss. Study for exams and you'll be fine. Sign up for research ASAP they're easy.

you HAVE to attend class. attendance isnt graded, but you will find everything very difficult if you skip. the three exams count for 75% of the grade. grading was very lenient. there is a stats section in the final third of the class, beware. had to teach myself all of that.

Tamborini is quite the professor. The class itself is complex and the way he teaches it doesn't really help. He tries his best though. The case studies and individual research assignments are graded very harshly and you have to participate in research studies. He is an interesting guy but the course was just straight up confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good professor but you need to show up to class, he doesn't post the slides and he gives surprise papers that's worth a good part of the grade. also required to participate in research.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor gave very few things for a grade and the majority of your grades were exams. He gives no extra credit opportunity and does not curve or round at all. The textbook is definitely used as well as online readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In this course there is very few things that count for a grade. The main thing is the three exams you must take in person. He talks extremely fast and does not offer PowerPoints so you have to come to class to take notes but it is hard to take notes when the class moves that fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 75% of this class was 3 exams. Very hard to listen in class when he rushes through loads of slides that he does not post online. Cannot miss class because you will miss a lot and he gives surprise end of class assignments from time to time. Exams also have a lot of information that you have to study. Good guy, not my fav class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ron's class wasn't too difficult, but could've been a lot easier. He doesn't post his slideshows, so you spend most class sessions writing down everything as quickly as you can, which really stood in the way of actually listening to him. You can tell he loves what he teaches as he is incredibly informational.

Professor Tamborini is a fun, great guy. However, I found it difficult to do good in this class because 1) If you miss one lecture, there is no way to access notes unless you know someone that takes notes 2) Your grade is pretty much only based on closed note exams 3) It's hard to fulfill the research requirement b/c if you miss one, you're SOL
His class was great!! Easy enough and he was engaging which helped a lot.
You need to attend this class or else you will not do well. If you just go to the lectures and it won't be hard at all
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally struggled a good bit in this class. The weekly case studies consumed a great bit of my time, but I learned next to nothing from them.  Also, be prepared for 3/4 of your grade to come from 3 large exams.  I wouldn't recommend this class unless it is a requirement for your degree.  It is one of the hardest classes I've taken at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Make sure to go to lectures, that is how he takes attendance
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was such a good professor, cared about student success and was sarcastic and funny to lighten to heavy lectures. It was a really lecture heavy class, but he did a great job covering the content and giving the information needed to be successful on tests. Participation is necessary because there are random writing assignments.
Take notes, and attend class, do the research and short paper. Make the effort to go to class, and you will succeed.

Very detailed in his lectures.  Explains the why's behind the formulas which helped me learn efficiently.  This is a study-intensive course.  I took it in the summer so it was condensed to a six-week session.  If you really want to learn this curriculum, I highly recommend Professor Tamborini for this course!  5 STAR!

Tony Mandarich

Terrible class and teachers. You are given #'s of lectures with an insane amount of content to memorize for THREE EXAMS for the whole semester and small assignments that do nothing to your grade. No open notes and Tamborini does not care about student success. The TA doesn't help either so the whole class is a joke. DO NOT TAKE THIS IF YOU CAN.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am a comm major, meaning I have to do well in this class. The professor truly cares about his lectures and you can tell he has a great interest in the subject, but the exams will kill you. The only points are 3 major exams and some other stuff, but mainly exams. They are all "As discussed in class..." questions - very hard to remember every word
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I do not recommend taking this class. He does not care about his students and does not want to see you succeed. Lots of lecture videos and 3 big exams. Be careful. Avoid this class and professor if you can.

The way this class was structured was not fun. The lectures aren't super easy to follow, the TA's are really the only reason I ever understood anything at all in this class. The professor seemed nice enough although it was an asynchronous class. If you don't put a lot of effort into this class, you'll probably fail or barely pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: While this class is lecture heavy, Professor Tamborini puts a lot of effort into this course and his lectures. He is organized and someone I would recommend. You do have to try in this class to receive a good grade, but if you put the effort in, you'll do good. Overall, I like him as a professor!

Professor Tamborini is a great teacher. You can tell he truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He was very accommodating during COVID. He gives great examples in his lectures, though the topics are a bit boring at times. If you take good notes you will get an A no problem.

All of the information in the lectures is important to the exam. Tamborini tries to be fun and engaging, lots of dad humor is involved. Exams are hard if you don't study, sometimes can be helpful to read the book if you want an additional review. If you study your notes and make flashcards you should be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: COM 275 with Dr. Tamborini was fine. I didn't really enjoy the class, but I'm not a COM major. I don't think I learned much and I didn't do great in the class, but Dr. Tamborini is pretty nice. Your grade is pretty much only dependent on exams, plus a few points for participating In research and showing up for class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Tamborini is a great lecturer. He keeps you entertained and if you pay attention, all the answers are right in front of you. If you don't show up to class you will not pass. He does not post his lectures or powerpoints so you need to be there. Research participation is a big part of your grade. Show up, pay attention, pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Tamborini is a good professor. His lectures are interesting and the course load is reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.
