Tough grader too as many massive projects usually aren't "up to her standards" even when they take weeks to finish.

You will learn a lot in this class, but she is a difficult prof. Very lengthy labs and projects that are graded harshly. Be prepared to be busy with the projects and memorizing every little detail for the exams.

For a 3 credit class, the amount of required work felt like a 5 credit class. We had to do labs that were supposed to be done outside of class time with little-no instruction. A lot of the time we got points marked off for things that weren't in the instructions or the rubric. Exams were also very difficult.

This professor was nice and I like her as a person, but I would not recommend this class. I got an A in the class but not without a struggle. Way too many group projects (especially right before exams) and tough grading. And the exams contained material that we barely glossed over. The work isn't too difficult, but there's a LOT of it.

Very few grades. Lectures are good but difficult to retain since projects and readings are only adjacent to lecture materials that are given once and then not seen until the midterm and exam. Assignments are good, but the grading style and course lay out need to be changed as it doesn't fit the conceptual discussion-based course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Burrow is nice and has a lot of good knowledge but dear god, the group projects were ridiculous. We had four group projects before the midterm alone and she's still assigning more. Beware, the group projects will make you regret taking this class. Only a bit of the subject material was science-based and the rest was often politically biased.

I'd like to start with the fact that this professor is so unorganized that I felt like I was in a maze for 24 hrs trying to find one simple assignment. She graded our group assignment COMPLETELY unfairly to my teammates. I mean, she might be nice in person, I can't speak on that, but never take an online class by this professor, I am begging you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There was a lot to read, as I was in the section about creativity. Weekly notecards are due, about the articles. She is pretty unclear at first but eventually posted what she was looking for in the notecards and I was getting 4/4s every time. In class there was lots of group work and discussions, that honestly were pretty boring. Easy 4.0.

she will not respond to emails but she is a nice lady and cares about your success she does take a while to grade things and did not give feedback when points were marked off going to class was only important when it involved assignments (index cards)or projects, besides that it was pointless it was a okay class but i would not take it again

I once heard someone say, "This class takes 6 years off my life," and I've never heard a truer statement. She is so unorganized, I don't think she understands half of the things she says, and a lot of her takes were ridiculous. Her grading never makes sense, and when you ask her about it, she won't give you a clear answer as to why
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Only in person once a week, the rest you are online. Grades are very easy, I had her for IAH206.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was asynchronous yet we still had group projects even though we didn't have zoom meetings. She would take off points on every assignment without saying why. Didn't respond to any of my emails the entire semester, even when my group mate wasn't doing the work and we had to do it for them. Don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I didn't know what to expect, considering I chose this course kind of last minute, but I truly enjoyed having her as a professor. Although she may come off as a tough grader, she is very understanding, just to-the-point. Just try your best to get to know her and how YOU learn as a student, and try not to fall behind on the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a very nice and great professor overall. Although, gives a crazy amount of work for a pre-requisite. Constantly having to do something its literally just an unnecessary amount of work and is a bit of a tough grader. She's helpful and nice though.

Overall she teaches through discussions within the classes about material she provides, as well as projects and papers. She actively works with the students to create projects that will benefit us. Overall, she is a caring professor who will talk during office hours or after class about any deep discussion or questions about the topic.

I found the class discussions very interesting. Dr. Atabay really changed my perspective and I think she is a very intelligent person. I had many great conversations with her in her office hours and she truly cares about your feelings and life outside of school. The class itself does require quite a bit of reading but it does spark for good convo.

Dr. Atabay was probably one of my favorite professors. She is incredibly intelligent and carries herself in that way as well. I've had discussions with her about the material that she teaches and I found them extremely valuable.

the amount of work this class requires every week should be criminal. Most of the people taking this class are full-time students, and a good amount of those people have jobs. Personally, I work 30 Ish hours a week and have the load of a full-time student. This class essentially requires about 10-15 hours a week. there are 10+ reading per-week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Atabay a lot. She said, "Remember it's my job to expose you to as many perspectives as possible. So you might think you're agreeing or disagreeing with me, but you're not." I think that sums her up really well. If you're willing to work hard and keep an open mind, you'll learn a lot from her, even if she sucks at responding to emails.
Class wasn't horrible, but only a few assignments. Make sure to work with your group to do well as there is a lot of group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While this class is not too difficult, I found it poorly organized. I emailed the professor several times over the semester, and she did not ever respond back to me. I had to go to office hours just to clarify things that I had sent over email. The class is long and can get boring, and there is a lot of group work. I appreciate the lack of exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took the asynchronous class due to my busy nursing schedule. This class is okay if you just keep your head down and turn in your work on time. There are no lectures. Just readings that you have to analyze throughout the semester. Make sure to follow the rubric, but she will take random points off for things that weren't in the rubric.

Dr. Atabay is passionate about teaching others about the middle east. this class could have been really interesting but I did not care for the professor to much. My classmates and I always seemed to be confused on what we were doing because instructions were very broad. there are quite a few discussion papers that require a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Atabay was really invested in the material covered in the course, she really loves speaking about the Middle East and stereotypes related. I will say, I thought this class was going to go over culture and politics within the Middle East, but it kind of seemed like I should've had a background on it to participate. Prof was great though, kind.

In my experience I would find another IAH to take or a different professor. Dr. Atabay was only focused on reading and writing papers. She NEVER responds to emails. You can only miss two classes the whole semester before being advised to take it again. DON'T TAKE HER CLASS!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was a lot more difficult than it should have been. We were expected to spend 12 hours a week outside of the class doing work. I thought the topic would be interesting but she made it so boring!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is not worth taking for IAH credit THERE ARE SO MANY BETTER OPTIONS!!! Attendance isn't necessarily mandatory but you can't miss every class.

reviews.comment: I thought this class was going to be an overview of the Middle East (history and culture), but we focused on very specific topics and learned very little about the Middle East in general. reviews.comment: I ended the class with a low 3.5 but Dr. Atabay curved it to an A!:) However, this class is essay heavy and she is a hard grader.

reviews.comment: WORST PROFESSOR !!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: All of your school work will be based on tough books and films. At least 30 pages per week. You MUST attend class. You only get four hours of absences and she uses participation as a major part of your grading. If you want a 4.0, attendance & active discussion is necessary. Her assignments are very subjective, 2 essays and 3 group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is more than a good one;)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Pros: Willing to help you and won't punish you for being bad at the skills required for the class. She will actually try and help you understand what you need to work on to help you in the future. cons: The workload is extremely heavy. Lots of reading and writing. Finnish reading early. Start your work soon as you know the assignment.
Teacher answers all questions you have and really cares that a student does well.
She is way too demanding. I would NOT recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She is an awesome professor, and very willing to help her students. I got a bad grade on one of my papers, and she let me re-write it at the end of the semester, even when she had a lot of things to grade. She really puts her students first, and the class was very alive and interesting.
She is a nice teacher but demanded a lot from her students.

Terrible. Too much work. She acts like its the only class we have and I just had a presentation to give today, I have two papers due within the next two weeks, and I have to read a whole book in that time too. The course information is interesting, but she is way too time consuming. I know it's 4 credits but I've never had a teacher give this much.
Learned a lot! She was friendly and very good at sparking conversation.
Excellent professor, and a wonderful kind person.

I took every course Dr. Athanason taught during my years at MSU. He was an extraordinarily gifted teacher and scholar. Today, I hold my own PhD in English and American Literature and teach at a major university. As a tribute to Arthur, I teach at least one of the plays I studied with him every semester - Joseph Pizzo, PhD, MSEd

I took every course Dr. Athanason taught during my years at MSU. He was an extraordinarily gifted teacher and scholar. Today, I hold my own PhD in English and American Literature and teach at a major university. As a tribute to Arthur, I teach at least one of the plays I studied with him every semester - Joseph Pizzo, PhD, MSEd

In 96/97 I had him for a undergraduate course on contemporary drama and a graduate seminar on Tennessee Williams and William Inge. I remember finishing a 20 minute speech in the seminar and Athanason asking, "Now what was it really about?"  Uh!  -- He was a one of a kind teacher and he will be missed.  Great guy.

I was heartbroken to see Prof. Athanason had passed away; he was an absolute revelation as an instructor and gave me one of the best academic experiences of my four-year MSU career.  He will be missed and I am sorry for future students who will not benefit from his teaching.

Sorry to hear that he passed away.  took him in the fall of 1999.  At the time, he seemed vague.  My grades in the class were poor and I thought he was a mean old man.  As the class progresed my work got better and it seemed I was better able to grasp the course material. A lot of difficult questions he asked but looking back the class was worth it

He said, during office hours, that when you are standing in a mob full of people, it is impossible to find the others that are willing to step away from the crowd. It is only when you have the courage to step away from that that you are able to locate the others who have also done so. He was a brilliant man and I try to live that wisdom every day.

Arthur Athanason died on September 5, 2005. I studied with him during the first years he was at Michigan State. He was the greatest of all my professors and my first literary mentor. The world has lost a great man. Susan Dormady Eisenberg

While I graduated several years ago, I came across this site and wanted to add my 2 cents on what a great professer he was/is.  While I the course was difficult and he was very demanding, it was one of the best experiences I had in my 5-plus years of undergraduate education.

Wonderful professor. First I thought he was harsh and obtuse, then I thought he was arrogant, then I thought he was crazy and finally I thought he was brilliant. I think he might be all of these things. I learned so much about how to approach theatre and literature in general. TAKE HIS CLASSES!!
brilliant professor, sell your first born to have one of his classes

Dr. Athanason cares more about what we learn in his classes and from literature than most teachers ever dream of. He isn't afraid to challenge students to think for themselves and he expects a lot out of you. I grew so much with his guidance.

I took this class in the early 90s. It's one of the few memorable experiences from MSU's teaching staff. He made me look at literature differently, with respect for the creator even if I didn't like it. Great professor.
This teacher was a frustrated thespian.  He should retire and let new teachers take his place. No one should have to endure him acting out scenes from plays ever again.
He's hard, he's passionate, a little over the top sometimes, but he knew what he was talking about

As an MSU graduate, I remember most those profs who made class come to life-Anthanason is one of the great!  As stated, he is a TOUGH grader who makes you work, but you will learn an immense amout about literature from the insightful questions he poses.
Tough grader, but just an EXCELLENT teacher all around!  Brings literature to life. Incredibly intelligent and a very personable and caring professor and person.

I took this course back in the mid 1970s and it was a life-changing experience.  Not a lecturer but a guide, he asks remarkable difficult questions that have no right or wrong answers and asks you to learn by answering them concisely. Outstanding!

First English courses with him, I was a freshman, took time to appreciate the total value of lectures (and sometimes didn't grasp them) until I was older - you will not forget this great instructor! My class was 1978-79!
Excellent lecturer.  Passionate and intelligent, tough grader.  Recommended!
Professor Ashley is caring, fun and genuine. I loved her class and woukd definitely take one of her classes again. She is very understanding and down to earth. Beautiful soul.

I loved Dr. Moore, and I had her for TE101. After reading negative reviews, it seems that people are upset due to the difficult discussions that were had in class, but Dr. Moore was always respectful to everyone while sharing her thoughts, and I never felt attacked or judged. She can be quite opinionated, but once you're used to it, it's all good.
Removed a student from her class for difference of opinions, the TE 101 and 102 classes are a complete joke and waste of time and content.
Had us turn in a rough draft, and then graded it on accuracy. 0/10, wouldn't recommend, would choose a different teacher.

I liked Ashley! She was super sweet and cared about our personal lives, would ask a group question at the start of every class. Class is only 50 min but flew by. Last 6ish weeks are student led presentations. Didn't ever really want to skip this class. Easy homework and the papers aren't bad at all. Would take class with her again any time!
Dr. Moore is a caring and accessible professor. She can be nitpicky with assignments but gives great constructive criticism. She pushes students to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Moore was an amazing professor. I would recommend her class. She grades kinda hard, but she makes the class fun and makes everyone involved.

Strongly recommend having her as your professor for TE-102. She makes the class feel like a community, allowing every student to speak and feel heard. She is very caring and understanding and is willing to give students extended time on any homework as long as they communicate. Amazing lectures, if you plan on taking TE-102 soon, take it with her.

It's as good as a general chemistry lecture can get, to be honest. She is a nice lady, and the course is set up well. Attendance is graded on iClicker, but you do get three drops. The class isn't that hard either, but it is chemistry, so if you aren't good at chemistry, it may seem harder.

She explained things very clearly and in an interesting way. Very easy to follow along and didn't go too fast for the notetakers. Very knowledgeable about the topic and was always very prepared for lecture.
She's a good Prof, however exams are worth %60. Final exam will replace your lowest grade but exams are tough.
Attendance mandatory. Pay attention in class or you wont pass. She moves pretty fast in class but lecture videos are posted. Put in the work and youll be alright.

Dr Pollock is an amazing Professor; her teaching style is good, and she tests what she taught with iClicker questions. She gives opportunities for extra credits as well, 4 total exams with 1 Final exam that will replace your lowest grade from the other 3. I had previous experience doing A' Level Chemistry, so the class was very easy to understand.

Mrs. Pollock was a good professor and explained topics thoroughly. 
-iClicker every lecture with questions for attendance 
-Homework twice a week graded by completion
-Recitation is mostly groupwork but is fairly easy and mostly completion

The exams were very lecture and recitation heavy. As long as you went to class and truly understood what she was talking about and could apply it to other concepts, you will do well in this class. I also recommend going to the help room for more clarification and exam prep. Overall, she was great and super nice.
Dr Pollock is a very knowledgeable person, and you are able to understand the lectures pretty well.  (I unfortunately don't do good in chem no matter what) But she is an amazing professor.

Amy Pollock is a great professor who truly wants her students to learn. PAY ATTENTION to her lectures and TAKE GOOD NOTES. These will be your best friend for the exam. DO NOT slack off on the BeSocratic HW or in the recitations. These are basically mini-reviews for the exams.

Absolutely amazing professor. The way she taught the class made everything in chemistry just click. All homework, recitation activities, and exams will be very easy if you show up to lectures. Made learning chemistry enjoyable.

Dr. pollock was seriously genuine about us succeeding in her class. she would give homework twice a week, but even those are done within 30 minutes. she would tell you everything to do in order to receive a good grade, provided tons of resources, and made it engaging. she is very educated on the topic at hand, and is very kind and considerate.

Professor Pollock took subject that I'm not very good at and simplified it enough for me to get a 3.0. Overall, a good, not great professor. But she can sometimes go a little fast so definitely be sure to stay up on the readings or at least use the help room.

Amy lowkey the goat at teaching, even for a difficult class. It was easy to take notes as she lectured and we would do iClicker for attendance points. Show up to lecture and recitation, take notes, try your best, and you will be fine. I literally got B's on all my tests and A's on everything else, giving me a 4.0 in the end. CEM 141 survivor.
She gave good explanations and clearly cares about students' learning. She has a lot of resources and tips for studying.

This class is taught in a big setting so not very personal. Everything you need to know will be taught in class which is mandatory. Lots of material to study for the test with. Class is not hard but she loves trick questions.

Great prof and made the course very easy to understand if you pay attention in lecture. Homework isn't bad and she goes over it in lecture. Attendance is mandatory with IClicker. Completion worksheet in recitation.
Great lecturer!
Made this class really easy to understand and she's good at explaining topics in a clear and concise way.

Amy is amazing. She is a super kind and a cute lady. However, if you do not come to the lectures, you will fail. Class material is basic chem and Amy teaches it super well. She is very passionate and explains every thing in great detail. There are about 2 easy homeworks a week.  Overall, if you come to class and pay attention, you should pass.
Super great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Dr Pollock. She explains things very well and made confusing concepts easy to understand so make sure to pay attention in lecture. I got a 4.0 in this class. I never did amazing on the exams but the homework and extra credit help a ton. The final is super easy too. I would recommend taking CEM141 with Pollock.

Love Dr. Pollock! She explains things well in class better than my high school teachers. I never went to office hours since they conflicted with my classes but I've heard that she explains things very very well there. Just make sure you shown up and pay attention in class!
Very informative lectures, she teaches you exactly what is going to be on the tests and how to approach it. Definitely make use of the practice materials before each test.

You really just have to attend lecture and pay attention. This class is a general chemistry class, so the concepts are fairly simple. Go to class, study, get what you pay for. The only con I have is that the due dates for homework can be somewhat random, leading me to miss two of them because it slipped my mind.

Amazing at explaining the WHY for concepts, wants people to succeed and is good at telling us how to, makes lecture interesting, easy to understand. SUPER organized which was the reason for my success, posts lecture vids. Doesn't waste a second of lecture, definitely memorizes her speeches. Use learning objectives to study for exams! I'd recommend!

I studied for 9+ hours on every exam and never received anything better than an 82%. One exam I got a 69% even though I studied for 9 hours. She's a decent teacher, but this course just sets people up for failure. I do not understand how people 4.0 this class.
Very good lecturer, explains topics well. She does a very good job explaining why the concepts work the way they do instead of just giving us rules to memorize. And the homework load isn't too crazy.

Very good lecturer, explains topics well. She does a very good job explaining why the concepts work the way they do instead of just giving us rules to memorize.
And the homework load isn't too crazy.

Dr.Pollock is a very good professor. She is well experienced and makes you really understand concepts that can be challenging. She goes slow over materials (which I liked) to ensure that everything is clear. I wished she taught upper-level chemistry so I can retake them with her.

Professor Pollock was a great professor and explained the material slowly and thoroughly. She was very accessible outside of class and told you exactly what you needed to know to be successful. CEM 141 is a tough class but if you put the work in and go to all the lectures you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof is very aimed towards students success and education, but you can't really miss a lecture. Multiple extra credits and clear learning objectives. She is very clear with the material and easy to learn from, gives many suggestions on how to succeed in the class and if you follow you will. The exams were straightforward but at weird times.

Amazing professor, genuinely so nice and as long as you go to lectures and pay attention, you'll be fine. The homework is completion and the tests are hard so make sure you go study EVERYTHING on the slides and go to the help room!

Dr. Pollock was one of my favorite professors of the whole semester. I don't love chemistry, but she has a great teaching style. If most of the class got a lecture question wrong, she wouldn't show us how we answered and would reiterate from a different approach with more detail, then ask the question again and it worked every time. Great prof.
Professor Pollock is a great teacher. Highly recommend taking CEM 141 with her.

Lectures are SO important please go! Pay attention and ask questions, she is more than happy to help! She wants to make sure students succeed and even though it is a general course, still wants to make kids love chemistry. Overall, a wonderful professor!

I love her class. CEM 141 is typically hard but the way she explains things helped me understand. Homework definitely helps with understanding the material. I recommend utilizing the learning objectives. Exams to me were easy. Don't be afraid to use the help room too!

I absolutely loved having Dr. Pollock! She lectures in a manner that is easy to understand and she does look for participation a lot in lectures- but I personally didn't mind. If you follow the learning objectives, and are good (and quick) at taking notes in class you will be just fine. She makes expectations very clear and is very kind overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a solid professor and conveys information in a digestible manner. If you pay attention and take notes in class, do the homework, and use the PAs for help as needed in recitation then you should be able to pass.

Goes way too fast in lecture. The TA's do a better job at explaining things than her. Extremely harsh grader especially on exams, which are worth 45% of your overall grade. I hated this class and struggled with it, which is weird because I did very well in previous chemistry classes I have taken.

She's great. I took this class with another professor and got 1.5 because the concepts are difficult and I couldn't understand. Now I'm taking it with Pollock and I think she's great. She goes fast but if you're gonna take this class every teachers gonna go fast. I have like a 3 in her class

she goes extremely fast and changes the slides before you have a chance to write anything down. plus, all the slides have so much info on them, which makes it easy to fall behind. she talks in questions, a weird teaching style. hard to follow, hard to understand. the exams are difficult, and she doesnt drop any of them. overall a difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She talks in a way you can understand chemistry! She records every lectures (posted) so it's helpful if you missed class. She gives extra credit for homework. You get a point for each lecture/recitation you attend. I think she takes attendance by iClicker. Go over lecture videos and your notes (that's what helped me) cus exams are a bit rough.
Professor Pollock makes the material easy to grasp, but the exams are challenging. With diligent studying and using resources like Unstuck ai, you can ace this class.
She Is awesome, does a great job explaining and breaks down concepts. I struggled in the class still, but she made it better and looking back now, one of the better chemistry professors

Pollock was a great Professor. Her lectures were very informational and easy to follow. Although chemistry is a tough subject she explains it very well. If you do everything you're supposed to do, you should have issues with this class.
Nope. Just no

Great lectures. May be a little fast-paced for some, but the unit notes are posted ahead of time. The environment is more focused on learning than being graded by using iclicker, so feel free to be wrong, but be prepared to show up to class!!! Lectured are recorded and uploaded after. Easy to reach via email and great at answering questions.

The homework she gives are decently challenging, but she grades them in terms of completion and not correctness. Exams are pretty difficult so you'll want to take good notes and study well. She offers recorded lectures and things to make it pretty easy to study. With effort you'll be able to 4.0 and with minimal effort you'll 3.0-3.5. Great prof
The professor ensured to explain topics and concepts to fulfill students understanding of the material. The exams are easy as long as you keep up on the material and attend help hours!

Professor Pollock is so sweet and caring when it comes to helping you during class or office hours. She always makes sure to explain everything clearly if anyone has questions before moving on and will not make you feel dumb for needing clarification. She really cares about making sure everybody can do well in her class. USE OFFICE HOURS!!!

Professor Pollock was great when it came to thoroughly teaching topics.  However, you MUST show up to lecture or you will miss a LOT of information.  She was also very straight forward with her teaching.  There were many extra credit opportunities and grade drops offered, so do it all and you should be ok.

Never opened the text book for the class because she explained the material so well.
She understands the material very well and presents it in a very clear way.
Pollock is a really good professor, very clear in her lectures and the best teacher for chemistry. If you don't get her, you'll regret it!

Awesome teacher! I switched from another prof and my grades increased dramatically, she is very helpful, her lectures are awesome and she has great office hours! Would recommend for any CEM class at MSU

She does a wonderful job of explaining things in a way that is easily understandable which is important with a class like chemistry. Don't waste any money on the textbook though, I 4.0ed it without opening it. Buy the lecture notes, the exam and solutions book and attend class regularly and you will be successful in this class.

She is a clear, helpful teacher, but the class itself is hard. The tests are hard no matter what professor you have. I would highly recommend buying the lecture notes and practice exams, but the chemistry text book isn't neccessary.
Great professor!
She was very helpful and clear.  The class requires a lot of work, but she does everything she can to help
I'm awful at Chemistry and she made it understandable for me.

Professor was great. She did a good job explaining the material thoroughly and in a way that was beneficial for everyone. I see she has quite a good rating here, and it's for a good reason. Highly recommended.

LOVE pollock!!! the class was difficult though but she is a great teacher very thorough and slow with the material and always willing to help out no matter when you need it... she is a great teacher but it doesn't mean slacking the class is a lot of effort!

This chemistry is hard, but Pollock makes it look so simple. She's very clear and her notes are so easy to follow. I loved the way she taught. My best advice is pay attention in class, then when you get home, do the Exam and Solutions qustions you can do. Good luck!
Great Professor, I hate the subject but she got me a 4.0
She explains everything very clearly, but in a monotone voice. I had the 4:10 lecture and needed an energy drink to actually focus on what she was saying.

Prof Pollock is an awesome teacher! People who got laduca or hunter were jealous of me because I had the best chem prof. She is super clear in teaching and does a great job explaining concepts. The course itself if pretty tough, i had to work REALLY hard to get a 3.0
Best professor ever
great! explained organic chemistry really clearly!!

Jeez... I have no idea how she got such a good score but I seriously disagree with most of what was said about her.  She goes out of her way to teach things differently than the way most people were taught in high school.  She over-complicates simple concepts, and the exams are absolute nightmares.

Decent prof. First time she taught the class. It can get boring especially in the afternoon. Notes are basically the same as the lecture notes. Use the study guide and do as many practice exams as possible way before the exams and you will ace the class or you can easily scrape by with a 3.0 by doing average on exams and all OWL questions

Dr. Pollock is a great prof. She is very clear and helpful. It is a pretty difficult class but it's chemistry. Go to class, take good lecture notes, start studying for the exams ahead of time, and do the practice exams!!! I would definately recommend this professor.

I simply LOVED this professor!  She is very clear, organized, helpful, enthusiastic, hard-working...etc,and I could go on for ever!  If you have any trouble understanding the material or doing homework GO to her office and she will help you.  Believe me when I say she is the sweetest professor you'll ever meet!  I am really going to miss her!

Dr Pollack was very helpful and available even though there were over 1000 students in the class. She is very good at chemistry and did a great job explaining the subject. Dr Pollack is the best professor in the chemistry department. I highly recommend her!

Excellent professor!  Very good at explaining and simplifying concepts, always willing to help, and her exams aren't too difficult.  I wish every professor was at least half as good as her!  God bless Dr. Amy Pollock!
Really enthusiastic about chemistry, and more than happy to help you out.  Great teaching style.
No Comments

Amy is an excellent professor!  I had her for 141 and understood everything she taught.  I don't like chemistry, but she teaches the information so that you can understand, and is always willing to explain again if someone has a question.  I definitely recommend her if you are taking 141 OR 143.
Very easy to understand. If you have a question she will be sure to clear it up for you.
The most wonderful teacher I have ever had! She makes everything so easy to learn, and she teaches in a way that makes it difficult not to understand.  I would highly recommend her to anyone!
Awsome teacher
She really knows her stuff, and she tries really hard to make sure that you understand it as well. Going to her helped me so much on the tests. I understood everything so much better.
The class is amaizng..even if its a big class..i lov the expirements she shows us!!..and she is a gr8 teacher!! Relaly like the way she teaches :)

Dr. Barnes Lee is kind, but the class needs improvement. We focused almost only on racism against African Americans without covering other groups or discrimination (sexism, ableism, etc.) and human development. Lectures were mostly her reading slides and the book. Discussions weren't guided and became personal/therapeutic rather than academic.

Dr. Barnes-Lee is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had. The discussions she facilitated were wonderful and productive. She was caring and relatable. Completely unrelated- but she has impeccable style. LOVE HER.

I took her 310 course in Fall 2023. Every time I left this class I felt refreshed and relaxed. She can be a harsh grader, but if you truly believe you deserve a better grade, then she is more than willing to go back over the assignment and see if there were any mistakes in grading. On one assignment, I bumped my grade from a 72% to an 89%.
He could care less if your writing was "good" or not, he just wants you to try your best and write something. Just don't turn in things late, he doesnt like that.

He assigns a ton of work, but he is very nice and grades pretty easily. There were so many different writings/assignments that I stopped trying 3 weeks in. He takes attendance but you have 4 skips. Rambles a lot during class  time but if you  just do the assignments you'll get an easy 4.0.

Professor Astle is an easy grader and likes participation. As long as you complete assignments, you will get a great grade in the class. A lot of busy work, but honestly, it just helps your overall grade in the end. I would 100% take a course with Professor Astle again.
Very good professor, super understanding, very compassionate and super willing to give extensions.

Although he rambles during the lectures, he's very caring and pretty laid back. The class is paper heavy, with not too much time in between papers. There are occasional group projects. He gives VERY detailed feedback. His grading style is weird. Each assignment regardless of size is 2 points, but you can fight for your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's super chill, the lectures are always very fun and while he does ramble a little bit it's usually entertaining or thought-provoking. You will often get out 15 minutes early or be doing individual work for the second hour of the class which I liked. Not a harsh grader and altogether the class is an easy + fun honors credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Astle has easily been the best professor I have ever had. The classes are long but all WRA101 classes are going to be long. He has a great sense of humor and extremely caring to all of his students. Definitely take your writing requirement through him if you can. He is amazing.

Dr. Astle is probably my favorite professor this semester. He gives insightful comments and will gives full credit if you show effort. The only thing is to keep an eye on assignments because there's a lot, especially in class, and you could miss some. He doesn't always remind students of due dates for writing projects so be on top of it.
Way more work than other WRA profs. A lot of unnecessary busy work.

Dr. Astle showed obvious care for his students with his assignments and deadlines. His lectures were philosophical in nature, and honestly had nothing to do with his papers, but he was very kind and thoughtful. You don't really need to go to class to pass, but always keep an eye on assignment deadlines. All assignments are posted online.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Astle is a very caring and helpful professor. He gives good and detailed feedback about your writing. We had a lot of mini writing assignments that I think were kind of unnecessary. He also talks a lot during lectures. Classes usually ended pretty early and the exam was stress free.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The professor graded clearly and specifically, but he is very generous. Even though the amount of work assigned was heavy, finish all of them and you have got a sure A. The lectures do not really relate to the work, but they are not mandatory, so your choice. He is also very kind and understanding, accessible and helpful outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a really great prof who grades pretty easily and gives great feedback. As long as you do all of the assigned work you should get a good grade. The course has a heavy emphasis on reflective writing and he focuses a lot on the concepts of intelligence and learning as well. There can be some abstract thinking but I found it to be worthwhile.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is essentially a ton of busy work. The lectures aren't super important, and they are long and boring. As long as you put in decent effort and submit all your assignments on time, then this class is no big deal. Dr. Astle is nice, but he doesn't hand out extensions like candy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: 99% of the class is writing a million mini essays on one topic, which i dont hate at all. the assignments themselves were relatively easy but this dude talks for a very long time while saying so much nothing. 7/10 since class ends early most days
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome class got B+ the only reason why was because I scored 77 on a major assignment but overall great professor . Take this class!!!!!!

Professor Astle was overall great. Did a good job organizing the class and was always willing to help the students. The course work can be time-consuming, but as long as you work hard, you should be solid for this class.
Awesome teacher very caring if ur a freshman highly recommended. If ur not the best at essay he really works with you and cares.
He grades really easy. this lectures don't really matter, and you don't have to take notes. 10/10 would have hime again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really great prof. He gives really good feedback on all assignments and grades pretty easily. Highly recommend him for WRA 101. He really cares about his students and wants them to do well.

She was consistently strict to the point of being unreasonable, and her tone often came across as dismissive. It's frustrating how she would make personal comments about students, often trying to define who we were or what we were capable of, which felt intrusive and unprofessional. The class environment was tense and unsupportive. don't recommend

You can tell she really cares about her students and her goal is to get everyone a 4.0. As long as you keep up with the work, which never took me more than 3 hours a week, and go to class you'll be successful. It is very discussion based and 3 hours long, but Dr. Moore makes adjustments for quieter students and gives breaks.

Dr. Moore is an incredible professor.  She is open about every decision made in the class. After the Feb. 13 event, she was helpful and reached out with support and resources. She was understanding of mental health. Her teaching requires participation and discussion, but she has reasonable expectations. Her reading is light and easy to follow.

Dr. Moore is a great professor! She does not require a doctors note when you miss class and is very understanding. She is very open to extending due dates and grades fairly. I would take this class again for sure! You need to buy a few things but she will work with you!

Ashley was one of the most caring professors I have had to date. She is very understanding and always wants you to take care of yourself before school. I think that she is very fun and always asks for feedback. She doesn't just look at our feedback either, she takes it into consideration and accommodates it to the best of her ability.
An amazing teacher! I took TE 101 with her and am going to take TE 102 with her again! She makes the 3 hour long class fly by. You could go get a cup of coffee with her:)

She is a professor who truly cares about each of her students and their well-being. She is respectful of everyone in the classroom when discussing important topics. She is so real with her students and this helps with her teaching which she is very well organized and prepared for. I would highly recommend taking a class with her.

I had her for a TE course and she is just phenomenal. Dr. Moore shows constant respect for her students and does a fantastic job at making sure you are interested and engaged with the course material. Genuinely one of my favorite professors and I would highly, highly, HIGHLY recommend her to anyone.
I absolutely loved this professor! she was funny and knowledgable and helpful. I would really love to take spanish from her again.

She is OK.  She seems more interested in trying to impress us and she seems uncomfortable when explaining difficult topics or if people have more in-depth questions.  I would take her again because she is nice but you might learn more from a different prof.

Professor Moore was one of the best profs I've had so far here at MSU. She's extremely helpful and does a great job with the course material.  She loves teaching and Spanish and it shows. I would highly recommend taking her courses if you can!

Horrible lectures. Reads straight from PowerPoint with little to no added substance. There was no additional homework when I took the class, so you just had to pray you did well on the 5 major exams. Stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Triplett understands that her class is hard, and she is always willing to help outside of class. Granted, the lectures are not super interesting, but it's a fair trade because the all the homework can only help your grade (so long as you actually complete it). You'll have to study hard-- exams are difficult. But she offers tons of extra credit.

I had Ashley for KIN 216 in 2020 and KIN 411 in 2023 and both times she was a great professor. I'm glad I finally had an in person class with her as she is a caring and funny professor. She can be tough but it is because she knows you know the information and just doesn't want to give you the answer right away. Overall, a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't bother going to lectures because she'll just read PowerPoints word for word at the speed of light. Dr. Triplett seems nice, and I'm sure she's probably well versed in human anatomy, but she definitely should not be a teacher. Tests feel harder than they need to be, and the course doesn't feel like it's set up to actually help students learn.

I personally loved this class. While class may not have been the most entertaining, the prof was very helpful with tips of what to study for the exam (go to exam review sessions!!) and her slides were straightforward. There were no surprises on the exam. Definitely a memorization class and takes lots of studying, but good instructors.

Professor Triplett was a great professor and KIN 216 was my favorite class this semester. There's a lot of content but her lecture slides are well-organized and easy to follow. She provides great resources for studying.

5 exams. awful prof. not understanding at all and very rude and short with people. doesn't actually teach prob cause she doesn't know the content. never wants to be there and often comes late. my friends and I all ended up teaching ourselves. good luck getting assignments dropped even if you have a literal disease

Terrible Prof. Doesn't teach, reads off slides but clearly doesn't know the content she's "teaching" cause she pronounces half of it wrong and corrects herself constantly. Lectures more harmful than helpful, resorted to teaching myself. Not understanding at all. I literally have never had a worse professor or teacher in my life. AVOID HER CLASSES.

This class was very hard for many students but the TAs were extremely helpful and so was Dr. Triplett. Highly recommend this class as it was very interesting but quite challenging. Lots of studying is required.

KIN 216 is a hard class, I understand, but that doesn't dismiss the fact that Dr. Triplett did not teach. Reading straight off of the powerpoint slides does not constitute teaching, and it didn't really seem like she wanted to be there. I am disappointed with how the class turned out, and it could be structured a whole lot better.
love her, very kind and understanding to students, tests are straightforward
great teacher, cares about her students
She literally doesn't teach at all the TAs are always unhelpful and the lectures do not help you for the tests at all.

Very bland when giving lectures. The biggest challenge is not taking notes, but trying not to fall asleep. I get ecstatic when I open a lecture and it's a TA's voice. Takes over 10 days to grade exams and will NOT respond to a SIGNLE email no matter how important. It seems as if I'm going to 4.0 this class, Dr. Triplett is just aggravating.

I had to teach myself pretty much this whole course with the help of family. Asa normally read off the slides and just skimmed the surface of the topic but never went into good detail with it. It almost seemed like he was learning the information with us. Clicker during class and the homework helped, but I don't think lecture helped me at all.

All exam questions come from past exams, iClicker questions during lecture, and homework. Take advantage of the online help room, the TA's are always making sure you truly understand what you're confused on. There are two homework drops, and one exam drop. Lectures are kind of boring but important to pay attention to.

Professor Brigandi was very chill and straight forward. He made is clear what was due and gave students the choice of coming to lecture or not. You'll do well in this class as long as you know most of the material. Only thing I didn't like was having to pay $100 for the textbook, but overall an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Asa does not give much explanation on the topics for lectures. He skims the surface of a powerpoint that is clearly made by someone else, and sometimes it feels as if he's reading the information on the slides for the first time. No leniency on the homework: Had to teach myself the entire course. Would not take again.

The class was an easy A, but class attendance is a portion of the grade. You have to buy the textbook to get online homework access, but you can go over the homework in office hours and get 100%. Really receptive to questions. Review lectures and study materials really helped with exams.

Dr. Steele is one of the best professors in Lyman Briggs. She genuinely cares about all of her students and wants us to succeed. Her lecture slides are posted online, but I would highly recommend attending every class. I would 100% recommend Dr. Steele for LB 145 - and I would definitely take it with her again.

I took her class in her first semester at MSU, and she was definitely new to D2L. I still don't know half of my grade, and there's a week left. However, she's a great teacher and cares about her students. She saves a lot of time out of class to talk to you and help you understand the material. The class isn't hard; it was just confusing.

Class is extremely easy to do well in but you'll feel like you have no idea what you're doing. The class structure is all over the place and confusing, everything is group work so if your group doesn't know what's happening, you have to teach yourself at home. Tons of extra credit though and free points throughout the sem make it easy to 4.0

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU ARE NOT ALREADY GOOD AT ECON. I got a 5 on AP Micro and still struggled. I loved Professor Mukherjee he was the GOAT but it is very fast-paced and the homework + tests are graded pretty harshly. No point in buying the textbook, it is hardly ever referenced and is not required (though he says it is)

I deeply regretted taking this course. Unclear grading, harsh grading, lack of accessibility to Prof Mukherjee, horrible teaching. I had to teach myself the material. On exams you will be asked to solve problem types that were never given in an example, never showed in class, nor in the textbook. This was a HORRIBLE experience, don't take.

Was nervous about taking this as an engineering major but overall was a good experience. Lectures were clear and conveyed material well, but I still found myself using the book a lot. Workload was extremely manageable while still learning to apply the material

He's an okay teacher. Class is very straightforward and bland. This class would be very difficult for someone who hasn't taken econ before. Get ready to teach yourself a good deal of the content from the driest textbook you've ever read. Graded off of 6 problem sets, 2 midterms, and the final. He posts the lectures as well, which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I found this class super slow and boring. There is a lack of enthusiasm and a great deal of monotone lecturing. I actually skipped the online zooms and waited until the videos were uploaded so that I could watch it on 2 times speed and not fall asleep.

Teaches directly off of power point, which do not correlate to exact exam questions.   Will be confusing by talking in circles and not covering exam concepts effectively.  It is unfortunate that there are not many other instructors for this course, I would not recommend this class.  Teaching assistants grade very harsh.

He is a great guy. However his tests are very hard, very hard. It's all math and no multiple choice. All math questions. He teaches everything you need to know though, just be ready to study hard, and be good at calc. Each tests only has 4 to 6 math questions that each take 10 to 20 mins to do.

Lectures could be boring at times but were easy to understand. Quizzes were somewhat difficult but the amount of extra credit offered made up for it. If I could do this class again I would probably take it online instead of having to be there 3 days a week for lecture. Professor was very nice though.

She's very understanding about any issues if you just talk to her in-person. I recommend going to the TA's office hours regularly because her slides are hard to interpret on your own, and her accent makes long lectures hard to understand. All quizes an exams are on D2L asynchronously. Concepts are easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: All quizzes and tests are online and open book with no lockdown browser, and she offers enough extra credit. If you want an easy 4-point, Professor ALZ's class is perfect. But if you want to actually learn, don't take her. She's pro-AI and the class is so easy that it would be hard to learn anything unless I was REALLY interested in the material.
Very easy class, every assignment is out of class and online. Plenty of extra credit opportunities, and slides are super helpful for studying. Would recommend, seems nice and class is easy.
Dr. ALZ is an amazing professor and prioritizes the learning of her students. She offers a lot of extra credit which had me prioritize my learning over worrying about my grade.

Dr. ALZ is a Wonderfull professor! She is a very fair grader, and she goes through the lectures at a steady pace. She brings in a lot of guest speakers and gives out many extra credit opportunities. She also does demonstrations on certain types of software that students often have trouble navigating.

I really enjoyed this course. The professor really cares about the students and will often be very lenient about assignments and quizzes. She also gives a bunch of extra credit opportunities which can REALLY help boost your grade. The only downside to this course was the TA.

She's very sweet, but unfortunately often hard to follow during lectures, and the slides themselves can be a tad confusing. Dates for quizzes weren't really communicated until the class before or the day-of, and I flat-out missed one or two of them. That being said, there's TONS of easy extra credit to be had; I felt clueless and still got a 4.0.

I knew this class would be tough when she started the semester offering 40 points of extra credit. She ended up offering over 80. I earned 60 and still only got a 2.0. Her accent is horrendously difficult to understand and her lectures are not very clear. Weekly quizzes on random days of the week, and the assign

I often found myself very bored in this professor's class because she reads straight from the lectures that can be accessed online. Attending this class often felt like a waste of time, however, attendance was mandatory, but she allowed 5 absences. She also offers a lot of extra credit, more than any other professor I've had before.

Professor Ligmann-Zielinska does not teach well and only reads off PowerPoint. She covers stuff we can easily memorize instead of going in-depth on how to do the math and coding the course requires. I am giving her a good review because of how much extra credit she gives. I failed almost every quiz and got a 4.0 truly amazing.

This prof is fine. Sometimes it's difficult to understand her point when she can't find the right words, especially for such a technical class. There is so much extra credit that even if you have no idea what's going on you'll be fine. Very sweet lady, kinda funny. It's easier to pay attention to the recorded lectures so you can go back and listen.
Terrible prerecorded lectures. She does not know how to teach online. I want to pull my hair out listening to her stumble on her words during recordings.

This was all online and she was a professor that didn't understand how to teach online. All lectures were pre recorded so if you were confused you would have to figure it out yourself, which was almost always. But easy quizzes and not stressful course load, just wait to take in person if an option.

Nice and funny professor. The quizzes and exams are all online and you have 24 hrs to take them. Although she said that you don't have time to look at your notes during them since they're timed, you do. I used my notes for every exam and quiz, so have good notes from the powerpoints. She offers reasonable extra credit too.

This dude picks favorites and makes it obvious. He will assign you one hundred fifty pages with only one day to read and be confused when you only read half of it. He says it's a work day then lectures half the time. He loves to make you write essays. He said we'd watch Sinners in class, and that never happened. He does bring donuts sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Aronoff is one of the best English teachers I've ever had, and I mean that very genuinely. I think I say this mainly because of the way that he grades papers. There's a lot of them, sure, they're a bulk of the class. But he gives genuine feedback, and it's very obvious that he wants you to improve and dig deeper into the text. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Reading was the main downside of this class, yet Aronoff made it significantly more fun. Brought doughnuts for students on days where lengthy reading or projects were due. Gives amazing feedback and is always willing to work with students to rewrite papers or improve their grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor who is super passionate about what he is teaching. He makes sure you engage in class and genuinely will listen to what you have to say. He gives really good feedback on essays and will meet one on one with you to discuss your writing. Overall a great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took section 3. Really passionate, but boring. The class is almost exactly AP Literature & Composition. Aronoff is really cool to talk to and very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Loved this class, theres a lot of reading and class can drag on but he is a passionate professor and loves to teach. I would take the class again

The class seemed really interesting in the beginning, but got really tedious and boring.  I fell asleep almost every class because the lectures were not at all engaging. Would not recommend this professor to a friend.
Great professor, highly involved in his students' work. Loves what he teaches, and it's so infectious, you will too.
Aronoff is a wonderful professor and man.  He cares deeply for the subject matter and his students. There is a lot of reading for his classes but it all ends up being worth it.
Professor Arnold is awesome! The class is well structured, and Professor Arnold gives very thoughtful feedback on assignments. I would definitely recommend this class to others.
Great person! Really cares and loves hearing your ideas. Interested in your work and always opened to talk.

Amazing amazing amazing. Super down to earth and relatable to students. Understanding of missing class and gives opportunities to make up points. Big project at the end of the course/throughout but I really enjoyed working on it
Best prof I have had so far at MSU. He truly cares about women's voices and the subject he teaches. Is very flexible with deadlines and cares about his students. Would take him again 100000%

Professor Arnold is a great teacher and you can tell they genuinely care about their students. It's really easy to get a 4.0 as long as you complete the assignments. Probably the easiest class I've ever taken and doing the assignment each week didn't take much time.

Professor Arnolds class was amazing. I felt that the material was good and easy to understand, and they were extremely understanding for every single assignment that there was. There were also no exams! Overall I really liked this class.

Pat is the sweetest professor I've ever had. They clearly want all of their students to succeed and make it a point to get to know every student individually. It's very easy to 4.0 their classes as long as you complete your assignments!

Course was easy and the professor was very caring and tried to make connections with students. I personally took this class for an honors credit so I didn't enjoy it too much, but i can see how others would. A lot of videos and readings. 1 major assignment a week with readings, articles, and ted talks to inform. Spent an hour a week for this class.

Prof Arnold is easily the best professor I've ever had at MSU. So knowledgeable, welcoming, caring. Everything you could ask for. Content of  class was so interesting and I honestly can say I learned a lot. Two in person participation projects required but are up to you as far as topic/event. Was fun and worth it in the end. Nothing bad to say!
very kind and understanding. easy assignments
Pat was super accommodating and did everything in their power to make sure every student succeeded. Very easy, but interesting, class.

Professor Arnold is one of the most caring professors you will have at msu. They are very understanding and want you to succeed. There is an assignment due every other week that only takes about 30 minutes or less to do and 2 campus event reflections. As long as you complete your work the best you can, they will give you a 100!

Super nice and actually cares for students. The class itself is super easy and has discussion questions every other week which is really nice. Grading is super lenient and the assignments and readings are easy. Sometimes you do not even half to read the book to answer the discussion questions. Honors option is also easy.

i took this as an elective, easiest class ever. prof arnold is very sweet and such a nice person. this class requires little to no work. there's 1 online assignment a week that normally took ab 10-20 mins. u have to go to 2 events of ur choice during the semester. no tests/final. love prof arnold!!!

Pat is a wonderful and easygoing instructor. They only have a few assignments per week that are based off of the assigned readings. Attendance can be made up each week by doing an extra assignment. They are also very helpful and their lectures are super interesting.

Pat is an amazing professor. They assign weekly homework but it is all engaging and may include readings, documentaries, videos, poems, etc. This was my favorite class and I appreciated the flexibility. If you were to miss a class you could do a small extra assignment from home, but the class is so engaging that you won't want to miss!
He is a really nice professor and doesn't assign any quizzes or exams. The modules he assigned had really interesting videos and articles. He gives lots of extra credit during class.

He's a genuinely nice person, and makes it known that he wants everyone to feel as comfortable as possible in his class. There's one weekly assignment, and most of them are opinionated, so I'm honestly not even sure what he grades,
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: They are so nice and you can tell he really cares and is passionate about the subject matter. The class is easy (basically never any tests, just discussion posts) and consists of a lot of in class discussions.

He did a wonderful job conveying the topics. This is an easy class for anyone who regularly engages on topics of gender/sexuality in their personal life + a good intro for anyone that doesn't. He's super understanding and genuinely wants you to succeed. The assignments help you understand the content better, which is almost never the case.

Truly cares for students and is not boring whatsoever. She is a delight to have as a professor and makes learning biology fun and interesting. Her lab consists of lots of teamwork effort. Make sure to pick a good group that you can rely on. She is very understandable and wants the best for every student!
Dr. Balcer is a great teacher and is very understanding of students. She is always willing to exempt you from class or give you an extension on an assignment. She also just made lab really fun.

Lectures were kind of slow and didn't always add additional information to the pre-class videos. Exams were on the harder side and it was sometimes hard to tell how detailed answers were expected to be. Group work heavy.  Possible to 4.0 if you submit all assignments and extra credit.

Balcer genuinely loves what she is doing and tries her best to teach that caters to everyone. It is a flipped classroom and tests can be way harder than you think. But the extra credit helps immensely.

Dr. Balcer is a great professor! She is a recent PhD grad so she understands what it is like to be a student and is happy to help work with you. You'll be in an assigned group the whole semester and there is a self-conducted research project at the end. She is super nice and gives lots of feedback when asked! Would definitely recommend her.
Love her! She's amazing and really goes out of her way to help students.

Madame Wolfgang is one of the kindest people I have ever met! Michigan State really is lucky to have her as a French professor. She is extremely accommodating and understanding and really makes an effort to know the entire class. Course expectations are very straightforward.

I love Professor Wolfgang! I really enjoyed seeing her each week; she made French oral expression tolerable and fun. She encouraged a community within our classroom, and created a safe and welcoming environment for everyone. She was also so generous and accommodating to us -- especially in stressful times during the course. A truly great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very nice, caring, and accommodating. Encourages lots of participation for grade which can be nerve-wracking. Fair amount of reading and homework. Attendance is  required. Can be a little picky with grading homework. Easy exams, sometimes take home. Offers opportunities to drop absences. Will accept homework if not in class the day it's due.

I took his 111 a couple years ago, and I remember everyone being really scared of him, a couple people crying on different occasions, he said all our reading journals were "stolen", which is what he says every year. Despite all that, I actually learned a lot from him. I use the theories we read in almost every paper I write to this day. Cool guy.

I took Prof. Jacksons writing and research class that dealt with Black popular culture. Actually we could choose almost any research topic so long as it had something to do with social justice and race. I was overwhelmed by the different parts of the research paper but the individual and small group meetings helped a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Excellent professor. Lots of reading but much of it was interesting. Great class discussions about race, class, and social justice. I was overwhelmed by some of the assignments, especially the first paper about "American-ness." The small group work and one-on-one meetings with Austin were very useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I got a 3.5 in his 111. Frequently 15-20 minutes late to class. Didn't return papers until the last day of class. Very opinionated, to a fault. His assignments were very wordy and poorly worded. Have told my friends not to take his classes. The ones who didn't listen paid for it. I learned nothing about writing from his class... Don't take it

I recieved a 4.0, but the course was stressful and impossible to enjoy. Jackson never gave me feedback on my first essay, lost every single student's journal, and never even looked at my final paper that was 12 pages and took forever to write. He was late often. I loved the course's topic, but connot recommend it. Worst professor I have had
Straight up loved this class!  Because Austin was so into to material, it made it easier to focus.  Probably my favorite class I've ever taken.

If you read an autobiography read it as if you were of the same race and gender as the author. If you are reading history think about how it felt to be the person affected. These classes aren't about you. They are about the texts and real world applications. Talk to him when you do not understand he made me a better writer.

Austin is an amazing professor, and he really opened my eyes to a lot of stuff. If you're not comfortable talking about race, you will be by the end. He's a little intimidating in class, but outside of class he's really sweet - he admins like 5,000 student organizations. His essay prompts are really elaborate and confusing, though. Overall, great!
The best of the best. Very good teacher. Very helpful, grades fairly, keeps you engaged. Be sure to discuss, participation is graded.

By the way, to those poor sports writing here, I am a hardcore conservative, and I love Austin. In fact, it seems they are rather close-minded themselves - he's incredibly open to other opinions. As he said this term, the conservatives do the best - it's true. If you actually understand what you're arguing, not just propagandizing, he's great.

This man is an inspiration. Everyone's had those teachers in high school or profs in college who really changes the way they think, not just their short-term memory. Austin Jackson is one of those men. Some stupid people complain that he's biased, etc...no! the information is radical, and most students just want to spit out what they heard before.

This professor is not at all professional.  He should not be teaching at all.  He is biased, grades unfairly, is late to class often, doesn't maintain office hours, and treats students not on equal terms.

Austin is very opinionated, and if you agree with him in class and in your papers, it is very easy to get a 4.0.  Although I resented him a lot in the class because he wasn't open to other opinions (and I am a liberal!), I realized after the class was over that I really did learn a lot and it made me think differently about racism, ect.

if you are conservative DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. if you want to talk about racism and slavery and how white people are terrible and malcom X is the greatest then take it. He doesn't give back papers till the last day of class, doesn't help your writing skills AT ALL.

Agreeing with the person before me, if you want to vent about bush and racism, take this class... If you are not and value your GPA, dont take it because if you dont say what he wants to hear, your grades will be bad. Also, his directions are confusing as hell.. and his emails are even more confusings... if you take this, good luck...

If you are a Bush-bashing, left-winged, liberal looking to vent your opinions on racism to the world, this class is for you! If not? Run for the hills!  Austin looks for people to agree with him, and if you don't, it's impossible to get a good grade. He took 3 months to grade one paper! I learned nothing about writing in this class. What a joke!
the most ridiculous teacher i have ever had.  he tries to put WAY too much into one semester.  the course was very repetative, and likes if you have strong opinions

This class started out alright and he's got a good personality, but he doesnt really teach how to write, and even though he says he wants other opions, he really doesnt. If you write in your papers what he wants to hear he'll give you a 100%.His paper topics never make sence. Theory (institutional racism) of class gets old fast. easy 4.0 though.

I just dont like him much... Is that a bad thing? I did like him, really.. and then halfway through.. his liberalness got to me and the class changed from Evo. Of American Thought to Evolution of his liberal thoughts on racism and discrimination.

One of the best professors I have ever had and would definitely take a bullet for this man. 
He genuinely cares about his students and their success; often, he makes himself accessible to students after lectures to answer any additional questions. Outside of that, he is super laid-back and chill in both his teaching style and grading.
Very easy-going professor who sometimes even stays after class to make sure that you really understand the material.

A difficult course made enjoyable. By far the best professor I've ever had. Has an obvious passion and can teach difficult material in a way that makes sense. I personally never was stressed on a deadline. He is incredibly lenient and extends assignments based on factors many professors don't even consider. Cares about students.

Professor Alan is an all-around good guy, and I genuinely enjoyed waking up and going to his class. While the tests can be challenging sometimes, if you do the proper studying beforehand, then you should be well prepared. Always in a good mood and made learning interesting, relevant, and fun. Would highly recommend him to anyone.
Best professor I have had at MSU so far

Very nice and chill but the class is literally three exams that are mostly on the insane amount of readings he gives you. If these were assignments it might have been easier but if you do bad on one test you're cooked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's okay, seems like a good guy, but the way he teaches is just droning on and on, as well as going off topic often. This class is graded mostly by exams (75%), which makes it especially irritating when he doesn't fully cover some topics in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy, but his lectures often bored me but it would be amazing for someone really interested in geography, he knows what he's talking about. Grade is based on 3 exams and attendance, and 10 extra points if you visit his office hours. No textbook required and attendance is mandatory.

There are 3 tests throughout the course which are the only assignments in the class. The class is super lecture heavy, but the professor goes off on tangents that aren't relevant a lot so it's important you pay attention because his slides also don't give you a lot of information. He's a great person though and super nice and do the class readings!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love this professor as a person, however his class is literally graded on 3 exams and attendance. His exams aren't overly difficult but if you make one too many mistakes it can easily jeopardize your grade.

By far my favorite teacher at MSU! He is so excited to teach each class, which makes it enjoyable. The only issue I have with him is that there is no study guide, and the grade is based on 3 tests. This caused me to get a lower grade than I wanted because the exams were so random. I learned a lot and genuinely loved coming to that class every day.

Very very hard course for an ISS 200 level. He's an interactive and nice Prof. I would save yourself the trouble and take a different course. Way too hard to be a 200 level. You have zero assignments, class is based off 3 exams (including the final.) The exams can be tricky and require lots of studying. You must attend every class! No curve either!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: by far my favorite professor. I was really sad to hear he is retiring, but it is well deserved. He has been at it for a long time. He really did make learning more enjoyable. Thank you, Dr. A.
He was a good professor just talked a lot and if you aren't interested in his subject you won't like his class. He can be fun and I like him as a person just wasn't a huge fan of his class

Alan is bound to be one of your favorite professors during your time at MSU. He is full of life stories and makes the lectures fun. As for the way he has his course set up, your grade is based off of 3 exams so if you mess up on one of the exams, your grade is going to be iffy.

Dr. Arbogast is such a dad, in the best way possible. Content of the lectures were boring (if you're not into geography) but Dr. Arbogast made it 10x better. You're only graded on 3 exams and then attendance, but they're all easy as long as you take notes. Overall, Dr. Arbogast is a silly guy and his class is pretty easy.

I really enjoyed his class. He was very engaging and didn't take the GenEd too seriously, like I think many other professors who teach them do. He seemed to really care about his students and gave credit just for coming to talk with him at office hours. I also felt like the things he taught were actually worth learning.

There are many other easy ISS classes, good guy. Only three exams, no assignments. So if you do poorly on one, you fail. He does not know how to teach because he yaps the whole two hours. People leave in the middle of his lecture because he goes off topic.I had to teach myself everything, and his lecture slides are only pictures.TAKE A EASIER CLASS
