Super nice guy and loves what he does. The course is basically geo and the concept are hard to connect as the course bounces all over. Only 3 exams so it everything he says matter. Lots of relevant content but class seemed to drag on quite a bit
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Arbogast is a girl dad to the core. He made the course so much fun and while blunt at times he was incredibly kind. He was very understanding about my test anxiety, and was overall very supportive. His class is lecture heavy and his slides are mainly pictures. So every word counts as anything he says is fair game for exams! 10/10 class!

only 3 exams. class was hard to connect but lots of real life examples that were relevant. be sure to do the outside reading as they are on the exams. you can tell he loves to teach but class can at times drag on

I loved this class and I loved Dr Arbogast! He made lectures super engaging, and he's really funny! You can also tell that he loves what he's teaching! The tests can be kind of tricky but overall not too bad! Just make sure you do the homework and show up to class for the points! If you have the chance to take a class with him I highly recommend!

He is a great guy but the class is doing to much to be a uni req. only three exams but they make up the entire grade so if you do poorly on one you are screwed. Also wasnt aware that it would be turned into a geo course when it was just labled as Big ideas iss.

Dr. Arbogast was pretty laid back, and easy to follow! His lectures were very straight forward and he used a lot of real world examples to reinforce the content he was teaching. Pretty easy as long as you show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This man is an absolute diva. I love him, he said the funniest things, I was always giggling. I highly recommend him he's a king and he's amazing.

This man is incredible. Never stops talking about his wife or his daughters, we love a girl dad. He gives his lectures with a good mix of actual knowledge and his personal life experiences. If you don't appreciate a woke professor, he's probably not for you, but I appreciated it. Love you Alan, keep up the good work king!

ISS205 is mainly a prerequisite, and the median grade across every professor for this course is a 4. However, he attempts to be different and unique by making this class harder than every other ISS. He believes a small percentage deserves a 4 even if everyone does well. This makes it completely unfair for his students compared to other professors

Arbogast was my favorite professor this semester! His lectures were really interesting, and he gave out study guides before each exam which were very helpful. He's very easy to talk to and understanding. If you attend lecture + pay attention and do the readings, an A is very possible.
Love this class! His lectures are engaging and really interesting to listen to

ISS 205 is mainly a prerequisite that students take, he makes it way to difficult and it is definitely not Big Ideas in Social Science. It should just be called current events and geography. He brings up current events and then gives his very liberal opinion on it attempting to brainwash other students.
Alan Arbogast is the man.

Really like the guy and his lectures, but I feel like he should make the lecture material actually available to the students instead of penalizing them for not retaining every word of what he says. His slides are basically just pictures, and are hard to make sense of after the class. His exams were fairly tough, but easy enough to get atleast an 80
He has good energy when giving lectures but the class just seems off. Should have just called it geology. He also loves brining up current events and giving his very liberal opinion on the situation.

I enjoyed this class a lot, especially gaining more knowledge about Michigan history as well as what is going on in other countries. I know that I would sometimes come late, but that didn't affect my learning, but I found that the exams were tough even though I would study in advance. Overall, great class and had a great semester with you!

Professor Arbogast is THE best professor I will ever have. His exams are hard and very outside-of-class video-heavy, but his lectures are entertaining if you interact. His wife is a mental health therapist, and it shows. A girl dad who loves what he's doing and is passionate about what he is teaching: if you can take a class with him, YOU MUST.

Professor Arbogast was really good at making class interesting and keeping the energy up.  He was a really fair grader, and would correct test answers if they were confusing and a lot of us got them wrong, blaming himself instead of students.

There's a decent amount of reading involved, but honestly you could probably get yourself to a 3.0 just by showing up and paying attention in class. Dr. A knows his stuff and is more than willing to answer questions for as long as necessary for the class's understanding. Great dude who really cares about his students!

Dr. A is one of the best professors i have had. He really cares about his students and his lectures are very engaging. Its easy to get an A in his class if you just listen in class and watch the videos or articles he posts for before class. He used top hat in my class and had 5 pop quizzes and took attendance but it wasn't daily.

Amazing professor, and definitely cares about his students. Grades very clear - 5 of 6 quizzes, 10 of 12 attendance dates. Very much girl-dad energy. Makes class fun, and enjoys what he's teaching. Would absolutely take again.

I took 206 online. There were no video lectures like in my other online classes. The lectures were made up of pages of reading. There was also a textbook to read from. Very reading heavy. Grade is made up of 14 quizzes (16 quizzes but 2 are dropped), 3 papers (pretty easy), and a final exam. The quizzes were tricky but open note and timed.

Online class taught entirely by the TA. Never communicated with Arbogast at all. Class was fairly easy. A few HW assignments and the exams were easy IF you read his notes. I briefly skimmed the notes, then copied and pasted all of his notes into a word document and used the search tool to look for relevant words. I 3.5 the class.
LOVE HIM! Very interesting, very enthusiastic, a bit difficult but totally worth it.
Great Teaching Style and Clarity. Course is relevant to current events and a must for anyone interested in understanding the interconnectedness of our planet.

I had him in sp. '96 and still remember how great he was. The class was very interesting.   I almost switched majors because of him and his class.  Also, very helpful during office hours.  Would highly, highly recommend.  (I only knew the course # because I kept the book (5th ed.) and the info is on the SBS sticker - that's how much I liked it!)
great teacher!
Very interesting! His tests are tricky but class is great.
I really enjoyed Ayman's lectures and I learned a lot in his class, I recommend him as a professor.

Inarguably one of the best professors I've had. I went into class looking to fulfill a language requirement and have left with an Arabic minor. I'm beyond excited to next semester! There's a lot of homework, but he's very good on grading. He makes the textbooks and curriculum, so he knows his shit. Overall, a great professor!

Absolutely amazing professor. Makes learning a tough language accessible and fun. The textbook that is used in the beginning of the course can be found online for free. Lots of homework in the beginning but drops off @ end. Probably my favorite professor I've ever had at MSU and I wish I could take more courses with him. Very funny and caring guy!

Professor Mohamed is honestly the best professor I have had at MSU. He truly cares about his students, and he works so hard to make sure you learn. He's incredibly understanding and truly wants you to do well. He's so good at making you more confident in your skills, although he will really push you. Every single one of us loves him.

Dr. Mohamed is truly my favorite professor!! Despite the circumstances, I never felt more connected with the professor and students than in this class! I can tell he is passionate about teaching the Arabic language and cares so much about his students!

Professor Ayman is my favorite professor!! He is incredibly sweet and caring towards each of his students and is very understanding. Although the material can get difficult sometimes, he is always willing to help both inside and outside of class. The class was taught extremely well even being online and it is definitely my most enjoyable class:))

This man is my favorite professor that I've had so far, he genuinely cares about your language acquisition and tries to make every class useful. I knew almost nothing of Arabic when I first started and he has helped me to be able to read and converse in simple ways. He's the best!!!
Best professor ever!!! He really cares about students and hes such a nice person. He is always available both inside and outside the classroom. I really enjoyed class with him.

This man has a HEART OF GOLD. The actual subject is difficult but Dr. Mohamed is a phenomenal teacher. He definitely cares about everyone and wants you to do well. He is easily one of my all time favorite teachers. To do well in this class, you NEED to show up, and do the textbook reading and listening. Get ready to speak a LOT in class.

Ayman is amazing, 11/10 prof. He is super understanding that the language is hard and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He also did a really good job of proctoring an online class in a way that felt personal. Homework is necessary for learning the material but it's not overly difficult!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Learning Arabic is super difficult and Professor Mohamed puts in a lot of time to making sure you understand the material. He's a very lenient grader as long as it's clear you're making an effort and is very helpful. Definitely one of the best professors I've had at MSU.

This man is the light of my life. He cares about everyone in his classes so much and is very flexible on due dates if you talk to him. He will grade you easier if you participate in class and turn in all your homework. Once he gave me credit for a conversation hour when I played Arabic hangman for an hour instead. He's a saint.

Yo, this man is the best. He is a gentle grader, because Arabic is hard af, but if you dont know anything, dont expect to pass. Hes funny, but v quiet, but its good. Hes the best ever, and I dont know a single person who has taken his class and wouldnt take a bullet for him

SWEETEST MAN ALIVE!! He is so cute (such a dad) and teaches Arabic so well. He grades pretty leniently because he knows how tough the language is but he also makes sure we learn our stuff. He's very quiet (kind of mysterious) and doesn't talk much but I would take a bullet for this man.
Honestly the best TA I have ever had. She made going to class worth it and I enjoyed every lecture. Professor A puts effort into being engaging and she is very funny.
Amazing Professor. She is super kind and down to earth. All you need to do is show up and participate in the discussion and you'll do just fine! Probably the best TA I have had so far.

While I do genuinely believe that she is well-intentioned, Professor A is condescending and passive-aggressive towards her students. 
Her recitations are easy, and I think that she does care about her students' success, which is awesome. She just really needs to work on speaking to people in a kinder way if she wants to make it as a teacher.
Professor Ismail was amazing!! I would recommend her to anyone in the university. She was constantly kind and funny. 100% would take again.
She makes classes really fun, she's very honest and down to earth, and as long as you put effort into class you'll do good.

Dr. Thompson (as she prefers to be called) was so sweet and I loved listening to her lectures. The course was relatively easy and even if you didn't go to class, you could just read the book and 4.0. I would recommend everyone take psychology of women with Dr. Thompson! It opened my mind so much and she gave such great insight.

I LOVED psy 101 and Dr. Aymor. If you do all of the assignments, required research hours, and understand the content to succeed on the closed note exams, you will 4.0 the class. This class is effort based. What you put in is what you will get out. If you go to class and take notes and study you will be fine. The workload was not bad at all.

If you're thinking about taking a class with Professor Aymor, do it! She's hands down one of the best professors at Michigan State, and it's clear that she genuinely cares about her students. If you're communicative with her, she's more than willing to make accommodations for you. In addition, the content that she teaches is incredibly interesting!

I had Dr. Thompson for PSY101, and while I wasn't a fan of some of the content, I really liked her as a professor! She made accommodations for students who did not want to do in-person recitations, and she had clear expectations. Also the final exam was optional, which was pretty cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy class, but not the most interesting. You get a 3% boost in your total grade for perfect attendance, there's plenty of extra credit, and exams are based off of practice problems (at least 50% the same). Cheat sheet & calculator for all exams. I didn't learn anything new from 3 months of statistics from high school algebra 2.

While she is a very friendly person, she is a terrible teacher. I don't know how the university would allow her to teach. She is very difficult to understand because she has a strong accent. On top of that, she does not know how to explain concepts at all.

Prof Alin is a very very nice lady and she loves what she does. She comes into class smiling and will ask everyone how their day has been. She is Turkish and has a very strong accent. She tends to take the old fashioned or longer route to solving problems and doesnt  know how to use a calculator. Shes always there to help. She gives random EC.

Not a bad class but would not take again. It was a bit of work for an online asynchronous class. You have zooms that you have to record and turn in (40 minutes each), and an interview to conduct over zoom as well. She was very sweet but would not recommend if you are looking for an IAH that is minimal work.
She is a very racist professor don't talk about your culture because she was rude when I spoke mine
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is very flexible and as long as you do the work for the class is will not consume your time and is a great IAH to take.

I enjoyed this class. a lot is busy work but everything was posted to D2L at the start of the semester. modules with a variety of assignments. many different modes of learning like through a book, movie, and short lecture videos. easy grader. two essays and online discussions. I would recommend for an IAH!!!!

CEM 251: This class was hard because of how fast he moves through lectures. He skips steps because he says that they should be obvious and teaches material that goes beyond the scope of the course. Friends in 252 said they had never seen several topics he lectured on for Unit 3. Exams make up 2/3 of your grade and the final is cumulative.

CEM 251 This class was extremely difficult because of how fast he moves. He barely explains the steps for anything and includes information that goes beyond the scope of the course. Friends in CEM 252 said that some of the things he lectured on were topics they'd never seen before. The first two exams were alright but the cumulative final was not.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He teaches his lectures like a review. Multiple times he will ask a question in lecture and the class with go silent because he never fully taught the material. The final was extremely hard. I would recommend you take this class with anyone else if you want a 3.5+.

Avoid at all cost, took for cem-251 said he would curve the grades in the beginning of the semester then later said he never said that. Test heavy you don't actually learn anything in class. Graded on quiz exam and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took him for CEM 251. He was a very fair professor. You have to study a lot for this course. If you put in the time you will succeed. I recommend taking him.

I took him for Orgo 251, you are only graded by a few things, so you HAVE to get good grades. He doesn't like to answer emails, I sent him emails about my quiz scores being rounded down like a MULTITUDE of other students. He gaslight me and never changed my scores back to their original number of points…..Also that final was hard asf, have fun ig.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took CEM 251 and the class wasn't so bad, same goes for the first two exams. But the final exam…..yeah idek. Also he takes forever to respond to emails, I emailed him about my quiz scores being rounded down AND provided proof. Yet all he kept saying was that I my score dint round down, even though it went from an 80% - 72%…..

Professor Borhan overall was not bad but the cem 251 TA's constntly mess up and make mistakes. I took him for orgo 1 and if you try hard youll be fine but he kinda doesnt care. you can tell he likes upper level classes better
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It wont let me select, but I took CEM251. Honestly, he was not a bad professor. He expects you to understand what was just taught in lecture immediately. Quizzes are all online (not lockdown browser), and homework isn't bad. Its a challenging subject, you do have to put in extra work and actually go to class.

Borhan likes to ramble in lectures, but only specific points matter. Graded on just 3 midterms and a final. Plus a little extra credit!

I hear from previous students that he likes his students to think the course is harder than it is, so it pushes everyone to work their hardest in the class. There tends to be a curve at the end because of this.

Overall, this professor was tough. We were graded on basically only midterms, and no lectures are recorded and no notes posted, so can't miss class. Orgo 2 is just a very hard class, but the midterms were challenging. Some extra credit given. Curved the grades at the end. Generally a very fair professor and listened to feedback on grade concerns.

Not sure what some of these rates are but he must have changed. He is not rude whats so ever. I think he's an amazing professor who knows what he's teaching. He goes over the mechanisms and shows you many examples. This class is test heavy but if you study or read a book, you can get 3.0 or better. 352 is also hard in general but he drops things.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Condescending and disrespectful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I feel like in a normal scenario that Babak would not be as bad, had the professor before him not been absolute garbage. Babak didn't care that we don't know the fundamentals, nothing is learned. He did provide a lot of help but was condescending and rude when we asked questions. The review sessions were extremely helpful, but he could not teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Barondess is a nice guy and good to get along with. Unfortunately, his exams a written pretty poorly and many questions do not make much sense. This is difficult because exams and quizzes make up the entire grade. He also tends to ramble during lecture so it is difficult to tell whether he is lecturing or talking just to talk.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Barondess is a good guy, but, unfortunately, his exams are so heavy, and that's all you get graded on + quizzes. He also rambles on a lot, so it's hard to tell whether he's going on a tangent or whether you'll be tested on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you go to class, listen, and put in effort, you'll do well. Students who rated him poorly likely lack sufficient attention span and discipline. Dr. Barondess does ramble sometimes, but what he says is relevant to course content, which is straightforward and interesting for people who pursuing careers medicine and public health.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're a student that puts in an average amount of effort by going to lectures and actively listening, you will be fine. All content is covered in lectures, and grading based on 6 quizzes + 4 exams. First few weeks of learning statistic interpretation is boring but after that it gets interesting. The reviews made me nervous, but he was great!
He was clear in teaching and a lot of this class was common sense. hes a cool dude tbh and the tests r easy if u take enough notes and he drops one exam and one quiz
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not listen to the hateful reviews. Insanely helpful outside of class, lectures are easy to follow even for someone with ADHD, and the class is very interesting. The workload/tests/quizzes are very manageable but hard if you don't pay attention. I've written some awful reviews on here but this guy does not deserve the hate he has.

Will just put up a picture and lecture about it for 90 minutes. Narcissist and loves talking about himself. Was obviously bullied when he was younger. Constantly likes to remind students that he's a forensic epidemiologist with an interest in X, Y, and Z. Mentored a grad student who now teaches at Wayne who's been indicted on multi murder charges.

Would get off topic during lecture or repeat the same ideas, didn't verbally add much significant information to lecture slides. Would maybe get through 4 slides in the almost 2 hour class. You can pass the class by self teaching yourself (reading slides and taking notes on your own) and going to office hours with the TAs about exam questions.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. take any other class or switch your major, seriously. In my four years of undergrad I have never had a worse teacher. An EMBARRASSMENT to the university.

class should be renamed psychological torture 390
seriously find any other class to satisfy the credit. any. other. class.

Do not take any of this man's classes. Thinks he is "generous" while doing the bare minimum. Awful lecturer, awful human. He doesn't care about his students and talks for over half the class about himself and spends maybe 30 mins of lecture time on actual content. Avoid at all costs, if this class is required: switch majors. Seriously, don't take

Do not take this class, or any of this man's classes. He is an awful professor who honestly acts like he wants you to bad. He is a staunch grader that won't round even at a .01%. He doesn't do ANYTHING other than coming into lecture (meaning everything is online and made from years passed) he is makes critical mistakes constantly. 0/10 prof.

Professor Barondess was an incredible instructor for spring 23. He understood and accommodated to the struggles of the semester. He reached out many times to check in; and was sure to respond to our emails if we responded. Lectures are very interesting just be sure you are interested in the material. Lectures and quizzes make up all of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never taken an online class that was so horrible before. The lectures are long and provide little information that is actually needed on the exams. The "study guides" with questions and topics for students to understand are essentially useless - the exams feature questions and topics you aren't told to even learn! Horrible. TA was bad too.

Barondess is the only professor that teaches this class so there is no way of getting out of it. Your grade is based off of only 4 exams and one gets dropped. He lectures for the full two hours, so taking notes can be difficult. I tried going to office hours for him and I found it hard to talk to him. Extra credit saved me - but don't depend on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No learning objectives and his lectures were impossible to take notes on because it was just him talking. Class only graded on 4 exams which he allowed us to drop one this year. He also randomly added an extra credit quiz at the end of the semester. Was going to use the respondus camera for exams but our class bullied him out of it.

As god is my witness I almost jumped off the red cedar of how annoying this professor is at being off-topic while at the same time only having 4 exams that are insanely difficult. I will literally build a teleportation machine so I can go in the past and stop myself from taking this class and starting my chronic depression. Please save yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Narcissist and self-centered. Im interested in learning about public health, not his life story, achievements, opinions, and what he thinks we should think.

I am a graduating senior, and Dr. Bardoness was the worst professor I have encountered throughout my time at MSU. He's a decent guy and I received a 4.0 in his class. However, his lectures are terrible and with his organization of the class is nonexistent. His "lectures" are just him rambling on without any slides and reading news off his phone.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unclear, arrogant, and condescending. There are three tests that make up your entire grade. I went to every lecture up until the first test, took notes, studied for two days-- and I don't normally study-- and then received a 53%. I then stopped going and started self teaching the material and received 91% and 94% on the last tests. He's bad. Don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Barondess is a horrible teacher, a horrible professor, and this class is absolutely not worth your time. The material itself is not too hard, but his lectures are terribly unorganized and he spends half the time bragging about his own achievements. Didn't show up to both of the his appointments with me and left me waiting in Fee for hours. Bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Barondess truly is a genius. Although sometimes he may not always be easy to follow, this class is an upper level epidemiology and it should be challenging. I think his way of teaching is exactly how other courses should be. You don't want to miss class because he says things of importance! Also our understanding and thoughts count.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Takes two hours to make a point about one thing. Nice guy, kinda funny, obviously knows his stuff, but those lectures get very long-winded.
There are pictures and documents shown on the projector, no "real" notes. He just talks to the class so it is hard to take notes.

ive taken phy183 with Bauer and it was great. BUT phy184 was lowkey buns. just make sure you're watching the videos and have a good idea on how to use the equations, all the exams is mc and all math. the final is all mc too but there were a couple of mc questions that were not math.

Lectures are absolutely horrible, but if you know how to teach yourself the material, you will do well in the class. Gives a whole 8% extra credit if you do the McGraw Hill textbook assignments. Exams are an exact copy of the homework questions, and you are allowed a single sheet of paper front and back for formulas. Overall, an easy A.

I took PHY184 online, however the online lectures were HORRIBLE. The course itself was well organized, but the online learning environment was unorganized, randomly thrown around content, no real direction. A LOTTT of self-teaching required. The prof is chill, exams are easy-ish but definitely could tune up his "lectures".

Took this course online since I took AP Phys C:Mech in high school. Lectures are okay, obviously lots of problems to do since no in person component. Book he wrote himself is like $75 on LONCAPA. 3 exams including final, you get one custom formula sheet for midterms and two for final. 50% homework final grade is nice as well.

Never showed steps on HOW to solve hw problems, so I spent SO MUCH TIME struggling and googling solving processes for them. Textbook didn't help much either. Basically you have to teach yourself all the equations, how to use them, know when to use them. Your grade is 50% HW, 25% for 2 midterms, 25% Final, and he offers extra credit which can add 8%
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bauer was a great professor and the lecture videos were really well organized. I think overall MSU physics sucks but Bauer was the best I have had so far. The exams are all heavily curved for the online section so I would highly recommend taking the online sections if you can. It is more work than in person, but the work pays off.

Physics really isn't that hard of a class but I really don't recommend taking the course online. There's just so much material to cover I really would recommend taking the course in person for your own benefit to get assistance if needed. Wolfgang is a funny professor and he does his best to help his students, but even so I recommend doing inclass
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He uses LON-Capa for all his homework except for the McGraw questions you must take weekly for the book he co-wrote. Offers NO extensions, even if you have accommodations, and will give a snarky attitude in his emails whenever you ask about something you're having difficulty with. Lectures are a joke, you're better off watching videos or reading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The lecture videos were long and I didn't learn much from them, however most of the tests were the same as the LON-CAPA questions just different numbers. You get a cheat sheet for the exams so as long as you write down how you solved each homework problem, you should do well. Go to the help room if you aren't able to solve the homework questions!

A lot of the information is in the textbook but even then there are still quite a few homework problems you wont ever understand unless you go to office hours about them, but he explains them incredibly well in person so its not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I hate physics but Dr. Bauer really made it bearable for me. Lecture videos were never too long and very clear, and if you do the HW and extra credit assignments you're already at a 58%. There are difficult topics and HW problems, but you just have to go to office hours. The exams were exactly like the homework. He really tries to help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If nothing else, prof. Bauer makes his expectations clear. The lon-CAPA covers every possible exam question, so you'll do well if you understand these. The asynchronous/online format leads many people to cram right before each test, so I can understand the misplaced emotions from others. It's on you to ensure your own understanding.

Ngl, exams are questions from the hw and he curves them. But the hw is still very hard as he does not provide all equations. The textbook does not help, and I would attend help hours for sometimes up to 12 hours a week. Still better than P-Cubed, as they are the same but P-Cubed has group projects and less time (more effort).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Bauer is one of the best at MSU. The class is graded on Lon Capa homework, 2 midterms, 1 cumulative final, and textbook readings. Seems like a lot but it's the same as going to an in-person physics lecture 4x /wk. Pack your exam sheet to the MAX and you will be set. Totally doable to 4.0 if you truly want it.

Homework is 60% of overall grade and LON-CAPA makes you want to walk on legos 24/7. 2 Midterms with no study guides and just rewritten equations used in past hw. So right every problem on the formula sheet and pray it is on the midterm. Final Exam is 25% of overall grade with two formula sheets. Do not take 183B just take in person.

Bauer is a great professor who makes the class very interesting, throwing in cool information and real world applications to physics in his lecture videos. The workload in the class is very little, but time consuming if you don't get the topics. You are allowed a formula sheet for exams and there's extra credit opportunities too.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Expects you to know formulas, lectures never help. No study guides for exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely tough class. A lot of the equations on tests are not talked about in lectures so be prepared to learn on your own if you want to take this class. No one in the class truly knows what is going on half the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Wrote the textbook and gives the absolute minimum attention to the class. Profiting off his students and won't give the time of day when the textbook doesn't cut it. All of his homework and exam problems are ripped off the internet with the values changed, doesn't even look over them to realize that he hasn't taught most equations they use.
Do not take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm just going to say have fun. The lectures did not help much and the book he wrote did not help much from all the exams we had. Every week we had a crazy ton of homework without knowing what formulas were going to work for the problems. If I was to tell you, take a different teacher for this class or you won't enjoy your semester.

The learning material for this class is a Textbook that he personally published and it is essentially useless. Be prepared to teach yourself how to do all of the homework, and quiz questions as you will not get any help from the professor or the reading material (Do NOT take it, or take it with a different professor).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bauer is the absolute worst professor that I've ever had. From someone with a very intense mathematical background, his lectures were completely nonsensical, and example problems were never applicable to any homework or exams. He wrote the textbook, so you can't even study it if you're confused because it's the same content!

He's fine I guess. His lecture is really confusing tho, included multiple slides including calculus that we will NEVER be using for the exam, and usually goes over questions by simply reading it but without going it with great details. The course structure is pretty good, where it offers 5% of extra credit to your grade. Overall decent course.

Professor Bauer knows his stuff, He wrote the textbook for crying out loud. The class will require you to pay attention due to its lecture-heavy style but other than that it was not too bad. Sometimes Professor Bauer will have his colleague teach but his colleague is a high-ranking nuclear physicist, so it's not like you are getting a downgrade

Professor Bauer made this class pretty fun. He often jokes around, and I think it made the class much more engaging. IClicker counts for credit so coming to class was mandatory. Weekly exams instead of just a few. The exams were pretty tough and took a lot of studying. However, lots of extra credit opportunities homework was graded heavily.

Prof. Bauer is a great lecturer. He knows the material so well. After all,he wrote the textbook we are studying. The lecture is fun most of the time. I respect him because he tries his best to make the class engaged. 
HW is the most important thing in this class; they count around 45%,I believe. Study hard for quizzes cuz most of them are difficult

Dr. Bauer is awesome, super charismatic and a good professor. Weekly quizzes are difficult but are balanced out by over 50% of your grade being homework, and participation which should = 100%. I hate physics but I enjoyed his lectures. Nothing is too extreme. I'd highly recommend at least taking Calc 1 and having a physics background beforehand.

This guy rocks. If you have to take physics I highly recommend him. He is extremely accommodating and the material is easy to understand. You are reading straight from the book he wrote himself also, which is a pretty big flex. He made me enjoy physics, I hate physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: It's quite a tragedy that he is one of the only professors who are "funny". Recommend 10/10.

Solid class. Bauer co-wrote the textbook, so he definitely knows what he's talking about. The lecture videos are well made, and are explained in a way where you can apply them to the assignments quite easily.

Professor Bauer manages to keep his lectures pretty engaging and I would say he does a good job at explaining the material. He is always willing to answer questions about practice quizzes/homework. Overall he seems like a really cool guy and his class is very straightforward. Grading always seemed fair, and he offers a lot of extra credit.

Azadnia doesn't come around much; TA-based. TA is either super critical or lenient. In my experience, TA explained the procedures so vaguely and we were confused most of the time. Really unfair that we're graded on purity/yield when the syllubus procedures are inaccurate and outdated. Difficult to prepare for labs. Goodluck!!

TA-based. Lab reports are short, and labs are mainly repeats of CEM 355. Literature assignments are annoying but easy when you know what you're doing. The last two labs (finding unknown compounds) take the most amount of time, so make sure you get comfortable with taking IR, NMR, and the melting point!

ta-based, there's like 3 different versions of the procedure so u have to ask ur ta about every step 😭 lab reports are easy. idk how many semesters tas stay with the same class but if u have indrajit he's goated

TA-based, but if you have Jenna Lepek, you'll do great! Gives you the procedures before class and helps you perform them. Some labs are based on attendance, while others on yield and appearance. Overall, a simple class if you come and do the procedure. Dr. Azadnia himself doesn't teach, but he grades your final paper at the end—pretty fair graders
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: TA based. Lab reports are mostly based on effort, but some labs (and they tell you) are very important to get right. Must prepare to know what you're going to do before class. Lab reports are due a week after which is nice. If you have Tommy Reason as your TA, you'll love the class! Albert himself is an easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Doctor Azadnia runs the overall course so you will likely never run into him; however from my interactions he is very kind and easy-going. This course is entirely based on your TA for most of the grading involving labs and etc. Lab procedures can often be confusing and you basically have to attend every lab to get a 4.0.

Dr. Azadnia is great! This is more a review for CEM 444 because as others said, you don't interact with him much in CEM 355/356. 355/356 are labs so it's pretty standard that you only interact with the TAs. 444 is an easy 1 credit lecture taught by Dr. Azadnia. He is very chill and funny. He's like a kind grandpa who tells chemistry stories

TA runs the course—Shoutout to Nikitia for being an amazing and chill TA. I also had him for CEM 444 and he was funny and chill (granted, it was a 1 credit class). You don't really interact with Dr. Azadnia much.

Like alot of reviews say, the class is heavily TA graded. Your sections TA grades all but two labs, so if you have a chill TA the class is pretty easy, despite how disorganized and vague some of the labs are. Azadnia only grades the green chem project at the end of the semester, and gives mostly everyone a 100. He also responds to quick to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had to show up to every lab in order to 4.0. Was very nice, but rarely every saw him as the TAs run the entire lab, but my TA was amazing. The course was barely any outside work from lab and lab reports weren't super serious, but that could've been the TA I had who grades them.

TA led labs. You cna finish the course early, and so you can do additional labs as an honors option/extra credit. The final project is very time consuming but not very difficult, and the grading is fairly lenient tho.

TA led course. Textbook is helpful to understand procedures beforehand but not necessary. Only time interacted with the proffesor was when giving final presentation. If you do your work, you will do fine in this course.

This class is TA heavy. However, Prof Az. is a cool guy! You can pretty much walk into his office to talk whenever. He is a friendly guy. He is super accommodating if you want to switch around your section/TA, or if you have issues within your lab group. Noting but smiles from him!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Like alot of reviews say, the class is heavily TA graded. Azadnia only grades the green chem project at the end of the semester, and gives mostly everyone a 100. He also responds to quick to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His TAs teach the material better than him, but you need to go to lectures to "know what you don't know" in order to get help from TAs. The TAs will also give you hints before quizzes. Don't get textbook. Do the labs, they are free points and easy. If you aren't understanding materials, recitation and office hours with TA will get you a good grade.
Flew through the lectures and the material kind of jumped around. He got frustrated when students weren't comprehending the material.

Really easy to talk to and was very understanding about timing and difficulties. Let me do a whole experiment the last two days of open lab. Quick replying to emails. Not very hands-on and you'll definitely work with your TA more than the instructor (as is normal).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I have not had a good experience with Dr. Azadnia regarding accommodating my disabilities. He is also difficult to communicate with via email (e.g., long response times, unclear responses).

Overall a great professor. He has weekly labs due which are not difficult, just time consuming due every Sunday. The TAs grade your labs, but most of them are easy graders and dont knock off too many unnecessary points. His lectures are very clear and he guides you on how to do the labs. Do you work, and you should receive an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. A is very clear about his expectations. I took the course online so I didn't really gain any knowledge from it but that wasn't his fault. He was not very in touch with the students as the TA's do all of the grading, but he was kind enough to invite us to study in the lab with him in the future because he felt bad we aren't learning properly.

Cool prof overall, but I don't want to say anything about grading because it really depends on your TA). Azadnia got back to emails in a timely manner, wasn't rude or condescending when answering questions, and told us what we needed in each section of our lab reports to get full credit.

He is one of the laziest professors I've ever had. He delegated most work to TA's that were obviously unprepared, and on top of that basically said to not ask him for points back on mis-graded assignments or he will go back and grade the whole thing and give you a worse grade 9 times out of 10. His laziness and unpreparedness is why he sucks.

Professor Azadnia is very friendly when you deal with him 1-on-1, but his lectures are super busy and hard to follow. I took this lab online during COVID and it honestly felt like the biggest waste of money and time. It was just copying down the lab from the lab manual and turning it in. This class would be much better in person.

He is funny and provided a lot of extra credit, although when we went online he canceled the final and replaced it with the extra credit assignment. The TA is who grades your assignment so your fate is ultimately in their hands, not a bad lab though. I never went to recitation and ended up being fine, but if you need help understanding, go I guess

The class is really led by TAs since it is a lab, so make sure you know what your TA expects. Some of them are better than others. Dr. Azadnia lectures during the recitation time, and this is helpful for the labs & learning about extra credit opportunities. This class is straightforward but will require some effort if labs aren't your thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Go to recitation every week because the final is all random/difficult things he says during recitation (it usually is shorter than 50 mins). Just work with your team and ask TAs for help if you ever need help. A couple of graded labs (accuracy) but most are not based on accuracy. Do the extra credit at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Azadnia is a good professor. He really sets the class up so his students will do well. A 50% is a 2.0 so he really wants his students to pass. There are a ton of points in this class and you get to drop an exam making it EASY TO 4.0. Just study a lot for the first two exams and you will be fine. Also go to the help room it does help!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I would never take another class with him again. Continuously lectured for 5 minutes past the scheduled time, made important announcements well after class had ended. Taught though examples which is not effective in chemistry since there are endless possible reactions. Rushed through all the material. Not an effective professor and inadequate.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice and interesting guy. Took CEM 355 and CEM 356 with him. He is always in his office ready to help if you need assistance with lab projects. But overall, try and get a good TA and you won't have to worry about orgo lab classes

Several labs are graded by the purity of the product you synthesize in lab, so get a good TA while you can, or switch to a good one immediately. No need to go to Thursday lecture, the slides are always posted. Pretty easy labs, but pay attention in CEM 252, a lot of those reactions make up the labs in CEM 255.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you struggle with big university-style lectures like me, the summer course-though more challenging-is a great way to get some personal attention. His analogies were sometimes confusing but usually hilarious and made the content easier to remember. He really cares about his students!

I took it over the summer and i would strongly recommend it. He made sure everyone was understanding the material and since it was a smaller class size he could go around and actually help you during class.
Took Org 2 over the summer with him. Spent every day after class getting stuff clarified. He was awesome and patient and speaks a mean Farsi.

Dr. Barnard is unfairly hated. I feel many students don't study properly and just blame her. She's very intelligent and explains concepts clearly when asked. She offers extra credit and is respectful if you are. Her exams aren't overly difficult if you study, 70%-80% is very easy, and that is good enough to 4.0

Dr. Barnard has the highest 4.0 rate out of any other chem professors. It's a hard class, but the way she breaks things down and makes it make sense. She wants her students to succeed and if you ever don't understand something, she stays after class for questions. Exams are also not worth as much as other classes. There's a lot of other grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor her exam retakes genuinely felt impossible her class averages for exams were not good I should've started studying for this class when I was like 7. Please please please avoid at all costs barnard was the professor left for me to take.

Do yourself a favor and take ANYONE else unless you wanna constantly be frustrated about your grade in this class. Is insanely condescending and talks at the speed of light, not waiting for students to even understand or grasp the concept of what is being taught. Thinks we already know how to do a problem and forgets we are learning.
Very rude and passive aggressive. Don't bother asking questions, because she won't give you an answer. Averages for all exams are 60% and she does nothing to help it. Take any other professor.
YOU WILL NEED TO RETAKE THIS COURSE IF YOU HAVE HER. VERY PASSIVE AGGRESSIVE. NOT UNDERSTANDING. NOT HELPFUL

Her class is set up in a way where you always know what you have to do, she sends multiple reminders so it's impossible to miss an assignment. Very easy class to 4.0. Lab's are actually fun but your experience depends on your group and ULAs. A lot of work for a 1 credit class but all the labs give the same experience.

Can be pretty passive aggressive but you have to move past it if you want her to help you. This class heavily depends on whether you have a good lab group or not. Lab reports and certain assignments can take forever to complete. You'll have to rely on your ULAs a lot. Really time consuming for a 1 credit course.

she's fine i guess. can be very annoying though. the structure of briggs labs is awful (idk if she made it or what) but that contributed to mine and a lot of others' terrible experience. very blunt in how she speaks, often sounding condescending, especially in emails. much more writing than any actual experiments which was disappointing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is okay in lab but her grading is harsh. She usually explains why she grades things a certain way but sometimes she does not elaborate which is a little frustrating. She comes off as very passive aggressive in her emails but is okay when interacting outside of lab.

she is very blunt and doesnt understand that for many students, this is their first time doing most of these experiments and expects everyone to understand the material just as well as her, also not great at giving constructive feedback and most assignments are graded harshly

Dr. Barnard is one of the most caring and respectable professors I know. If you come to class engaged, with your phone put away, and genuinely interested in learning, she will love you, and you will easily get a 4.0 in her course. I work for her as a ULA and think very highly of her. She is a blunt communicator, but she is a great prof overall.
Actually worst teacher I have ever taken

Dr. Barnard makes me want to jump into the Red Cedar. I think she made it her personal challenge to make her lab room as uncomfortable as possible. I cant recall a time she spoke in lab where she wasn't yelling at someone. She is so rude that it makes me wonder what happened in her life to make her this way.

Dr. Barnard is the most condescending, rude, disrespectful, intolerable, unpleasant professor/teacher I have ever encountered in my 18 years of living. I hate her so much. If you have questions she will NOT answer them, and she will direct you to the Friday email that also does not answer your questions. I have more to say but I am at word limit.

s long as you show up to class, do your work, participate, you should be fine. Barnard herself is really intimidating and can often be rude, but most of the lab is run by the ULA's. So for the most part it shouldn't be super difficult to 4.0 in the class.

Dr. Bernard seems intimidating at first, but only if you're screwing around. She's actually very nice and helpful if you treat her and her lab with respect. This class isn't a free A, but it's really not that hard if you just complete your assignments with standard effort and show up to lab when you need to.

Barnard is incredibly disrespectful and rude. Trying to get a 4.0 in her class is almost impossible. Barnard was never moving in the best interest of her students. she says if youre sick stay home... NEVER miss one of her labs. will probably ruin your grade. don't even bother asking her questions either- she will just belittle you or your group. rely on your ULA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She literally laughed at me and my lab group because we didn't explain something correctly and said that our idea was not good. Not a good or helpful professor. Also randomly started grading so harsh halfway through the semester.
Comical. The only way I can describe

She is useless when it comes to asking questions and is so rude and condescending when you ask her for help. This professor is honestly so inconsiderate and rude. After being severely ill and missing an exam she provided no flexibility. She also is a very fast lecturer giving nobody time to understand anything. She's condescending and passive aggressive. She also never takes that mask off idk

Please listen to the reviews that say not to take this woman. I had her for lab & lecture. Was by far the worst teacher I've had with the worst attitude I've ever seen. I cannot believe somebody who acts like this is a professor and has not been fired yet. So much more I could say, but please do not take her if you care about your learning or grade

Dr. B is certainly an expert in her field but the problem is that she can't understand that her students aren't. She can be very condescending if you ask her a question. I was ULA for her and I was her student. She is condescending, she creates an environment where students do not feel like they can ask for help because she will make them feel stupid. She can be a little passive aggressive and condescending, and does weird things like claims its not hybrid when it is (lecture videos posted, and no attendance points lol). But she is pretty smart, and it's not hard to 4.0. Could be kinder, but not bad.

Lots of work before class. Expected to know the content before coming to class. Only the beginning 20 minutes of class are spent going over material, the rest is group work with jamboards. Avoid this professor at all costs. This will be your worst class, despite it being a single credit.

No new subject matter is covered in classes than which is covered in preclass work. Her exams are notoriously difficult and if you don't like SIPS maps you're sol. Her attitude comes off as very forward and bossy while I know she does care about students she makes it very hard to believe. If you have the option to take cass or saraha take them.
Poop teacher. Condescending not helpful. Take some1 else.

She must think that everyone automatically understands the content. She went over mass amounts of content in 1/4 of a class period and expected everybody to get it with nothing provided except more graded opportunities.  I'm giving her a 2 instead of a 1 because she would help you in depth 1 on 1 during her office hours that nobody else goes to.

It's a chem lab. Barnard has no control over it, just like all the other LB chem lab profs. It's a ULA-run course, which is honestly hell, but Barnard does her best to help out and step in when the ULAs give blatantly wrong advice, which happens more frequently than is acceptable.

I don't understand why people hate her. If you ask a question answered in the syllabus, she'll answer your question and tell you where to find more information, and other students think this is judgmental? she makes the simple problems hard. dont ask her questions because you'll only become more lost. just dont take.

reviews.comment: My first issue with her was the amount of work that is due before class. You are required to read and understand content before class starts. My other issue is her mask policy. reviews.comment: Not a bad prof. She's so lazy. Gives us hours worth of content to teach ourselves before class, and then in class you just work with your group on a jamboard the whole time as she walks around in case ppl have questions. Like pls just teach me in class

She is honestly the worst professor in the department. The quiz averages for my class were almost always 50% or below. Dr. B is the worst professor Ive ever had. She is a tough grader, and marks people down for "not being able to understand their handwriting" and other silly things. This is the worst professor. If you get her PLEASE run. Just know she doesn't teach at all, and you're basically the prof at that point. Dr. Barnard has been a frustrating teacher to deal with. She is incredibly passive aggressive to students and overcomplicates every aspect of her class to the point no one knows what we're doing or learning. The TAs don't even know what we're doing since her instructions are so vague, and then she gets mad when you inevitably do something wrong.

Dr. Barnard is incredibly condescending, her instructions are vague, she makes you feel incompetent when you ask her any questions, and she does not work well with you and help you understand anything. She will not budge on due dates or work with you if you have any difficulties of any type.

I do well in chem class, but this lab makes me feel like I know nothing. The background info before each lab leaves you confused and with no idea what we will actually do in lab. She is beyond condescending, failed half the class, and barely did any instructing. If you want to pass you should go into this class already knowing chemistry or accepting that you're going to spend 6+ hours a week studying.
A very difficult professor, will not work with you if you have to miss an exam (even if you have covid). Grades quizzes/exams very hard, averages are normally 50%.

Barnard is quite possibly one of the worst professors I have ever had here at MSU. She grades very hard on the quizzes, and on top of the grading she has extremly low averages. Most horrible, inconsiderate professor I have ever had. Barnard does not know how to lecture. She also makes her quizzes extremely difficult. In my opinion, Dr. Barnard was very condescending when I asked questions. The test are very hard, but I would suggest going to the LA's office hours because they are definitely the most helpful. I think the only reason I did somewhat okay in this class was because of the LAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. B is a great prof for LB 171 and 172. She is intimidating at first, as are most professors, but once you get to know her she's awesome. reviews.comment: Make sure to use the lecture slides as your primary study guide. If it showed up in the slides, it can be on the test! reviews.comment: To do well in this class you have to make sure you are understanding everything presented in the lectures as Dr. B goes through them. It was an easy A putting in the time starting 2 weeks before the test.

reviews.comment: At first, Dr. B may not be totally likable but she is very genuine if you put in the effort to get to know her. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: A great professor- doesn't deserve the hate. Her class is tough, but the difficulty helps you learn the material better in the end. I highly recommend Dr. Barnard if you're a first year Briggs student!

reviews.comment: Dr. Barnard was a great teacher and is very passionate about chemistry. Her lectures are fast paced, so you have to keep up, but she explains concepts well and uses many analogies. reviews.comment: Chemistry is a very hard subject but she does her best to break down the material so it is easier to understand. She is very passionate about her job and it shows through her teaching. I would highly recommend her if you're a first year Briggs student.
Worst professor I've met at Briggs. I only have her for lab and I want to die every second.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. IMO she is the easiest professor of the LB Chem trio. However, this doesn't mean that her class is easy. Make sure to read the textbook, etc. She is really cool and tries her best to be down-to-earth. Honestly she may be my favorite professor (just finished my 1st year). Office hours are cool as well. Also, take lab with her!

Dr. Barnard is amazing! She is always pleasant in lecture and is extremely helpful outside of class too. It is a Briggs class so it is expected that it will be more difficult than standard university chemistry. She emphasizes the "why" to chemistry, not just the "what," which is extremely useful for future classes if you are a science major.

Dr. Barnard is a overall good professor. The content in chemistry can be difficult and she tries her best to teach it during lectures. Definitely take advantage of going to office hours if you need help! She also sometimes gives out a few extra credit points on exams which is a plus. If you put the work in you can easily get a 4.0.

Dr. Barnard is by far one of my favorite professors in Lyman Briggs. The content itself is challenging, but it's standard between all the chemistry professors. As long as you put the effort in (actually try), you can 4.0 the course. If you need help, see her during her office hours! Do not wait. She is extremely friendly and willing to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easiest 4.0 you literally just have to do a few quizzes online during the semester and a couple exams and even then he replaces your best quiz scores with your highest ones. No final exam and there were a few packback discussions but super easy overall.

reviews.comment: ISS 310 was an easy course with Dr. Marley. The class was very lecture heavy, but he would give breaks here and there. The class can become slightly political in aspects of different parties.

He also replaces the lowest grades with the highest ones. He offers some in-class extra credit, so it's important to attend lecture. Overall, an annoying but fairly easy 4.0.

reviews.comment: The content was very interesting and I found as long as you did the reading you were fine. Just know this is NOT a class you can AI or not read for. Going to class helps with understanding so much too he explains things very well in lecture.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: When I first started this class I really didn't like this professor, but as time went on I just learned to love him. It really opened my mind!

reviews.comment: Dr. Marley is the GOAT. The only people who give him low ratings are conservative corn balls who know they don't have an argument against him. He welcomes debate and additional viewpoints (it actually seems to really excite him lol) but you have to have some semblance of an idea of what you're talking about. He is also super kind and funny.

If you took AP classes in high school, the exam format should come easily to you. I would only recommend taking this class if you really enjoy this subject, because I often found myself bored.

Nice guy, and he's pretty silly. Heavy lectures, pay attention. Make sure your cheat sheet is covering all topics, you do all the reading and ask and answer questions. He gets happy when people answer his questions, so be nice to him

If you consider even remotely conservative, do NOT take this class. You're opinions are not welcomed. The entire 2 hour lecture is the professor and his TAs sharing their opinions, and then other students agreeing with them or staying silent. There is also 30-40 pages of reading outside of class. I dropped very early on.

Writing this review in past tense before I graduate. Avoid this guy for SOC161 at all costs. Even as a blue voter, this guy gives “the left” a bad name. Maybe his other classes are good, but this one is a moderates worst nightmare. Hope it's changed since I took it.

Dr. Marley is a pretty laid back, lighter-toned professor. reviews.comment: The class is structured around lectures with no direct notes and open ended discussions which are clearly opinionated and subjective, yet he grades you on definitions and clear answers even though the entire 1 hour and 50 mins is just ranting about why the world sucks. reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class and lecture, and if you are privvy to the knowledge and information of the class topic and dismantling Capitalism, you'll definitely enjoy the course. Pretty chill professor, always kept things light. It's easy to get a good grade as long as you do the readings and show up to class. ISS310 specifically don't take Marley. The man simply cannot teach. Instead of teaching he goes off on tangents about things that are so unimportant. Half of the videos shown in class aren't available on any first-party streaming sites cause they got taken down for misinformation.

reviews.comment: this professor is so amazing whoever gave him a 1 just can't handle science and research challenging their political beliefs. he welcomes debates and invites people to challenge him, if he wins the debate and you're salty about it, that doesn't mean he's a bad professor it means you are a limited thinker.

Ben is by far my favorite professor I've had at MSU. His class has fully changed my views on this world. His lectures focus on the interconnectedness of climate change, inequality, colonialism, dualism and many more things that have challenged my beliefs coming into the class. A really not great professor. He seems to like what he teaches, but isn't super supportive of facilitating unbiased discussions. I get writing can be graded subjectively, but if your thoughts don't line up exactly with what he says, your grade will be spiked into the ground. Other reviews from most other classes he teaches in says he's decent, so maybe this is just an issue in some of his classes. A decent enough guy but not the best professor.

The Masked Man fallacy loves this guy. He "wins" debates by just moving on to the next topic as quickly as possible. No one who took SOC161 should rate this guy 5 with a straight face. I've heard he's a good prof in other classes (other reviews seem to like him), but definitely not this one.

Had three students teach a few lectures without giving them any kind of time to prepare.
