reviews.comment: PHL344 was one of the best classes i took at MSU thanks to Dr.Bluhm. She is passionate and caring but also very clear and firm on her grading criteria, bc she is also very clear and thorough on her lectures and explains difficult concepts easily. Her course has changed my perspective on medicine and i recommend her course for anyone in pre-health.

Super interesting intro course for bioethcis! Dr. Bluhm makes the online course super easy to understand. Lots of reading, writing, and group discussion, but that is expected for an online bioethics course. Really fair grading and is super easy to get in contact with! She also gives great feedback. She really cares about her students! Easy 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Bluhm is a great professor and clearly cares about her students. The course is very accessible, and was one of my favorite classes of undergrad so far.
Very caring and sweet professor. Its the type of professor you want to take. I highly respect her, and she respects students back.

Class is graded based on three exams, in-class activities, and reading responses. Other than exams, it's pretty much graded on participation. Lectures can be a bit boring (probably due to long class periods and uncomfortable seats), but the material is still very interesting and valuable. She is very kind and easy to get along with.

This is an online asynchronous intro course for bioethics but it was still very interesting and valuable. Lots of readings, short reading responses, and discussion board posts. Graded pretty much on participation so long as you give a respectable effort. Course was organized and easy to follow along with.

reviews.comment: Dr. Bluhm was amazing for LB 326A, this class was an intersection of ethics and medicine which was really interesting to me.  Bluhm is really caring and wants all students to succeed. This semester we had 2 papers due per week with 3 larger assignments throughout the semester with no tests because of COVID. Overall, great prof!

Dr. Bluhm is thoughtful, compassionate, and an overall great professor. She makes herself available outside of class more than she should, she doesn't require camera's on or attendance in the first place, and loves her cats like nobody's business. Hard class, but if you put in the work and time, you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Bluhm is a thoughtful, approachable, and overall great professor. I was a music major thrown into a class full of abstract neuroscientific vocabulary and I was able to succeed in this class. Definitely not easy and there is a lot of reading, but the class is valuable if you respect the time it requires.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She's very passionate and knowledgeable about bioethics and the class was very interesting. She creates a very good learning environment in the class that encourages discussion all sorts of issues, controversial or not. I definitely think that if you are doing anything involving bioethics you should take a class with her!

Dr. Bluhm was easily one of my favorite profs at msu. She knows a ton about bioethics and explains things very clearly with examples. Everything we discussed was so interesting. The tests are 7 essay questions but it is not hard to do well. There are a few extra credit points on the exams. This is a pretty easy 4.0.

Every HPS professor in Lyman Briggs teaches their course differently and Professor Bluhm taught hers from a bioethics perspective. I'm not even a health major but I found this course extremely worth-while. She is very knowledgeable in the field and navigates raw and controversial topics very easily. Definitely would take her again.

Extremely rigid and stressful. 4.0 cutoff raised to 94. Attendance policy was not clearly enforced until around week 4, then grades were suddenly penalized with no drops or real makeups. Missing one class can ruin your grade. Heavy workload for a 2xx course and little openness to questions. Strongly avoid.
Really nice professor, very understanding. Material was covered in a way that was easy to understand. Also allowed for Zoom attendance, so very accessible. Would absolutely recommend!

WRA 210!!! Super easy grading. If you turn in the projects asked you will receive a 4.0. You have plenty of opportunities to submit late work and fix work in general to receive full credit. This class involves coding and learning the basics. Your final exam is the portfolio you create and it's super easy to receive a 100% on that!

reviews.comment: He was one of the best professors I have had here at MSU. He really makes an effort to get to know his students and is incredibly understanding if you have stuff going on outside of class. Instructions for the assignments were clear and easy to understand. He really helped me a lot with my writing!

Two projects and attendance counts towards your grade, so don't skip! On-campus, the class was a breeze, online though. He made us take weekly quizzes and do an entire project with peer reviewing still. He's very unsure of himself and he wasn't prepared at all. Barely heard from him, due dates were very frequent. Try to find a more organized prof.

reviews.comment: Two major projects and a final exam. Stuart is funny in that awkward nerdy way. He cares about your learning.

Professor Thompson is very passionate about what she teaches. Attendance is mandatory but you get three freebies. Guest speakers come each week to expand on content. There's weekly reflection papers for completion points and 3 noncumulative, open note + open book online exams. Also easy honors option, just an extra reflection paper.
Very kind professor. Very passionate about Social Work. Exams online and reflections due each Sunday but not hard at all.

Tina is an amazing prof! Her class was not difficult at all, she's very understanding, down-to-earth, and isn't a harsh grader. I definitely recommend taking her classes, she makes course materials easy to understand and doesn't sugar coat anything.
She is genuinely so sweet and cares a lot about what she does. Very much enjoyed having her class this year
Tina was absolutely amazing, and even convinced me to pursue SW as a career. I am applying to MSW programs simply because of her. I cannot recommend her classes enough, she really loves her job.

I loved this professor. The only complaint I have is that there is a lot of reading but you'll just have to face facts that you just have to skim a lot of things. She is a caring person, organized, fair grader, and very clear about her expectations.

reviews.comment: The best MSW prof at MSU--- caring, helpful, passionate, and has clear instructions.

reviews.comment: Good. Good.
Nice.
love love love.
Very helpful and insightful on semester assignments-would not do my paper for me but showed me the right path to walk down to get the right grade. Blaschke and Rypkema are a good team.
She is a young teacher but is very good at becoming a great teacher. She is very helpful and insightful on questions I have asked her. Hands down a good teacher.

The professor was very nice and the class was easy 6 reflections and 6 open note quizzes. The only thing that was hard was the quizzes included a lot of stuff that wasn't talked about in class and very niche things from the book. The questions were also worded weird.

Kelley absolutely changed the trajectory of my college journey. As a psychology major, I was interested in taking this class, and now I am a double major in social work because of it. She brings in guest speakers, and she herself has a significant amount of experience in the field. Quizzes are easy and every other week, and papers every other week!

She was very sweet! There was one guest speaker a week, and homework was split between short online quizzes and short written responses. A very easy course, but she did a lot to keep it interesting. I had no problem reaching her outside of class hours, and she was flexible about attendance, grades, due dates, etc.

loved professor Blanck, most students weren't very interactive, but she was. The class is easy and catered to the social work major. she uses guest speakers to teach about real world experiences working in differing social work types, very accommodating. assignments are very easy. only downside is passing with a 93% which is only a 3.5
He made the best study guides for the exams, including the final. They are the main thing you need to study and they are what helped me get grades I was happy with on the exams.
I feel March is a great professor. He is talented and care about quality of teaching. He is super nice and every time I ask him question, he answered patiently and friendly.

Very condescending when answering questions pertaining to the course material. Additionally he uses his own documents than those provided by the school which makes learning harder. Although not all his fault understanding the lessons can be difficult. He does have office hours available as a positive. Great guy at heart I'm sure, but not professor.

reviews.comment: I loved taking this class with Bob. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students and takes time to give them valuable critiques. He is very nitpicky when it comes to each video, but you can tell it's because he wants you to learn and grow. Overall, a fun class.

Bob is very engaging and clearly cares about students' success. The projects and assignments may seem intimidating at first, but they are manageable if you stay organized and ask questions when needed. The class is well-structured, easy to follow, and enjoyable overall.

Professor Gould has lots of knowledge in news production and would be a great professor for any high-level class; however, for a 200 level class, he often didn't do enough to make sure the entire class was up to speed on the skills we were learning for the first time. Overall, he was very helpful and you can tell he cares deeply about his students.

Bob Gould is one of the best professors I've had. He's a tough grader with high expectations, but if you participate and engage, the class is very enjoyable. His fun, goofy personality makes it interesting. The required video kit is expensive, but I would take this class again.

Bob is a good professor, but he switches up. One day he likes you the next he is so rude to you. The projects are a lot outside of class, so make sure you have time for that. He also teaches and grades like this is a 400-level course even though it's the beginning of journalism for a lot of students. Does get frustrated easily. Overall, a 6/10.

Bob is a charming and funny guy, he sometimes likes to talk about fun things at the beginning of class, which created a very open and welcoming environment; everyone seemed comfortable talking. He kinda expects a lot from a 200 level class and might get frustrated if everyone missed something, but he is very helpful and accessible outside class.

He is very passionate and has a good personality. I think he fails to take into account this is a beginner class and some of the things he has us doing is very complicated and he grades pretty harsh. If you miss one lecture, especially on a day were editing, it will be very hard to catch up. Also he is hard to reach outside of class.

He really does mean well, but towards the end of semester he will give you 2-3 projects to work on at the same time and they aren't super easy. Also he will only let you have 2 absenses or he will knock your grade .5 GPA.

One the most difficult graders I've ever had and grades as if it isn't an entry level course, expecting students to already be experts and grades just so. The equipment required is also very expensive, and the course is not well-organized or easy to navigate as a student. Don't take this class if you don't have to. Ruined my GPA.

I think Bob is a fantastic professor and cares a lot about students and their learning. His grading can be harsh, especially when you don't follow instructions EXACTLY, but he wants us all to succeed and create quality content rather than allowing us to put out something we aren't proud of. He's not easy, but that's why he's a great professor.

Seems like a nice enough guy, but the course organization was horrible. Very hard to navigate syllabus, find course instructions etc, and even then they were very unnecessarily complicated. He also seemed like he didn't know what was going on lol. It's easy once you figure out what you need to do, but just a very weird organization

He is a tough grader and attendance matters to him a lot. If you miss 2 classes, your final grade will go down .5. He gives a lot of projects and grades them tough if you don't do them exactly how he wants them. It is a 200 level class but feels like it is a 400 level class with the expectations.

Bob Gould is a good professor, but this class can be difficult. There is only one exam that you take at the end of the semester that covers everything. There are are weekly quizzes you take at home on D2L, and the writing assignments are relatively easy. He certainly makes the class interesting.
You'll think that you're doing well until you get your final grade. He's picky about details and doesn't take into account that you may be a beginner. He ruined my GPA.

tbh the other reviews confused me because I had no problem with prof black. i felt like the grading was easy and while there were onlines quizzes each week, you can take them as many times as you want. the essays weren't graded harshly either. the MC tests can be tedious, but its online and open note

Professor Black has essentially created this course to tank your grade. This is not a class that prioritizes student learning, it is set up to test your ability to follow his rules. I understand that most people are probably taking this class for credit and have no other choice but if you can avoid it then I would highly recommend that you do so.

He seems like an amazing guy and the lectures are interesting. However, the course grading is a nightmare. Exams make up a huge portion of the final grade. You could get every question correct and still lose the majority of points for not writing an additional sentence for EACH question.

Do not take this class and avoid this professor if you care about your mental health and GPA. The workload is not worth 3 credits (6-8 quizzes a week, 6 essays, 4 exams) and the grading criteria for written exams is so stringent and arbitrary that even if you excel everywhere else and get the exam questions right it ultimately won't matter.

Don't look at any of these low reviews. You have 4 exams the entire semester and they are 2 essays and a hybrid true and false section, that are both done online at home. uses iClicker but not for accuracy just for attendance purposes. Honestly, i loved the class, and professor black is a great instructor.

Despite the horror stories I read when signing up for my PLS course, I enjoyed Dr. Blacks course. If you don't do the readings and look at lectures, this class will probably be impossible. Attending and taking notes, doing the readings, and basic review should be enough for almost anyone to 3.0 the course with average effort.

reviews.comment: I LOVED him. One of my favorite professors I've had at MSU. Exams 1-4 are online, and the final was in person. He was able to keep my ADHD brain focused even during an 8:30 am lecture.
The class is super interesting but be prepared to get a bad grade even if you do the work and pay attention. The exam questions are meant to be trick questions he is literally out to get you

reviews.comment: Legit my favorite class this semester, all you really have to do is pay attention to the lectures and do the exams. Exams can be hard, but he makes it easy to get half credit on questions, and you can pretty easily do decent as long as you know what's going on. Overall great prof!

Dr. Black is SO kind, funny, and such a great teacher. I am a journalism student with no interest in political science, and I was able to make it through this class. His lectures are great, and he is just an overall very likable guy.

He is a hard professor- but if you are planning on working in Policy, his lectures and coursework are completely fair. Takes up a good chunk of your time but he is so willing to help and lend a hand when needed!!!!!

i am in his online PLS 320 class right now, and can already say Professor Black is one of the best professors I have had in my 3 years at MSU. His lectures were fantastic!! I took this online and loved it. Yes, there is work. If you actually watch the videos and read the writing will be insanely easy. reviews.comment: Listen up, this class is NOT easy. Class is graded based on a midterm and final that include a multiple choice true/false section and 4 essays per exam and lecture/reading quizzes. reviews.comment: Ryan was a really good professor. He has you read a book over the course of the semester which I cannot say I loved but his mandatory lectures made up for it. ISS 325- Video Games and Revolution: I took this course over the summer.. it's interesting and fun (easier if you're a gamer), but it is SO MUCH WORK! He only taught topics that he found interesting. Attendance is mandatory if you want to do good on exams.

reviews.comment: I took this professor before and loved the class(it was also a judicial politics class). This is a similar class and I have never hated a class so much. I ended up dropping the class because I would have 2.0 it. The grading is all over the place and if you do not mention something (within the 100 words you are given) you fail the assignment.

The first half of this class was rough, but after complaints came in about the class, the professor sent out a survey and made huge changes in how the course was being conducted. My grade went from being a 2.0 to a 4.0. Very few professors would be willing to make a 180 change like that mid-semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Two books were required for the class I barely picked them up and was still able to get a perfect score on the GBR's by skimming through. The class was an hour and 50 minutes long and he talked that whole time. The exams very long in questions so it was hard to make sure you got a good grade on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved prof. Black, he's happy to teach, but this class is insanely hard to succeed in for me personally. I would definitely stray away if you're neurodivergent, the workload may take you 5x longer than others. Never got higher than a 76 on exams even after studying harshly. Great dude but a really tough class. Uses I-clicker and records lecture

Not the worst professor, he does his job, is very intelligent, and is passionate about what he teaches. I respect him for not being a lazy professor but... he's a yapper, assigns a lot of reading (I ain't reading all that), and uses i clicker. If ur lazy like me and just want easy iss credit look elsewhere. exams are difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class has very long lectures and the exams get up to 100 questions. There are numerous articles and passages assigned to read along with a book assigned over the span of the semester. If you do not have any interest or prior knowledge in politics, this class will be very hard to learn in. Professor Black is funny though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is difficult. By the time you turn in 10 C4 assignments they just get around to grading. Then when they get around to grading them you messed up, and you wrote the 9 others the same way. So, you're never given an opportunity to learn and fix mistakes in future assignments. This is all due to their arbitrary grading scedule and scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: A theme I have seen, as well as experienced is that the professors grading is "shoddy" at best and the workload is a bit much. I can agree with both of these claims. The professor is not someone I would take again, and if I could drop this class without to much difficulty in the future I would.
The class is a good idea, however, choosing this professor to teach it may have been the wrong choice. I am doing more work than any of my other courses, and I am not seeing the benefit.

For a professor that pretends to be for the students mental health he is certainly testing mine. Says that the reasons he makes you do a bunch of essays is to alleviate the stress of doing essays. I would much prefer the stress of a 2 hour essay than the grading of his TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Takes forever to grade assignments. When they do come out you have about 4 assignments all with the same issues and cant do much to fix it because your grade has already been tanked. Would be nice if they graded promptly and gave you feedback in a timely manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The format of this course is so bad that if you mess up a few small things they snowball and can basically lead to you being on ther verge of failing.

I find it interesting how I can be told "Great job!" but get a 60% on an assignment. This course prioritizes quantity over quality and cares little about whether the work you submit is good. If you are 12 letters off of the required number, he will fail you. Sad that a professor cares more about a word count than that of the words themselves.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I would rather be doing 4 exams than 60 essays. Every week you have to write about 3 essay-type papers. They are graded by the TAs who have very different views on the grading process. Minimal interaction with the professor seems to delegate everything to his TAs. No drops, so if you mess up a couple of essays you can kiss your grade goodbye.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I'm only halfway through the course and it is by far the worst class I've taken. All of the lectures he posts are from 2 years ago and he has multiple different people grading assignments, so grades are never consistent. Insane expectations for weekly assignments and readings

Professor Black seems like an amazing guy, very nice person.  However, this class is truly agonizing. To be fair, the topic of the Supreme Court isn't for everyone. But it is a 2-hour lecture, and all we do is listen to him talk and flip through slides. The homework assignments aren't terrible but you have to have read all of the material to do it.

Dr. Black's online PLS 320 class was very enjoyable. He has a bubbly personality which made listening to his lectures fun, although they were a bit long in some cases. His grading criteria for exams was very straightforward and I am happy that if you didn't get full credit there would be a reason why so you could appeal it.

This course is extremely lecture and reading heavy. However, the content isn't very difficult. The weekly quizzes are a great grade boost and the questions are reused for exams. Professor Black is passionate about judicial politics and it really shows in his lectures. Overall, a good course and not a GPA risk.

Professor Black has such a heavy lecture amount for this class. I took an online class for working while a student to make my life easier, this made it so much harder. No lecture is under an hour, making it very hard to retain information. The tests are very elaborate for being an online class with unfair grading. I would not take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took ISS210 online. I personally enjoy having the expectations/Due dates set at the beginning, *no-budge* deadlines, and playing some of my favorite games as an assignment. But, if youre looking for a more engaging session, take it in-person. Pretty sure the professor is more funny. Expect quizzes on reading and games. Outside of that, 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: One thing that sets this professor different than the rest is his ability to teach. His lectures are very engaging and clearly thought through, making his exams and quizzes easy to take - as long as you do the lectures. He was a very fair grader and made sure everyone understood the assignments every step of the way. 10/10 would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Black is a nice guy but that doesn't correlate with his class. The amount of time reading and watching lectures is outstanding. The format of the exams are not your typical exams. He does however give you the material beforehand but even then it's extremely difficult. His TA's grade your exams and most of the material is his own studies. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While I will say he is great at explaining things and his lectures are enjoyable to watch online. The exams are very book/readings heavy with much of the grading coming from the essays and short answers of exams. Usually 30-50 questions, 6 short answer, and 2 essays. TAs do all grading and not great at explanation of whats wrong, has to be perfect
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Black is one of the best professor. He really cares about students success. The class are well organized and provides a detailed understanding.  The papers are relatable to your life, and then a few quizzes that are mostly unlimited attempts. His grading criteria is very doable.

Would not take a class with Professor Black again. While he was funny and knows his stuff he is unaccommodating. Most of the things you read for the class are his own works and he expects you to explain them perfectly back to him. Multiple people in my semester had issues with him, and when confronted he was uncooperative and sometimes just rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class made me want to drop out. Exams are extremely writing heavy and has no partial credit. Reading is absolutely mandatory if you want to answer the essay questions and even then good luck. The format of the online exams is awful and I hated the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For the online class, to 4.0 you HAVE to get the books and you have to watch the lecture videos. Take good notes, he tests on what he says, not what is on the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you put the work in listening to the lectures and reading the books, it is easy to succeed in the class. Prof. Black is extremely passionate about these topics and it shows! Also loved how he didn't include any personal opinions since the course (predictably) gets into social/political issues. Overall- amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of reading and his lectures are long but hes probably one of the most caring professors at state. Hes very willing to accommodate his students and is passionate abt what he teaches, great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Black was an amazing professor. He really cares about students success. I have taken ISS305 with him as well, and his classes are very well organized. A few papers about that relate to you life, and then a few quizzes that are mostly unlimited attempts. He is caring, and his grading criteria is very easy going. Amazing teaching style!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I cannot sing enough praises for RCB. He's a great prof and his classes are enjoyable. Even his ISS 325 War & Revolution. These classes he bases off of video games and you simply write journals and take quizzes but you also learn a lot about the effect of videogames and society. Would recommend 10/10.

He tries to be funny ... but is not funny and very well a know-it-all. Regret taking this class because it tanked my 3.7 gpa. I found his test to be very convoluted and not focused at all. You will literally have to remember every little thing he said or that you read. Would not recommend whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lack of care for the online class over the inclass version. He should not have taught an online class concirrent with the regular version, as he got very sloppy.

Professor Black makes a dry topic interesting. He gives a 5 minute break in the middle which really helps me get through. If you dont do the readings, you wont get an A. He makes a lot of jokes during lecture which keeps you on your toes.

He is funny and sarcastic to listen to. He knows the information he teaches well. Partly because this class is basically all his data. There is ALOT of extra reading. No official text book but like 3 books and regular research articles you must read to pass. He is condescending and so are his TAs they know they are smart and are rude in email.
easy homework and quizzes, light workload, fair grader, easy 4.0
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Black was the first professor I ever had for an online course. His video lectures are easy to follow and he has a really good sense a humor. He also offers a bit of extra credit. I recommend taking a class with him.

I took one of his classes online over the summer and overall it was an easy A. Basically we read a handful of chapters for each module and then toke a quiz and then answered a few short response questions. He even worked with me on the due dates while I was out of the country. If you do the readings you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: We had to do many papers, but the exams were extremely easy and he's an overall chill guy. The lectures could get boring half the time, but half the time they were pretty engaging. He offers a good amount of extra credit. But in general, I wasn't too fond of the class though I liked him.
I loved this class. Most of your grade is a weekly current events type paper (only about 1-2 pages). He was funny. He also uses iclickers every class that counts for points.

Best professor that I have had. Lectures were very intriguing and I like how he weighs the homework way more heavily than the final (which is the only exam). If you write down the True/False questions and answers that he does at the start of the class, 100% on the final should be no problem. Would definitely take another of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far the best professor I've ever had. He recognizes that college and life can be hard, so he is more than willing to work with you if something comes up. He's also super clear about what he wants from you- you just have to write the NAPS assignments, show up, and do well on the final. The final literally the review he gives you.
Great professor, available and accessible, humor and easy grading system.

Professor Black is a great professor! He doesn't intend to make the class difficult because he wants his students to learn. We had no midterm but did have weekly writing assignments (only 1.5 pages). He is very kind and loves to teach! Attendance is mandatory through iClicker. I would recommend him for an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Black was a great professor. Lectures were clear and also very funny. NAPS assignments (50% of the grade) were challenging at first, but became easier as time went on. Would take another class from him.
Great professor! The material was easy to learn and his lectures taught pretty much everything you need to know.

Professor Black was a great professor who always made an attempt to make lecture funny and/or interesting. The exams were SUPER easy and very straightforward. If you go to section and come to class to get attendance points, you'll 4.0 easily. You also get to use a full page cheat sheet (front and back) on all exams. Highly recommended.

Ryan is my favorite member of the Political Science department, by far! Although his lectures can be dry sometimes, he adds in personal anecdotes that usually make up for it. We had a weekly 1.5 page paper due up until after the midterm, where you had to find a newspaper article and relate it to the class. The grading for those were extremely tough
Awesome political science teacher, and very fair grader. Reading and extra work is necessary to receive a 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Easy A and non bias

Professor Black was awesome. Super clear in class, plus he puts his lectures online, so you can review. While the tests (2 of them) are not open book, he does allow a 1 page (8.5 x 11) cheat sheet, which can have anything you want on them. The exams are easy, as long as you go to class and review. Definitely recommend him.

His lectures are super long and boring. He thinks hes funny be he rarely is. The class overall is easy and would be nice if his lectures didn't kill the material. He also says "normative" all to often.

Personally, I felt that lectures were boring. If you took AP Gov in high school, this class is going to be more than a breeze. There are clicker questions every day for points, but he drops your 4 lowest participation scores. Assignments every Sunday. Midterm and Final are easy--you  can make a cheat sheet with whatever you want on it. He's funny.
super funny and easy!
amazing!

He's a nice guy and keeps the class fun. Knows the material well and makes everything clear in class. Chose an interesting textbook to teach with too and the textbook is good as well. Not too hard of a class considering you can bring notes to the tests. You need to do the work but if you do it's an easy 3.0 at least

Class is somewhat hard but a 4.0 is easily obtained if you regularly attend class and section meetings. Prof. Black is super chill and funny. He's relatively young so he can still relate to his students.
Teaches well and keeps the class pretty entertaining.

I recommend taking her CSS101 class in person because of how interactive she is with her students. She makes a point of learning all her students' names and talking to them before class. She can be hard to reach sometimes, but she is busy with two young kids. If you pay attention to lectures and use the note-taking guides, you will do well.

Erin is incredibly kind and helpful. She can sometimes be late on responding to emails, but she has kids so it is understandable. As far as the class, it was the easiest of my 100 courses, and as long as you complete study guides and do the note sheet for exams, it will be the easiest 4.0 you will get. Overall a very nice person.
Easy class, just keep up on work, and you should be good!

This professor was enjoyable in class. She went around the room and spoke individually to students before class started. However, the lecture was not my favorite. After class we often had online discussion forums; she required you to reply to other student's discussions. I would be confident for exams, then it went out the window at the first Q.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Idky she is not rated well. I had zero issues in class with Erin, everything is straight forward and I felt that I not only learned while in class but retained information too. Also, it's a level 100 class it's not hard, just do your homework and study for tests and you will 4.0 it easily. Do not be worried for this class!! :)

Had her for CSS101L in-person and it was quite a straightforward experience. Weekly quizzes, a couple of lab reports, and that was pretty much it. If you paid attention to the lectures you would be pretty set for a decent grade. She even tells you what will be on the quizzes.

I took CSS101L online and had a relatively good experience. Weekly assignments were doable, and graded fairly. Not too much work/content compared to other labs. I would recommend taking this class online vs in person, I had a good experience while those that took it in person weren't as positive. Saves a lot of time too.

This class was horrible. She would give guided notes with material not covered in the lectures making it impossible to fill out. Everything in this class was a guessing game, and good luck emailing her if you have a question. Exams were absurdly difficult, even being open notes the notes did not cover the material on the exams. I would avoid.

Some information was not accurate on lectures. Tests are extremely hard, and some information was NOT covered in lecturers. She never responded to my emails when I had questions, so shes very hard to reach and leaves you on your own for this class. Definitely harder than any other 101 class Ive taken.

Overall, the lectures were old and the information on the study guides didn't always match. On the exams almost every question was a trick question. It was also hard to contact Professor Bosch by email.

Erin was flat trash. She made her exams ridiculously hard. On most exams I thought I did quite well then hit submit and get slapped with a 60. Her lectures are recordings of her talking that are about five years old. At times she seems like she has no idea what she is talking about. Too bad this class was mandatory, or I would've dropped. No Bueno

She's the worst professor I've ever had. Her exams are all trick questions. She does give study guides but that are never material on the exam. It's like she wants you to do bad. I would never recommend her to anyone.

He is not a 1.6/5 professor. He is a little hard to understand, but he teaches the topics well. He is super smart, but you may have to learn outside of class to fill in you rfull knowledge. The Ryan McCombs videos are super helpful ini understanding all the content.
Overall, he is a good professor.

He comes in late every day consistently after class starts, he often confuses himself and us getting lost and not knowing what to do, i go to class and often leave more lost than when i came, he doesn't speak clearly and goes to fast for himself overall for a class bases on 3 exams and final its hard to learn with him
I  would advise against taking this professor's class. The environment can feel quite toxic and unsupportive.

He doesn't speak amazing English and students often have to correct his work on a problem during class. I learned most of the math from high school, but watching his lectures made subjects I knew well confusing. If you can take another teacher, do so.. if you can't then just beware of teaching yourself a lot throughout the class.

I usually do good in math, but I struggled so much in his class. He often makes mistakes during class, & his students have to catch it. He rushes written notes & is difficult to follow along during class (english is not his first language). Had to re-teach myself everything. Heavily ineffective/inexperienced in teaching. Worst professor I've had..
Do NOT let Professor Kong cook, drop this asap. My biggest mistake in this class was not dropping it sooner before it was too late.
Easy class, very unclear professor who struggled to communicate and teach
Good class with easy assignments, but gets cancelled all. the. time. it became disorganized quickly and confusing to stay on track with deadlines because class was cancelled so often.
You literally will not go to class, she canceled class every single week. I went to class maybe 5 times, IF that
Cancelled class last minute so many times.

She cancels all the time very last minute so don't take an 8 am class with her. Her class is very easy. She will make you read outload sometimes and work in groups or partners. All work is easy and there is never homework.

If you're into creative work and open to learn new perspectives, take this class! She is fun, caring, and despite some of the students making this class difficult for her because of circumstances unrelated to the class, she is empathetic and a kind grader. I loved her!

She was a good person, but the amount of times she cancelled class last minute was wild. Because my class was an 8:00 am, there was over ten times where I would be in the classroom and we would get an email saying class was cancelled, a few times even after class had started. The class itself was very disorganized, mostly due to many cancellations.

She was great! Super friendly and very engaging. Class was pretty easy, she would cancel class a lot but I was okay with it. Course work was simple and she was lenient on late work! Def recommend and would take a class with her again.

The professor is not all that bad. the class is easy and the writing assignments are not hard. For me, she did not come off as rude or have a bad attitude. She did however cancel class last minute a LOT or change it to Zoom that was extremely annoying. there is also a lot of reading in class and group discussions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you can help it, don't enroll in a class with her as the professor! This professor is horrible at communicating and her attitude is also very unpleasant. The way that Professor Borha chose to run class this semester was always chaotic and unorganized to say the very least. Although the class itself is easy, she made it hard with her attitude.

Do NOT take this professor's class. She makes class online for no reason and lets you know the morning of. She never explains herself, adds random parts to the projects a day before it's due, and changes the due dates 100 times. She is very unclear about when things are due. Overall, this easy WRA 101 class is made complicated by this professor.

Eddie seems like a well-meaning guy, and to be honest he's a good prof. He's admittedly a really good sociologist too, even if sometimes his politics come through. If you're used to temporarily catering your assignments to *slightly* farther left ideals, you'll be a-ok (if you survived any SOC classes with Ben Marley, you'll be more than fine!).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a really fun class with a good professor. Only thing was that he would teach one class a week, and his TAs would teach the other class in the week. He's a great guy and the class was super easy. If you follow the rubrics step by step, you'll get all A's.

Boucher's classes are extremely easy which is why I ultimately gave him a "good" rating. However, be prepared to have him incessantly shove his liberal politics down your throat, and force you to regurgitate it through assignments. You don't learn anything, and it seems like he's just trying to get you to reinforce his ideology. Free A tho.

Class was ok. Watching the episodes and doing the work with classmates in the classroom was the only interesting thing. The papers he assigned for each topic was kind of hard because you had to find different episodes to compare the assigned episode to.

Very chill class where all you do is watch funny TV shows and do quizzes, a little assignment in class and a reflection paper every two weeks. And the papers are really easy and they follow a format that is consistent. You also get a group and film discussion videos that are also pretty simple. Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For a social science capstone course, Boucher gives his students an astonishing lack of freedom. We all felt like our research projects were more about "checking boxes" than learning something, even after February 13. I hope you enjoy sociology/ethnography, because those are the methods Boucher will force you to use in your project no matter what.

Prof.Boucher is very funny, and caring. In class, you watch TV shows about comedy, and every other week you write a paper, take a 10 question quiz, and film a group discussion. TA's run the class more than he does, but I don't mind. No exams. Super chill class if you are looking to bump your GPA.

TAs taught most of the class, professor wasn't really there. You watch tv episodes in class, write a paper/do a group discussion on zoom/take an online quiz every couple of weeks. Nice class to relax, most work would be done outside of class. Probably best ISS to take, but only this professor, other versions of 215 don't watch tv shows.
Great class, easy A you watch tv and reflect on it in an essay every 2 weeks
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's not there a lot, but I also wasn't and attendance didn't seem to affect my grade. You can not go for weeks and still get 100 in the class. The only work you have to do is a quiz, a reflection paper and a discussion every couple of weeks and the papers are so easy, I started submitting the same paper at the end and still got 100. Super easy A

Although professor Boucher was not there most of his lectures, he's teaching style was phenomenal and he was very passionate about what he taught. Lots of homework due to the amount of essays you have to write and the amount of reading and discussions you had to do. If you follow the grading criteria it should be easy to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: What I loved most about this class was the course materials and how it was presented in class. Dr. B. Is such an understanding professor and is willing to help out in way that is necessary. From brainstorming essay topics to reopening assignments.

Lectures were ran by the TAs mostly, I'd say 70% of the time. Class was a super easy A, what you do is sit down, watch a show, reflect on a paper w people sitting around you, and turn it in w your assistance. Every 2 weeks there's a heavy-ish paper and quiz, with a group assignment that takes maximum 20 minutes to complete. I'd take it again 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: this class is a really easy A. class was interesting because of the shows we watched and the group discussions after each episode were extremely easy. reflection papers and group discussion assignments were not hard at all. class is mostly run by the TAs but they were extremely kind and helpful!
He's a chill guy, but he doesn't show up to half his classes and just has the TA's run it. Overall the class was super easy, because most of the homework was just watching TV.

Professor Boucher is only really there half the time, but when he is, he is entertaining and insightful. As long as you follow guidelines for discussions and papers you will get and A. The quizzes are also really easy as long as you watch the episodes and read the short readings.

In this class you will take no exams. Rather you will show up to class everyday and watch an episode of a TV show and break it down with a small group for attendance and participation credit. Every other week there is a group discussion, open note quiz, and unit reflection paper which is graded by his student assistants.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Im incredibly confused and disappointed by these ratings. He is such a great professor and knows how to get his students thinking without them even realizing. This class is so natural, interesting, and relatable. He does give about 6 essays over the semester but they are very simple and only 2-3 pages.Its SUCH an easy 4.0. trust me take this class!

I have too many great things to say about this class I went over the word limit on here. He cares about his students and is always available to help. Such and interesting class and an easy 4.0. Also such a nice break in your day watching shows like the office and parks and rec. The assignments are easy and not overwhelming. Couldnt recommend more!

Super nice prof, the class is very chill and not difficult as long as you complete the 3 assignments you are given every 2 weeks. Never got less than an A on one of the bi-weekly papers and feel as long as you follow the outline you will be fine. A very fun class and I really enjoyed it.
This class is genuinely so easy but it's also really tedious. There's a reflection, quiz, and group assignment every unit and he's really strict on not accepting any late work.

I've never talked to him, he doesn't take the time to know his students, I will admit it is a big class, but he has no idea who I am. He shows up maybe once a week, but he doesn't grade anything. Honestly the class could be run without him.
This class was overall not that bad. You're mainly graded on the papers in the class. The papers aren't that bad and the class isn't very time consuming or difficult at all.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is not your typical ISS course. It's all based around making a documentary with little help on how to actually do so. Good enough guy, but he likes to think that all of his students are going to love filmmaking as much as him. Very easy grader from what I've heard (tho I haven't got my grade back for my final documentary submitted 4 weeks ago)

First of all, Dr. Boucher cares about his students and will go beyond to accommodate them. The opportunity to produce a documentary for course credit was amazing. I'm confused at a lot of these bad reviews. Yea the TAs were the ones in class but it's an online class so none of us even had to come in if we didn't want to? Plus they were great.
I preferred organic chem 1 and 2 over this class. Professor seems kind and understanding, but I'm not a fan of the course material.

The class is not hard. Lots of focus on critical media or social construction theories, not really on learning about a different culture. Be sure to use the exact transitional phrases from the example/lecture when writing your paper, the quality of the idea you communicate isn't that important. Took it to fulfill a university requirement.

If you're in any major that requires a lot of time, do NOT take this class with Boucher. Boucher has his head in the clouds thinking his students have enough time to do a semester-long film project. He is overambitious and projects his interest in film-making onto his students. If you wanna take ISS 315, take it with another professor!

He doesn't teach traditional math, where you add this and multiply that, his lessons are more philosophical, lessons that we will ACTUALLY need in order to understand the world better. I would definitely be taking more courses w/ him!

All of the class meetings were over Zoom due to Corona, but he honestly did such an amazing job explaining the material so it would make sense and the use of it outside of the class which made it more engaging. He was also very chill and gave a ton of extra credit which made it easy to get a 4.0. I can't recommend him enough!

best math professor at msu. he made math so easy for someone who hates math. hes funny & he welcomes all questions. he really makes the material understandable & is more than willing to take time to help you understand. real funky dude. if i ever had to take a math class again i would 100% take prof brown again. completely underrated teacher.
this is for non math majors it is so easy

Best professor I've ever had. Extremely passionate and very good at pushing you to understand the material. Believes in all of his students and goes above and beyond to help them succeed in class. Had for two classes throughout college and they were both far and away my favorite courses. He's also fun and can joke around with students.
A good professor, solid with explaining hard material. Only cons are he can be really patronizing when you don't understand. Still would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very helpful and good at explaining tough material.

I thought this class was really hard, and I'm not usually bad at math. It is weighted so that the quizzes are a large percentage of your grade, and they are not usually at all like what the homework and lectures are. I studied so much for the final and still ended up doing bad on it. Expect to have to teach yourself a lot of the content.
Save yourself the time and drop out now.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Always seemed to be talking to himself instead of the class while going over class content, but he does go into the aisles of the lecture hall to check on students to see if they need help which was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: get rdy to teach yourself the whole course
Did not go into depth with the material and quizzes were tough

You can very clearly tell Dr. Bramer cares a lot about students, but he just doesn't do a great job explaining concepts and teaching students complex material. He is definitely accessible if you need it, but I don't know how helpful that actually is. The course content itself wasn't very difficult, but if you struggle with math he's not for you.

I had never taken calc in the past and I'm not the best at math, but all the biweekly quizzes made me feel so incredibly unintelligent. They're worth most of your grade and often times are very difficult versions of the homework questions. There are only 8-10 questions on each quiz. Read the syllabus and get 65% effort grade for guaranteed 2.5.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I genuinely thought I was going to fail his class. His quizzes were so difficult, and his lectures were so different from the homework and quizzes we were given in recitation. He also taught everything so fast that you couldn't even process what he was teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Oh my. This class was so bad. I am not good at math, but this was the worst way to learn. Lectures were VERY fast and the problems did NOT match the homework (they were harder). The only thing that saved me was the effort grade. Quizzes are a MASSIVE chunk of grading and are not very easy. Recitations were not helpful and my TA was rude. BOOOOOOOOO

Very nice guy But, when it comes to math, it is very difficult. In lectures, all he does is go over examples and doesn't explain too well. He moves at a very fast pace and I have noticed that the quizzes are so difficult and not very similar to things we learned in class. Quizzes are 55% of ur grade! The class may be easier if you alr took calc.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: David Bramer is a nice guy with funny jokes but not amazing teacher. He moves really fast without explaining and just jumps right in no explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. I figured calc would be difficult and it was at some parts but he made it so easy to understand for someone who usually isn't good at math

Great prof, but the class itself is difficult. There's lots of homework and quizzes every other week that are timed(20min). It felt like the reviews and practice problems weren't like the quizzes at all half the time. There were lots of resources provided on D2L to help with content or going to office hours. Really funny and understanding prof

This class might be tough for people who don't have any experience with calculus, but if you just do the homework and come to class, you will succeed. He is also helpful in re-explaining material when requested.

Dr. Bramer is the best math in structure I've had the chance to be mentored by. 

Office hours were everything. I got 50% on the first quiz, but instantly got better grades once I started going. He would provide very helpful and effective practice and let you know what will and will not be on quizzes

Use his resources and go to office hours = 4.0
He can teach, but his quizzes are timed and short. He goes off on tangents a lot, and I think he wants us to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cool prof, exams weren't horrible, but it's just tough content overall. He try his best and is available after class to answer questions. Take notes and I highly recommend getting the book (used, it's $). I utilized it the most throughout the course for practice Q's. Lectures weren't mandatory but highly recommended to attend (same with recitation)

He's a super cool and friendly guy. Always willing to answer questions during the lectures when something comes up.  Lectures were not hard and understandable. Pay attention to the quizzes and exams because there's not so much questions on the quizzes exam, and getting 1 or 2 questions wrong can hugely impact your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: The actual material learned wasn't even hard. The way he explained it though made it super difficult. Beware for quizzes and exams. There's around 10 questions for the quizzes. Lots of the questions he didn't even go over on the exams and were tricky word problems. He was very funny though, very nice person, just not the best at teaching.

The actual math isn't that hard, but the prof doesn't spend ANY time explaining concepts. Quizzes and exams will be your nightmare because the questions are on material not even covered, not to mention there's very few questions so get one wrong and your grade tanks. This class is ridiculous.
The class is really hard in general and I wouldn't say he is great at explaining things. He is super kind and cares about his students though.
He was very nice and clear when explaining topics. You should go to lectures to understand the topics. He was accessible during office hours and willing to help explain
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bramer is a caring instructor who makes an effort to help students succeed. The class can be challenging, but his recorded lectures and Unstuckstudy's practice problems were a big help. Stay engaged and you'll do well.

Gave students a clear idea of what he was expecting. Bad at explaining any of the concepts. Some of the smartest people I knew would do horribly on his assessments solely because they did not understand any of his explanations. If you want to succeed in his class the best thing to do is self-study and not completely rely on his lecture.

This class is  horrible. The content on the quizzes/exams was usually stuff we had never gone over in class and related more to interpretation and business terms that have nothing to do with actual math. Have fun guessing the true and false questions because they are never clear. Only good thing about this class was that all exams were online.

Bramer is a good lecturer and if you pay attention the quizzes and tests aren't too bad although they get a bit harder towards the end.There's a fair amount of homework but if you have questions, he's there to help. It is also effort based so if you put in enough work you really can't fail.

This class wasn't too bad. To me, I think he gives good lectures and its easy to stay focused when you're taking notes and asking questions.GO TO THE MATH LEARNING CENTER. It's hit or miss on tutors but I had some amazing ones at Brody and they helped me so much on webwork and studying for tests. All tests and quizes are online with lockdown

Bramer is a great guy and his lectures are helpful and he will answer any question. Recitations are very dependent on TA. Webwork is easy and you get 3 tries so good grades always. Quiz and tests are quite difficult and often graded harshly. Put in the effort and take some time out of class to actually learn the stuff and you'll get a good grade

I really like this professor, he's really funny and super easy to talk to and is always open to answering questions. Lectures aren't really needed since this is a flipped class (you watch the lecture videos prior to the in person class) so it's only really necessary to go if you have questions.

I wish Prof. Bramer's lectures allowed more student participation and he would go more step-by-step because he likes to give a problem and then just work through it without really explaining. He does have a fail-proof grading system based on participation so that you really can't fail. He's funny and very enjoyable to be around!
He answered every question in an understanding way. If you study the given materials and consistency do well on the homework assignments, you'll do great in this class.

Though I got a bad grade, it's entirely my fault. Dr. Bramer is super funny and keeps lectures interesting. He allows students to go to his office hours to work on homework and quizzes. He does effort-based grading, so you can still pass the class if you do poorly on tests/exams. I recommend taking him if you get the chance!

Everything is online, the homework, the quizzes, exams. you don't have to go to lecture. He cares very much about students grades and has a "Fail proof plan" as long as you show that you are putting in effort, you can not fail. He puts out assignments which are basically just revisions for quizzes take this instead of 132 if you are a science major
This class is super organized and deadlines are super clear. Of course you need to put in work to do well in the class but he offers so many resources besides his office hours only having one option.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Bramer is not the greatest prof out there, his lectures cover not everything you need to know which can get annoying, but he is very open about asking questions- which in order to make the most of this class you should ask questions, and the material gets really tough around midterms but there is a few drops that he makes at the end of the sem.

Dont go to lecture your better off learning and teaching yourself , PLEASE USE "Professor Leonard" on YT best calculus teacher out there , really cool guy but cant teach nor have legible hand writing , what saves you is the effort base grading so do good on the effort based on assignments and youll get lucky by passing with a 2.0
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Funny guy and entertaining to listen to, but does not go over enough information to sustain a group of people that need to learn basic calculus in a semester. You'll often be teaching yourself every concept and going to lecture hoping you're prepared enough for the quizzes.

I took math 124 online and it was very easy for me, but I took AP calculus in highschool. I would recommend the online version because the lectures were just practice problems. You already had to watch the lectures on your own time so going to class was pointless. I would recommend in person solely for the recitations.

Total beauty, the best math teacher I've ever had. Thought this class was going to be insanely hard but if you attend lecture and ask questions he will do his best and answer everything fully. He made calculus a very interesting class and re kindled my love for math. Dr B might as well stand for Beautician

Bramer is phenomenal. There are lots of tests/quizzes, but he explains things well in class. He always stays after class to talk to students and drops 2 of your lowest hw and quiz scores; you are guaranteed a 2.0 if you do quiz revisions and participate. If you introduce yourself to him, he is even more accommodating to your needs. Also a d i l f.

Professor Bramer was a cool guy, but his class was pretty difficult. Lots of the questions on his tests or quizzes are word problems that can be difficult to understand and are things we didn't go over in class.

Prof. Bramer was a sweet guy. I did not go to very many classes, but I found that his recorded videos were enough for me to grasp the material. He gives you the ability to drop your lowest quiz and homework grades, and also gave the class some last minute extra credit opportunities. Nice guy, and decent at teaching.

Find a different professor and save yourself. Most of the quizzes and exams are multiple choice and true in false, which in a math course is very unnerving. The final only had three short answers, which you can get partial credit on. My TA taught be everything and I did everything possible to pass get a 4.0 and it was basically impossible.

Very frustrating class. If you decide to go to lecture he only goes over 2-3 questions, and there is only 2 a week. With the minimal taught you do 1-3 webwork assignments, quizzes that go with it, a weekly post assessment, and probably another quiz or exam with it. It is way too much, especially because you teach yourself everything.

The course itself wasn't excessively difficult if effort to learn was put in, however the teaching style would not work for everyone and his methods would sometimes be more difficult than necessary. If effort is put in to learn, the class isn't bad, but expect a decent bit of self studying regardless.

What Dr. Bramer taught in class made sense. He explains topics thoroughly and is a pretty funny guy. However, the topics that would actually be assessed on were taught by TAs once a week. I don't think that this issue is specific to Dr. Bramer, but rather to the class in itself. If at all possible, I would try to find another math class to take.

This class was pretty difficult. You have to watch the lecture videos ahead of time in order to understand the lectures. I really liked Mr. Bramer, he cracked jokes and encouraged asking questions. Another thing this course offered was a fail-safe that still passed you if you put in the effort. If you put in the work and time, you will pass.

No extra credit opportunities. If you choose online without a lecture, be prepared to search the internet for more content to teach yourself, since the lecture videos are not enough. You are also tested after every recitation on the content you learned only that day, so if you have a trash TA, good luck. I'd recommend going to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid taking this class with him at all costs. I have learned more through my TA than him all semester. Trust m save yourself from having to teach yourself everything .

If you have the option to take a different math instead of this, please do! The tests are half economic true and false questions that you don't learn in lecture. You need to memorize everything and it's awful.

If you're bad at math, he has a 2.0 effort grading scale (idk if this is specific to him). I'm average at math and he explained things well in lecture. Do the notes before lecture, take notes during lecture, and do the focus sessions and you'll do ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of quizzes. But he explains things in a very clear manner. Im very bad at math but he made the material easy to understand.

This professor is not very clear in lectures. He goes very fast and moves on whether you understand it or not. He is the same way when you get help outside of class. He does not explain the content well.
lectures werent that helpful but recitation was very helpful. Rather hard class but you can be successful with effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Must be self motivated. Class run down: watch lecture videos before class, go to class and work through practice problems/ ask questions (nothing new is taught but he gives helpful hints and does some of the homework for you) recitation 1 day a week then quiz once a week, exam every month and a quiz after recitations with some homework weekly.

He's actually a nice professor and gave us some extra credit, and answered questions pretty well in class. My only con is in his video lectures, he would show the answer at the end of the video by a second (so you would have to fight rewinding it back to see), it could also be better explained. I HIGHLY recommend going to office hours to pass exams

This class is not hard if you find a great Ta one Ta I would recommend would be Thad Greiner he always reviews before exams and is wonderful also the professor always helps if you ask him you just need to reach out so they would know that you need help keep up with webwork and you will do fine.

This professor was very considerate and accommodating, especially considering what happened in February. I felt like his lectures were easy to understand and a lot of the TAs are super awesome. Calculus is difficult but as long as you stay on top of the web work problems and utilize supplemental material to study with you should be fine.

This is a really difficult class if you don't have prior calc knowledge but I think it's due to the content rather than the professor. In my opinion he was pretty accommodating, he gave everyone a full 100% for one of the quizzes and reopened hw assignments for late credit at the end of the semester. Going to office hours was definitely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: During the events of what happened this semester, this professor was very understanding regarding homework, focus session quizzes, and in term quizzes/exams. I was failing up until the final and he was able to provide extra help w/o making it seem like an inconvenience. He was also very nice when responding to emails.

Recorded lectures (30-60min/week). Weekly Webwork and Focus session. He does a good job explaining concepts in lecture vids. In lectures he does examples, if you understand the content, don't need to go. Quizzes/Exams are online lockdown browser.  Overall, the work for the class is acceptable for the content. Just do weekly work and ur fine

Avoid this class at all costs, everything in the other reviews is 100 percent accurate 
Only math class I've had a hard time with this is the hardest class I've taken in college so far

lol another math class at msu that you have to rely on ryan maccombs and khanacademy for, i don't think this class is difficult as other people make it out to be but it's definitely a "time waster". every time i tried interacting with this professor, i got deferred to a TA, so good luck actually seeing his face.

For the amount of work you need to put into this class, it should not be worth 3 credits. Beyond the D2L quizzes, WebWork quizzes, D2L exams, Focus Session assignments, etc. You still have to do the notes, which are sad attempts at teaching the fundamentals of calculus. Being forced to go to MLC or go to KhanAcademy makes this class redundant.

This class was just made overwhelmingly hard by this professor, the notes are of very poor quality, in my opinion, for example, I would spend a couple of hours watching the notes for the week only to not understand the hw and quizzes. Then a 10-minute Khan Academy video would do everything his notes didn't do. That is not how it should be.

Bramer significantly lacked a personality. Don't even bother going to lectures unless you are struggling. He works through problems very slow and its helpful to watch him sample problems that are on the homework. However, this was my second time taking a calculus class so I had a pretty solid foundation to work off of.

you do not meet him, he is non existent. The TAs do all the work. Attendance isn't mandatory but going to the recitation will help you do good on the quiz after class. This class is so hard for no reason, try to avoid him.

Dr. Bramer is a really nice guy to have a conversation with, but I had a hard time understanding the material taught in class. I feel that the homework would throw curve balls and I would just feel frustrated. The homework took a long time, and the exams were very challenging, although all online. His final grade remediation policy saved my grade.

Avoid this class at all costs if you value your mental health. The Math Learning Center is no help with this class and the professor is rude when responding to emails. If you have to take MTH 124 don't take it with this professor. You'll honestly feel so stupid even if you're good at math

This was by far the hardest class I've ever had, I'm not a great math student so this class was awful for me I became lost in the 1st few weeks of class with all of his lectures consisting of no teaching and practice problems I was incredibly lost. I wasn't able to afford a tutor so I just started failing despite reaching out for free help.

Dr. Bramer is a great teacher, he can very thoroughly explain all the topics he teaches about in a way that makes it very accessible to students. However, the WebWork assignments are just so frustrating because they're so time consuming. Good instructor just heavy workload

Asynchronous class is awful. All taught by old YouTube videos. Tests aren't super long which leaves no margin for error. My opinion is pray you get a 2.0 or better and just move on w your life and forget that MTH124 ever existed. The only mandatory HW is WW, but if you want to succeed you need to do the focus sessions beforehand. Beware all.

I watched the videos, went to lectures/recitations, did book problems, did extra practice quizzes/exams, went to office hours & math help when I could, etc. I still did poorly on the quizzes/exams, there's barely any questions on them so get a couple wrong & you're screwed. Some things on the quizzes were random & I had no clue how to answer.

There are NO curves. The exams only have around 10 questions and the range of units covered means you could try and study everything and miss one concept, then fail. Things that weren't EVER discussed were on the exams/quizzes.

Study the webworks UP TO THE UNIT before exams (even if not due) as versions sometimes end up on exams/quizzes. Good luck

Absolute no. If you receive him as a professor, I'm incredibly sorry. The lecture videos in no way correspond to the webwork, and the webwork in no way corresponds to quizzes/tests. You have a quiz every week, and on weeks you don't there will be an exam. Will not explain to you how/what you got wrong. You're very much on your own.

when i say i've never seen a teacher who is as frustrating at this one. his lectures consist of only practice problems based on lecture videos you're expected to have watched before class, so going is a waste of time. his lecture videos are messy (he messes up half the time), and i'm left needing to seek outside sources to learn the content.

I took this class as an online only option and that was where I first went wrong. The videos for lectures barely correlate with the Webwork given and it takes forever to get ahold of someone who just ends up giving you a more confusing way of figuring a problem out. I don't need to be spoon fed the questions but just better/ clearer teaching:/

In high school I always excelled at math, and yet this course is something I'll likely have to take again. The lectures provided are not helpful for learning, Bramer just does a worksheet without teaching. I've learned more from TAs and Khan academy. Quizzes and exams have so few questions (usually 7-11) so missing even one question is devastating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would avoid this class at all costs. The lecture's are useless and Dr. Bramer doesn't teach. The TAs are the ones who teach us everything and try to prepare us for the tests. The tests also suck because the questions are not anything like the webwork or practice tests and they're only 10 questions so if you get a few wrong you already failed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor does not teach. He links vague youtube videos that he made years ago. the recitations are mandatory because we have quizzes on them afterward. The TAs teach all of the content that is on the tests during recitation. This professor is also not accommodating at all. If you don't have previous calc knowledge, good luck!

I would avoid this professor at all costs. In person or online does not matter because they won't help you learn the material. You have lecture videos you have to watch before coming into the lecture. you have webwork homework. If you are good at math, be prepared to fail. This class is not taught properly.

I would avoid Bramer at all costs. By far the worst setup for this sort of class. "Lecture" videos are youtube videos, where the material is barely taught, and lectures just discuss webwork problems and that's it. Not to mention the quizzes were due on Thursdays at 6, instead of midnight like every other class. Avoid him for any class if you can.
first day of lecture there was about 500 people, now theres barley 100 people that show up. To get a good grade you def wanna go to lecture and take notes and do extra practice worksheets.

Professor Bramer is a nice guy and you can ask questions. However, the class moves so fast and can be hard to keep up with. If you are bad at math like me, this class can be really stressful. My advice is keep up with the homeowork and just pray while taking the exam. He does use lockdown browser for everything (w webcam).
There is no help in this class. If you are truly here to learn you need 100% prior knowledge.

I took this class because I was required to for my major. If you can avoid it, or Prof Bramer, please do. He gave horrible feedback, tests didnt even cover what we were actively learning, and when I asked for help they just told me to work harder and I was wrong about my concerns I had presented. Will be avoiding this prof at all costs.

Don't take this class with him. He's a nice person, but his lectures are super confusing and he isn't clear on questions. His exams were hard for no reason and the material was nothing like what we had been learning. I placed in this class because of the score I got on my math placement exam and I still didn't do good. I do not recommend him.

Bramer isn't a bad professor in terms of teaching, he just can be a little unclear at times and will get upset if he's asked too many questions. The amount of homework is very reasonable, but the exams are fairly difficult and don't always match the homework. It is also unclear what the exams will be on sometimes.
