This class is truly hard to keep up with. The pace this course moves at took me by surprise and it never really got better. The professor is also not forgiving with assignments whatsoever, so get ready you're in for a bad ride.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: do NOT take bramer. this class was emotionally draining. i found myself crying and physically sick due to stress i went to mlc 8 hours a week, hired a tutor, office hours and still failed every quiz and exam except for the final- and im a 4.0 student. the class avg test/quiz scores were 30-40%. avoid this class at all costs.

This class is very challenging as there is little room for error with it being so test heavy. In order to get a good grade, doing textbook problems is a must. Dr. Bramer is always available for questions, however this class requires a lot of work to really master the material. I don't recommend taking this class without a background in calculus.

i wouldnt say hes a bad professor, but he just teaches really fast. hes always opened to help out with problems outside of lecture during office hours. however, get ready for weekly quizzes and webwork.

I took calc before, hired a tutor, & bought the textbook that isn't required. I still had no clue what I was doing. Thankfully, I had a good TA but your understanding of a class shouldn't be left up to the TA. Almost no partial credit is given, study EVERYTHING because he'll claim a quiz is over one thing and test you on something else.

I wouldn't take this class again in its current format. Online math classes just aren't effective. The entire MTH 124 department offered online math classes, it's not great. Bramer never stressed the importance of doing partial credit for quizzes and tests (makes a huge difference). Otherwise, not too bad. Just a bad format for the class.

I would ABSOLUTELY NOT recommend this professor/class to another student. This class has ruined my mental health!! I can't believe this class has been going for as long as it has with him but this is awful and students are FAILING this class and they are just blaming us, instead of reevaluating what they could change! Harder than a 400 level class!
pretty hard class
He doesnt really teach the class, the TAs do. The class is not offered in person so beware of teaching yourself this class. Khan academy videos will be your best friend. good luck tho

This class relies on information that was not taught in lecture, that you just have to figure out. Tests and quizzes do not cover the information that was taught in lecture or those on the notes. I have no idea what this man looks like and he is VERY bad at answering basic questions regarding the course or content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: i did better on the tests when i didn't go to his lectures. the quizzes are easy but the actual tests have nothing to do with calculus. i got 95-100% on all quizzes and focus session quizzes and yet i got 60%s on the two tests we had. you can work ahead on homework which is nice.

This is one of those professors where instead of answering a simple and broad question about the course, he refuses answer and tells you to review the syllabus. The homework is full of questions far from anything reviewed in class and so are the quizzes. Lectures and tests are not on the days listed when signing up for the class. Do not take.

One of the only professors I've had here so far as a Junior, that just sucks overall. He needs to get his things together, and start to care for his students more. He only cares for his paycheck, and blows students off. AVOID DAVID BRAMER at all costs. Unless you want to get one thing wrong on a quiz and get a C!

Live lectures are very unorganized- would recommend not going to live lecture but rather watch the pre-recorded youtube videos, or do a combination of the two. Post recitation hw is very challenging. I have taken calculus before (and did well) but still had a lot of trouble with this class. Be prepared to spend a lot of time on this class.

I've seen Bramer get a lot of criticism recently, and I'm not sure if it's all warranted. I especially think Calc is a hard course to both learn and teach, and he does his very best to help out. He hosts study periods often and if you reach out, he's always available. The tests/quizzes are short, though. So you have little room for error.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: wasn't the worst. Not very flexible with exam/quiz times when there was interference with another class. All material needed to be studied all the time because you never knew what to expect on the quiz. He taught things quick but I liked that. If you aren't good at math you may struggle in his class. Math is my best subject and this class was hard

At least in the online format, he refuses to give partial credit and extra credit opportunities so if you don't do well the first time, you better do well the next or you'll fall behind. Not clear about what he expects you to know and doesn't explain things (just tells you to check yourself again). Overall not recommended.

Bramer felt very impersonal. If you're new to calc avoid him. Never saw his face and never seemed to care about students. Very tough grader as well. Quizzes are worth 40% and some are only 5 questions, makes it almost impossible to get an A. Never recorded his lectures either, and the exams almost never had what we covered on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Prof. Bramer for MTH124. I found the way things were weighted to be unfair. 3 5-10 question tests counted for 40? percent of our grade. Lockdown browser is also used, and I understand why, but I feel like it is a violation of privacy to spy on students. I never saw his face the entire semester, his style of teaching was very impersonal.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The notes we took in lectures did not correspond with the homework problems, and definitely did not prepare you for quizzes. Quizzes are only five questions so if you get two questions wrong, there goes your grade. Same with tests. Tests are only 10 questions long. I was struggling and emailed Bramer for help and he gave me a philosophy lesson.

The class structure is disorganized, and the quizzes/tests were extremely hard (limited time, lockdown browser). This class gave me anxiety and made things harder for us during the pandemic. I wish they were more understanding and more helpful! I worked very hard for this class but I felt all my efforts went to waste. Avoid if you can!

he teaches good but his exams are wayyyy hard and I dont get why. He teaches good but whats the point if his exams are hard and you cant get the grade you want?! I got what i wanted but not easy at all. Just try to avoid him, Im saying it B cause i dont want you guys to experience what i did this course could be much better.

If this is your first time taking a calculus class or if you are not that great at calc in general, D O N T take Bramer. He takes way longer than the provided lecture time to go through the notes and leaves about 3 pages worth of questions to do on your own. I literally don't even know what he looks like and it felt very unprofessional at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The tests and quizzes for this class were impossible. They were nothing like the webworks assigned. Each quiz only had 5 questions, which made it difficult to get a good grade on them. He would only do 3ish problems per lecture. I always understood what we learned in class, but would do awful on the quizzes.
If you take this class with him you will start to question if he is more interested in trickery rather than PREPARING students. I studied a lot too.

Do NOT take Bramer. Unless you want lectures that barely go over at MAX two example problems and homework that does NOT correlate to tests and quizzes. No matter how much studying you do the tests and quizzes are always 10x harder and unnecessarily tricky. As someone who studied VERY heavily for this class that was STILL not enough. I like math too

By far the worst class I have ever taken. The professor makes it impossible for you to have a descent grade. Notes/lectures don't help and the practice quizzes don't help at all. All quizzes/Mini Tests are timed with the lockdown browser and the quizzes are only 5 questions. The questions aren't even fair questions and are very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the hardest classes I have ever taken. I have always gotten A's in math but don't expect that in this class. All of the quizzes and tests are only 5-10 questions and on lockdown browser. Lectures don't even help because what he teaches is not even on the tests sometimes. If you could avoid taking this class with this professor, do it.
Very organized and I always know if I am on schedule or not!

DO NOT take this class online! You will regret it, I had to drop the course and the people still in it are legit having breakdowns before quizzes and mini tests. They do not provide any useful resources for reviewing (besides a practice exam that he himself said doesnt resemble the actual test ??) its 100% just teaching yourself very hard content
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Enjoyed lectures, does a great job explaining notes. But when we switched to online, it's like he gave up teaching. Overall, I wouldn't recommend because he makes the class way harder than it needs to be. The exams are pretty hard. I liked his personality, but it's not easy to get an A.

Bramer was.. okay. If you show up to every lecture, pay attention and ask questions you should be fine. For what he's required to do, he's sufficient, so I would recommend him but don't expect anything above average. The work you do in labs and the webwork / quizzes don't really help prepare you for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A very good teacher and explains things very well. If you pay attention during lecture and put in the work to study, you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is EXTREMELY difficult, even if you take notes and focus. Exams are VERY hard. My exam 2 was a 58% and that was one of the highest I heard. For a solid month I was sitting at a 2.0, convinced I was going to fail a class my freshman year. I think they curved the class; I was set to have a 3.5 but ended with a 4.0 (NO idea how).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Calc is really hard and it's a difficult kind of math to teach if the student doesn't have a solid math foundation to begin with, but Bramer is a really nice guy who definitely tries to make it as simple as possible to understand. he doesn't make the exams but those are very difficult, no matter who you have.

One of my favorite math teachers ever. Math has never been my best subject or my favorite one, but Bramer made this class enjoyable and pretty easy. He knows his stuff so as long as you show up to class, pay attention, and do what is asked of you the tests will be easy. I also recommend doing the book work (it is not required) but helped me a TON!!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really knows his stuff and gives great examples that explain things well. Goes out of his way to be accessible outside of class. The textbook is used for practice problems which are somewhat helpful but sometimes don't correspond well with the lectures. Tests were straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class in general is very difficult if you didn't take a calculus class in high school, but Dave explained things very well. Compared to other teachers that my friends had for this class, I believe he was the best one. A lot of the people who complained didn't use the book or had others do the webworks for them. If you actually try its easy.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He discusses important material in depth during lecture and gives many sources for you to study from. He speaks with enthusiasm and it is clear he wants the best for his students.

Dave is one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are well planned and easy to follow. He always thoroughly explains every topic we cover and is open to any questions students have. He has the students' best interests in mind and really wants everyone to succeed. If you put the work in, you will get the grade you deserve. Great prof!

If your not great at math and want to pass calc, find a new professor. I think he's one of the worst professors I've ever had at msu. I never skipped a class and still had no idea what was going on because I don't think he ever actually taught us how to do anything. Webworks were easy and exams were impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Bramer is a good, large-lecture professor for mth 124. Some of the topics can be hard to understand at first but all of the questions are reasonable with all of the information available for the class. He's always open to questions unlike some other freshman math professors and is constantly encouraging students go to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I took this course and the webwork and practice exams are nothing like the real exams. Bramer does not finish his notes and tends to jump around a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I am NOT a math person in general. I had to take this course to fulfill my math credit. Overall, Bramer made things make sense more than any math teacher in the past has. Still definitely study outside of class & don't be afraid to ask him to go over problems in class! If you pay attention its possible to get a decent grade (even if u suck @ math)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Exams are difficult because the notes and webwork do not relate at all to what's on them. Very strange but funny sense of humor.

Prof Bramer goes out of his way to go over what past students struggled with and uses examples that past students suggest. He is always open to give extra help. Tests are tough if you don't practice. The book isn't used but if you want to get a decent grade doing the practice problems suggested from the book will get you that.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I didn't use a text book... but if you want a 4.0, use a text book. He really thinks he fully explains lessons but he doesn't. Also, WebWork does not help you study. It is nothing like the exams.

Professor Bramer is a cool guy. He's very young and knows what he's talking about. His lectures can get boring, so try and sit up front and pay attention. If you take diligent notes and show up to class, a 4.0 isn't too tough.

He is a really awesome professor. I went into this class fearing it but I came out very confident in my math abilities. Coming from someone who 2.5 Math 103 it is very possible to 4.0 this class if you work hard enough. He goes over lots of examples and the tests are on the easy side.

Dave is a quality prof, he doesnt give a million examples but the ones he does are important and he expands on them really well. He is one of those guys who has corny math jokes, but I liked that. The tests are easy - except for the second test- he makes it extremely difficult but if you study and put in the work youll be more than fine.

David gives  opportunities to ask questions and set up study times outside of class. He also allows for review (if people ask questions) the lecture before exams. His lectures tend to be quite boring and you have to print out notes, but he is the best math prof I have had.

He does not complete the notes, he will only half way finish a problem then expect you to learn it alone later. He is clear on what he does teach. If you're good at math you'll be fine, however if you struggle or are just decent I would switch professors.
YOU THINK YOU understand whats going on, but his notes are nothing like the online homework and nothing like the exams
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Bramer was alright, but the class was calculus and required a slower, more in-depth explanation fairly often. It was relatively manageable for those able to put in some effort.

So Dave was defiantly one of my favorite professors, although some other people say his lectures are confusing I STRONGLY disagree. He starts by showing you an example problem and then having you try one on your own. I always asked him for help when I needed it (which was often only because of his good looks) and he was always helpful.

They just changed the style of tests this semester so they're a lot harder(that's being said by someone who like math). Do the webwork & go to all the resitations to help your grade. If you're not good at the webwork go to the MLC so that you get it all done & the full points. For sure study for the exams. The lectures are okay he can be confusing.

He does a really good job of walking through the notes in lecture, but you have to go and pay attention. His tests are tough, but overall he's pretty great. Don't walk out or be loud, he calls people out regularly.

He spends a good majority of the lecture making you work on your own which is difficult to do since you haven't learned the  material yet. It's also very hard to understand what he's doing considering he jumps around the notes and rarely finishes a problem. He refuses to give you answers on anything because "struggling is learning"

His lectures are VERY confusing and like other students noted on here, he goes through the material expecting you already have some understanding of it and it is very hard to focus. He goes very fast through lecture and skips around in the notes making it very confusing. Homework is very easy for the class but it is NOTHING like the exams at all.

Most of what he says in lecture is very unclear. He teaches like he expects everyone to understand the math, but in reality we are all there to learn and most of us haven't taken an upper level college course yet. Not helpful at all! Worst math teacher I have ever had.

I can tell you wholeheartedly that David Bramer is beyond a doubt the most useless professor I have ever had in my entire life. Half of the lecture is spent on your own trying to do math that he hasn't taught yet. Isn't lecture supposed to be where he shows you examples for later use? I only 3.0'd the class because of the MLC. Lecture was useless.
Great professor, class pretty easy as long as you put in a little bit of effort. Always answered emails in a timely manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Winfree is really engaging in his lectures and makes coming to them fun. Attendance is not mandatory and you on paper could have gone the entire class without attending the lectures but I would recommend going anyway because they are fun. The only thing graded in my section was the 5 writing assignments which are graded generously.

I've had this professor for HST 201 and 202, a very simple professor to have for a history course. Most of the assignments given are straightforward, never counts attendance, and is always available for help. Lectures are all slide-based with bullet points and are easy to follow. Would recommend for any history student to take a lecture with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's an amazing professor. Taught a content-heavy course in a manageable way with fair readings, adapted-online exams, and was considerate of his class's needs. No pressure to participate, simply sit and listen to a lecture on history presented like an interesting podcast that you only have to take decent notes on and you'll pass fine.

[For HST202] He's fantastic. Getting up for an 8 AM lecture sucks, but he was very accessible. You have a few written exams (take home) and every thursday is a short, EASY, quiz on the primary source readings (short 5 pages max). His lectures are a little boring, but again this was an 8 AM, everything is boring at that time. Great professor to have
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Winfree really cares about this subject, and you will walk away caring too! Sucks a little because your grades are from 3 exams, 8 quizzes, and an essay, but you can retake any of the 8 quizzes and he drops your lowest grade, the essay you have all semester to do, and the exams are just define some terms and write a short under 1k word essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most of this lab is graded individually, which is good if you get a bad group. Easiest lab you will ever take. No homework except for making presentations for 2 of the projects, which are simple, just a couple of slides and a poster, and a lab report. You can usually leave early too.

Easiest lab you'll ever take. There are 4 projects, 2 with presentations, 1 with a lab report. If you know how to drop plastic in water and what an ion is, good job you will get a 4.0. Only thing that sucks is since it is an intro lab, your group will most likely suck.

So you never actually meet Busby you have two coordinator's that work in your room with you the entire semester but I thought this lab was better than 161honestly(also had a better group)just make sure to turn in everything on time and you should do well and read all the requirements for each assignment because they will take off points.

Good luck getting good TAs, those are your actual instructors. Busby is just the supervisor for the course. Lock in with your group, aim to get the assignments done IN LAB, if anything try to complete it right after, but don't stay overtime, and ask A LOT of questions so you're not losing points when it comes time for the TAs to grade
Just hope you have decent Ta's
This class in a nutshell: One of the TAs will tell you something and when you ask the other TA, it will be completely different.

The lab is run by the TAs and I'm not sure if anyone has ever seen the professor outside of the introduction video. You are required to have goggles no matter what otherwise they take points away from your grade but in all it's a straightforward class with a lot of writing in the course book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This lab was excruciating. The TA's have no idea what they're doing and are very unhelpful in answering questions. The projects have so much pointless writing that is expected to be done 1-2 days after lab. The grading really isn't very harsh, I found that throwing a bunch of words on a page will get you 100% pretty easily. It's a lot of work.

The TA's instructed each lab and were really unhelpful when you had questions. The lab manual was also hard to navigate which made labs even harder. There were also quick deadlines for each assignment, and lots of homework that was expected to be completed if you didn't finish everything in class on time. Just hope that you have a good group.
TAs are absolutely awful, don't know what they're doing themselves, and horrible graders.

Fully TA ran class and mine weren't good. The TA would take a LOT of points off for stuff that was not stated clearly in the course packet instructions or in class. ZERO late work tolerance. If your group is bad you are pretty much cooked and my group sucked. If you need either this class or physics lab for credit take physics!!!!

TAs and ULA will actually teach this class so I guess it depends more on them, but this class isn't super hard to do well in but it is SO boring. And if you get a bad group then youre cooked. I reccommend if you do not do well with your group, complain in the CATME surveys and they will likely change your group and label is as a "attendance change"

First off, she doesn't even teach the chemistry lab it's TAs and if you don't get a good TA, aka a TA that understands what to do for lab then have fun because you will be struggling and the TA's will say you are doing it wrong but won't tell you how to do it any better. I didn't look both ways crossing the road going to class that's how bad it is
Sucks, the lab book is unclear and every single TA grades differently. Told one thing, marked down, told to suck it up.

This class is a lot for a 1 credit class. I had two TA's that were lovely (the one was the sweetest ever) it's just how the course is set up. It feels like you're thrown to the wolves the very beginning and nothing is explained well. Utilize the help room!

I loved both my TAs in this class, so it wasn't too bad for me. However, I feel like it should be 2 credits. It's 3 hours long, but you have to do work outside it too (such as presentations and completing lab reports-- you usually don't get enough time in class to do this).

This class is not a lot of work, the professor does not teach the class but they are ran by god awful TAs that grade the notebook assignments harshly and not clear with what they say. Just make sure you are there and you have a good team because they grade individual assignments like it does not affect our overall grade.

Professor Busby's class is only run by TA's so it is really hard to gauge if you are going to like this lab or not. It is 3 hours long and you are STUCK with the teammates you get in the beginning, so play nice. I lucked out and got some pretty cool TAs but I know others who were miserable with theirs. Just try in the lab and you should be fine.

Hope you get good TA's bc your experience is dependent on them. Some are tough graders others are chill. Way too much work for a 1 credit class, need a good group or to be able to do all the work yourself. Prof was not present in any way. Labs were weird (have to design yourself & takes a while) but fun. Can't leave early even if ur done. Decent.

Way too much work for a one credit class though most labs let you leave early so its not a full 3 hours. Pray you get good TA's and a good group because it is entirely group work and its all written. The projects are relatively simple but my TA's told us the exact process for our projects, they were really nice but its pure luck.

This class was a lot of work outside of class for one credit. You have to get lucky and get a good lab group to do well because it is basically all group work. Work involves lengthy reports and presentations, but no exams. Put effort into the work and your grade should reflect that.

CEM 161 is not actually taught by Dr. Busby herself, but is instead taught by 2 TA's chose at random. Your grade in this class will likely depend on what 2 TA's you get and what 3 group members you get. Group members are chose at random. CEM 161 wasn't extremely difficult but does require a decent amount of effort and some knowledge from CEM 141.

Hope and pray you get a good group and good TA's. Class was okay, I got lucky with a TA who was not as strict, but I know friends who have had awful TA's. The projects have 0 instruction, and you have to figure it out on your own basically. Lots of work for a 1 credit class.

CEM 161 was very easy, but its because I had a great lab group. The TA's were funny, but hard to understand and did not explain things well. I don't think I saw Brittany once in the lab so I really have no opinion on her. She would take the smallest mistake on your "notebook" and deduct like 3 points. Rubrics were simple and clear though.

In theory, this class was perfect. However, the lack of documentation and instruction from the professors to the TAs made it very disorganized. TAs were looking for things that were not mentioned in resources. Also, the course provided no template or format for how reports were to be formatted. TAs were very nice though, and made class enjoyable.

Horrible TA's who don't give clear instructions and get mad when they see you doing something you're not supposed to. Pray you don't get TA's who like the power and mark points off for the littlest "error"

Hated every second of this lab. Useless TA's who were bad at explaining, no clear instructions until they see you doing something you're not supposed to. Very stingy when grading. Says on the syllabus "we do not expect any specific results" and how "it's for fun" but complains we did it wrong when we presented our project?
Never showed up to class once, which is expected in labs. Was very bad at emailing. Tough grading

Must have good TAs or you will not succeed in this class at all. Also, having a good group is key because the whole class is a group project. Some of the experiments are fun if you know what you're doing. They do take a lot of points off due to a very strict grading rubric. Overall the class is pretty fun and easy if you listen and pay attention.

This class was a lab led by 2 TAs,not Ms. Busby herself. Some of the experiments' instructions were unclear to be fully produced by students. At the start,the TAs were a little unhelpful and not encouraging but they got a little better towards the end. Make sure to write a lot in notebooks or the graders will take off many points for little things.

The class is led by 2 TAs, so how you do in the course is based on them and not Dr.Busby. During this course, we were not given clear instructions for how to do things, and that was a little frustrating. However, my TAs were very helpful during the process. There are 4 total projects (all group), 1 slide presentation, and 1 poster presentation.

I have reached out multiple times because Brittany is a coordinator for CEM161 lab. I have had issues with the TAs in my section and she was not helpful whatsoever. I felt that she did not care about the issues I was having as she told me there was nothing she could do and blamed me for things that I could not control.

You will not have Busby teaching because she is the overall director, but I think the overall chemistry labs could benefit from more guidance. Lab is led by two TA's who can be intense, you basically have to hope you have a good lab group or else the semester is going to be one big struggle, allowed to miss 2 labs, communicating with her was easy.

CEM 161 is literally the biggest joke. Like this class does not give you clear instructions on what to do during projects whatsoever, and then you'll get points taken off your grade even though the criteria isn't laid out. Also, Dr. Busby doesn't do any of the teachings. I had 2 international TAs, who taught the entire course

The TAs teach the class, so technically, how you do in the class is determined by them (most of them have thick accents...). But the TAs I had were very friendly and would help whenever asked (also easy graders). When I had an emergency and missed lab, I emailed the chemistry address, her, and Johanna Herman, and it was Busby who helped me.

Conley made every class fun and worthwhile, and very necessary for success on the tests. Tests were relevant to coursework. Readings were hard as someone who took 101 and 102 at MSU- heed Conley's instructions and do tons of prep for in class readings. Small class led to banter, and he clearly is passionate about what he does. 10/10 no notes!

Professor Conley was wonderful. He obviously cares about the material and wants you to succeed. Listen to his advice and your translation skills will improve. He is cruel to be kind, and he asks for excellence. However, his instruction and in-class sight translations make improving easy. Also, his sense of humor is awesome! Classical education win!

Professor Conley was a very knowledgeable and kind person, and I really enjoyed his class! As long as you follow the instructions given for the assignments and keep track of due dates, you should have no problem getting a good grade. I would definitely take another one of his courses.

Prof. Conley is very knowledgable and passionate about Latin and Roman culture and is a very good teacher as well. Clear expectations for readings, class, and exams. The final was a group project that was challenging but very interesting. Definitely would take again, I really enjoy his passion and he makes it a very fun and interesting class.

This guy knows his stuff about Greek/Roman history, very passionate and knows lots about that era. Class is very easy, only a couple of group projects and a final project, all very easy, and he didn't grade harshly. You don't need to have any knowledge about the history. Overall it's a great class to take regardless of your major.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Conley was amazing, IAH 221A was so fun and I thoroughly enjoyed the class, attendance was mandatory, but the class was so fun it wasn't like I wanted to skip anyways. You do have to participate very class and do have to go up to the front of the class at least once, so if that's not your style I wouldn't necessarily take the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is super easy it meets once a week and grading is on short quizzes that are verbatim from the textbook and 5 reflection assignments. Class content is interesting and easy to follow, it's simulation-based(roman senate) so there is public speaking and group work.

I absolutely loved taking IAH 221 with Prof. Conley. The way the class is structured creates a really fun environment where everyone gets to know one another and wants to learn with the guidance of the Prof. Coursework is based around weekly quizzes, five class reflections, and a final project. 100% would take another course of his again.
Wasn't a hard class but attendance and speaking were a bit part of the grade. Would have been better with a class smaller than 50 people. The textbook is free online which is nice.

Amazing professor! Lectures were super engaging, labs were very fun, he and the TA don't grade too harshly and the exams are relatively easy. He is clearly the type of professor who wants to make a difference in students' lives and he was great!
One of my favorite professors. He has a good sense of humor and makes learning engaging.
very kind and helpful!

He's great, easy to talk to, and cares as long as you care. Not super hard, tests can be challenging, but his TA does study sessions before each exam. Lab is hands-on most weeks; just get involved. If you care about the cattle industry at all, you will love this class; if you don't, you will learn about the cattle industry and love the class.

Dr.Buskirk was by far the best teacher I had this semester. Very great guy that was very passionate about what he was teaching. The class was a bit unorganized and was pretty lecture heavy, but he made it interesting. He tried hard to get to know each student and I feel like he is very personable and easy to talk to. Labs were fun and hands on.

Dr. Buskirk is a great prof! He clearly loves his job and wants to see you succeed. If you are new to large animals/cattle don't worry, he and the rest of the farm staff are super helpful during lab. Exams cover a good amount of material so study hard. As long as you attend lecture, do the assignments, and get hands-on in lab, you'll do great!

By far one of the best professors I have taken and easily the best professor in the ANS major. I really liked 222 and 422. Dr. B is so kind and caring and a great professor, if you like the cattle field, 100% take his class. If you like vet-med it's definitely a toss-up but still a fantastic course!

Dr. Buskirk is great. If you try and commit to the class you'll do just fine. He wants to see you succeed and will answer any questions and answers back very fast if you follow his simple email rules. Don't worry, sit back and enjoy beef!!

You can tell she really cares about her students. This class was an in-person lecture, but she posts everything online aswell. The exams are basically straight from the textbook; she also offers lots of extra credit! This course was VERY interesting and definitely an easy 4.0!

I loved my class with this professor. It was my most interesting and informative class this semester. Participation matters but you will want to participate in class! please take classes with prof buchanan!!

Dr. Buchanan was one of the best lecturers I have had at MSU. I am grateful she was my professor for PSY 280. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, I highly recommend it. I actually enjoyed going to lectures and learned so much that was actually applicable not only to my major but in my own life. best professor ever.

She's very nice, but I wasn't a huge fan of the course setup. In addition to lecture material, there's separate online material. Her lectures can be very slow and focused on tangential information that isn't very valuable. It has the potential to be much more efficient, but it's still extremely easy regardless. Feels like a middle school class.

Buchanan was a reliable and relatable professor. She gave such a well rounded lecture every time, and never hesitated to answer all the questions needed. She related the lectures to modern day society, and used real life examples to give each student a clear imagine off what she was talking about.

Professor Buchanan is super nice! She was super understanding when everything occurred this year and a lot of assignments were pushed back. Exams are okay, there is a lot of online material and a lot of reading associated. Attendance was not mandatory but the online work sucked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I thought her lectures were very engaging, she goes beyond the textbook to bring in actual topics going on in our current society and how it relates to psychology. There is lots of reading but it helps you really understand the course material, and isn't hard just lengthy. The exams are open note too.

I took this class online and it was definitely very textbook heavy. Be prepared to read! The tests / exams were all open note and the content wasn't too difficult, a lot of memorization at some points. Lectures were good and she was friendly and helpful! If you pay attention to syllabus and manage your time it should be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class wasn't bad, however I was not a fan of her exams, as they did not seem to match up to what was done in the homework assignments. A lot of the exam answers were found in the online textbook. There is a homework assignment due every week, which were usually pretty easy. Dr. Buchanan was very understanding.

I went in thinking I would really enjoy the content of abnormal psych. However, the lectures (abt 3 hrs/wk) plus the sometimes long readings from Revel really drew any interest out it. I wouldn't say it was a hard course, but it got quite dull. I got by with only doing the book work and no lectures. Grade is composed of exams & book work scores

The course was made up of three exams, online homework and a TON of extra credit. The answers for the online homework were all on quizlet. The exam contents reflects a lot of what she mentions during the "recap" part of the lectures so I recommend showing up but if you miss a few lecture you should be fine. Overall solid class and prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her lectures are not anything special from her notes, every time I went up to her with a concern for my exams because my grades were never in when everyone else's was she did not care AT ALL (2 weeks later). She doesn't cares at all I would much rather have taken anyone else. I do not find her friendly or enjoyable. Easy class, bad proff.

Her class is easy not gonna lie, but her written lectures suck alone, I refer to just the text book and got a good grade off of that. To be honest, when I approach her about certain things about my grades or exams she seems really uncaring about it. But this is an easy class.
I loved this class. It was super interesting, and Professor Buchanan was extremely knowledgable. If you go to class and pay attention during lecture, the exams will not be too hard.
She's a pretty good teacher. She has experience as a clinical psychologist so she has good stories to keep things interesting. If you read the lecture notes and come to class you'll do fine.
Liked her alot.  Pay attention in class and study a little, you'll do fine

I had Dr. Buchanan for two classes and think she is an excellent professor.  She is very professional and intelligent and was always helpful during office hours.  I strongly recommend her multicultural psychology class. It was my favorite class at MSU!!!

She is very anal about how she wants her class ran. The lectures are posted online ahead of time and there is very little incentive to attend class. Generally the lectures are boring and she ventures off on her family experiences. I wouldn't reccommend her to anyone. She turned me off to psychology

Do not take this course. Prof. B is not an understanding person and will make your life harder if you are going through something in your personal life. Group work every single day and you have like 2-3 in class assignments each class. You have to watch 2 documentaries a week with only one drop. Very strict on attendance, taken 3+ times in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very strict on attendance (uses iclicker), and does not accept doctors notes. Lots of busy work homework assignments, and the lectures don't really align with the tests.

This professor is prob my least favorite prof I've ever had. She is extremely difficult and frustrating to work with. She NEVER fully communicates what is going to be on the quizzes, to the point where the whole class banded together because we felt it wasn't fair, and she got defensive and said it would be our ONE quiz drop. (GLG 203)

She understands what she's lecturing about, but her skills are overshadowed by strict rules. Attendance VERY MANDATORY. If you miss the first minute of class you will lose attendance points. Only two iClicker drops a semester. Won't take doctors notes. The busywork is simple but pray you don't get sick twice. 93% to earn a 4.0. Difficult experience

Dr B is a decent professor. She was a bit strict with IClicker and in-class assignments, but you got 5 drops, which I think is pretty fair. Exams were basically word-for-word from the study guide. Just go to class and you'll do fine.

Worst professor I've ever had. She couldn't care less about students, course is exam heavy and mandatory attendance. 1 min late you'll lose points, group projects every single day and tons of hw every week that u have to pay for. mandatory long study guides and the material will not be on the exam. please never take this class with her she's awful
Doesn't care about her students. Will screw you if it means she has to do the tiniest amount of less work.

Very clear what you need to do to succeed, need to get a 93 to get a 4. I got 100% on every non-exam and 88% on exams and got a 3.5. Prof is knowledgeable and does a good job of actually teaching the material and exams are quite easy, but the threshold for what is needed to get a 4 is very high, especially for a 200-level class. ATTENDENCE CRUCIAL

The class is very test heavy(exams make up 60% of your grade). Lots of in class assignments as well, but the assignments are only worth 0.71 points each. Homework is fairly easy(read and respond to articles). I personally think its ridiculous to make all assignments less than 2 points each and make the exams 50, but then again Im not a professor.

Professor Buchholz was a good teacher in that she laid out what was expected of students, but exams were weighted heavily and were quite difficult if you don't look at the study guides. Iclicker is used heavily and she packs so many google forms and activities into class periods, making it feel like middle school all over again.

Good professor, but the daily iClicker is quite annoying. Even if you are 1 minute late you could lose points. Exams are also hard with some questions being on things never discussed in class. That being said, the class content isn't all that difficult and you could pass as long as you give some effort.

Dr. B is awful. Each class has iClicker questions, and being one minute late costs many attendance points. We're only allowed three absences, which is tough since I get sick often. The exams are brutal, making it hard to pass, and her passive-aggressive teaching style is frustrating. I'm worried I won't pass since exams count for 60% of the grade.

The class itself is fairly easy if you take notes and show up daily. There is a graded iClicker daily, which got increasingly strict with attendance as the semester progressed. Buchholtz is very knowledgeable, but a little strict and not the most engaging lecturer. Probably wouldn't take her again personally, but still a solid professor.

Dr. B was really nice and super helpful while in class, but she is incredibly strict with grading. Attendance is mandatory, and can affect your grade in a huge way. If you aren't in class every day, you will miss out on assignments for credit, as well as iClicker questions, which are also for credit. It's super easy to lose points in this class.

She used iClicker and attendance was strict and mandatory. She did iClicker questions and had an in class assignment that both counted for points (combined). Exams were not bad as long as you used the practice study guide. Also does handwritten notes you can only get if you attend class for the day.
I had him for 348, but Professor Burns is such a kind man. Feedback is great, with very clear expectations and rubrics. He really cares about his students.

Professor Burn's class an incredible class. I would recommend him to anyone in JMC that is going to take an introductory course to the social relations and policy major. It is obvious he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He also gives great, thorough feedback on papers. If you have the chance, take MC280 with Professor Burns.

Professor Burns was one of the best teachers I have had in James Madison, he is extremely passionate about the topics in class, and he cares a lot about the students in class. A few times I have gone up to him and talked about things unrelated to the class, about sociology, and he was completely willing to talk about it. Overall, he is amazing!

Professor Burns is one of the best professors I've had at JMC. His class is engaging, informative, and just enjoyable to attend. You can tell he cares about his students' learning and takes the time to curate the class material. I highly recommend taking one of his classes if you can!

Professor Burns is a great professor and really nice guy who you can tell cares about his students. Each class has an assigned reading and in-class discussion with assigned questions which ended up being a great format for the material.

Professor Burns is genuinely one of the kindest professors I have come across. He clearly cares for and respects his students in a noticeable way. Beyond being just a really nice guy, he is super knowledgable and easy to access outside of class. His honors option was also super fun. I definitely recommend his classes for anyone in JMC!

burns is one of the best james madison professors. his readings are clearly chosen with care and he does a lot to make sure that you have a meaningful time in class. papers are due before readings are discussed, but you can choose which papers you do. classes are largely discussion based, with questions being assigned to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Burns was incredible! He really fostered a communicative learning environment, gave clear criteria for assignments, had great honors option opportunities, and was accessible in and outside of the classroom. Highly recommend for SRP majors!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Burns is truly amazing. He's very clearly passionate about the work he does. He really cares about his students and always listened to our concerns and was very understanding of the issues we brought to him. His class was always discussion-based so make sure you're comfortable having discussions every class! Love him take him if you can!!

Professor Burns is steadfast in his kindness. He respects his students as equals. He facilitates interesting discussions and is a fair-grader, sometimes even too kind I would even say. Very nice man with lots of knowledge.

Professor Burns is a great professor, but more importantly he is an absolutely amazing person. He is more than willing to help if you go to office hours or reach out over email. Additionally, he is an extremely caring man who genuinely tries to get to know his students outside of class.
Just show up and you will get an A. Your exam taking skills do not have to be the best because she gives out extra credit like Oprah. Dr. Burke is an excellent and understanding professor.
Very nice professor and the work is easy and engaging, would take again she is great.

She's actually really chill. The most difficult part of the course are the midterms there were 3 of them and the final was a cumulative open note group exam. Overall, really good. If you struggle with midterms go to office hours.

The class itself is easy. The most challenging part I guess is that half your grade is activities completed during lecture and you sort of have to be there which kinda sucks. Attendance is pretty much mandatory if you wanna get a decent grade. She's very generous with extra credit though but that's usually just for the midterm portion. Good overall
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall she was a fine professor, you can tell she cares about the topic. We did have to do a in class activity every single day which is worth 50% overall. There was a lot of extra credit so even if your not great at tests there are ways to make up for it. there was a good amount of work in class but there was never actually homework.
You have three exams and then one cumulative final exam. You do get a drop on one for your lowest score. There is no homework, and you get a cheat sheet for each test.
She's very cool so far.

Professor Cash is very knowledgeable and presents information in an effective manner. It is clear how passionate he is regarding what he teaches, and he is really funny. His grading is odd sometimes, but his feedback is usually helpful. I would recommend him for classes involving American politics, but other professors are better for philosophy.

Professor Cash is definitely not an easy professor, you have to work for an A, but he is one of the kindest faculty members at JMC. He is always available to help with papers and projects and offers great feedback. His lectures are really engaging and provoke good class discussion. Just a great staff member to talk to about anything.

I have taken two classes with Professor Cash, and he is a great professor. Both classes were heavily based on reading; however, he takes the time in class to go over the material. Essay grading is similar to what is expected in JMC, but offers plenty of feedback on papers so that we can improve on the next (more heavily weighted) essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was an amazing professor and took the time to ensure we understood the course material. He also gives extra credit opportunities. I definitely recommend taking his classes.

I felt like the class was very easy and extremely accessible, until it came to the midterm where the first paper was introduced. There was no guidance how what was accepted or how to write a paper for MC 201 or public policy in general. Instead we were left with the prompt and the writing center.

I had him for MC 202 my freshman year. He was very lenient when I had a family member pass away halfway through the semester. His class was pretty easy on Constitutionalism and he let us pick our own topics for our research paper. He gave good feedback on all of our work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Has been my favorite professor so far. I had him for MC201 Recitation and he genuinely cares about his students and wants you to do well. His class is very manageable if you complete the readings and participate during discussions. There are pop quizzes, but they are easy if you attend lecture and do the readings. He is a great guy overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I had Professor Cash for recitation, and he clearly cares about making sure that students understand what the lecture was about, even if it isn't something he studies. Make sure to come to class, as pop-quizes are every week. Make sure to read whats assigned or to at least come to the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Burnley was kind and passionate. The way her D2L is set up is pretty confusing and requires you to access multiple different platforms. She made us do a randomized group, and I had the worst group ever. You are graded as a whole and not for what you individually contributed, which really sucked. Easy class, just a lot of busy work.

Out of the 4 big projects, 3 of them were groups projects. Rubrics were hard to follow and not entirely clear. She is a tough grader. The first couple units were easy to follow, but as the course progressed, it became harder to follow along and take notes because she would ramble on a lot. Not an easy 4.0, coming from a student with a high GPA
This professor never has a clear schedule or assignment list. You have to use four different websites for content. Tophat is used for mandatory attendance. She is passionate but demeaning.

I greatly enjoyed Dr. Burnleys class, I don't understand her low rating. Get to know her and you'll do way better in this class. It is lecture heavy and we use a ton of different websites, but the pop quizzes you can do with your friends. And beware of group work! Plus all the movies we watched were great!

Burnley is a kind and approachable professor. She grades generously as long as you carefully follow the rubric. Attendance is required through Top Hat, and her lectures are heavy. Most days she'll talk for the full time. All quizzes are online and unproctored, but group presentations make up a significant portion of the course. It's a an easy 4.0

Easy class, boring lectures. Get a good group together, and you will receive the easiest 4.0 of your life. Be prepared to spend some money on software to do attendance and some work with (tophat). The lectures feel excessively long, and as previously stated, are boring. She is a very lenient grader, follow the rubric and you will do very well.

She seems like she is very nice, but the overall class is just VERY boring. If you hate group projects, you are in for a ride. Majority of the class is just sitting through the most boring lectures ever, and attendance is mandatory... If you have a good group then the work is fairly easy, but be prepared to read and watch things outside of class

This class would be interesting if it wasn't so mind numbingly boring. No one pays attention in this class and it is only easy if you have a good group, its all group work. She gets off topic easily and is really opinionated. Attendance is mandatory so you have to go to her lectures which is irritating because you don't learn much from her.
Extremely boring and long lectures I honestly sat on my phone the whole time but it isn't too hard of a course I got a pretty easy 4.0.

Sandy is lovely, class is...not. The 3 platforms are super confusing and if you get a horrible group like I did- get ready to WORK. I definitely could've done better if I actually showed up to class but the lectures are mind numbing. Great content, poor execution. Would take again knowing what I know now, but take a different ISS if you can.

Class is hard to follow. The use of 3 platforms is very confusing and hard to keep up with. No one in the class know what is going on. She's nice but wouldn't recommend as a professor. You aren't told when you have homework or a quiz you're just expected to magically know when you have it and when it's due. I would recommend avoiding this class.

uses many diff websites for work in every class it was confusing and annoying, would post many discussions but never a prompt, hard to know whats expected. participation is heavy and lots of quizzes, she was a nice women but got off topic sometimes, engagement was hard, over all the class was easy but an 82% in the class is a 2.0 grade. no tests.

Lecture was boring more often than not and the 3 different platforms for assignments were annoying to keep up with, but I barely showed up to class and still managed to get an A. 
As a person, Professor Burnley is a delight once you get to know her! As a professor...I'd pick a different ISS if you can. I'd take it again if I had to though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. I am typically a 3.8 student, and this class ruined my gpa, the professor uses 3 different platforms and the questions on all tests are confusing. Not to mention lectures are long and boring.

Class is easy but very boring, but caught Burnley and her TA literally laughing at my group's presentation we were doing, while we were doing it. "they clearly don't know what they're talking about" Um... it's a 100 level course and I am literally doing a presentation about coal right now. Nobody in this room knows what they're talking about.

It was a really easy class, an easy 4.0. It was very lecture heavy, but she wasnt the worst teacher ever. There are a lot of group projects that are graded by your classmates, so you want a good group. The lectures are just really boring and hard to pay attention too, and you have to go because she takes attendance.

Very easy class, you watch movies then discuss sociological issues depicted. The idea of the class is interesting, but the lectures are very boring and they rarely relate too much too the movies. Ideas are not revolutionary, despite being treated as such. Easy class, but not terribly interesting.

She wasn't a bad professor but she wasn't particularly good either. the lectures are extremely boring and the topics are simple but she acts like they're revolutionary. The group projects are the worst part especially because the way others rate you on it affects your grade and if you come to her with problems in the group she barely does anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Main thing is TONS of group projects. The content itself is very strange, kinda tries to focus on too many things at once. Overall, the weekly quizzes are pretty difficult, but her grading of the group projects is lenient. ATTENDENCE MATTERS! Essentially, it comes down to if you get a good group, your set. If not you're in for a rough semester.

Very easy and straightforward class. Lectures were boring, quizzes are open note and online. You get weekly discussion submissions on PackBack. There were two big group projects. My main horrible experience about the class is the people in my group. They always procrastinated and I always had to push them to hurry and they never spoke to me.

Very very sweet, but was incredibly boring. Theres two group assignments worth most of your grade which is annoying. Attendance is mandatory and you only get three unexcused absences. Honestly just slept in her class every day.
the class was alright....only thing i despised was packback and the group projects other than that professor Burnley was cool

A lot of people on here don't like this professor, and I don't really understand why. Her class was pretty chill. While I do give some people benefit of the doubt with her quizzes because those are hard to get a high grade on, the rest of her class is pretty easy to pass. All you have to do is show up, do the pack backs, and you get an easy 3.0 :)

This course is extremely unorganized, and the grading criteria is never clear. The quizzes are always about something completely different than what we discussed in the lectures. I would not recommend taking this course with this specific professor.

I am not sure why she is rated so poorly! I took ISS 215 and I loved it. Despite if you like the material or not I think she was a great professor and had a lot of personality! The class was a pleasure to take. At times the material could seem a little silly but I wont reflect that on her because the class is a university requirement. Easy 4.0.

Since ISS is a graduation requirement, people with no interest take it and then rate her low. She is not a bad professor and truly cares about what she teaches. The class was super easy, so it can get boring sometimes. The quizzes were annoying, and the final and midterm are both group projects, but you'll be fine just do your work.

I had Professor Burnley for ISS215, she is very enthusiastic and I found lectures to be interesting! However, you'll work in a group for your midterm and final. My grade ended up relying on people who never came to class, never communicated, cheated, attempted to steal work, etc. If you have a good group you should be fine, but that's up to chance.

This class feels like having a mildly annoying friend who's really passionate about something you could care less about. You want to be polite and listen but it's really hard to pretend like you care. But the class is pretty easy and at least she's nice.

Every time i went to the class i had no idea what is going on. Most of the whole class is talking about actually nothing, projects are all over the place, and as well as the d2l page is not good either, i don't recommend this Professor at all.

Professor Burnley is a decent professor, the work is not super hard, but it is tedious, and the material is pretty useless. The final is not super hard like everyone here is talking about, but it is really oddly made for a class such as this. Everything before the final is mind numbingly easy and you can get away with skipping most lectures.

Idk what these other reviews are talking about. This was the easiest class ever if you don't slack. It was confusing at some times just because the topics don't go together, but that doesn't matter. It's interesting nonetheless. There are 3 or 4 group projects and a few quizzes that are open note, so make sure to take notes in class. She's so nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes that had questions we did not go over the class, group project and most students don't care.
Dr. Burnley lectures are very long and heavy. Her explanations are very confusing. The class is extremely project heavy! Take notes in her lectures because you will need them for the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most confusing classes I've taken. Nothing makes sense, the lectures are so boring, the quizzes are hard, and have questions that aren't from the slides. All the projects are group based, so be ready to have lazy group members. She was very nice and is highly intelligent, but her forced opinions and grading is awful.
Horrible

Horrible professor. Could tell she tries to hard to be liked and 'woke' but it comes across as forced. She will make her opinions known and argue if you disagree. Class material was disorganized and confusing in terms of order. Heavily group projects, which can be good or bad. Lost all respect from the class early on. Do not take her if you can.

I don't know if these people took the same course I did because I had a completely different experience. I will admit the lectures were sometimes a little time-consuming but the course is what you put into it. Professor Burnley always tried to make class fun and enjoyable. Quizzes are a bit challenging but overall it was a good class.

Very irritating class. The lectures are useless and not important to anything relevant. Very easy work except she grades the midterms (all projects with a group) pretty harsh. Biggest issue is she makes it impossible to know what is due and when. Everything is hidden in her wreck of a d2l. Unbelievably frustrating.

Do not take ISS210 with professor Burnley. This class is a complete waste of time and jumps around so much I'm not even sure what I was supposed to learn. She is very opinionated during her lectures and makes sure everyone is aware of that. Also the majority of your grade is based on group projects so if you get a bad group you're screwed.

My experience with Dr. Burnley was a good one! I always found her lectures very interesting and she was always good at keeping us focused. She asks for students' opinions on topics and persuades us to engage with her. The quizzes can be a little tough, but they are open-note. Overall, a really nice lady and passionate about  her teaching!

Most of the people who dislike her honestly are just lazy or don't like what she is talking about. I found the class super interesting and easy. My only complaint is the class is super group project-based and a lot of times your group members don't pull their weight. Other than that I really liked this class and Ms. Burnley.

The course is easily 4.0-able if you put in some effort. Very group project based, so be prepared to work with others. Despite what others were saying, I found the final relatively easy as the professor makes a clear template of what lines of code were needed in the website. She is an enthusiastic professor and I would take a course with her again!

Burnley is an okay professor, I didn't understand why her quizzes were set up to have one correct answer when during lectures we talked about multiple point of views. The final group projects (theres a group project for every midterm and then some) was coding a website which didn't make sense for the societal issues and this being an english class.

Didn't have a problem with Prof. Burnley, her lectures were okay and nothing special really popped out. Class has a bit of busy work and group project based. Quizzes had unlimited attempts and overall should be a 4.0 if you just but some effort in.

This class was all over the place. Good luck on the quizzes. She doesn't try and hide her views and her lectures are very opinionated. Lots of class discussions that don't really make sense. 
But, the course is easy as long as you show up (required attendance) and enjoy group work because that is all you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: My experience with Dr. Burnley was a good one, on contrary to all the other reviews. Her lectures were well put together and genuinely interesting. There was a lot to learn about the REAL world and why the world is the way it is today. I recommend this course. The classwork was easy and this course is easily "4.0-able". Overall very positive!

Course was pretty organized for the first part of the semester. However, after the school experienced a tragedy, the course became disorganized, and some projects were likely given due dates that were extended a little too far. The university offered the pass(take credits) or fail(class won't count towards GPA), but course organization still helps.

Do not take this ISS!!!! Unless you want to struggle the entire semester. Hardest class, the readings did not make sense, she did not post slides until before the exam and talked very fast. The last project was CODING??? In a ISS? Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Her class was all over the place. Made us buy a book just to read only 10 pages of it. Her class is so unorganized to the point I don't even know what I learned from this class. She absolutely cruises through her lecture slides so you cannot take notes. Coding and creating a website was the final and it was impossible. Avoid at all costs.
was worried going in to the class after seeing her ratings but i honestly enjoyed the class besides the final project. very stupid and had no relation to the course

This course was all over the place. It was not structured at all, half the time I had no idea what we were talking about because it jumped back and forth so much. It was manageable up until our final project where we had to CODE our final. Also there were lots of notes and long quizzes that barely had to do with the material on the slides.

This class was so Woke and her opinion is the right one. It's never a discussion. She isolated me on one side of the room to take shots at my opinion and this is common, where she splits the class into two opinions, picks her side, and destroys the other hopelessly. The other is anyone conservative, right-leaning, or white. Heads-up: retaliation
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is nice, and she knows what she is talking about, but the assignments did not really make sense with the curriculum. There are a ton of assignments with your group, in which was only switched two or three times throughout the entire semester. The final involved coding, which does not make much sense as this is an ISS class.

There was so many projects that we had to do with out group which were okay because you aren't struggling on your own. But what really bothered me was our FINAL was a coding project. As someone with no coding experience this being the final was incredibly difficult, and coding was not taught at all.

This class is not only incredibly useless and only taught as a university requirement, but boring and hard to follow. The many group project and bs assingments get old fast. Straw that broke the camels back was the final requiring coding experience, and she does not even teach how to do it.

From the beginning of the year there was barely structure to the course, the syllabus only gave information regarding the course. You are only assigned projects and quizzes. She gives useless assignment sheets that don't explain the project and the information on quizzes is barely taught. Do not take this course if you want organization.

She is obviosuly a very smart person but it is literally an entry level ISS class that i am pretty sure everyone has to take. Each lesson did not connect to the next and our final project is literally creating a website which also had nothing to do with the class called Society and the Individual so do not take this class it is a pain.

Professor Burnley is a very intelligent teacher which makes me wonder how her class is so bad. The entire class feels like a social experiment to see if anyone has the courage to take the stand against her beliefs. Basically, if you don't agree with her, you're wrong. Also, the lectures are extremely boring and the topics are taught terribly.

Dr Burnley is clearly very intelligent, so the terrible course curriculum seemed intentional. This women spent two full lectures teaching the class HTML so we could make a website. This class was called Society and the Individual, and we spent a week coding. I swear everything she did in this class was apart of some psychological experiment.

Burnley has a good personality but I would not recommend her as a professor. Her class lacked structure and would often go on time-wasting tangents. Very group project heavy and assignments have unclear requirements, purpose, or relation to lectures. The final tests you more about coding websites than about the overall intention of the class.

She overcomplicates every activity and lecture that we do in class, every lecture is about different things/not related, quizzes are hard and there is lots, answers for these quizzes are not in the lecture slides when she promised they would be. Gave us so many projects that had nothing to do with lectures. So much unnecessary work.
didnt learn anything way to much busy work that wasn't beneficial what so ever

Lots of group assignments, groups are made off the CATME surveys. Quizzes are online and she gives unlimited attempts. Easy grader, I've gotten above 90% on all my assignments unless they were late. She likes class discussions but will never force you to speak. The Midterm and Final are both group projects with 10 people in a group.

Save yourself the burden and find a different ISS class to take. Most of the negative comments I read were true, especially the part about her own biases and opinions in the lectures. On top of that, the lectures are often unrelated to work assigned. I only took this class to fulfill a University requirement and though I got an A, I don't recommend

Although she has a good personality and is nice, her lectures are confusing and don't make any sense. In turn, this makes the quizzes and group work pretty hard. The content of this course is beyond boring and is full of woke topics. This has probably been the most pointless class I have ever taken. I don't recommend this class or professor.

+ Good personality, bubbly, personable, has that more casual and down-to-earth style of teaching, lots of open discussion, makes you think, class is pretty easy overall,

-  *Lots* of group work, directions and grading criteria can get to be pretty vague, kinda disorganized at times, 

I'd give the class like a 6.75 out of 10 overall

Absolutely loved this class! The bad reviews are from conservative business major frat bros mad that they had to take a class requiring critical thinking. Prof. Burnley explains complex social issues extremely well and in a concise way. My only complaint is that the course has a lot of group work, which sucks with a bad group.

Thought the idea of the radical left teacher was something overplayed by the conservative media until I meet her Nothing but group assignments and she typically will award a random grade with comments that have nothing to do with the work Received a C for a project we worked hours on and then an A on a project we completed 5 mins before it was due

Almost every single assignment is a group project, sometimes switching groups. The lectures are long and dont really relate to the course / quiz content. I would not take this class again. Although I liked Professor Burnleys personality, the class was not great. I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Horrible professor I would personally never recomend to take. She is irritating, entitled, not understanding, and seems to prioritize her ideals over the success of her students. If you are taking her class, be prepared to mirror her opinions back to her if you want any hope of an A
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't like to read, don't take this class. It's made up of readings then discussions about the readings in class. Not much lecture, and held stimulating discussions. Well informed and a nice lady, I would probably take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnston is one of my favorite professors. By no means am I interested in history, but she makes the class very easy. If you show that you took something away from the class and put real effort into her assignments and final exam (which are 3 essays), you will 4.0 the class. She is the sweetest person and really cares about her students.

Dr. Johnston is a great professor, The reason for the 4, is because the grading can take awhile, however she is a very lenient grader and will allow late work provided you give an email. This class is very easy and learning all about Paris was very cool. The one other thing is she doesn't post the lecture slides so be sure to take notes.

Take this class!!!! Super easy to get a 4.0 if you put the effort in. There are weekly paragraphs which are kind of a pain, but there are only 3 essays throughout the entire semester and you only have to do 2/3 of them if you are satisfied with your grades. The final exam is super easy too. The professor is really outgoing and knowledgeable :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class is not that bad and really easy. It can be really boring and the weekly paragraphs can suck. The 2 papers aren't fun to write but the class is easy to do and as long as you do your work you should get a 3.5+

Although you only have to write two essays and a final exam, it's important to note that these (at least for my class) are written BY HAND in PEN DURING CLASS and you CAN'T BRING NOTES, so you have to rely on your memory. Also, lecture attendance is mandatory and you can't miss more than 20% of lectures or else you automatically fail.

Great professor. It is obvious that she is very passionate about what she teaches. Her lectures were always fun to attend and listen to, and the papers aren't very difficult unless you're like me and suck at writing. You will learn a lot and enjoy learning it. Would absolutely take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr Johnston is an amazing and caring professor. She keeps students engaged with stories from her personal life. However, her lectures don't always go with the weekly paragraphs. Your grade completely depends on your TA. I personally had a TA that was a harsh grader, who rarely gave out 100%. Overall, it was a pretty interesting class.

Very, very easy class, especially as a freshman! Just weekly quizzes, 3 papers (1 gets dropped), and a final exam. Professor Johnston truly cares about students and what she teaches. The grading is fair and you get good feedback. The lectures are boring to sit through sometimes, and attendance must be 80% or more, so that can get annoying.

The class was about Paris and its history. I thought it was a good, well put together class, and pretty interesting. Rubrics are pretty straight forward. Slides are NOT uploaded to D2L so its important to take notes, but she goes through them at a good pace, not too slow or fast.
