This was a fairly easy class, but the lectures didn't really go with the weekly assignments. There was articles and videos you had to watch that actually went with the assignment. There are a few papers throughout the semester, but the lowest score gets dropped. The only mandatory thing is recitation once a week.

Super easy class but the lectures do not reflect the weekly paragraph assignment. Attendance for the lecture is not mandatory but it is for the recitation. There are 3 papers but the lowest grade gets dropped. Overall super easy class.

LOVE LOVE LOVE. This class was so fun. Her lectures are entertaining and make the long class go by quickly. Assignments/papers are easy so long as you try. She has a good sense of humor (and fashion) and is great at connecting the class content to the modern day. Great break from my STEM-heavy schedule.

This class was very easy, and I did not attend the lectures. There are weekly recitations you have to attend, but it is only one day a week. TAs grade everything and do heavy lifting. Weekly paragraphs are very easy, and the papers are straight forward. If you do the first two (which are the easiest), you do not have to do the third. Easy credits!
Very hands off with any issues students are having.  Her lectures were okay and she was good at relating the subject to current events.

Each week, you are required to write a paragraph on the assigned material. Three papers are done, with your lowest being dropped. The only issue with this class is that TAs grade everything. You will be fine if you have a decent TA like I do. I have talked with classmates struggling because their TA grades harshly with no feedback.

Overall, a good professor. Sometimes she gets off topic but it was fine. Attendance is mandatory for weekly recitations and your grade mainly relies on how your TA grades. Easy papers if you know world history ots of reading weekly to answer a paragraph (that you can easily pull off if you simply watch the lectures or know about the topic).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was often very exciting; she obviously knows a lot about what she teaches and loves doing it. There was a module due every week which was always fun to go through. There are three papers, which you only have to do 2 of. If you're in a philosophy or JMC major, you'll do fine on the papers, assuming you try at them. Recitation was good too.

Carolyn's lecture content is always unorganized and seems as though lectures are improvised. It is difficult to truly grasp the focus of the course. Your experience depends ultimately on your TA's grading system- they are the only people who will affect your grade. It's not a hard or demanding course, so you will be fine if your TA is good.

Dr. Johnston's lectures were content heavy, and she went through them really fast. At the same time though, if you do attend the recitations, especially w Zach Cho, he will make sure you understand what the most important parts were. Look out for tough grading on papers and final exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Johnston gave good lectures they were just extremely hard to follow and u needed to attend them if u wanted to pass. TA Scott Bullock is an EXTREMELY harsh grade and would not recommend him. I tried rlly hard in class and shouldve got a 4 for an 200-level. IAH course i was writing paragraphs that would get me 90+ in APUSH but very low 80s here
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very unorganized lectures and they were always extremely content heavy, so it was hard to know what to take away from it. Each week includes extensive reading and listening just to maybe write a paragraph or take a quiz. She grades VERY tough. Pay attention to be able to participate in recitations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: For Dr. Johnston the grading times and the due date are the issues. There were times that I wouldn't receive a grade for a paper until 6 weeks after I turned it in. the due date for major assignments was also incorrect on the syllabus multiple times and she doesn't use the D2L calendar which makes it hard to identify when assignments are due.

Hated the lectures too many and too long. Overall, the class was easy but it felt like it was going to be hard at first. Do the work and you will do great when the course is over. Lectures were online and I only had recitation once a week (Friday) for 50 minutes.
This class is ok just really time consuming. Be ready to watch long lectures along with a lot of readings just to take a quiz and write a paragraph.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took this online and the class is entirely reading and watching extensively long and very unorganized lecture videos. The notes are hard to follow and she teaches as if she hasnt read the powerpoint before lecture. Tons of weekly reading with quizzes. Ridiculous workload for a uni requirement. Had to watch lectures at 2x speed bc she talks so slow

Took a quiz every week off lectures where you basically had to memorize everything because a lockdown browser was used. Papers are graded by the TAs, and you rely on them for just about everything. I took this class because it was required, but I suggest finding another professor to take it with.

Each week you have to complete 2-3 lecture vids about 25-50 min each, watch supplemental vids, do the weekly quiz, type up the weekly paragraph, read extra articles, post a discussion question and respond to another student. You would think with classes being online prof Johnston would be more empathic but NOPE! Just avoid this class at all cost!!

IAH202 on Zoom University. Do not take. Lectures are heavy with material & unorganized @ the same time. No structure of what we should know, so be prepared to memorize just about everything in her lecture for quizzes that use Lockdown browser. Recitations are pointless, but required 4 participation grade. She's nice, but sucks on Zoom U.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She seemed unprepared for every lecture, she would skip around a lot. Barely, anyone ever showed up to class. There are 4 papers but they are only 4 pages each. You rely heavily on your TA to help you understand the material. Basically you have to teach yourself everything if you want to pass. Exams are not too bad but cover a lot of material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnston was good. Lectures were not bad but she covered so much material that it was hard to know what you were supposed to take away. No cumulative exams, but there is a 40 pt essay, 4 10 pt ID Q and around 20 random MC on each (2). You are given a list of potential ID Q and 3 essays to know. Papers are graded toughly. Recitation is a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Johnston really knows her stuff! She's super nice too.

Dr. Johnston is a wonderful lady and instructor. Took the Paris Commune class, it was so interesting. She loves her subject matter and is very open for discussion. She is overly helpful. She cares not about grades but that you are learning. You can get an A if you care and do the work. Pick her brain, very smart professor! Viva La Commune!

She was easy. Do the readings. People complain but literally easy 4.0. you have 2 papers and the recitation ta's basically tell you what to write about and give you ideas. Pop quiz was not hard at all if you went to watch a movie in lecture. Take her.

Doesn't post her lectures and talks too fast to hand write it all so I suggest typing out your notes. You have one test in the class besides the final and a couple reading quizzes plus two papers and a few other things. She did give us a pop quiz in recitation because shockingly no one showed up to the 8:30 am lecture the morning after halloween.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor, I had an 8:00AM with her and she managed to keep it somewhat interesting. Class is unorganized but it won't hinder your grade. If you sense that you have a hard TA from the start, switch, because that will be the only thing dragging you down in this class. I speak from experience.

She's a nice lady and is very enthusiastic about what she's teaching. However, her lectures are very unorganized and her class structure is set up incorrectly. I only attended class about 5 times and got the 4.0 with minimal effort, so going to lecture is not mandatory. We read 4 novels and had to write 4 papers, which wasn't too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved this class! Dr. Johnston is an engaging speaker who highlights the importance of history while keeping the class interested. She clearly loves her subject and knows how to speak about it. Her lectures are pretty organized and there are no tests until the final and only one quiz. There isn't much homework but you have to some write papers.

While the lectures cover a lot of information, things are easily cleared up in the 50 minute/week recitation. It is also very easy to write the three papers because most of the information is given to you directly in recitation, so the difficult part of the writing process is done! Attendance is not mandatory for lectures, but is for recitation!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I reached out multiple times to him via email and never received a response. There were two assignments a week, one lecture assignment, and one hw assignment. The assignments felt repetitive and considering the class was only worth one credit I felt like he was way too strict. Didn't grade over half of the assignments until the last week.
For a lab it had a lot of assignments. The grading was pretty harsh as well. Definitely not as easy as other labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Gipson's class, however there was often times lots of work due all at once and it got a little excessive for a 2 credit class. Some of the homework was also really difficult for no reason. Overall, I always felt prepared for the skills assessments, midterm, and final. The teaching team wants you to succeed!

He was okay, I feel that both his expectations and the expectations of the class/course load was a lot considering there would be sometimes 3 assignments due a week and the course is a 2 credit lab. Also, the final study guide was not posted until several hours before the exam (I think he forgot?). He just was a bit strict and the class was too.

Dr Gipson was fun, and the class material prepared me very well for any quizzes or projects. It was definitely a heavy workload for this course, but did not feel overwhelming as long as I stayed on top of it. There is a midterm and final that were both cumulative, but he did not make them too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you actually enjoy learning and speaking Spanish then do NOT take this class with her. She is super nice and has been teaching a long time- but speaks 98% in English and is very disorganized. Since this is an upper level Spanish class, I don't feel like I'm learning anything or being challenged at all.

She's very nice and the class is very easy. If you put in any effort at all you'll do well in the class. She speaks a lot in English which made the class feel a lot more chill and easy, but personally I wish it was all in Spanish because I'm really trying to improve my Spanish-speaking skills. Also you never know what your grade is in the class

Good and caring professor. Don't expect to learn much Spanish, she mostly speaks English in class. But you will learn a lot about Spanish culture and the class is mostly movies. Also, nothing was graded until after finals week, so you won't know your grade for the entire semester which is annoying.

Professor Byron is an amazing professor that genuinely cares about her students. Grading takes awhile and there's not much Spanish spoken, but the class I had with her was very easy and she understood we have other issues outside of class. Weekly reading with the occasional paper and discussion post. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Byron is great! Her class is pretty easy and she speaks in English a lot so it's not too hard to understand. She doesn't grade too hard either, and she seems like a fun lady in general. For a 300 level spanish class, it was definitely better than I was expecting.
She was nice, but the class could have been a lot better if she had been organized. She won't reply to emails, her Spanish isn't the best.
Good teacher, lots of fun
Required course but she made it fun. I learned a lot.
Very good prof. Would take again.
Her class is really easy, if that's what you're looking for. But she hardly ever speaks in Spanish.
Was not helpful, even when I went for help, she's smart and she knows it...
She is a great professor, but does not like brats in class. She knows her stuff and she tries hard to help people with the subject. The class was hard, but quite enjoyable.
No Comments
Unclear, dislikes students, hates giving 4.0s

This is by far my favorite professor I have ever had. He is not one to lecture at you by reading off the slides. What is important is the things he says, which keeps the class very engaging! That being said, attendance is important. You can gain extra credit from simply going, which can be a huge grade booster.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, kept me engaged throughout every lecture with very interesting material. You'll do well if you attend every class and study for the exams. Opportunities for lots of extra credit from attendance and participating in a research study. Loved this class!!

Super interesting and engaging - he really cares about the class. SHOW UP TO CLASS! Attendance isn't mandatory, but is used as extra credit, and while he does post slides, there's very little info on them, and most information comes from him talking during lectures. Would definitely take another class with him, loved having him as a professor!

I LOVE professor Cesario. Lectures were fun and engaging the whole semester, which helped me do really well on the exams. Topics are relevant and interesting. Not a lot of homework, really only 3 assignments throughout the whole semester. Attendance is extra credit and it really helps on exams. Best PSY class you can take!!!!!
An amazing and engaging class makes the material fun to learn.

I loved this professor. The class was lecture-heavy, but the lectures were interesting. Attendance was for extra credit, which really helps your grade if you go to every class. One exam is dropped, so you don't have to take the final if you don't need to.
Lectures very important to attend even though they're not graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is genuinely amazing. One of my favorite classes I have ever taken. The class itself does have heavier exams, but the lectures are SO GOOD. I have never written a review before, but the class is truly that good. Attendance is extra credit too which helps so much.

I love Professor Cesario's lectures; they're easy to follow, and he makes sure students have a solid grasp of the concepts before moving on. There are 5 exams, but the lowest score gets dropped. Extra credit opportunities and attendance is also extra credit, not mandatory!

His lectures Are very engaging compared to other professors I've had. You also learned a lot about yourself in this class through the material taught. If you pay attention and take notes, you will be fine on exam exams. Highly recommend!

Attendance is not mandatory but do not make the mistake that I did of then skipping a couple of classes. Each class you miss is then like -7% off your exam grade because the exam material only makes sense after attending the lecture even though he posts slides. Graded very largely on 4/5 exams (one drop) w/ a few assignments worth like 5 points.

Seriously take this class online at your community college and save yourself the headache. His lectures and objectives do not prepare you for the tests. No matter how much I studied, not once did it make sense on the test. You have to show up to class and listen to his lectures or u will fail. He doesn't post anything from lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He genuinely does care about your grade, and always was willing to schedule appointments for office hours if you couldn't make it to the original time. A lot of your grade is based on exams, but if you attended lectures it was impossible not to do good. I finished with over 100% in the class, as he gives a lot of extra credit opportunities.

awesome funny guy, who is more than happy to explain a concept to you. I promise you if you do the readings and study based off of his LECTURE, NOT his slides, it will be an easy A for you. Show up to class!! It matters in this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very funny guy, will use lots of personal stories to explain what he's trying to teach. Tests are not hard or tricky at all. Will give you lots of extra credit for just showing up to class so a 3.5-4 is not hard to get in this class at all.

I studies for every single exam, tried to record lectures, take notes and I still did bad on every exam. He had told us in the beginning of the semester that he will have someone take notes and he will try to post them. That never happened. His exams were so hard and made me hate a good and interesting class.

Class structure was absolutely horrible! 100% exam based, lectures don't have any slides to go off of you just have to sit there and listen to way he says, the D2L page has nothing in it to prepare for exams he just tells us to look at our notes then it is very difficult to take notes when he doesn't post any type of notes from the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is AMAZING! He is fully engaged and ready to get your brain involved; all you need to do is match responsiveness and readiness. However, I will halt my praise and say only one comment: the lecture slides he posts are sustainable for frequent absence, but attendance is SO beneficial to gain connections and associations and actually learn!
very engaging lectures, great at answering any questions

Professor Cesario was my favorite professor at MSU, as a second year student. His lectures are engaging, as he does many class demos, and connects real time news with the topics. He is also just genuinely hilarious. His exams match his study guides, and he sets clear guidelines for the papers. I would 100% take him again as a psych major.

This class was one of the most interesting ones that I have ever taken. You can receive extra credit on random days for showing up (I recommend but you can still get a good grade without it) and there are several exams and a few other assignments to help your grade. There are also a few readings he posts but you'll have enough time for them.

Dr. Cesario is very clear about what he expects from students, and I think that helped contribute to my grade in the course. You NEED to attend lecture if you want to do well in the class. You get extra credit for doing so, and majority of the content is not in the slides. If the content doesn't come easily to you, STUDY and go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are worded horribly and are meant to confuse you. Readings are ridiculous and long. His lectures were very interesting and cool and there is a reason why it was full most classes, but having a class where 200/215 available points were from exams is brutal. Overall, this class is hard for no reason and takes hours upon hours of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His class is difficult because his tests are worded in a way that is difficult to understand and he requires you to read graduate level papers, however, he gives so many opportunities for extra credit. He is also very kind and caring and will help you with the material. Go to office hours!!!

If it wasn't for the extra credit, I legit would've failed. This class is way harder than it needs to be. The amount of readings is insane, like he thinks we don't have any other classes. Also, he tells us not to rely on the slides for notes, but then just lectures straight off the slides anyway? Super frustrating. If you can, I'd avoid this class.

Left this class confused by the other ratings. I will say there's a LOT of reading but this is also a 300 level PSY class so I'm confused on how that's surprising. Professor Cesario is very smart, and gives great lectures that always make me think. If you attend class and do the readings you really wont have any trouble with this class. Lots of EC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: My GOAT! Dr. Cesario is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. Dude is hilarious and insanely knowledgable on the subject, bringing in a mixture of his own views and others. If you pay attention to the lectures (hard not to pay attention) and take notes, you will do very well. Can't wait to take another class with him.

This was my favorite psych class ever! Attendance isn't necessary, but you won't do well with the content if you don't go to class. He also gives a bunch of extra credit for just showing up to class. He is so funny, you won't regret taking this class. 5 exams, you drop your lowest grade (including the final).

Genuinely one of the worst classes I have ever taken. This professor is a chronic academic who views the world in data and statistics while ignoring the context. Assigned scientific papers each week that appear on the exams and are not discusses in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the first time I've actually learned from a professor! I took the honors version of social psychology (in 2024), so it's a bit different from the regular one. The professor doesn't rely on slides; he wants us to take notes instead of just reading them, which is why I feel like I've learned so much! He's very charismatic and helpful. :)

3 or 4 exams (one dropped), 3 assignments, and extra credit on random attendance days. Pretty easy he just lectures the whole time while everyone takes notes. He's very interested in his job and goes over a ton of studies. You do have to read some articles before class sometimes but it's pretty easy. Exams aren't too hard either

I have very mixed feelings, because I really liked listening to his lectures, and I like him as a person. That said, it was incredibly frustrating that the tests (which were open-note) felt like they were worded in a way that was meant to trip you up. Not a bad class to fill some credit hours, but be warned that getting a 4.0 is an uphill battle.

Cesario is def my favorite professor thus far. You get extra credit on days he takes attendance, as well as extra credit for doing a 5 question optional quiz every week. There's 4 exams which are moderately difficult, helps if you go to his lectures. Sometimes boring, but he tries to keep you entertained.

His class covered various aspects of social psychology and he always found a way to keep the class engaged and laughing constantly. His lectures were never boring and he offers extra credit points for showing up to class here and there although attendence isn't mandatory. Exams aren't too hard but study well.
He is amazing!!! should for sure take his class. Best teacher ever

I genuinely don't know why people are dissing him. He is amazing! Love him and his class. No regrets for PSY 235 besides the fact it is making me question my individuality and existence as a human, but that is the class topic's fault lol. Study, and you will be fine. He is a lovely guy, and the class isn't difficult, but getting an A, honestly, is.
Prof Cesario Z
As long as you go to class (he takes attendance some days) and pay attention you will do well on the exams and 3 hw assignments.
I dropped his class on the first day. I'm a deans list student and this guy wasn't worth the drop in my grade. BEWARE.

He is lecture heavy, come to lecture and take notes. Not mandatory attendance, but you get extra credit. He uses current and relevant research to guide his lectures, instead of a textbook. The only grades are exams, even if you get 80's on all the exams, you can still 4.0 with the extra credit. I advise going to office hours it helps

His format is based on test scores, supplemented by extra credit which you can receive by coming to lectures. Material is not solely his own work, but recent research.

Bad person

I never liked this guy from the beginning

We just did an exam and I know for sure I got more answers right than the grade he put in he has no problem with making you fail
No assignments just 4 exams

Honestly a great prof. Just be prepared to put in actual effort when he asks you to read. Other than the exams, there's no other grades/assignments so as long as you attend class and read required reading, you will do pretty well on the exam. A lot of people complain but that's likely due to them not going to lecture enough

reviews.comment: He is by far the worst professor I have had in my 4 yrs at MSU. He gets side tracked every class which makes him miss material in the lecture slides. The slides are repetitive. Exams are the main grades aside from occasional attendance extra credit. Most of the exam questions are from long readings. If you can avoid having class with him at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He repeats things often in lectures and often times the lectures can be boring. This classes only grades are four exams and they are long exams which are extremely detailed. He offers a study guide but does not give it until right before the exam and it is little to no help. Did not find out about exams until a week or two before the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've never had such a horrible class in my 4 years at MSU. He changed the way he taught the class, made it way more challenging. He seems to want his class to be hard. Exams ONLY focus on the papers assigned. Extremely hard for a 300 level class, and lectures are very dry and heavy. Only grades by exams, and minimal extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's Awesome

It's so hard to stay engaged when he just rambles on about the same topic and uses absurd examples to back up his points. Half of his lectures make no sense and you're sitting for 2 hours listening to him ramble. You're graded only on paper exams, and he expects you to memorize every paper and their data for the exam. Just don't take it.

reviews.comment: You can tell he cares a lot about teaching and some of his lectures were pretty entertaining. As long as you show up to class, actively listen, and do the study guide it is a pretty easy A

As a non-psych major this was my easiest class by far. Take good notes, come to class and you'll get lots of EC. Engaging material presented in an understandable way if you follow his train of thought, but can be hard if you zone out. Only complaint is that the TAs are not very transparent about their grading on the application assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite professor from this semester! Lectures are not mandatory, but you should treat them like they are. He gives extra credit on random days for attendance points, drops your lowest exam grade, is super funny, and clearly loves his job and his students. If I could rate him above a 5, I would.

I love love love Prof. Cesario, he's funny and is great at teaching. Exams are super easy on one condition: attend the class, the slides are not enough. It really is an easy class, and he makes it fun by doing experiments on us and showing the class's data match the data of the experiments and theories he teaches.

Class itself is easy but seems as if prof goes out of his way to make it harder to succeed Ex: having 5-10 points of attendance credit on days it's hard for students to make it. Showed studies that were only done with white men instead of looking for better studies + would nitpick studies to make them support his idea when that's not what was meant

Hard class to teach, I can imagine. Don't go into this class closed minded, be open for discussion. Material can be hard to hear and understand but you have to separate opinion from statistics for tests. He is open for in class debates and very open to questions. Often times rambles on about one topic. Great class to be in, really eye opening
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you are taking PSY 235 with him, I would recommend him. However, I would not recommend taking 342 with him unless you want to sit through hours and hours of curated data he finds to back up his points. He essentially lectures you, as a white man, as to how no discrimination exists and how it is minorities own fault for any problem that exists.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly I just didn't love his lectures. He's okay at getting his point across, but he's a bit of an over-explainer which makes him hard to listen to. The lectures in general aren't great for people with learning disabilities. The material is fine. He wasn't terrible, I just didn't enjoy his class.
Easily the best prof at MSU. Repeats himself to get the point across, but makes sure you learn something. However, you do have to go to class and pay attention to do well/

Easiest class I've taken. Lectures are kind of long, but it is extremely easy to do well in this class. There are 3 writing assignments and 5 exams (one is optional) and nothing is weighted. The writing assignments are over anything you have learned in class and only are a page long. Also a very interesting class if you need an elective.

this course is genuinely depressing and makes you truly appreciate the wonderfully meaningless gift of human existence. thanks. while Prof. Cesario is very coherent and delivers the course material well, it doesn't compensate for the bleak nature of the course material which ultimately leaves one more depressed than when they first arrived.
Genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. 10/10

Cesario is a super caring/nice guy. Online quiz every weekend of just 10 questions. Plus a final thats made of previous quiz questions. Thats literally all you're graded on, plus Extra credit if you want it. super easy A. he repeats himself a ton to get his point across

It's making me mad that some of these people in the comments don't realize that professors are humans too. The way he taught material was phenomenal. He actually made sure you learned it. For those complaining that you had to show up to class to learn, what did you expect? I have learned some stuff that I apply to my every day life! Great class

Professor Cesario is one of the best professors I've had. He is clear with what he expects, there are papers due but they couldn't be easier to write. The only downfall of this class is it was SUPER disorganized. Takes WEEKS to get exams and papers back, you're taking the next unit exam without having your grade from the last one. Overall easy A

This class could have been so great if it was not for Dr. Cesario being SO disorganized. We did not get our 2nd exam grades back until after we took the 3rd exam which was so frustrating. He also never responded to emails!! The TA's were useless and not helpful whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is literally so disorganized. This class was a joke. The lecture slides are not detailed, so if you skip class, you will do awful on the exams. The TAs for this semester are also so god awful. We had an assignment due in February... Grades are still not all out yet. This class is a joke. Exam scores take up to 3/4 weeks to know how you did.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome guy. Straightforward class. He runs through all of his slides and gives explanations. There are weekly online quizzes and a final, which is composed of the questions from the quizzes. He sounds like Kermit the frog which made the lectures so much more entertaining. The only downside of Joe is that he says "ok" after every single sentence.

My favorite proffessor ever!! He is so nice and tries to get to know the students that show up and participate regularly. All lectures are posted online so you don't really have to go to class but I found it to be helpful because he'll often explain conepts more clearly and answers any questions you have. 10/10 would recommend this class!

I would highly recommend taking your ISS with Cesario, he gives great lectures and makes sure you learn a lot while having a light work load. I wish I could have him again for another class, Easy A and makes lectures interesting. Overall great prof

Cesario is one of the best professors I've ever had. He taught the highly politicized subject of social inequality in the most pragmatic way I could have imagined. Doesn't ask hard questions on the weekly quizzes, just make sure to pay attention in lecture. He definitely knows what he's talking about, and you'll get a lot out of his class.

It has been 4 years since I took this class, but it's still the first that comes to mind as my favorite. Cesario is a fantastic lecturer and the class is so engaging and entertaining. I wish I could take it again, no joke.

The only grades in this class are weekly quizzes and a final exam. Professor Cesario is a great lecturer and makes the concepts extremely clear. He keeps you engaged as well. I skipped a lot of class and still four pointed. As long as you study past quiz questions for the final exam, you'll be fine. It was a fine class, Cesario is a great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: All you are graded on is weekly quizzes and a final. I'm a bad test taker so this makes it hard to be successful.

I'm a psych major, so going in I knew this class was going to be important to me. Cesario made lectures interesting and easy to understand, which made coming to his class even better.  Show up to lecture and you're set. He also gives out extra credit for those who attend lecture on random days.
Amazing lectures, very funny professor.  Gives many extra credit opportunities, content is fun to learn about.

Great class and subject matter, super fascinating and great for learning about the world. Teaches it well and genuinely cares about material. All lecture, lots of time to ask questions, no mandatory attendance, and does offer some extra credit. Grades based on open note online quizzes and a final. Reading not really necessary. Not too difficult.
One of the best professors I've ever had.
Really gets you involved and interested!
Cant say enough about Prof Cesario. Great guy. Lectures are usually entertaining and fly by. Exam questions are pulled right from the lectures, and assigned readings.   Highly Recommend
Super cool guy and gives interesting and funny lectures. Great professor!

I loved this class! If you show up to lectures and take notes you should be able to pass easily. He is super funny, he cares about his students, and his lectures are easy to understand. Plus he gives extra credit and drops your lowest exam! He really relates content to the students. One of his GA's made a big google doc before exams that helped too

I really enjoyed having professor Cesario as a teacher. He made the material very easy to understand and was clear. His lectures were generally pretty easy to stay engaged in and he employed many real life examples. In addition, on many occasions he even engaged the class in different optional participation experiments to provide the class withdata

He is HANDS DOWN the funniest/most inspirational professor/teacher I've ever had. Every single lecture is full of funny real-world examples of concepts that make 300+ students laugh. Everything is very applicable to your own daily life, and this class allows you to understand yourself and your life on a deeper level that VERY few classes do.
I enjoyed the class a lot!! Learned a lot, she has great lectures sometimes fast but she is always available for extra help. Loved chemistry because of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A professor that really cares about what she teaches. Always ready to help if you don't understand something, and provides multiple avenues for success. Class schedule is clear and multiple reminders are given about upcoming due dates. Exams can be rough but offers optional retakes on exams instead of a final exam.

you need to move fast on exams, if you are not confident in the material you will not do well. look back at everything she talks about in class because it will probably show up somewhere, mock exams are not like the actual exams, if you dont come in with AP chem or anything maybe find a different professor

The exams are extremely difficult and she will put questions on the exams that we have never seen before. She is passionate about chemistry, but does not seem to be passionate about having her students suceed. Take any other professor if you want to have an enjoyable experience. No amount of studying could save me.
Genuinely don't take this class. I started out as a chemistry major, now I am a human biology major...

Genuinely just prepares you to do poorly on every exam. Mock exams are not helpful when studying for tests because the questions are so drastically different and so much easier than the real thing. Her lectures do not teach the content beyond the surface level.
I liked talking to her one on one sometimes but she would put the most difficult questions we've never seen on exams and would blame us for not knowing what to do.

Spent countless hours preparing for exams, just for the exams to be a very poor reflection of anything we have learned in lecture. Lecture and homework is much simpler than anything you will be tested on. Currently at a 0.0 credit for the class. Got an 89% in Chem 1 with another Briggs teacher. So exam heavy... don't waste your time on this class.
I spent so much time studying for this 100 level class but still didn't do well.
Take a different professor, you will thank me.
If you haven't taken a chemistry class, or if you are a slow test taker I would suggest taking this class under a different professor. I think she prides herself in making the exams hard.

The class itself is fine. Exam averages are around 70% or less for each exam (you need an 83% on each exam to pass with a 4.0). Almost every single student of hers is retaking exams. Complains that she will have hundreds of retakes to grade if she lets all her students take exam retakes on the same day. Joke of a class, take anyone else.
If you are seeing this, you have either realized the nonsense the professor is on or are a new student. You're lucky if it's the latter.
Exams feel like getting hit by a speeding semi truck
I can hear people groaning when they open the test...

DON'T TAKE HER CHEMISTRY COURSE! Her exams are HARD, it has unfamiliar material, and long questions designed so you cant finish. She made one of our big exams 50x harder to punish the entire class because a few students skipped recitation. Her mock exams and homework are nothing like the test. Test average is 60% but you need an 85% for 4.0.

Her exams are super difficult and she purposely gives you not enough time. It's worth over 60% of your grades but the class averages 59%-65%. She has a attitude and gives unclear answers when you ask questions. If you NEED a 4.0, take a different professor. For a 100 level class, it's absurdly difficult, worse than my 300 level science courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I feel the exams did not reflect what was taught in class. I wouldn't say the class itself is difficult, but more along the lines of wishing there would have been more of an emphasis on the type of viable test questions instead of everything just up in the air.
Genuinely walk of her exams hoping its my last day

Between the different Lb 172 professors, take anyone else. She neglects to teach you the important conceptual understanding you should be obtaining, instead focusing on simple problems and formulaic approaches.The tests are much harder than the lecture material. Take another professor, they will give you a better understanding and a easier 4.0.

Well structure class and ZERO wasted time. Minimal hmwk which is good so you can study the way you need to. She is very approachable and lectures well. The bad reviews recently are literally just because the class is hard imo. Just a little heads up Exam 2 is WAY harder than the other ones so just make sure your ready for that one.

Spends most of the lectures on simple problems then tests you on more difficult problems. Tests are far too hard for the time given and the material taught in class. No extra credit and very hard 4.0. You will have a easier time and better understanding of chem 2 if you take it with another professor.

I have a love-hate relationship with this class. She is a great teacher and is good at explaining things, but her exams are very difficult and almost impossible to study for. You will need a hope and a prayer for her exams. They are long and hard to finish in the time allotted.

Exams are nothing like the mock exams or any study material. Even if you fully understand material, exam questions are completely unpredictable, not enough time on exams as well, 4 full pages with only 50 minutes, 5 exams, weighted very heavily, any other chem professor is better

She teaches poorly and does not prepare you for her exams. She gives you more questions than Dr. Barnard or Dr. Laduca and 20 less minutes to do them. Many people run out of time or rush. She weights tests heavier and provides no extra credit unlike the other professors. Take any other chem professor for a easier time and better understanding.
Just take Dr. Laduca instead and save yourself the annoyance.
Incredibly hard class, is super mean a about a lot of things. Seems like she deliberately tries to make people fail on purpose.

The method of teaching was a lot of doing all the learning outside of class then coming to class to do practice. Her method of teaching just did not click with me as a student who needs in-depth explanations for difficult topics. Not a super hard class but if you want in-depth explanations I would recommend trying a different professor.

I had her class when jamboard was used. Course was flip model, so we worked on materials during class and learned the stuff at home. It was lots of team involvement so pray you have a good team. Most of her exams was very hard since she was picky with the answers. She is seriously one of the harder prof for first years taking intro to chem.

I had Dr. Cass for both chem 2 and my senior seminar, and she is such a warm and caring professor. Her grading criteria is very clear and she is willing to make exceptions when necessary. She encourages thoughtful conversation and engagement with course content and going to her class was always pleasant.

Dr. Cass really wants her students to succeed and if you put in the work, you will be able to 4.0.  Exams can be hard but there is enough extra points with HW and other assignments to cushion your grade. She has really good lectures and explains things well! Very helpful outside of class as well.

The exams this semester were insanely difficult and always had questions we never saw in class or on the mock exam. But there were retake opportunities to bring your grade up which I really appreciated. Got mad at class when everyone did bad on a question instead of realizing that the reason we did bad was because we never saw a question like that.

Exam heavy, lectures are mandatory. Some of the exams were super tough and included material that was briefly covered. There are far easier professors in the Briggs program that offer tons of extra credit and aren't nearly as exam heavy. If you aren't a good test taker don't take this course!

I had LB 171 with her as well and I don't know what changed but class genuinely class began to feel hostile, I know she had personal issues but I do not believe that is grounds for yelling at a class who got low grades (consistently low grades is a teaching problem not a learning problem). Take LaDuca if you can (he guest lectured a few times).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't get me wrong, Cass is not a bad professor at all. She has years of experience in chemistry, however exams can be something else. If you haven't taken AP Chemistry in high school , I would try to take CEM 141/142, which is the natsci sequence. Taking LB chem it is implied that you have a very good understanding of chemistry from high school.
Dr. Cass is the best professor at Lyman Briggs. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Her lectures are actually helpful and her teaching style is top tier. Highly recommend.

Even though the content may be hard, 3.5/4.0 is easily attainable if you put the work in. I will forever preach Dr. Cass's name--she is the best prof in all of Briggs. Take her for any class possible. Her lectures are engaging, she teaches you well, and she is an amazing person. No hesitation, choose this prof.

She is a hard grader on exams, and even though she says that it's based on the work you do, not the answer, she's most definitely lying. I've lost a ton of points because I got a first question wrong, and the subsequent questions were based on it so I got zeros for those, even with the right process. You can do it, but good luck.

Dr. Cass is a great professor who really cares about her students. The course is team-based, so your experience depends a lot on your group. Take advantage of her office hours - they're super helpful. Unstuckstudy was a lifesaver for exam prep.

Although Dr. Cass wasn't the right professor for me, she did everything she could to help the people in class that needed it. She always recorded her lectures and posted them. The exams were heavy, but Dr. Cass always had plenty of prep material posted so you could prepare as much as you needed

This woman made me rethink if I am worthy of an education. She acted so biased towards the men in my class and I truly had no problem with it until she used my womanhood to undermine not only me but also my education. I never expected this from a university professor, nonetheless a woman in this day and age. Frankly disappointed and flabbergasted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is a hard grader and tests are tough, but don't be scared! She is AMAZING. You will not be confused and if you are, she is extremely accessible and will do everything to help. Homework is pretty light (there's not a lot; it's mostly completion grades) and it's never just busy work. Every time I thought I wasn't going to be prepared, I was wrong
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass definitely knows what she is talking about. She is amazing at answering questions and explaining in a way that is understandable. Her exams can be difficult and very comprehensive, all written/no multiple choice. If you study hard and go to class you will be successful. Would take her again.

I loved Dr. Cass's teaching style she genuinely cares about whether her students understand the material or not and is often available for office hours. She provides lots of content for exam preparation and allows for exam retakes at the end of the semester to attempt to improve your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass definitely knows what she's teaching. Very approachable and transparent about expectations. No final- you can retake up to 3 individual exams- that being said you do have to take team exams which cannot be retaken. Recitations are mandatory. If you cannot make it to class she has annotated slides and lecture recordings. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass is a great professor. She definitely knows what she's doing. It's best to go to lectures because you have a group, but she posts annotated slides and lecture videos. Recitation points are attendance-based and groupwork. The class is test-heavy, but instead of a final you can retake up to three individual exams, but not group exams.

I would consider her a good professor, but she is very test heavy and homework heavy, and does not really cover what is on the homework in class. The most inconvenient thing about her is that she is a harsh grader, and makes you meet for 6 hours with the ULAs who are rarely available.
Overly demanding requires you to spend 6 hours with peer mentors over the semester, which makes sense until it gets messed up and you have to do double the work. I do not recommend it it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass is a good lecturer; I would advise to go to class even though she posts videos, because you will work with your group. You will have individual exams as well as a group exams. Exams are very comprehensive and math heavy but I felt prepared most times. The pre-class activities are worth actually attempting and not skipping over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Cass was great! She really tries to help all of her students succeed and makes it possible to do so. The final exam gives you a chance to retake up to three previous exams which is very helpful as well. She does a great job of explaining content in lectures, and will take time to meet with you outside of class if you need extra help.
Dr. Cass is a great prof but the class is very team based so that could make or break your experience

Dr. Cass is an excellent professor! Course is really team-based heavy, so pray that you have a good team for the team project and team exams. Make sure to attend her office hours because they offer amazing tips and insights for exams. If you took AP chemistry, this course will be a breeze for you. Those who didn't, ask a lot of questions.
This was one of my favorite professors!
One of the best professors I have ever had. Really cares about student wellbeing and teaches content with passion. Totally recommend!

Dr. Cass is a very strong lecturer and she explains things conceptually. This is reflected in her exams which tend to be very concept heavy. Overall, she is a great professor to take chemistry from. Definitely recommend for LB 171 and LB 172.

Dr. Cass was one of the best teachers I have ever had. Even though during the middle of the semester I had around a 83%, I had brought it up to a 4.0 by the end because of much she helped. Her lectures are so helpful and the preclass is helpful at times. If you had to pick a teacher for gen chem, pick her. I took her again for chem 2.

Dr. Cass is an amazing professor. She makes herself available for help often. Her syllabus and expectations are very clear and easy to follow. It can be a lot of work, but it is well worth it. No busy work that made me think "Why am I doing this?". Aside from being an amazing professor, she is just a very kind and funny person.

I highly enjoyed Dr. Cass. She is a great lecturer and gives lots of time during class to work with groups on practice problems so you know what you're doing. If you do all of the free points, it is very realistic to 4.0 this class. Also, there is no final and you can retake other exams. I highly recommend her, definitely the best LB 171 professor.

Best teacher for Chem 1. Lectures were extremely helpful to explain the concepts in the preclass activities. Very friendly and easily reachable for questions and help over email and during office hours. Difficult tests but retake opportunities during finals week made them easier. ULA office hours made concepts easier to understand.

Best professor for gen chem. Students from other professors would skip class to come listen to hers because she taught so well. Super funny professor and is very understanding and reasonable. The tests however are very hard, you just have to find a study strategy that works best for you.

Dr. Cass is one of the best chem professors at LB. She posted lectures and had available zoom office hours in D2L. She deeply cared about the students and often stayed after class to elaborate on lectures. Chemistry is hard enough so ofc this class won't be so easy. Mock exams aren't really similar to real exams, so study with other resources.

She was a great lecturer. Explained things very well and by far gave the best education for LB chem. Exams are SO tough tho. So fast paced and tricky. But overall a really quality job teaching and provides more opportunities to practice than many other profs. Take her if you want the best foundation for all other chem classes. Great person overall

Doctor Cass is a great professor for chemistry. She is someone that is great at teaching Chemistry at lyman briggs. She is the best one by far. The class is very challenging however, you need to put in the work in and study a lot to do great in her class.

LB171 was way too difficult for an INTRODUCTORY chemistry class IMO. Exams are harder than in class work and pre-class videos are useless. If you're up for a challenge or love chem, take this Prof's LB171. If not, take gen chem. It ultimately still counts for credit in Lyman Briggs - even if your advisor tries to imply otherwise.

She makes you watch youtube videos for the pre-class and that is how she teaches. There is useless workshops that are REQUIRED and a total waste of time. The entire lecture time is doing jamboards with your group. This class is the reason I am dropping out from Lyman Briggs. Don't even think about asking a question because she is passive aggressive

She is a good professor when it comes to teaching, however you need to pay attention because she moves fast. Exams are really difficult, so be ready to study a lot. I would study 15 hours per exam and get 70s. Try to pay attention and ask questions if you need help.

She was nice but if you need ANY test accommodations, tell her way ahead of time. I had to take a group exam on my own due to a doctors appointment(even with a VISA, I couldn't get the exam taken a different time.) Lots of extra credit. She's very approachable with questions and isn't judge-y at all.

pre class activities are not good and dont help with learning. youre expected to know the content when you get to lecture. spend 70% of lecture doing group jam board problems that aren't helpful. extremely hard exams nothing like the practice ones from class.

Dr. Cass is awesome!! Pre-class activities are where a bulk of learning happens, so those can be a little tough, but she always goes over the material in class and gives us plenty of practice. The tests can be hard, but I would say she prepares us well for them. She is one of the best profs I have ever had.
Cass is awesome but her tests are so hard. Ive heard a lot of people saying that it makes later chem courses super easy but not sure if it is worth it yet...

If you do not have a good foundation in chemistry, you will most likely have a harder time since the basics are taught through short preclass assignments and she goes over harder material in lecture. Go to office hours, she goes a lot slower there. Expect hard exams. Grading is fair and you can earn many points to make up for bad exams.

A really good and easy to follow teacher. You can tell she is passionate on the topics and making sure her students succeed. Attendance isn't required but I heavily recommend going to all as the topics can be hard and you can fall behind easily. Exams can be pretty hard so expect a decent amount of studying.

Dr. Cass is a strong lecturer which is reflected by her hard exams. Exams are a good part of your grade, and deeply understanding concepts is crucial (1 exam and 1 group drop, including final exam). Extra credit awarded if you do all pre-classes and recitations. Studying after class is a must, she goes quickly. A 4.0 is achievable with good effort.

The only way to 4.0 this class is to put in a lot of work outside of lecture each day. The exams were difficult, and not similar to the mock exams. To prepare for exams, rewatch her lecture videos! She does drop two exams (1 individual and 1 group exam) and offers 15 points extra credit if you do all pre classes, and attend all recitation.

Avoid if at all possible. Exams were extremely difficult. Many out of class activities were much harder than they had to be because of a lack of explanation. Cass could sometimes be quite rude with students. If you're not a chemistry or bio major, check with a Briggs advisor about taking CEM chem rather than Briggs chem; it's likely much easier.

Professor Cass's class was the highlight of the week! Her teaching style and ability to engage students in class made learning easy. Her willingness to help students in and outside of class is amazing. The exams will require many hours of studying, but mastery of the material is definitely possible if you pay attention in class and ask for help.

Cass is a great teacher with an amazing personality that keeps everyone engaged throughout her lectures. The tests are difficult, but all the material is covered in class/mock exam. You also get a drop exam which can include the final! If you attend office hours and put in the effort, you will get a good grade.

I came into this class already taken a year of honors chem and AP chem in high school, and struggled in this class. Her test are much harder than any of the other teachers that teach this class, and she thinks that a 70 is "good" on tests. If you do not have a GREAT understanding of chem from high school, DO NOT take this class.
Prepare to learn all of the material by yourself

Cass is such an amazing professor. She truly cares that you learn and are able to apply the knowledge you learn. Although she is a great professor, her exams are honors exams so they are much more difficult than the other teachers.

DO NOT take Cass. Her Rate my prof reviews are old, class is much harder. She goes over the material very fast and is extremely test heavy. Her tests are very hard, and she admitted that she makes her test really difficult. She wastes 2/3 of the class with useless Jam-boards. Be prepared to put in 10+ hrs of work outside of class each week.

She is very loud during lecture, and is very test heavy. She claims in class that a 70 average is good on exams. She also admitted that she purposely makes her exams more difficult. She goes over the mock quiz the day before the exam and got upset when another professor went over the mock days before the exam. She expects you to know the material.

I came into Cass's class hearing that she did an incredible job, and although she is a decent teacher, her exams are unfathomably difficult. Despite this, It is exactly what you would expect from taking a quantum physics class.

easy assignments but will take off points for one thing wrong, even if its grammar. there's prob 50 assignments you'll do but a breeze, and a ton of extra credit. don't really know the prof but light class.

She is awesome, if you have any problems just email her. No tests/quizzes! The class is super easy especially if you've ever taken any sort of high school level bio. You can honestly just do the hw and checkpoints without looking too much at the lessons.

There are lots of extra credit opportunities, so make sure to take advantage of those. I'm not super into bio, so it was a little challenging for me, but the work isn't stressful at all. Overall, she's super nice, and I highly recommend her class if you need an online ISB.

While there is a lot of content it is easy to comprehend but the grading can be harsh. I had an incident with this professor at the beginning of the semester and it ruined the class for me. She is not very understanding to students or at least me. I never rate professors but this is my least favorite professor I have had during my time at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took the online asynchronous and it was super easy to understand and do well

Dr. Weebadde is such an amazing professor!! Although ISB 202 was an online course, Dr. Weebadde was very engaged with her students and always very accessible. She is incredibly caring and thoughtful, and her course is very easy. I also learned quite a lot from her course! Super easy and manageable. :)

Attending office hours will be your best friend if you don't understand the material, she's really helpful and gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. She does not accept any late work, but you get the chance to ask for extensions if needed. You only get 3 late passes so I would recommend using them only for emergencies.
chatgpt will be your best friend (coming from a humanities major). just do the assignments on time and you will be fine!

Pretty easy class overall, you get 2 homework assignments each week that can be done relatively quickly if you just use the PowerPoint slides as your guide. No exams in this class, just a final project. Lots of extra credit opportunities and overall nice professor.
She was very flexible after the events at MSU and changed the class a lot. Still a pretty difficult class for what should be a pretty easy bio class.

Don't take this class if you are not very familiar with Biology. The content itself isn't crazy, but the biggest issue is that she leaves next to no margin for error. If you don't recite things word for word it's wrong. The grading is also very confusing. No rhyme or rhythm to it at all. The assignment rubrics are also very confusing.

i had tremendous amount of stress given by this professor. She is very strict on her grading, even if the assignment is worth 2 points. I could get a 0.3/2. She tries to take off as much points as she can, and makes it her mission to fail her students. Ridiculous!

This professor is a very tough grader and is very intricate in how she grades. If you miss even a small topic that she was expecting in your answer in homework, she will dock you a lot of points. If you need help, her response will not be helpful at all. It feels as if her mission is not for us to pass but to make the class as hard as possible.
Super easy 4.0. It is harder to not 4.0 this class than it is to get one.

The fact that this is a university requirement and the content she teaches is meant for people with a thorough background in biology. Let alone was the content extremely hard, she posts powerpoint lectures and expects you to text yourself.

I took this online, asynchronous class and it was pretty easy to pass. You only get 3-4 assignments a week which dont take that long to complete, so if you schedule time to do the assignments, its and easy A. I really liked how she structured the class, since she made any topic we were learning about easy to understand.

This class might seem to be a lot of work but if you take your time and organize the work it's really easy. There are weekly quizzes which the information can be found in the weekly notes which are really helpful. Im not a huge fan of science classes but I was able to get a good grade in this class with how engaging it was.

Prof Weebadde has her online version of ISB202 very easy to navigate, there is kind of a lot of work, but if you take notes on the mini lessons and complete the assignments on time you should be fine. She is usually available for office hours or encourages us to meet with our TAs
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Weebadde is the coolest professor I've ever had! Bio isn't my strong suit but she made it so easy to learn and understand the material that half of my section, including myself, passed with a 4.0. Just show up to lectures and do your work since a lot of the questions from class and the homework are on the exams.

I've never had a professor that genuinely cared so much about their students. She will stop the whole lecture and focus on one concept until she's confident the entire class knows what's going on. She also offers exam retakes and LOTS of extra credit opportunities. Super nice and loves what she does.
She makes her lectures with lots of pictures and videos so that you are able to visualize and understand easier. Plus she is very kind and makes sure you get help if you need it.

She made sure if your not doing that good in class, that you can see her during office hours and she will personally help you be better. I went and she told me she would never tell someone to drop her class. I backed better because of her and she has a very kind heart in class and outside of it.

Professor Weebadde is such a great professor! She actually cares about her students and offered retakes on the exams because she wants you to be successful. If you have a question on anything, she is super approachable and is willing to help. I recommend you take her class if you have the chance!

Amazing prof, she is passionate about her students and the subject. She treats everyone with such kindness and inspired me throughout the semester to fall in love with language and writing and sharing it. The syllabus can be a little confusing, and the grading scale is challenging (96% to 4.0) but if you put work in your grade will reflect that.

Cindy Hunter-Morgan is an absolutely amazing professor. I cannot stress enough how inspirational her passion for writing is, or how much she cares about her students. She helped me improve my writing tremendously over the course of the semester, and even as an "English person" her class challenged me to become a better writer. tldr; she's awesome!

Cindy Hunter Morgan is the best human that I have met at this university. She has inspired me to WANT to read and write in my free time. She makes you work for the grade but I know that she just sees everyone's potential. I just wanna give her a hug.

Cimberly's organization was extremely confusing, and assignments were very loosely defined, leading to a lot of confusion. Attendance is MANDATORY. If you don't show up you won't pass. Group project is a huge part of the class with multiple presentations. She gets mad at students for having their computers open or doing anything besides paying attention. She will also get mad at you for being 5 mins late.

Overall, the class is an easy 4.0. If you go to class and complete your assignments it's a guaranteed A. The problem I had with her is that she can be very condescending whenever you speak to her, as many have said before. She gets worked up when the class isn't engaged, but gives lackluster lectures that sways no student to be engaged.
Super easy class but she is a micromanager in every way

Cimberly is a very nice professor. But I felt like she would send condescending emails to you if you hadn't submitted a discussion, even if it was before the due date. She wants the best for everyone. Super cool and understanding. wants to set you up to succeed outside her class

She is an okay professor, I would recommend taking another professor if you have to take this class, I relied on the TA, he is the reason why I passed this class to be honest, she talks when students are taking a quiz, not to mention she can be condescending in a way that she talks to her students. just HORRIBLE. don't take her for your own sake.

She is a great teacher. She really cares about her students succeeding. Please attend her office hours she will really work with you so you can have that grade you would like.

She is honestly the best math teacher I have ever had and my grades reflect that. I have always struggled with math but not in professor Cionis class. Great professor! She is very smart and cares for everypne in the class to learn and ask questions. The class is never boring and she good at explaining.

I love this professor. Super nice, communicates well, and truly cares about the mental health of her students. She was also ready, present, and prepared for class, She was super engaging and I wish more professors at MSU where like her. She should be teaching a class on how to be a professor. :)

He really cares about what he teaches and is very knowledgeable about reproduction! Cares about his students.

I didn't have to contact the professor or the ULA so I can't comment on her responses/response times but I literally just didn't need to.

Obviously the professor cares about the subject, and the lectures reflect that, but the quizzes are worded strange and you have to sift through hours of material to find one answer.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

As an asynchronous class it is very disorganized and you only learn from YouTube videos or ted talks, not from any information coming from the professor. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very disorganized course, lectures did not cover what was discussed in the readings, hard to follow what was even going on. Learned more from YouTube videos than the course.

This class was the worst class I have ever taken. Despite taking this class as an elective, it ended up taking more time than my common core classes. The teacher does not respond to emails, lectures are confusing, things have not been graded since week 5, and you have no idea what your grade is in the class. Only take this class as a last resort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Way harder than all of my college pre-core science classes. Teacher did a poor job communicating schedule changes and if you ever want to see what grade you got on something forget it. Its finals week and I still have stuff ungraded from week five. Save yourself and don't do it. The amount of work given for a two-credit class is more than what I do for my rigorous 4-credit classes. Class is super light and easy, you'd get to do weekly discussions or participate in the online discussion through Zoom (which I highly recommend if you don't like writing). The materials are fun and enlighting, quizzes are easy and you can do as many time as you want.
Very kind. Had optional lectures that I think added a lot to the class. Work and quizzes were very doable and she was very understanding.

I took her class Fall 2019, the class was a two hour lecture. She can be very monotonous but the class has no work other than her online quizzes and in class worksheets. She lets you retake the quizzes as many times as you want and the midterm and final are online and you can retake those twice. The professor is nice, and gives class breaks.
Super easy class. Pretty boring. Just make sure to write down all the quiz questions. You get unlimited attempts on them, and they show up on the final. Julie is awesome.

She's nice and approachable. In each class, you answer mandatory ICA questions from the slides with your table group as she lectures. Iclicker attendance. Group CER's. BEST PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD. She's extremely passionate about biology and it shines in her lectures. She's well rounded and cares about her students plus she's funny and adds memes to her slides! Overall good professor. Her lectures were engaging and she tried to make the class fun. The work was mildly difficult but she made it easier to understand. Not too sure about other BS162 professors, but she would be a good option if you need to take BS162.

BEWARE. She was the worst professor I have ever had. Disorganized and the TA did more work than she did. Seems passionate about the subject matter but doesn't come across as someone with a PhD. My recommendation would be to take any course she teaches with someone else if you can.

The class setup was different than what I was used to so didn't like that. Attendance matters and so does participating with in class questions. Exams were short answer and took her a while to grade. She was a very understanding professor though.

TAKE THIS IAH. We did have to read 2 books, not a harsh essay grader. She is so understanding as well. Attendance does count but class is entertaining. Sometimes we would watch tiktoks or the olympics that related to the topic. no tests either!

I really liked Dr. Contreras as a professor. She is mildly disorganized and can go on tangents but it's clear she's really passionate about the material that we're learning about and encourages us at where we are with our analysis while allowing us to go deeper.

just terrible
