reviews.comment: Most unreasonable professor ever. I'm a 4.0 student and I got a 2.5 in this class. Others I've talked to easily 4.0'd this class with other professors. She expects WAYYY too much on her exams and she assigned a 10 page research paper at the end of the semester, which is unheard of in other classes of this level. Avoid her at all costs.

Might be one of the worst professors I've had. Her lectures are very unclear and do very little to get across the information that you need for the exams. This class is designed for Non STEM majors and it is still impossible. The final project for this class is a confusing mess worth 20% of your grade. Abandon all hope ye who have this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Not clear during lectures, hard tests
The material covered in the course was much too in depth for an introductory class.
Don't ever take this professor. Her lectures are useless and so are her office hours. Don't take it even if there are no other options

One of the worst classes I have ever taken. Tests are way too indepth and not close to the power point and free response questions are graded too strict. There is no extra credit, no make up work, and no curving.  Her lectures are worthless and she repeats herself over and over. GET OUT AS SOON AS YOU CAN.

Please save yourself and get out now. A waste of time and money. I was 14th in the class of 250 and was less than a point away from not getting a 4.0. I WAS 14TH and almost didn't 4 point! I'm not sure if she curves or not but I don't think so. If you are unfortunate enough to not have a say in the matter- READ the BOOK!!! It will save your grade.

Dr. Vergara should be teaching an upper level biology course.  BS110 is an introductory course.  I feel as if she expected us to know the material to a greater degree than others.  Her exams are extreamly difficult.  They are multiple choice however there are multiple correct choices!!! She says she wants you to pick the best! horrible professor!

First of all, she has an interesting accent... haven't quite figured out what kind though... She REPEATS herself to DEATH!!! I'm pretty sure we spent over a month talking about Meiosis.  Haven't learned a thing...  AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!

This woman needs to be taken away from the possibility of ever teaching again, not only was she incapable of teaching the class, but she had entirely capable people at her disposal, who I know could have taught the class, yet they never got a word in edgewise...I would try to get as far from this prof as possible.

Out of all the professors I've met during my time at MSU, Timothy Conrad is the best. He goes out of his way to make connections whether you're shy or extroverted. He's understanding and accommodating and truly one of MSU's gems. He's insightful and always happy to chat with students about classwork or the english world as a whole. #GOAT

Conrad is genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had the pleasure of working with. He's hilarious, very kind and extremely understanding. He cares about his students, not just when it comes to their academic careers but their future's aswell. Just stay on top of the readings and be open minded within workshops!
Really helped my grow my writing. I've taken things he's talked about in class with me as I've moved through my Creative Writing degree.

Had him for ENG428 but it's not an option on here. Professor Conrad was great, he was super funny and I had a great time in his class, but it's very heavy in reading outside of class, so be sure to stay on top of assignments.

This prof is amazing and very engaging. By the end of the year, the whole class was pretty close and felt more like a writing community instead of a group of classmates. His feedback on workshop pieces really helped me with my writing process. He assigns a lot of reading, but other than that, his class sessions were a lot of fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: An awesome professor! He is very kind and laidback. He is also very understanding, and the content that we have to read is not boring at all! We have a lot of freedom with our assignments in this class and I would 100% take another one of this classes!
Helped improve my writing a lot through the semester!

Professor Conrad is the most amazing professor I have ever had. Super nice and very relatable. Lectures are comfortable but you still learn so much! My writing has improved so much because of him. Lots of reading, but the material is actually FUN to go through. Best class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Crank was easily one of my favorite professors at MSU, he helped work with me to get internships and his class ultimately led me to change my major for the better. Very inspirational and the class was extremely easy.

Honestly, he was not a bad professor. He does really care about the future of his students and constantly would bring up opportunities and opened himself up to help guide students which I thought was really nice. The exams are a little hard but if you show up to class you will understand whats going on. The group project was pretty easy too.

Crank is a piece of work. Easily one of the worst professors on campus, but is a God in his own mind. Never take this man, as he will make your semester 10x harder than it needs to be. (He is also the type of guy to read all these negative views on him, and conclude everyone but him is the problem.)

William Crank, is a misunderstood professor who just wants to push his students. He provides many opportunities for career readiness. He is a bit strict with grading, but if you participate and give your full effort you can succeed. The tests were pretty hard though.

This professor constantly changes the syllabus and is very disorganized. Likes bragging about himself to the point where any material you're quizzed on has something to do with him. Quizzes were also phrased to trick you and usually had little to do with the material covered in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yea so William Crank got cranky and made me stay after class to give me a lecture on being on time. I also was surprised by how much he bragged. He would  brag about things way off topic all time. If you tell him you know something he might argue you or brag he is better at it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: William Crank made my semester a living heck. He would constantly brag about the most insane things, like how he taught his dog to do a backflip. I asked what this has to do with the class, but he completely ignored me and continued bragging. He also farted during his lecture and pretended like it didn't happen, even after I called him out.

The worst professor I have had at MSU and I am going into my senior year. This guy will make your semester terrible, if you see his name of your schedule run as fast as you can in the other direction.

Crank was mostly just disorganized. His lectures were all over the place. Nobody seemed to be aware of what was happening, and he would constantly change dates on the syllabus. He didn't give out a ton of homework, but when he did, the instructions were usually pretty vague. Brought in a few important guest speakers. The class was a waste of time.

Don't take this class. Professor Crank is the WORST professor I have ever had. To start, he did not stick to his syllabus and constantly changed the dates of things. He loves to talk himself up and talk down on his students; very obvious that he is extremely insecure. His quizzes and final exam were extremely difficult for a basic skills class.
he is very unorganized! he doesn't stick to his syllabus, sends last minute emails about important things, test and pretty difficult with way too much info on them. and he always brags about himself

Crank is a horrible professor, he does not teach he just talks about things he's worked on and brags. He gives no instruction for projects and assignments, then gives you a 60% at most when he grades it. Only reason to take this class is because it is required for pr major.
Goes off topic, doesn't explain assignments at all, gives 50% on every assignment, talks about weird things that do not relate to class, many people dropped because its so bad, do not take this class
extremely disorganized; will change due dates often. he will go off topic during lecture to talk about himself. many assignment directions are unclear
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am currently taking PR 305 with him this class is easily the worst class I have taken at msu He does not make any assignment clear every assignment he will not provide exact details of what he wants us to include. Most of the time he just talks about himself & prides himself that his exams r 15 pages single spaced & that they are not passable.

I have never felt the need to come here and rate any professor until him! I went as far as to even report him to our school. Please just find a different professor! He called students "a joke" to their faces, made racist comments, and his teaching was disorganized and honestly weird. I questioned him a few times and was not responded to kindly.

I had Professor Crank for ADV 486 as a capstone class. It was a perfect class to end my time at MSU. I learned a lot and got to work with a group of my classmates to help solve local business owners' problems in the area.

This professor deeply cares about his student's success. He provides his phone number to students to text or call if they have any questions regarding an assignment or help on the exam. This is something that few professors are willing to do. As long as you try and use the resources he provides, he is happy to help.

The single most disorganized professor I've ever had, assignment and quiz dates that were told in class almost never matched with the syllabus. Spent more time hearing stories about his life than learning the course content. He cares about his students and goes as far as to provide his personal cell phone # if needed, but he is just a bad prof.

Syllabus and rubrics often unclear/messy. Had to beg him to post slides which he flies through. Sometimes he's fair, but that's largely clouded by his inability to run a class or make things easy.

reviews.comment: I appreciate that he used his own experiences in the business in lectures, as that gave applications and context to lectures. However, that's how he gave lectures. Almost purely through his own experiences. You have so few opportunities to earn a grade, so every little thing matters. This course caused so much stress. If you can, avoid his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Other reviews are definitely harsh, I was shocked to see his ranking was so low. He's super unorganized but admits it and is lenient with students in return. The lectures are engaging and he relates class materials to things we all experience. He gives you 4 absences, but otherwise you have to go to class. I honestly like him and he makes me laugh!

While I understand some people frustrations with professor Crank I feel he's being criticized too harshly. Professor Crank provided us all with his PERSONAL PHONE NUMBER. This is an extremely large degree of trust to endow all of his students with and that resource was the main reason I passed the class.
I strongly recommend you don't cause yourself the stress and anger of taking any of his courses

Never met someone who was as rude or as angry as him. Possibly has short man syndrome. Tests had little relation to the lectures or textbook/homework we did. reviews.comment: Straight up says racist and inappropriate things and doesn't take criticism well. Confusing the way he releases assignments and quizzes.

He uploads every lecture and the presentations online for his students, yet he still expects you to come to class.  He is very stubborn when students express questions or troubles they have in class and does not like to listen very well.  Also his attitude towards the class is inappropriate and unnecessary for students in a gen. ed intro class.
Very stubborn and expects too much from an intro class. Will not listen to students recommendations and problems

This semester is his first time teaching ADV205 - Gen. Ed. He talks too fast to accurately take notes, and doesn't give enough time to adequately cover lecture slides. We had an open-note quiz, in which most students scored under 4/10. Despite studying and taking notes, I scored a 7/10 due to poorly worded questions. The attitude on this guy.......

reviews.comment: Was flippant about teaching new material to students like it was something we already knew. Never explained material she deemed unimportant. Mad if students got iClicker questions wrong but instead of explaining the answers she would tell us to talk with a neighbor which could go on about 2-3 times for a question. Wasted time on unimportant items.

I think professor Cooper is funny. I enjoy her dry humor during the lectures. Unfortunately, I wasn't enrolled in JOKES101. She doesn't go over things in very much depth in lectures, and when we get something wrong on an iClicker she has us "talk to a neighbor and try again" instead of actually trying to explain the subject to us.

Melanie Cooper can be funny at times, but has the worst attitude of any professor that I've had. She doesn't seem like she enjoys teaching. She often rushes through topics that she feels are unimportant, quizzes on them, and gets angry when students don't answer correctly. I would recommend someone that is more inspiring when it comes to learning.
She is a bad teacher and does not explain any content well and speed through.

Honestly she was not bad at all. I took CEM 141 last semester, now taking 142. I have a different professor for 142, and honestly I prefer Dr. Cooper. No, she was not the best prof; yes she is blunt at times, but I found her lectures much more engaging than my current professor. People just can't handle semi difficult courses.

she mumbles into her microphone  while teaching new information as if the class knows it already and doesn't go into much detail about anything and has frequently started debating with students in the lecture hall about the wording on her questions. not approachable during office hours either
“I don't want to be disappointed again” - Cooper 2025. Just don't take her…..just don't for your sanity. The other CEM 141 professors actually teach you in a way you can process what's being taught.

reviews.comment:
Dr. Cooper is a caring and honest professor. She might be a bit blunt for some people but I think she's hilarious, She definitely does care about her students' learning too

Actually pay attention and take notes in lecture, take the 45 minutes to actually do BeSocratic activities, check your notes a few times a week and no reason to not get a 4.0

Professor Cooper made the class way harder than it should've been. She states the facts but doesn't teach the reasoning behind them. The tests weren't difficult because of the material, but because they were confusing and worded badly. Homework is assigned after every class but doesn't take very long. I'd recommend choosing any other professor.

This class was hard. I ended somehow with a 2.5 but had a 1.5 for most of the class. Never got above a 50% for the first 2 texts. Textbook is a waste it doesnt help. Homework is due before every class. There is iclicker for attendance but you can drop 2 and its not for accuracy. some people get this chem and some dont. I had many tears here

Chemistry is always hard, however i truly love her. watching lecture videos immediately after class is a LIFESAVER. She is so funny, and makes the class more enjoyable. she responds to emails very quickly, and truly wants the best for her students. If you are taking this class, you will do fine if you truly apply the work and take the extra time.

she honestly was not that bad. as long as you paid attention in class, you'll do fine on the exams. i did amazing on all the exams with little to no studying. there are clicker questions, so attendence is mandatory, but they're participation graded. she explains concepts pretty well + the ta's and recitation are super helpful.

Overall average prof. Reviews on here scared me but she's really not that bad. Can overcomplicate topics but if you pay attention, go to recitation and review besocratic a LOT before exams, you'll do fine. lots of resources for this class so don't freak out if you're stuck with her. cem141 is not THAT bad.

She was so kind. Her lectures, while they had a lot of info, were engaging. I loved her accent! She responds to emails and really wants to help her kids. Any chem prof is gonna have a bad rating/bad grades, it's a hard subject to learn. However I love her!

i'm not the greatest at chemistry, but my god this professor made it worse. she never thoroughly explained the material and expected people to just know it, even though she was supposed to be teaching us... i really struggled in this class and i do not recommend this professor at ALL.

Ms. Cooper was a solid lecturer, but had some issues with technology throughout the semester and could occasionally go too fast. Exams were not that difficult, they were mostly down to paying attention in class and recitation and understanding the learning objectives. Very attainable 4.0.

The content for this class was alright. However professor Cooper's lack of skill with technology and her difficult explanations made it harder to learn overall. She tries to teach in her own way in which majority of the slides are skipped over which has important content. The audio for the recorded lectures were also terrible. Exams are alright.

Dr. Cooper really cares about her students' success. She goes over everything pretty well, and spends extra time on stuff the class doesn't understand. In-term exams were straightforward and weren't hard if you paid attention. Final exam was much harder for some reason and not similar to other exams or lectures.
She does like a million examples of each topic in lecture, and recitation gives you extra practice with the TAs, so the exams are easy as long as you pay attention and do the mock exams she provides.
I thought her class was okay. I think there were things she could have explained better, but it wasn't horrible. Exams are very hard. The book is not very helpful either in my opinion.

Dr. Cooper was honestly one of the worst professors I've ever had. She explains things in such nonsense ways and I learned more talking with others outside of class than I did during the lecture. She makes everything seem so complicated in class but a lot of things that she taught have easier methods or explanations that she just never goes over.

While Professor Cooper is great at lecturing beware that she may call you out in front of 250 others if you are on your phone, talking, or otherwise just not paying attention. Also, she doesn't seem to be nice to her ULAs/TAs if they are trying to help someone when she is talking.

I could tell she was smart, but she has not a good professor. She got upset if she felt like we didn't understand as a class, rather than realizing she needed to teach better. She went through lectures fast, and barely taught anything. The only reason I did good in the class was because I taught myself everything outside of class.

Professor Cooper was rude the entire semester and belittles the class for not understanding material that she can't teach correctly. She doesn't write on slides so if you're rewatching lectures, you will be lost. Alex (hw site) was painful to get through and is worth 10%. Recitation helped for understanding content. You can find Textbook pdf online
horrible professor. doesn't care if you understand material. will move on without explaining.  worked my butt off and even got a tutor and still didn't pass the class.

I do not recommend this professor to anyone. I took chem in high school and she picked by far the most confusing way to teach the material which landed me with a 72%. Plus, she did not care if we understood it or not.

She did not seem to care about her students and seemed to be in a very bad mood every day. Horrible at explaining things and I feel like that's one of the reasons I did poorly in chem. There is hw almost every night and the exams were very hard. They were never anything like the mock exams. Do not recommend her as a prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cooper was weird, seemed like a fine lady though. Didn't have office hours, and I feel like she didnt really care about us much and whether we understood the material or not. Personally, I'm happy this class is going to be over. Had online homework 3x a week, recitation 1x. If you study on your own enough, you'll be fine.
She has no faith in her students and is a very negative professor. In addition, her condescending comments and poor lecture quality made this class a pain.

Honestly did not expect this kind of teacher at MSU. Clearly needs to retire. Yells at people for coughing or sneezing. Can't hold a sentence and never actually explains things. Makes weird comments and basically says, "welp if obvious nobody understands this, not my problem". Recitations are even worse.
The exams are very difficult.

So for a standard week in this class, there is a prerecorded lecture online and associated homework, and class is only to go over that homework and not have a lecture. I hated this but some kids loved it. It doesn't necessarily make her a bad professor, but it makes it so she doesn't mesh with everyone in the same way.

Cooper really teaches the class in a way that is useful for students who need to have a solid base of knowledge for the future. I really recommend taking her for both orgo 1 and orgo 2, her examples and explanations make it easy to understand. HW is based on effort, not correctness. Exams are MC and short response but some points are given back.

Dr. Cooper is really sweet and genuine. She wants you to pass and she wants you to love chemistry as much as she does. After everything that happened this semester, she really tried her best to make us feel supported and appreciated. I actually had a lot of fun with the final project. Love ya Dr. Coop.

Dr. Cooper is a great prof, however she does make you work for your grade! She gives many resources and is available and willing to help students. She is very fair and will give points back on an exam if a question didn't perform well. Some people may not like the flipped classroom style though.

Dr. Cooper teaches you the material and if you put the time in, you learn. Going to office hours for the TA and ULAs are what helped me get a 4.0 in the class. make sure to know how to do the mock exams bc they are similar to the exams, and knowing the homework also helps. Does not really care about her students but if you try, you will learn

She really makes you work for your grade but she knows the material pretty well. She gives lots of extra credit on exams which helps a lot. Mock exams are very similar to actual exams. Going to office hours is really helpful.
Avoid this women at all cost. She made my life a nightmare
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Cooper's research is on how students learn better and she somehow has her class formatted in a way students learn the worst. Online lectures do not resonate at all with exams and you will have to self teach throughout the semester. Recitation is also very hard and does not reflect lecture. Exams are worth a ton of your grade.

Dr. Cooper is a very intelligent person and knows what she is doing when it comes to organic chemistry. However, she is not a great professor. Her class is a reverse style where you watch lectures before coming to class and she goes over the homework during class. There are 4 exams and then a final. No cheat sheet until the 4th and final exams.

For warning, some may dislike the way this class is set up.  There are lecture videos and homework before class.  In class, you go over the homework for better understanding.  50% of your grade is based only on exams: no curves, however there is extra points.  The recitation helps you go over problems and understand the  content.  Sassy teacher.

reviews.comment: You will have to teach yourself everything. If you ask her a question she will not answer and act like you're stupid for asking anything.

reviews.comment: She is not a good professor. You're pretty much just doing self study in her class, she just tells you to watch pre-recorded lecture videos and do homework on beSocratic, then goes over the homework in class.The videos aren't even helpful, I have to go to YouTube for everything. Would never take a class with her again.

Cooper is overall a decent professor. If I had the choice to take others, I would, but if I had to take her again I wouldn't mind it too much. The class is mainly graded on the exams and they are difficult. She does an okay job at explaining things but oftentimes she doesn't correctly relate her teachings to what exactly is going to be on the exam.

I would not recommend her unless you like teaching yourself. she expects you to already know everything and barely goes over the homework. that being said you can fail every exam and still pass this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You will succeed in this class if you apply yourself. Professor Cooper is a fine professor, I have no issues with how she taught. I feel that her class was set up fairly and that she wants her students to succeed. A lot of her examples in lecture can be found in her notes.

I took 251 & 252 with Dr. Cooper, 4.0 both. She is patient w/ students who ask questions or need things to be gone over again. She goes over every hw assignment in depth, and gives a couple extra credit opportunities at the end of the semester. Hw is based on effort, exams are open not/plenty of time to complete. Orgo in general is tough material.

Professor Cooper provides a free orgo textbook that includes all information and orgo I and Orgo II as she was the author. She is one of the most knowledgeable professors that I have ever known and is always willing to share her knowledge. Asking questions is easy and she goes up and beyond to answer any student's questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took this and 252 online. Lectures went over homework but I didn't watch them often. There's a free textbook, didn't read it once. I got a 3.5 and 4.0 in the first and second semesters respectively. Make the most of recitations and ask questions. Exams were open note. Multiple short prerecorded lectures and hw each week. Put in work get an easy A.

Although all homework is through BeSocratic and "gone over" in class, it's impossible to do well on the exams because she rambles the whole class time and expects you to know the material. As an honors student, this class was still challenging for me.

I feel like I should add professor to my resume after taking this course because I taught myself everything. Professor Cooper is lazy, condescending, and simply not good at teaching. The text book has a ridiculous amount of typos, and her handwriting is simply impossible to read. Do not take this course with her.
Personally, I am not great at chemistry, but Dr. Cooper did help me learn. Her lectures are easy to understand, and straight forward and she gives good help if you have questions about homework, etc.

She is an amazing professor. She cares a lot about her students and was always quick to answer my emails. The class does require a lot of work, though, and those who struggle are typically the ones who assume it' a blowoff class. Most of the concepts you have to teach yourself, that's just the way the class is set up. If you care, you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is very down to business and professional. She knows her craft and does a good job explaining concepts. She runs this course in a flipped classroom format, which I found most beneficial to my learning style. I don't think she particularly cares about her students, but you definitely get back what you put into this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Cooper does not take the time to thoroughly explain things and on the rare occasion that she does, it is with a rude and condescending tone. Lectures are just used to go over the besocratic homework; for TWO HOURS, and all material is self taught via watching prerecorded videos and reading the book. Would never ever take her class again.

She is an awful teacher. DO NOT TAKE HER FOR ORGANIC CHEMISTRY!!! Her exam never correspond to the exams. She talks a big game but in reality, she is terrible at what she does. The TA's are also clueless, they themselves do not even know the material well enough to teach you. 0/10 do not take any of her courses. I don't even know how she has a job.

Professor Cooper knows what she's talking about. However, this doe snot make her a good prof. She uses terms we have not yet learned to explain concepts we are currently going over. The "lectures" just go over homework She answers a handful of questions very vaguely. Don't take her class if you don't have a solid background in chemistry!

Dr. Cooper knows the material, she also expects you to know it too. If you haven't taken CEM 142 don't take this course. I took this class online in the midst of covid, but Dr. Cooper was very understanding towards us, she offered extra credit and dropped 1 of 6 bi-weekly exams (short and based on the OCLUE book) which aren't too bad if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She may not be everyone's cup of tea, but I thought she was a good prof. She wrote the book for the class, so she knows what she's talking about. While I do enjoy her lectures quite a bit, especially with how clear I found them to be, she does spend a lot of time covering homework. If you do the homework and practice exams, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Attendance counts and the exams are difficult. However, each exam has extra credit points, so you typically get a 10% curve on each exam. She also provides practice exams and clear learning objectives for each one. She genuinely cares about her students and wants everyone to do well. I would recommend her for 251 & 252.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I absolutely despise Dr. Cooper. She is rude to students, uncaring, and generally seems rather unpleasant. There were several times where someone would ask a question during class and her response would be demeaning and rather condescending. The lectures were okay, but she does not seem to enjoy it. Read the book. All exams have extra credit though
She really doesnt know how to teach. Too fast and not very descriptive. Doesnt answer questions, acts pretentious! Such an awful teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Cooper is by far the worst Professor I have ever had. She goes through the lectures so quickly and flies through the slides that students hardly have any time to ask questions. She will blatantly ignore students questions and never gives a decent answer. Orgo 2 is hard by itself but having Prof. Cooper takes it to a whole extra level. Run.

Melanie is rude and condescending. She expects you to know things that she doesn't teach. She put exams the Monday after Superbowl Sunday, Easter, and St Patricks day so you have to spend the whole weekend studying. Only professor that actually gives homework that is pointless, and recitations are required unlike other professors. Don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Melanie (call her Dr. Cooper if you'd like) is probably my last choice for an orgo prof. She's the only one who assigns homework. Not only does she ignore students raising their hands, but the 3 exams were the days after Superbowl Sunday, St. Patrick's, and Easter. I recommend taking any other prof if you plan on enjoying any of these holidays.

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst profs I've had at MSU. Rude to students, does a poor job of explaining the material, talks too quickly during lectures, HORRID handwriting on her notes that detail important reactions, and gets upset if we ask questions and don't understand the content. Take CEM 251 with another instructor.
