Don't skip lectures because they are most helpful! Do the pre-classes as well because they help with the lecture. Don't be scared to ask questions!!!!
SO nice and passionate!! The lectures are interesting and she makes sure to answer all your questions. She has very helpful office hours that you should attend!

Dr. Dzurka is wonderful, I would definitely take her class again. Not only is she a good teacher, she is a lovely person and clearly cares about the education and wellbeing of her students. Her classes are split between lectures and jamboards. Her lectures are engaging and questions are encouraged. I recommend going to office hours before exams.

Great teacher. Very lecture-heavy, and moves pretty fast. However, you can tell she genuinely cares that her students understand the material. There's a pre-class assignment before most classes, which she expands on during lectures. Her office hours before exams are also super helpful, and she's really good at explaining tough concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Monaca is the best. Very caring, understanding, helpful, and supportive. Class is organized, fun, engaging. Really good lecture and activities in every class. She gives very helpful feedback and great advice on how to be a good social worker.

Monaca is one of my favorite professors. Her lectures are filled with things we can apply in practice. For a 3 hour class it is a good mix of activities, small group, and large group discussion with lecture in between. She is incredibly supportive, helpful, and responsive to her students. You know that your learning matters to her.
Take anything she teaches. She is super caring, does tons of different types of things in class and wants to see you grow and succeed.

You can tell Monaca is a social worker who cares about teaching and her students. Her classes are really intentional in helping us learn. The conversations in the class are great and pushed me to learn.
She is awesome!
in her 310 class right now favorite class of the semester. great in class discussions class is pushing me to think  in new ways. can tell she cares about students.

Her self-care class is the biggest waste of time and money. Be ready to read a bunch of self-help books, do silly activities, practice yoga and meditate. The whole basis of the class is on Pinterest and you don't really learn anything about self-care. It's an overly positive, unrealistic class. Disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her self care class has taught me more than my clinical msw courses. This class is invaluable! Every week she makes a video answering our questions and gives feedback to each student individually each week. Most connected I've felt in an online class so far.  Wish all online classes could be this good.
She's the best, helped us learn. First time a professor has stopped and taken time to figure out what we wanted from the class. I hate research yet this class was pretty good.
Monaca is the greatest professor. She really cares and you can tell she loves social work. Class was fun and the discussions really pushed me to think. I can't wait to take her again.
best class and instructor I have ever had. she is interesting, fun lectures, good and interesting assignments.  made learning fun.

Dyksen seems to go out of his way to embody every cliche of toxic managers. I laughed out loud in many of his lectures because of how unbelievable the things he said were. Expect a zero tolerance policy for everything, including what you are allowed to wear to class. The class could be really cool if not for him. Hope he gets a vacation. Or meds.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not recommend, toxic micromanaged sweatshop from the 80s. The whole course treats grown adults as kindergarteners and cultivates stress over the smallest things e.g. filenames, being 10 seconds late, etc. Disconnected from reality, punishes students who work to survive. Health policy is dangerous, leads to sick students coming to class.

Joke of a capstone. He will fear-monger you the first 2 days of class about coming to class on time and then have the most useless lectures afterwards. Just pick the most fun/easy project and don't give this class your peace of mind.
Dr. Dyksen uses old slides and material to lecture when every single lecture could have been an email. Any value in this course is provided by external clients or peers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I understand that he cares about student success, but he tries to achieve that with overly strict policies and grading criteria, making me rate this class a 1 in quality overall.  You will lose points for very small things and missing any day of class severely affects your grade.  One of the most stressful classes I have taken at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The hate for Professor Dyksen is a little overblown in terms of the attendance. Although, it is annoying that even if you give ample notice for a single absence, he might not let you take it without a grade penalty. The real issue is the grading structure of the class. You will have no idea how you are doing in the class until the very end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He clearly cares about students' success and can be blunt about it. If you show up and do your work, you'll do well in the class. I learned more from this class than any other class in my degree, and it is partly because he has it structured like a real internship. If you disagree with his teaching style, you probably won't succeed in a real job
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a class where you'll actually learn the most compared to any other comp sci classes you've taken throughout your undergrad. However, I do agree that the kind of group you get can be sometimes a deal breaker but professor is really fair in grading when it comes to individual contributions.

Dr.D is misunderstood. He tries his best to relay the importance of professionalism and timeliness so he is strict about absences and missed work but thats what makes his class so important. Many people miss this point and find reasons to blame him for their poor grade. He clearly outlines expectations and genuinely wants everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: On top of mentally torturing some of us with these insanely hard projects, the cherry on top was when a simple web application won the Best award. It convinced me that there is 0 point in doing any hard project and I highly suggest anyone in future classes to pick easy projects and save your sanity
This man's grim little goblin smile haunts my every day. ironically abysmal with technology. pits students against each other.  I bet he loves global warming.

The most disrespectful prof I have encountered in my entire college experience. He clearly thinks all the students are indebted to him. He has no experience in industry and loves the fact he can boss around students. Constantly gives incomplete directions and then yells at the entire class. Truly disappointed in MSU Engineering dept. at this point.
He's making me lose my hair. What a shame that this class is almost unavoidable. If I ever have a boss like him I'd quit on the spot he thinks we are in the 50s.

Honestly, this guy is someone who has never actually had any real life experience in the industry and his entire shpiel is based on other people's experiences. I get that he has close associations, but the way he operates doesn't happen in most companies and if you ever face management that operates like him, that's not a job you'd want to stay in

Rude and disrespectful. Pulled me aside one day while on my phone waiting for class to start to ask if I had "accommodations or a visa to doodle and draw in his lectures" (i draw random lines to not zone out in lectures). When I replied no he said, "then I need you to pay attention and stop doodling in my lectures". needs to retire immediately.

He has a strong ability to make you feel worthless for making the same mistakes he makes. Expects not one mistake to be made and subtracts points for every single thing wrong. Laughs it off when he makes all the same mistakes, presentation errors, broken software, wrongly accusing you, etc. He needs to grade himself the same we he treats students.

If you are a bad student, good luck. If you are the best student, good luck. The hardest man to please I have encountered in my entire schooling. When I first saw these reviews I promised myself i would see if she's really this bad and come back and write a true review. Everyone is correct. If you plan to take this don't panic it is possible to do well it is just an insane amount of work for a 100 lvl class. Exams cover FAR too much content, she doesn't make the lectures, or grade anything.

I know this was an online class, but 6 hours of work a week is unobtainable. I had over 300 flashcards to memorize for every exam (she doesn't give a study guide, just learning objectives). Lectures are broken up, and not concise. D2L was not organized at all. For multiple weeks we had to watch a documentary on top of lectures. Doesn't answer email
A ton of work for a 100 level class. She also never responds to emails.

I know many reviews make HNF150 sound daunting, and while I don't think the professor is very involved in the class, it's doable. The first exam is a bit of a wake-up call as to how much information is required to be memorized, but chances are if this is a required class for you, that's something you'll have to get good at. Start studying early!

Dr. Ekstrom is not accessible outside of class. You send an email? You will not hear back. There are very few accommodations for anything. The lectures are useless. Lots of busywork. Exams are in person and heavy. I regret taking this class, and that is primarily due to the professor. This should not be labeled an intro/100 level class.

Took this online with her, she uses Dr.Alaimo's pre-recorded lectures from 2020, not even her own lectures.  Extreme course load for a 100 level class, I spent more time studying vitamins than I did trying to learn material in my own major. Clearly does not care about you, I would take this at CC or with Dr.Alaimo.

As a student, I feel let down and unsupported by this professor, and I can only imagine how many other students may have felt the same way. It's unacceptable for educators to not prioritize their students' needs and create a negative learning experience. She does not deserve the title of being a professor! Truly disappointed at her teaching method
THE WORST PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD!!! She is awful and does not care about her students. She NEVER responds to emails!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: In person exams for asynch class. Wasn't accommodating exam wise after tragedy. Uses a website for questions but doesn't respond half of the time, avoids certain posts, and doesn't respond to email. Has TA's do everything for her. Class is full of busy work. If you have to take this class, do it w/ someone else or at a CC. Absolute waste of time :/
Course load was extreme for a 100 level class. Definitely a weeder class for KIN/Nursing - would not take if you're looking for a STEM credit. Did not feel as if prof saw students as actual people.
Just don't take her, expectations are set too high for a 100 level course.

Very difficult class with tons of information to memorize. The professor does not respond to emails, the workload is insane for a 100-level intro course, and the exam questions came out of nowhere. The in-person exams were just so much information to remember it almost seemed impossible to get above a 60. There is tons of extra credit offered.

Yeah, you don't want her, or this class. In terms of the professor, she's a joke. She is insensitive and immature. How you getting paid to teach an online class but have your TA's doing everything and can't respond to emails?! Regarding the work, she makes the mini lectures so boring, and the exams are on too many topics. Must memorize everything..

Do not take a class with her, ever. Worst professor I have had, by far and large. Does not reply to emails, requires in person exam for an online course, course work is FAR too much for one exam, as well as for a 100 level class, very insensitive tot student needs.  Need assistance? Don't bother asking, she doesn't care about you, only her paycheck

I don't recommend taking this class with this professor. I have no background in this kind of field but needed to fulfill a STEM credit. The load of information is TOUGH. There is a lot of material, assignments, and the exams are extremely hard. She also was not very accommodating after the recent tragedy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The content of this course was very very tough for a 100 level class, but if you study hard you will succeed. Professor Ekstrom hosted review sessions before every exam which was helpful. She was also very helpful- I was sick and unable to come in person to one of the exams so she gave me an online version.

Hard class in general. Don't take the class unless it's the last professor available. This class has tons of work to be an introductory class and is also very test-heavy. You can get a 100% on all homework and still end up with a C. She once forgot to print our exams out resulting in half the class going home in the middle of the exam.

Dr Ekstrom was very unreachable and the class was extremely difficult & the assignments for the week were just over the top. She was rude in email exchanges and not very willing to work with students at all. The course was supposed to be asynchronous but exams were in person. This class should be a MUCH higher level,students had to teach themselves

This class is required for my major otherwise I would have dropped it. Was an online asynchronous class, so basically taught myself everything and had to do in person exams. Review sessions put on her were never helpful, I relied on other classmates to prepare myself for the exams. \

Throughout the semester not one of the online lectures was made by her and reaching her by email was very difficult. I once tried to contact her about an assignment I was having trouble opening and I never received a response back so I had to figure it out myself. The exams weren't too bad but there was a lot of busy work which was very annoying.

Had to take HNF 150 for my health promotion miner and can confidently say I would have not 4.0'd the class without previously taking biology, physiology, and organic chemistry. This is a 400-500 level class disguised as an intro class. Dr Ekstrom has a horrible approach to teaching, which involves reading off a script instead of actively engaging.

Don't take this class unless you have to. It is so much work, luckily there is a good amount of extra credit but still exams are so difficult for no reason, but a lot of the material is all memorization and there is just so much to do. The professor doesn't do any of the lectures, it is someone else. I don't recommend it at all.
Just lots of information you have to teach yourself basically because of the class being async. which is difficult.

There’s is an overwhelming amount of information to be learned for each exam. It’s all just memorization and you basically teach the course to yourself. If you study the shared learning objectives you should do decent on exams.

Not my favorite professor. Showed up to an exam with not enough exams for the number of students and gave half of the students an option to take the exam online. This class is completely asynchronous, and you are expected to memorize the material with in-person, closed book exams. Shows up unprepared and does not teach whatsoever. Do not recommend!

Her class is definitely tough, especially because it's asynchronous, but not impossible. She hosts weekly review sessions for questions and tries to facilitate as much interaction as possible. There was an issue with not printing enough tests, but she seemed genuinely concerned and people make mistakes. Doesn't makes her an awful prof.

She only comes around when its tome for in person classes, even though the class is all online. She is very unprepared and I feel like I am teaching myself everything. This is supposed to be an introduction course, but there is way more info and not much instruction. I would not take a class with this professor again.

Worst professor I've ever had. Showed up for exam and she didn't make enough copies, so she told us we could take an online option (lockdown and proctored) or wait 15 minutes. Little did I know that 15 minutes meant an hour. Her exams are nothing like the hw & expects you to memorize everything, without any instruction because it's an asynch class.

Widely considered one of the worst profs at msu. Insanely difficult for a 100 level course. She’s incompetent which forces you to teach yourself the material. Tests are crazy compared to coursework & everyone does poorly. Not sure how she hasn’t realized that a low class average is a reflection of her lack of teaching skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I’ve ever taken. It was all online asynchronous, but we were required to take the exams in person after teaching ourself all of the content from the dense book. Far, far too much memorization for an intro class. Please save yourself and do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is extremely dense in terms of material we’re expected to learn in the proper amount of time. Online lectures are scripted, unrealistic homework expectation, and she doesn’t bother to check that the proper amount of exams are printed by the time of the scheduled exam.
Way too much content to fully grasp, this entry level course is not entry level. Some pointless activities and exams are terribly specific and exam reviews do know help at all.
Took her 4 times to print enough exams. Doesn’t teach well in the first place. Terrible professor.
Horrible class. Very unhelpful and bad at replying. Wayyyy too much work for an intro class, and she is no help at all.

Although I managed to get a good grade in this class, I absolutely do not recommend Dr. Ekstrom to anyone! The class format is completely scattered, there is an unreasonable amount of info to memorize for tests, feedback and grades take absolutely forever, and the prof is not easily accessible outside of class. Be prepared for dense course material

Grades weighted very heavily by exams and the Dietary Assessment assignment. Nothing prepares you for the exams especially right now on lockdown browser. Problem sets are completely unlike the exams. Grade turnaround is absolutely horrible. Did not receive grades for DAA2 or Exam 2 until the last week of classes which is over 1/4 of the grade alone
She is terrible. She showed no interest in her students or their success and offered little support.
She seems to put little time into actually helping her students succeed. It's hard to get a decent grade in this class due to the amount of memorization.

Good class, lots of reading. Don't buy the textbook right away, instead look into MSU's affordable textbook program where she has set it up for you to rent online for free. The class is pretty challenging due to volume of content, but there are many opportunities for extra credit. Very applicable to real life, take the honors option if you need it!

Would not recommend to anyone. A 100 level class should NEVER have the amount of work she assigns, and during a pandemic this was almost impossible and felt like 4 classes in one, on top of taking OTHER classes. Horrible communication, unclear test material but STRICTLY graded and no notes allowed. Treats a 150 level class like its a 400 level.

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. This is the worst intro class I have experienced. Refused to listen to students. Help yourself, do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In my four years attending a university, I have never had a professor as awful as this one. She ignores student questions. Her exams are impossible, even if you are a good student. She posts incomplete notes. Her feedback time for grades is ridiculous. Please, for your own mental health, avoid this professor.

No idea how this is an intro class. It is by far the hardest class I have taken at MSU. They accepted over 900 kids to take the class, 60 different groups and 8 different TA's none of which really know what's going on either. The amount of information you need to memorize is nearly impossible and the exams are 60 questions with a 60 min time limit.

reviews.comment: I took this class online which I kind of regret beacuse I dont ever taken online classes so it was hard to keep up but if your good at time managing then you could try online class cuz I heard her lecture is boring but I feel like it will keep you on top of studing at least it would for me Her exam are hard and one gets dropped outof4:60% ofurgrade

Lecture was SO boring she put everyone to sleep. Don't buy the book. I only took one exam in person and there was so much information and memorization of things needed. One exam is dropped out of the 4. There are few opportunities for EC. Don't take her for an elective SOO much work and memorization needed

The exams in this class are difficult. They are 50 questions, but each question is worth 4 points making it challenging to get an A. The material is long and tedious. I do not recommend taking the online section because it is hard to keep up with and learn the material.

Would be a really interesting class except Dr. Ekstrom is hands down the worst professor I have ever had. Her lecture slides are a mess and she NEVER posts slides or grades in a timely manner which makes taking this course online extremely difficult and stressful. Please save your sanity and take this class with a different professor.

Crazy obsessed with nutrition, all she does is lecture and she is less than helpful to prepare you for the exams, very oblivious that everyone is doing poorly, makes TAs do all the work and run review sessions and they also don't really know what to do. homework is manageable, exams are very hard

Theres iclicker points but she allows 6 absences. I thought the assignments were pretty easy and for the online quizzes you can just google the questions and find the answers easily. She tells you exactly whats on the exam and overall the class was easy HOWEVER her lectures are extremely hard to sit thru she doesnt know how to teach.

There is literally no reason for her to be employed by the college. Worst lectures ever. Reads directly from the PowerPoint and does not face the class half the time. reviews.comment: Great professor, lectures were a little boring though. Definitely study hard for the exams.

Dr. Ekstrom was one of the worst professors I've had. She's a nice woman and clearly educated in her studies, but she gives the most boring lectures. She shows no passion, no change in tone, and doesn't seek any opinions from students. The class content was okay, and the homework/exam load was reasonable, but her teaching made the class unbearable.

Do Not Recommend! Horrible Professor, class is extremely boring and consists of her reading everything off the slides and not further explaining anything. reviews.comment: All of the information is in the slides, she takes attendance from clickers. I personally didn't enjoy the class but it wasn't too challenging. I'd still recommend her class.

Definitely one of the worse professors I've ever had. Literally reads all lecture material off the slide in her monotone voice and doesn't add much other information. reviews.comment: Super boring lectures. Have to do a lot of studying to do well on the exams. Claims the learning objectives are what will be on the exam which was totally false. Really need to attend class to get a good grade.
Very boring lectures, basically reciting the power points. Mandatory lectures. Wouldnt take this class if it wasnt mandatory for my major. Everybody shows up to do their own thing

This class was unnecessarily dreadful to attend. Professor Ellison often comes off as pretty condescending, and the lectures are just not that interesting for being attendance mandatory. reviews.comment: She does grade the debates pretty harshly, but other than that the weekly assignments are easy points. There's 1 assignment each week and 1-2 readings you have to do before the weekly quiz. She also does so many group activities that are pointless but most of the time you don't have to turn them in.

I don't even know where to begin. This class was a waste of time and money. She grades so harshly on our debates and assignments. The class is entirely common sense and there is a quiz every week. I'm so happy I never have to take this class ever again. Easy 4.0, but please choose a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: In my opinion this professor doesn't seem to understand that everyone in that class is somewhat forced to be there. Her lectures suck and instructions on projects are often very vague. She grades using ChatGPT and responds to emails rude.

The class itself is not difficult, however professor Ellison can be condescending at times when asking for help. She is a tough grader on debates, but compare everything with the rubric to be as close as possible to her unrealistic expectations. Try to take the class with someone you know so you can have hope for a good group. Overall, easy ISS.

She isn't necessarily a bad professor but her way of lecturing is painfully boring. Attendance policy is overly strict when showing up to the class doesn't really offer much in the way of learning. An easy class just not very enjoyable in any way. Not a bad experience, but also not good

Professor Ellison was difficult to gauge, she was nice on occasion but there were times where a group member would go up to ask for clarification on an assignment and she was condescending in her response. Easy class if you do your work, you can easily get an A, but I found lectures disengaging even when I actually was interested in the material.

Overall, this class is manageable. The weekly quizzes and assignments were due at the same time every week, so remember deadlines; she does not give late credit. You work in groups pretty much all semester and have 2 big projects. Her instructions are not always clear and she can be difficult, but if you do your work, you will 4.0 easily.
Very boring lectures and everything is based on group work. Grade is based on weekly quizzes, weekly assignments, and two group projects.

Dr. Ellison is a really great professor, she is extremely kind and cares deeply about her course and the students taking it. The class was very easy, each week we would have a simple homework assignment due at midnight on Fridays, and a simple 5 question quiz on the 1st meeting of the week. The course is simple, you can get an A with little effort

Professor has a superiority complex and was very condescending to me and other students whenever we needed help. Her instructions are never clear when assignments are due when it comes to weekly assignments or the big projects. The material itself is not difficult; however, the professor is difficult to deal with.

Prof. Ellison is extremely nice but has incredibly boring lectures. You pretty much only get graded on 2 group projects and weekly quizzes. The only reason to take this class is that it is an easy 4.0.

Super easy class. Dr Ellison is honestly pretty rude, although she has a good sense of humor during lectures. There is no final assessment yet instead a final group project. The entire class is mostly group work and there are weekly quizzes. Most of the time lectures are pointless but  there is Clicker for participation each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Ellison was the best professor I've had. She is SUPER chill and has a good sense of humor. She takes the time to learn everyone's name and is super respectful. Attendance is mandatory, but there are no exams. This class is heavy on group work, but not in a bad way. TAKE THIS CLASS!!

This is my favorite professor every. She is very chill, makes class fun and you'll actually want to go to class. She does use iclicker and attendance is mandatory. There is a lot of group work. There are 5 question quizzes, they are easy points if you do the short readings. It is just an amazing class and Dr. Ellison is awesome. Take this class!

Ellison is one of those professors that is able to teach a topic someone might find boring and make it into something interesting.Her sense of humor is hilarious and she is always finding new ways to teach, she is a bit of a harsh grader tho. You will also have lots of group projects and are constantly meeting with your group in and out of class.

I don't think the class itself is super hard but she is not understanding at all. She is really mean honestly and just likes to argue with everything you say. I had a terrible time in this class and I would never ever recommend her or her courses.
Lovely professor! She is the sweetest and I always looked forward to coming to this class. My only critique is about the course and having to work with the same group the whole semester.

I took the honors option and it was easy. I didn't read a single reading and guessed on all the quizzes and still got a 4.0. The only thing you have to worry about is the class presentations and group projects. She grades those pretty hard so try your best on those and come to class. She also has a funny sense of humor so that's also a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ellison is an amazing professor and the course is integrated with various interesting topics (course is discussion heavy) that go well together. There are a few group projects so hope that you have a good team; she is a tough grader for projects. There is a weekly quiz that's 5 questions but it's lightwork and readings are usually easy too.

Dr. Ellison was a cool professor. Lots of group work, 2 presentations and 2 other "big" projects. Seemed intimidating at first, but the class wasn't too difficult, she just wants you to have discussions and think. She grades kinda strictly for projects, but it's not difficult to do well. I hate social science, but I still got smth out of her class.

Dr. Ellison was amazing. Funny and laid back. 5 question quizzes every week based on material learned the week before. We were put into groups of 4-6 and had about 5 assignment/projects that had to be completed as a group. She cares more about if you are learning something from the class rather than getting things "right". Very eye-opening.

She is a good professor, don't get me wrong. However, I feel like it is nearly impossible to get a 4.0 in this class, you are hardly graded on anything so a 5 point quiz can have a 1% impact on your grade. And she grades extremely strict. I would take her again compared to other professors, however I am sure there are better professors for ISS 305

She literally was my favorite professor ever, she used iClicker for attendance but you were allowed a few days to miss and still get a 4.0. She's super real, straightforward, funny, the content was easy. There is 1 group project to present and 1 solo that isn't presented. She had fun topics to talk about and made it fun to be a part of. Slay Brandy

Prof Ellison was remarkable and probably the best prof I had in the semester. We had lots of fun classes and museum visits. Assignments were not that tough and could be easily managed. I recommend taking her class.
I took Brandy for my seminar aboard and I loved the class the entire time. She was so caring and helpful for anything we needed help with. I would 100% take her class again.

Dr. Ellison is great! However, I took asynch in summertime (which I would not recommend). I missed a quiz once and she let me make it up by just writing a half page paper on any article! If you ask for help, she is VERY accommodating. This class taught me SO much and really helped improve my research abilities. Be prepared for group work though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The hardest part of this class is the group projects but it can be easy depending on your team. Class was always fun and attendance was tracked. If you do the work you will 4.0 the class. Professor Ellison was always enthusiastic and willing to answer any questions.

Great professor who actually cares for the well being of her students. I missed an online module one week and she reached out to me through email making sure I was well. Easy class along as you keep up with online assignments.

So much reading and listening to podcasts. The professor told us at one point that the workload should take you 16 hours to complete. The work for the class opens every Thursday and is due on Mondays, leaving it to be done on the weekend. When class complained and asked for it to open sooner her response was pretty much I don't care.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Profesor Ellison is very easy going and understanding. Her projects are fun and interesting and allow you to be creative. You can miss class here and there but I always enjoyed going. It was relaxing and homework was never bad and very manageable. Definitely take her course if you can.

Easy class and chill Prof, however, a stupid amount of busy work, like way to much for this class. I on average have about 10-15 things due just for that class, while it is easy the sheer amount is what is insane, especially with heavier class loads.

Extremely chill and likable professor, I couldnt recommend her enough. The group projects are fine and easy if you have a decent group. Lectures were pretty interesting. She constantly gives opportunities for feedback so her class is always improving. Great class for first-year students.
Very laid back and did not have anxiety when going to her class. This course was not stressful at all, it was more of a breather class from all of my other ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to take Prof. Ellison, do it. She is one of the best professors I have had and she is very personable. She is so caring of her students and her class is extremely interesting.
As long as your group works together you should do awesome in this class. The work took me maybe 20 minutes per week. The group projects are a little tough, but there is only 2. No final either!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: So I took this class completely online and it's a really easy course with a really easy professor. There is a lot a busy work (as I like to call it) but most times it takes less than an hour to do. Two group projects so hopefully you get good teammates because its random and no final exam. Prof is also lenient with due dates. Overall easy 4.0 class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Heavy workload, reading heavy and very short powerpoints. Workload is repetitive and mostly busywork. Course format is difficult to follow. Laid out week by week in D2L but each week has some info for week before and after. Discussion board requirements are difficult to follow with two different charts to use to find when and what to post.

Don't waste your time, and money. Ellison apparently thinks making students read WaPo articles, and watch YouTube is teaching. I get that ISS classes are just mandatory courses in ideology, but this one was a waste of everyone's time.

Professor Ellington did a good job given the online format of the past semester. The lectures could have been more detailed, but aside from that I have no real complaints. She assigns a fair amount of work, but as long as you do it all you shouldn't have a problem.
Beware of discussion boards. Professor Ellison is super nice, but she definitely gave the appropriate amount of work for a 4 credit class, don't expect it to be light.
I found the class to be pretty fun and the professor is very receptive with questions and will provide you with feedback really quick. The quizzes get kinda annoying but they arent bad

The class sounds interesting but I found myself dozing off. The mini quizzes every Monday where you have to answer five questions got old real fast, even though I listened to the assigned podcasts and read the assigned reading I didn't do well on them until the class went online. Pray you have good teammates for the group projects.

Every Monday, there are 5 points quizzes. The material gets confused and can't even find it in the readings. If you do bad on these, like get 3 out of 5 everytime, you will be in bad situation. I hope her quizzes are more easy and not this confusing...

She is a very good professor. Not only is her class very interesting, but she keeps the lectures alive. They are not your typical "sit and take notes", but decently paced and interactive in a good way. Also, when having some sort of illness, she is very understanding. Even if you are without a note, she really does care about her students.

The topic was Education. NO EXAMS! Group projects include discussion panels (your group leads discussions on some aspect of Education) and a communication project (a brochure or infographic). Nice class

oh my god this class was actually the worst I made an account just to write this. you have to read the text book, take the quiz and do the homework every day before class, then go to class for her to repeat bar for bar what you just read. then she'll go on long tangents about things that do not matter for the rest of the class. it was so awful

I am not usually great at science so take this with a grain of salt but I had to work and study extremely hard to get my grade up to a 4.0 in this class and had to get a tutor. Do not take this class if you have a rigorous schedule.
she sucks and is extremely exam heavy, more than half your grade is exam based, if you want to fail, take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: The professor herself is kind. She wants to see her students succeed & will help you if you reach out. But, I would NOT recommend taking PLB 105. It's the hardest class I've taken in my undergraduate years. It's not what you think is extremely exam heavy. To put it in perspective; I've been 4.0 student for years. This class I got a 2.5. It's hard.

Beth seems like a nice person overall but the way the class is structured can make getting a 4.0 hard if that's your goal.  You need at least a 93% and there's four Respondus-proctored, closed-note exams that are worth a total of 60% of your grade.  If you don't mind a 3.0 though the class isn't that bad.  Expect to do a lot of self-studying.

At least for PLB105, not really a stand out professor. Online meetings weren't mandatory attendance so I really never interacted with her. The class wasn't super hard, just weekly videos and quizzes on them, plus small projects every two or so weeks. Not a bad class but not something super interesting.

Take your ISB class with someone else. Everyone else that I know that took ISB 202 had no trouble at all, yet this was the hardest class of the semester for me freshman year. Because of her. Her lectures do not prepare you for the exams and she the amount of work she requires on about 5 different platforms is terrible. Take it with someone else

Professor McCann has the best energy I have ever had from a professor! She loves what she teaches, and has great interactions with her students. There is weekly homework, and pre-class quizzes, but they are not hard or time consuming. You have to purchase an online textbook that comes with the homework, but she gives you a discount code!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McCann made biology truly enjoyable. I am not a science person but with lots of studying, I was able to get a 4.0 in the class. The course is mainly graded on the 4 exams taken. I would definitely recommend her class since there is not a lot of work and some small extra credit assignments available.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Where do I even start. The entire class failed an exam because she assigned it over thanksgiving break. Now she has closed the course module without submitting our final exam scores so we have no clue how we did. Overall one of the worst experiences I have had with a college professor. Also half the material on the final wasn't even in the review.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor at MSU. She's very passive aggressive and rude to students. This was an online class, yet she expected way too much for an introductory biology class. If you have her, RUN. Also lockdown browser exams and this class will 100% ruin your GPA.

Expects way too much from her students for an introductory class. Doesn't care about what grades her students are getting (even when the class average is a 60%). Also, she WILL assign HW and Exams over breaks. Do not recommend.

Terrible grader, no information on assignments, and little to no help

reviews.comment: There is a LOT you can say about her. She does not use D2L, or much technology at all, her lectures consist of her talking for 50 minutes with a few words on the white board. There is a midterm exam, a final paper, and a final exam, that's it. Tough grader, with the rubrics/syllabus formatted where you almost have to ask her questions.

reviews.comment: Excellent professor, really teaches you how to write and analyze history. In order to get the most out of her classes you definitely have to ask questions and participate. reviews.comment: Awesome professor as long as you actually try and show up to class.

reviews.comment: I have not enjoyed her class at all. She only lectures with no slides or any visuals at all. She never asks for participation

reviews.comment: If you want to take an easy and fun history class DO NOT take this class. The proff is nice but relies too much on the lecture and has no slides. If you want to sit in class for 50 minutes listening to a dry lecture three times a week, sign up. Also, your whole grade is basically the midterm, final, and a book report so good luck if you bomb one.

reviews.comment: Expects you to take notes solely off of her words and uses no visual aids or slides. Grades are only determined by three things, two exams and a paper. L class, L teacher, get ratio'd

I took Prof. Tabuteau as a freshman in 1981, HST 349: Constitutional and Legal History of England after 1399. I wanted a challenge, and got it. Her lectures were intense but fascinating, her grading system very clear: rehash, get a C; analyze and succeed. Do the work. Wish I had taken her again. BTW, I've been a lawyer since 1988. Thanks Prof. T.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: the lectures were given in written form. closed minded professor who doesnt respect others opinions. Do not take this class. She is rude in her grading and insults you. She doesnt teach and you will not learn anything. She should not be teaching.

Listen. The reviews here are always going to be critical because she actually makes you do work outside of class. That's to be expected in a university course. She grades on three essays that you're expected to read for, especially during the pandemic. Very accessible and grades are based on your evaluation skills, not opinions. Awesome elective
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly, she's rude and not open to other opinions. You need to start the class knowing everything she knows or you won't pass. I barely learned anything and what I did learn, I taught myself. The term paper is written on a book that isn't discussed in class at all, so you're entirely on your own. Don't take this class if you care about yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this class because I needed another for this semester. Ended up being a nightmare. She doesn't give lecture note outlines, is a harsh grader on papers and exams, and even grades spelling/grammar. You have to do assignments her way, or you get marked down for them. Don't take her if you can help it, it's not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor at all costs! I went to every class, but it was not enough. Only 3 graded assignments given over the semester (2 exams and 1 paper). Exams are all writing (several pages expected of you). Class is treated like an English writing course. Entire class was critiqued about writing skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She ONLY lectures  for an hour and twenty min, does not use slides or notes - You have to write down what she says the entire time. No attendance is taken but if you skip class then you have to read the textbook which is almost as bad as her babbling lectures. There's only three graded things during the semester all of which are essays. it sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Emily is a very well educated professor and had non-stop information through out the entire lecture. Emily does not appeal to the visual learners because she simply talks the entire time. The material is very interesting and it is easy to get lost in her lecture (in a good or bad way). I do not recommend taking a class with her, she is very tough.

I admit that I was surprised and very pleased to see that Professor Tabuteau is still at MSU. I had the pleasure of taking both of her const English history courses back in 1987-88. Her knowledge and style were very impactful on my decision to study law and my love of history. I would highly recommend Professor Tabuteau.

She is awesome. Very passionate, knows what she is talking about and really helps you learn to analyze and think critically. Always willing to help and answer questions. She is critical while grading papers but in a good way that helps you learn. You should definitely take one of her classes.

Emily had a lot of impact on me 30 years ago.  A wonderful professor and teacher.  She lives her history.  An inspriration and I am a professor now.  Tom Eppink, Univ. SC  Take her and see your mind change.
Dr Tabuteau ignited history for me. And more important, she taught me to think.  And write.  And question.  A sterling example of what a professor should be.

She was quite hard. I was a history major and have since graduated with a BA in history with high honors. I aced all my history classes but 3.5-ed hers. She wasn't mean, but definitely a no-nonsense type who talks expertly on the topic and so you might get lost...you can tell she is from Harvard...expects exceptional papers. Super challenging.
Had her class years ago.  She was superb--really taught you how to take apart an argument.  One of the two best professors I had at MSU.

Almost every single lecture was a guest lecture. A lot of the exam questions were based on what guest lecture speakers would specifically say aloud while teaching. This class was frustrating with exams and just seemed disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's awesome. A great person to talk to especially if you want advice on more career and education oriented stuff.

Very sweet & passionate about what she teaches. If I ever had questions outside of class she was very helpful & timely over email. If you show up to class & engage you should do well, the slides dont always have all the info.Use office hours to your advantage (for any prof). I just wish there would've been a clear study guide for exams.
You will do well if you go to class and engage with the content. Dr. Pomeranz is a good professor and clarifies any confusion if you ask. I learned a lot in this class and enjoyed it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Enjoyed this class a lot. I think a lot of people don't understand how important HD is. She was disorganized at times but in general had informative lectures. Lots of readings but I got by without doing most of them. Exams were a little hard to study for but I found that I was pretty prepared just from taking notes and attending

Dr. Pomeranz completely lost the class a month in, maybe 25% came. Lectures are extremely boring and disorganized, you gain absolutely nothing from going. It's supposed to be a writing class, but 2 exams are worth 45% of the grade, in which she gives zero study references. She does not respect your time either and rambles about nonsense. STAY AWAY!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Jackson was a good economics professor and I enjoyed the class. You're allowed to miss 2–3 classes, but otherwise attendance is mandatory, and there are iClicker questions graded for completion. The homework was challenging, but the exams were relatively easy, and you can drop one exam, which helps.

Fine teacher, but her lectures are the worst, and she sometimes does not explain things enough and goes really fast. Not the hardest class ever, but the only class that I actually took away from was one that a TA led.

This class was pretty easy and I even skipped a couple of lectures. Attendence isn't necessary but does factor into the final grade slightly. The exams were relatively easy if you studied beforehand. The homework is very easy. I would recommend this professor and class.
3 exams + final, and one was dropped. Homework was like an hour a week and half is completion and half is accuracy. 10% participation on iclicker which is curved 15%. Would recommend

Prof. Jackson made the class super understandable. There is weekly homework, but your bottom 6 grades get dropped. The exams are super easy, and if you do well on the first 3 you can skip the final since you get to drop an exam. Do not skip class, she does iclicker questions and you get a 15% curve on it which can get you extra credit.

A very likable and overall good teacher. As someone who doesn't know any basic econ, she teaches in a way that helps students to easily understand the topic. Tests are easier than expected. Just review the practice exam and also the Achieve(homework) questions, and you're pretty much set as the questions are basically similar.

Went to a tutor (first time ever) because I couldn't understand a basic econ intro class... what was going on and my tutor couldn't believe the assignments and test questions. Over complicated, poor teaching. WIll not ever take again

Fantastic professor who makes econ extremely understandable. Average workload with midterms that are easy to score highly on with her guidance. Seems to care about student success and therefore makes very organized lecture slides that break down material in a succinct and clear manner. Definitely one of your best bets for an econ professor.

This professor deserves a rating higher than 3.2; her class is tough, but it's a college class, and you can't expect an easy A. If you put in just a little more than the minimum amount of work, you'll be fine. She is a very kind professor who you can tell is passionate about history.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lectures can be boring sometimes and she sometimes talks very fast so it is hard to keep up. You will not pass if you do not show up. She is a great professor and if you like foreign relations you will love this class. I though the papers were actually kinda fun. The quizees are kinda hard, DO THE READINGS. great professor!

When it comes to lectures, the slides give no information and the lectures are reliant on her talking about what is being discussed. She gives multiple readings, some literally being whole books that are 300 pages. When it comes to writing papers, her criteria is horrible and does not explain anything. Just terrible all around to be honest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She graded way too hard when her instructions and rubrics were not at all specific. Way too difficult to figure out what she was asking for. A majority of students did an assignment wrong because she lacked the ability to instruct and she gives until the end of the day to redo it. Horrible all the way around

I would take this professor again in a heartbeat. I actually tried to see if she is teaching any other courses that apply to my major and was very upset that she didn't. A lot of reading, but that is expected. Two short group presentations that are very relaxed and both exams were take-home essays. Attendance was not required as long as you read.

Can't believe she doesn't have 5 stars. She was reading-heavy (expected for a 300 class), and her lectures could have been more entertaining, but she's an amazing professor. Due dates and assignments are incredibly reasonable. Genuinely happy to answer any question. In my top 3 for best educators I've had at MSU. Didn't take attendance either!

Professor Conroy-Krutz was extremely knowledgeable and passionate about her class. There was a lot of reading but that is to be expected from a History class. People on here complaining about her lectures want everything handed to them on a silver platter. If you do the readings and listen/participate during lecture, you will learn a lot.

Disagree with most of the reviews on here--she is great! Lectures are engaging, she knows her stuff, and most of the work in the class gets graded relatively easily as long as it's clear that you read the material and learned something from the lectures. She goes fast because there's a lot to cover, but it's not hard to follow or keep up. Big fan!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: She's an amazing professor! Her power points are a little vague, but all of your grades are from essays that you write, anyway. Lectures are really helpful for writing your essays. You do need to know a fair amount of U.S. history, but this is a 300 level history class, so it's obviously not a blow-off class. I learned so much valuable information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Her power points are very vague. She talks way to fast for me to take notes and there is no slowing her down because she is alway behind her schedule. She gives a final exam as an in class essay exam in which you have only a commonplace book with quotes, for your notes. STAY AWAY unless you are in need of boring lecture.

This teacher seemed like she expected you to know the material prior to you attending the class. Her notes are just an outline and you literally have to take notes based on what she says in class. She goes too fast and it is really frustrating. She also expects you to read like 4-5 books during the course. STAY AWAY!!!

A very hard grader. If some people in class do not prepare she punishes the whole class by not explaining the materials. The amount of reading is unreasonable. PowerPoint’s are useless.  rambles, very philosophical,taking notes is hard. course is not organized. Responds to emails very late. Doesn’t acknowledge student’s progress and participation.

Katz cares a lot about her students and what they take away from her classes. Second time having her and I'd recommend with my dying breaths tbh. You'll enjoy the class a lot more if you're engaged and participate in discussions, and her study guides make it very easy to excel on the exams given out. Very helpful with papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's a good professor; knows exactly what she's talking about. However, if you plan on doing at least 5-10 hours of reading a week, this would be the class for you. The reading blocks were very excessive (4 days before class, having 30 pages to read. And 2 days in between classes, having 60 pages to read).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Very good and entertaining professor; provides multiple ways to succeed and cares deeply about the students and the topics covered.

Multiple writing assignments handwritten in class, but a very lenient drop policy allows you to miss classes a couple of times. Exams are strictly based on study guides provided (not many surprise questions).
Nice professor willing to help
The lectures help significantly, if you go and actively participate in class it is not only enjoyable but also engaging and easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: She is the best prof ever! so sweet and loves what she does and her students. Lectures are very interesting, and assignments are easy. Would take again 1000x over.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Katz is my favorite professor at MSU. She's kind, funny, and genuinely cares that her students have fun doing philosophy. Her grading is super clear in the syllabus. Make sure you're doing the readings and taking notes. If you can do the basics for this class, you'll be fine. Couldn't recommend her more.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Katz was funny and thorough at the same time. Tests were based entirely on the study guides, so if you fill those out it's incentive to do the readings and be prepared for the tests at the same time. Class itself was easy, though it was more philosophy than anticipated. I enjoyed it a lot, despite wanting more of the sci-fi aspect.

Katz was the best professor I have had so far. She is very passionate about philosophy and is very clear. She manages to be very interactive in such a big lecture. The study guide and the exams are close to identical, so make sure that you stay on top of that and ATTEND CLASS. You definitely won't pass if you don't come to lecture and take notes.

There is a lot of reading to endure in this class if you want to do well, but it's interesting. She goes over the readings the next day & explains it all very well, but if you miss a lecture you have to get notes from someone else as she leaves the slides pretty bare. She provides EC & is easy to reach outside of class & provides great feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She was a very kind professor. Her lectures were very clear, and she made philosophy pretty interesting for a stem major. you can tell she is very passionate about Philosophy, and she's very experienced. Exams are completely based on the study guides, so if you don't get an A that's on you. Loved her class, highly recommend for IAH

For HST 201 our final was a 15 page paper. Prof. Elliott is very nice and caring, she gives great feedback on assignments preparing for the paper. She is very easy to get in contact with and responds to emails pretty quickly. She also made it clear that she is always willing to help and care for her students. Very passionate about her job.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Basically half your grade is one paper, but you spent most of the semester just working on it, so it was ok. Elliott is a great speaker, and the class was very entertaining. She would make us work in groups during class sometimes, which was fine but there were some students that made it suck. Clearly very passionate about Russian history.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Elliot was a very understanding proffessor. She did go through lectures pretty quickly but she does post them at the end of units, but just paying attention helps. There are no tests or quizzes, just 3/4 major writing assignments. She is really timely in replies and you can tell she really enjoys teaching this class. Recitations are also fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: So, shes a little rude, and she goes through notes a lot faster than some people are prepared for. But, Her assignments are very easy and clearly detailed. 4 assignments including the final. Compared to MSU's other ISS 210 course this one is MUCH easier. The other having almost weekly tests and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was super easy. Lectures are not mandatory at all due to her slides being posted before the lecture. Recitation is mandatory but overall only 2 papers for the whole course and 1 test and the final exam. Super easy would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 10/10 Professor that I'd recommend to everyone! She's enjoyable and makes her content easy to understand for the class! Her TA, Scott Bullock, is very understanding! As long as you go to lecture, take good notes, go to recitation, and participate you will surely pass with a 4.0!

Professor Elliot lectures every class and then recitation is set up to talk through her lectures and the assigned readings for the week, I found it to be easy because she posts the power points but I would definitely suggest still going to her lectures. There are pop reading quizzes and very few assignments, so try hard and meet the deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Elliott is very knowledgeable and can lecture the full class period. You have to take notes during the presentations as there is nothing written on the slides for you. She does have an accent that can be difficult to listen to for extended time periods. The assignments are reading and essays   and you have to participate in recitations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is a menace. He embarasses students and doesnt put effort into teaching students or making the classroom welcoming. He also does not care about his students especially those who struggle to obtain information or those who are of special needs. If you disagree with him he makes it a huge issue in class
Professor Engram was disrespectful and handled the school shooting awfully. He was often disrespectful to students in class. He has been one of my least favorite professors during my time at MSU.

Dr. Engram was a pretty good professor, The discussion posts are graded are very strictly and he won't tell you your grade until the end of the year. He does offer volunteering for extra credit which was very helpful.

Despite the tragedies Michigan State experienced in February, he remained indifferent: attempting to assign work during the allotted time away from campus, mandating attendance upon return, and violating numerous university policies. Although the nature of this course preaches empathy, his actions fail to embody his teaching.

Dr. Engram weighs discussion posts very heavily and gives you absolutely no idea of your standing in the category until final grades are released and you have no way of changing them. I submitted all but 1 weekly discussion post and somehow received less than a 50% in the category...NOT in line with the syllabus.

At the start of this course, I enjoyed Dr. Engram's. But after a while, I saw that he was extremely difficult, discouraging, and rude. I love the message he speaks on in the class and overall the class material was fine but due to his irrational expectations for students especially after we had all gone through a MASS SHOOTING, it's a no for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Engram is exactly what the kind of professor you fear getting in a course like this. He presents his agenda and is not interested in allowing class discussion on topics causing the class to be silent. He will then take your participation points away. Classic tyrant professor not pleasant to be in his class at all despite interesting topic

This professor is not understanding in the slightest, makes it very difficult to get good grades on things like participation! Take any other ISS class if you don't want to absolutely stress about grades.

I thought a lot of the content he spoke about in class was about his personal opinions not necessarily content from the book. The tests had all content from the book and readings so I was able to study, I just don't agree with his teaching style. I also felt it was hard to give my opinion because if it didn't align with his, it would be a problem.

I wish I could give him a zero. He started screaming at us when we had just returned to campus when we had returned from home because he was reported to the dean after he had tryed to have us take a test 2 days after the shooting. He did not support us students, we tried to express our thoughts and feelings and we were screamed at. Avoid him!!!!!

Though many may have negative things to say after the msu shooting, Dr.Engram is by far one of the professors I respect the most. He is so passionate about what he teaches, encourages students to engage in discussions and wants to help us grow. All of his exams are open note, open book. Eye opening course. Highly recommend.

After the MSU shooting, Dr. Engram displayed a lack of empathy towards the students and did not make any changes to the class syllabus, initially asking the class to take an exam two days after the shooting, also continuing to enforce a strict attendance policy. In class, he also tends to ramble and not provide facts or evidence of the things said

Not a super difficult class, but it is more complicated than it should be because of the D2L layout and instructions for assignments only being located in the syllabus. Pretty much no margin for error on assignments in this class due to tough grading. You really have no idea how you are doing in the class until the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Provided an outdated syllabus so it was SO hard to find information about the class, 5 absences and you were dropped from the course so watch for that. He wasn't as bad as people say about the shooting, he just wasn't lenient. Be prepared to sit through long lectures. 2 papers total in class and the Exams are open note and right off slides.

I love Dr. Engram. Signing up for his class wasn't what I expected it to be, but I was not disappointed. This class challenged me at first. I have never been one to raise my hand and participate in a lecture. Being in this class changed that. I now feel confident to share my input with the class. Every citizen in this country needs to learn this.

After other students and I went through the MSU shooting Prof. Engram showed no empathy at all in any of his emails. At first, he made our exam due 5 days after the shooting and then sent out demanding emails about how we must stay in attendance just the week after the shooting happened. Even before, he had always been very passive-aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: On Feb 13th, there was a mass shooting at MSU and all the students were appalled by this horrific incident. He doesn't care how students feel, refuses to make any amendments to the syllabus, forces them to let student get back to the classroom on the following week, and showed no sympathy at all.
Hours after the school shooting, he told us our exam would still be due in 5 days.

If you like long, lecture-based classes (like myself), this course is great. Enders lectured for at least an hour a day and was accompanied by power point slides, which were later posted online. Don't be mistaken, however- this is a very difficult course. But if you want to learn about the ins and outs of congress, it's worth your time and energy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof was really nice,  but the course layout was not designed for success. Midterm was 30% of the grade, final 35% (cumulative). TopHat was used for lectures/quizzes. While it was nice because I didn't have to go to class, I had to pay for it and I didn't like that. No study guides for the exams and the final covered 472 pages of material. Not easy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Instead of using iClickers like other teachers, Professor Enders had us buy a tophat subscription which was pretty annoying. Attendance was supposed to be counted, but due to errors with the app, it wasn't. There are online quizzes every other period, but with the app, you can take them online without showing up if you sign in at the same time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Epps is genuinely my favorite professor I've ever had. He sees and hears students and pays such close attention to feedback. I am taking his class again next semester and I'm very excited!
Rick has been one of the best professors I've ever had at MSU. No matter where you are in a class, he will meet you at your level, treat you with kindness, and push you to do your best.
The class was really organized. The videos were very well articulated and detailed. All we have to do is pause the video and follow directions. I learned a lot!

I love Professor Rick. He's enthusiastic and makes assignments fun! He will personally get to know you and have your name memorized by the second lecture.
