reviews.comment: This class made no sense. I made it though the whole thing and I couldn't tell you one thing about programming. It was miserable and professor Enbody doesn't do anything to help you. The layout of the course is not effective and the only way to get help is the help room, but you have to sit there for four hours to get help with one line of code.
Not a fun class, if you get caught cheating tho Ive heard he might not submit an ADR if you go talk with him.

This professor is a joke. Clarity is around 0%, the projects take hours and hours every week, most video lectures and assignments are ancient, and we have seen him MAYBE 2 times in the whole semester. The heavy lifting is done 100% by the TAs who are students. The exams cover content that has not been taught. Overall, this professor is a joke.

This dude did nothing during the course, doesn't know how to write a final exam. Seems to not care about his students. The entire course is run by the TA's, so i don't even know why there's a professor let alone two of them.

Class needs to restructured. I am the type of student to ask a ton of questions. I felt at a loss for help due to how many people were in help room/some TAs and professors were condescending. Something needs to change whether it's the way help room is ran, allowing dropped projects, grade boosters for lab participation, or easier/less projects.

This is one of the most brutal classes ive been through. There are no lectures. I went to the helproom a couple times when it opened and sat until it closed without being helped due to the mass of students. Tests are very tricky, TAs are pretty condescending, and instructors just dont care. This course should only be required for CSE students.

Whether taking the online section or not, the class is basically all online. You never meet Dr. Enbody, unless if you schedule an appointment with him. However, all of the ratings on here are too harsh. The class is definitely a lot of work, but if you ask for help and don't keep projects until the last minute the class is definitely not THAT bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The exams are designed to tick you and you will never need to know what program will do without having a compiler in front of you. The projects get challenging towards, but they are still possible. Coding is typically self taught and this class relies on that heavily. Also don't buy the book, all the information you would need from it is online.

If you've ever wondered what it's like to not have a professor then take his class. I'm almost done and have seen him with my own two eyes twice. You may have to work for a few dozen hours on weekly projects so go to the help room but go early. Your life may start to revolve around this class. Be ready for that. Goodluck

Enbody is a sorry excuse for a professor. He barely even teaches and makes us watch his pointless videos. 231 is a glorified online class and Enbody could care less about his students. He finds pleasure in administering the trickiest exams known to man and watching us suffer. Wouldn't be surprised if he drinks our tears instead of water.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Your success is based on how well you are at teaching yourself. Don't bother with the helproom as it's frequently an hour or two hours to get assistance. I wish you luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This dude was one of the worst professors I could have had for an "introductory" class. I only met the guy once. I went to help labs twice a week and I still got a 1.5 overall in the class. Luckily, he's leaving next year. I'm shocked he wasn't fired sooner. Be prepared to be your own professor in this class.

Terrible class, terrible professor. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS unless it is required. Exams are designed to be incredibly tricky. Went into the class expecting a 3.5, I am able to successfully complete all projects (which are HORRIBLE), but with test scores I'll be happy with a 2.0! As long as I pass and never have to take the class again.

Hard class. Can't get around it. Pretty easy to do well,expect to spend a lot of time in the help room. There is a lot of old exams online, study those, he doesn't really change from the old ones. I didn't have any programming experience but I'm doing pretty good. Over all I liked Enbody, I thought this class gave me a solid understanding of coding
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class is too fast paced for an introduction class. The professor expects the student to have intuition on a subject that they have no background in. If you want to pass go to the help room...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This teacher not only wrote an expensive textbook that we're required to buy, he makes it nearly impossible for someone who has never programmed before to keep up. Projects descriptions and instructions are often unclear, and he has a habit of arbitrarily taking points off for things not on rubric. Also hands out ADRs like candy on Holloween.
Projects are too difficult, exams are too tricky.

Most useless professor ever. I am not even done with the class yet and I can say with a clear consciousness that Enbody is the embodiment of "if you can't do it, you teach it". The programming you do is completely useless and will never be used outside the classroom and the structure of the class is ridiculous. Shame that MSU hasn' canned him yet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Definitely a tough class, lots of projects, exercises, pre-labs, and tricky exams. The exams aren't necessarily hard, he just puts lots if tricky programs in to read. Just gotta start things early, and make sure you really understand your stuff. You barely see the professor, so I wouldn't worry about it, he is fair if you make a major mistake.

This dude is hands down the most booty professor at MSU, literally the class is the equivalent to a doctor diagnosing you with cancer and then telling you to figure out the treatment by yourself. The help room blows cause theres 2 TA's helping out 150 + students so its impossible to get anything done. And the exams might give you aids.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: You will never see him other than the short video's for the projects. be prepared to learn everything on your own and wait in the help room for over an hour just to get one questioned answered.
Pretentious refusal to curve incredibly difficult exams. Excessive homework, but manageable.

Definitely not recommended. I am a 4.0 student and got nearly 100% on all projects but almost failed because of how the exams are. To clarify, they are never curved and if you miss one question, it is almost guaranteed to snowball into losing a significant chunk of points.

A heartless sociopath of a professor, whose exam's are notoriously difficult - I managed to get straight hundreds on the programs yet the tests are formatted in such a way that if you miss one question in one section of the test, you'll miss all of the ones relating to that problem. He refuses to curve  grades and is completely unhelpful.  0/10 IGN

Online videos are only so helpful, although he doesn't do all of them. The book is not necessary but can be helpful if you're not catching on. Projects take a lot of time, but there is plenty of time to do them. Try to avoid starting them on the weekends like I did.

Best Teacher I've ever had. Takes time to review everyone's problems. Brings interesting facts to class. Projects and exams relevant to lecture material. Just show up, pay attention, and start projects early, and you'll pass 4.0 easily.
great great great guy! I learned a lot in this class and gave me a new outlook on life. he likes us to write, but he is not a tough grader at all. there are a few quizzes and no exams

He is passionate about what he teaches. Super knowledgeable and respected. His lectures are engaging and he cares about his students. The writing may seem like a lot, but it helps you understand the topics more.

Amazing teacher, he cared about his students and what he teaches. He's tough on his students but he pushes you to become a better student. Going to his classes matters because he provides a lot of material that will be on the quizzes and papers that you write. There is a lot of work that needs to be done for the class but it's all doable.

This class is very similar to how he runs his other classes if you've been in them before. You'll be reading more and using those readings along with his lectures to write papers, he grades a bit harsh on them but it pushes you to become a better student in the long run. The lectures go fast so you really need to pay attention durning class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor M is an inspirational teacher but his lectures are super hard to follow and he doesn't even use the slides most the time so everything is verbal which means if you miss a class or you're a slow writer you're cooked. No study guides for the midterm was given so we all had to guess what it would be on (he gave us a broad number of sections)

I love Dr. M as a person, but his classes are truly the most disorganized I've ever taken. I've taken 3 courses with him, and as much as he offers interesting perspectives, his lectures are impossible to follow, his grading is incredibly subjective with poor criteria, and the quizzes aren't reflective of course material. Don't take if you have ADHD
A very cool guy, down to earth, and passionate

If Dr. Montgomery could teach all of the social science classes at MSU then we would all be soooo set. He is an incredible professor and a super cool guy in general. Keeps you on your toes and expects greatness, both qualities are really great together. As long as you keep up with the reading and pay attention in class, you'll kill it!
1,000,000/10

Dr. Montgomery is one of, if not the best, professor I have ever had at Michigan State. Not only is he incredibly passionate about the work he does, but he fully transfers that passion into the topics he teaches. The only assignments were to read a couple books and write an essay every two weeks. Live, Love, Dr. M. 
TAKE HIS CLASSES IF YOU CAN!!!
Dr. Montgomery has been my favorite professor so far here at MSU (I'm currently a junior). Absolutely loved this class and loved learning from him.

Do not take this class if you can help it. Professor Montgomery is a great guy and he is super passionate about his work, but he is a little too passionate. We wrote SO MANY papers for this class, pretty much the only thing we do, and he is a very harsh grader on these papers. This class gave me multiple mental break downs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do not take this prof if you can avoid it. He grades extremely harshly for papers, has crazy high expectations for students and is extremely unorganized. Do not recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: coolest prof ive ever had. he is very chill & theres a ton to learn from him. he is very knowledgeable & interesting. no exams but two big papers. theres also weekly discussion posts which end up being about 2-3 pages. reading isnt necessary except for discussion posts. he makes class easy & fun to go to. i definitely plan on taking him again.
Wow, a mix of social justice and a spiritual awakening. Really great class, best Ive had at MSU

Loved his class so much. Professor Montgomery is passionate about what he does and is willing to work with you and foster your creativity. Some requirements aren't all that clear, but he will give you the direction you need. Very accessible outside of class and willing to work with you.

Very interesting professor! If you're an anthropology major or minor, you'll be in pretty good shape, but it's hard to combine this Prof with STEM classes. Cares about students, the material. Expects a lot from you, but it's worth it. Difficult class, ultimately it depends on how much time you're willing to put in it. Do things well ahead of time!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: ANP 236 was one of the best classes that I have taken in college. Professor M is one of the most kind and understanding professors I have had in my collegiate experience. He gives great feedback on all assignments, and truly hopes for your success in his class! 11/10

Professor Ericksen is such a nice guy! He seems like a nice dad kind of guy. Class was easy but you have to go to class to take attendance on a google form. study guide lines up with exam. four easy exams in the semester and then a final exam.
Great professor would recommend to any person!
Super easy and nice professor!

This is a great ISS class to take if you are busy or if you just need an ISS. The set up is the same every week with a quiz and discussion post. Open note and open AI. He is a caring professor who wants you to succeed. Extremely easy 4.0 that you can actually learn some great things from. Couldn't recommend this enough as an ISS class.

Dr. Ericksen is a great guy. He encourages (and grades on) participation and is always quick to respond to emails. Quiz heavy but all exams are open note, open AI, open lecture, and had a dad joke/pun extra credit question. My class was "Social Science Perspectives on Happiness" and most lecture materials were short articles or TED talks :)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He was super nice and funny in his lectures. Content was easy to understand. Just a discussion post and quiz each week that were super quick to do. Great for a busy schedule.

He's amazing. If you're looking to take your first ISS and his class is available, this is who you'd want. He was completely online and modules were great. Weekly discussion posts and quizzes were easy and quick. He links many readings and Ted talks but honestly the lecture notes can get you most of the quiz questions pretty quickly.
Such a nice man. For the weekly quizess its open note but a little tricky, so maybe take with friends. Super nice and caring!
Best professor

This professor seems like a nice guy. The weekly work consists of watching a lecture (~30 mins), taking a 10-question quiz where one question is a joke, and doing a discussion which usually isn't too bad of a prompt. This class is on happiness and I found it to be very helpful to improve my outlook on life so I highly suggest it.

Usually returns graded assignments within the week and is very lenient on discussions and quizzes. Easy to get in contact with if you need help or have simple questions. I would 100% take another class with him if given the opportunity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. Would absolutely recommend taking a class with him. Work load is totally manageable and grades very fair.
This was the easiest class I have EVER taken.

had class online asynchronous he is the best professor there is one 10 question quiz every week with 2 questions that are dad jokes so he gives away points easy and then a discussion and reply every week that has to be 5 sentences, he is super funny and interesting lectures are usually around 20 minutes take his class if you can easy 4.0
Such a kind person and a great teacher. His class was fairly easy, too.

I personally loved professor Ericksen. I had this class fully online so I never got to speak with him personally, but he loops in personal stories in his lectures and I feel like I know a lot about him without ever actually meeting him. He's a great guy and his class is easy. He puts little dad jokes into his quizzes for an easy extra point :D

Very fun guy! Super empathetic and is very lienent, but makes sure you will still learn! His lectures actually feel very useful to everyday life and his requirements are clear. All of his assignments feel necessary and are easy as long as you understand the curriculum.
Good guy, easy class, maybe an hour of work each week, great choice for the is requirement

This was the easiest and most enjoyable class i've taken. Lectures covered everything on the test so as long as you paid attention to them and wrote notes you'll do great. I took this accelerated in the summer and had no stress from the class at all! I highly recommend this professor!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was very enjoyable. Every week we had lectures, two discussion posts, and a quiz. We had a few writing assignments throughout, but those were two paragraphs maximum. The professor was understanding when it came to a problem or concern any student had. I liked that he genuinely cared about teaching us skills for the future.

Such a sweet and genuine man! I loved how he made personal references in his recorded lectures because I felt like I got to know him really well without actually meeting him. The quizzes are pulled straight from the slideshows from his lectures. Don't bother watching any TedTalks or reading anything he assigns. Incredibly easy.

I really enjoyed this class! the lectures were interesting and I liked how the layout was straight forward as well. I learned a lot. I kinda wish that this class was synchronous because I enjoy lectures more in real time. Professor Ericksen was a really chill professor and as long as you take notes and listen to the lectures you will do well.

This was an insanely easy class. The exams were online and youre allowed to use the posted lectures. Professor Ericksen does require attendance, which was the only thing I didnt like about this class, because his lectures can become very boring. Overall, I learned a lot of useful information from this class and its an easy 4.0.

Prof. Ericksen is truly a guy that wants you to understand the material and is very patient to students who cannot afford the resources to pass at that very moment; something I am truly grateful for as I was one of those students. He also is very good at preparing you for the tests. Overall an easy A but his lectures can get kinda stale at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Wonderful Professor. Interesting lectures. Not very much work outside of exams and papers. Cares about students and material being taught. Highly recommend this professor and course! Gives great feedback on assignments too!

Easy 4.0 just have to do the assignments. Really good professors actually reads your assignments and gives feedback even though he has probably thousands of students. Quizzes and exams are exactly what are on the lectures and can use the lectures he posts while taking them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super funny and nice. Easy class

Loved this class, would take again. He's just starting out with it but he does a really good job of getting the message across, the homework is easy, the quizzes are open note, all you have to do is show up to pass basically (he takes attendance with top hat). He's just an overall great teacher and nice guy.

Professor Erickson is very passionate about the topics he teaches. It was clear he wants students to actually apply the concepts to their lives. All information needed is posted on his slides which are uploaded. Exams are online and are open book/note. Reflections are guaranteed 100% as long as you try. Buying the book is not necessary

This was his first time teaching this course. Throughout the semester we had 4 exams and 4 reflection papers. The exams were 20 questions and online given a 2hour span to complete. Questions pulled from lectures. Exam and reflection not hard!! Lectures posted online. Easy 4.0. Would definitely recommend taking this class with Professor Ericksen.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I disagreed with professor Lambert a lot in class on his philosophy and the way that he presented his opinions very strongly and rather weakly presented the oppostion (which I tended to be in). However, he is still a good teacher and someone that, if you have conversations with him, can be great to know and talk with.

reviews.comment: Super fun and a really easy grader. As long as you attend class and do the assignments you'll get a 4.0
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Lambert is one of the best professor's at MSU. He genuinely cares about the topics he teaches, and wants to see every student do their absolute best. He encouraged healthy class disucssions and the format of his exams were unique and easy to take/ do well on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This professor was amazing, throughout the whole semester. Very kind to me throughout the whole semester including my unexpected extenuating circumstances. His classes were interesting and informative and you could tell he cared about what he was talking about. Highly recommend this class!

I have his class fully online, grading criteria is very random, not put into D2L so he expects you to go into excel and plug all of your grades in from the comments on assignments. Never clear why he doesn't just use d2l. It reads all of your grades as 0s. Overall class is not very entertaining and a lot of random inconsistencies.
I absolutely ADORED this professor. Such a validating class and he teaches very well! If you want to have good intellectual conversation take this class!

Dr. Lambert was fine, he wasn't anything special though. He isn't super clear about grading criteria so you kinda just have to learn as you go. His lectures are boring and the readings that you base your papers on aren't super interesting either. It's not a super hard class, but it's also nothing I necessarily recommend.

Lectures were so long and boring. I felt that a lot of what he said in lectures was very opinionated and he did not do a good job of engaging the students as he was lecturing. He is a very passionate teacher, he could (and does) talk about the content for hours on end. But the class was not for me, wish I would have taken a different IAH course.

I learned so much in this class and his lectures were amazing. Even though it was a 2 hour class I wasnt bored. I know he got a lot of complaints but honestly if you do your work and pay attention youll be fine. I got a 4.0 without many difficulties. I would definitely take another class with him.

Professor Lambert is one of the most rude professors I have ever had. Lambert will absolutely hate you if he sees you even peak at your phone, get up during class, or not show up to class. Has a final choice in your grade, so even if you get a high 3 or a 4 he will not give it to you if he "did not participate" or if he didnt think you deserved it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you care about the class he will care about you. To improve your grade go to OFFICE HOURS and go to class! He gives extra quizzes to make up your grade and they are so easy. I DO recommend speaking in class BUT it is most effective when you only talk when you really have something productive to say. There are a lot of big talkers in PHL.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Go to class and ENGAGE. Professor Lambert is very informational and very passionate about what he teaches. Such fruitful lectures and endless links that are relevant outside of class. A great class paired with a great speaker! There is a lot of reading, but the texts/articles have much to teach.

Lambert was an interesting guy. We went on a lot of tangents that didn't always relate to the material. I did well in his class, but I have to say it wasn't what I expected. It felt like he was constantly trying to push his political bias on us. I tried to be open-minded, really. I still love philosophy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes I have taken. Ridiculously hard for a 100 level class and I'm a junior. His grading is ridiculously hard and purely subjective. If he disagrees with your point, you do not do well. He tells kid he's going to stop taking attendance and many kids then don't show up, but he continues to take attendance.
You must attend class to understand the material. Also 15% of your grade is based off in class quizzes. As per most MSU IAH classes there is a heavy load of reading material to cover.

Prof Lambert is a Philosophy prof through and through.  He is very interesting to listen to and has interesting views on things.  His class is very open minded and is very comfortable.  He also puts in the extra effort to make sure everyone understands what he is going for.

He cares a lot about what he teaches and is very encouraging when it comes to trying to start a discussion. Overall the class is pretty interesting if you go into it with an open mind and make sure you don't skip and bring the readings with you because he does give out pop quizzes. They're easy and help your grade a lot.

Bert Lambert is incredibly dull. He speaks inaudibly and show a complete lack of respect for most people. I am so sorry I did not drop this class when I could have gotten the full refund. He grades 15% of your grade on pop quizzes in lecture. How is that indicative of how you understand the material?

This professor is very "old school". He doesn't really use technology unless it's for D2L or Youtube. I kid you not the first day we came into class, he said "put away all technology for these two hours" and he did take up the whole time just talking. Now it's doable but other than that it's not really worth it for me personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Good teacher, absolutely underrated. He's a nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was super excited for this class but it turned out to be a let down. The class is way too hard for the amount of credits you receive. A lot is expected of you and the directions are not clear of what is exactly expected. He has good intentions however the class is lacking in purpose and motivation.
Did not enjoy. Very unorganized.

His grading system and philosophy on education are terrible. His course contains interesting material and concepts but he himself is a terrible teacher and more just sits there waiting for students to create the course for him. His class time is boring which is truly a feat considering the material he has at his disposal. Not worth your time. He does not respect the fact that students are enrolled in other courses.

The ratings here come from a place that doesn't do Dr. Tibebe justice. One of the most passionate, eccentric professors I have ever had the pleasure to study under. The lectures are meandering, the notes confusing, but everything he cites or mentions is easily verifiable of your own resources. I have never seen his passion for history matched.

Dr. Tibebe Eshete is one of the most educated and passionate people I have ever had the privilege of learning from. He has such a host of real world experience that makes him an extremely engaging and unique professor to learn from. While he is semi-disorganized and does have an accent, these are truly dealbreakers. A great teacher with minor flaws

He's very unorganized, horrible with communication, and has no D2L page. If you become ill or an emergency pops up, you'll most likely be on your own because he doesn't communicate. The work criteria are based on reading (on your own). He'll show you bullet-pointed notes but that doesn't have a lot of information. His accent is very strong too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was a thoughtful/interesting professor. His accent is perfectly understandable, his class isn't the most organized, but he truly tries to bring in real-world information. I appreciated his lectures and still think about them 2 years later. Coursepack was intriguing, but I didn't use it much. FYI, he makes up terms that he likes to see on exams.

I liked Dr. Tibebe as a person and he truly shows his passion through is teaching. With this being said, he can be very unorganized, making his class hard to follow. The group papers and the final exam were the main grading aspects for the semester which made it difficult to determine class standing overall.

Tibebe has real world experience in what he is teaching, and he is uniquely qualified; however, his class was very hard to sit though. The notes were hard to follow and not focused. His accent is hard to understand but understandable and the final exam/quizzes were very difficult. I would not take his class unless you really really enjoy history.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tibebe is a very nice man, and you can tell he cares a lot about teaching and is passionate about what he is trying to teach. However, this was the worst class I have ever taken. He is extremely unorganized, directions and lectures are unclear always, and his accent doesn't help for clarification either. There is a ton of information for just 1 sem

I can agree with the rest of these reviews that his lectures are not that clear, but he's an easy grader so it didn't really matter. This class really was not difficult and i attended probably 70% of the lectures. My only real complaint is that the 'group essays' were annoying and pretty useless, but they were easy lol.

He seriously is such an awesome guy who cares about his students a lot, but it is very difficult to do well, because he can be hard to understand. The study guide did not help for the exams, and that was huge for me and my grade.
He is very hard to understand, and its never clear what you are supposed to be learning.

Disorganized. I never know what's important and what's not important to know. Important things in notes are highlighted, but some important things are not highlighted. Have to draw your own conclusions with the innumerable facts given.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Super nice guy, but his lectures are super confusing and make no sense. I feel bad because he is very sweet but his class is so hard to focus in because his lectures are about random parts of history

Seems like a very nice guy, but the class was extremely disorganized. It was about a wide range of topics that did not relate to one another. Different parts of the world from different time periods. Notes in class made absolutely no sense. Took attendance occasionally. Overall would not recommend.
A goofy and smart dude who cares about his students and the material. Super understanding and ready to connect with students who reach out.
I really enjoyed coming to class because professor Estrada really seemed to care. He was really funny and down-to-Earth.

Professor Estrada is a gem. JMC is an extremely difficult department at Michigan State, all the classes are hard, the grading is hard, and is really disheartening. Having Professor Estrada for your introductory sequence is more than a godsend, it makes 201 one of those classes you're looking forward to, and miss when you leave.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Estrada is a great, engaging professor, but very disorganized. The D2L page was difficult to navigate and class felt disorganized, but Prof. Estrada is very understanding and will answer any questions you have. Be prepared to talk in this class. It will help you a lot.
I really liked Prof Estrada, he's very understanding and he allows you to turn things in late. You don't actually need to buy the books, I never used them. Easy A for sure!

I thought she was pretty clear and she's really interesting in her discussion of the pieces.  I wish she would label them though, sometimes it's really hard to guess how to spell 15th century Italian surnames.  Overall, I think it was pretty easy and the tests were straight forward.  Unfortunately, my TA is a stickler, could have had a higher GPA.
outstanding class & even better prof...definitely take this class for one of your iah credits! estelle is awesome & very willing to help--tests are extremely straight forward, yet graded by the TA
awesome prof...very helpful & easy to talk to.  would definitely recommend any of her courses, IAH or HA.
Both Lingos are outstanding. They're two of the three best profs I've ever had, and the two best at MSU. By far.
Best prof I have had at State. Keeps class interesting, encourages opinions, tests are incredibly straight forward...Take any of her courses!!
Very well taught, fun.
No Comments
Awesome.  Estelle is amazing and super helpful.  Her and her husband are great professors.

I had Professor Frantz course last year and it was a overall easy class to take. She does a good job of making the lecture videos funny and engaging, overall a good class to take if you like political science or want a flexible online elective/class.
AMAZING. Loved her lectures so much, I felt like I actually learned something. She knows what shes talking about and all you have to do is show up and skim the homework and you will pass.
she clearly knows what she is talking about nice class and not really difficult. just study lectures before test and youre good. class is intresting

Frantz's class is extremely easy, don't need to read outside material as the lecture content is enough to coast by with an A. However, she is anti-tech in class, she will recommend using physical textbooks, notebooks instead of laptops, she will also call you out in class if you are on your phone, occasionally, kick people out for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took her online course and I loved it! She splits up her lectures into separate short parts (I don't know why but I like this way more than one giant long lecture) her lectures are straight to the point, and she explain things very well. I would love to take an in person class with her in the future!

Dr. Frantz is amazing and has an open personality; she is always smiling, laughing, or giggling during class, which creates a fun environment. She encourages discussion in class, which makes the class more engaging and fun. Attendance is tracked with clicker questions (which you are graded on), and those questions are on the quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: - Took it as a summer class and was super straightforward on what we had to do. Easy 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Class was super straightforward, and interesting and engaging lectures despite being an online class. All the supplemental articles and videos were always super interesting. If you pay attention and are atleast somewhat interested, this class will be super easy for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The online version was great! She's always so upbeat and explains things very clearly in the recorded lectures (I basically listened to them all on the treadmill in the middle of winter), and your final grade is mostly based on quiz grades, which are the average of your two attempts. Would absolutely recommend!

I took the online honors section of this class and found great success. Prof. Franz has amazing lectures, and she operates each unit on a 2-week basis, giving you the flexibility to create your schedule. The Honors section was an analysis of one research paper every two weeks, and the graders provided great feedback to help with success.
I really enjoyed this class. Attendance was mandatory because of iClickers, and tests are majority of your final grade. But other than that it was easy and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really like this professor she is funny and makes class enjoyable and not something to dread. You do need to come to classes because it is weighted more than the quizzes.

Very sweet professor. She knows what shes teaching and has a passion for it. Lectures are engaging. Grades are simple, 4 exams -30 mcqs. Does use physical iclicker, but clicker questions are not graded on accuracy. The quizzes are the clicker questions. Overall easy and interesting, just show up to lecture, gives us a 5 minute break every class

She is a nice professor overall but her class is extremely loaded with facts and things and can be all over the place with things. Make sure to read the textbook or you will not do good and it's a lot of reading. She is also very strict with phones or anything distracting in class and you have to have a physical clicker in class polls.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: AMAZING professor. Long lectures that did not bore me out, and made it very clear she knows what she is talking about. Extremely accessible and helpful outside class, exams you did great on if you showed up to class and participation based on IClicker questions. Weekly readings but you will do perfectly if you don't read. All lectures on D2L
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Units are split up into 2 weeks and she allows you to start whenever you want

Overall a well-rounded class with lots of good content. While lectures are uploaded to D2L I would recommend attending class for the discussions the professor has on important course materials in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The video lectures were interesting and seemed to cover the content on the quizzes pretty well (I didn't read the textbook at all after the first week and got 100% on almost all of them, but nothing below like 85% otherwise). The one thing I found annoying was how the weekly short written assignments were graded (seemed nit-picky and inconsistent).

Such a great class! Professor Frantz is an expert in teaching politics and it shows through in her lectures. She is  very funny and never gets too off topic. As long as you take notes in lecture and write down the clicker questions you have a guaranteed A in this class.

Attendance is very important but it is almost impossible to get lower grade then a 3.0 in this class. She allows for 4 absences and drops 1 quiz and there are extra credit opportunities. Show up, do the work, study and you will do great. Only negative is that you need a physical iClicker.

Prof Frantz is the best so far. You really need to attend her lectures because the iclicker questions will be on the final exam. She drops one quiz grade, your participation in four lectures, and one section (recitation) participatio grade. Plus, she's easy to talk to outside of class and makes lectures fun. Highly recommend!

I studied for the 2 big analysis exams by going over my lecture notes since they were about broad course concepts. The textbook readings are more useful in the weekly section quizzes, but most of the content was pretty intuitive. Definitely go to the lectures or watch the recordings because the review clicker questions are the final exam questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall this class was fairly enjoyable manageable. The content is pretty interesting and Prof Frantz is a great lecturer. Lots of reading but not always essential for learning class material. Analysis exams can be kind of tricky but content mainly covers general themes from class. Weekly recitation quizzes are pretty easy and allow extra credit.

This class isn't a cake walk by any means but just go to the lectures and recitations and pay attention and you'll be fine. The analysis exams were a little difficult so make sure to review your notes before them. Overall, Professor Frantz is a great professor who makes lectures pretty interesting and knows what she's doing.

Awesome Professor. Readings are important but not required. There are quizzes in section weekly but are multiple choice and you can score 110% if you pay attention in class. Analysis exams are largely about general themes and terms so I recommend taking notes on terms more than specific examples

Dr Frantz is great! Fun to talk with after class. Tests are easy. 8 newspaper assignments to write (drops lowest score) aren't bad, just tedious. I got 3 100s and never anything lower than a 94 on my papers by following the guidelines closely and relating articles to the book instead of lectures. Rent a free iClicker from ASMSU for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Frantz was a pretty laid-back professor in class, you do need a physical i-clicker for this course so be ready to rent one from ASMSU. The newspaper assignments are a little tough and they take points for dumb things, but I averaged like an 80% on those. Tests are super easy!

If you show up for class its super easy to get a good grade, only tricky part is newspaper assignments which are graded by TA's kind of inconsistently. Exams are based off clicker questions asked in class so they are super easy to prepare for, as long as you go to class and answer clicker questions, you will get a good grade. She is also super nice
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not the worst and not the best. The newspaper assignments are really where she gets you. She grades tough on them and takes points for silly things. Got an 80-90 on every single assignment. Luckily there are only eight and maybe 3-5 quizzes per module. All of her lectures have captions so search them instead of listening when you take the quizzes.

Papers were for the most part easy, she preferred you write about the book rather than the actual lecture. I didnt buy the book opted to use the old edition that I found free. The way the course was set up you only had to pay attention to the parts of the module that you had to write about. You'll be deducted points for little things on essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were good but they are very tough graders. The class was easy but the papers were not, you would get marked down for the dumbest things. If you are not a strong writer do not take this.
This class was nice because there are no exams but there were 8 papers which were graded fairly critically. The lectures were interesting and quizzes were not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class is AWFUL. The quizzes were extremely hard for an introduction class. I was doing a 300 level class which was way easier than this class in which I got a 4.0 with a 99.6 percentage. She graded the newspaper assignments badly and didn't care if you made improvements.

The material in this class was quite easy. However, the newspaper assignments are tricky to master. On the paper that I felt I did the worst on, I got a 93%, and on the paper that I thought would for sure get me 100%, I got a 90%. The TAs are not consistent with their grading. My grades from all the NAs ranged from 90%-100%.

shes a great prof & ive had her before. love the way she makes class interesting & funny. super easy going & light hearted. wonderful person & genuinely loves teaching. this class did require three papers & eighteen identification terms a month & she cherry picks one essay and six terms to grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took PLS 200 during the pandemic and it was the most manageable class I had. The quizzes are insanely easy and you get 2 tries with the same questions. The content is pretty self-explanatory. There are 8 papers that you have to write and they are just hit or miss. I turned in all of my papers with the exact same format and got grades 75-100 .

The quizzes in this class were extremely easy, but the newspaper assignments are where she gets you. I'd literally go to the writing center and have a meeting with a former student of hers and still end up with low newspaper grades. Whatever you do, it never seems to be good enough. Happy to be out of this class.

Prof Frantz made PLS200 a really interesting class and was more focused on her students learning material than throwing challenging assignments at you. No tests, lots of quizzes (open note) and 8 papers due for the whole semester. Easy class, just make sure youre specific in your writing because she can be a bit picky about some things.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Tests are literally clicker questions from in class. Lowest I got was a 96 on an exam because they are the exact same questions. As long as you go to class and get the answers to the questions (she doesn't post the answers, only the question on the slides), you will pass exams. There is a weekly writing assignment, but it is super easy
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: easy class, exams are based off iclicker questions! theres a few easy papers, a quiz here & there but over all super easy. loved this course & the prof- frantz is an amazing prof who makes class enjoyable. she comes in with a great energy & her humor makes class 100x better. i highly recommend this prof & this class. will take her class again.

Put in minimal effort and you will pass. Weekly assignments and 4 exams composed of true or false questions. She is an interesting woman who is obviously passionate about her field. If you do more than the bare minimum, you'll learn a lot. Loved this class.
Prof. Frantz is awesome! She does iClicker questions for attendance points but allows you to miss up to five lectures, and the tests are made from the iClicker questions.

I love this professor! She makes the topics interesting, gives you a five-minute break in the middle if the class is too long, and knows what she's talking about. Take her class if you get the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I think that Frantz is an awesome prof it's just that this class is not easy and I dedicated a lot of time to this class and still got a 3.5. The grading scale is super confusing and grades don't get entered into D2L, and the tests are essays and she grades them tough. BUT if you are willing to work hard and learn alot, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class isnt hard, never even opened the book and apparently neither did she cause she never knew what was in it when asked (ps she wrote part of it). Overall just disappointed. If you asked a question related to the days topic 95% chance she didnt have an answer. Expects lots of details on exams. Map quizzes are just irrelevant busy work
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I found this class easy, as she literally gives you what's on the exam. She posts slides, but participation counts. Go to class. She lectures well and is helpful. Do the readings and put effort into the homework because it was 40% of the grade for my class and will catch up to you if you slack. If you put in a little effort, you'll do fine.

Dr T is such an amazing professor! I hate geography but he makes it enjoyable and is super passionate about what he does. He is also super caring if you are struggling or have any issues whatsoever. He is a great professor and I highly encourage taking a course from him if you get the chance. He's also energetic and has dad jokes.

Overall an okay online class. I found the quizzes to be pretty tricky, and projects easy. But I know that some other students felt the opposite. It's a lot of reading and he's very detail oriented. He offered 1 extra credit and a few extensions. If you apply yourself 3.5/4 is definitely attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: (FOR GEO 411 -- It wouldn't let me type it). I loved this class. It was very dynamic - field trips, group projects, presentations, etc and they are all fun and casual, nothing graded too extreme. If you ever are struggling or have late assignments Dr T will definitely work with you. He is such a great professor and keeps the energy light and fun.

For an ISS class that doesn't help anyone in their respective major, he wants to shove it down your throat. It's great to see that he's very passionate about his field, but not everyone shares the same interests in coastal processes. There were so many discussion posts and at the beginning of the semester, iClicker was mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. T was incredible! Very willing to work with students around any circumstances that get in the way of attendance or assignments. He also is clearly insanely passionate about all the courses he teaches which makes them even more interesting.

One of the most understanding professors I've had at MSU. He has worked really hard to accommodate students needs and this class is pretty interesting. Dr. T is very passionate about his field. Show up to class take notes and you will be fine. The exams are fairly easy.

This class is a lot of work. Half the questions on the weekly quizzes are short answer that have 3 separate questions you need to ask within one, and each quiz is worth 30 pts. The discussion posts are usually lengthy and the quizzes take much longer than they should. A lot of unnecessary work for a university requirement class.

Lectures progressively become more full of pictures instead of the content you need to remember. Rambles and expects you to remember everything. Requires over a 95 to 4.0. Takes ridiculously long to grade exams.

Dr. Theuerkauf is an amazing professor! There were weekly quizzes that are easy as long as you pay attention during lecture. Tests are also very easy as long as you pay attention. He allowed you to take the class asynchronously online, synchronously online, and in person. Dr. T is truly passionate about what he teaches too! Highly recommend!

Dr. T is a great professor. I took ISS 310 with him during Fall 2021 and he was a very flexible professor. He offered in person, online synchronous, and asynchronous options. There was a quick discussion post after every lecture; you would work in a group for in person and synchronous or respond to other posts if you were doing synchronous.
I did not like geo330 i found it frustrating.

I had Professor Theuerkauf for GEO 330. It was fully asychnchronus so you could complete assignments at your own pace during the week as long as they were turned in by the due date. The bulk of your grade revolves around a Road Trip Story Map project. Professor T is super easy to get a hold of, and gave thorough feedback on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor assigns nearly 3 tests a week, plus 20-30 pages of mandatory d2l reading. This class is supposed to be an elective but is graded harder than any 400-level class I've ever taken. Would never recommend it to someone trying to get GPA points.

His grading is extremely subjective to what he specifically wants to see. I was accused of using AI when I did not, in fact, use it. I am an upstanding student in stem and this was the most demanding class I took all semester. I would not recommend this professor. He expects you to memorize way to much content and overall isnt good at teaching.

Dr. T is great. His lectures can be heavy with info, I recommend downloading them beforehand so you can look at them as he goes along. There are random attendance checks, 10 quizzes, 5 group discussions, and 4 exams. Exams do have quite a few short answer questions that often need specific examples from class for full credit. It's not too hard.

Doctor T as he will insist you call him is a great professor, If he is an option for you to take in one of your ISS classes, definitely do it. He grades things fairly and is often lenient on many things.

Cannot stress this enough take Dr. T!! He's great and really passionate about what he teaches. He does ten random attendance checks throughout the semester worth 20 points each so make sure you show up, he does offer two attendance drops for the semester. All of the exams and quizzes are online and very easy if you take time to learn the material.
Awesome and caring professor. He is truly passionate about his course. You will love GEO206 or any course you take with him! CHEERS!

Dr T is an amazing professor. He lectures very quickly, but posts the slides ahead of time so they are available for downloading. Showing up to class is a must, attendance is worth points, and passing would be much harder if you skipped. He genuinely cares about his students, introduce yourself to him! He understands if life happens and will help!

Dr. Theuerkauf is an amazing professor! He truly is passionate and very knowledgeable about what he is teaching. There’s discussion posts, quizzes, and tests, but they’re super easy if you watch the lectures. The class material was super interesting too! Would highly recommend for an easy 4 credit class.

Dr. T was one of the best professors I have ever had. He is a really caring and overall a chill guy. All the discussion posts were easy and the exams and quizzes are just like the lectures. This class was pretty fascinating and he showed us some cool documentaries too.
easy a as long as you do the work. lectures were in person but recorded so you didn't have to go. a lot of discussion posts but complete them and you're good. easy iss class

This is a great class to take for your upper ISS credit. The information was pretty interesting and professor T made the class enjoyable. Exams were straightforward as long as you took good notes from the lectures!

Professor Theuerkauf is the best professor I have had these past two years. He listened to what worked for us and what didn't and made adjustments to make the class smoother and to ensure we learned the information. He made class fun and the topics interesting.
Amazing prof who actually listens to feedback and then implements it in the course. Good amount of extra credit and work is easy to complete. Take a class with him if you get a chance!

Class was always fun! Lectures were very informative and easy to understand. I only had to use the textbook to get more in depth info on a given topic, but you can pass the class without the textbook.

I don't think anyone wants to take ISS classes so signing up for his was just because it fit my schedule. That said, I had more interest in his class on coastal geography than I anticipated. He actually says some really interesting things and while it's definitely not my cup of tea, I really enjoyed having his class. I would take another with him.

Lectures were long, always tophat questions to test understanding and for attendance. Only graded on exams and 5 homework assignments, and attendance, but plenty of extra credit opportunities at the end of the semester to boost grade. Nice guy, talks fast sometimes I think because he gets excited about certain topics and tries to get all the info

Dr. Theuerkauf was one of the best professors I've ever had. Genuinely cares about his students and their success in his class. Was extremely understanding in the times of zoom university and was pretty lenient. You take notes during 99% of the class but it's definitely manageable. Homework is spread out And manageable as well. Exams are easy.

Professor Theuerkauf is the best professor I have ever had. Not only is he hilarious, but he really cares about his students. His top concerns are that his students actually understand the information, and that they enjoy learning it. If you have the chance, DEFINITELY take a class with him.

I couldn't believe how stressful this course was. Each week you're required to write 400 word discussions and 200 word responses about the most boring and confusing topics. Don't meet word count? Zero points. There's 30-60 page readings every week along with nearly 3 hours of lecture videos to watch. On top of that, 3,000 word paper as your final.

Several extremely long lecture videos, readings, documentaries, discussion posts, and an exam every week. This is a semester worth of content shoved into 7 weeks. Incredibly time consuming already, and there's also a 3000 word research paper due at the end of the semester. Not accommodating at all and refused to turn on transcripts for lectures.

This class did nothing but drain me. He gives lengthy lecture videos and readings every week along w/ discussion posts and exams with no logical way to study them. claims the exams are open note but puts them in lockdown. Extremely rude responses when you email him with a simple question. 3000 word research paper for final. Don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: really bad prof., grades based on arbitrary guidelines instead of content of what you write and if you dont meet them exactly you get a zero. doesnt have a syllabus document its all posted in the table of contents. he has his name attached to every class in the department like its his own vanity project. interesting class, but prof ruins it!

Cool dude, terrible professor. Gives unclear instructions for assignments and then totally roasts you in his feedback. Refuses to create grading rubrics for 400 level classes, so he does not grade in a fair, standardized way. Does not answer emails in timely manner. Absolutely would NOT recommend.

Difficult class, but an exceptionally smart professor who knew what he was talking about and was extremely funny. LOTS of writing, but the final project is graded liberally and is good for a portfolio. The midterm is way harder than he says it is, but all the information is on the lecture slides for it. Exceptional course, but it wasn't easy.

Ethan is very laid back, and knew a lot about our topic. Lectures were long but interesting, and the homework was actually fun and made sense for our class. Beware: the test questions were super specific details from the lecture, so if you think it will be on broad topics, you're wrong!

THE WORST COMMUNICATION EVER. Required to follow him on twitter, which was fruitless. Changed the classroom without telling me because I signed up later than December for the class. Never answered questions directly. Sent me the wrong course website and then denied it. Is a talk-yelling, pretentious human being. DONE.
Easy class, and he helped outside of class. If he marked answers incorrect on tests, he changed it as soon as you asked him.
His online class is easy and interesting and the most well structured online class I have ever taken!

I have a strong feeling he does not care for or enjoy this class.  Also, he takes FOREVER to grade anything, and you have to write a 3,500 word paper due finals week that you get no rubric, no nothing for.  He doesn't give any guidance and spends most of the day on Twitter.
great class; pretty easy. Ethan is a really cool guy who knows what he is talking about. TC241 is really fun as well.
No Comments

Dr.Lee has this class laid out so well and the lectures lay out how to do the labs. There is a lab each week, along with two projects, and two exams. There is a discussion board for all students to post questions which I found extremely helpful. Your skills in ArtiosCAD and SolidWorks will be greatly enhance. GREAT PROFESSOR!
Dr Lee is a great professor, extremely helpful and truly cares about students. Responds quickly to emails and his course layout is very well done.

Dr. Euihark Lee is an amazing professor and one of the best in the school of packaging! His online lectures have taught me so much. He responds to emails promptly and will always help you understand the material. I highly recommend taking his elective classes too

She was very nice, sometimes unorganized. She just wants to help and will give as much time as needed. She is persuaded easily too if the entire class feels like an assignment is too hard or too confusing. She understands that this class is not the whole world and will work round busy schedules.

Eunjung is a very sweet lady. She may not be the clearest at times, but she was always putting so much effort into the class. She appreciated all the work we did for the class. She genuinely cares about her students and their success. If you want a teacher who cares about you and knows your name, pick Eunjung. Sweet sweet lady.

Her directions were never clear, she was constantly changing her mind, she was sometimes difficult to understand, and she collects a ton of things and never will give back a grade. You will have no idea what your standing is in the class. Avoid at all costs.

Eunjung is very friendly and genuinely cares for her students, but she is very unclear. It was often hard to know when assignments were due or what the guidelines for them were. Everyone got the same grades and the same comments. The assignments were often pointless, and we were reflecting on reflections. There were so many writing assignments.

Eunjung is a very nice woman who cares a lot about her students, but she is not an effective teacher. Her classroom was often very confusing, stressful, and full of unnecessary papers and assignments. I did not enjoy my TE 250 experience very much, which is a shame b/c I have wanted to teach since kindergarten. VERY nice, but NOT a good teacher.

Very boring class. On our longer papers, everybody in the class got the same grade. Attendance was required and I really wish it hadn't been because it was a waste of my time. Jealous of students who had different profs.

SO SWEET. I missed a few assignments and emailed, and she always responded quickly and helped me figure it out. Very easy grader and really does not expect much from us given it was an asynchronous class. Sweetest woman ever. 10/10 recommend.

Easily the nicest prof. I've ever had. So so sweet and understanding as well as very intelligent and respectable. Would definitely take again, she is seriously amazing. The assignments have meaning and she is very kind with grading and extensions if needed. Take her if you can :) such a lovely lady!!

Easily the nicest professor I've ever had. Did an amazing job at giving timely feedback on assignments as well as structuring class to be engaging and worthwhile. I did the honors option for the course and she was very understanding and helpful through that entire process as well. Take this professor if you can!

Nicest women ever, I don't think she has a mean bone in her body. I also don't think she's capable of giving a bad grade. Super understanding, her only flaw is that she does lots of lectures. Very easy class, lots of group work.

Professor Kim was really nice, helpful, and great at teaching. Since my class was small, she adjusted to our individual levels and really pushed us based on our skills which helped so much. As a freshman, this class was minimal stress and very fun but attendance and participation is so important. Anyone should be happy to have her as a professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Eun Hee is a super approachable and understanding prof and you can tell she cares a lot about her students. As with any language class (esp intro levels), participation is key and as long as you show up, you should do generally well in the class. We used the textbook a lot in class but the workbook was mainly for self-check homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: yikes. would not take this class again. he is very unclear about what he wants, and you had to probe him for exactly what he wanted to get a good grade. often rambles and goes off on tangents, and never seemed satisfied to the answers of the questions he'd ask. it's possible to get a 4.0, but you have to try to pry exactly what he wants out of him.

very little organization. prof is not engaging and puts no effort into making content interesting. so boring, no rubrics for ANYTHING, just gives you a zero and THEN tells you the correct way to complete the assignment. very vague. presentations required. would NOT recommend.
entire grade relies on a group project with zero provided rubrics or clear expectations. do not take this class.

It feels like he talks at us and wants us to teach the class for him. He gives you a week notice if you have a presentation and is very unclear of what he wants you to address. Half of the class is spent Googling what he wants you to know or you sit there awkwardly not knowing what he wants you to do. Considering dropping the minor bc of this

Awful experience with irrelevant and out of date content, an insufferably long class period, and relied solely on students to lecture each week with only a weeks notice if it was your turn. If you missed class you had an awkward hour long zoom with the professor while he read other students slides. This experience led me to dropping the minor.

Class was most based on group work and assignments due outside of class. Participation and attendance matter a lot. Some assignments weren't very clear rubric wise. Sometimes it felt like he wanted something very specific but didn't have a clear rubric.

I went into this class just exploring my major options. Dave is one of the most caring professors out there and was the reason I managed to go to such an early class. His lectures were enjoyable and straightforward. I totally recommend!

This class is very lecture heavy. If you don't attend, the slides that are posted on d2l aren't enough to help you "study" they don't have any structure to them. You have to take like 5 quizzes throughout the semester, the professor isn't very active on d2l so theres no reminders on due dates coming from him, it's more of your job.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most genuine human beings I've ever had the pleasure of interacting with. It's rare that you find someone let alone are taught my someone with so much empathy for others who is willing to say the things that need to be heard. I came into the class not expecting much but walked away with far more than the essentials of the class.

Professor Ewoldsen's class is very engaging! He is open to discussing any topic related to his subject, which makes lessons interesting and thought-provoking. He also has a great sense of humor and shares many examples that help make the material easy to understand. I highly recommend his class!

I am writing this in the third day of his class, so obviously this review might not be the best. But, I have his class at 8am. This is the first 8am that I've had that has actually allowed me to justify this early of a class. He is a great lecturer. Not sure what the rest of the semester will look like, but so far he is great.

Dr. Everett was very considerate and helpful. He was very open to considering my view of a topic instead of just shutting my ideas down (as is typical). The quizzes could be a little tricky, and the films we had to create took me a very long time to create, but I had a great time in his class and learned a lot.
Lacks consideration for students.

super chill guy. class consisted of watching the films and taking the quizzes together. you have to make 3 short ‘films' about environmental issues, but otherwise super lenient and learned a decent bit

He doesn't require too much of you, hardest part is just doing discussion boards on the films every week. Going to class makes your life easier but you'll do almost as well if you watch the films on your own time.

Prof. Everett is pretty good. His lectures are quite boring, but attendance isn't mandatory. He does a good job trying to bring a wide variety of guest speakers and viewpoints to the class, but I just found the class super boring. The weekly quizzes are super easy, and we have three big projects. You'll succeed if you dedicate a little time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall Professor Everett is Super nice and wants you to do well! The weekly quizzes are a little hard but if you show up and take some notes you'll do good. The three big assignments are very open ended with instructions which is good as you have a lot of leeway in ur choices to do the assignments on. Easy grader if you do the work.

Don't expect this teacher to ever give you an answer for a question, he'll just say look at the syllabus. He doesn't actually teach, he reads off the PowerPoint slides he posts which are very bare. Quizzes are super easy cause you just have to look at the slides. He is an easy grader but you'll have some work to do with big assignments.

The class itself is easy, but the quizzes can be a little tricky. You will really want to pay attention to the movies and try to come to every class (although attendance isn't technically mandatory). 3 big projects (2 of them are movies that range from 3-5 mins). He's not picky and super nice. Overall, just do the work and you'll get the A.

BS161 is my nightmare class. Insane amount of work outside of class. You basically have to teach yourself since the in-class meeting times are basically just recitations (not lecturing). Super confusing due dates, so many assignments every week. I dedicated all my weekdays just to stay afloat in this class, and spent weekends on other classes.

Farre is a delight outside of class...This course was actually a nightmare though. It's doable but be prepared to work a ton outside of class and pray you get a group that's slightly competent. If you struggle to teach yourself topics take it with someone else because the "lectures" are just applying the concepts you taught yourself with iClickers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had to teach myself everything. This class structure and professor is a nightmare. Dont even know how i managed to get an A.
She gave me an academic dishonesty over a month after the class what done.

Be prepared to spend LOTS of time outside of this class doing work, and then do barely nothing in the actual lecture time. TA's were very helpful in explaining the topics but the class format is frustrating.

An absolute nightmare of a professor/class. Even as a senior I barely managed to pass her class. All the coursework is backwards with lectures being videos to watch before class and homework being done in class. The due dates for all assignments are all over the place and the exams are difficult to manage as well with none of them being dropped.

This class was a nightmare. I dropped it last semester after failing the first exam. Dr. Farre has a very thick accent, and the mic in the classroom only made it harder to hear her. The class is set up to do lectures at home then group assignments in class. Every class we either had a graded FR quiz or an exam prep activity. No exams are dropped.

This professor is the worst I've ever had. BS 161 is already an incredibly difficult class but taking it with them makes it even harder. You have to learn all material by yourself through pre-class lecture videos. Eventually you do in-class activities with a small group and no help from the professors. Good luck
if you're taking this class soon, run.
that class was horrible and NOTHING is explained. it's all up to you and you learn from videos. no thanks.

it was probably the worst class Ive ever taken in collage. So many tests and quizes so this class is just constant stress. Iclicker questions are graded and on material we are currantly learning so its hard to know the answers when you aren't comfortable with the material and its graded tough. Very heavy accent so if that's an issue for you too

This professor is a very kind and intelligent woman, but she does not teach well. Heavy accent, so if that's an issue keep that in mind. She has the course set up in reverse where the lecture takes place out of class and some homework takes place in class. Some. There is so much homework in this class. Too much.

Eva Farre does not care about you as a student. Lectures are hard to follow as you have to watch them online, and everything is on you. Hardest class I have taken in my life, harder then Organic Chemistry. Make things so difficult you basically fail the exams. No exam scores are dropped so everything is on your exams. Do not take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She would over explain a simple question that it makes you more lost and confused than ever before. Everything she "taught" would counteract what was on the exams and quizzes. She is one of the most confusing professors I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: PKG455. AVOID this class. Her lecture slides have no context (lectures NOT helpful at all). She's not clear in her instructions and what she wants from students regarding exams. No reviews and will make you feel bad if you reach out to her for clarifying questions. Group projects crammed in on top of exams. Unclear grading for assignments as well.

I took PKG455 with Professor Almenar. The lecture slides have very little info & are outdated which makes it hard to take notes. My biggest issue is that she won't give a study guide or even a list of topics included on exams. Overall this class is difficult but the professor makes it even more difficult. Don't take this class unless necessary.

This review is for PKG455. The hardest professor to work with, lecture slides are outdated, and hard to follow along. No reviews for exams, and gets defensive if you call her out on anything. Not willing to work with you, so do not take this class unless necessary.

This professor is the only one I didn't like at the School of Packaging. Her lecture slides are poorly put together with little information on them. She does not explain things well, vague details for everything. She doesn't provide a study guide, review slides, or a breakdown of exams beforehand, the "reviews" are her talking and giving no slides.

The only professor I didn't like in the school of packaging. She had a superiority complex, thinks she's better than everyone. Not helpful, not caring, not understanding. Makes you feel guilty if you reach out. Avoid at all costs!
Inconsiderate professor who doesnt care at all about her students success. Nit picky grader. Doesnt explain things well and very vague with directions. All around awful experience with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Slides are right out of the book. She turns simple concepts into extremely difficult ones in an accent & poor grammar that uses half your concentration figuring out what she's actually saying. Don't ask for deeper meaning beyond the text.She says "that's just how it is." Won't post slides, likes to pop quiz & wonders why half the class is failing.

My girlfriend took this class at umich and said it was an easy 4.0, but I ended up spending more time working on this class than I did for Calc. Be prepared to do a bunch of problem sets that have nothing to do with class content or any tests. Exams were stupidly easy, problem sets and homework were unnecessecarily complicated. Tough class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor grades her students like they know everything about sociolinguistics. So unless you're already a sociolinguistic genius, I really suggest not taking this class with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I like Dr. Wagner a lot. Although her lectures were often long & boring, I appreciated her enthusiasm for the course, her helpful nature, and her kind spirit. I do wish, though, that her lectures were more clear. Exams were difficult to prepare for b/c I never knew what was relevant info and what was excess, untested info -- even from recitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Suzanne is a doll. She is British, which I think is hilarious because she teaches Linguistics. But she knows her stuff and she wants you to know it too. She is super helpful and really wants you to think and participate. But if you're wrong, she doesn't shoot you down. Overall she has been one of my favorite professors here at MSU.

only gives negative feedback and negates points for petty issues, capitalization, commas, you get the point, she is also extremely inconsistent with grading. class is 2 hours long and you learn NOTHING, she just reads off slides in broken english, the slides themselves have little to no information and are poorly structured.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There was a lot of homework, but it was manageable. There was a group project, but the professor grades you on individual work in case your group is not good. The exams were easy as long as you paid attention in class. There are also a lot of extra credit assignments. Overall, a really good professor.

She has broken English yet she'll be petty and grade your assignments with negative feedback on EACH and EVERY assignment!!! She doesn't even follow her own rubric when grading. Me and my fiancée took the course together and we studied together. But, she shows bias to females whereas I got an A and my girlfriend got a C. If you are a female, beware

She was a fine teacher, but you have to participate and there is a lot of group work with in the class. Although there are no tests sitting through the lectures are pretty bad, its two and a half hours of talking about the same thing for weeks on end. Her grading was not very consistent.

Take this class. Extra credit and good teacher. Allowed to miss 2 class periods, no tests, exams, or quizzes. Whole class is about Islamic Architecture and based on a couple in class activities, and weekly discussion posts that are very easy.
