Final project is researching a building, then you do a slideshow at the end. Participation is not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor in teaching you soft skills that are needed for art history field. There is a lot of reading, but that's common for art history classes. Information can be difficult to understand especially when you don't know anything about islamic art, however, she is a fairly easy grader and is fairly accommodating. show up and do the work=4.0

Lectures are painful to sit through. Additionally, as others have mentioned, she ties in history from other regions and cultures that are not supposed to be included in the unit. Something like that could be interesting or deepen understanding if taught more cohesively, but in professor Fathi's case, it felt like she just shoehorned it in there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is for IAH 209. Do not take this course with Prof. Fathi. Throughout the semester, she puts out slides that are extremely vague and expects us to be able to take notes on them through conversation that does not relate to the course. She then grades the entire course through three quizzes, three short papers, and a three-page research project.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class I took was IAH 209. Personally what we learned did not interest me and it was really hard to listen and follow through with the lectures. Her slides do not help much, but she does post them. She makes you do about six papers, three reflections, and a three part final project. Three quizzes as well. She is a good professor overall.

Either art history or IAH she makes all her classes only around Islamic culture and art even when the class isn't supposed to be only about Islamic culture, which is fine it just isn't what a lot of people sign up for. She uses the whole class time lecturing if you get out early it is only by ten minutes. Very hard class to sit through
Annoying

I took IAH 209 with Prof. Fathi. You'll have to pay attention in lectures (I'd highly recommend taking notes). lectures are important for the quizzes but she has slides with highlighted information that will be on them. It's a class you should stay on top of but not incredibly assignment-heavy. She's also very easy to communicate with and flexible

You just gotta show up pay attention to lectures. 5 quizzes total all based on lectures. 2 reflection papers, one of them was summarizing an article and explaining what you found interesting, the other was based on your group project. Group project was easy if you picked a good topic with the group you are working with. 10/10 very easy class.

The class i took was IAH 209 but it won't let me input that. Amazing teacher but assigns a lot of work - a group project, 2 papers and 5 quizzes with mandatory attendance and participation in class. Not the class to take with a slacker mindset but a super interesting and engaging class to take if you're interested in art or history.

Pretty easy class but the zoom lectures were incredibly boring. We did quizzes and forums that were pretty simple, and I'm pretty sure you could get away with not reading the large amount of readings that she put up.
Super easy class, gives literal step by step instructions on how to get an A in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such an awesome guy. Wish I could take this class again.
Available whenever, would always go out of his way to attend a one on one zoom meeting for any extra help. Instructions very clear!

The best professor, down to Earth and just wants us students to succeed. Obviously theres essays that have some pre-work to do, but just follow the rubric and you should be good. He seems like a honest guy who just wants us to learn and understands this is a credit we have to all take. I took this class asynchronous but still felt seen.

A dedicated professor who has perfected his craft to share amongst his students! I recommend WRA101 to everyone thats coming in as a freshmen. You work at your own pace and still can manage to pass the class with a 4.0.

Professor Choffel is seriously one of the coolest professors I have ever had. I enjoyed writing papers for this class, and he would give me very helpful insight to make my papers better. He was always available during his office hours and would answer his email often. Overall, I recommend him to everyone and I would 100% take this class again.
Go to his office hours so he can get to know you. Very willing to help and very understanding that the class is a university credit. He just wants to make you a better writer.

Very down to Earth professor! Willing to work with you and is quite flexible. There are only a few assignments throughout the semester and no exams. If you just put some effort in, this class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very nice and chill professor. If you come to (most) classes and put in effort for your four essays you should get a 4.0. I feel like grading and the class itself was too easy honestly and I'm not sure if it prepared me for college writing as it should have. Also, introverts, beware. He does discussions/ group work like every class.

Unbelievably smart, but very down to earth professor. If you show up and give effort, you will get the grade you want. He understands that nobody in his class is pursuing a writing degree so he focuses a lot on general ideas like getting your point across and writing in your specific field.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: For a freshman writing class, I learned a lot. We only had four total projects that were all relatively easy to manage. He is willing to work with you and gives good feedback. The grading on the papers are sometimes unclear, but he is an easy grader. He also allows you to redo every paper if you do not get the grade you want.

Chao Fang (Jerry) is THE GOAT. I took this class 3 semesters ago and am just now coming back to write this--thats how awesome he is. Exams are near identical to the practice exams (which he posts videos of him doing so you know exactly how). Jerry is unbelievably funny & the most likable guy. My favorite prof/class I've EVER had. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Literally the best professor ever. He'll help you with everything whether it is understanding concept to helping with homework. Most accommodating and helpful professor I have had at MSU. Must take his class atleast once, will spark lots of interest in microeconomics. Lectures are so fun to attend, attendance is mandatory though but he's funny.

Very caring, funny, and relaxed. The exams are similar to the reviews. The HW can be confusing at times, but he helps you with them after class if you ask. The lectures were boring, but that's just how the EC301 content is. You were only allowed to miss a few classes, and attendance was taken daily. Easy A overall.

ISS 315- Very lecture-heavy. Only graded on quizzes and exams. Not one singular skip is allowed/gets dropped, same with the weekly quizzes. Offers extra credit, but you have to volunteer weekly through the semester and write 2 essays, 3 pages long each. Lectures are boring...
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can be very long and boring. He is very passionate and knows what he's talking about. Overall the class is very easy. He can be hard to reach outside of the class but the TAs are always available. Pay attention to the stories he tells in class cause there's questions about them on the quizzes/exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I thought the class would be interesting to learn about, but his lectures are unbearable. All his stories from the lectures are always included in the weekly quizzes so you have to stay awake to understand what will be on the quizzes.

One of the nicest and respectable professors I have had. It is definitely important to pay attention and take notes in all of his lectures since the quizzes and tests are a direct reflection of them. Lectures were often boring but his personality and passion for the subject made the class a lot more enjoyable. Show up and you will 4.0 no problem.

I loved him as a person, and his class was pretty easy, but if you take bad notes, you're in trouble. Write down everything that comes out of his mouth and study quizlets for quizzes and exams and you'll be fine.

The class is generally easy, but make sure to study for the quizzes and exams. The lectures are insanely boring, and it is very hard to concentrate. I would try to take this class online, also the grading is very unclear, and the professor takes forever to put in the grades even online quizzes.

Prof Hussian clearly cares about the material. During class he goes over PowerPoints and you take notes which you are allowed to use on tests and exams. His enthusiasm made me really enjoy the class. Exams and tests are easy as long as you take notes. Class is very easy as long as you put some effort. Strongly recommend

fayyaz hussain, wow... what to say? lets start with the jokes about the shooting. really man? how about the fact that he also doesnt answer emails, this man could not do absolutely anything without his TA. she does EVERYTHING for him. I honestly feel really bad for the girl. my heart goes out to you sophia for all you have to deal with...
Fayyaz Hussein was really boring but the class is an easy A and you do not have to do a lot of work. The ULA is mad helpful as she opens any quizzes you miss.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hussain was really good, I enjoyed his classes, we had weekly quizzes but it was all online so it wasn't hard, he is the best

Overall a fine class. Although, I would not recommend taking with this teacher. Got above an 85's and mostly 90s on every quiz/test and somehow finished with a 3.0
Lectures are boring and not much is done to make the class interesting.

My favorite prof at MSU. If you take notes on everything he says you'll get a 4.0 and it's a pretty interesting class as well. His tests/quizzes are online and their straight from what he talks about. If your taking ISS take it with him.

I've had an awful experience with this professor. The course trajectory is generally unclear, and he is not willing to help with issues that come up. He miscalculated my final grade for the course and was very reluctant to fix it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Hussian is genuinely one of my favorite professors. His lectures are very thought out and interesting. He is very well spoken and always makes you think. He involves personal stories to keep the lectures interesting and also cares for his students. Although his class is difficult (4 exams and a quiz every Thursday) it is 100% worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is super nice and grades fairly. My class was online, but basically just had to watch the lecture every week and take a quiz on it. There was a weekly zoom meeting where he literally tells you every question on the quiz, same goes for finals. Really laid back, just have to take good notes because its all open notes. Extra credit is nice too.

Difficult class, but excellent professor. Interesting lectures and great content. You really have to study for the exams and read the texbook to get a good grade but Hussain offers gracious extra credit. He also drops one of the 4 exams he gives, which is a grade booster. 10/10 would recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Standards based grading made relatively easy material nearly impossible to get a good grade on. multiple quizzes included questions on topics not discussed until the next day in class, amplified by the credit no credit nature of his grading. He did everything in his power not to be held accountable for any mistakes. Required a 100% to get a 4.0

Took Trig/Pre-Calc with Dr. Fessler (Spring 2026). Material isn't very hard, but earning a 4.0 is tough due to “success”-based quizzes and no clear grading scale. Lectures can go off-topic, even during work time. Uses AI for lectures/grading. Quizzes sometimes cover material not fully taught in class. Cool dude overall but not the best teacher.

Very passive-aggressive when asking questions, almost rude even. Not good at teaching and with the most unclear grading criteria possible. I legit couldn't see my percent grade all semester. Expect lots of meaningless group projects and busy work. Weekly quizzes that are pretty easy, but oftentimes hard to understand. Do not take.

A nice guy to talk to, but awful teacher. Does not give any instructions and expects you to know everything before hand. Does not grade until the last minute and does not grade resubmits fast, so you don't know what you get wrong.

I took LB 117 online, for the most part it was the same content as my high school calculus class but he either never elaborated on what he wanted us to do on the labs, or briefly went over what material he wanted us to turn in and always took so long to grade stuff. Overall horrible experience.
I would not recommended taking this class. This professor briefly goes over material and expects 100% understanding and some. There are also labs in this class?? A math class.

Dr. Fessler does not teach, but rather reads equations and makes you solve them all class. He does not handle criticism or suggestions at all. Makes you buy a new calculator for the 3 tests that we have. Be prepared to teach yourself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: horrible horrible horrible never ever take mth103 with chuck fessler. he may be the worst teacher i've ever had in my entire life. his grading doesn't make any sense, the exams do not correlate with the material we learn in class whatsoever and he does not respond well to criticism or feedback and blames everyone failing on us not being prepared.

super nice guy but grades lab reports insanely. it is insanely hard. extremely tough grader on the lab reports for the pre-clac equal. for exams in MTH 103, it was very hard to gauge his expectations on tests/quizzes. i felt like i never knew what he was looking for

I took calc in high school, and struggled with his class. He does not explain well, and examples we do in class are completely different than assessments. I turned in an assignment in the beginning of October and it was not graded until early December. It was also nearly impossible to tell what your actual grade was throughout. not a good time

Dr. Fessler was always very nice and supportive for me. I went to his office hours often. He pulls some questions from the book for quizzes and exams but you can never be prepared enough. Seek as many sources as you can for studying. I did have to study very hard for his course but I managed to 4.0 with never taking calc in highschool!

professor fessler is a great guy however he was a terrible professor. he left me and my classmates very confused after every class and expected us to know everything presented in front of us. he didn't teach properly and all the homework that was assigned per unit didn't correlate with anything we were "learning" in class.

Would give 0. Didn't grade majority of assignments until end of semester. Never taught in class + majority of the class was always confused. Tests and online homework did not match examples done in class. Hard to succeed unless you have a strong calc background. Never helped w/ problems and didn't seem like he knew what he taught. Save yourself.

Nice guy, but can't teach at all. He works very fast in class and expects students to already have some background in calc. I was also having medical issues this semester and he was very hard to work with on this. He also lost one of my exams after I took it in his office hours. Don't recommend at all

If I can give Fessler a 0 I would. He doesn't teach any of his subjects and expects you to know everything already. You have a a quiz every week that's 50% of your grade and there is no dropping but only 1 retake of an exam at the end of the semester. The homework is on webwork and doesn't really correlate with what he is "teaching".
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fessler is an amazing guy to talk to, but he is not a very effective instructor. I often found myself leaving lectures confused and unsure of how I would be able to succeed in this course. Once again, he is a very caring, but please try to get an override if you have to take one of his courses. I left Briggs because of instructors like this.

Chuck is a great guy but should not be teaching math 103. He changes the way he grades constantly, gets irritated at students for asking questions, and barely teaches. He just makes us do the notes and expects us to be math wizards. He is very kind but if you get stuck with him for class, I would recommend taking math 103 through the university.

Nice guy, awful professor. His grading is harsh and confusing and forces you to do most of the work in terms of determining your actual grade. He does not teach the material well if he teaches it at all, and the questions seen on assessments are ones not previously discussed, found in the notes, or in any of the hw or review problems. Do not take.

Terrible professor do not take him! Grades very tough and gives weekly quizzes on material he barely covers. Treats this introductory Calc 1 course like a upper level course. Do not take him no matter what you do.

Does not teach. Once got annoyed with students for asking questions and not understanding content, which was only the case because he teaches way too fast or not at all. Sometimes is unsure about his own questions. Practice exam material does not always match actual exam content. He is friendly and a good person but not a good teacher.

Very good person and could have been a more effective instructor. He is a great guy to talk to, but when it comes to course material, I am always left confused, and so are my classmates. He is accommodating but also really likes to talk, which is inconvenient when you need help with class activities.

Great guy, terrible teacher. This class was genuinely one of the worst experiences I had in college, I would come into class and leave more confused than when I had entered. You can easily learn the content online (organic chem tutor) rather than in his lectures. His teaching style just did not resonate with me and friends who took his class. 3/10

The professor is very nice and sweet, but he's not good at teaching math, as he demonstrates how to solve things fast with barely any explanation. He also grades extremely hard on tests and quizzes, giving some problems that are barely within the range of what he taught. Everyone's left confused after every class period

Incredibly nice guy but occasionally difficult to work with. He is not the greatest at explaining material, and many questions end up being taught to yourself because it is challenging to understand them in his lectures. Would  honestly make a better English or history professor
Chuck is a great guy who wants you to succeed if you demonstrate to him that you care. He is very helpful and understanding!

I had him for both trig and calc. I will say I saw improvement in his grading between the two semesters, but it is still very difficult to succeed if you're not already good at math or have had no prior calc experience. Quizzes every week, you can't miss them without a doctor's note. I liked him as a person, but he isn't the greatest professor.

He's a nice guy but take someone else for calculus. He means well by standards-based grading but it makes it more difficult to get a good grade. Quizzes are every week in recitation and I felt like I didn't learn concepts in lecture. Our ULA would go over content before the quiz and that's when I'd grasp the subject.

He is a good person but that is it. He teaches terrible and gives you quizzes every week during recitation. He gives problems and questions that you never really learn in class. The TAs felt bad for us because we would all be so lost in his class. I would try to take calc through the university. The grading scale makes it impossible to do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice person, but I would recommend taking Calc through university. Quizzes every week during recitation. LA's always felt bad for us because of the immense struggle we all had. Grades based on standards and I had no idea what my grade was all semester. Some questions on the quizzes 1 exams I had never seen before.
Just so bad, so so so bad. do not take. take university calc and do not take lyman calc. or u will be screwed. best of luck!!!

Actually a horrendous professor (nice guy though). Ended up teaching myself everything because of it. Study guides do not help, and a very misleading grading system. You will have quizzes every week (on and off independent and group style) in recitation which is required. You cannot skip these quizzes without a doctor's note (same for exams).

HORRIBLE class. He is a nice guy but I dont think teaching math is his thing. take calculus through university you get online exams.  if you don't want to watch your grade drop every week take it outside. really bad grading his teaching style is also wack.  the exam study guide doesn't correlate with the exam. Nice guy needs to consider changing su

Whatever you do, do not take this class. He changes the way you're graded constantly and literally cannot teach. If you are not already a master at trig, STAY AWAY. He overcomplicates everything and will take points away if you don't do work the way he wants it. He's actually a pretty nice guy, but worst prof I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fenn was very knowledgeable in what she was talking about. However she came off a little rude. As long as you try to go to class and study a good amount you'll do fine. Extra credit is offered which is nice. (just don't wait until last minute to do it). Also do your SONA research on time.

Dr. Fenn is a great lecturer and definitely knows her stuff. However, you can tell that she dislikes her life.  She is extremely hot and cold towards students. One moment she will be nice and the next she will lash out at you with no warning. I would avoid her if given the chance. Also expect rude emails and responses if you ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She did teach me important information. I highly reccomend to not miss classes even though the lectures are quite boring they are important. She can be very passive aggressive and asking questions becomes daunting because of her responses. She is very knowledgable though, study for the final as best as you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Can be a bit hard on you, but just have common sense. Attendance not required, but it becomes an easy A if you do. Just show up to class and complete the homework, and you'll pass easily.

Professor Fenn is very straightforward about all lectures, assignments, participation requirements, and extra credit opportunities. While some may find that the content is difficult to understand, if you attend class and do the homework, it's hard to do badly. Overall, I really enjoyed the class and learned a lot!

She is a fine professor. Easy class, the only problem I have with her is that she is very condescending to students. It is a mostly freshman class and she kept going on and on when the class was confused about filling out the scantron with no instruction from her how to fill it out. If you don't want to be yelled at don't take this class.

Professor Fenn is good but can be rude towards students at times. Just dont ask questions and dont let her see your phone(she will call you out). She also called someone out for leaving class 10 mins early. There is extra credit which raises your grade +3%. Homework isnt too hard its due every friday. Tests are just alot of memorizing.

I enjoyed this class. Fenn has great informational lectures, it is sometimes hard to be there for an hour and 20 minutes, but it is an overall easy class. Homework and exams aren't hard. My only advice is to not ask questions during lecture, you will see why. But overall worth getting as a professor.

Attendance is not mandatory but HIGHLY recommended, as lots of test questions are directly from the lectures. Homework is a weekly inquizitive + research participation. you'll be fine as you just do your work. Her lecturing is also great and she's very knowledgeable, and just be polite.

Professor Fenn is definitely knowledgeable, and her psych 101 class is really easy if you just go to lectures. You cannot get all the information off of the slides. She is sometimes rude to students, but usually only when they ask questions that waste time. Overall, if you just go to class and don't talk, you'll probably get an A.

Prof. Fenn is an engaging lecturer who makes the content very applicable and easy to understand. The comments of her being snappy are true, but if you pay attention and don't ask silly questions or talk during her lecturers it won't be a problem for you. If you go to lecturers, do the readings, and study for the exams they are pretty easy.

I personally though that Dr Fenn, was amazing you can tell that she cares about her students and about her craft, she is a great professor, make sure that you are going to class, and pay attention. She can be condescending sometimes but overall as a professor she is amazing. I have seen Her yell at a student for the dumbest reason, she can be rude

The class is very lecture heavy, but the lectures are very informative and interesting. She is quite rude especially to students whose questions she deems a waste of her time. Attendance is not mandatory but I highly recommend going because I found that going to lecture and just going over the review slides, was enough to do well on the exams.

One of the rudest professors I have ever come across. Will ask her a simple question, and will get a passive aggressive answer. I don't know one person that thinks otherwise and isn't absolutely terrified of her.

Undoubtedly, Professor Fenn definitely knows what she's talking about and she is a great professor. The only thing that throws me off is how she is sometimes rude to her students. Other than that, she goes in depth into the material and ensures that you understand it. Be sure to pay attention to what she's saying. Only reading the slides won't work

Personally, I thought Dr. Fenn was a great professor. She could be a little snappy at times if you were rude to her, but overall she kept things professional and educational. She didn't just read off of the slides presented and made the audience engage with her. She can go through topics a little fast, but luckily the topics aren't too difficult.

Great and engaging lectures. If you take basic notes and study for a few days before the exam, you will do amazing. I can see why people call her rude, but she doesn't want her time wasted and lowk I respect that. If you show up to lectures and pay attention you'll pass.

Went into this class thinking I would actually learn & realized very quickly that I will have to teach everything to myself. Her slides would help if she was acc talking about the course but she side tracks often and tbh is very rude in general. I have witnessed her being rude to her TA's which isn't a good look and put me off. Very tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself was fine it's just really important you attend lectures (she'll get really heated if you don't). Honestly one of the rudest, most disrespectful professors I have ever encountered. She was rude to her ULAs and especially in her emails. I never once sensed an ounce of kindness nor care in anything she said or wrote. Beware.

Dr. Fenn can come off as standoffish, but you can tell she really cares about her students under her rough exterior. She taught me a lot and I would take her again. Just pay attention and do your work its not that bad.

Nice but can be a little condescending. This class was so easy but it might be a lot if you fall behind. Try to attend most of the lectures, even if you don't take notes they're still helpful. Also, the extra credit is time consuming but so worth it as something to fall back on just in case you don't do so well on one of the exams.

Professor Fenn was cool. The class was easy if you study a normal amount. Homework can be annoying, but not bad. Her lectures are organized and engaging use real-world examples to make things understandable. She can be passive aggressive, but the bad reviews are exaggerated- she is a fine professor. Textbook is unnecessary- don't waste your money

This prof is so rude/passive aggressive with all of her students. Every encounter I have had with her or watched her have with another student she has not shown any kindness, which spoils the whole class for you. The class isnt that bad, she gives extra credit points, attendance isnt mandatory, but is urged. Her attitude just ruined it for me.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fenn is very educated in her field, and definitely knows what she is teaching. Although, she tends to be rude to students and passive aggressive. No attendance is required, but I strongly advise to go because all the exam information are from her lecture notes and videos played in class. Weekly homework, but fairly easy if you stay on track.

Professor Fenn was very thorough and outlined all expectations of the course. There is research included so be sure to get this done on time! Generous curves are provided and overall it is easy to succeed. Going to lectures are important and the course is test heavy---but there is a drop and a final will replace lowest score.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fenn teaches an informative and no-nonsense course. Some people refer to her as rude, but seeing as most of those people ask questions about things provided since the beginning of the semester I can understand her frustration. Lectures are not mandatory but you WONT pass this class without continued attendance and detailed notes. Would take again.

Make sure to attend class and take notes! The exams are based on lectures, the slides will not help you, attendance is not mandatory so don't let that tempt you. There is Inquisitive homework due every Friday night which is easy. Part of your grade is from research hours, and extra credit will be available to you.

Super knowledgeable, probably more than most professors in her field. That being said, GO TO CLASS!! The exams are almost entirely based on class discussions. The lecture slides barely help and the textbook is basically your only option. The homework is chill but can take a very long time. Can be passive-aggressive if you ask dumb questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fenn is knowledgeable and respectable. Some find her passive-aggressive, but if you put in effort and check provided information first, she's chill. The class is content-heavy, so attendance and focus are key. Exams are curved, homework is a little bit long but an easy 100 if you're trying. TA's are helpful, and office hours are highly recommended

She gives pretty massive curves which I am grateful for. Make sure to buy some index cards to make flashcards. She gives occasional extra credit problems which you would only know if you attend lecture. Weekly inquisitive HW due on Friday 11:59pm (can take up to 4 hours so plan accordingly). All exam material in inquisitive textbook

Very rude and condescending while talking to her and in her emails. Exams are completely based on discussions from the lecture and the review slides she posted commonly didn't include stuff from the lecture that was on the exam. If you must take it with her make sure to go to every lecture or else you're cooked.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fenn is not everyone's favorite professor and definitely wasn't mine. She is very knowledgeable about psychology but sometimes it can get the best of her where she can forget that it is a 100-level class. She is very passive aggressive in lectures towards students. Tests often have questions directly from class.

Even tho she doesn't take attendance you will fail if you don't pay attention to her lectures. Also if you don't read the textbook you will also probably fail. Your grade is basically just based off exams and the questions are absurd. Don't take this class. Kims also just rude to every student that talks.

Annoying homework every week, give yourself more time than you think you need. Lecture heavy and questions on tests are based on things she says in lecture. She drops one test so if you do good on the first 4 you don't have to take the final. 8 hours required SONA with 6 more extra credit hours (3%). Curves tests.

Fenn is extremely advanced in Psych and her lectures were very organized. To do good on tests attendance is SO IMPORTANT. Not only that but also writing in depth notes of all of the slides & memorizing all of it. Fenn was aggressive at times and made me feel like I couldn't ask questions. She will single you out if you are off task or leave early.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, she's fine but was super snarky in emails. Her lectures are very interesting but can get boring quick.

Interesting lectures, but LOTS of info. Minimum of 8 hrs of psych research participation (max 2 online) and extra hrs are bonus. She cares about helping you succeed as long as you put in the work required. Lowest exam is dropped, so if you pass the first 4, you don't need to take the final. As long as you memorize everything, the class is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The reason I didn't pass the class my own fault. Although attendance isn't mandatory if you do not go you will not pass which is why I did not. She can be passive aggressive at some points but the lectures are put together well.

Dr. Fenn is a fair grader and is a no-nonsense type of professor, but she can be passive-aggressive and condescending at times. Not easy to approach. Attendance was not mandatory, it is NOT recommended to skip often. There are 4 exams, 5 with the final, BUT one of them is dropped, so you could drop the final. Also, there are curves. She's solid.

Most of the questions on exams were based of things she said in class that were not included on slides so although attendance wasn't mandatory without going to class you essentially would fail. You could possibly not hear something and miss a question on the exam. Homework was once a week and took forever. 8 hours of research required too.

Professor Fenn gives amazing interactive lectures that made me enjoy going to her class. She has a very professional personality that could seem strict but she is funny and a great professor. Homework is easy but don't wait til last minute cause it can take a few hours if you dont know the content. She is very lenient with a curve on exams.

Dr. Fenn was an amazing professor. Attendance was not mandatory, but some questions on the exam are about things she showed in lectures so if you don't show up, you'll miss easy points on the exam. She is very, very passionate about psychology. Listen to what she says in class because it provides a more in-depth understanding.

I love this professor! I saw all the comments from Rate My Professor before the first day of class and I was worried. But she is an amazing teacher. The information is clear and if you need help there are multiple opportunities to get help. She is funny, smart and values hard work. Be prepared to work but the class is only hard if you don't try.

She set a very clear criteria on the first day of class and what to expect throughout the semester. If you put effort and work into the class, it's not hard to get a 4.0. I highly recommend starting research hours early to give yourself enough time. Dr. Fenn is very blunt but funny at times and seems to care for how well her students do.
Didn't make me feel great about myself in the way she talked to me or responded to emails.
Extremely rude in emails.

Professor Fenn's class is very lecture heavy, and is not a good fit for students who don't like to show up to class. It has more requirements than I expected for a 100 level class, however she is very clear about how exams will look and what is expected of you. If you are someone who doesn't mind putting in some work, I would recommend her course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely homework heavy without any guidance or actually helpful advice to not spend hours on it a night. Fenn was weirdly rude after I had just asked for a bit of help with her system and told me not to contact her about this again. Not to mention 8 hours of research studies. This is a crazy amount of work for a 101. I ended up dropping it.

Professor Fenn is a super sweet woman who knows what she is talking about, I really liked her and the class, however the class itself is so lecture heavy and has a huge emphasis on remembering things for tests, so it was difficult for me to learn that way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Fenn was a good professor she is very knowledgeable. Exams were lecture heavy. If you didn't go to class you would miss easy points on the exam. She used a lot of examples in her power-points which were very engaging. Her exams were fairly easy if you attended class regularly. Decent amount of homework, but it was easy and for participation.

she told us the exam was online open note, then 2 weeks later said we were "cheating" so changed the exam to in person. I hated going, I hate Kim. during exams her goofy little minions would walk around me and distract me when I was trying to focus. The questions would be like "In Friday's lecture we watched a video based where" I didnt go idk kim

You can do well if you don't go to class but will do better if you do. Lectures were very engaging and she uses lots of examples for each concept. Exams lineup with the lectures. A lot of people didn't like her and besides the occasional attitude I don't understand why. Lots of professors just read off the slides, she actually teaches you.

3 practice quizzes a week for homework, across 14 chapters on Macmillan Achieve. 4 exams with a final, class adjusted to in-person exams after reports of cheating, avoid cheating on exams. Very good lectures and readable/understandable slides for review. Overall the class was very enjoyable and you get what you put into it.

Prof. Fenn was someone who was blunt and did not have a ton of patience. However, a lot of the complaints against her are ones you won't deal with as long as you go to class and actually try to pay attention/do well. Tests were very consistent with in lecture material, and she does a great job explaining things.

the class started off good in the beginning and then it just went downhill. she would go off on tangents about herself and would not stick to the syllabus. her ego is so high it is torture listening to her. if you do take this class with prof. fenn make sure you go to lecture because most test questions are on stuff in lecture.

Professor Fenn is very educated but was weird and lowkey rude. She suspected our class of cheating on our first exam due to having a higher test score than her previous year (it was open note), so changed all exams to in person and no open note in the middle of the semester. I never went to class and ended up okay. Would've taken online instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Fenn was a great professor. Sometimes she could come off as rude but most of the time she was a very joking person. She is very open to questions and student participation during lectures. The textbook was $90 but you must buy it because it is what the homework is done through. Just study, go to lectures, complete the homework and you will be fine

professor fenn has a very rude demeanor and tends to put students down a lot when they ask simple questions during class. our exams were originally online but she changed them to in-person due to suspected "cheating" because we had a higher class average than previous classes even though it was all open-note. she seems to have an ego issue.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Go to lectures!! Her tests are primarily on her in person lectures so take notes and pay attention. You will not do well on her tests if you don't go to class. Other wise, the work load is no big deal and she's nice.

Professor Fenn is very educated, but she is overall super rude. She changed online exams to in person tests because she claimed there was cheating because we did better than her prior class. She is harsh when it comes to answering questions in lectures as well as picking on students who leave early. She makes very unprofessional remarks in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She doesn't follow what's in her syllabus and is super rude when she's asked questions in class. She changed our tests halfway through the semester, and her reasoning was the class average for the first exam was higher then the other years she taught it. I would try to take this class with a different professor.

Please do not take this professor, took class suspecting an easy 4.0 because it's a 101 class but professor Fenn has an ego problem. She is very educated however is rude and lacks logic, changed entire format of class over people 'cheating' on a online, open note exam, and then made it in-person, no notes to benefit us? Take a different elective
She was sort of mean when it came to asking questions in class. She has a bit of a short temper, and grading was kind of harsh. Class was VERY lecture heavy.
Snippy with questions so be careful about her short temper. She gets incredibly angry if you leave class early so watch out for that as well. Overall rude and unkind but educated.

Dr. Fenn was in all a great professor. Whenever I went up to ask a question, she was friendly and was willing to help. Although the exams were changed from being online to in person, they were also made significantly easier. As long as you pay attention and attend lectures, this class is a breeze.

Changed the class & exams to in person because she refused to believe we were smart enough to do as well as we did on the 1st exam (and this actually came out of her mouth), automatically suspected cheating and held this over the class for the whole semester. Also, she stated that the original exam was open book, note, etc.
Had exam's online to start the year then on first exam the average was "too high" so she suspected cheating and made all exams in-person

Good professor knew what she was talking about but was snotty. Exams were supposed to be online but she changed them to in person due to "cheating." Which idk how that is possible because they were open book, open note, open google, open everything, as she literally said that to the class. Also have to pay $80 for homework access.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Fenn was one of the few professors I had this semester that was very passionate and skilled in what she taught. Make sure you go to class if you have Dr. Fenn because the exams are pretty much based on the lectures. So as long as you go to class, ask questions, and study some, you will do well and the exams will be a breeze.

Professor Fenn is a decent professor. If you pay attention in class, study, and do your homework, you will be fine. Homework is easy. She's a good teacher, but sometimes she has a short temper. She will get mad at the class if she finds people cheating or not paying attention, so just beware. Very interesting lectures. Try not to skip class.

Prof.Fenn was very knowledgable, but is not very open to asking questions, and often responds in a rude demeanor. Homework and exams are online which is super nice. Homework is just taking notes from the textbook, and taking non-graded quizzes at the end. Very interesting information, and you will succeed as long as you put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: good professor very entertaining during lectures, a couple of homework assignments per week, a couple of exams throughout the semester, but overall very easy. the one downside to her class is that the required homework and book resource is $80.
Her lectures were interesting. Used a lot of videos that were interesting. Around 2-3 homework assignments a week.

Fenn was an amazing, well-educated, and well-respected professor. The only downside to the course is that you do have to spend about 80 dollars on a service for the textbooks and the exams. Course was easy to do well in as long as you manage your time well!

She's a nice professor, but the class lectures are just repeated info from what we had to read from the book (it was ~$80 and required). The textbook is a good read, though, and the assignments are linked to the textbook, which is really cool b/c you can find your answer in the section of the book without looking for it yourself. Not for exams tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: She was great loved her lectures but the exams are very long but she offers a lot of resources to help
Loved her. Respected. Interesting lectures.
I loved PSY 101. Super easy if you just go to lecture and pay attention with a little studying before exams I think I got close to 100% in the class.

The professor is nice. But the content is huge in this course. The exams are very lengthy and require a thorough reading of the book. She gets irritated if you do email the questions she addressed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's rude when responding to emails, doesn't give good lectures, and grades one of her assignments (personal statement) based on whether she thinks you would get into med school, even though this is a psych course and it's subjective. She's a harsh grader and unfair about it. This is the first prof I've felt the need to rate bc of how bad it was.
I took this class as asynchronous, but the lectures were easy to follow and the assigned reading was 100% necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took this class online. Every week you had to read a chapter from the textbook, answer homework questions, and take a quiz. Mid-term and final were based completely on textbook. Super easy. Extra credit is available, BUT MAKE SURE YOU GET YOUR RESEARCH PARTICIPATION DONE EARLY. Professor was nice, even though I never spoke to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I wish I had her in person. Yes, this is an asynchronous class, but her video lectures are great. She replies fast to emails if you ever gave any questions. Definitely have a textbook handy at all times, reading that book is what will help you in this class and on her assignments.

Professor Fenn was incredible in my opinion. Her lectures (although online and asynchronous) were extremely detailed yet so intriguing! She does an amazing job of explaining things. The exams were on the difficult side, however the extra credit offered is a great grade booster. I would definitely want her as my prof again!

I loved going to her lectures simply because she was just a joy to be around. She makes lectures fun but I have never been a fan nor really good at psychology but the nice thing is that the text book is available online. Just make sure you read, practice the material, and study for exams because that will help understand the course material to pass

You must participate in at least 7 hours of the psychology lab. This is demanding for busy students. You can get extra credits by participating in up to 6 hours of lab. So it is not easy to get extra credit. All the exam is a multiple-choice but doesn't mean it is easy. Especially don't recommend international students cos she speaks so fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Fenn covered a lot of content in easy to understand terms (lots of examples). She gave reasonable expectations and clear guidelines. She gets frustrated when people ask stupid questions and email her constantly, which is understandable due to her class size and research load. Would 10/10 recommend her for any course--amazing prof.

One of the best professors I've ever had. She is so nice and clearly states the do's and dont's at the start of the year. Lectures were almost always interesting and she gave a good extra credit assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class is composed of 5 exams including the final one of which you can drop. Exam questions come right from the study guides that are provided on D2L. Clicker points are used for attendance. SONA Research is required and extra hours can be used to raise your grade up to 3% overall. Exams are all multiple choice and have an extra credit question.

Honestly as long as you show up to class you're good for the semester. She's very funny and personable but can be hostile if she needs to be. She connects real life situations or examples to the material which helps. I'd take this class again!
Great Professor! I really enjoyed her lectures. Very fair tests if you go to lecture. Extra credit possible through psy studie hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures and recitation are mandatory, however you are permitted to miss more than enough. Your grade is heavily based on exams, but the exams are fair and she always curves them (dont rely on curves). You can get up to 3 percent extra credit. Drops your lowest exam score, so I didnt have to take the final. Never got below a 94 on an exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: although she can be rude when asking dumb questions, she is a great professor and made learning psychology fun. she was able to make lectures engaging and is always wanting her students to succeed. she offers extra credit at the end of the course too which helps a lot!!

Good teaching style. She does take attendance using clickers. I haven't used the book once, it's online so you don't have to buy it if you do want to use it. Tests are easy, just pay attention to the lectures and clicker questions.

You don't need to read any type of textbook with her. she supplies study guides and if you understand and know everything on it you'll do fantastic on the exams. There aren't surprises. Questions are VERY easy on exams. Basically know the terms she gives you and know how to apply them to real life scenarios and you'll be set.

Clicker points - so you should attend class. Lectures are easy to follow and she explains things very well. Have to participate in research projects, but can also get extra credit by doing more than required.

Definitely makes lectures very interesting, but you'll want to read the material in the textbook to have a solid grasp of the info. She was very generous grading, everything on the exam was presented during the lectures at some point. Would definitely recommend her if you're interested in psychology.

Fenn structures her class great. There are 4 exams throughout the semester, but there is no final because of all the material covered. With that being said, the lectures are boring, but you basically have to go to receive credit for attendance and to understand whats going on. You also have the opportunity to receive 3% extra through SONA.

Professor Fenn is pretty funny and sarcastic sometimes. She does a great job at making her lectures interesting by using videos of real life situations that relate to the material. I would recommend her!
Easy professor if you study her powerpoints. Interesting presentations as well, good choice if you have to take this class.
Shes's pretty sarcastic and can be disrespectful of the students but she presents what will be on the exams. Will not change grades.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Dr Fenn's class overall. If you're respectful to her she'll be the same to you. Her exams are reasonably difficult but she provides clear and helpful study guides and offers lots of extra credit. I liked taking this class.

I loved Dr. Fenn, I'd definitely take another one of her classes. You don't technically have to go to class but clicker questions count for points. She's really sweet and nice if you're respectful towards her and the TAs.
She talks very quickly and seems to have a desire to be the "cool prof". She wasn't terrible though.
Great psychology teacher! Lectures were interesting but attendance is mandatory. Tests are clear and if you take notes during lecture should do well.

She was a good professor and I would take a class with her again but her tests were exceptionally hard. her pacing is distracting but you get used to it really quickly. Her lectures are hard to take notes from I recommend going to office hours and the TA's.

She was an amazing professor. I absolutely loved being in her class and you can tell she has a passion for this subject. She provides so many opportunities for clarification, to ask question, and extra credit. She really cares if her students succeed and I felt her tests were set up so that anyone who paid attention in lectures would pass.

I was in the High Achievers Summer Program and she was an amazing teacher. Very interactive. Attempts to teach visually and in a hands-on fashion. Debate days were the best. Do the work, and you'll easily get an A
She reinforced my love of psychology.
Fenn was a great professor, she made the class very interesting. Always posted lectures online and answered any questions.

Dr. Fenn is a very interactive teacher that is friendly and funny. She gives you  multiple extra credit opportunities and asks if anyone has questions during lecture. She posts the lectures and study guides online. Overall easy intro class.
Mrs. Fenn is a wonderful, interactive teacher
Projects students wanting unethical relationships with authority figures, creates mess in between unethical thinking processes.

MSU was amazing. except that there is a projected gender bias that instruments thinking that girls are only interested in education for male validation & attention. Preserves & pushes notion that all women actions revolve around a men & not a women's intellectual curiosity. Projects own male wanted attention to students which causes chaos.
Unfortunately likes to make inappropriate comments. Might want to review how to keep students engaged.
Projects insecurities on to students. Subconsciously wants to cheat on their partner
Makes comments about cheating... might want to cheat on partner. Comments have nothing to do with the course
Likes to make inappropriate jokes.

Professor likes to start class talking about TV shows explicit s*x scenes, also likes to talk about how hot fictional doctors are and where she would have s*x with them, and shimmy (shake shoulders) her way to greet and hug students.

Gave great feedback during writing of research paper, was available and made time to check in with students. This was online over summer, and expectations were clear, and appropriate. If you're stuck just ask a question! A little bit of reading, but not that hard, chooses interesting articles and content to digest.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was a big fan of the material for this history class, as we learned about times of bottom-up progressive movements in U.S. history, many of which do not get covered as extensively as they should. I loved reading the Combahee River Collective Statement for an assignment. Also, Dr. Fernandez is engaging in her lectures and accessible out of class.

This is NOT an easy 4.0 200 level class. Exam questions are not straight forward, she lets students determine what terms will be on the exam, but then uses those terms and finds the MOST complicated question to make out of it. Unless you LOVE history and challenging classes, DON'T TAKE THIS. It will bring down your GPA more than you expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Fernandez made lectures interesting and is pretty funny. You have to go to lectures though to truly understand the material and do well on the tests. Recitation basically gives you all the questions that will be on the tests. Didnt read any of the books assigned and got As on the midterm and final.

Dr. Fernandez is probably one of the best professors at MSU. You have to go to lectures though and take good notes to do good in the class. She tries to throw in extra credit every now and then which is great. For the midterm and final I didnt read any of the books and still got an A. Overall easy class if you study for the tests.

He was probably one of the worst professors I have ever had. All of his lectures were written on a chalkboard with terrible handwriting and would not post anything on D2L. He acted like he was so much smarter than everyone instead of actually helping you learn. He also requires a physical textbook which I found to be annoying on top of everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His D2L was a mess, and he was difficult to contact outside of class time. As far as his lectures go, I thought he was very clear. However, his grading was relatively harsh on irrelevant things. I enjoyed the style of this class, with a heavy emphasis on Ethics Bowl tournaments, but midterm and finals are still worth 45% of the overall grade.

Lectures lacked clarity, hindering understanding. The professor was inaccessible, there was poor email response, and no clear office hours. The schedule is chaotic, assignments unclear, and deadlines vague. Disengaged atmosphere in class.

Dr. Ferkany himself is a good guy; however, I did not enjoy him as a teacher. His lectures were difficult to understand because they were so unorganized. In fact, his entire class was unorganized. He gives odd assignments with huge weight attached and makes grading flaws constantly. He will also never respond to an email.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. His lectures barely cover any information and don't translate to the exams. He stated that he likes to see students struggle on exams. The textbook is the only important thing in this class. This class also requires students to do a group debate and he doesn't care that group members aren't helping.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Ferkany is a good guy but the class itself sucked. You HAVE to buy the $55 course pack. Pop quizzes are given that do not at all translate to what he teaches in lecture. You also probably will not understand anything you've read better after leaving his lecture. Heavily discussion based. He also will never respond to an email.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Refuses to let us use laptops to take notes, and his notes are very hard to follow. Required course packet you have to buy with all the readings for the semester. ZERO chance of passing without this. Random pop quizzes at the start of class. Claims that philosophy can be interpreted in different ways but takes points off for "misinterpretations".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Class is almost entirely discussion-based and how often you participate in discussions is recorded. You will lose points if you don't participate a certain number of times in the semester. Lectures can be hard to follow. Several essays with very short notice (I'm talking assigned and then due the next class period), and are graded pretty hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I believe Professor Ferkany is passionate about philosophy, however he does not translate the concepts well in the classroom. Lots of reading and writing in this class. Moat of the time I left a lecture not understanding anything we just covered. He does take attendance and will deduct points for absences.

This professor has no communication and leadership. The class is discussion based. However, the professor cannot appropriately distribute in-class activity and results in chaos in class. In addition, you will never be able to reach this professor by email. He had to give me his phone number since hes so slow and unaccountable through email.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He rarely responds to these emails. His way of grading is very tricky and the exams are hard if you don't read the book. you HAVE to read the book. the only PHL class that has exams in person. he has in-class assignments which are graded. And the overall course is graded over a few things. Would not recommend it unless you love philosophy a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This dude was not great. He didn't know how to teach a classroom. Maybe he did better with the online format, but dear Lord, he wrote on the blackboard in cursive and abbreviated long philosophical terms. Taking notes was a nightmare. Ferkany can't keep up with emails at all, so office hours are literally the only option.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The worst professor that I have had in my entire 4 years at Michigan State University. Professor Ferkany grades subjectively based on his own opinions rather than assessing assignments based on grading criteria. He is seldom available for office hours, does not respond to emails, and writes his lectures on a chalkboard. Refuses to use projector.

Easily the worst professor I have ever had during my 4 years at MSU, extremely unclear grading expectations, outdated syllabus, does not follow it, very unorganized. This was not created as a 100 level class. He is rude, and condescending. His class notes are written in a terrible cursive that is really hard to read.

Professor Ferkany is awesome! I am in his class now and he gives engaging lectures and makes homework assignments and articles easily accessible. He is a tough grader, but as are most humanities and philosophy professors. The grading rubric is clear and it is one of the few courses I enjoy attending online.

The class itself and its material is not that hard but Matt made passing near impossible. Unreachable expectations. Had to learn everything from Youtube. Treats all written assignments like an Honors English/writing class. Gave me a 0 for a completed assignment. Has three tests big tests and without attendance points, you need all the luck possible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This is my favorite class. Great prof!

There is a ton of reading that he expects done in one night. He comes off as very rude at times. And, at the end of the semester, he gave me the wrong grade and when I confronted him about it, he got attitude with me. The class isn't too difficult, but the lecture is really boring and the professor isn't always pleasant.

Honestly Dr. Burns was better he was lowkey overhated but it was really easy to get a good grade. Class was enjoyable and not too difficult, lots of reading but it was nothing I couldn't handle after Dr. Burns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took WRA 202 with Kate. Very caring and funny, and is a great instructor. The class has a decent amount of work but is structured well to keep things even. She was always available to give feedback on my work, or if I needed advice on anything. Great prof, highly recommend!

Kate is super awesome! She made sure that there were plenty of assignments so that the midterm and final did not wreck our grades. She did an excellent job of balancing readings, translations, and general homework. She was always listening to and asking for feedback, and on several assignments she had us come up with a rubric together.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I actually had Dr. Kate for Latin 101, but that wasn't an option for this, but either way my love for her still stands. Dr. Kate was easily my favorite professor I have had at MSU. She truly adapted the course to the needs of her students and cared about what we were doing and wanted to know what was going on in our lives. 10/10! Love her!

Kate is so understanding, and such a nice professor and I recommend taking her 202 class. Attendance is mandatory but the classes are actually interesting and engaging, I actually found myself wanting to participate in class. I learned a lot for an entry level course and will definitely be taking another class with her.

Super caring and genuinely cares for her students. XA242 was a breeze with her and would definitely take other courses with her. You have a textbook that she recommends, but this can be found online very easily. The readings involved with the class are always connected, and she has a structured course. She has many opportunities for extra credit!

Intro to XA was engaging and she cared for student success. She values student feedback and is lenient with deadlines and grades. Be prepared for group projects, teamwork, and collaboration. Peer review makes up a decent portion of your grade. A little bit writing heavy but she's not a hard grader. Overall, enjoyable class!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took ALL, which is basically ISHALL but in Latin. Magistra Fedawa was the best teacher I have ever had by far. She encouraged discussion and would go on fascinating tangents when we asked questions. I learned so much about Roman history, language evolution, and culture. She was almost always free after class, and via emal.
Shes a very nice professor, and super understanding. I like how she had a clear outline of assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kate is such a nice person. I took a Grammar and Editing class with her and she was so knowledgeable and super fair when grading. It wasn't hard to get good grades, but you did have to put in the work for it. She is an awesome professor and I would highly recommend her.

Kate is a real gem. She's so understanding and caring to all her students. She' s definitely tough, especially if you're taking ISHALL, but its because she knows her students well and expects only the best out of them.
An amazing teacher, yes there is work but try and apply yourself. But at the end of the day, shes the nicest and she is understanding. (Dont take advantage of that though)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I enjoyed taking WRA with Dr. Fedewa. She's caring and is always willing to answer questions or provide feedback on a piece of writing. Her comments are always constructive and guide you in the right direction of a 4.0. If you are actively engaged with the material, discussion posts, and projects, it's truly difficult not to pass with a 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He tells stories in class and will put questions on the quizzes and exams about them. Quizzes and exams are open-note but if you don't go to class you won't get some of them right. There's no homework or assignments. He takes attendance using iClicker and you have to actually be in the room for it to count.

No homework was the only good part of this class. He tells stories in class and then puts them on the quizzes and exams without ever telling us the actual story or the meaning of them. His quiz questions can be extremely confusing and his lectures are so long and boring. Please find another ISS to take.

Guy obviously cares about his topics, but goes over the same things over and over again. Be prepared to learn a lot about the culture of capitalism. Tests are every week and are not well put together. Make sure to pay attention to his anecdotes they do often show up on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will be forced to sit there and listen to him talk for two hours and take non-stop notes. Every story he tells will be on the exams, so pay attention to the minor details. I went to every lecture and took notes on EVERYTHING and still couldn't understand the exams/quizzes. Overly hard and complicated wording.

The lectures are long and participation matters like Iclicker. There's no homework. Just weekly quizzes with open note open book and 3 exams and one of them gets dropped. The quizzes and exams are hard because he shares stories to which you have to pay attention too.
mandatory attendance in a small cramped seems like a good guy but not worth it i dropped

i do not advise taking this class attendance is mandatory the lectures are long and boring the classroom is small and cramped which gets hot ontop of it being in akers basically the corner of campus. if you do bad on one quiz your entire grade is cooked and there is a quiz every week of the semester then 3 heavy tests as well. take a different ISS!

Everything is open note open book, but some questions were based on random stories/ stuff which wasn't in the text or lectures. Very funny and passionate. Grading based solely on exams and quizzes, no homework.

A great guy who you can tell is deeply knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches. People complained about his accent, but it really is not that bad and didn't affect my understanding. Quizzes can be tricky but basically no safeguards against cheating on them, and somewhat entertaining lectures, although they do drag on sometimes.

No Homework so all you really have to do is show up for the 2 lectures Tuesday and Thursday. Quizzes every week and 4 Exams including the final but everything is open note. He is really passionate about his lectures but can be long and repetitive. Easy class if you just show up and take notes. Not hard to understand his accent IMO.

I have many bad words to say but this would get removed. Such a THICK accent. Almost unmarketable tomato level. I'm sure watching paint dry, filling out tax forms, or counting grains of rice would be more enjoyable than this. I would rather graze my square against concrete for 2 hrs every Tuesday & Thursday than listen to milk stories again.

2 hours of pure agony. I hated Tuesdays and Thursdays so much that I would come 25 min early to class just so I can find a seat in the back rows. Every single seat in the back 3 rows were filled. From milk stories to reading off the slideshow, you'll be more concentrated on trying to understand him than the actual lesson. Don't fall asleep either.

Professor Hussain is very obviously passionate about what he teaches which I greatly respect, however because of that the lectures can sometimes drag and be a bit boring. If you're interested in what he's teaching, it's going to be a great class. All tests/quizzes online with answers on quizlet.

Hate this professor and hate coming to this class. Very test-heavy, quizzes every Thursday, always trying to cram in boring content, and probably one out of his 30 stories was actually interesting. Easy 4.0, just do iClicker at your dorm and keep it open until he opens it. And copy and paste questions into search to find Quizlets with the answers.

I would say only take this course if you are really interested in learning about it, since the content is very lecture-heavy. You'll have a quiz or an exam every Thursday, so you really need to listen to what he says. Also, the extra credit is worth A LOT, so even if you think you are doing well in the class, just do it either way.

Talks nonstop. It's hard to keep up with his talking when he has an accent and talks fast. Quizzes are annoying. I would get an 8/10 half the time, and they wouldn't say what I got wrong. Overall, I don't like this class, and it dropped my GPA. I have 4.0 in every other class except for this one. Grade relies on exams, weekly quizzes, attendance.

The lectures were really well thought out, like you could tell he has been teaching this class for a long time. Beware the final exam is more difficult then the other exams and it can tank your grade. Hussain is not rude but he is socially awkward so just keep that in mind. Grading is handled by the ULAs who do not care so you will get no leeway.

He is such a sweet guy, some people struggle with his accent, but really it is not bad AT ALL. The quizzes come from the lectures, and you cannot get the information he says in class from the provided D2L slides. Also, he will tell stories, and he quizzes on the stories. Very kind just go to lecture and write detailed notes:)

Easy 4.0 Topics are pretty much common sense but interesting, however, a portion of your grade is iclicker attendance. The weekly quizzes and midterms ask many questions about the lectures specifically. No homework. Professor Hussain is great at lecturing and his stories are very entertaining. Quizlet is gonna be ur best friend. Easy to cheat lol
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, Fayyaz is a good professor. Likes to make jokes and does well staying neutral on political discussions. Note taking is critical. Some random stuff he says in lectures ends up on the exam. Textbooks are used but not really required. Just ask AI to provide overview notes and that'll suffice.

This class was the most boring thing to have ever existed since the dawn of time. Easy to cheat on tests and weekly quizzes, there are also ways around the attendance. The final exam was the same as every other exam. I never studied once and ended with a high grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is the most boring thing known to have ever existed on the planet earth. Sitting there is like watching paint dry. You can do well if you cheat, otherwise you'll get a mediocre grade. The final exam is the same as all the other ones, so it's chill and you won't have to worry at all. I would take it again since its so easy to do well.
Made my roommate crash out and i legit saw only pure hatred in his eyes for this man.

He was very confusing. He relied primarily on lectures and slideshows with vague bullet points. He couldn't clearly convey his message about the bullet points and offered no way to find his explanations outside of class. He was incredibly rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class. While the class is very lecture heavy, the lectures are so much fun, and you do learn a lot from this class. There are a lot of readings to do, but to be honest the readings are not hard and the professor goes over the readings in class in case you forget to read a chapter. The quizzes and exams are all open note.
It was very clear he was passionate about the subject and made it easier to be engaged as well. However, the only grades are quizzes and tests and the questions tend to be pretty specific.
I wouldn't look both ways before crossing the street on my way to class.

super long lectures, and if you dont take notes about every single thing he says, your going to fail the quiz. you have a quiz every single week, but theyre open note. he will clock you for not paying attention though, especially about your airpods.

I enjoyed the lectures, but the quizzes were confusing and needlessly difficult in comparison to the class material. Class is exclusively attendance(mandatory), quizzes(every Thursday), and exams(4 total, last one is cumulative). You get one exam drop, though. If you go to class every day and take notes on every single word he says you can do great

Very passionate about the course but if you don't pay attention in lecture it's hard to do amazing on the weekly quizzes and the exams. They ask very specific questions about what he said during lecture so make sure you pay attention. You will get called out if you sleep or are on your phone in class. Quizzes and exams were open note so not to bad.

I appreciate Dr. Hussain's passion for what he does, however, I would not recommend this class. The lectures are very boring and he WILL call you out for not paying attention. The quiz questions are very specific to what he says in lecture, so if you do not pay full attention for the whole two hours you will miss stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a fan of him. his lectures are boring and the only grades are quizzes and exams. Uses iclicker for attendance

This class was fine. No hw and all quizzes/exams are on quizlet, not 100% right all the time tho. He screams at you every lecture and makes you feel like a bad person for being able to go to college. He is unintentionally funny though. Heavy accent but easy to understand. Hard to 4.0 if you don't cheat. DON'T SKIP CLASS.
Pretty easy class if you listen to his lectures closely and take good notes. Everything is open note, and you get an exam drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I lived in Akers and had this class so it was so convenient. iClicker was geolocation so I didnt have to leave my room. All the exams and quizzes are on quizlet. I never went to class or studied and got a 4.0 so I would def recommend this class.
