Do not slack off, and do not leave your group members in the dust. You will do well if you try. Attendance is randomly graded, everything else are projects and peer evals.

Not a class you can slack in. Group projects are not easy and you can't coast by on your teammates. He gives tough criticism, but you can tell he wants students to turn in their best work. Helps you develop thicker skin, as his feedback after you present won't always be nice. Would not take this if you're looking for an easy elective. (ADV492)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People diss on Professor Taucher because you can't be lazy and expect a 4.0 in his class. That's why so many kids come on here to complain. Taucher is one of the most proven and knowledgeable professors at MSU, and he drops a ton of game in his lectures. If you put in real effort and actually care about the assignments, your grade will reflect it.

This class is a put in what you put you on. If you're only complaining about one of the few professors who will try to give you real-world experiences rather than an easy grade why even go into this industry? This guy has been at the top of the industry, and has seen it all.

This class is mostly graded on group projects that don't have anything to do with the lecture content. There was little direction given on the last two assignments that were the largest portion of the grade. He is very unapproachable, borderline disrespectful. He will humiliate your group in front of the class, and will make snarky comments. AVOID!

As a creative student who took his class you can tell he looks down on creatives. He poorly explains projects and when you ask questions he treats you like your dumb and can be disrespectful. The content I enjoy but he is unkind. I did fine in the class but dreaded going and dreaded talking to him. I've considered calling him out for rude behavior.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So tough it borders on unkindness. Will not accept late work no matter what the reason. Entire course is graded on group projects, the groups are randomly assigned at the beginning of the semester and if you have a bad group, you're screwed. Attendance checks are random and worth a large portion of the grade. He does not respond to emails as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was extremely unfair. Every grade was derived from group projects. If your group was not doing the work, his only advice was for you to complete the projects on your own. Not accomidating whatsoever. Random attendance checks. The lectures had nothing to do with the projects. I learned nothing in this class. It was extremely stressful.

Taucher is a harda*s. But for him it does kinda work. He is not afraid to chew you out in front of the class. The class is almost all group projects, but it's not terrible if your group is good. It can feel like you're actually working for an ad firm sometimes. Lots of great experience from a highly respected Advertising professional. just Be wary.

I took ADV 330 with Taucher, and I would recommend you find another teacher for this class. Random attendance checks, very poor at explaining assignment information, and if your group members are not there to help you may have the whole assignment on your back (like I did).

Professor Taucher is a great professor and I rated him so highly because he is one of the few professors who gives you knowledge and experience that will 100% be applicable in the real world and your career. Although his projects and teaching style can be a bit tough if you put in the effort he will give it right back and make sure you do well.
The exams were extremely hard as they were fill-in-the-blank taken directly from the slides. But he made the midterm and final extra credit and that saved my grade.

He's got a bit of an attitude, and can be passive aggressive at times. However, if you really apply yourself to the course, he'll recognize it (at least he did with me), and will work with you. He really cares about the material and teaching it, so as long as you reciprocate that back to him, you'll do fine.
Did not help a brother out in time of need.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's questionable on how Greg would deal with situations. At times he'd be a hot head/give sassy remarks,unprofessional towards his students. He'd blow-up on students or groups and at times because of how they approached his projects with no guidance given. The guy is literally passive aggressive. RED FLAG: Take a different section class.

I was put into a very bad group when this class is very much group project based. When other students were not doing their job, he was unsupportive and would not offer me any additional help despite me having RCPD accommodations. He told me that it was just bad luck and the only thing he was willing to do is let me do all the projects by myself.

Taucher is the worst professor I have ever had. Taucher and I were in advertising association at MSU , he used stories from the meetings in his lectures, and twisted the information. I don't trust anything he says about his "experience in the field". His lectures were irrelevant to the assignments. His feedback was useless. Avoid if at all possible

Prof. Taucher is a good ADV professor. He has some pretty amazing stories from his experience in the field. I did not like how his slides provided very very little notes for us to take. His exams are all written, but he gives the questions ahead of time so that you can prepare. Overall a good prof who needs improvement.

This class is based off on group-work. There are no exams or quizzes, just group papers and long assignments due frequently. Attendance is randomly taken. Due to this structure, you don't learn or study for anything. Don't get your hopes up- you will learn nothing in this class. Lectures painfully drag on.

I had him for ADV 330. One of the worst classes I have ever taken. He does random attendance which sucks. His lecture material doesn't relate to the projects at all. You have a small amount of time to do the last two projects. I learned nothing and got so stressed out over excel. If you don't know how to use excel goodluck

The first assignment I got 100% on and positive feedback, but on the past couple assignments I havent done as well. I use my first assignment as a guideline to help with the other ones since he seemed to like that one. I was wrong and the feedback he gives is more like personal digs rather than constructive criticism. Not a fan :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Prof. Taucher for ADV 330 over the summer and loved it! Amazing professor, if I ever had any questions he would email me back right away, he really cares about students and wants you to do well! On top of that I also learned a lot about AD Management! Take this Professor, he's awesome!

If you don't know anything about philosophy this class can be difficult. He does make you buy a textbook but it helps with understanding the texts and you can use it on exams. You aren't graded on a lot: 2 midterms, a final, and random in-class activities to get you in class. But Dr. Grey is amazing, would take his class again in a heartbeat.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty boring, but if you're into sentience/consciousness topics you might still find the material interesting. Grading feels harsh, a 91% is only a 3.5 and you can't make up missed in-class assignments. Overall, interesting content but not the most engaging class or flexible policies.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes that I have taken! Dr. Grey knows his stuff and is willing to answer anything you throw at him. Weekly papers, but: Go. To. Class. Not only will this help you understand the content better, but he does random in-class activities which can help your grade. Not a Philosophy major but I will be taking more of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: no real assignmets except in class discussions and weekly deliberations which is easy. no quizzes or exam except midterm and final so u rly gotta study for those 2 but he makes a review to follow. great teacher love him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: easy class as long as you actually study for the midterm and the final
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class. He doesn't teach you anything more than the 274-page book does, along with the 4 other books in the class. You can't use outside resources to study because it's so based on niche books. He has 2 exams covering 60% of your grade. Also, the recitation pretty much exists solely to turn in your homework. Do not take this class...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Grey is an amazing professor and knows what he is lecturing on, attendance is mandatory (especially for reviews before exams) if you want to receive a good grade in this class. Annotations every week which are about 1 page and are easy to write and definitely help you understand the material better, and he hand grades each one with feedback. :)

Professor Grey knows what he is talking about. The material is very difficult to understand without a philosophy background, and the tests are very difficult but Professor Grey dedicates a lecture to group study before each exam. Other than the difficult material, I enjoyed the class.

Genuinely the most boring class and professor. This class sucked. His exams were in person closed note (LA, SA, MC, TF) over lectures and readings. He has like 40 book requirements and all dumb/expensive. Readings are super long as well. Do not take him for IAH. There are way more interesting professors, classes that are easier for this credit.

Probably my favorite class I've taken so far, really interesting materials covered in a fun way. The class is super enjoyable if you're groupmates are also interested in the topic, would def recommend.

Prof. Grey has engaging lectures but if you zone out for even a second you are done for. Discussions in class aren't mandatory and attendance is taken via in-class group assignments where you record what you talked about. Fair graded papers and curved exams. Content heavy, you can scrape by without reading if you attend the lectures religiously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend Prof. Grey. He's very understanding and genuinely cares about his students. There are random in-class assignments, but they usually aren't difficult. The exams are very fair (only midterm & final). There are lots of class discussions, but he never requires you to talk if you don't want to. Overall a great professor.

Really chill guy, good takes, spells out explanations well, but there is a lot of random quizzes and difficult problem sets. Attendance is not mandatory but you will most certainly be lost if you have a choppy attendance. You have to stay engaged to maintain a good grade.

He is, by far, one of my most favorite professors. He is extremely accommodating if you ask for an extended deadline, and he tries to meet the students where they are at when it comes to understanding. I genuinely debated on dropping this class when I had walked in the first day, but I am so glad I didn't.

He posted lecture videos which were extremely helpful and clear. I would say the textbook isn't mandatory, but it was useful to have for further information to write the papers. There were a total of 4 papers to write for the semester, but they were all less than an 800 word word limit. Overall, he's a nice guy and a very good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor, love talking to him and learning from him. He keeps his classes interesting and I'd definitely recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While he seems like a cool dude, I really did not enjoy his class. A majority of the points are in 10 assignments, which each weight about 5% of the grade for each question. So, if you mess up one you're gonna have a bad time. The course itself was fairly boring and I did appreciate his efforts to try and make it less so.

Professor Grey is such a cool guy that it almost makes this class worth it. He's sarcastic and funny and encourages debates. But it's extremely difficult material, with a problem set every other week and random in class quizzes. There's only a written midterm and final in terms of exams. A 92% is a 4.0 which is really hard to achieve

Prof. Grey's powerpoints don't take away from his lecture. The relevancy of his arguments and his snarky sense of humor keeps one invested. The clarity in his communication is evident in his concise syllabus, midterm survey, and when he allows students to bring in their own arguments to debate in class. Reach out for help and the class is easy.
Great professor, very nice and understanding. Clearly loves what he does and explains everything very fluently. I would love to take his class again.

AMAZING PROF TAKE HIM FOR 222! PHY 222 is a hard class, but Prof Gulyuz makes it amazing. He actually lectures before class, and will always sit down and talk with you about assignments, even outside of his office hours. I genuinely think he is what helped me pass this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Gulyuz was amazing. PHY 221 is set up horribly, but he takes the extra time to explain concepts and go over problems. He is always willing to meet outside of class and wants his students to succeed. If you study hard this class is manageable, just be prepared for bad grades on labs because they give no rubric.

Professor Gulyuz is kind and helpful, the best physics professor for 221. The class itself is set up poorly and grading takes weeks, along with harsh grading on the labs without true instruction of what needs to be included. It's not his fault the class is set up like it is. Take it with him, his sections constantly had the highest exam averages.

Good Professor overall, attendance matters for in-class group participation grades. Pretty much all group work aside from exams. 2 drops for the in-class portion. Relatively difficult course if you don't prepare well. Run pretty well but exams and formal labs take 2 weeks and sometimes potentially longer to grade.

kerim is sooooo nice and lovely and its not his fault that the class is set up in the WORST WAY POSSIBLE. you can tell he wants to give more to his students and help them more but unfortunately the curriculum for the PHY 221 course does not allow it. always has the highest class averages on exams so def take him over anyone else.

Dr.Gulyuz is the best physics professor I have ever had. He exudes girl dad energy and came to every class with a beaming smile and passion for his job. He strives to support all of his students! The class is still difficult, due to the inexperienced TA's, but this man made it bearable. No amount of words can describe how amazing Dr.Gulyuz is.

Dr. Gulyuz is probably the best professor to take physics with, he always lectured the class despite it being a flipped classroom and would always give the best help on formal labs and homework. This class still sucks though, the grading is super tight and formal labs are graded by TAs. Exams are not bad if you study the practice exam, good luck!

His classes always have the highest gpa out of all sections. If you pay attention in class and actually participate you should do just fine, and even if you don't fully understand something he does an great job in explaining it. The labs are graded rather dubiously, however that's a fault more of how the class is run and is outside of his control.

Flipped classroom but Dr. Gulyuz goes over the content. Terrible class but this is the professor to take it with. I learned everything before the exam from homework questions and practice exams, using youtube for additional explanations. Take your formal labs to help rooms to do well, otherwise grading sucks. Dr. Gulyuz was the only good thing.

This course sucks but he is probably the best professor for it. He explains more than the other professors but the course is still really tough. If you can avoid taking it, definitely do but it is more convenient since lab and lecture are in one class. Difficult because there is no clear rubric and material is terrible. Good Luck! Ur gonna need it!

EM is challenging, but Kerim has this great strategy of taking a challenging Griffiths problem and solving it with the class using iClicker at successive stages of the problem then reviews the correct reasoning immediately after. Thus, he monitors the class understanding effectively and adjusts his lecture accordingly. Very kind, highly recommend!

Flipped classroom, students basically teach students, with only readings to back up learning and in class activity. Formal labs are the most horrendously graded material, they have no rubric just a "general" rubric but are nitpicky about everything. No strong exam studying material, only material is to review all taught material and past exams.

I had Professor Gulyuz for 221 and 222 and he is such a kind an understanding guy. His lectures were better than most of the other physics professors and it showed by the exam grades. He was very good at explaining things and helped out students where he could. Very approachable.
Gulyuz was one of the worst profs I've had. Slides were taken from previous professors, exams were very difficult, and it wasn't clear ahead of time what to study. Not a good lecturer.

I would highly recommend Professor Kerim for physics 221 & 222. He is hands down the most approachable and kind professor I have ever had at MSU. His classes usually always have the best averages, & I believe it's because he's so helpful and interactive with his students. He will explain things to you as many times as you need. Highly recommend.
TRUST NOBODY, did you guys eat lunch?, talk to your friends, measure with your forearm, this one is easy

Professor Gueye is great for teaching about the material, but not applying it to math at all. This class was a headache completely. Multiple problems with homework and quizzes. Not to mention there was very little interaction on piazza. Changed the quizzes format 3 different times.

Firstly, Paul was an amazing professor, him as an instructor, was a positive of the class. However, everything else was nothing but a headache. The class structure itself is completely terrible. Piazza feedback was MINIMAL. The lectures teach you what you need to know, but not HOW to apply it. I gave above a 4.0 effort but got a 3.5 instead.

Prof is hilarious and enthusiastic about teaching.  Lectures are abundant and do cover the material, but unfortunately, the organization of the class was awful.  Complete lack of online communication via Piazza and technical errors were common.  Enjoyed the teaching itself, but those issues make it hard to improve my rating.

Took PHY 183 P-Cubed with Professor Paul and nothing but good about him and the class. He cares for students and wants them to succeed. The class material is in-class problems that you solve with your group and the help of the ULA's. Homework is a big part of your grade so I would make sure to do well on them. Doing badly on exams isnt the end all.
Professor Gueye is great. Physics is hard but he actually cares and teaches. You definitely need to put in the work though and read the textbook.

This professor was pretty good! The class was lecture heavy, so pay attention to those if you want to do well on the homework and quizzes. The professor is sympathetic to personal life events, & helpful outside of class. Attendance technically wasn't mandatory but iClicker questions take place each class. Shared some helpful life advice as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Das Gupta; she makes sure you understand the content and even gives visual aids. Her midterm was open-note, and she even let us redo our first essay after she graded it and left comments. Her lectures are filled with examples that help us understand the content; just be ready to participate, but her office hours help!
Tons of reading and really rude. Hard to understand with her accent and always makes mistakes when speaking. wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor was amazing! I was out for a month due to illness, and she was extremely accommodating and helpful with me and had great feedback. There's a lot of reading and work, but it's worth it and I definitely feel like I learned a lot.

Professor Das Gupta was an incredible professor. She gives great feedback and is a very approachable person. One of the nicest people within the James Madison College. If you have the chance to take her class, take it.

201 is all lecture based, and Das Gupta did an amazing job. Her lectures were fascinating and very informative. All exams and papers were easy and fit the content. Das Gupta put together an amazing team of lecturers, and the topics were diverse. From the U.S. to India, from Brazil to Syria, Das Gupta covered interesting stuff and did a great job.

Das Gupta is the best teacher I have ever had here at MSU so far, and will probably sustain that role for the years coming. She is not only good at teaching and making sure we understand what is happening in class, she cares about her students and their well-being. Would 1000% recommend taking any class you can with her.

Professor Das Gupta is an outstanding professor. She makes an effort to get to know each of her students personally. She has a way of explaining tough concepts in concise, clear ways. She offers great feedback on essays and goes the extra mile to meet with students outside of class. I'd highly recommend taking this class with SDG.

When subbed in for Prof. Elmo, my grade went from bad to good. She was so accessible outside of class and willing to help. When asking for feedback, she went through my paper step by step with me over what she thought I could improve on, it was amazingly helpful when it came down to polishing the draft of my essay. Overall, super caring and helpful

Gupta is a wonderful teacher and person! She came in for Elemo the second half of the semester and the vast difference between those two teachers is insane. I felt more comfortable participating in this class and as if my opinions mattered and she did very well at teaching us the material and to improve our understanding.

As one of my first professors for the major I am pursuing, I was inspired by her and this class. She is very intelligent and wants us to understand these concepts and how applicable they are to our lives. She will make you a better reader and writer. She makes an interdisciplinary study very intriguing and inspiring.

Professor Das Gupta is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. She's tough but it motivates you to work hard and do your best. She does an amazing job at taking complicated theorhetical framework and making it accessible to students. I also think the case studies she chooses are extremely relevant to her work and the CCP major.
Sweetest guy ever. Cares so much about his students and the communities he works with. He is extremely understanding of student circumstances and works super hard.

Bro he is obsessed with himself it's kinda insane. He rambles on and on, forces us to read websites about him and videos WITH A PAYWALL. He starts playing good songs and then stops right before the best part. He wears performative hats.

Biggest humble bragger I've ever met. Teaches a prison poetry class in which students go to a juvenile detention center and an all male prison. Very interesting of course, however throughout your journey Guriellmo is going to do his best to drill into your mind what a great person he is for what he's doing. Kind of gross and feels self righteous.

Guillermo is a very good professor who is very committed to his community engagement work. He cares deeply about his students' success and did an amazing job facilitating the incarcerated poetry collaboration project. One of my favorite professors so far.

I absolutely loved having Dr. Gurinskaya! The class was async and there were weekly assignments due Sundays. She graded fair, and laid out clear expectations. You do have to pay for and frequently use the book to pass, though. She also takes forever to reply to emails (most take over a week to reply back to). But she does grade things pretty quick!

She makes everything very clear on what needs to be done. She gives lots of extra credit opportunity  on just about every assignment. She gives you study questions that are almost identical to the test questions. You do have to do presentations, so there is that. Lots of respect tho, cuz she makes it easy to succeed as long as you give some effort.

Only homework you have is 4 research assignment papers which are due around the exams taken in this course. I feel she only reads some of them whereas one paper I would receive a 100 next a 68. Attendance was not mandatory and you would receive EC. for showing up. Not horrible because you could do everything at home for no penalty.
Beware, she does NOT do extra credit nor does she round grades. Otherwise, I liked her and she's fair but unfortunately she would not give me a 4.0 even though I was off by a single point.
Great professor! Very understanding & flexible! I took her course during my 1st semester in the MS Law Enforcement Intell & Analysis program :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was fine, and pretty easy butttt hardly anything is being graded and if you don't do well on one assignment/ exam, it WILL impact your grade. with that being said, the exams were okay, I mostly got high 80s and I was fine. Weekly assignments I'm not entirely sure if she reads but they are also not hard to complete (less than 200 words).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of writing assignments (aprx. 400 words each), exams are directly from the reading. She does not provide any lectures, you learn simply by reading the book/teaching yourself. Assuming this is a required class for you I would suggest taking it online with Gurinskaya, 4.0 is definitely attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was an online course and I don't think she really grades the weekly writing assignments, I've always gotten 100% and no comments on them. Exams come straight from the book. Take her, she's pretty easy.

Good class, and professor. Interaction was minimal due to it being online. The class was set up that you'd have quizzes, easy opinion-based writings, and discussions. The quizzes were 100% based off the book so be prepared to buy the book in order to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Super easy class with weekly assignments of up to 200 words on common sense questions and tests are pulled directly from book so you can Control F

Ricardo is one of the most wholesome professors at MSU and if someone tells you otherwise they're 100% lying to you! 

He is such an inspirational, caring, and understanding professor and cares for all of his students and their work! He always gave honest feedback and gave good and honest real world advice for those going into the industry too!

THE sweetest professor ever. extremely caring and is always more than willing to help. Very laid back, you can turn in work whenever as long as it's turned in like a week before the final class. Can't express how much I recommend his class.

Ricardo's lectures are always so inspirational, and his friendliness truly engages people to try their hardest in his class. He also shares his experiences of working in the industry, which are incredibly helpful. Homework is light and fun if you enjoy drawing. I heavily recommend taking his courses!

I really loved the organization of this course, and Ricardo definitely made the class enjoyable. I would highly recommend him as he knows a lot about the gaming industry and always gives good feedback.

Professor Guimaraes was great, and for CAS 116 he graded us on participation and understanding of concepts rather than artistic ability. He also taught us a lot about the games industry in general, as the beginning of every class was spent answering student questions about pretty much any topic.

Ricardo's CAS 116 was a fun and simple (1 small HW per lecture) class that I learnt a lot in. It's graded on how you understand concepts, not how well you can draw. He also did a QnA session at the start of every class and I learnt a lot about the games industry through it. He also gave feedback to students and was very approachable. Awesome guy!
He's fine tbh

I originally made a bad review on Professor Gupta. After further consideration, I understand him a lot more. He comes from a great place, definitely has a few issues to work out in the coursework, like the Quizzes being super heavy, and in my opinion drastically different from lecture. Not at all a bad man and really does want to see you learn/win.

Hes not that bad. "Coding on chalkboard" is good because it feels like he is writing it with us and easier to follow. "Errors" that he makes while writing code are very small like spelling something wrong. Grade is based 60% off of weekly quizzes. Lots of extra credit. Sometimes he is grumpy and crashes out most of the time he is pretty funny

A lot of the hate could be mitigated due to his first time teaching. Yes, he can improve on the lectures, and yes the blackboard is tedious. More than half your grade is basically free, all you have to do is the projects and the labs. The quizzes are definitely difficult, and will require thorough reading. Not as bad as they say if you just work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not as bad as ratings say. I've you've taken a coding class before this class should be easy, if not, it'll be a lot harder and you'll have to do a lot more out of class to learn the material. Quizzes are worth a massive chunk of your grade for no reason. Use the TA's to teach you cause they're the most helpful.

Wasn't as bad as people say. Projects and labs were free points. Chalkboard's annoying, but he gives class-wide extra credit for catching his mistakes. Quizzes are tough—I got 60–70s but will still 4.0 thanks to the end of semester bonus project. Not the best prof, but easy to pass.

Pretty chill and lenient with grading. Ok at lecturing SOMEtimes, but often easy to get lost. Homework & lab relies on figuring concepts out on your own and if you have no coding experience that's essentially impossible. TA teaches more in 5 minutes than he does in 40. Extremely disorganized & clearly an inexperienced professor. 

"Oh dear" indeed

About half the grade comes from weekly quizzes, which can be tough if you don't read the recommended textbook. Isn't the greatest, but isnt as bad as everyone says. He isnt too organized, and uses a chalkboard. He makes mistakes, but when pointed out, he gives the whole class extra credit. Really isn't that bad, but def learn on your own. Use chat!

Attendance is not mandatory, only gives bonus points. Labs are mandatory (highest you can get is 50% w/o attendance). I like the chalkboard, it's like he's writing the code with us and lets us learn by catching mistakes. Quizzes covers textbook content. Those who say that it's on stuff he hasn't taught just haven't read the textbook.
Very test heavy and not clear on what tests will be on
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For a computer science class, Gupta loves to NOT use his computer. He writes on a chalkboard that's barley visible, commonly gets his own examples wrong, and he takes attendance via a piece of paper that he usually forgets to pass out. The quizzes don't cover what he does and I hope I never have to take another of his classes again.

BEWARE if you take this class, be ready to read code off a chalk board. Ayra, is so funny that he sometimes he doesn't know his own answers. He also has weekly quizzes that everyone fails because the quizzes are topics that he doesn't even cover. Attendance is also mandatory with a piece of paper that you need to sign and he forgets to give it out.

Professor Gupta is quite the guy. Mandatory attendance, and if you miss two quizzes you receive a zero in the course. We didn't have a syllabus until the second class and since then we've had 6? iterations. He is not very good at lecturing or explaining, you won't be able to see his code and even if you could you wouldn't be able to read it. GL!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super sweet professor, the class had LOTs of extra credit + you didnt have to take the final if you did good on your other exams. Super easy class and very interesting. Worth taking !
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were incredibly boring. Not engaging, I found it hard to pay attention in class. 2 -hour class is too long. Exams are manageable if you study. Honestly, going to class was pointless; you can do the iClicker from any location, and her teaching is just reading off slides that are on D2L. Lots of extra credit that saved my grade!

Not only is this one of the few psych classes where attendance is mandatory, but ofc the majority of your grade is her long tests that btw she writes herself. Her lectures are so boring and disengaging that 30 minutes feels like the entire two hour lecture which umm is already pretty insufferable with her laughing every three seconds.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I will say she is very nice and keeps our lectures fun. I had taken her for PSY 101 and she made the 2hr class nice and not boring and gave us a break in the middle to stretch and go to the bathroom. I will say the one downside was that attendance is mandatory but she is understanding if you need to miss.

I did not attend lecture and got an A, the study guides are truly your bff! It is pretty important to show up to labs though or you'll be lost. The most annoying thing was TAs grading differently, and during finals week there is both a final exam AND paper due within less than 24 hours of each other, but you get 1 exam drop which can be the final.
set up not good, slideshows r uninteresting and not engaging, an exam the class before the final exam and paper due the night before the final

attendance is not mandatory but I did very well in this class and attended most lectures and know some who did not attend and did pretty bad. Also just depends on how you learn. Professor Seidman is great. Honestly the TAs are what bothered me the most as they all grade differently.

Dr. Seidman gives good lectures with plenty examples. Her exams are in person and based off her slides. As long as you study her slides and exam study guide, you'll be good. There's 4 midterms and a cumulative final, but you can drop your lowest exam grade (including the final). Most of your grade will come from labs (attend and do assignments)

Ms. Griffin seemed like a very good professor, but in this huge lecture it was hard to keep up with the fast-paced environment. As a freshman, I would say that you will be okay taking this class if you at least took pre-calc in high school and attend almost all of the lectures and recitations.

Ms. Griffin was great! Always very positive and easy to talk to. Explained things fairly well and color-coded almost all of her work. Only expected you to know the things you should know going into a college math course. Gave us so much extra practice like her own additional exam review & answer key.

Literally the worst class I've ever taken in my life. Profesor Griffin is extremely harsh and shows lack of care for students. There's a good chunk of homework, but it's only worth 10% of your grade. I can't believe I even passed this class.

I would do everything to get out of this course. To her credit she does give you a lot of resources, but her lectures are extremely fast paced, and it's difficult to comprehend the material she gives you. The bigger issue is the structure of the course as recitation is basically just a place to take exams and test tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Griffin is very quick in lectures and follows the syllabus strictly. After reviewing the videos, webwork, and practice problems on D2L, my grades improved. I would highly recommend doing all the possible "learn it" and "practice it" objectives in D2L. She does teach new material right before an exam when the new material isn't on the exam :/

Won't talk to you about grades, tells you not to email her over many things, talks really fast and you can't understand her, is basically the only one who teaches this class at available times and is so bad I had to take her class twice.
She is very nice and super outgoing. A very fast-paced class but if you come in with prior knowledge you should be totally fine.

Griffin is nice and approachable, but she moves quickly through lectures. She speaks fast and only leaves notes on the screen for 15 seconds. The course includes WebWork hw and quizzes every recitation. Unlike other professors, she rarely holds math exam reviews, so I usually attend Allen's review sessions. I would definitely recommend Allen.

Although it is a fast paced course, Ms. Griffan does a great job throughly explaining material and her videos on D2L and extremely helpful. Go to your lectures and put in the work outside of class and you'll be fine (coming from someone not good at math).

RUN from this professor. She rushes through everything in class and in her videos, but at least you can pause those. She solves problems without explaining the steps or giving students time to try them. Recitations were basically just quizzes and tests.
Please for your sake avoid at all costs.

Talks too fast during lectures and has NO REVIEW during any of the lectures. Even when an exam is coming up, she will be teaching new information you need to know that wont even be on the upcoming quiz/exam. Be ready for a quiz or exam every week. Wouldn't recommend.

The class of MTH 103 itself is bad, not necessarily the professor, but regardless she did fly through the lessons VERY quickly, according to MSU-grades there was a 25% fail/drop-out rate last semester, i got through the course with a 2.5, although barely. Unless your already very comfortable with Algebra, you will likely struggle.
Very clear explanations during lectures and videos. Very strict with syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Ms. Griffin's a nice lady, she is engaging in the lectures. But she talks very fast and seems to rush through things. Some units are easier than others but attending the lecture is a massive help to understanding the content.
You WILL feel like you're drowning. She moves too fast to understand a thing. You're better off skipping lectures and teaching yourself, honestly.

Griffin herself is a good and nice person, but teaching MTH 103 is hard because there is so much content to shove into one semester. avoid taking 103 with all you possibly can, and if you must take it, just know it will be your hardest course even if you were decently proficient in math in highschool.

I thought Dr. Griffin was a great instructor for a beginning math course. She has good lectures and is very involved during class. Although attendance isn't require, all the quiz and exam information are from lecture, so I would advise you to go if you want to pass.

I took her MTH 103 lecture/recitation and I failed. I retook it this semester with a different professor and got a 4.0. I missed a quiz because I was sick. I went to spectrum and got a note. I sent it to her and her response was that I needed to be hospitalized in order to retake the quiz. Doesn't teach, just has you READ about MATH.
Very kind teacher. Her videos are very helpful. Don't be afraid to attend her office hours to get extra help if you are struggling or just have questions!

Attend her office hours!!! Ms. Griffin is there to help you and is willing to help you learn if you put in the effort. I hate math but Ms. Griffin helped me find the confidence in myself to do well and learn. For a hard course she is a very kind and understanding teacher. She will push her students, but she does care about how you do.

God forbid you miss one class you are behind for the whole semester. She is a nice woman but is not very good at teaching. She just writes down everything barely explains it at least enough for others to understand. You better hope you get a good TA because that is your only chance of understanding this class.

Did not attend one single lecture and still managed a 3.5. The videos are really helpful, as well as the recitation activities, reviews and worksheets. Not a complicated class if you have taken algebra 2 or precalc/calc in high school. Dropped one of the quizzes (every week during recitation). easy to talk to outside of class and my TA was perfect
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and take MTH103 A and B. I know more people who failed this class than I do who passed, including myself. Second round taking it, and it is hardly easier. Quizzes every Friday, four exams, tough grading criteria, and SO MUCH HW! Unless you pick up math like a second nature I DO NOT recommend.

I missed one class at the beginning of the semester and never was able to get back on track because she covered entire units in each lecture. She speeds through it like she's got places to be. There were several occasions where she straight-up invented new math terms. She uploads videos explaining each lesson on D2L, but they're absolutely useless.

Mth 103 is a hard class for anyone, Professor Griffin does the best she can. She cares about how you are doing and cares about the class. She wants you to pass and gives you the best tips in the short amount of time that is given for lectures. My TA is terrible tho.

yes I did poorly but she was a professor that I couldn't learn from. I had my friends in high math classes help me and they said the way she thought was backwards. I would highly recommend you pick a different professor

The course is hard(multiple homework assignments due weekly, quiz/exam at almost every recitation,  lots of notes). Although it can be challenging, Ms. Griffin is so sweet and helpful if you take advantage of her as a resource. I went to her office hours every week, and she always made sure I understood the concepts.
If you want to pass don't take this class. Doesn't explain anything, goes over 5+ lessons in 50 mins. Quiz every Friday.
If you can't deal with a fast paced environment, go for 103A&B
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: JUST DO YOURSELF A FAVOR AND TAKE MATH 103A&B. Professor Griffen was okay, but she didn't really teach, just gave us skeleton notes. I'm begging you to just take a&b. All the teachers are like this.

Not good. Goes WAY too fast and does not explain concepts thoroughly. I along with other students just watched the videos on D2L and basically learned the material ourselves. Very thankful my TA was helpful and knew what he was doing and actually explained the concepts to us. Just bad. Terrible. Would not recommend this professor to ANYONE.

She's very sweet but also knows what she's doing, she'll do pop up attendances if she sees a lack of students in her lectures, and likes to interact with us. I would take her classes again for sure. The main issue I have with her is that she goes fast, which sometimes isn't her fault, and her d2l can be hard to navigate through.
Doesn't teach or explain. She simply just tells and writes it down. This class was absolutely horrible

The class material is incredibly difficult, especially for an entry-level class, though that isn't Professor Griffin's fault. She talks SUPER fast, and doesn't go back to repeat problems, so your attention better be focused.

Dr. Griffin gets a lot of unnecessary slander because she teaches mostly freshmen. Dr. Griffin's teaching style is very clear and makes sense if you go to class. Attendance is mandatory if you want to pass, but I got away with missing a few and was fine. All tests are in person, paper pencil, during recitation. Easy to reach outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Griffin is a very kind and funny professor and I really enjoyed her personality. However, I feel as though maybe it's the combination of her talking fast + her teaching a very fast paced course that made me struggle. Quizzes are nearly every week, and they don't look at all like the webwork/notes. Grading policy is very good though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This lady is the goat. I never even had her as a professor, but she was the one who created all of the online notes for my class. She went through the lessons really well in the videos. My teacher often went too fast with the notes in class, so it was nice having her online lessons to help me understand much easier.

Griffin is very nice, but as someone who excelled in math before college, this class was unreasonably hard, especially in terms of quizzes. We go over topics very fast and she often skips review problems that would have made homework and quizzes so much easier. Most people don't even show up because the online resources teach much better.
Never again.

This class gets a bad rap because it's taken mostly by freshman who are new to college classes. Don't get me wrong, it's fast paced, so in order to succeed you need to put in the work. Go to office hours weekly. Go to the math learning center! Ask questions in recitation. The ULA's are there to help! Mrs. Griffin wants to see her students succeed..

Griffin is a very nice lady, she definitely cares for her students and is willing to accomodate, but she is not a great teacher. I really struggle with math and I'm worried about failing, although I frequently go to lectures and office hours. Her exams and quizzes are really difficult and sometimes not what the review material is like.

MTH 103 has quizzes or tests every week during recitation. Griffin is kind but it's a huge lecture with like 100 people so don't think about asking questions until your recitation. She loves what she does but goes through extremely quick, and rarely goes back if you missed anything. Good luck but it's college algebra so it's not too hard.

Ms. Griffin was a very straight forward gal.  She made it clear that her job was to simply teach.  There is a quiz every week in recitation, so don't miss it.  There is a lot of partial credit offered on exams and quizzes so write down everything you can for more points.  It is homework heavy but if you get it all done it helps boost your grade.

although she seems like a very genuine person, it is very hard to understand this class if you are not a math person. she moves extremely fast, and you take notes the entire class period. there is a quiz almost every week, and they are tough. when taking notes, there is no explanation, you are just expected to know how to do the problems.

Math 103 should not be this challenging. I passed this class by 3 points. The professor was nice and willing to help but her quizzes and exams were never like the homework or the reviews. Honestly, save yourself the money and choose a different professor, other classes seemed to have a better success rate...
Very nice, funny professor but she is not a very good instructor. Her lectures are frustrating and confusing. I found myself learning better when i taught it to myself.

I am not good at math to begin with, however even my friends who were good at math struggled in this course. Ms.Griffin is so kind and funny but her course is difficult, again math is not my strongest category. Be sure to review class notes, and pay attention to the reviews given by TA before quizzes and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Taking this class Fall of 2023 there was an issue with resources available to help all the students who were struggling. Just look up this teacher's average grades the past few years on msugrades, the average never went above a 3.0. At this point, this is a curriculum issue, grading. Im sure she is a good woman at heart just not meant to teach.

This class gives no credit other than homework, quizzes, and very heavily weights exams. There is no credit given for attendance or participation. Professor moves incredibly quickly and does not stop for questions. Does lecture notes byd and her hand blocks the projector camera. No time to copy notes. Very challenging if not a math person.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For the love of God be weary of taking this class. I came in as a confident freshman and left as a broken man. While Mrs. Griffin is nice and caring as a person, the math curriculum along with her lectures is bound to fail you.
Good luck!  Hardest class at MSU

Don't take this class unless you hate yourself It's so hard and the professor makes it even worse. She is a horrible teacher in lectures she goes way too fast it's almost impossible to keep up with her. There is way too much homework for one student to keep up on. This class is so time-consuming there is also a quiz every Friday.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not a bad teacher, just teaching a hard class. Homework multiple times a week, with quizzes and exams every Friday. Extremely fast passed class making it very hard to understand the topics enough to pass the quizzes.
Her lectures are very fast-paced. A lot of homework on Webwork and weekly quizzes. Great person, she's just a tough teacher.

Nice lady but with class she goes through problems very fast and doesn't quite explain them well. Class is test heavy. Tricky test problems worth a lot of points for short amount of questions. If u r an incoming freshman, I would honestly take Susan Allen's class.I had to go to her lecture just to better understand the work. She's much better.
She was just mean
lecture heavy and test heavy

Dropped this class about midway through the semester as it was horrible. This professor speeds through lectures and will on the regular ignore students raising their hands. The homework she assigned was completely different than other classes of 103 and much more difficult. I had an easier time in my asynchronous 103 than here.

The class is very fast-paced, but she offers office hours for multiple days every week. Listen... you need to go get help outside of class, that's the only way you will pass this class. Overall, she is a very nice lady.

Attendance is mandatory and she will go out of her way to make sure it is taken again if too many people leave the room. A large portion of your grade relies on the 4 Exams (granted you drop one). She allows crib sheets during exams for examples, definitions, etc. Personality wise, she's a nice lady, but you have to be on top of your work.

Professor Griffin is a sweetheart - nevermind all the freshmen reviewing her. As a junior, she is amazing. She talks fast because the courseload is heavy - she stays after class to help and discusses everything in detail as needed. She offers a ton of office hours to help if you need it, too. Reach out if you need help!
Her class was much more difficult than the other math 103 sections
she talks so fast its almost impossible to keep up with lectures while filling out notes
Ruthless- she will rip you apart. Be prepared to work hard.

Goes way too fast and will not slow down or answer any questions during lecture. Homework load is absurd considering this is entry level algebra. No make ups and no retakes. She will not do a single thing to help you pass her class... in fact she will make it easy to fail. Tests are difficult and her video reviews don't help in the slightest.
she goes too fast and will not allow makeups for tests/quizzes even if you are sick.

She goes quickly through the lecture. You need to pay attention because like all other math courses you will need to be able to apply the information you learned to other problems. She makes some jokes in class that keep you engaged. If you have trouble with pacing they offer 103A and 103B for a reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Griffin is definitely my hardest professor. You would think that college algebra would be easy, right? This is a very hard class, even though I go to every lecture, I complete all of my homework, and spend nearly 2.5 hours in the math learning center every night. She is nice, but not very understanding. Her exams are very difficult.

She goes through lessons pretty fast in order to get everything done in the 50 minute lectures. The class wouldn't be terrible if the exams and quizzes were worded similarly to the lesson notes and homework.
I love her
She literally moves so fast you wont learn anything by going to lecture

She talks to fast in lecture she doesn't go over a lot of the stuff you see on exams and quizzes you have to buy a subscription to web work and the homework you are assigned there are nothing like what you see on quizzes and exams. Overall just pick a new professor for math 103

Awful lectures, sped through with no care for students and for what? I have to pay for this? I don't even bother taking notes anymore, just show up to the lecture for the attendance credit. My ULA (Chen) is worse, confuses the entire class with her reviews before the exam. When we ask questions we are told "it just is." Should be online only.

This class was the only class I got a 3.5 in during my freshman year. This class progressively gets more difficult throughout the semester, despite being about topics I already learned in high school. There is a learning center available, and I regret not taking advantage of it. For me, the amount of time given on the exams were not enough.

She seemed nice but I went to every lecture and still failed the exams. The class was unnecessarily hard, it's been my worst class at MSU so far. I thought chemistry and calculus were much easier to pass.

Very very bad class, the professor did not teach well, as she went too fast, and did not care for students trying. The webwork is worth a really small amount of the grade, and the quizzes and exams are worth the rest, and they are not even related to the content being taught, Don't waste your time. Go or not go to the lectures, you will still fail.

Well How About the fact that the class average was a 2.0 for the course in the fall. More people have failed this class under her than any other Math 103 prof at MSU. Don't waste your Brain Cells in her class. Especially don't waste the time and money doing Math at MSU. Go to LCC so much better!!

I absolutely love Ms. Griffin. I think many students anticipate her classes to be easy and they are if you attend class. She is very accessible to students, helpful, and really cares about her students. She is a teacher who pays attention to her students and knows who cares about her class and who doesn't! Reach out to her and connect!
You will be teaching yourself this course by yourself seven days a week. VERY test heavy. Four exams with one drop (fall 2021) that are all worth 66.7% of your grade. Webwork is useless.

The form of application used on homework is the complete opposite of the tests, and because of this I was always reteaching myself how to do the material just to complete some questions that didnt help me prepare for exams.
Literally awful, prayers to the ones who will take her class. She made me wanna rip my hair out. The actual worse.
worst teacher ever

The math department at MSU is honestly messed up. This is the only class I would study for, had a tutor, went to every lecture, did the notes and all the homework and still couldn't manage to get better than a D in this class which that was even hard for me to get. I learned more from my RA teaching me in the study room at 2 am than I did in class
Not much to say just read the ratings. Homework and lectures don't prepare you for the exams. its just a struggle to learn and do anything well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not much to say you can put in all the work in the world into this class and fail.

Had her fall 2021 online. I thought her lecture videos were okay because my math teacher in high school taught like Griffin, but I dont feel like I can ask the questions I need to, being online. This was definitely a class for students that can take initiative to study on their own and often.

Worst class I have ever taken. I entered this course with math being not only my strongest subject but also my favorite, unfortunately, I will be leaving the course with a hatred for it that I never thought was possible. The exams and quizzes are much harder than any of the material presented in the lectures. Props to you if you actually pass.

The tests and quizzes are harder than the material learned and the professor is not very accommodating. This year we had 2 quiz grades dropped as well as a test, this may sound like enough I am not sure I personally know anyone that is happy with their grade in this class. Professor Griffin is nice during lectures but does not meet people halfway.

Terrible professor. I'm usually a straight A student and now I probably won't pass this class. Her exams are extremely hard, so much homework, and her lectures aren't helpful at all. Won't respond to emails, won't help students. Seems like she wants us to fail. Avoid taking her at all costs. Worst professor ever.
If you pass haha I will be shocked. Not worth the time or money spent. I will be retaking this class somewhere else. Please stop using web work its not worth it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I learned more from YouTube than her 50 minute lectures. Not worth the time or money. You can study 20 hours a week and fail and just not know what to do. MSU math Department should be shunned and frowned upon for their poor teaching practices and poorly preparing kids for life.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is awful Get ready to be on the cusp of failure. Not only that but everyone struggles straight A students, AP students. This class is terribly taught and not worth the time or money to put in to it. with a 50% fail rate better off taking it at LCC
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As another review said, you seriously get screwed over in this class so easy. Get sick, you're done. Miss some homework, you're done. It is literally impossible to consistently do good throughout the course and the tests were much different than the notes, homework, and even the reviews

Hardest class I've ever taken. I got straight A's in high school, passed AP statistics, and even took a college math preparation class, and nothing could have prepared me for this. Didn't start off too bad, but got a lot worse and I found it hard to prepare for tests and get help.

Thought she was a good teacher, who provided a lot of resources to succeed. My tips for quizzes/exams: go to class, study your notes, do the WW, read the textbook, watch her videos, and do every single problem you see come up. Difficult course, but not impossible. You can teach yourself with the resources she provides. She does go very fast though.

The most difficult class I have ever encountered. Entered being a straight A student and left extremely discouraged, barely passing. There is no amount of work you can put into this course to be confident and get a good grade consistently. With this being a course that is required, the level of difficulty is astronomical.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was terrible. I treated this class like a 9 to 5 and it never paid off. The assessments are not even comparable to the class notes/unit reviews, it's so much harder. There is no extra credit either so you are screwed. Webwork is terrible and a waste of time. I cry over this class daily. I would not take this class ever again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hardest class ever!! You dont even get a chance to pass. If you get sick you are done. Miss anything you are done. Don't know how kids pass this class. Worst teacher and class structure I have ever been on. Also web work is terrible, no test feedback for wrong answers and to make things worse she has literally no office hours.
she is horrible. Goes way too fast and doesnt teach anything important.
Tests and Exams are so much more difficult than the practice problems given.

I am good at math. I was not good in this class. She goes by so fast it's almost impossible to keep up. The amount of times I cried while taking this course is astronomical. I am thankful math is not something I need for my major, just MSU attendance. This is basic algebra and I am actually dying. Also, Webwork, the homework, sucks.

Mrs Griffin is nice person at heart and means well, but if you miss one class you are screwed. and don't look at down at your notes for more than 30 seconds or you wont understand what she did because of how fast she moves, i understand she has 2000 students but holy smokes lady give your students a chance to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She doesn't require attendance except on recitation days with your ULA's. I never went to class but 100% recommend watching the recorded ones or else you will struggle a lot. There is a ton of homework that takes forever. She does care about her students and provides extra practice videos which were helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Fast lectures, cant make up tests, quizzes, or recitations. Lectures arent mandatory recitation is. ULAs more helpful than teacher. Exams make up a good portion of your grade and are like 7 pages long barely enough time to finish. I was not even a full % from a 4.0 and didnt even consider rounding my grade.

Professor Griffin is super nice and caring. She is available outside of class and genuinely cares about her students. Her lectures can go kinda fast, but as long as you print out the lecture notes and follow along it isnt too bad. Make sure you study lecture notes before exams because theyre kinda hard. As long as you go to her youll do great.

This was an online math class. She sped through the lectures like we were on a time crunch. She wouldn't give any help and left all of that up to the ULA's. The tests were 7 pages long, with only 50 minutes to complete the test, so I left part of my test blank most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am not sure if it was because the course was online, but she hated interacting with her students. She did not like to help anyone and just wanted to keep doing lectures and be done. My grade was only good because I taught myself everything and spent hours studying She also is not forgiving in emergencies with a doctors note no matter how bad.
The absolute worst when it comes to understanding issues students might have. Not accommodating at all, even considering the pandemic and troubles with online learning. No care at all for students
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ms. Griffin is hilarious! She can be vague in explaining new concepts at times, but shes a solid choice to go with.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She answered your questions but only if they were during class, her office hours, or whenever she's on campus. She doesn't grade your assignments but tells the Undergraduate Learning Assistants/Graduate Teaching Assistants how to grade them. She assigns a project every semester which isn't relevant unless you plan on going into politics.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite person at MSU. Sharon Griffin is a blessing to this world. I suck at math, and not only is she the best math teacher I've ever had, but she's also the sweetest and most fun. Most math professors struggle with "dumbing it down" for us kids who suck at math. Griffin is fantastic at that, and she doesn't make you feel stupid for it.

I love her!! Best math professor at MSU hands down. She's very helpful and super funny. 5/5 recommend for freshman. Its an easy 4 class, but you HAVE to go to class or else you'll miss well needed information. Now, as far as the TA's, everyone had a different one, but if they aren't helpful, she sure will be. And she's very easy to talk to.

If you get 1 question on a test or exam wrong you fail. 1 question can be worth up to 24 points out of 100, unless you are some sort of Math expert. Shes also the only trig teacher so you are screwed. Honestly, math courses at MSU suck. If you want to do STEM have fun teaching yourself. Office hours are a WASTE OF TIME, use khan academy.

My experience with Ms. Griffin wasn't very pleasant. I'm a very hardworking, attentive student who admittedly struggles with math so Trig was tough from the start. I didn't learn very much in class. She makes bad jokes and quickly runs through material... I spent a lot of time with my TA in the MLC. She also grades very harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is one you have to work for if math is not your strongest suit. Lectures are only 50 minutes so it is hard for her to cover material as much as you would like. Be sure to get help outside of class if necessary. She is very nice and super funny as well.

Class was very hard for me but Ms. Griffin is the nicest and funniest prof I've had yet. Cares about her students greatly. Attendance isn't mandatory but I never minded going to her lecture and it paid off in the end.
It's not her in general that makes this class hell it's the whole program. The class and it's set up is awful.
best teacher every. im sad not to have her next year
She's a good teacher, but she grades down on the tiniest things. Got a B on my second quiz because I forgot a theta symbol.
She is a good teacher, but she doesnt hand out A's. She makes you work for it, and she is always there to help you. and its crazy she learns everyone's names within the first 2 weeks.

I understand that technically a basic citation error could be taken up with the university as a ADR. However discretion as a professor exists for a reason, and mindlessly chasing every error, no matter how trivial, is sure to lead to a generation of students despising you!

Louise isn't horrible, but this class really doesn't teach anything that couldn't be learned from a quick google search. Essays are graded by random students leading to huge variance in grades among students with similar essays. Lectures were just her arguing that AI is the root of all evil, unlike other professors embracing AI into their courses.

ADR simulator. A lot of writing for a 1 credit class. You'll almost 100% get an ADR if you ever get flagged for using AI. Getting spelling mistakes, wrong references, etc WILL get you an ADR. Ironic how the course is designed using ChatGPT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is bad. she will give tell you vaguely what to do and what not to do for ADR, and also in a learning environment you believe you can make mistake. But according to her you are Einstein writing paper to Roosevelt, so no room for error. Gave me an ADR for a spelling mistake, when i told her i can reverse it, I understood my mistake she says nah.

This professor is extremely unprofessional and it seems as though she doesn't enjoy teaching at all. If you meet with her to discuss a citation error, for which she threatens you with an ADR, she will tell you that anyone with a decent high school education can write a citation correctly and berate you. Course is boring and repetitive.

Super easy course based on essays, all of which are graded by your peers and ran through an AI detector rather than manually graded by TAs. Professor seems nice and she brings snacks for the 6 in-person discussion sessions.
Very easy class, to be honest the difficulty level is a joke. However, will give you an ADR for the smallest things so be very careful.

Unremarkable class with assignments that are very easy and quick to complete with high marks.  Discussions were mandatory but infrequent, requiring no actual participation.  A few essays were required and grading was moderately harsh, but not hard to succeed.  Communication via D2L was consistent.  Material is interesting but not anything special.

Everything in this class is automatically graded unless you ask for a review. Some test questions on the quizzes came out of the blue and did not match the readings, which was strange. She communicates with us through D2L announcements which is unfortunate because it easy to miss the notifications from those.

Some of the homework questions weren't in the notes or they were but the notes weren't straightforward so you still get the wrong answer. I believe she just started teaching and is still using some content from Owen, and she did offer a significant amount of extra credit so the class should still be an easy A.

Easily one of my favourite professors I've had. I hardly had to study for this class because his teaching was genuinely that good and made the subject very easy to understand. He genuinely helped my learning a ton. The group projects are also pretty easy and honestly took about 1 hour total. Definitely take his classes!

Alan was a great and caring professor! Linguistics is a hard subject to teach, but he makes it as manageable as he can. It's highly encouraged to ask questions. The final project is a group project, and there are two exams. The homework assignments are a little bit odd but you get used to it.

Dr. Ke is a very good professor, although Linguistics is a tough class in general, he tries to make it simple. They're are in-class quizzes, practice problems, and group projects, but as long as you go to class and pay attention its not bad. The class is Midterm and a Final which are open note. He is very kind and considerate for students.

I have him for multiple classes, and the lectures are both the same content pretty much. Assignments are long and complex, and he is a tough grader. Also participation is mandatory. Nice guy, but the class style is a lot to handle and remember, and D2L can be hard to navigate. Just a very complex style of teaching and grading, and a lot is expected

Really nice guy, but the class structure and assignments are really complex and confusing, and exams are HARD. Also this course in particular is very linguistics heavy with him as a prof, so keep that in mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I'm taking IAH 231C and I would not recommend at all. None of the course information makes sense. He is a very nice professor, but the course material is dumb and confusing. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE

I loved having Professor Ke, he was funny, engaging, and approachable. His lectures were clear and he was always willing to go over confusing information. The content itself can be challenging at times, but if you pay attention in class and ask questions during or after class, it's not difficult to do well in the course and genuinely learn a lot.

Professor Ke is an extremely kind person. Linguistics in general is horrible and hard to teach, but he tries to make up for it by being an easy grader. For assignments you have to record yourself to explain yourself, which was annoying, but trying to explain it out loud helped for understanding. Attend class or you will be confused.

IAH 231 not lin
Genuinely one of the worst professors I've ever had.I should've dropped this after the first class. Super nice professor when you talk to him after class, but truly horrible course overall. The grading is super messy on D2L, in class quizzes can never make them up either. I really hate this class and  it has been a waste of my time.

Alan is very nice and a great teacher, this is the second class I have taken with him and I still really like him as a professor. Linguistics can be confusing, but really just pay attention. He gives you extra credit for asking questions in class, so if you're confused you have a big incentive to ask!

Probably the nicest professor I've ever had. Unfortunately, most of the semester I was confused because the material is extremely difficult. I missed one class and I was pretty much a goner till after the midterm. If you take this class, make sure to never zone out, and keep asking him questions until you understand.

Alan is very nice, and really cares about his students. Students often walk away confused, although he tries his best. Linguistics is a hard subject to understand all together, and his teaching style isn't great for it. A good amount of homework. Midterm and final is online asynchronous, open note. No in class tests. Extra credit is offered.

Professor Alan was very friendly and he knew his stuff. Unfortunately, his students do not. I paid attention to lectures and still found myself confused often. Difficult topics were brushed over. There are 6 big assignments along with daily 4 questions lecture quizzes. The assignments were very difficult. A pro: he curves grades and offers E.C.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I personally found this class really difficult to the point where I couldnt finish. However, take that with a grain of salt. Ive personally heard amazing things about this course from other people but this class was just NOT for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super nice, approachable professor and generally very open to suggestions and feedback. However, he wasn't always the clearest when explaining more complex concepts. The book wasn't really needed, but could be helpful when Alan's explanation just wasn't cutting it. Grading was generous and TONS of EC opportunities. Almost everthing was open-note.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Alan Hezao Ke was very nice, yet the class was very difficult. Prepare to be confused during lectures. There are six major assignments, one paper, and two exams. Lots of extra credit opportunities which is nice, but there are also a lot of confusing lecture quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class was difficult and not recommended for freshmen , even though many take the class. Textbook use was optional but included EC readings. In-person lecture quizzes and participation is part of your grade and be prepared to spend a lot of time on assignments and preparing for the difficult midterm. Prof was nice, not super clear on things...

You can really tell she cares about her students. You're given an online textbook and homework quizzes that are based off the textbook, but I never opened it and just used what knowledge I had and a little bit of google too to complete them. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it really helps if you do show up and participate.

I enjoyed your class a lot! Even though in the beginning of the semester, I was nervous about college physics class and the amount of coding you would have to do, I managed it and thanks to your help, I'm able to code anything with the knowledge and skills you have given me. I personally would say that I'm bad at taking tests, which hurt my grade.

Dr. Hinko is very caring and gives back 40% on exams as long as you do corrections. She does do daily homeowork and have you whiteboard everything out and share with the class but if you are scared of physics I would recommend taking her class. She is so kind and will listen to you and truly wants everyone to do well.

Sime people may say that the class is hard, but that is simply because physics is hard. Dr. Hinko was very kind and lenient, allowing students to get 40% of points wrong back on exams. Ex. I got a 80% on an exam, after corrections I recieved a 88%.
very caring prof who wants students to succeed but fails to provide a course structure that allows them to do so. take university physics with the extra lab instead.
She was very caring and often fair with grading

Dr. Hinko is absolutely fantastic for students who are intimidated by physics, she teaches everything with clarity and as if you have no background knowledge for physics. The final is only worth 5%, and the midterm corrections earn a LOT of points back, so grades are not as stressful. It's hard to access her through email, but she is a great prof.

Very kind, caring professor. Allows late work and is a very understanding person. Exams are challenging but only worth 10% each; we were able to do exam corrections, as well. Final was only 5% so not a huge deal. A few group projects so make sure you have good people in your class. Only downside is extremely long class and huge homework packets.
only group work pretty much no lecture

This course required a lot of work (in terms of hours put in), and there was a bit too much group work for an online class (IMO). However, Dr. Hinko was very caring and understanding & is flexible with almost anything if you reach out to her. The readings will definitely help you with the material--just make sure to really budget your time!
