Dr. Hinko was incredibly receptive to our complaints this semester due to us being entirely online, but she in general was a bit disorganized. It was hard to be certain about specific things. Also, we never got grades back in a timely manner. Furthermore, we never actually learned physics content through a lecture. We did group assignments everyday

She is extremely disorganized and hard to reach by email. She constantly changes her mind about assignments, she's a tough grader, she puts most of the work on our confused TAs and she wastes a lot of class time talking about social issues instead of physics, which we basically have to teach ourselves.

Prof. Hinko is extremely disorganized. Her classes have no structure whatsoever. Does not provide sufficient descriptions to students physics-related questions. For being a Physics teacher she is not very good at describing physics in a way that can help the students understand.

The class itself and its contents can be difficult, but most are easy to understand. Hinko is pretty disorganized and never gives a clear answer to questions we have in class. She is pretty nice though, but I feel like she needs to completely overhaul her class to make it more enjoyable. She also does coding a lot, and it really really sucks.
Find a different prof for physics.

Doesnt answer questions. Often late to class. Unorganized. Too much free time that it is impossible not to get off topic. Doesnt provide correct way to solve problems. Video editing skills are more important then physics in lab reports. Would not recommend.
Eh just a boring class all around. Theres profs who may give you more interesting work with less of the effort of the random assignments.
Honestly one of best professors I have had here. Actually cares and interacts with the students. If you have the chance to take her please do so.

Very nice prof and easy class, mostly just show up and you'll do fine. Exams are a little difficult so study well for those, some questions are very specific to her lectures but she gives a nice study guide to work with. Attendance is mandatory but you get one free drop for it so nbd. Only 4 easy assignments homework-wise for the entire semester
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Paula is a wonderful teacher. She guides her class through training techniques practiced at the farm and is there to provide feedback. The training methods taught are those that have worked best for the program at MSU. Hard work and a good attitude are important. Show up ready to learn and you'll benefit from her many years of expertise.
Great professor. She is very knowledgable. She's definitely not mean, contrary to the other responses. If you've been around horse trainers, she is actually one of the nicer ones.

Professor Hitzler has years of past experience behind her, but she also possesses the mentality of "it's my way or the high-way" when she teaches about how to do anything in the horse industry--our class ended earlier than what it was supposed to because she "was tired of dealing with certain students" which meant we didn't the full class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Paula has extensive industry experience and is passionate about teaching. She seeks out the students who exhibit a passion for horses or want to work professionally with horses. Paula can be intimidating, but talk to the students who work with her to get a full picture. To make points, stay after class to talk horses and SHOW SOME INITIATIVE!

Took this class several years ago, and just came across the name now! I think Paula means well but can come across as rude a lot of the time. Although I don't regret taking the class, I think another professor could have lightened things up a little. I respect her greatly as a trainer, but not necessarily as a person.

She is a wonderful professor. I had her for the horse management lab. She knows what she is talking about & often shares anecdotes. She is open to questions & really helps students who ask for it. The lab final is not too hard, just pay attention & go to lab!!! Studying helps too!
No Comments
She seems scary at first, but shes just very articulate. She is a good professor and you can really learn a lot from her if you pay attention

STT 200 is a very hard course overall. Lectures and hw do not line up with exams at all. Not all of this is Dr. H fault, but he just read off slides. Little extra credit, there should have been way more. Lecture is not engaging with the material. Not easy to 4.0 or get a high grade in, workbook does not help either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class overall, just pay attention

Great teacher! He's the professor who cares about the students progress and explains everything very clearly during lectures. If your show up to lectures and do the homework you should be ok. Do the extra credit associated with each assignment can bump up your grade by 2.5%. Tophat points for 15 each week that can be make up until next week.
great teacher

Dr.H is funny, and stays after class to help people and is open to it. I asked to talk with him because I missed due to illness and he said no, thought that was weird but otherwise chill and communicating through email. I failed the class but I'd def take Dr.H again!

He uses tophat for attendance which you can do remotely. Overall if you attend lectures and recitation, understanding the content is really easy. Exams are a huge portion of the grade so you have to prepare for them. There's some extra credit built into the homework too.
Really well taught course. Dr. H is a good professor and makes this course easy to understand. Pretty easy 4.0 if you go to lectures and recitations.

He was a great stats professor. If you go to recitation and go to class everyday, you will do great! One thing that annoyed me was him letting people go early which was super distracting to people like me who stayed all of class. Overall, super easy math requirement with only 3 exams and a lot of extra credit offered to bump your grade 2.5%.
He is very nice. As far as a Stats class goes this one wasn't bad. He does a lot of things to help you succeed so just stay on top of your work and study for tests and you will be fine.

This class was sick! So to start off im one of those laid back chillers but me and hairy long lets just say we live on the wild side. To start off were both diabetics and we would wake up and shotgun dr peppers like dawgs and I swear me and the boys would be buzzing off the peps like no other. Will Long is a lifetime friend.Class is mid ngl.
He was a good professor
Great professor and very personable, as long as you pay attention in class, attend the recitations, ask questions, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Go to his lectures and do the tophat participation questions. If you miss them, you can make them up the next week for full points. Would have probably gotten an A instead of B if I showed up to all his lectures

Friendly professor for STT200, down to earth and tries to make his lectures fun. Class becomes fast paced after first month. One hw assignment a week (hr to complete) and one recitation a week. Complete both and attend lectures and the exam material will come to you very easily. 2.5% grade boost for extra credit

Going to class is important because its easy to fall behind. Lots of extra credit. If you show up to lectures and recitations and do your homework and extra credit you will be fine. Tough grader however, Would not round me up .2 to next highest grade which was frustrating but like i said there is a lot of extra credit opportunities getting me close

He is a quick teacher, and there is a note-pack. Attendance is kind of mandatory since he asks questions on TopHat during the lecture, but he also has makeups for the attendance open for a week after. To succeed, stay on top of homework and do all extra credit after completing homework.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Don't need to go to class can do top hat makeups from home and still receive credit. 
Complete extra credit and an extra 2.5% is added to final grade. 
Course isn't hard go over lecture notes, he moves pretty fast.

STT 200 exams/curriculum is all the same but Dr. H is the right professor to choose. He is kind, funny, and very clear in lectures. Make summary sheets to make sure you remember everything. Extra credit can up your grade by 2.5%. Only one homework assignment/week. He posts all the lecture slides & info so don't worry about missing a few classes.

Dr. H was a very nice and friendly man, but I felt like his lectures were too fast paced and at times he didn't fully explain the material. I would go to study for exams and would teach myself the whole exam material the week before the test. The content was not difficult it just took time to learn. There are many resources to get help such as SLC.

Dr. H was a great professor and super down to earth. This class was so easy it literally just requires you to do the bare minimum of go to class and do the webwork. Lectures are only 50 minutes but are 3 days a week so it's a little annoying but nonetheless, super easy class and exams are EXACTLY like the study guides

Overall, I found Dr. H enjoyable to listen to and learn from. If you follow along in the textbook/workbook, you will not have a problem taking his class. The homework is almost entirely things learned in lectures, and he posts the lecture notes after every class in case you miss a lecture. I would recommend taking Dr. H.
I just could not understand the way he teaches. He would bounce around from page 30 to page 120 in the span of 5 minuets, lectures were all over the place.

Super clear lectures, accent isn't thick at all, don't worry! tests were hard, 3 exams, all non-cumulative which is good. Class gets really boring though. DEFINATELY recommend the printed lecture notes, you WILL need them.

Overall the course was easy as long as you attend lectures and get top hat points. I landed 0.33% below the 4.0 grade. I emailed Professor H and he proceeded to give me a 3.5. Just thought he would be more caring then that so make sure to do all extra credit homework assignments, may save you in the end!

Dr. H's lectures were a bit fast paced as the stats classes have to adhere to a strict schedule, but he'll post the lecture slides after and there's a stats help room as well. From what I heard, he's one of the stats professors who tends to cover content slower in comparison to the others. If you complete all the extra credit, you get 2.5% boost.
Dr. H is awesome!! He made the material very easy to understand, and he just is such a nice guy. He was my fave professor this semester. Would highly recommend!
So sweet and great at explaining. Every thing is so straight forward and coincides very well with the exams and homework. If you have to take STT200, make sure you have Dr. H.

Dr. H is a fantastic professor. His lectures were super easy to follow, there was not a lot of homework, and the 3 exams were super easy. You can tell he really cares about what he teaches and is always willing to help. If you go to recitation and class, it's an easy 4.0. There is also extra credit that adds a whole 2.5 percent to your grade.

This course requires a lot of time and effort, especially if you get stuck with a bad recitation teacher. I recommend going to the SLC if you're struggling because that was the only way for me to pass since the lectures were fast-paced and confusing. Exams are similar to practice exams and study guides, but the questions tend to try to trick you.

Overall, Dr. H was quite good, but occasionally his accent made it difficult for me to understand the material. Also, the lectures were fast-paced, as he tried to cover a lot of content along with the TopHat questions. However, the recitations were very helpful and managed to review most of the lecture material in just one hour.
Not a very organized lecturer. Rushes towards the end of lectures because he's on a timeline and things get lost in between. Overall, an easy course tho.

Dr. H was a fantastic professor for statistics. Attendance is mostly mandatory, there will be participation questions throughout the lectures but the points can be made up with extra credit opportunities that come every week. Very helpful and knowledgable. He basically gives you the exams beforehand so preparing for them is extremely easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. H's classes were amazing. He would randomly talk about little stories he has (mostly about his cats) and he would teach the content very well. Show up to Classes and Recitations, do the HW with the Extra Credit and do the practice papers before exams (they are EXACTLY like the actual test) and it's an easy 4.0. I ended up getting a 101.5%.

If you're taking STT200, defo take Dr. H. I had a great time in his classes and he's very funny, always talks about his cats. Show up to classes, recitations and do the homework with the extra credit (extra credit is actually more helpful than you think) and it's an easy 4.0. Also, the practice exams are EXACTLY like the actual exams.

This class was overall very easy. Lecture attendance is mandatory as there are multiple participation questions throughout each one. Review sheets before exams are identical to exams. Overall he is a very nice guy and often makes jokes.

Very good professor who teaches statistics very well, you have to go to class to get points every week but the lectures are only an hour long. There is weekly homework that isn't very long. If you go to the lectures the class isn't very hard, Dr. H is also a nice guy so the class doesn't get boring.

His classes are too fast, leaving little time for the in class and timed questions, which require calculations and written answers. Only 30-60 seconds per question makes it tough to keep up. Lectures are less helpful compared to recitations. Good beside that. Exams 2 and 3 are harder.

Good prof, probably the best one for intro statistics. Ensure you get a physical copy of the coursepack at the beginning of the semester. It makes things so much easier. Go to all the recitations/lectures and you will get a good grade.

My favorite professor thus far! He's a very personable guy, and I felt very comfortable in his lectures and always made sure to go to them. He was a very clear teacher and made sure to explain everything thoughly. When they print out the notes and bind them it's super useful, and I 100% reccomend! He really made me enough learning stats!

The class isn't easy and imo very boring but it was a box I had to check off, if I could go back in time I would have showed up to more lectures as it's very easy to get behind.  Show up to every recitation or you it will negatively effect your grade and you cannot make up points.

Go to lectures or you'll fall behind and be confused real fast. Exams were like the practice exams and study guides. Homework was confusing but do the extra credit homework first and it'll make it easier plus that is the only extra credit you will receive so that helps boost your grade

Dr. H was a very straightforward, fair professor in my opinion. As long as you do the homework assignments and show up to lectures/recitations, you will get a 4.0. He provides a "study guide" and "practice exam" before each midterm and final, which was almost exactly how the tests were on exam day. Those were super super helpful.

Great professor who explains things clearly. With each homework assignment there is a corresponding extra credit assignment with unlimited attempts, meaning you should do the EC before the actual homework to ensure you get a good grade on it. Exams are fair. He WILL hold you right up until the end of class with Top Hat questions so be warned

this class was honestly easy if you paid any attention to the lectures, showed up to recitation, did the homework and extra credit, and then did the practice exam before the real one. I have never taken stats and did not think this class was hard. When he talked too fast I would go to SLC tho just to get extra help.

Professor H was a very good teacher. He explained the material very well and was extremely responsive to any questions you had. It is clear he wants students to do good in the class and succeed. The homework goes with what you learn in lectures so make sure to go and pay attention. Do the practice exams to help you prepare for the exams.

There are many things your grade will count towards (ie. recitation activity, tophat, webwork, exams). The content itself is not too hard I'd say as long as you go to the lecture and do the notes you should be fine. However, the professor was too fast-paced and did not want to slow down when asked.
everything was easy but makes you second guess yourself. grades are based on 3 exams, top hat in class, webworks, and recitation activities.

I loved this class and that was definitely because of the professor. He's always prepared and has a positive attitude. I thought the layout of the exams was easy to predict because of a lot of preparation materials. One of my fav classes I've taken!

He talks SO FAST and I don't know a single person who could keep up with him. Lectures are mandatory to get TopHat points. The notes they recommend you buy don't follow the slides super well. He's a nice guy but the class is so chaotic and I never have a clue what he's talking about. Exams are a carbon copy of the study guide though.

Exams are worth 70% of your grade so beware. They were somewhat difficult but also exactly like the study guides. He was a fast talker and I relied on having friends on the class to do homework and pass overall. He is super nice and tries to connect with his students.

He reads off of slides that he creates himself with one example done in class on TOPHAT. 30% of the class will get the correct answer and he assumes the class has the concept mastered due to the 30% getting it correct. He does not give adequate time for exams either.

He often teaches in a fast paced and confusing manner, and without having prior knowledge of stats I would have been lost. He is kind and professional, randomly discusses his cats which is nice. Recitation TA answered any questions I had. Quite a lot of material is covered, Middle of semester most difficult, I wouldn't recommend missing lectures.

My largest problem with this class occurs in the middle of the second semester. I took this class in fall 2022, and halfway through the second semester the professor around the Thanksgiving break the classes jump around the coursebook and introduce some of the most important parts of the semester which got very confusing and tanked my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you did well in AP Stats, you'll be totally good for this class. Class is kinda fast paced, but there's just a lot of material. I had to study a lot on my own. Prof is nice and funny and good at lectures, talks about his cats a lot. Tests are very important, but they're not too hard if you keep up with the class. Once a week homework sets.

He is a good professor. You should go to the lectures and PAY ATTENTION especially during the middle of the semester bc it has the hardest content. The practice exams are just like the actual exams, If you put in the work and understand the concepts you will get a 4.0

I took this course online asynchronous. It was pretty easy for me. There is extra credit that you can complete with every week of homework through webwork. The site isn't the best but not the worst to use. There were lecture videos that went along with the notes. As long as you completed everything every week, you should get a good grade.
Poor professor

I took this class during MSU's first full Covid semester. The lectures were immensely helpful for understanding the concepts introduced by the class, and the professor was sure to re-introduce concepts that became relevant again had we not used them for awhile. The structure of this course worked really well for me as someone with ADHD.

reviews.comment: took during covid and the course was taught by 3 professors. all were amazing! while the material can be confusing they do a great job of explaining and have help rooms with tutors you can go to. there is extra credit which is extra problem sets and seems like a lot but DO IT! very accommodating due to health/personal probs and want you to succeed

reviews.comment: I never had an actual encounter with my professor since it was taught online and a different professor was the one teaching in the videos we had to watch for notes. Do not take him for online math. I chose him as a professor because he was so well rated on here. He has been unwilling to help me during the entire semester. Every email that I've asked for help after explaining my notes and videos arent working, he tells me to use my videos or notes or go to the learning center. unwilling to adapt teaching style

Took online During Covid-19: For an online professor he is unhelpful and not willing to adapt teaching style to help those who really struggle in math. I eventually had to go to another professor in my online section to understand anything that was being taught. Asking him anything in unhelpful. Tells you to go to the STT center, use videos , notes

Due to COVID-19 My math class was switched to online. Harish Sankaranarayanan is the most unhelpful and rude professor I have ever had. Math is my worst subject and each time I asked for help through zoom or through email, I was met with unhelpful explanations and comments like "this is simple you should know this" and "I already went over this."

Dr. H is so understanding and kind! He genuinely cares about each and every one of his students and wants to see them succeed. After meeting with him once, he remembered my name out of the other 900+ students that he taught over the semester. I thought that was truly amazing. Dr. H is an incredible professor with some pretty great dad jokes ;)

He is awesome. I learned so much and was able to pass the class with flying colors. Attendance is taken by TopHat, but he has makeups each week if you decide to skip class. He was very easy to understand and made sure his students understood what they were learning.

Dr. H is my favorite math teacher ive ever had. Although the work can be challenging, he tries to do his best to teach. Class is 3x a week and uses tophat points, but you really only have to show up to 1 or 2 lectures a week to get the full credit. Theres also 2.5% extra credit if you do the practice webwork, so do it. Exams are same as practice!

He is not a bad prof at all the class is just so boring that paying attention is very difficult. Not paying attention makes the class harder than it needs to be. Recitation helps a lot. If you show up and listen you will be 100% fine
Dr. H is one of the best professors I've had at MSU. Gives you everything you need to succeed. The class was hard by its nature, but Dr. H worked hard to help his students. He is funny too.
Awesome professor! Clearly a great guy with good lectures. I did not 4.0 the class because of my own lack of effort.

Harish is so funny. His class is very confusing and theres are SO many pages of lecture notes. Webwork is super annoying but it ends up helping you in the end. Going to recitation every week REALLY helps. This class is an easy A if you study and go to recitation.

He really exceeds the expectations of being a good professor. I love him. He really cares for students to pass. Approachable, will help you any way possible, and very reasonable. The work is fair. The test aren't too terrible but this is not a class to slack. Have loads of respect for him and became one of my favorite professors

Pretty solid professor, he's very approachable and charismatic. He takes attendance everyday. The homework is large percentage of the grade, if you don't do it you will fail. The tests are pretty easy as long as you understand the basics of the material.

He truly wants ppl to master the course material and is willing to do anything to help students succeed. This is difficult in large classes like his, but he did an excellent job making it work. Always willing to meet & even adjust deadlines if I felt that I needed more time. OFFERS SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT! I'm bad at math & he made this so easy!!

He was a good professor however I found that the lectures were just a waste of time. You had to figure out most of the HW by yourself however once you figure out the HW you will be good to go for the midterms.The final however I felt like was very hard. At least when compared to the midterms. 2% extra credit, iClicker, weekly HW, 3 midterms(1 drop)

Great teacher! Lectures were logical and well organized, and he explained everything clearly. The content itself could be a bit challenging but he and his TA offer help room after class in case you have any issue with homework or lecture content. Attendance isn't taken but you need to take the iclikcer quiz during class.Overall a great teacher!

One of the best professors I've taken at MSU. I was nervous to take this class as I'd never taken any type of physics before, but everything was explained very clearly and he gave us a lot of info/material to prepare for exams. He was also available to help with questions after every lecture and all of it felt very simple and doable.

reviews.comment: I love this guy. Probably my favorite professor I've ever had. Class is so easy, tests are so easy, and you get a front and back cheat sheet, with a curve on the test. He is so nice and helps you when you are confused. One of the few instructors who can clearly explain concepts. Highly recommend.

Could I easily gotten a 4.0 yes, did i try no. He made the exams so easy, allowed students to make a cheat sheet front and back (could be typed). Exams were almost identical to practice exams. Attendance wasn't mandatory but there were iclicker questions 1 point for answering 3 for correct. Would give feedback on loncapa hw questions immediately.
Going to class is a must, difficult class but for exams you are given help sheets that you can write down formulas. If you do the work the class grade will come!

I was surprised to see that Professor Iwasaki didn't have at least a 4. The class can be difficult, but he and his TAs are constantly available and offer office hours for homework help, and his practice midterms and review lectures are very similar to questions on the actual exam. Overall an honest and kind professor who I would gladly take again.

reviews.comment: Professor Iwasaki is a very knowledgable and respectful professor. I had never taken physics before and wasn't required to take physics here. Dr. Iwasaki was really great, and seems like a good guy. 

Points for this class come mostly from homework, which isn't easy. Some points also come from clicker questions, which are reasonable. Hiro's very accommodating with taking questions about the homework and granting extensions. There were no exams, just a final paper which wasn't too long.

Hiro was a great professor, genuinely a great professor and wants his students to succeed. I think a lot of the bad reviews on here are just because the class itself is hard. This is probably my favorite class I have ever taken, I loved him so much and I was genuinely EXCITED to be going to this class. Tim I know you read these please teach more classes, we love you.

VERY easy class, almost everyone got 100%. Go to class and complete the Thursday assignments and you will be fine. Very very helpful for CJ and you learn a lot of helpful information. I will say the class will STRESS you out in terms of your future and make you feel like you are way behind but you aren't and you will benefit majorly from this class

All of his lectures are helpful for future careers in criminal justice. They were interesting since Tim is an interesting person, super funny and caring, and the class wasn't hard at all. Assignments about the lecture and some projects, but they were easy and you barely get points off.
Tim is one of the best criminal justice professors I've ever had. His class and teachings have helped me so much in my criminal justice professional development. I would 100% take his class again!
Not a doubt, one of the best guys you will ever meet during your time at Michigan State. Love Tim and everything he has to offer.
Tim is the goat. So nice & super easy homework. CJ294 is a super helpful class & he provides so many great resources.

Professor Hsu seems like a cool person; the class is just so poorly structured. The clicker questions are difficult, the lecture videos are unhelpful, and the help room is useless. On the bright side, the exams are online and not on lockdown browser.

She seems like a nice person but sometimes her lectures were confusing and hard to understand. The class overall is pretty hard as there is a lot of homework assignments, iclickers, and exams which are pretty hard.

I know five students who are currently taking this class, and they are failing. There are not enough resources to study for the exams.

Not enough grading opportunities to accurately judge a student's ability on the subject at hand. His lectures also follow a random pattern with no chance to study correctly due to his lack of assignments and withholding proper study materials, such as the slides.

ISS 320 consists of three exams, 1 extra credit opportunity for 5 points (usually a random lecture midday on a weekday) Exams are poorly written, shows up late, gives indirect answers to questions, and studying effectively is nearly impossible because he doesn't post slides. Goes on unrelated political rants. Exams are opinion-based, not an easy A.

I was so surprised to see negative reviews on Dr. Hourani. He was truly one of my favorite professors, and while his classes are reading heavy, he is very patient and understanding. He is a good professor, but he expects a lot from his students. There are at least two readings per week (and I mean long scholarly readings). He is very knowledgeable but not the best at communication basically never tells you your grade.

I enjoyed Dr. Hourani's class a lot. I found the key was to take notes on any topic from the reading he mentioned in class. I thought he was usually pretty funny, but his exams were definitely a lot of work. The TA had given us a couple extra credit papers to write which def made the class easier.

reviews.comment: I took a course in "Special Topics in Urban Design and Urban Regeneration" with professor Najib in the German Jordanian University, and he is wonderful! Gives a lot of amazing readings, holds great discussions, he is very competent, really knows his thing. He gives great feedback and motivates everyone to do their best. Definitely taught me a lot.

If you are looking into whether or not you should take a class with this professor, consider yourself lucky that you went to rate my professor first. I studied my ass off for this class and barely came away with a passing grade. This is the type of teacher that would read this review and be proud of it. Heed my words, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!

This was by far the worst class I have ever taken. Exams are tough, and the only thing you're graded on the class is exams! This class is very lecture heavy, and there are rarely any power points to look at. The Professor easily gets off topic for most of the class and the concepts he is teaching are very hard to grasp. Do not take this class!

This class is called "World Urban Systems", so if for some wild reason that's what you're expecting, do NOT take this class. The entire course content is up to the jurisdiction of whatever Dr. Hourani wants to talk about that day & issues/history in the Middle East. Hourani seems ok, but he is very closed-minded to those with opposing viewpoints.

Dont get me wrong he is a good guy (hence 2 not 1), but the class quickly transitions from Urban Planning to being a class about his interest in Islamic culture and "relevant" topics in the middle east. He says you wont pass if you do not read, but if you take good notes on the review sheets you will pass the exams with ease. I would NOT recommend

(I actually took ISS 320 but it wasn't an option)

I took ISS 320 with him. The class itself was about "urban planning." However, rarely have we talked about any cities, and when we did, we only talked about Arab cities. reviews.comment: The reading load is heavy, and the exams are insane, but this class has been the best I've taken at MSU. If you want an old-fashioned course experience, take this class. No powerpoints or busy work, so if you want the easy way out take a different class. If you're interested in social & cultural theories  of anthro and you want to learn, take it.

I took his class based on the reviews here and he is a good teacher but he is kind of a dictator in the class. He gives lots of reading and you have to be ready for class discussions, the first exam was easy but the ones after that were hard. All I can say is keep up with the readings and GO to class most of the exams are from class discussion.
He's a really cool guy! But geography is not his thing. He should stick to antropology. Assigns a lot of readings and you have to be ready when you come to class, gives points for participation.
No Comments
He challenges you and makes you think. However, he's a bit scatter brained, quite disorganized, and often appears to be on the verge of a breakdown!

Ok, class is doable just study hard for everything tbh the lectures don't help & examples given aren't worked out in class so you have to figure them out on your own. Homework sometimes looks like the quizzes but most of the time they don't match. Best bet for the final is study the prior quizzes. Get the highest grade on anything you can.
Didn't add any grades other than quizzes to D2L so you had to manually calculate your grade. Office hours weren't very helpful, and lectures often didn't line up with the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really great guy, had lunch with him. Truly a goat. MasteringPhysics is horrific, and the worst homework site ever created, but Joey didn't make it, so it's not his fault. Quizzes were ALWAYS straightforward, but meant to trip you up as entry physics courses build intuition. He cares about you and your grade as long as you care. Highly recommend.

Out of all of my years in college, I've never had a professor like this. Hes a decent guy but as an educator, he takes months to post quiz grades the great majority of your final grade comes from the quizzes, which are, respectively, poorly written and not reflective of the material we learn in class. Expect class averages of 60-70% on every quiz.

This class is intended for people who have a physics background (AP Physics or the like) so it is very fast paced and the lectures wont be super helpful if you are already behind. However, he does an amazing job at explaining concepts when asked to do so. His office hours are always open and he cares a lot about his students.

He is super nice, Have you heard of the type of teacher who threatens you with a low passing rate? he's the opposite.he uses I clicker to gather data on what people struggle with the most, always trying to get the full class to get the right answer and adapting the content as such, great feedback,I told him about a tiny issue w clicker and he fixed

A lot of people taking the honors classes have taken + done well in physics before. So this class is a fast-paced review of stuff they already know, and Dr. Huston makes it interesting with lots of random stories and asides. If this is your first time taking physics, I don't think this course is great. But Dr. Huston is very nice and helpful in OH!

The MasteringPhysics questions get on my nerves as well but considering we only have one assignment due every week, there isn't as much homework as many would think. Additionally, I believe Joey is very forgiving in terms of grading. If he sees that you provided clear work that seems reasonable, he won't hesitate to give additional credit.

When I was taking this course, he took forever to put grades in. Quizes were 40% of the overall grade, meaning they mattered very heavily. This semester, he did not put any quiz grades in until the end of March, giving me almost no time to try to pick my grade up after finding out that I did bad on them.

He did not spend a single lecture actually teaching the material. He is very nice and well-respected in the field of physics, but none of that translated into teaching ability. He spends most of lecture telling stories or talking about Big Bang Theory, then blitzes through all the material in 10 minutes, then posts the lecture slides a week later.

The majority of lectures were spent talking about random historical physicists instead of the actual content we needed to be learning.  The lectures were weeks behind the homework, and the practice quizzes would be completely different than the actual quizzes.  Do not take this class if you don't have a good understand of physics already.

reviews.comment: I wish I could take all my physics courses with him, he is genuinely passionate about physics and his classes are enjoyable to go to.

Great guy and a great prof. Very respected and experienced in his field so get ready to hear a lot of stories about his work and the people he's interacted with. Get to class early to have some good conversations with him.

Pearson's Mastering Physics grading system will be the bane of my existence, but the lectures in this class were pretty good overall. The content could get pretty boring at times but Professor Huston would add in stories and anecdotes to make it all more interesting. iClicker is worth a lot. Overall, an easy class and a very nice professor.

This guy loves physics more than life itself. Puts a lot of real life examples into his lectures, which makes it interesting if you're into that (I wasn't). Class attendence isn't mandatory and most lectures are just a repeat of the reading, but he uses clicker questions as a big part of the grade. If you're a physics major, he'll love you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is entirely taught by TA's and they determine your grade. I might've received an email from Dr. Huston at the beginning of the course for an extra credit survey. brother was all up in my space and he's very condescending, loud, rude, everything. not helpful at all and everytime i listen to him talk i'm on the verge of having a stroke.

Worst prof I ever had at Michigan State.

She's very passionate about what she teaches and easy to reach outside of class. The tests were pretty easy but you have to get a 93% to 4.0 the class so that makes it a little harder

Excellent professor! You can tell she is a very knowledgable individual. Always provides great examples, and breaks down concepts very well. I would definitely take this class with her again.

Ask questions in this class.

Dr. Cho is knowledgable and passionate about SW. He is kind and compassionate and is quick and glad to implement feedback provided by students. He grades quickly and his expectations are clear. I would love to have him again.

He's a pretty nice guy. Reaction papers are due every few weeks and are pretty easy never got below a 97% despite putting in like no effort. Exams are kind of hard but if you really search through the lectures you'll be able to find the answers. He's good enough

Ian is in my top 5 professors at Michigan State. He makes coming to class a treat as he is quite funny and implements real life into his teaching. I could not say enough positive things about him. Awesome teacher and person to be around.

Best professor I have ever had. Funny and teaches with passion and interest.

Professor Osobov willingly over-complicates formulas when teaching lecture, and expects students to "follow along" with his overly complex explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: hard professor, thinks you have a lot of background in the topic. lectures are long and boring but attendance plays a large role in your grade. do the practice problems for exams. he's nice but struggles to explain things making the course difficult. put in the time and effort and you'll do well but don't expect it to be an easy pass.
Best teacher, and easy to pass
Cool dude

I am a terrible math student and I was really worried about taking a calculus class. He does have an accent but he explains things extremely well and if you come to class and ask questions he will make sure you do well. Like I said I'm not good at math at all but I did the homework and came prepared and got a 4.0. He's also really nice and funny!
He has a russian accent, but you get used to it. Very funny at times and loves to teach. Goes quickly so be prepared on the first day.

I don't know what everyone else is talking about. His accent is not bad but he is a terrible teacher. He doesn't explain anything. Last class I asked whim where a number came from to which he replied, "I put it there". Unless math comes natural, stay away from Ignat!

Ignat is great. If he sees that you are actually trying and participating in class you will get a 3.5 or 4.0. At the end of the year I got a 91 on the final and an 88.5 in the class and he rounded up my grade to a four point! He is a really great guy and anyone in 124 should take his class!!!

I took his calc 2 course this summer. It was extremely fast paced, and very time consuming. Ignat really pushed all of us to do our best, and I feel like I learned a lot in his course. His summer calc 2 course was very difficult, and I feel like a lot of people will fail, due to the course load, not his teaching (much easier in sem). Great teacher.

Good teacher, highly recommended. Slight accent but very nice and helpful. Go to class and you will ace the exams and quizzes. He really wants you to succeed in the class and it shows. Most people got a 4.0 or 3.5.
overall, pretty good teacher.  cracks a joke here and there.  Off the boat from Russia, has a slight accent.easy to understand.

The only thing the prof grades in this class is the final project and the feedback given by the TA is completely different from the feedback from the prof so the feedback given throughout the course is not very related to the final grade from the professor.

Nice professor and you can tell he cares a lot about the subject. There are 9 pop quizzes throughout the semester that you have to be in class for to get the password so attendance is practically mandatory. Recitation once a week that is discussion-based you have to participate in.  3 essays graded relatively hard, hard to 4.0 the class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy. Have to attend recitation, it's ridiculous how many points taken off for each one. There is none dropped. Essays are graded hard
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hawthorne really really cares about the material he teaches. If you care about Africa BCE, then this is the class for you. There is kind of random quizzes in classes that aren't hard. Just pay attention. There is three essays instead of exams. They grade hard on them. The prompts are stupid. Make sure that you meet all the requirements.

Learned so much from him. Super interesting guy and probably my favorite professor I've had so far. He really cares about the material and wants you to learn. Pretty easy class as long as you try on the papers, never got anything below a 92%.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was a very nice guy who always answered my questions. He also gave excellent resources for us to use to write our research papers.

Although my grade in the class mot bad, I can still say I had a tough time in this class due to the teachings and confusing lectures. I wouldn't say I didn't learn anything in this class, but I would recommend finding a different professor if you need this for a requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would honestly NOT recommend to take this course with Professor Walter Hawthorne III. Grading system is very inconsistent, the likelihood of your grade tanking because of 1 assignment is high with his course.If you prefer to have a high GPA and a professor who actually responds to emails in a timely matter, his class will never be worth your time

Prof Hawthorne is nice and knowledgeable. The most important things to do well in this class are the weekly readings before recitations. The readings set you up well for the essays which are worth most of your final grade. There are pop quizzes occasionally over the lecture material so it is smart to show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hawthorne is really great. The workload has a great balance. There are not exams in this class, just three essays for each unit, which are very easy to write. Lectures aren't mandatory but overall help with your understanding of the material. This class has two lectures and one recitation a week.

For his first semester teaching the class, he did a phenomenal job. You can tell he is deeply passionate about Africa and its history. The readings he would assign seemed carefully selected and enhanced understanding of the topic well. He engaged directly with students before/after class and had a good system for mental health of students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a really nice guy and you can tell he loves statistics. However, there was no structure to the class and you have to teach yourself everything. I mean everything. The exams are exactly like the practice exams which is nice. Definitely try and take with a different prof.

He said at the beginning of the year that a lot of people will drop because it is so boring and that his lectures won't help with the assignments because he talks about the theory behind what were doing. You need to teach yourself. Takes him days to respond to emails (if he does). No one knew who was going on in this class (not even him).

While friendly and nice, there is no clear proof that Ikpe knows what he is doing. He is very knowledgeable and clearly loves statistics, but lacks the ability to share his knowledge with his classes. He was not able to answer any student questions and claimed he would come back to them (he never did). Take at your own risk.

Professor Ikpe seems like a nice guy, but his lectures are very difficult to follow. There is no clear structure to what he is saying. Lectures often felt useless to attend. What was nice was that every quiz was a question from the homework, so you could easily figure out what you needed to know beforehand.

He clearly loves statistics a lot but he can't teach. Never clear about assigning work, due dates, or even class content. I don't think he answered a single question anyone asked him, he'd either say "great question save it for later" or ask the class to answer it.  No one knows what goes on in his class you really have to teach yourself.
No course structure, professor is teaching on vibes. I think he is as lost as I am in his class.
Very talented and makes sure you understand the concept and problems.

You can tell that he is very passionate about statistics and cares, but he is very bad at teaching. His lectures are very boring and confusing. I took AP stats so I already know most of the material and could get up in front of the class and explain it better than him.

This professor like he has no idea where he is going with his explanations and often don't help. He also has a strong accent making it even harder to try and understand him. We seem to never learn much in class and he goes off on random tangents. He also has said "I don't know the answer or how to do it so I cant tell you what is right".
He is very kind and passionate about statistics. If you put in the work and attend lectures you will do well on exams!! Homework is important to do right away and is similar to exam questions.

(STT 351) Professor doesn't teach required material in class, so you have to review the lecture slideshows on your own time. This course is essentially a learn-it-yourself class. Overall, I can say confidently that this is the worst professor I've had in all my years of education. Please for your own sake, take it with another teacher!

Couldn't stand his teaching style, taught myself more in 2 hours than in 2 weeks of lectures. He's really into the material and super excited to teach but his pacing is weird and his lectures are all derivations, no example problems. Will tell you exactly what is on the quiz, exams are just like the study guides, hw or quiz every week
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor does an extremely poor job being accessible and providing feedback to his students. Takes multiple emails over the span of several days for him to respond once, does not give feedback on homework or exams, and has students running his office hours. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Enthusiastic and obviously loves the topic but does not care about students and very confusing when answering questions. Tests are almost exact copies of the practice quiz. HW is very hard and graded even harder; no answers or explanations of HW questions (not even which you got wrong) are ever given. Attendance is extra credit. Book is online.

Very enthusiastic professor but poor at actually covering the material. Sometimes he would intentionally skip material to do something "fun" and show the beauty of stats but it didn't really end up helping. Prepared us well for exams, they are carbon copies of quizzes. Hardly helped prepare for homework; no similar examples done, just derivations.

Had him for accounting i. He is now a professor at Notre Dame. Very nice, likable, funny guy but also a great teacher. He will explain things several times to make sure you understand and will slow down if people are not getting the material. Fair grader, and it helps to participate. Cant put it into words how great he was.

He really takes an interest in his students and making sure they understand the topic, adjusting lectures to make sure no one gets left too far behind.  However he is also demanding and expects you to earn your grade.
Very nice guy and is very willing to help at any time. Was very helpful as a TA in the weekly recitations. Grades fairly.

MKT 301 - He is really nice and caring. Class is very lecture heavy so be ready to take notes, but he makes it enjoyable. He only gave about 3 homework assignments and you don't have to come to class on homework days. There's 2 test and a final. Tests can sometimes be a little hard, so make sure you study. You have to present a 2 minute speech.

Amazing Professor, Could not ask for better. You leave the class with a good sense of knowledge from the marerial and he makes the class so much fun. He's seriously one of a kind. He's British which makes it even better! Take him so good!
this teacher is the BEST!!

Great Teacher, gave out candy for participating in the class, puts his notes online but you still have to come because you do in-class assignments, but it is a really easy class that he makes interesting
He is an all around nice guy. Great class.
trevor taught my summer course at U of M Dearborn and he was an awesome prof... he made the subject interesting and fun... just an awesome guy
He is soooooooooo COOOL! He is such a helpful and awesome teacher!

Prof. Ingersoll is the platonic ideal of a professor, role model, and citizen. Sometimes—if you're lucky enough—you have the privilege of spending time in the company of a truly great mind. She is a genius. Nay—a visionary.  She slays. She sashays. She commits to the bit.

Lectures were online and when we had to come to class once a week we basically did nothing. Exams were difficult but she was generous with the curve on the midterm. Lectures went into tons of detail and exam questions were really specific (barely any guidance for studying). Loved her as a person (very sweet) but disliked structure of the class.

This was an extremely hard class and Dr. Ingersoll made it impossible to do well in it. She was not concerned with how terrible the class as a whole would do on exams and blamed it on our poor study habits. The study guides were so long it was impractical for the students to know all the material. I wish I didn't take this class for my PSYW credit

This was the worst professor I have had in Psychology. Her mentality is that there's nothing wrong with her tests, the students just need to study harder. The tests were impossible and made up a large part of your grade and the literature review was extremely hard to do well on. I would not recommend this class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ingersoll is great. She is incredibly passionate about her job and that shows in her lectures. She also gives great feedback on papers.

Exams are worth most of your grade, but he allows 5 double-sided note sheets on the final. Not the greatest teacher, but you can tell he cares and is trying. Content is easy if you pay attention, lectures aren't recorded but he also doesn't take attendance. Don't try and not come to class and just look over his uploaded notes, that won't work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take IBIO341 in general at MSU - let alone with this guy! First off, the way they teach the material is an absolute joke...and then they give ridiculously difficult exams that are clearly not written by the professor. Also graded very harshly. This guy doesn't care, nor does the department. Just avoid this. What a waste of time and effort.

Avoid this prof for IBIO341. I don't think I've had a worse teacher at MSU or honestly in my life. It almost seemed like he was learning the content with us. He would also never answer a question straight on and would offer no help when going over what you got wrong on exams. Please avoid him. He is also very rude.

This was the hardest class I have ever taken. Dr. Braasch no doubt has a good character, but his lectures have nothing to do with the Achieve homework, the Problem Set Checkers, or the quizzes. His exams are impossible and they total at 70% of your grade between the three exams. If you have another option, don't take this class.

I really like Dr. Braasch as a person, and I enjoyed his lectures as review sessions where everyone could work out problems together. He definitely has a passion for teaching, I didn't rate 5/5 because I felt like some of the assignments such as the Problem Set Checkers didn't get much explanation, and I hated how we never could see keys for those.

Class definitely requires you to put forth some effort, but Braasch is great at presenting the material and exams are fair. Only reason I'm not giving 5/5 is because the final unit of content is extremely difficult and could benefit from some revision in the way its taught. Just be prepared for the course to go from 0-100 real quick towards the end
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exams are written fairly, lectures are interactive, highlight the important information well, and keeps your attention. Only need 75% on homework to receive 100%. I took this class knowing it would require lots of attention and I went to office hours with Dr. Braasch every couple weeks and sometimes to the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Prof Ingle for CE 275. The class was easy and self-explanatory. Show up on your lab days and put in a good 2 hours each week and you'll finish the class ahead of schedule. Well respected man, easy to talk to and he clearly knows his stuff. I found this class super useful as it correlates well with civil internships.

The class was graded by 5 projects with in depth lecture videos that went along with each project. Dr. Ingle was available during class time for questions in addition to the TA's. He was very knowledgable on the technology used.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was difficult at first due to not understanding the software. Dr. Ingle is nice, but not very helpful when I was confused about a project. The projects follow videos he posts almost exactly, which is very nice. The final project was more confusing due to no video tutorial and the TA's and professor weren't very helpful.

Professor Ingle is very nice and accommodating. The first week of the courses seem really difficult at first as you figure out the software, but overall, the classes are easy. He does homework tutorial videos basically going through everything you need. Lots of open lab hours and no required materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Inbody has a sense of humor that can be hard to connect with and can turn some away. Personally, I loved her teaching style and her use of terrible puns (a fine art). She cares about the students and normally lets class out early. While she does complain about work, she's just the professor equivalent of a normal college student.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Most sarcastic teacher I have ever had. I appreciated it and was humored by it until it turned completely off-putting. She made rude comments about inappropriate things and made me fear I would be the brunt of her next snarky comment. Talked often about "loving her job" (sarcasm) and had a bipolar grading style. Love English, hated her class.
she makes rude comments and repeatedly talks about how she hates her job and one day she made fun of the school shootings that were happening around the country.
know about the subject, cant teach at all. Will not reply to teaching assistants, takes 3 fiscal years to put in grades. If you want to learn any statistics, dont take this class.

Nice guy, very passionate about the subject. Attendance is technically mandatory but there weren't any penalties for skipping. If you take this class I highly suggest learning how to use your calculator to do most of the work for you, it will make this class so much easier and will take significantly less time.

Hard class, but his teaching style is hit or miss, and it was a miss for me. Lectures are mostly derivations with no examples or homework help but he will tell you exactly what is on the quizzes (and there is a quiz every other week, with more exams). Seems willing to help, but doesn't respond to emails, and when he does it's vague. Nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is very bad at teaching an undergraduate course. He often reads the equations out loud in the lecture, and that confused me a lot. And the lecture does not make any sense whatsoever. His notes are okay, but he goes over them very fast. We had to tell him to slow down, but he responded, "We should remember these things in Calc 4."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Accused me of cheating because my work "was confusing" and then proceeded to cuss me out after addressing the matter in scheduled office hours. All negative reviews are accurate. He does not want to be teaching and take any other section if he is offered.

Laziest professor I've ever seen. Switched our homework to 0% of our grade and quizzes to 45% because in a "class of this size" (115) he didn't want to grade that many homeworks. Offers test corrections based off of average score, but told us not to do it if we got an 85% or over because "that's a lot of work for me so you can get 2 points back".

This guy is genuinely heartless and full of himself. Really wish the class wasn't JUST based off exams. Homework or some sort of extra credit could be nice but he is lazy. He makes up the structure of the class as he feels like and doesn't care about the students.

Homework isn't graded, very quiz and test heavy. Very lecture heavy, moves fast and does expect you to know calc 4 by heart as class is “review”. Quizzes/Exams aren't bad if you study and memorize since based off HW. I'm just a crappy test taker. Textbook exists but wasn't very helpful for me. Best is to practice and review notes for test

Womp womp so many people complaining about a junior level math course. The quizzes are completely based on the homework, of which he uploads solutions (hard to read sometimes). I really don't see why people hate this guy, there are so many worse professors out there. At least he actually cares about his job instead of someone like Imen Zabaar

Homework taken out of syllabus because he couldn't hire another TA. Lectures are fast paced with 4 quizzes and 2 exams. Expected to know Calc 4 material inside and out with exams not receiving much partial credit unless near correct. Handwriting isn't great. Practice exams and Hw practice is provided but is quite confusing and not well written.

The professor doesn't upload lecture notes, making it hard to keep up. They write so quickly that note-taking is a struggle, leaving many of us lost. Instead of focusing on practical problems for quizzes and exams, class time is spent on theory and equations that feel disconnected. If you need structured support, look elsewhere.
Brilliant professor! Tough class, thanks to this class I realized there's more to life than academic achievement, dropped out of my masters after one course
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was one of the most poorly taught classes I have ever had the displeasure of being apart of. The professor frequently references material from other classes which are not prerequisites for this class. Additionally, this class focused not on introducing material to students, and instead focused on derivations of graduate level material.

Combustion Guru. Absolute genius. I consider it a honor to have been in his class. Online course - grading structure was homework based (different from his undergrad courses). Wonderful to chat with & absolutely teeming with knowledge. Old school cool. Was solving fluid and combustion problems before computers. Lecture sometimes disorganized
Worst experience I have ever had in class

If your schedule forces you to take ME 332 with Wichman, you're better off transferring universities.  In fact, give up going to college for engineering entirely.  You'll be better off that way, anyway.
THIS CLASS IS AWFUL WITH HIM PLEASE SAVE YOURSELF AND TAKE WITH ANOTHER PROFERSSOR
Good
He teaches really bad. In fact he teaches in a way that you get confused even for topics that you already know.
Great professor, wish there were more like him.  Soft spoken but stands his ground.  Very intelligent.  Would recommend.

The Good: very well spoken and you won't have a difficulty understanding him, he's a nice guy outside of class and is VERY smart. The good doesn't last tho, his tests are nearly impossible to complete in the time limit and gives WAY too much homework. Very intimidating during lecture so nobody askes questions. Not a good prof

Worst professor ive ever had. makes going to class feel pointless because you will not learn anything or better understand the material. He expects students to understand everything immediately and if you dont he treats you like you are stupid
Teaches an undergrad class but expects everyone to comprehend grad level material, and then tests you on the grad level material.
Best professor at Michigan State!
He made tests very challenging so that only the best students could complete them.
HE'S THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD
Excellent classroom instructor...Gives clear and concise lectures.  Would highly recommend.
The best
Great prof
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Iqbal was extremely unprofessional in the time I spent with him. He offered no further explanations to assignments and expected us to understand difficult concepts in a short amount of time. He was difficult to understand and was EXTREMELY unclear about assignments, deadlines and papers. Avoid this professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard to understand and expects us to know everything about everything. Gives a ton of reading homework and grades discussions super harshly. You have very few grades so everything counts for alot. Also mandatory attendance and he knows if you skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is hard to understand. He is not specific about what he is looking for in your assignment and he grades insanely hard. Terrible class. Gave me lots of stress and anxiety. 10/10 would NOT recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Xagoraraki is absolutely amazing. Her class is composed of 9 quizzes and a cumulative final which composes the entirety of your grade. At first it seems cut throat but once you get a feel for her lectures and quizzes, it will all work out. Highly recommend attending her lectures. You're paying for your education, might as well get educated.

She is really easygoing. There is no homework or reading or any outside work required. The only work is a quiz a week. If you study the lecture slides before the quizzes, you should get at least a C. Meeting with TAs help. She is very chill and sometimes cracks jokes. Final cumulative but not hard.

She refused to adapt to online learning. She does not teach the class. She told everyone on the first day of class that she didnt want to go through everything since we are not in person. She will show you the lecture slides, but will not go over what you are actually tested on.
Wonderful Professor. I went into class expecting to hate it and have left really enjoying physics. 10/10 would take again.

Amazing professor all around. Although the class isn't easy, Paul does a great job at helping you to get on track. He is extremely kind with a great sense of humor, and despite running a mostly TA/ULA based course, he is involved in all aspects of the class. As said before, fantastic professor in just about every category.

Paul was a great guy with an awesome sense of humor. Personally the teaching style for this course didn't work for me. You are on your own for the notes and in class is all group work on complex, real life problems. If group work isn't your thing I wouldn't recommend this course. Paul and the TAs were very helpful and care about your understanding

He's an overall solid guy. He doesn't expect you to be an expert on physics material, so he helps explain through things thoroughly in class and on Piazza. TAs are helpful. My only complaint is that the homework felt unnecessarily hard sometimes, but still bearable. Recommend!
Good guy. In-class problems are more difficult than necessary, piazza is pretty trash, fortunately, the class structure is forgiving, and good teaching staff. Overall Paul is a good option

A really great prof that definitely cares about teaching. If you hate working in groups I would not recommend his class, but if you are like me and enjoy it (or if you have no preference), I would 100% take this section. The format provides for a great understanding of material and grades are less dependant on individual exams.

Paul is such an awesome dude. Probably the coolest person I've had as a professor, just an all around nice, funny, and caring guy. Only reason why I rated 4* is because I did all the work for an honors project and he didn't give us credit and never responded to emails about it.

I had Paul for PCubed (trial version of PHY183 in Spring'16; class met 2x a week for group based work; attendance was a big portion of grade). Paul is funny& explains difficult physics concepts simply. He has a heavy Irish accent, loves Star Wars & clearly cares about students; he knew my name& would say hi outside of class. Would HIGHLY recommend.
Boring lecture. Grading seems unfair. Stuff on quizzes not taught in lecture. AVOID
Boring lecture. Grading seems unfair. Stuff on quizzes not taught in lecture. AVOID
No Comments

Essay tests that are 20 questions.  TA grades the test and unless you write down whats on the answer key you won't get full credit.  His lectures are boring and he isn't that great of a prof.  Don't take him if you have a choice.
He cares.

This class is really easy if you're prepared to put in the time. I love the prof; she is super caring and is passionate about what she teaches. Lectures are long and kinda boring, but attendance isn't required. Exams are multiple choice, offer tons of extra credit, & you can get points back.

The required textbook is super expensive and there's way too much homework that goes way too in depth for a 200 level class. Prof is nice but exams are super long too and final is not optional. I felt like this class should only be for anthro majors. Takes awhile for grades to come back too
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is not worth it. I like her as a person, but her lectures go over so much information, and she doesn't tell you what parts of these lectures will be on the exam until a few days before. I spent more time studying for this singular class than Ochem 2 and IBIO 341 combined. It's not required for any major so I wouldn't recommend it.
This class was so fun and easy! I took it to fulfill a natural science credit for the honors college, and it was probably the easiest class you can take for a natural science substitution.

Dr. Isaac was extremely nice. The lectures were quite boring and contained loads of information but exams were very easy. I did find that much of the information in the published study guides gave me a better understanding of what would be on the exam rather than in the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wasn't a big fan of Dr. Isaac, sometimes I got the feeling that she did not like her students. Lectures contain too much content. I'd spend the entire class period frantically writing. The first and last exams weren't too bad, but the second exam had wayyy too much content to study for. But at least the exams were heavily weighted.

Carolyn is very kind and understanding. Only odd thing is that if you leave early then she will be call you out. Exams have a large weight and are based on a study guide she gives. You have to memorize. But the study guides are like 20 pages long min.

I liked everything about the class but the content from the test is way too heavy. Lots of memorization for a level 200 course. The stuff we were expected to memorize was like 20 pages and the content we had to memorize like the age, appearance of anatomical features felt unnessencary

I loved anp 206 with Dr. Issac but by main concern is why tf do we have to have a 4th exam in guest lectures, we went through the whole material before thanksgiving, so now we have a final on guess lectures. But great class.

The study guides are long but extremely helpful for the test if you take the time to fill them out. I think she is extremely accommodating and still learning, since it is her first semester teaching this course. Lots of EC built into exams, labs are easy. The InQuisitives can be kind of hard/annoying, but you have unlimited attempts to get 100

dr. isaac is a great professor, and she was extremely accommodating to her students this semester. she's easy to reach outside of class and is always willing to answer questions. study guides were provided; labs and exams are easy if you take the time to study. extra credit is also offered! honestly she's a great professor and person in general :)
Dr. Isaac is very caring and understanding; you can tell she has a passion for anthropology. The exams were long but not too difficult, and the labs were easy.

overall, class is easy. when people emailed her at 11pm the night before the exam she pushed it a week. most profs will not do that!  yes the study guides were long but they were copy paste from the powerpoint. inquziitives were sometimes challenging but just sit down and do them. she offers a lot of extra credit and curved the exams. take her!

While Dr. Isaac is very nice and the class is interesting, I personally found it very difficult to grasp/memorize some of the material. Study guides are very long and you need to study early in order to understand everything for your exams. The labs were interesting though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the class, I didn't find it to be too difficult. If you find it challenging at given points, multiple resources are available. I highly recommend taking this class in general!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a very kind person, but she goes through class material very fast, and expects you to remember everything. Study guides are 7 or more pages long, and are only posted a week in advance. Overall, it is way too much work for a 200-level class, but it is very interesting.

For ANP 206. I like her as a person but not necessarily as a professor. For her exams we have to study over 10 pages of material (yes it is as bad as you think) and when we emailed her about it she was very passive aggressive. For a 200-level class it is a lot of work that we have to put in. Labs are easy. Tests are difficult based on memorization.

Dr. Isaac is a nice teacher and I can tell that she cares about teaching anthropology. However, I am taking this class as an elective credit and it is way too difficult for a 200 level class. The study guides are multiple pages long with about a hundred different time periods you have to remember. It is basically just a difficult memorization class

Taking ANP 206, there is absolutely no reason why I should be spending more time on this class than organic chemistry. Professor is nice, however 75 question midterms and multiple page study guides are a little ridiculous. Do not take this class, find a different elective. Professor is nice, however class layout is abysmal.

I took ANP 206 with Professor Isaac this semester, she is a great lecturer and makes class very entertaining. Her lectures are very fast paced however, so fast that sometimes I could not fill out my notes. When it comes to exams, it is terrible. Our first exam was 75 multiple choice questions on paper, and study guides are 12 pages long.

She is such an amazing professor, and the content is super interesting! however, there is an attached lab in this course that isn't listed online and that was more difficult than the lectures. barely any hw/quizzes, exams are easy and straightforward. Take this course if you can, I really enjoyed it!

Dr. Isaac is amazing, and so was this class! The content is so interesting, and Dr. Isaac backs up her lectures with her own experience in the field. She genuinely cares about her students and is always willing to help. She's also pretty funny. Exams are very fair, but you have to put the effort in to study. I honestly have nothing bad to say :)

Sadam is one of the best teachers at Michigan State. Arabic is a difficult language to learn, but his teaching methods are unmatched. Be sure to do the homework and required readings, he will be sure to tell you he's disappointed if you do not. Super caring guy, and attendance matters to him the most.

One of my favorite professors. Very effective at teaching Arabic, but if you don't actually want to learn, don't take him because you will fail. If you care about the language and the material and you put in the work to learn a second language, he will help you succeed. Also he's hilarious.
As long as you are passionate about the class you will succeed. Saddam is the best professor I have ever had.
Class was easy, but never graded my final and other assignments even after emailing him and talking to him in person. Assignments were turned in on time and done correctly
A really nice professor and was very interesting to listen to! Lots of participation needed in class and must attend all classes. He was very fun and easy to talk to and get to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of if not the best teacher I've ever had. He takes something as difficult as Arabic and somehow makes it easy to learn, and is engaging at the same time. This is the kind of class where you have to want to get better at, but the prof gives you the resources to be very successful. also he is hilarious

Dr. Sadam is the BEST professor I have had at MSU. He is funny, kind, smart, accommodating, respectful, professional and by far, has such a good heart. He really cares about his students and whether or not they are excelling/ learning the material. He encourages and helps students when they need it. His teaching methods are fun and effective.
He was a great professor very funny and takes into consideration a lot when it comes to this class especially with the homework and the assignments due. I would 100% recommend!!
Beware. This man is a sex offender and got charged with aggravated assault... got found with CP. Great guy though.

professor takes attendance on certain days but tells you at the beginning of the semester. homework is super easy as long as you review the in class assignments. exam is harder, but graded relatively easy. final project is the most difficult and is based on everything you do in the semester, but no final exam.
Amazing professor. Truly about students educational and personal success.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I was really pumped to take the class, but this prof's lectures sound like a student giving a presentation. For the first exam I went to every class. For the second exam I skipped every class, didn't study, and skimmed the book. I scored only 2 percentage points worse. So it's good news if you like skipping class, I guess.
Very boring class....extremely dull tone throughout the course of the semester, not really worth taking. She seems like a nice person though.
Good professor, if you study & read the book you will do well. Also helps to be a good writer. Overall easy class.
Very dull.  I had to drag myself to class every day.  Not worth it at all. Of course, as these things go, she seems like a very nice person.
