dull, very dull. General type tests which offer no surprises but some questions are tricky. Not a horrible class but not the funnest.
terrible teacher
Great professor! Very helpful
She is the sweetest!! It's an accounting class so it's supposed to be hard...
bad experience

She is not a honesty person.  She told us that we could have as much time as we want at final, but she ended it up giving only 10 minutes more.  Very few people could finish all the questions at her final. Also, she told us that the final was more like the homework.  Guess what?  Her final is a big surprise and have nothing to do with the homework.
No Comments
No Comments

Bad Professor. Gives out over 20 quizes this semester. 2 Exams that are more than half your grade and 8 homework assignments. Alot of assignments quiz given at every single class that is heavily graded. Do NOT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Mumbles during lecture, cannot understand at all. If you skipped this class you would not miss out on anything because he does not teach. Only grades in class is tests. The tests are way harder than what we learn. By far the worst instructor I have ever had in history. I ask for help on practice problems and tells me ask my classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures in a mumbling Russian accented voice while reading straight for the pages of the book he prints off. Even less helpful in person. He explains everything as 'intuitive' and 'obvious'. I took calc two years ago and could not learn from him. the Class gets exponentially harder at the end and you won't get through all the material for the exam
SUCKS and can't teach at all!  Tests are way too hard and you can't understand what you are supposed to do for them, and what you are supposed to be learning.
Professor Ivanov is a great teacher!  He has an amazing ability to make graduate-level mathematics very easy to understand.  Take his classes if you enjoy math!  :-)

He seems to have decent knowledge of the subject, but its often difficult to understand what he says or writes.  Tests are almost impossible, quizzes are homework problems, but still difficult.  Make sure you show all work and use the right notations.  Wouldn't suggest taking a class with him at all.

Ron is a great professor and he might be tough on you, but overall his goal is to prepare you for your future as a PKG professional and I think he does an exceptional job at that. As long as you go to class and pay attention to what he is saying you should do well. Exams are long, but should be easy if you have pay attention and take time to study.

He gives awful exams and thinks he is god. 22 out of about 50 students received under a 50% and he blamed the students for not listening to the lectures. He is rude and thinks that he is the best lecturer to walk the earth. In reality he is the worst instructor I have ever had.

PKG 315. This has been the worst class I've ever taken. You will lose track of what he is saying halfway through the sentence because he talks so slow. I used to feel bad for him because he seemed sad, but I don't anymore. He gives very unfair exams that have material he doesn't teach you in the lectures. He is grumpy and creepy.

Not good a teaching.  He reads off the slides verbatim without adding anything else in lectures.  Fairly easy class though. He puts the slides online, but there are only 2 exams which are really hard!  The course average was low so he curved it!! That was nice!
The class is really easy if you go. It is somewhat interesting but can get a little boring.

Sweet guy, fine professor. He doesn't really teach the material for the labs (which is the majority of the course hours). Try to learn the MatLab coding on your own time and build relationships with your labmates and instructures.
Lectures were good and easy to follow. Lab depends on TAs but the content wasn't hard.

I understand the reasoning behind why one would not prefer a final assessment; however, the decision to use a group project worth 20% of our grade and an individual one worth another 20% is incredibly stressful. New topics and ideas were covered, but help was limited, and printed instructions were convoluted, misleading, or insufficient.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very engaging lectures

At the time of writing this review I'm a freshman, and this is my favorite course I've taken at msu so far. The lecture for me was a little early but it was always entertaining plus you learn a good amount in lecture. The majority of this class are the labs which consist of group projects in matlab(programming) and a few in excel

Took the honors section of this class. The TA are very helpful when you are confused on something and very attentive. The professor is very nice and explained very throughly when anyone had any questions. Quizzes are a bit difficult but if you do the practice quizzes you should be well prepared. Overall great professor.
Professor Smith is a great teacher, EGR 102 is mostly labs with TAs teaching but Friday lectures with Professor Smith are never boring. Definitely worth taking it with him.
Very sweet professor and person overall, the class just sucks. It all depends on who your TA is and if you get a good group if you do well or not in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor himself is okay but never responds to emails. The TAs are what grade the projects and they are not helpful at all. No clear grading rubric and the organization of the class is poor. Based on groups and if group members don't help the TA doesn't care. The projects get hard toward the end do depend on the ULAs more than TAs.
Professor Smith had great enthusiasm for lectures every Friday morning and he encouraged students to do their best by working with other students via lab and class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Jason was pretty good for the semester. The weekly quizzes aren't great in the beginning but if you're attentive to your TA then it's easy to get by. You do have to buy the online textbook but that's what the quizzes and reading grades are based on. Overall pretty easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Took the honors section of EGR102 and had prof Smith as my main instructor in the lab. Very helpful and overall a very nice guy. He helps students understand the material so they can succeed and his assistance was very helpful as coding is very confusing as a beginner.

Professor Smith is a great guy, he explains material well and has a great personality. Labs are the most important part, you will do group coding projects, so getting a good group is important. Grading will vary based on TA, but they will help you with your project during lab, so you should end with a high grade. Weekly quizzes. Course is very fun.

Fun professor, he taught the content of the course well. Lectures usually went over the next topic with a good tutorial of how to do the next week's lab project. Hope for a good team for labs (randomly selected). There's a big project each week, but it's manageable with a good team and you can get it all done during the labs most weeks with no HW.

Professor Smith is a really nice guy and is really helpful when you reach out to him. You have to go to the labs if you want to pass the class. The group projects can be a little confusing and stray from the lectures but if you show up to class and ask for help you can get them done.

Professor Smith was a nice guy. The problem I did have was his teaching didn't equate w/ the projects we were given. In lecture I understood everything he taught; however, the projects were always so confusing & much more difficult. For example, in lecture we would practice w/ ~5 lines of code, yet projects are 20-100 (or more) lines of code.

Professor Smith seems like a great guy. He was super light on homework and if you just show up to labs you'll likely be fine in this class. If you don't get a good group it'll make the class harder but it's still manageable. There's also no exam, just final projects, which was nice (although the final group project was kind of all over the place).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: What a guy! Jason Smith is an awesome professor. I really enjoyed this class. It was fun, and I think that anyone could do it if they kept up with everything. As long as you go to class, and do all of the assignments, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class online and it was very tough!! Jason as well as the TA's were very helpful in getting back quickly on Piazza as well as having office hours over video chat. I would recommend this professor, but do know that the class itself is so much work! I got a 4.0 but barely, (90.07% where the 4.0 mark was a 90%)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a really good professor, attendance is not required, but if you don't go to the lab sessions you will not pass the class. The lab sessions are where you learn everything for the homework and the tests. Tophat is used as participation during lectures.

Very lively professor, always had a funny joke or story to liven up class in the morning. Online lecture videos and supplemental material are made by himself, which I appreciate. Labs clearly relate to lectures given during the semester and are often fun and always engaging. Probably the best professor I have ever had.
FOR 101 was one of the best classes I have taken as a freshman! The labs were always interesting and engaging, and professor Saralecos was always easy to work with and enjoyable to listen to.

FOR 101 was an incredibly easy and insightful course! The online course has a very clear structure, and it is very easy to follow along with. The course is made up of 4 assignments, 6 tree time tests, 6 exams, and a "tagging trees" assignment, but it is SO easy! You learn about Michigan Trees, so it is a cute class (easy 4.0)!

Easy class and the exams and quizzes were also pretty easy. The only problem I ever had was the websites he uses for the assignments, however there is only 4 and once you know how to use them its easy but figuring it out at first was a struggle for me. The tagging trees was easy and it's funny seeing random people doing the same thing as you.

Easy online class. No textbook. Every 2 weeks you have to complete 2 tests, open note. After units 3 and 6 you have to "tag" 20 trees noting the trees type, age, where it's native to, etc. It is easy, he allows you to be unsure about its type, just time consuming.

Such a sweet guy, I had a lot of fun in this class! I took it for credits online, but I feel like it would've been a lot of fun in person! You get to tag trees for your final, really fun and easy hands-on stuff, loved this class!

This class was overall easy because our work was due biweekly. However, the assignments could be so confusing to follow which would take up so much time to complete. The tree tagging assignments are easy, but it can be difficult to find trees that aren't tagged as all the trees on campus and the surrounding areas all tagged - no even exaggerating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There was a lot of reading and notes, but not a super heavy amount. Throughout the course you get to tag trees, which is super easy. 10/10 I would take this class again!

Currently taking FOR101, it is an easy class overall. The only difficult and most time consuming thing is the assignments. Sometimes they can even be difficult to follow along. Other than that, lectures are interesting, test and exams are every two weeks, but not too bad compared to the assignment.

I took this class because I was looking for an easy, low work elective. Although it was straight forward there was more work and lectures than I thought. His units are 2 weeks long and he gives you about 4-6 hours of lecture to watch before the test and exam. It is an easy class and is great but some people were complaining about the workload

Professor Saralecos is a great professor! I took his class online asynchronously but he was still very easy to contact and helpful. Not too much homework and overall a pretty achievable 4.0! The content was also pretty interesting!

Great professor, very passionate about his field and makes lectures engaging. Does a great job of designing the course so students actually learn relevant and interesting content, and he actually wants to support students. There's a lot of homework, but it's all easy, you just have to keep up with it and turn things in on time. Fun class overall!

Professor Saralecos is an amazing professor. His lectures were easy to understand and his class format was very easy to follow. He was also very accessible outside of class. This class should be an easy 4.0 if you do the work, which is incredibly simple and easy.

Professor Saralecos was one of my favorite professors, he is so funny, caring, and super passionate about what he does. Classes were always somewhere new and I always had a fun time with our activities. There were mid sized writing assignments every week and a discussion post, but if you're on top of it you'll do great in the class.

Caring and kind professor, willing to work around your schedule. We met once a week for our lab, that was in a different location each week, but the labs he set up were enough to keep you engaged. Other than that everything is done online. I didn't like the essay assignments, though they were easy, just long. Very good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Saralecos is great, he is funny and engaging and does a great job with presenting new material. This class is held outside, and he sets up lots of cool and useful activities for us. The bulk of the work is done online, and the writing assignments can be a little overkill. Otherwise the class is really fun and easy, as long as you participate.

She's very nice but the lectures are hard to follow. The material itself is not that difficult, but you end up teaching yourself most of it. The grading scale also feels unfair, and the required packet does not align with what is covered in lectures. The slides are not her own, and she mostly reads off them without deeper explanation.

She's very nice, but I found myself not understanding what was going on in lecture, where'd she'd kinda just repeat the same things over and over. The course pack was different to the lecture slides and I found myself getting the most out of the class through recitation.

I'm not sure if I am just good at accounting or not, but I didn't find her class too hard. The biggest thing was that the course packet for the class didn't match the actual slides, so it was kind of hard to follow along in class. The exam setup and process to get to the answer are very similar to the practice exams in Connect.

Lori is SUPER nice but I genuinely have not learned a single thing since coming to this class. Every day I go to her lectures I stare at the slides and have no clue what's going on - and I think this is because she didn't create any of the material she uses. The workbook makes no sense and half the time doesn't even correlate with the slides.

She is a nice lady, but her lectures are all over and hard to follow. She doesn't show much energy, has bad slides, and overall the class doesn't seem full ready to be taught, since the course book isn't complete and HiTa isn't set up. Be prepared to learn the material yourself.

Very nice teacher but it's impossible to understand what she's teaching. The notes packet doesn't match the slides and I can't tell what she's trying to get across most of the time. First exam was easy but after that it's downhill.
Absolutely loved this professor, she is so sweet and genuinely passionate not only about accounting but also about her students' success. By far one of my favorites, especially for a required course.
I don't know what I was taught the entire semester. The teaching wasn't on point.
Beware! Didn't have a nice time doing this course. Kinda difficult to understand what is taught.
Great professor, content can get challenging at some points.
Super nice professor, online exams, attendance not mandatory, one group project at end of semester. very caring. Curved everyones grades at end of semester.

Professor Lambert has been one of the best professors I have ever had. He is very knowledgeable and helps you to see different perspectives on things we overlook in everyday life. I recommend taking his class; it is very interesting, and I think most people would get a lot out of it.

TAKE THIS CLASS. Easiest 4.0 ever. His lectures are long and boring, but the assignments are so easy, and he grades very fairly. He genuinely cares about his students and wants to connect with all of them.

Do not take this course. In the syllabus there are two books to purchase but you will also end up printing about 20 other readings. Harsh grader, will give no credit for completed work because it is "inaccurate" meanwhile the assignment will be opinion based. Too much work for a 100 level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I found the workload really manageable, and none of the assignments or exams were especially challenging

Cool and knowledgeable teacher, be ready for a very BORING lecture. I think this is more so on the class but its slow and boring. Quizzes and exams are easy asf, can fade 4 classes. Gives pop quizzes (16 of them, 12 are graded) but you can fade. I faded probably 10 times and still easily passed without reading once. Writing assignments are light.

Overall the class was easy to complete. He is very lecture heavy but does allow for discussion. Attendence was not mandatory but there are assignments asked during class and he gives 16 (12 in grade book) so you can miss 4 quizzes w/out penalty Recitation is required (can miss 3x). Perfers hand written notes he does not like tech. boring but easy

He will try to scare you the first day of class, but the class is very easy. He's going to summarize everything in the readings that's relevant for the tests in class so intensive reading is not needed. Very passionate about what he teaches and will ask for class participation often.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lambert's lectures were always interesting and helpful in preparing for exams and assessments. The course is well designed and expectations are clear. Attendance is required as there are graded in-class assessments randomly. Very light course as long as you complete the readings and pay attention during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Most boring and Un-useful class I've ever taken. If you need an IAH don't take this unless u love philosophy. So heavy philosophy based it's insane. All he does is yap about the readings he assigned. A lot of reading and a lot of written assessments based off them. You have to go to the class to get credit. Not a hard, just strange and boring 2/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, doesn't use much technology and instead outlines work very well in class. Very easy to keep up with as long as you pay attention in class. Highly recommend.

Amazing Professor. In my first semester of college, I enjoyed his class the most by far. I wasn't always focused, and it was okay; he and his TAs were there to help whenever needed. Doesn't take attendance, but we had random pop quizzes, and as long as you did them, you basically got a 4.0. Very kind and accommodating to anything you might need.

This guy is great, highlight of my semester. Lots of interesting reading and lots of essays. The essays are fantastic as they make you think and, as long as you mention the broad points you can write about it anyway you want. 

Its a very intellectual class.
The professor has dry humor but if you like that you will find him funny.

Not a fan of Professor Lambert. For an IAH class that has almost zero benefit for anyone taking it he is way too serious.  You have atleast one essay a week if not more, and they are graded on a 4 point scale. You do one thing wrong and your grade is automatically a 75%. Class is boring and more than half the class stopped coming. Bad feedback too
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Lambert's lectures were engaging. He was a tough grader on certain assignments, lowering them easily, and is not afraid to give a 0 if he's the one grading instead of a TA. He is also not one to help out a student. The cutoff was a 3.66 to be rounded to a 4.0, and I ended with a 3.65, which I went to office hours about, but no help was offered.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved Dr Lambert! Attendance was not mandatory, so unfortunately, no one ever showed up for class, but they were to be honest missing out. He made class very engaging, and honestly, I learned a lot. I 100% recommend and definitely recommend going to the class, even though it is not graded by attendance.

Had him for fall semester, great class, and super knowledgeable on the material. Very clear guidelines for each assignment on the syllabus, so as long as you follow it you should get an easy 4.0. Decent amount of writing and 1-3 readings every week, but easily manageable.
LOVE LOVE LOVE, very understanding and really connected with this class. Great professor, gives good feedback, and easily gives out 4.0s
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Class is super easy. Attendance isn't required, but you won't be able to write critical thinking questions or papers if you don't have an idea of what he talks about in the lecture. He is very passionate and can come off a little harsh but overall hes a cool guy

Really enjoyed this class, 6 weekly reflections that you can do over 14 weeks, 5 critical thinking questions, 2 short papers and one final paper. He has really clear instructions for each assignment so you know exactly what he's looking for. Lectures aren't mandatory but recitation is, class is mostly just discussion on the week's reading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Lambert is very clear on the syllabus about what the expectations of the course are, and if you follow the criteria, you should end the class with a 4.0. Attendance is not mandatory aside from recitation, however going to lecture can help with the writing assignments. If you don't mind reading and writing, I would recommend his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Lambert can come off as intimidating at first but he is a really caring and passionate person and wants you to do well. Class is pretty much all discussion about the readings, so it is not necessary to go to all lectures (but they are beneficial). The grading is very clear cut, if you do what is says on the syllabus; you will get a 4.0 easily.

I really enjoyed Dr. Lambert's class. Dr. Lambert is very passionate about his feminist views, so if you share those views take this class. If you don't, do not. He assigns readings and holds discussions about them in class, so make sure you do the readings and participate in discussion. A few very short written assignments and no exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring lectures and gets off topic very easily. Goes on rants about things not related to the readings or topic of his lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are long and take up the entire time designated time. Class is easy and interesting as long as you put a little effort into reading some of the content. I would recommend this class.

He recently redesigned the class and made it much easier. The content is incredibly interesting and his lectures are fun to attend. Dr. Lambert is clearly passionate about what he's teaching and it shows. He really wants to see you put in effort, but honestly you don't have to to get a good grade. I loved this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: do not take this class in the morning, while its interesting material it is also incredibly boring. attendance is not taken but there are a lot of in class assignments with no warning to catch skippers (me) and it can hurt after a few. dr. Lambert is a nice guy though and really cares about his students, if you miss something he'll be cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I had him in the Fall of 2022 and looking back at it this was by far my favorite class and my favorite professor. Starting that class thinking I would hate it but ended up loving it. Class is easy if you show up and actually listen to the Lectures.

I'm not even done with this class yet, but I want to make sure he gets the rep that he deserves on here. He is very personable and remembered my name because he's seen me at work a few times, even though I'm quiet in class. IDK if it's just my TAs, but I put minimal effort into writing (never full essays!) and have aced every "paper."
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is two hours long which felt so long but they always made you actually think about the world we live in, and he seemed to care. The beginning seemed kind of slow with book but towards the end I probably learned more in any of my other classes. If you try on the papers and take your time, you get a good grade. Forces you to talk in class.

Professor Lambert always grades and assigns work with the student's best interests in mind. The assignments for the course are not difficult, but force you to think. He gives clear feedback and guides you to improvement on the next assignment. Professor Lambert provided intellectually challenging material interesting and/or relevant to the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Loved this class and would take it again with him. I would make sure to read the material. If you read the material you will do good in the class. Lots of class discussions and a couple of random assignments (sort of like pop quizzes but really easy). Definitely go to class because you will develop a deeper understanding of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I've never felt the need to rate a professor before but I'm taking his upper level IAH course next year because I enjoyed his course so much. Reading wasn't super heavy and usually reasonable. The way he lectures and speaks gives incredible perspective of racial and gender inequalities and gave me a greater perspective on my own identities.
The class is not confusing if you actually pay attention, go to recitation and office hours. He is a funny guy and very passionate about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: So insightful and straightforward. There are basically only 12 assignments in total.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment:
-i didn't read and still did well
-as long as you turn in the assignments and actually try you will be fine
-very liberal and will tell you his views
-go to class, he does in class assessments which basically serves as a pop quiz
-allows you to drop one assignment from each category 
-2 hours long
-easy
-always changing due dates
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: On the first day of class, he claimed that nothing he lectures about is his opinion, yet has lectured completely biased every class and pretty much invalidates any opinion that contradicts his. Basically if you don't have far left liberal views, you will not be right in his class.

You're going to want to do the readings for his class, if you do the readings you don't really need to go to the lecture. His grading is not very hard, just know what you are talking about! Most of the quizzes are on Quizlet but not all, the PowerPoint really help with quizzes.

Wonderful man and wonderful professor. If you are willing to listen to others and discuss ideas, you will love his classes. If you are not open to other ideas and diverse perspectives, you will not like him. Overall, best PHL prof I have had at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class was easy and the papers don't take long as long as you write down what he says during class and put it in ur papers. Problem is is that we have the same conversation over and over and it can be really frustrating when the same question is asked in different words a lot.
The best professor I have ever had. Very engaging and respectful with material. Loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Just, no. Dont waste your time with this class. Probably the harshest grader Ive ever had. One little thing wrong with your paper turns into a D grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Horrible
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lambert completely controls all lecture discussions and also grades papers in a completely subjective way. That is, he looks for a correct interpretation of the text and if youre not spot on (in his mind) you will be marked down for it. Discussions are boring and only consist of his own notesnot discussion. Not a way to teach a PHL class IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He says attendance isn't mandatory but then gets very angry when people don't go. I understand he cares about what he's teaching, but he doesn't get that people are enrolled in his class because the university makes us take 2 IAHs, and makes it more difficult than necessary. Cool info to learn about though.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you are thinking about taking his class... just dont do that to yourself. He tries to make kids that dont go to class fail and chooses favorites. If you look at the wall you should be scared for him to yell at you. He says this class is not about opinions, but the whole class is based on his opinions. He thrives off of the power that he has.

Lambert was a good teacher overall but there were so many books to read and essays to write. He says attendance is not required but you should definitely go because he asks questions on the exam about videos he showed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Lambert was a good professor, his lectures were very interesting and easy to stay tuned into. You aren't graded by much though and half of your grade is made up of the final and the last paper. Overall, the class was not too hard and he was a good professor. You HAVE to go to lectures, though, or you are going to have a rough time on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Enjoyed his lectures, does grade somewhat tough but the final was set up to boost your grade.

Professor Lambert is a nice guy but gets on your nerves. My class started to not show up halfway thru so he made attendance mandatory or else he wouldn't share his slides at the end of the year. Don't let him catch you on your phone he WILL single you out. He opened my eyes to a lot of things concerning race so his class was important and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Irina Kadyrova is a very sweet lady! She is retiring this spring. Despite her passion for teaching, her accent is thick Ukrainian and hard to understand, and the online classes are VERY boring. All HW, quizzes, and exams are online and unproctored, so there is NO reason you shouldn't get an A. TAs pick up most of the heavy lifting in teaching.

She struggled a lot with the technology and was hard to understand sometimes. She didn't grade too hard and the content wasn't too hard to understand. Biggest problems would be her accent and lackluster explanations of some concepts, but the work load was not too much and the quizzes were not too hard.

If this is your last math class at MSU, you should take MTH116 with Kadyrova. If this isn't your last, there are much better options. She is a very good professor, but online math lecture is not worth it.
Professor Kadyrova is a sweet person, but her heavy accent makes the class a struggle. Utilize resources like unstuck ai, the textbook, and TAs to grasp the content.

She has a very thick accent that makes her hard to understand. Often slips up when speaking and takes a while to explain topics. She doesn't explain them thoroughly so I rely on asking the TA my questions. If you ask for help she just explains it again instead of helping you. She uses webassign yet doesn't understand how to retrospectively grade .
Very difficult to understand and she has a hard time explaining things sometimes. She has zero sympat

Professor Kadyrova isn't awful, but it is very hard to understand her. She is a very sweet lady, but you definitely need to have some other resources to get a grasp on what you're learning. All the exams and homework assignments are online and on the same platform so if you do your homework, you'll do well on the exams.

The class isnt that bad as the workload is pretty light compared to others. However I would rather go thru 3 rounds of medieval torture instead of sitting thru another zoom call. She is a very sweet person, but to this day I cant grasp how someone can speak so slowly and still write fast as hell.
class is easy, but when asking for help she just tells you what you did wrong instead of actually helping.

Prof. Kadyrova is an old Russian woman with a difficult-to-understand thick accent. Her lectures are online thankfully, but very boring, and not always very helpful. I often find myself having to google concepts. Homework is pretty light and there are weekly quizzes and 4 exams, no final exam thankfully. She isn't that bad, but there's better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She is a good professor but it does help to have some baseline understanding of precalculus concepts before taking the class. She is sometimes hard to understand in a lecture hall but I could fill in any gaps with context clues (this as someone with regular auditory processing issues). She will help you with problems if you can show her your work.

I four pointed this class, but if you're taking math 116 do not take it with this professor. I took trig in high school and passed it, but her material is still hard. I pretty much did all the work myself and she's very strict in lecture, and her teaching just didn't make sense to me. (Not to her own fault) but she can be difficult to understand.

Should have dropped her class 1-2 week in. Obviously she has an accent and hard to understand, but she is a nice person. TA help a lot, shoutout Cameron. There are weekly quizzes and like 4 lowest ones are dropped. Had 4 exams and no final. Had to pay $100 to do my homework. She reads off of a slideshow and explains things the most complicated way

Didn't go to lectures after the first week because I couldn't understand her. Quizzes and Tests are all on D2L and WebAssign. If you are new to the topic don't take this professor. If you do take this class find a friend that is good at math that can help you.

Worst class i've ever had to endure. Unfortunately (by no fault of her own), I could not understand a single thing said in this lecture. As someone who struggles a little with math, I strongly recommend you don't take this course with her. Most of this class was self-taught, alongside having to go to the math help center bi-weekly.

She's pretty hard to understand but you get used to it after a while. Even then, I didn't feel like I got much out of her lectures. If you want to do well I'd recommend the MLC and going to recitation. Although I will say her class structure is super easy compared to other math classes, no final and everything is online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: If new to the topic of your class do not take this professor. Hard to understand and seems to not like in class questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did not like this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Irina is very smart and understands calculus better than the instructor. I have her for my recitation for my asynchronous MTH132, and while her accent may be hard to understand at first , she is very good at explaining and every time I join her recitation I learn something that was not posted in the webinar or pre lecture videos. Overall she tries.

Tries to be understanding, she moves due dates back if students are having issues. I found her lectures teach me nothing, it easier to teach yourself the material through doing the hw on WebAssign. The homework isn't super difficult, and the tests are the same as what you see on the homework. However the quizzes are hard and only a few questions.
Lots of homework. At times the lectures do not make sense. Everything I learned was mostly through Khan Academy. Very boring lectures that could have been improved and made more interesting.

This class is pretty much completely self-taught. There are weekly quizzes and a weekly homework assignment both of which are graded off of correctness which makes this class difficult when you don't understand the content. She also is extremely hard to get ahold of and often ignores questions, she does seem sweet however.

Barely understand her when she speaks because of her thick accent, isn't interactive and her homework is nearly impossible. Graded homework, quizzes, and exams, no partial credit if half of the problems are correct or for your work. If you even put a space accidentally, it will count it wrong and you can't do it again. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES!

Couldnt understand her in a single lecture and contemplated skipping classes because I wasnt getting anything out of the lecture anyway. Had to rely on working on homework with friends because I gained no knowledge through the lecture.

SHE CONNOT BE UNDERSTOOD! She is one of the worst professors I have ever had in my life! She is rude when people ask questions and mumbles through the whole lecture. Lectures are unhelpful and many times a waste. The recitations and MLC are your best bets for learning anything.

The lectures were online with in-person recitation, and recitation was far more helpful than the lectures. She's hard to understand due to her intense use of technical math vocabulary. The lectures are slow, yet the material goes by very quickly. She's also very blunt. Overall, a pretty difficult class, with homework and quizzes every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kadyrova is caring and understanding, she wants to see you do well. The class isn't easy super easy though, you have to put some work into it. Personally I could've gotten by without buying the textbook, there's enough information in lectures/recitation/online. Basically if you put the work in, ask for help when needed, you should be ok.

Absolute worst classroom experience I have ever had seriously makes me wonder how she got a job here had her as both a professor and TA and I will jump off a bridge if I have her again barely speaks English, ignores most questions if she does see your question will get mad at you for asking highly doubt she understands the material she teaches
She moves fast and it can be hard to understand her. She also gets mad when you ask a question.

This class was honestly a joke, and dont bother buying a textbook. The class itself is completley self taught, going to lectures is pointless. The material itself was not tough, quizzes are on d2l and exams are on some other website with no lockdown browser.  Dont panic if you have her, just be ready to teach yourself the whole class.

She is hard to understand at times but I've had many foreign math teachers so I was used to it. Follow along with what she's doing in the lecture and do practice problems and the class is fairly easy.

Honestly don't bother with the lectures. It's hard to understand anything and it is not necessary to pass. Take advantage of recitations and if you do need extra help just go to the math help room or talk to TA. She seems nice though and the class is not very hard overall, just lots of work.
Can't understand a work she's saying, and the TAs didn't give answers during recitations so you couldn't even see if you did things right until the next day or so when they were posted
She's a bit too silly (derogatory) for my liking

Do not do what I did and think that you can get past an accent. Her accent is very thick and she is very hard to understand. She is also not caring at all. The class material itself isn't too bad, but I think any other professor would have made it a lot easier. Avoid if you can!

Spoke quickly in lectures and rarely went over things multiple times. Often was mean to those who asked her questions in class. I was in her online course so it definitely could have made an impact on my experience, but I did not enjoy this class.

Lecture attendance was not required so I almost never went because I had taken plenty of algebra classes in the past. I dont need to be leaning about slope intercept form as a freshman in college. Did not communicate well with students. Class was an easy 4.0.

Professor wasn't good at all during the past semester. A strong accent combined with poor audio quality due to the online format made lectures almost impossible to understand. She also was awful at answering questions, frequently missing the point or not going into enough detail. Class itself isn't too hard, but you'll need to learn it by yourself.

Honestly the worst professor I've ever had. I struggled in this class which is not typical for me in math, and she was not helpful at all with questions or mistakes. If you end up in this class, I highly recommend you switch out. It's not worth the time nor money.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is difficult even if you have taken similar classes before. It will take a lot of time. You will be tested on things that were not in the homework. The material is not explained, and often her math is wrong. I had a waiver for the first half of the class, and I left the lectures confused on things that I knew prior. However she is nice.

I loved this professor. I will say the content in this class is difficult, but if you put in the effort and pay attention youll do fine. Theres ULAs to help if you need it and theres a lot of support too. The professor does have an accent, but after a while you get used to it and can easily understand her. Overall, she was great!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A lot of people don't like her, but honestly, I just showed up, paid attention, and did the work. I would answer questions she asked in class and didn't go on my phone (that's a big thing for her). She was super nice to me and understood if I needed more time to work things out homework-wise (I was having some computer problems at the beginning).

Class content isn't too difficult, TA's are what make it more difficult. We were often given wrong answers on the worksheets that were used as study material for the quiz. Professor Kadyrova is an understanding and nice woman, lectures aren't required, recitations are, you'll get an A as long as you make sure you know whats going on.

I think she gets too much flak for her accent. If you can't understand her, just take notes posted on D2L and you'll be fine. Going to class is not necessary to pass or get a good grade, but RECITATIONS ARE REQUIRED. If you don't know what that is, just wait until you take her class. The TAs are very helpful. Prof Irina also allows some extensions.

Weekly quizzes, graded homework(which help with exams and materials), go to recitations, they help with quizzes and material for the unit. Read the lecture slides and highlight/star equations for units. I've done precalc before so it was easy for me but maybe work with others to understand material more. Given ample amount of time to do assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Lots of homework, weekly quizzes. I stopped showing up to any classes a few weeks into the semester and still got 100%'s on quizzes and midterms. Everything is online due to covid so that may be why.

So I took this class in the midst of the corona semester where it was all online in the fall. She made multiple mistakes on the quizzes, but theyre based on worksheets we use during recitation. Irina is no help whatsoever, shes stubborn and the language barrier makes it worse. Content isnt difficult, but rely on YouTube, the MLC and your book.

DON'T TAKE HER IF YOU DON'T HAVE TO! Her lectures are boring and all she does is read off the notes. She also goes off topic a lot causing us to not get through the information we need. The recitations are fine to get help, but they aren't allowed to show you the answer to a problem which isn't helpful. Take anything but this class, it's horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I've had the pleasure of having. Steer clear of her if you can. I'm sure this would have a been a slightly different story had we actually gone on campus this year, but I digress. This prof is disrespectful, refuses to acknowledge when she or her programs are wrong, and she somehow deleted our quiz. Can't learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was ridiculosuly hard. It's very hard to understand her accent. If you have questions, you might as well not answer them because she won't answer them. Quizzes every week based off of the lectures. But, lot's of times she won't give out the lecture note answers so you really need to know what you're doing in order to pass. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't bother to go to lecture, just spend that hour and a half studying online, by yourself, and you will 3.5 the class. Plus you won't be lost in translation. Use your calculator on exams, as it can do almost everything if you know what your doing. If you want to 4.0 to the class, you have to go the study center.

Kadyrova was just fine. Probably on the lower end of fine but not the worst. I was always confused and she wasn't always helpful. If you want to pass, lean on the TA and basically live at the math center.
One of the hardest classes I've ever taken. I went to every lecture and nothing ever made sense until I went to the MLC which is the only reason I did well in the class.

I went to lecture for the first week of class and then stopped. You don't need to put yourself through the hassle of hearing this professor explain concepts not in the notes or babble on and on about beautiful Russian girls. Instead of going to lecture, focus on the worksheets and quizzes due in recitation and go to the MLC and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Rambling in class, difficult to understand, rude and even disrespectful in one on one meetings. Has hard tests as well. I was looking forward to the class, as it is important to my future. I wish that she could have stayed on task a bit more while teaching. Advice for future students: Find friends to study with and make good use of recitations!

Plenty of homework, as well as weekly worksheets done during recitations that require extra study time. You'll be sinking more time than you expect into this class since you'll have to work around a useless professor and her incomprehensible lectures. Expect broken English in your textbook, worksheets, and any sort of review material.

Her accent does not impact her teaching. She's one of the best professors I have ever had. These comments that I am reading are likely from the kids who showed up, sat on their phones the entire time, and failed the tests. I showed up, listened, went to her office hours, and got an A. Anytime I had a question, she went the extra mile.

The professor does not lecture about math nor does she explain it. It's about her life. Very thick accent that's difficult to understand; took me 5 weeks to understand her accent. Don't bother showing up, just read the textbook. You'll learn more by reading the book than you will by attending the lectures. I would suggest taking a different prof.

While she is a nice person, she is not a good professor. She was very hard to understand and he lectures often made no sense. Rather than going off of the pre planned in class notes she would go on random incoherent tangents. It was so bad that in my 130 person lecture by the third week in the semester only 6-10 people were attending lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very hard to understand. Tests are hard. Shes tough, would not recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's a hard class but if you can focus for an hour every day then you'll be fine. You can't fall behind and you need to focus in class or you wont learn. Book is useful and online homework helps too
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's a challenging professor. I wish you luck.

If you've worked hard in previous math classes, congratulations because this class is 90% review. Kadyrova is useless, so I recommend asking your TA questions or forming a little group to work with. The graded homework will boost your grade, so try to rake in those hundos. Definitely do the test reviews and go to the review she has. You'll be fine.

Overall, I thought she was a good teacher. She gives you notes to print, which is really helpful and the recitation is also really helpful (if you have a good TA). She can be a bit intimidating and her accent can be hard to understand, but she really does want to help you learn the material and succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Be prepared to do double the amount of work you expect out of this class. My biggest mistake was putting my trust in her for too long, and because of that I had to put hours into getting a decent grade. Her lectures and homework assignments are meaningless. Just read the study guides she sends out and you're set if you understand the concepts.

I get that its not easy teaching in a second language, but its not hard to teach efficiently in general. Shes not approachable, shes not friendly, shes rude to her students, and makes learning precalc 3x more complex than needed.

This professor was maybe the most boring teacher I have had. Her voice was very dull which made the lectures very difficult to get through. I would see a lot of students not show up and if they did they would usually leave half way through. I feel like the amount of homework was decent, but the homework was definitely more difficult than the tests.
You need 100% attentiveness to understand her accent. The language barrier is incredibly difficult to overcome. Luckily I already took pre-calc, so retaking this class was a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Awful language barrier. Tried taking this class twice and had to drop out because of her lack to communicate both times. I thought online would be easier so I could read what she was saying instead of having to listen and even that was rough. Horrible at doing problems, does not actually teach, and when she does she just does the problem w/out expl

Absolutely terrible. Made easy concepts way more difficult than they had to be, did every problem in an extremely complicated way that was in no way necessary. Stopped going to class because there was absolutely no point in going. She gets mad when you have questions and makes no effort to be understood with her incredibly thick accent.
Terrible teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is the worst teacher ever. Nothing else needs to be said. There is literally no reason to go to lecture. If you do go you will want to tear your hair out. Good luck.
Makes mistakes on problems during lecture and online notes even her tests have mistakes.
Worst professor I have had and the tests are hard and makes everything way more difficult than it needs to be.
Lectures seem long and boring. The material she taught was not that difficult, but the way she taught it was not useful and often made an easy concept seem confusing.

Kadyrova was hard to understand in lecture and often times her lectures would be confusing and hard to follow. She often regraded tests because she was unhappy with the TA's grading and she would change grades on some tests and not others even though the answers were exactly the same on both of them.
Not a great professor. She gets mad if you ask questions and always makes mistakes when doing math.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Irina is hands down the worst math professor. My recitation TA even believes she should be fired, but the problem is she has tenure. Parts of this class are easy and some parts are difficult. The class should be an easy 4.0 if you do the extra credit and do decent on tests, but I would avoid this professor at all costs.

During lectures she doesn't explain the process of working out problems, she doesn't spend enough time on challenging concepts, and her expectations of what to know for tests are unclear. The content itself is not terrible, it is just the teaching style that could improve. Avoid this professor at all costs or prepare to teach yourself with youtube.
She is not a good teacher to begin with, she doesn't explain anything and then she has the thickest accent which doesn't help.
Worst teacher ever possible. Does not talk nearly loud enough to hear in lecture and has an extremely strong accent, making it very difficult to understand her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Awful. You have to learn everything on your own or find a tutor. Her lectures are hard to understand and she doesn't explain things well at all. Recitation might help if you have a good TA. Not being rude but the teacher is foreign so I would try to get an american TA that you can understand. I would avoid this class at all costs if possible.
Her lectures are basicsally useless, she commonly makes mistakes. Most students after the first week have been using the MLC instead of attending her lectures.

This class was made needlessly difficult because of poor teaching. Dr. Kadyrova's explanations of material did not make sense, and most students depended exclusively on recitation to learn anything. Attendance drops astronomically throughout the year because the lectures are so unhelpful. The night class has another teacher, take that if you can.
If you follow the notes and go to recitation (which was mandatory) then you can easily get a 4.0. The final exam was easy and I studied all weekend for it and it was so super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Shes really hard to understand during lectures, makes frequent mistakes, & be prepared to be spammed with emails. The textbook is only required for the worksheets in it.  The MLC and recitation will help you learn the material. Offers a good amount of extra credit. Do the reviews, they are essentially what the exam will be.

She's the only professor for MTH116, so you're kind of stuck with her (or at least I was). Her lectures can be confusing. Sometimes, I left class more confused than when I went in. Lecture attendance is optional. Exams are similar to the review. I learned everything from my recitation TA, so honestly if you go to recitation, you'll definitely pass.

Good luck trying to figure out your grade, you won't have the class registered on D2L so you won't really know by the end of the semester. Lectures are borderline optional, but you will actually learn in recitation so I strongly recommend you go to those.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her accent was hard to understand. You need to work hard to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The mathematics isn't bad, its just the professor. Her Russian is very thick and hard to understand and she doesn't always finishes a problem or explain how to do it very well. I stopped going to the lectures and got myself a personal tutor instead.

Kadyrova is an awful teacher. She has a very thick accent that makes it impossible to understand what she is saying during lecture. She commonly makes calculation errors and mistakes while trying to solve problems. If a student asks a question, she assumes the question before the student even finishes asking. Go to the MLC for help instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I would not take a class with her again. Her accent is very difficult to understand, and on top of that, her grammar is not great. The textbook is "required," but it is only used to rip out the Problem Sets in the back. The rest of the book is only used for recommended problems. I would just buy the online access code if possible.

-Accent really bad, not her fault but still -No point in lecture, besides knowing the pace of the class -Often uploaded wrong notes and made mistakes in class -Took this class in high school and still struggled, requires a lot of time and work put in -A good TA or MLC is key to understanding topics -Offers up to 40 points in EC, which saved me
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I think a lot of people are hard on her because her accent is thick, but the more you go to class the more used to it you get. She is always providing extra credit opportunities after exams and she holds study sessions almost every week. The material is not too hard and she explains it pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Literally the worst professor I've ever had. She knows what she is doing but does not know how to teach. If you have this class i would definitely recommend dropping it while you can because it will kill your GPA. I got a 100 in pre calc in high school, and all the work we did was the same. The organization of the class sucks is all based off exams
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The accent is heavy and takes some getting used to. Other than that she is a phenomenal professor. Highly knowledgeable and she cares deeply for her students and their success. Utilize her office hours!
She's has a strong Russian accent and is a bad professor

She's Russian so don't plan on being able to listen and know what she's saying at all. My advice for this class is to make sure you have a good TA that explains or simply, that you can understand. She was the worst professor I've had but you have to get through the class because she's the only one for 116, so good luck.

The class is easy to pass, but Kandryova makes it harder with her lectures.  The lectures do next to nothing for her students and you will realize that about 2/3'ds of the class skips because other students realize this too.  She is quite literally the worst teacher I have ever had as a student.  Period.  I passed only from my own work.
She saved my grade. She's rough around the edges, but she's Russian for goodness sake,  give her a break. She's always available to help and is amazingly knowledgeable.
I really haven't learned anything from Kadyrova. I'm essentially going off of what I learned in high school

I only go to lecture because I paid for it.I never got past the accent so her lectures are pretty confusing. If anyone asks a question she gets so frazzled and confused. Going to lecture isn't necessary but go to recitation.  I was stuck with a bad TA so the MLC saved my life.

Kadyrova's class was very pointless. You cannot understand her so it is not helpful to go to the lectures, you learn everything with your TA in recitation. MY TA was very helpful and he retaught everything in a way that made more sense.

I had recently taken precalc in high school, therefore, this subject comes easy to me. Although Kadyrova has a Russian accent, she is funny and knows what she's talking about. Once you get pass the accent, you begin to understand what she's saying and she often clears things up. Only downfall is some of her reviews have incorrect answers.

Pointless to go to the lecture, the teaching is just about useless. I took pre-calc as a junior in high school and passed easily, but for some reason I was placed back into this class this year and I'm struggling to pass. The recitation is the only time you will actually learn, and use of the MLC is crucial to understanding even simple topics.
I go to class just to show up because i paid for it. My T.A. teaches everything that I need to know.

She is very nice and encourages you to come to her for help but you can't understand her and it takes her 50 minutes to explain 2 problems because she goes off on tangents about pointless math. Just go to the mlc.. It's a lifesaver

Absolutely useless teacher everything is learned in recitation, Examples have almost no relevance to actual test. Lecture is honestly pointless to go to you will learn nothing with her thick accent, bad jokes, and poor teaching method when you can understand her.

I didn't even bother going to classes. As long as you go to recitation you will be fine. I recommend definitely going to help rooms though because they are awesome and saved my butt. You definitely need the book but you can't resell it which sucks.

Her accent made her incredibly hard to understand. She also wasn't helpful at all. I set up a meeting with her to go over my notes, and she continually canceled or blew me off until I stopped trying. Very difficult and frustrating.

She posts the practice exams online then she posts the STEPS OF HOW TO DO THE SOLUTIONS. The practice exams are usually harder than the real exams so it will prepare you. Extra credit exam that will give you 15 points on final. You get 10 attempts. Not hard if you're decent at math.  Accent is thick but get over it. Get a good TA & you'll be fine.

Her accent is very thick. If I hadn't taken almost this exact same math class in high school I wouldn't have done well. Ask your TA questions. The lectures aren't super helpful, but there are some good things to get from it. The textbook is only necessary for in class assignments. Never opened it otherwise.
Hard to understand her. I stopped going to lecture and relied solely on my TA to learn the material. I tried asking her a question once and she lectured me for 15 min about something I didn't ask.

Kadyrova is hard to understand in lectures and she tend to get off track. Just hope you have a decent LA. She tries to help you if you ask for help one on one but her accent is somewhat hard to understand. I do enjoy her humor though.
She's very hard to understand because of her thick accent. I ended up skipping most of her lectures and either teaching myself or counting on my TA.
Honestly one of my favorite teachers. Ignore the hate. She tells you what you need to know. The only reason to get less than a 4.0 is not trying... At all.
Her accent isn't very easy to understand and I barely ever went to lecture

Her accent is very strong indeed so its hard to follow,so most of the time you have to learn stuff on your own, but she's super nice and is always willing to help. She send notes, and her exams review are very close to the actual exam.

She is terrible! Although she has a passion for math, you cannot understand her. The lectures are pointless and you need to learn everything on your own. If your taking Calc 2, pick someone that is clear in communication because this is one of the hardest math courses I have taken!!

I don't know how anyone could say she was helpful. English class is one she must have skipped back in her day. If you speak thick Russian accent, she still won't teach you. She was so many lessons behind on our final exam there was a whole chapter our class was tested on but never was taught. Worst Professor I have experienced.

the thick russian accent isnt that bad, she obviously retains a lot of russian culture. but she is not really that good at math, she wrote my textbook and its basically worthless because of her adition i think, anyways i think she was not good at teaching but the material isnt difficult really

This class is not easy to say the least. However, the professor is very helpful if you go to her office hours. Trust me, it is worth spending some time in her office going over notes and exams. I got a 4.0 in this class and so will you. Don't hesitate to ask her questions. Also do the recommended homework and go to review sessions before exams.

Kadyrova knows what she is talking about, however, she is very condescending to her students and does not take time to make sure that the students understand the material. If you don't mind a thick accent and you are exceptional at math, you should be fine.

This professor really knew what she was talking about in the class but was basically useless when it came to getting that knowledge out to the students. She was completely unclear and snapped at some students who asked questions in class or corrected her. I do not recommend this class.

She is very confusing and unclear. When you try to ask her questions she never gives a clear response and IS NOT approachable. I e-mailed her 4 times in a 2 week period and never received a response. I then went to her office hours and she didn't have a student in there and told me to come back at a later date. She should not be a professor.
Her accent is very thick and difficult to understand. She presents easy concepts in a very difficult way and her lectures are hard to follow.

Her accent is extremely difficult to understand. In addition, she takes relatively simple concepts and makes them very complicated. I basically had to teach myself all the material or I would have failed.
cannot understand her and the review answer sheets she gives out are all incorrect
She was very confusing in lectures. I relied entirely on the MLC and my recitation TA.

her accent is hard to understand at times but she is a GREAT professor. If you attend lectures regularly and do your homework you should have no complaints, she is very helpful if you need help and cares about the course content. Give the class a chance and you will see that it is only as difficult as you allow it to be.
Irina and her class are an utter atrocity of what a math class should be. Her methods are ignorant and flawed, overall a terrible class. Lectures do not coincide with any work that is done

She is very knowledgeable about math, and is very nice. However, she hard to understand while trying to teach and it is hard to comprehend what she is talking about sometimes. She always makes herself available to help tough. Most people stopped coming to class by the end of the semester and just went to the MLC.
Very nice and knows the material but you can not understand her at all so it is pretty much all self taught. Very strong accent and jumps around on notes.
A terrible professor. Her lectures are useless and she is extremely difficult to understand. Stay away unless you want to teach yourself the material from the book.

The only reason I passed is because I took this class sophomore year in high school. So easy. Hard to understand in class, no extra help. Textbook was absolutely useless. I had to keep in contact with my high school teachers if i wanted any help at all. get used to the MLC if you have her.
She is well versed in mathematics and offers a lot of extra help.
With out a doubt the worst teacher I have ever encountered, pretty much a self taught class.

Understands math. Does not understand how to teach or present material in a clear way. Teaches straight from notes and presents material with formulas rather than examples, does not show steps in work but merely does it in a massive jumble that is nearly incomprehensible. I have always been proficient in math but I am completely lost.

Professor Kadyrova is a great professor. Yes, she has an accent, and you have to comprehend what she is saying, but she actually cares about her students. If you want to get the grade you want in her class actually do the homework and attend her reviews for exams. Her reviews are just like her exams, so put in some study hours and you'll do well...
Difficult to understand at times, which caused me drift off during the lectures
Very good at math. Hard Grader

I can understand her accent.  She just can't teach.  My friend asked a question and she responded "look in book." She says she is interested in you, but really isn't.  She makes math harder than it should be. Her "review" sessions consist of you asking questions, not her teaching. Doesn't do examples in class, and when she does, they are irrelevant

She would encourage the class to ask questions, but then proceed to be condescending when answering. Homework, worksheets and lectures, did not run in tandem. In fact the text book was mostly useless. The accent shouldn't be an issue for anyone that actually pays attention. She also provides her own review sessions.

Honestly, I think the crap she gets isn't justified at all. Yes, she has an accent! Hey, welcome to the real world kids! Sit in the front row, focus, do the homework, and you'll be fine. Yes, sometimes her English and teaching methods can be a little confusing, and that's what recitation and the Math Learning Center is for.
Not a very good professor. She cares about he material, but her accent is so thick and she is so unorganized going to lecture became useless. Try to avoid her.
Ouch.

awful experience with what I thought was my favorite subject. It became so frustrating to attend class that I began to not go. It didn't matter when I showed up to class ready to learn the lady couldn't even do the problems herself. Plus even if she did understand the material she can't talk. Avoid at all costs. waste of time and money
Accent is heavy but if you listen carefully and concentrate you can understand her. Sit in the front row, she uses a projection screen and can't see it in the back. Extremely nice and cares a lot.

Worst class I have taken so far at MSU. Her accent is so heavy I couldn't understand a word she said. When I went to talk to her after class she acted as if she knew everything and talked down to me. You can tell she cares about her students but has a poor way of showing it.

A professor who is very passionate about teaching and a sincere human being.  But to be honest, the thick accent, disorganization, and difficulty of exams made me regret not switching out of this class. I stopped going to class and instead went to the MLC to learn, just like most of the people in the class.
What are you guys talking about? Kadyrova is awesome. She has such passion for her students, she wants you to succeed, always willing to help, no matter what. Nicest professor I've ever met!
The biggest and most obvious obstacle with her is the think accent. But beyond that she can really be pretty helpful.
cant understand at all switch out into another teacher youll thank me later
She's not bad at all. The class is extremely easy, especially if you know math. Just do the homework and you'll be fine.

WORST.PROF.EVER. I don't like math but I tried really hard and still did bad. I was constantly at the MLC because going to class was useless.The class was just terribly organized to begin with. AVOID.AVOID.AVOID

not my favorite teacher.. she doesnt go in any sort of order and only teaches certain parts of each section so knowing what hw to do is very difficult. she is very hard to understand , and i do most of my learning from my TA. She does a lot of reviews, but if she cant teach me in class then i dont think the reviews would help
cant understand and teaches you something new with 5 min left in class.  sometimes quizes have material we havent covered yet

This woman was impossible to understand and half the time, corrected her own problems because she forgot how to do them. I'm sure that if I had a good TA, I would've been fine. Not worth the gamble though. Only class I didn't get at least a 3, even after going to all reviews. STAY AWAAAAAAAY!!!!!
She was pretty much useless. It was a challenge just to stay awake in class. I felt I had to teach myself the whole class

I am not a math person. Prof. Kadyrova did not make it any easier for me. Had I not taken math all four years of high school I probably would have failed this class. Kadyrova possibly the great proffesor ive ever had. She make learn fun. I love learn math now.
Don't get her as a math teacher!!

Complaining about the accent is not an excuse, although her methods of explanation aren't too clear, regardless. If you're any kind of English major/minor, know that she will butcher the language on every test/quiz/e-mail. Which lends itself to issues.

oh, honestly, her english is entirely clear most of the time, her review sessions are infinitely helpful, and, well...i'll admit that lectures are pointless but she's very good one-on-one. Besides, who wouldn't want the head of the russian mob as their prof? yeah. she kicks ass.
She didn't make any sense... at all... ever
She does not explain how to solve problems conceptually, but rather just does examples. You can get by doing this in earlier maths, but not Cal3. Do not take Calc with her unless you have to.

Pray to God that you have a good TA for recitations because you won't understand/ learn what she says in lecture.  Friday's are pointless (don't bother waking up at 9am).  If you ask questions, she rarely understands what you mean by it and will ask  you to talk to her after class.  Teach yourself, it's not that difficult.
She has such a passion for  her students! She really wants you to get a 4

I really liked Professor Kadyrova.  Her accent wasn't that bad, you could understand her very well once you got used to it.  She had lots of review sessions - if you went to those and paid attention in lecture, her class wasn't bad at all.

Once you get past the accent, she is an incredible teacher. She has really helped me to enjoy math. I have never had a 4.0 in math class before. She goes out of her way to do review sessions and provide extra help. I am so glad that I'm in her class!
Can't speak English, like...seriously !
No Comments
she can't speak english!!!
Well i'll have to quote a girl from my class to list this comment "i didnt know you needed a prerequisit in Russian to take this math class" cant understand a single word she says
