Impossible to understand.Horrible translations. Just go to class with the T.A. twice a week and get a good study group.
completely sucks. takes off points when nothing is wrong. i.e: you can have all the problems correct and get a 95%. tests are much more difficult than other profs.
you have to really listen to understand her through her thick russian accent. but makes jokes which can be funny. dont need to go to lectures but makes it easier if you do.  have to go to recitation
I hated this class, Never show up anymore because of difficulty understanding her. Just go to recitation with T.A. Don't take class if you hate math, it sucks, put it off!!
GET OUT IF YOU CAN! That's all that needs to be said.
Her Russian accent makes it impossible to understand.
Very harsh grader. Do not recommend

I just sat through a 50 minute lecture about how capitalism is bad and Karl Marx is a genius. Beware of ADV 475.... One month into the class and it's been more liberal than my freshman year ISS with a professor who had blue hair and was named Seven.

She is the best! Very relatable and lectures were engaging. She is very understanding and cares a lot. She has a lot of real word experience which she talks about to help us learn and succeed. She is a quick emailer and grade. Uses McGraw hill for assignments and quizzes, alongside a group project worth 200 points. Would 100% take her again!

Professor McDermitt is awesome! Her expectations are laid out clearly and concisely and she is a fair grader. Her lectures are engaging and entertaining due to her endless real world experiences. 10/10 would take her class again.

you can tell he cares a lot about stats. he doesn't always do the best with breaking down information in lecture but is very helpful in office hours. attendance isn't mandatory but if you show up and pay attention you will get a 4.0

This was my first time ever taking a statistics class and it was the most unorganized and confusing class. I ended up with a 4.0, but if you're confused make sure to attend office hours or ask questions in class. I give a lot of credit to my TA for helping me immensely with homework and recitation assignments. Don't be discouraged, just study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: a little quiet in lectures, but do good on the homework and 4.0 is easy, can get away without going to class as long as you look over notes before exams, practice exam questions show up on exams so do them, enjoys his job :)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kaiwen is a nice and cool professor. The exams are much easier than what you are doing in the lectures, recitations, and homework assignments.
Good professor overall, lectures are difficult to follow so attend office hours if you need help. Exams are pretty straightforward and easy.

He is incredibly kind and helpful. You can tell he really loves his job and he made this class super fun. Definitely go to class, because while you technically can do the in class assignments at home, many of them reference a specific activity you did in class or he'll tell you just to do one specific question. Grades leniently! Lots of free points

Dr. J is middle-of-the-road in terms of teaching quality, he's by no means a great professor but he also isn't terrible. He struggles with breaking down information and giving further explanations but is overall fine so long as you go to every lecture. Your TA will make or break this class, mine was terrible but if you have a good one you'll be ok.
Good professor, just kind of boring. Very easy to miss some information but as long as you follow along with the course pack in class you should do fine.
Amazing professor who truly cares about his students success in the class. Easy to get a 4.0 in if you put the effort in.

Professor Jiang was very helpful in his office hours and had a lot of patience when I didn't understand something. However, there was only one day of the week he had office hours, which was the same day the homework was due. This made it difficult to seek help for the course.

No mandatory attendance and lecture notes are posted usually within 2 weeks, or if you email he'll post them. More of a coding class than a stats class, super sweet guy overall though and really understanding. Go to class and do the homework and you'll be fine.

More of a coding class than an actual stats class, homeworks are graded and there are 2 parts to each exam. First written part of the exams are easy, coding ones are hard because they don't give you the needed codes and just expect you to know it. Just do the work and you'll be fine.

He really cares about the students' understanding of stats. During lecture he always stops to allow us to ask questions before moving onto a different topic. He said that he cares more about our actual understanding of the concepts than if we get the correct answer for every calculation. So kind as well. Great professor, would take his class again!

super nice professor, i wish he taught all my math classes! the gradescope homework is harder than the exams (there are 3 exams), but everything you need to know for the exams is in the notes or practice exams. he also responds quick to emails and is overall a really good professor!

He is a very nice guy. Lectures can get boring at times, and there is a large amount of content but it is not tough to understand. 7 assignments that are just graded on completeness. The rest of the grades is primarily exams, but as long as you review lecture slides you will be fine.

Knowledgeable on the subject, but not a good professor.  Lectures are disorganized and hard to understand, study guides are long and lazily put together, and will take forever to grade any assignments.  Don't waste your time or tuition money with him.

This class was not super easy, but not too hard either. As other students said, exams make up a massive portion of your grade, so attending lectures and studying are important. Content is easy to understand, and lectures are a bit lengthy, but he usually ends class early. I would recommend this course!

I definitely recommend this teacher. 
-no required book
-attendance is mandatory (for credit, lectures: really interesting/vital to attend to pass)
-Heavily based on the three exams throughout the semester but, as long as you attend class regularly, and study your notes for a couple days prior to the exam you should be all good.

Very knowledgeable and a great professor! Great examples and associations made to promote learning. Very straightforward. 60% lecture attendance required for 3% of your grade. The lecture slides have everything; that's why I rated him a 4 instead of a 5, because he doesn't really elaborate on the slides; class is very much him reading off slides.

Brascamp is a very nice prof, and his class is pretty interesting. This class does have A LOT of content, so the exams can be a bit hard, but if you study, you will do fine. 60% of the lectures are mandatory for attending and there are studies you have to do, but they are easy. Exams are massive part of grade, so beware of that

I'm not going to lie…the material of this class is very easy. I was able to get a good grade on tests without attending lecture. If you aren't a good test taker, go to class, and trust you will be fine. (lecture can feel very boring and lengthy)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is one of the easiest psych classes I have ever taken. The professor doesn't go in-depth, which is nice since it keeps the exams really straightforward. It is test-heavy, but honestly, the questions are super easy if you actually study and understand the material. He uses PowerPoints, SO if you miss class, you can just read the slides.

Professor Brascamp knows what they are talking about, and the lectures are very interesting. There isn't a lot of homework, and the material is easy to understand. He is super funny and makes the lecture fun to listen to.

I would recommend. Yes this class is hard and yes it is mainly lecture + exam-based. Brascamp's slides are amazing though, he is the first psych prof I've had that I genuinely learned from. He is passionate, gives tons of visuals, and explains very everything well. For exams, if you just study the slides and make a quizlet, u will be just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very heavy in content and he moves decently fast through the slides. He doesn't do much extra talking outside of what is written on the slide. Attendance isn't mandatory but you do get extra credit for going to class. There are no quizzes, just experiments and SONA. You'll definitely need to prepare for exams, but they're not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Brascamp is very knowledgeable, but I found his lectures to be quite monotone. The material is pretty interesting but complex. Graded pretty heavily on exams which I found to be pretty difficult. Could do Sona/online experiments for credit, which was nice, but if you don't do good on the exams then you have a low chance of doing well

The lecture slides did not help you on exams, 80% of your grade is exams. There is no curve, the study guides are long and not helpful for the exams. It's basically a copy and paste of the slides. Not a good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are three exams and two homework assignments; if you're not a good test taker, I wouldn't recommend it. Attendance matters, but he also offers 4 points of extra credit. He's a nice guy, and he seems passionate about the material. I thought the material was interesting, but if you don't, this class will probably be a difficult snooze fest.

This class is all based on exams and attendance. If you fail one exam you're basically screwed over because there's barely anything else that goes into the grade book. Study guides are so unhelpful, notes are so hard to follow and the class material is so dry. Don't recommend this course.

The class is solely graded on exams. If you do poor on exams, you are not passing the class. No extra credit, his lectures are so confusing and the TA's notes do not help at all. No curve in grades, this was by far the worst class I have ever taken here. I'm an empath, so I feel Jan as a person, but this class was terrible.

I've had him for LIN 463 + PSY 200, both of his lecture slides are 80 pages long that jumble up the material. Theirs a disconnect between the exams & lectures, you are given a study guide but it's vague topics to focus on. Overall, I wish he was just more straight forward in his lectures to give better understanding since exams were difficult.
There are no quizzes or anything to aid in learning. Feedback is required for biological mechanisms to learn, no? Am I an ANN? No. So disappointed. In person tests that you don't get back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but your grades are worth basically your whole grade and non are dropped so if you do bad on one exam you won't end with a good grade in the class. Rarely any homework since your homework is mainly just studying for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: love him class was kinda hard for a psych class tho but prof brascamp is awesome and super understanding and supportive

Prof. Brascamp is nice, and seems passionate about the course. But 80% of your grade is on 3 exams, no quizzes or anything. Because of this, I at most could only get a 3.0 due to getting a 75% on the first exam. A lot of the exams too have poor question correlation compared to the study guides- (which are just paraphrased lecture notes).

Great guy and very accommodating and considerate, but lectures are entirely based on slides that are pretty much read off of word for word. On top of that, the exams are quite difficult in comparison to the content as a whole. You have to study a lot to succeed in this class, and even with that, the exams often include unexpected info.

Don't know what happened between now and the past, but the style he teaches in isn't great. Most of the information given is via slideshows, but the information cherry-picked for the exams tends to never appear in the study guide or slides. As with previous posts, he's a nice guy and clearly shows a passion for the field, but not a good professor.

Do not take this class. Prof is nice but formats the class in a way that makes it nearly impossible for ANYONE to do good in it. Every exam resulted in a 24-hour straight study session the day before only to still receive a very bad grade. On top of that, this class is only graded by exams a few assignments and sona so fail one exam and that's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He clearly cares about his students doing well but unfortunately, it's very hard in this class. So much content for every exam that it's almost impossible to memorize, lectures are explained like we are experts already, study guides are almost always over 30 pages long, and the tests have a lot of topics that were not talked about during class.

please dont take this man... i dont care what you read before. i read reviews and thought it was going to be so great but honestly having mandatory lectures (aka you wont pass) then exams that are 80% of your grade combined with "study guides" that are literally exactly whats posted on the slides just isnt it. he is a nice guy, but not best prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the prof himself wasn't bad, the 3 exams are 80% of your final grade. You just have to try & memorize all the lecture slides. His "study guides" are given out a few days before the exam & are just the same things on his slides just on a doc.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were super important for this class! If you took good notes, you will definitely do well on his exams. This semester, they were online, but I am not certain if they will remain that way. Overall, Professor Brascamp was awesome, and I enjoyed Cognitive Psych a lot more than I thought I would!
Professor Jan Brascamp was very nice and allowed extra credit through coglab. However, it is easy to mess up in this class there a were only 3 exams and they are very heavily weighted.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 10/10 professor. His lectures can seem long & boring at times, but it goes by quick. In class, he'll read exactly what's on the slides, so you aren't required to go to class if you understand the material. This course is test heavy since you only take 3 quizzes and 3 exams, but Coglab quizzes are easy and exams are decent. Don't buy the book!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: absolutely awful, the lectures are tedious and redundant. the information on the slides are no help during the exams. dont bother going to the in person lectures because he just reads off the slides and goes on and on and on.
Tried his absolute best to make the most he could out of the course. I missed a quiz opening by a few minutes and he was extremely accommodating. His honors option is also really fun!!

Great professor. Tried his best to make lectures interesting with everything being online and exams matched the lectures. If you paid attention during lecture then you'd do fine on the exam. Coglab quizzes were also super easy if you actually did them and took notes. He's also super flexible about moving test times around. Grade reflected effort.

I took this class all online fall 2020. This class is super interesting. Make sure you watch the lecture videos, they help so so much! Also I suggest taking notes on the slides before you watch the lectures then add to your notes. The book isn't necessary at all. Professor Brascamp is super nice and the TA's are great. Definitely recommend.
I loved Brascamp. His lectures can be dry at times but he's really good at getting all of the information across. I definitely want to take him again if I get the chance. 11/10
Pretty nice professor. Course was a kinda hard. Wouldn't take again because content wasn't super interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easy class, don't buy the textbook, lectures are to the point and interesting, supplemented rly well with examples, class ALWAYS ended 30 minutes early so count on that but overall Prof Brascamp is very kind and willing to help his students when needed, grades consist of quizzes and tests only.
Awesome guy! Had a very good time in his class.

He is an extremely nice man who cares about his students. Class never goes the full amount of time and sometimes it makes the lectures rushed and boring, but the class is easy enough where you could never go to class and still 4.0.

Very chill professor, more than half way through the semester and we havent had a full length class yet. Answers questions through out lecture and his powerpoints are very well structured. You can tell he really cares about his students & is willing to help!
His socks are the best.

Coglab quizzes are easy; (10) HPR credits are easily attainable during a whole semester; he has entertaining lectures that are occasionally riddled with humor; he tries to answer questions the best he can and help students understand what he is teaching.

The first day I went to class and saw her, was when I knew I'd love the class. Didn't disappoint at all. She genuinely cares about her students and makes sure each student is doing well. Wish I could take the class again, and that will never apply to any of my other classes for sure.

Greatest professor I've had at MSU so far. Instead of just throwing assignments in your face, she gives you parts of the assignments to complete over a reasonable amount of time. Always willing to help and is straightforward with the class.

Dr. Chrobak is so sweet and helpful. Her class is honestly very easy, and she keeps everything very organized in D2L. She is accessible outside of class if you have any questions. A lot of the times she lets you out of lecture early which is really nice.
My favorite professor so far!

Amazing prof! Super well organized with her schedule and resources. I would recommend her to any student! I definitely grew as a person from the projects in her class, she was very intentional with what she assigned which was so helpful. She really does have everyone's best interest in mind. An easy and enjoyable 4.0!

She is so amazing and funny. Got out of class early each day but she was so willing to help you and doesn't make you feel stupid. She made me feel like I can be myself not only in class, but in the papers I write

I had her for a hybrid WRA 101 course. I was worried initially but it was really nice. We got out of class early most (every) day and while there were occasional readings and assignments to do outside of class, they didn't feel like busywork. A lot of the smaller weekly assignments directly related to the large assignments. Definitely recommend.
She is a great professor and is very open to different writing styles

Dr. Chrobak is the sweetest professor ever!! She is always willing to help her students, and she is very accessible outside of class. Her class has a very easy and clear structure. Each of her assignments have a purpose (she does not like busy work), and she provides great feedback. I would gladly take another class with her!!
Amazing Professor who cares and is willing to help. Lectures are clearly stated. Beautiful women as well!

reviews.comment: Awful professor do NOT take him unless necessary. I will put hours into an assignment following instructions word for word only to get a 65% absolutely ruined my gpa

He is a nice person but an unreasonably tough grader who takes points off for vague reasons and "missing information" that he never indicated should be included in our work. Also did not stick to the syllabus and held class on a day that the official course schedule said was off with only a last-minute heads up about the change. pretty bad tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is very little original content or ideas in his lecture. If by chance you are not required to take this class, find something similar taught by someone different to peak your interest. As others said prompts are general yet points will be taken off for specific things not in the prompt. I had hoped to challenge him on this but prompt was gone
Awful professor. He barely tells you what you have to write in your assignments and then he gives you awful grades. And genuinely is an awful grader!

He is an extremely strict grader. Often times his prompts for assignments are quite short, general, and not very clear on what he is looking for yet he expects very specific things while grading and never seems to be pleased with your work. He enjoys giving only half credit on weekly homework that is sufficient to the instructions.

His grading doesn't make sense. A lot of other students and I get bad grades on the "easy" assignments for no reason. We follow his directions carefully and he gives out Cs Ds and Fs. This class avg is 3.5/4.0 among other professors, but his avg is 2.5

This class might be better if taken in person, but is very difficult online. He posts way too much material to be read and understood in one week and it seems outdated and is hard to follow. He grades the weekly writing assignments very hard and never gives full credit meaning you have to do good on the lengthy short answer exams that take 2 hours.
The course is demanding though. Course has lockdown quizzes so study for those, and heavily reliant on group for practice exams. The exam consists of multiple choice and CER writing portion.

He's a really nice guy and clearly cares a lot about the material he teaches. MGI 301 is a hard class that requires a lot of time outside of class every week if you want a good grade. His office hours before each exam helped me.

Dr. Hardy was very fun to talk to and kind. MGI301 was difficult, but he was understanding and explained course concepts well. He frequently came over to explain course concepts and talk to students. He gave out candy on the last day of class. Lots of reading, but if you do it you'll be ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Incredible professor. He teaches a hard class. I won't lie this class needs a ton of work and effort, but Dr. Hardy is amazing and will meet you where you're at. He's also got really interesting research and knowledge. Ask him about it if you can, it's fascinating.

Dr Hardy is super approachable and really wants to see you succeed. This class is difficult, mostly because of the exams. Prepare for a massive time crunch with 35-39 long MCQs and 2 paragraph free responses. I personally felt the exams mostly tested your reading comprehension and speed more then your understanding of the material.
Really cool guy. Office hours are incredibly helpful.

The hardest part about this class is finishing the exam in time in my opinion. You have to prepare well but I felt like the flipped classroom really helped with that. Office hours with him are great. I mainly went to them to go over the exam keys as everything builds on each other. This class is definitely doable but you have to put the hours in.

Dr. Hardy is the sweetest prof ever. He wants to help his students succeed and encourages students to reach out whenever necessary. The class can be a little tricky at times but he was always willing to help break it down and walk you through it.

Dr. Hardy was a great professor. This class is very difficult, content heavy, and requires a lot of effort and time studying. Dr. Hardy is very kind and understanding. He wants you to do well and encourages you to ask questions and go to office hours. He is willing to Zoom if you can't make it in person, AND he's willing to Zoom over the weekend.

Hardy is one of the best profs I have had. He cares so much about microbiology and loved to talk about it. Super helpful in office hours and recitation, super approachable and I would definitely take him again.

Dr. Hardy was great! He is so kind and really passionate about microbiology. He has a lot of cool research that he loves to talk about, so ask him about it if you're interested. The class is hard, it's microbiology so that is to be expected, but it is manageable. I made a review of all vocab and learning objectives and studied that for exams

If you have the opportunity to take his dark comedy class, do it! Very interesting, and he's very passionate about the subject. This is a discussion heavy class with a fair amount of readings, but he is understanding if you have a bad day and has reasonable expectations. My personal goat!

While this class definitely isn't everyone's cup of tea, I found it very interesting. The lectures were 2 hours, but he does do his best to keep them engaging. The class does have four pop quizzes and a midterm but as long as you go to class, do the readings and watch the movies, you'll easily 4.0. Prof Lam is also very caring and willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you don't like discussion. Most boring class I've ever taken, we literally talked from the start of class to the end and I don't think I gained any knowledge whatsoever. As for the professor he was great! Just not a teaching style I could learn from.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Every once in a while you run into an absolute gem during your academic career. Prof. Lamb wasn't just a phenomenal professor to me, he was a kind-hearted humanbeing. Extremely understanding, very open-minded and was super receptive to feedback given to him. One of the best professors I've ever had. Take his classes, I promise you won't regret it!

I actually took ENG 280 with Professor Lam and it was pretty easy other than sometimes the quizzes were a little difficult. He based the class mostly on student discussion which was a little frustrating because I felt like he should be doing the teaching that my tuition pays for. There's mainly 3 quizzes 2 essays event reflections and participation
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: We had to do weekly discussion posts and replies which weren't too bad. Prof Lam was really understanding and gave great feedback throughout the semester. My only complaint was his lecture videos were quiet and his quizzes are a little hard

Lam is a great professor and he's very smart but the entire class is him talking. It's hard to even stay awake for the full time we're there. He's very knowledgeable and I feel like I'm learning a lot. A lot of the grading is by one single group project and attendance.
Josh is a good guy, and is very clearly knowledgable about the source material (which is very interesting). He makes you think about the material you consume in a new way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Josh is a great professor! He made coming to class really easy, even though it was fairly early. He connected with almost the whole class, and I still talk about how his class has been my favorite class and I took it last year.

A lot of people complain about him, but if you just show up and do what you're supposed to do you'll get an A. You have to participate to get a good participation grade. He did go completely off syllabus, but he emails you weekly letting you know which articles we will be discussing in class. There are a few group projects which can be annoying

by week 2 he had gone completely off syllabus and free styled the entire semester. puts people on the spot & interrupts them. constantly makes us sit in a circle, then at our desks, then repeat. impossible to take notes. made up an assignment on the spot as an “apology” for telling us the wrong exam time & because it was so hard.

Extremely vague grading criteria for all assignments. Assignment instructions very unclear. He grades participation and attendance but I did not miss a single class and got 80%. The assignments are very easy, but extremely frustrating.

Worst explanations/teaching style. Will cut people off mid-explanation. He has no rubrics for his assignments + makes them due at random times when most people have class. Doesn't give you an explanation as to why you did poorly on an assignment. Took a CSE class in the same semester and did worse in this class… your grade is truly a flip of a coin

While he does lecture, most of class time is spent discussing material from the readings or making group videos summarizing the material. Disorganized D2L setup and confusing discussion prompts. I understand why he has mandatory attendance; everyone would skip otherwise. Seems like a nice guy, this is just the weirdest class I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: super easy grader, just a lot of writing and reading. interesting class but a bit content heavy, i didn't mind. super understanding and responsive
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is a joke. The professor gives us tons of readings every class but half the people just skip the reading and do as well as the people who read. He gives us *graded* attendance based on videos we have to make outside doing fake coach interviews, running football plays and recreating historical photos. Idk how this guy has a job here.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a professor who genuinely cares about the success of his students. He is kind, accommodating, and definitely enjoys teaching. Exams are straightforward and come directly from what we learn in class. Show up to class, take notes, and you will excel. Interesting content, thought-provoking lectures, I would highly recommend him as a professor.

I had him for a seminar and he was really good. He was really invested in making sure we understood the topics being covered and he really seemed to enjoy what he was talking about. There was a lot of reading involved but most of the time you could skim and would be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He actually did not follow his own rubric, he had a tuition assistant do the complete lecture and grading for the class. This meant that the TA gave people across the board grading and this across the board grading was low. Pescador for his part supported the TA and claimed no wrongdoing or fixed the problem. He is an academic gangster at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Had him for an honors seminar. Lots of reading but he was enjoyable to listen to and good at starting discussion. He also gave good feedback on papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Lectures difficult to understand, posts all lectures online. Seven 1000 word min. essays (70% of grade). Final research paper (3500 words, 20% of grade). Participation taken every class (10% of grade). The 7 essays are tolerable, all based on readings (approx. 3 per week) and lectures. Difficult if you don't like writing, easy if you like history.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The guidelines for some assignments were different on D2L than what he would say in class. He only took attendance whenever he felt like it, and gave me a 100 on participation because I talked sometimes even though I barely showed up. Exams were all written, and there were a lot of essays which he doesn't talk about in class so look online!

This class was completely terrible. Totally not what I expected. I expected to learn and to enjoy this class but I was completely let down. He is hard to understand, does not give clear instructions, and gives horrible feedback to the assignment that you do complete. When answering your questions, he is vague and gives no context.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are a lot of readings outside of class and a lot of review essays that are due. Very hard grader and doesnt explain why you got your answers wrong. Reads off the slides!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Pescador is seriously just awful. Reads off the slides. Takes attendence. Forces people into groups in a 300 person lecture hall and makes people talk in front of the class. He takes attendance which is 10% of your final grade. The class and content itself is easy. Your assigments are just weekly essays with one group project in the middle.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good professor. He assigns a lot of reading but you don't really have to read that much of it but you will need them to use them as sources for papers. The papers can be tedious and require a lot of sources but he's pretty lenient on grading them and grading in general. Overall not a bad class, just make sure you actually are into history.

Horrible professor. He does not respond to emails and provided us with contradictory information in the guidelines of our first essay. He also reads directly off of his slides and then forced ~10 students to come to the front of the class and regurgitate the details of some article concerning an unimportant time period in athletic history.

Pescador's section is much more difficult than Fisher's. Fisher's class has 1 paper, written in a group. Pescador's has 3, 4 page papers and a final 16 page group project. TRUST ME, just try to get into fisher's, if not wait until another semester. He also grades pretty tough also. nice guy.
class is doable but the exams have really specific questions, i dont think im going to be able to pass this class
Tough grader. Exams are all short answer/drawing. Class is all group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Lawrence was amazing. He cares a lot about his students and their success. His content can be pretty tough, but as long as you go to the lecture and ask questions, you should pass. There are quizzes before and during class that don't count for your grade, but if you do well, you get extra credit. There are also many extra credit opportunities.

Doesn't know how to teach at all, and doesn't even know his own content to help. You have to teach yourself with the videos he gives for homework the night before. Lecture really is just recitation, he gives everyone packets for busy work basically the whole class. His tests don't even correspond with what was taught.

Prof. Lawrence really cares that you understand the material and come to class prepared as it's a flipped classroom. He does cold call sometimes and you take a reading quiz every day. His exams although hard, you could get points back and the final was a self reflection that we asked for the grade we wanted. Effort needed but not hard to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I struggled a little in his class as the exams were a little tricky but he was a great professor and truly cares about his students and you can tell he is very passionate. He also is always very helpful with questions.

Lawrence is a good prof. He really wants you to understand and like biology. Will answer your questions no problem. Although I'm not a huge fan of the flipped classroom model. You'll do many in class activities with an assigned group, as well as take 3 question mini quizzes to help boost your understanding of the material. HAVE A FOLDER FOR PAPERS!

Dr. Lawrence is a great professor! You can tell that he really cares about our growth and understanding of the material. Although the self grading system wasn't my favorite, it did challenge me to think about the topics and review areas that I didn't fully grasp. If you put the effort in you will do well!

Kind professor who is passionate about Biology and encourages students to find their passion in it too. Lecture heavy but very clear expectations. New grading style allows students to increase their test scores via self-assessment. Will end with 4.0 if you put in the hard work. Very accommodating prof; communicate w/ him if struggling! Will help.
Great professor, really cares about our learning and development. Very understanding and makes lectures fun!

Overall Dr. Lawrence is an enjoyable character and really cares about student learning. His 'Alternative Grading' is designed to help students learn but it's more confusing than anything. Exams are extremely long and difficult and the in-class activities take all class to complete. The pre-class videos are important so make sure to take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class had a new structure this semester, but it was overall good. It promoted learning. The exams are insanely hard but they were take home this year. Not sure if they will be next semester. Great professor, hes very kind and understanding. Take over all the LB profs if you want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is a 5 credit course for a reason. Dr. Lawrence himself is a great guy and does a good job explaining things. For the final exam, there is an option of doing it orally in which you meet up with a TA face-to-face and answer questions that they ask you in-person, out loud. If you pass it then you don't have to take the actual written final.

Dr. Lawrence was a great prof. He wants students to understand the material, which is why his exams are so difficult. They are all free response, but he has study sessions that were beyond helpful. If you want a 4.0, you're going to have to WORK for it and go over the notes and lecture videos multiple times. Grading is tough but it makes sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Content of the class is difficult, first exam average is always low. Expect to study for hours for the exams, as they are long and time consuming. However, he is accessible outside of class and is willing to help you understand topics. He is a good prof, but again the class is difficult so you have to put in your own work.

Go to office hours to receive challenge questions from him, this is helpful for his exams and verbal exams. His office hours are VERY good. Exams (3) are a huge part of the grade, don't tank the first one. He offers a verbal final, 3 tries, if you pass, you get an automatic hundred, they are NOT easy. Hard class, but he wants you to four-point.

Okay professor. Doesnt really explain well in class. You basically have to learn on your own through preclass videos. Tests are unnecessarily hard. He does give you a chance for extra credit to make up those points, however, his class makes you hate learning. In lab, hes horrible at mediating and trys to help but doesnt.

Dr. Lawrence was a great teacher overall. He gave good feedback and offered extra credit and was accommodating when extenuating circumstances came up. The exams are difficult but passible if you study a lot. Would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: probably the best professor i've ever had. incredibly sweet, funny, and caring, and made the class really engaging. (also makes me wish this site still had the chili pepper ratings ngl)

Dr. Lindquist is amazing!! WRA 260 is taught in such a way that we learn how to recognize and apply rhetoric. She ensures we have the opportunity to demonstrate this, whether it be through individual or group projects with almost everything built off of past assignments. She is humorous and caring-- consider yourself lucky to be taught by her!

Probably the best professor I've had at MSU so far. Julie is just so REAL. She allows for lots of leniency and really just understands her students and wants whats best for them. She has such a unique outlook on life and as a rhetoric professor that is very important. Her dry humor and wit makes for fun classes and the projects are worthwhile.

Take a course with Dr Lindquist! WRA 330 is structured around one project that you will complete throughout the semester. She gave us lots of creative freedom and she genuinely cared about all of her students and their respective projects. We had many fun and introspective discussions. All readings can be found online. Shes an awesome prof!

Dr Lindquist is an amazing professor. She has so much care for her students and generally takes interest in what we were writing about. She has a very lenient way of grading with, quote, "A hatred for grade curves" and started the semester by saying "If you follow everything I say you WILL get a 4.0." She also has an amazing personality.

She's an absolutely wonderful professor. Had her for WRA this past semester and it's abundantly clear that she really cares about her students in a way most educators don't. I was really lucky to have her as a prof - her class has taught me not only about writing but about myself.
I love Julie! She is very nice and personable, I have a great relationship with her. If you do the work for the assignments you will get a good grade.

Professor Lindquist is a phenominal professor.  She really cares about her students and wants them to do well.  She will talk about projects with the class when they are assigned to see what they are nervous about, then she walks you through it.

She is not a good lecturer and spends 90% of class time off track. She is not tech savvy at all which is annoying. She is a decently easy grader but does not provide feedback on what is wrong. Also no grades in the gradebook and prefers emailing students with specifc grades when D2L does the math for her and would be easier to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Does not put grades into D2L for the entire semester, so it is near impossible to know what you will end up with. Does not give good feedback, either. Got points off, and never figured out why. Work is not particularly engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Singh is vague regarding her assignment expectations. And when you do eventually get a grade back, she doesn't tell you what you got wrong. Whenever she asks a question in class, she doesn't always wait for students to respond either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Entire grade is based on 3/4 projects. Attendance not required. He makes you buy his textbook. Dont buy it. Its a waste of your money. ALL of your assignemnts are graded by TA. I got a 4.0 in the class beacuse I had a nice TA.

He would constantly change the syllabus where the instructions for most assignments and projects were. He would come across as mocking of students in class after he'd ask for people to share their opinions. So many written responses, it makes a fun subject into a chore.

Youre whole grade is 3 projects basically and is all graded based on the TA's. If you get a TA that grades harsh, you're cooked. Mine graded harsh but my friend got straight 100s. Also just a waste of time learning this bs
I would never take a class of his again. Please incoming freshman take a different IAH class. This one is easy but still many more easier and enjoyable classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You're WHOLE grade is determined by the TA you have, and they grade so hard and it is almost impossible to get an A even when you follow the rubric. PLS DROP THIS CLASS ( Afrofuturism)

Professor Chambliss is fine, the lectures can be a bit boring, however attendance is not required! I know people who went to no lectures and passed just fine, the course is based on 3 large projects (20% each) and 20% for recertation. They take attendance and if you miss 2+ that's 25% of your grade, befriend your TA thats how you get good grades!!

Although the course is about afrofuturism, you never really learn much about it as he lectures about the randomest topics ever. He wrote the mandatory textbook which is hard to understand. Your grade is dependent on your TA and most were very harsh graders. Dropped this class with zero regrets

You can take this class, never go to a lecture, and still pass with a 4.0. Your grade is solely dependent on who your TA is and how clearly they describe the projects. Dr. Chambliss will tell you to buy his book about Afrofuturism, do not buy it. You do not need that book for this class at all, I never read a single word of it. Class is super easy.

Four projects make up the majority of the grade and they're graded by the TA, not Dr. Chambliss. His class material is a lot more interesting than he is engaging, but his lectures aren't mandatory-- only the recitations. I had the pleasure of having a great TA (Journey Smith). Can't speak for those who don't-- simple projects though.

Like others have said, your grade depends on your TA. You don't have to go to lectures, but definitely go to recitations as attendence is mandatory and they recap lectures. You're graded on 4 projects and then recitation attendence, worksheets, and we had to take notes for one lecture and then teach one topic to our recitation class.
TAKE THIS CLASS ONLINE IT IS 10X LESS WORK. Also, most of the TA's in this class grade your papers like they are harvard professors.

Every IAH/ISS class is taught by someone who spent their entire career studying a niche/pointless subcategory of literature. They probably wrote a book that they require you to buy for the class (like this guy) if you have to take this class because it's required (like me) I suggest you take it online. Every assignment can be found on the internet.
I never went to a single lecture and got a 4.0, there are a few projects and thats mostly all you have to do. i would def take this professor again hes so chill

Chambliss is a nice guy but because of the way the class is formatted, your grade is entirely based on who your TA is. I would reccommend going to lecture in the beginning of the semester. Your whole grade is based on four projects and then your recitation grade, so I reccommend not taking this class because you can't pick your TA

Even though lectures were boring, I attended all of them yet still did bad. My TA was a harsh grader, you have to get lucky and get an easy one to do well. It's not worth it, take another more interesting IAH class.

Great professor, always cracks a few jokes in class. I would recommend going to lectures at the beginning of the course, but toward the end, it's less necessary. I did not read a single reading assigned to me and still got a 4.0. The TA was good; a little picky and slow with grading. I recommend going to all recitations if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My grade dropped drastically because of a missed assignment in recitation 3.5 to 2.5. Lectures are boring you don't even have to honestly. Put all that work into my assignments just to receive a C for one assignment. Just a waste of time. Save your money and enroll in a different course. Emailed TA about grade never got a response.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I maintained a 3.5 in the class the ENTIRE semester but at the very end my grade dropped to a 2.5 because I missed ONE assignment from RECITATION! I had B's on every major project that was given to me and a A on my final but somehow that didn't matter because since I missed one assignment in my recitation my grade is now a C. Don't take this course
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a really good guy at first, but the topic can be super uninteresting and hard to stay engaged with. It is also really hard to find good sources/examples online for projects. Lecture was so boring! The one major problem with this class was my TA graded super hard and it is usually very inconsistent. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Seems like a chill guy at first, but when I talked to him about a grade dispute he was very condescending and disrespectful. Limited work makes it hard to get a good grade in this class, and I wish I took a different IAH since this one messed up my gpa.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I HATED THIS CLASS! I was one of the few that actually attended lectures and still learned nothing. Your grade depends on only 4 projects, so if you do bad on one your whole grade tanks. I would NOT recommend this class.
Most uninteresting lecture I've ever taken. The TA was not good and very rarely gives out good grades. Not worth your time or sanity.
Extremely rude when you speak to him. Very unclear measures for grading and takes points off for no reason. Do not recommend him. Please stay away from his class.

Don't take this class. Course description doesn't mention it's about Afrofuturism. People stopped showing up to his lectures because they're boring and useless. Grades depend on the TA, mine was a super harsh grader. Project instructions were unclear, no rubric.Talked to the professor about my grade, and he laughed in my face, very unprofessional.

Dr. Chambliss is a great teacher if you are interested in the subject of Afrofuturism. I didn't really have an interest in this subject but still had a great time. Attendance is not mandatory for lecture but the recitation attendance is, and all the grading is done by your recitation TA. Only about 4 assignments in one semester. Lots of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a great guy, but I just wasn't interested in the topic. I didn't need to attend lecture which was nice. However, you should be aware that your recitation teacher for this class will be someone else, typically Master's students who are not the best at what they do.

Professor Chambliss is amazing! He gets everyone engaged in the lecture & gives some prompts to get you thinking at the beginning of lecture that are honestly very interesting. He doesn't do the grading but the TA I had was amazing also and a very easy grader. His lectures do not require attendance but the recitation that goes along with it does.
Very unclear to what you need to know before the labs and hard to follow during lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you go to class, you will do well. I got a 3.0 but I rarely showed up and if I did, I wasn't taking notes or paying attention.   All homework answers are on chegg, which  bit me in the ass later on.    Professor Weng is hard to understand sometimes and can be pretty boring at others but if you stick with it and put in the work you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Explained the class material pretty well. The material is tough and therefore many students blame him for their own failings.

Wrote his own book for you to use, half of his work is incorrect.  Homework's he states is just a minor modification of his example, ends up being completely different and 10x more complex.  Seems as if none of his research and examples even work.  Very bad professor, forces students to correct his book for his own benefit without credit given.

Had him for 202 not 201. As long as you actually come to class and do the classwork assigned outside of class then you'll get a 4.0 in the class. He actually cares about teaching which makes the classes pretty interesting. Only thing to note is that there is a LOT of work to do outside of the classroom, so expect at least a few hours of hw weekly.

Great professor, very understanding and always adds in interesting and useful information during class that teaches you French outside of the traditional classroom context. Really cares about his students and the class and wants to help you succeed.

Great professor, never met anyone who uses so many dad jokes. He is obviously very passionate about French and linguistics, and if you ask him a question he'll answer it and then some. Very engaging and his lectures are easy to understand. There is a bit of work, but it's not too difficult and he is a very fair and generous grader

FRN 330 is a phonetics class more than a french class. There are homework assignments due before and after each class. He tries to be kind with grading and is funny, but this class was one of the hardest and most frustrating I've ever taken. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I love Professor Kanefsky! He makes his lectures very interactive and makes it easy to participate. Hes great over zoom, but I wish I had him for an in person class! Homework isnt too difficult, but you have around 3 assignments a week. A great professor!

Very difficult class, but it is required. Lots of homework to do for the class, but I'm sure it's much easier online than the class during the school year. Easy access to answers to assignments to improve, accepting of late work, and grading is not too difficult you can pass well with hard work put in. As always, I wish French had a 90 -100 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: awesome.. that's all
Online French class is hard, but he is very helpful if you can go see him in person or on Zoom.

Matt was incredible! Easily one of my favorite instructors. He's so nice and will make conversation with you before class starts. He's so willing to help you with anything and.. I just can't stress how nice he is. Really full of quirky/helpful information too. Won't forget how to say good idea or egg in french.. Just a great teacher!

The work in her class is very easily manageable, however the lectures were extremely boring. She had random in class assignments only accessible with a password she gave in class, however you did get two drops on these. She rambles a lot but is a nice person and she does care about her students. She gives lots of extra credit opportunities.

Fairly easy class if you put in the effort. Lectures can be a bit dry, but she offers a lot of extra credit. She uses McGraw Hill with 1–2 SmartBook activities weekly and an open-browser quiz every weekend. Attendance isn't required, but she does random in-class activities with a password, so going to class is important.
The only reason I came to lectures was to do homework for other classes. Only a midterm and a final exam, but do not worry about it.

Dr. Wood is one of the sweetest professors I've ever had, she does have very lecture heavy classes but it is important to go to make sure you keep up with in class assignments. She offers so many different extra credit opportunities so take advantage of those. She is super kind, I would recommend taking her class!

She always posts assignments after lecture and they're due that Friday at 9am and it's usually about the lab which we have during the week.  We never know what to look out for during our lab and often barely mentions the assignments due Friday during lecture.  Changes assignment due dates often.

Syllabus and schedule change often. Late work gets 50% off—even if it's 1 hour late—though assignments may be graded weeks later. Due Fridays at 9 AM. Little communication with mentor teachers and minimal feedback before the next assignment. Templates are repetitive. Only .docx accepted, no resubmissions. Do work early.

The professor is super nice, always answers questions, and did online reviews before the exams — sometimes giving hints for the tests. Lectures were a little boring, with a lot of info, and a good amount of work. Do the extra credit, it really helps your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: i loved professor wood! she was really sweet really cares about her job the extra credit really does make a impact on ur grade so make sure u do it! she was understanding when it came to any online issues and her lectures were pretty interesting some were boring ans she do online reviews and give hints for the tests i would take her again!

Not recommended. There are only 10 in-class assignments, and missing two due to illness meant no flexibility or makeup allowed. I earned an A, but only by teaching myself. Lectures mainly involve reading directly from PowerPoint slides.
This class included a TON of work, but if you do the work, you will be fine. Do not get behind! This particular lecture is long and boring but if you put in the work, it will be fine.

very nice prof. lectures are super slow and boring, but she means well and explain everything well. I never pay attention in class, no exams, everything is based on connect quizzes and d2l quizzes (no lockdown), 2 larger assignments. Changes deadlines to help people. has difficulties with technology which is hard when ICA dont work.

Her class was mostly connect assignments and weekly quizzes. There were no exams. You barely need to go to her class and she posts before if there is an in class activity. I missed 1 class a week and I still ended with 540/515. Plenty of EC. Her lectures are very boring but I would just finish all of the hw during class.

idk why Dr. Woods rating is so low. She is an older lady so the lectures can be boring but you don't even have to pay attention to the lectures to pass. There is no exams, multiple extra credit assignments, and 1-2 short open note tests a week. literally so easy. I passed with a 535/515 points because of all the extra credit.

Class is beyond easy. Graded by weekly quizzes instead of exams, homework assignments, in class activities, & 2 application assignments. Everything was easy, we only had in class assignment sometimes. She's very sweet & caring. If she's not answering your email, go up to her in class, her and her TA are understanding & more than willing to help.

Kellye is very sweet and kind. She is willing to answer any questions you have in class or look over assignments for you. The class is long, but we end early a lot of the time. There is a good amount of work outside of class, but if you budget time, it's doable. It is difficult to reach her via email, but she does hold office hours.

You can tell she means well, but lectures are so insufferable. Class is structured poorly, there's weekly assignments and quizzes. Overall, work is not difficult, but she is such a boring lecturer and you will learn nothing. She will randomly assign in-class assignments, so even though attendance isn't mandatory, you usually have to be in class.
Insinuated that I needed therapy because her unorganized, unstructured, lack of proper instruction she likes to call lecture caused me to be confused. Needs to be fired.
Lectures are insufferable.

please please please answer my emails ;( 
ive sent her at least 30 emails in the past 2 weeks and not a single one got a response.

never EVER answers emails and will set you back 3 weeks struggling to try and figure out how to still pass the class being 3 weeks behind without a clue on what to do. debating on switching my certification so i dont have to take this class. help.

reviews.comment: Super tedious about small things that don't matter, yet forgets to open up drop boxes every week....
Lectures are boring, makes it hard to engage... especially since they're so late in the day. Emails left un-responded to, don't take this class with her
Overall seems like a nice lady, but if you're not going to respond to emails, don't teach.
All busy work, lesson plans on top of in class quizzes on top of field assignments on top of in class assignments on top of anti bias assignments on top of placements. So unnecessary
Just don't do it, truthfully. If you can take it with anyone else, do yourself a favor and do that.

Take it with her if you want to pull your hair out due to confusion and lack of structure in the class. 
She also doesnt respond to emails

Legit does not respond to emails. I emailed her a total of 23 times over the semester and she didn't reply to a single one. D2L is confusing and the class is unorganized and chaotic. DON'T TAKE IT WITH KELLYE

If you don't have to take this class with her, don't. She claims we can reach out to her anytime, but does not respond to emails. She assigns 100 different assignments per week and is such a tedious grader that one little typo will cost you -3 points. Lectures are pointless, but required. Unhelpful and overall needs to just be done teaching.

Kellye was a fantastic professor. Lectures could be a bit boring but were informative. Great feedback on assignments. If you go to class, go to the lab, and do the work, you should do fine overall. Many complaints come from people who skip class and get frustrated by assignments explained in class. Not the best tech wise but TA is very helpful.

Shes a nice professor and does her best to answer questions. The course itself is very overwhelming, not super organized, lowkey chaotic. Am I learning a lot, yes? But there is so much information being thrown at us at once that it's hard to remember everything and it feels like you HAVE to remember everything. Lots of overlap of assignments.

Do NOT take this class with Kellye Wood!  Her lectures are hard to follow and rarely have anything to do with the homework assignments.  She will NOT reply to your emails, no matter how many times you email her.  She is unhelpful, has no clue what she is doing, and really just isn't cut out for teaching this class.  The final paper is 20 pages long

I know a lot of people didn't like this class but I actually thought the workload was manageable and the exams weren't too hard. She has a lot of opportunity for extra credit, and there are enough assignments throughout the semester so that if you do bad on one thing you can make up for it. There is a LOT of content so it can be overwhelming.

Despite what everyone else says about her, I really like Kandy. She's great at explaining and as long as you do the reading, you'll do good on the exam. She gives study guides and extra credit which is convenient!

She was okay the tests were on days right before or after break which was annoying. There were some days you needed to go to class for activities but other than that you didn't have to. She was a lot more nicer than Fenn.

She gave in class assignments occassionally, in order to track your attendance. She seemed really lazy and all over the place, was incredibly disorganized, and gave us an exam either right before or right after break which was really irritating.

It is so easy to get a 4.0 if you actually take notes from reading the textbook and homework. Other than that, lectures were pointless. I stopped going because I taught myself every unit! There were a few in class assignments you had to participate in for credit and she also gives us tests before and after break which was annoying. Tests were easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The ONLY way you will do half decent having Dr. Kandy is if you have a vast amount of prior psychology knowledge. Her lectures are useless, don't bother sitting there for 2 hours. She schedules exams on the most inconvenient days, especially if you are sick or live out of state and are traveling home for holidays. The homework assignments are long.

The only way to do well in this class is if you spend like 8 hours doing every reading thoroughly and actually understanding the material. The extra credit helps! She just doesn't offer much in lecture. I stopped going to lectures after the first two weeks and spent all my time on the readings and got all 100% after failing ap psych in high school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are horrible. Told everyone in the class that they are now 1/4 through their lifespan. Asked us to raise our hands if we had a will or advanced directive (no one raised their hand) then scolded us about how every person needs one as soon as they turn 18. Talks about her personal life a lot in a very uncomfortable way. Would not reccommend.

I got really bad strep and mono and instead of taking my appointment summary which literally said I needed to stay home(they wouldn't give me a note) she said oh well looks like you used a drop. When I got sick again all the sudden I could make it up lectures are useless. assignments don't match up with exams at all so have fun knowing all the info
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good luck if you get sick, this lady hounds people over sick days and if you can't get a doctors note good luck. Exams and assignments are horribly planned, exams are the day before break, or the day we get back from a break. Goes on useless rants during lecture about her personal experiences overall not a very well put together class, good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: In her syllabus she says we are expected to act and treat each other like professionals, along with her. Do professionals hound you over sick days with a note from the doctor like you're a little kid? I like her personally but her teaching style is god awful. 250 practice exam questions for a 40 question exam, it's unreasonable and unnecessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take another prof, Dr.Kandy goes on so many tangents it is difficult to understand concepts in her lectures. The tests themselves are hard to study for because the tests are so far from the textbook. Tests and reading due dates always awfully placed, during and right before breaks. She doesn't grade herself, all harsh TAs that don't follow rubrics.

Lots of outside work involving study time, textbook work, and essays. These essays are graded extremely harshly by TA's for a 101 course. The rubrics for these assignments are typically very vague and are very easy to misinterpret. TA's will grade you on things that were not disclosed in the rubric.

Like others have said, she talks about herself and her lived experiences for large parts of lecture time, going on long tangents that get away from the original source of what we were talking about. She also places exams at inconvenient times and is very unforgiving with the workload concerning when we have breaks and university time off.

She is so inconsiderate of people's own lives. Only talks about herself. Makes the exam dates on the worst days and won't take any retakes. I don't have a car here and have to stay here for Thanksgiving due to me being an out-of-state student and having no way home, just because her exam is the day before Thanksgiving. Doesn't make accommodations.

Never in my life have I had a professor so inconsiderate of what was going on in other people's lives. No make-up exams (even though the syllabus says we can) for family emergencies, illness, etc. I had to use my exam drop due to an emergency, and I now cannot use it on the exam the day before thanksgiving break to go see my family.

She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities near the end of the year, but during there year you can't give her a single excuse to retake an exam if you can't make it. Her lectures are actually useless, she talks about herself and her personal experiences for 15 minutes to explain ONE concept. Very frustrating class, no leeway at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: she talks about herself a lot and assumes you know what she's talking about. her grading is pretty bad, although she does let you drop assignments and an exam. she's very monotone and passive aggressive towards things. she places her exams on poor days and refuses to make acceptions.

her exams are super easy if you study the textbook and the study guides, however, her exams are placed on the worst days like the day after fall break and the day before thanksgiving and she won't do anything to change that

Your only need to be in class for in class assignments but she tells you when you have those. Her tests are hard and on inconvenient days. You do need to buy the text book and will use it for homework. She does let you drop one exam, 2 homework's, one in class assignment.

DO NOT LET THE good RATINGS FOOL YOU. Dr Kandy is a terrible professor. She is lazy, incompetent, and very self-centered- always talking about herself. There are a few in-class assignments mixed in with exams. Dr. Kandy's worst quality is her communication.

Her lectures are the most useless lectures I have taken in my academic career. The exams cover absolutely nothing talked about in class, so no matter how confident you feel in the material it is hard to be prepared for the exams. Her practice exams are HUNDREDS of questions. Class avg for exam 1 was a 67, that's insane for a psych class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Participation only really matters for the in class assignments. Has drops. She puts the exams on annoying days so you have to drop them on purpose like she makes the exams the day before thanksgiving or the day after fall break and if you ask to take it another time she will deny your request. She's great but she doesn't believe in study guides.
I am just going to say she is not good for the sake of my grade.

She is kind, but difficult to deal with. Lectures are very disorganized. Refuses to use a powerpoint, but one would be helpful in avoiding accidentally giving out false information. Fixation on the fact that she did not have the technology that younger students have, which is a pet peeve of mine. Do the assignments, focus on memorizing the book.

Worst teacher I've ever had at any level of schooling. Took in 2024 fall, gave us study guides with hundreds and hundreds of questions and threatened ADR's on everyone if we worked on them together. Changed syllabus guidelines 5-6 times, and forced us to do a 7 paragraph essay the day before thanksgiving, it was opened and due this day needlessly

reviews.comment: You definitely have to read the textbook since most exam content comes from it and she never really lectures, more like a group discussion. I would recommend making quizlets for all of the vocab terms from the textbook as well as make quizlets for the practice quizzes questions since those tend to come up on the actual exams.

reviews.comment: Dr. Kandy is a great professor and the 238 course was very interesting. The lectures are more of a led discussion, and attendance is only required on days where there is a group discussion/activity. The course is fast paced, but as long as you put in the work to read, show up to class, and complete the practices quizzes, a 4.0 should be attainable.

reviews.comment: Participation only really matters for the in class assignments. There are drops which are helpful. There is a textbook but it isn't really important and the test are kinda hard. She is an amazing person but as a professor it is frustrating to study because she doesn't believe in study guides.

Dr. Kandy was a great professor! Very interesting lectures, and we learned how to write a research critique which is great to know if you intend on pursuing grad school. She shared a lot of personal anecdotes that helped reinforce the real-life implications of the material. Would definitely take a class with her again!

I loved prof K as a person. this class takes a lot of work and commitment so it is not an easy elective! the material was interesting but we moved very fast. study guides are pools of possible questions which I found very helpful when it came to studying. best i have ever done on an exam even though it took a lot of work.

She is a nice person but I don't recommend her class. There are no lectures, it is just like a class discussion. For her exams, if you memorize 300+ questions from the practice tests, u will do just fine. I just feel like I didn't really learn anything in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very sweet lady, but the exams are awful. They are based on 4-5 chapters and you have to memorize weird statistics and are easily missed while reading. Gives 25 extra credit points and one exam grade drop. The lectures won't help you on the exams, you just have to memorize the textbook

sweet lady. but this class is so disorganized. exams r non stop on the book. but im sorry, who is reading a chapter a night? the lectures dont align with the exams in the slightest way. do not take this class bruh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Easy base level psych class. There were a few assignments a week, nothing crazy. Not much to say, she was nice enough, she just didn't really want to be contacted for some reason. She always said to contact ULA's first, and then her as a last resort. Attainable to fit into a busy schedule since it doesn't add much workload and is super easy to 4.0.

Super nice professor, but most of the exam material was in textbooks. Sometimes, questions on tests were not covered in either lecture or textbook. Barely went to lectures, mostly relied on textbooks and memorization, and ended class with a 4.0. Memorization heavy. Good professor to talk to for professional career questions and very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Psych 101 is a very easy class, and the content is easy to learn. However, the professor is impossible to reach. Takes 3+ days to respond to emails. She also sends out announcements on d2l that are very confusing. For example, she sent two different announcements with two different due dates for our final exam.

I've never had a professor this bad. Dr. Kandy gave us false information, changed the format of exams without notifying us, and gave us 400+ question study guides. The exams were randomly assigned questions from a pool, so people weren't being tested on the same concepts or at equal difficulty. I didn't learn; I memorized my way to a 4.0.

While Dr.Kandy was definitely a caring and even funny person, she was a below average professor whose lectures were pointless. Extremely disorganized class as she changed the syllabus so many times. Yes it's a fairly easy class to 4.0 if you study a lot and memorize all the questions and answers, but it just takes so much time and not worth it.

It's hard for me to write this as she's such a nice person who loves what she does. This semester's class, however, was bad. Very disorganized, with several changes to the syllabus, assignments, and exam format, often without warning, and exam-heavy, with no EC. Unlike any other PSY 200 lvl here. lectures are good but won't prepare you for the exam

Very exam heavy class but she is a great professor. A lot of people hate on her and it's because they're bad students. Constant complaints in the GroupMe due to kids simply not doing their work. Her class is easy and everything is outlined in her syllabus. Brought snacks for kids before class to have.

Very good professor, the people who rate her badly just didn't do good enough in her class and didn't like what was expected. Brought snacks before for kids every class. Very exam heavy (5 exams, 1 drop), packbacks, ICAs, weekly quizzes, gave EC. Was trash talked in the GroupMe by everyone for no reason. Good professor and great class

I think Dr. Kandy was great! She only took attendance on certain days and she would tell us ahead of time which days those were. Our exams are worth a lot of our grade but she also gave a decent amount of extra credit over the semester. Go to class, make sure you understand quiz questions and it's an easy A!

All memorization. Unorganized class, changed syllabus several times. Funny and nice person don't get me wrong, but just not worth the amount of time and stress for a 3 credit elective. Exams were very very easy if you memorized the questions and answers. But the preparation for the exams was insane (answering 100 or 200 or even 400 questions)

Assignments were often announced last minute, like a surprise seven-paragraph essay on a documentary due the night before Thanksgiving. This class was frustrating and disorganized, and most of us regretted enrolling. I genuinely do not understand how she has such good ratings (which is why I took the class), but don't let those fool you.

Disorganized. Lectures were pointless. Too many exams. Weekly quizzes. Weekly quizzes and exams were overwhelming, with a massive number of potential questions to prepare for (e.g., 200 for the first exam, 400 for the third). Although she provided the questions in advance, it felt more like busywork than genuine preparation.

While my professor was a kind person, she was a disorganized and ineffective instructor. The syllabus changed over 11 times, creating constant confusion. Her lectures were unhelpful—essentially reciting definitions without engaging with the material—and most students found them pointless to attend unless points were involved.
She was an amazing professor and you can tell she loves her job. She would always have snacks in front of the class if you were hungry. Extra credit was offered as well!

I cannot recommend Dr. Kandy enough! She is the first professor who I truly felt able to connect with as a friend. She will go out of her way to help and accommodate for you. Lectures are super informative with lots of opportunities to personally connect with the material. Learned a lot about scholarly writing; will help me immensely in the future!

Dr. Kandy is amazing. She is super understanding and she genuinely cares about her students. The textbook we used was free. Attendance does count for this class because we did a lot of in class activities, but she does offer extra credit that can make up for days missed. This class consisted of 6 quizzes and 3 writing assignments.

Dr. Kandy is a fantastic professor, she's very caring and you will learn a lot from her! Attendance was mandatory but I never wanted to skip her class anyway. She's compassionate and her lectures are enjoyable. Her expectations are clearly communicated. Do the work and the reading and you'll do well. I plan on taking another class with her.
