Kandy is by far the best professor I've ever had. She truly cares about her students and has a lot of passion for what she teaches. Textbook is available for extra credit but not required. Attendance was mandatory at the beginning of the semester but was changed to optional. Exams are heavy but with good notes, easy to succeed. Highly recommend!

Dr. Kandy is one of the sweetest professors i've ever had. She truly cares about her students and will give you plenty of chances for extra credit. Her lectures are filled with personally stories that help to keep you engaged.

Textbook reading is EC but I def recommend because exams are very textbook content heavy. attendance was mandatory at first but eventually removed. First exam was in person, rest were moved to online. Prof is an extremely caring person and prioritizes your mental health and welfare.

The textbook is not technically mandatory, however it is very helpful to have read it before lecture and to take the quizzes on the chapters to get extra credit. Professor Kandy is as sweet as everyone says, cares about her students, and is passionate about what she is teaching, in turn making students excited to learn about the material.
The best professor I have had here at MSU, she makes learning fun and that's why it was easy for me to get such a good grade.

By far the best professor I've ever had at this university. Her lectures are very interesting and she is such a caring person (random mental health days). The textbook is not required, it's only used for extra credit. Your grade is only exam-based, but she offers so many extra credit opportunities to prevent failure. Love her!!

By far one of the most understanding and patient professors I've had thus far. She lets you take mental health days and provides a lot of extra credit opportunities. You do have to buy the McGraw Hill textbook online that comes with connect questions (that are for extra credit) little to no homework, & grade is based on exams and participation.

Best professor I've had this semester. Dr. Kandy genuinely cares about her students and loves her job. This course is very self-motivated in terms of reading the chapters. There are tests every other week online. Homework and readings are easy if you keep up. Provided opportunities for extra credit and I ended up with over an 100% in the course.

Dr. Kandy is great. All the information taught is interesting and very applicable to the topic. She's incredibly caring and easy to talk to if you run into any issues. There are exams every other week, but they're online and as long as you understand the concepts, you'll do great.
Very sweet and understanding professor. She wants what's best for her students and brings food to candy to each class period!

Best psychology professor hands down. Responds to emails extremely quickly and all exams are online but can be taken at home. There is a lot of reading and notes but it is extremely manageable as long as you stay on track. Take her for PSY238 !!!!

Dr. Kandy is an incredible lecturer, and she really made class interesting to attend. She's very accommodating and will work with you if you're having a tough time. Some of the questions get really specific on tests but so long as you go to the lectures you're fine. There's a lot of reading assigned but she covers the vast majority in the lectures.

I took Psy-238 in the fall with her and it was great. All exams and quizzes are online, they are challenging but if you read the chapter and go to lecture it makes sense. She offers a lot of extra credit and she is a very caring professor.

PSY 238: Interesting lectures. Long readings assigned for every class. Password-protected quizzes after most classes, and password only given in class (unless you email her beforehand). Quizzes are closed note, unit exams are open note (very similar to quizzes), and the final is closed note. Do the readings and study for quizzes to be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had PSY 238 and it was the best class I've had. She's very engaging, easy to talk to, and cares for her students. She is extremely understanding if you have an issue with tests or if you have to miss a lecture. Attendance was expected, but not completely 'mandatory', there is some in-class activities and you must be in class to get quiz code.

PSY 238 
Amazing teacher. She is super engaging with her students and clearly cares about each one. Although attendance is not mandatory, there are some in class activities or you may need to be in class to get a quiz code. This is one of my favorite classes that I've taken and the material is not difficult to understand with her.

She's a great professor. Attendance isn't technically mandatory but she has assignments in class that need to be done in class. She made all the assignments enjoyable, and the class was as well. Had it at 8:30 am and was dreading but she made it really fun and made me enjoy waking up for class.

Professor McKeown was very sweet and kept everyone engaged during all my lectures, as she was funny and brought our material into real world applications. She is very easy to reach out to and has her class set up for the student's benefit. I had an issue with something during my exam and she was able to help me very quickly.

Prof Kandy was the best and most caring professor I've had so far. Her exams are just like the readings and notes. Pay attention in class for extra credit on exams. She gave out candy and snacks all the time and she wanted all of us to get a good grade!
Absolutely loved Professor Kandy and would definitely take one of her classes again!

You need a 94% in order to get a 4.0 for some reason and every class you miss is a whole percent taken off of your entire final grade. There are also only 5 assignments the whole semester so you pretty much need to ace every single one and if you miss any class your final percentage is screwed. Her grading system is just weirdly flawed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kent was an amazing professor, she is very caring and flexible with deadlines. As long as you show up to class and spend some time on the essays and group projects, you will easily 4.0. She is also funny and is pretty unserious as long as you get your work done. I would definitely recommend taking WRA 101 with her, she was great.

Dr. Kent is a nice lady and she is very approachable. You are required to be in class, and she gives you four skips which is nice! If you are not in class, you will be confused because we cover different assignments in class. all work can be done in class to prep your essay, and you will have to write outside class as well. grades based on improvem
Suuuuper easy class. Grades based on your improvement from your first draft. She also allows late assignments, and just a great person overall. Would definitely recommend this professor.

While there was times I was confused as to what was happening, schedule and work wise, she was always there to help and answer questions. If you're in an IAH prepared to use Perusall and there is no way around cheating the attendance unless you have friends in the class. I enjoyed this class and would take it again.

Dr. Kent was wonderful. She grades your essays mostly on how they improved from your draft, not necessarily how good the content of the paper is. She was very nice, easy to talk to, and gave great feedback. She did a great job at keeping the course fun and making students engaged even when we had low energy/didn't answer questions. Awesome prof.

Leanne is very cool and this class was a great brain break from my major classes. Homework was very light with a short journal and a quiz due every Friday. Splits classes into cohorts so you aren't in class the full two hours. Very group work heavy, be prepared to participate in small group discussions. Loved the people I worked with in my group!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For a general education course, Kent does a tremendous job keeping students engaged and interested in the writing process. You will have five different projects with a focus on group work throughout the semester, grading for these projects heavily depends on the "process" instead of the product. Fantastic professor, would take again.

IAH 231
The kindest professors I have had at MSU. Incredibly caring and understanding, and truly cares about the feedback of her students and what they have to say- whether it is about a class topic or not. Passionate about what she is teaching, which makes lectures easy to understand. Graded by quizzes, journals, and group projects, no exams.

Super sweet professor, and also a pretty easy grader. This class focuses on the writing process, so each essay has a few components, typically a proposal, a rough and final draft, and a reflection, plus a few auxiliary assignments. She is also lenient with deadlines, but beware procrastinating; the work can pile up quickly. Highly recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Kent for IAH 231H; this was her first semester teaching the class. A lot of what she did was experimental, so the curriculum was still a work in process. She was forgiving with due dates to some extent and gave tons of feedback + opportunities to redo assignments. The most respected I've ever felt in a classroom, and I highly recommend.

Professor Kent sees you as a person and wants to see you thrive. She is so kind and considerate of you and what you might be going through. She really sees what's going on in the world and how it impacts her students. She also goes over some really great topics to help her students grow and get the credit they need.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kent is one of the best professors I have come across yet. I had her for my WRA 101 class, which is 99% of the time just taken by everyone to satisfy the university requirements, but she made me interested to learn. Plenty of time to do projects, which are mainly papers, but also a group one too. She takes the time to connect with everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kent was so friendly and made class enjoyable. All the projects are papers, but she is very lenient and understanding, and you have a long time to complete them. She provides outstanding feedback on assignments and seeks feedback from the class and recognizes sitting in class for two hours is unnecessary. Great professor, I recommend.

I loved Prof Kent. You do have to write an extra reflection essay for the projects, but it's nothing which is hard and she's a really light grader. She cancels class a lot so that you are able to work on your essays wherever you want, and as long as you are engaged in the writing process and show up to class she will give you 90+ on the projects.

All of her essays did have an additional reflection essay to write. But her grading was so easy. High 90s for everyone. She clearly explains exactly what she wants to be included in each essay and reflection, if you use that assignment sheet as you write it will be even easier to do well. She is also very flexible and understanding about due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best teacher I have had at MSU thus far. She is very understanding and has been very lenient on due dates. This class is mainly based on group work, there will be a lot of peer reviews, group activities, and group work. However, she makes every class enjoyable and fun. I would recommend taking Prof. Kent for WRA.

She is really nice but I noticed I had to do more papers than my friends who were in the same class with a different prof. If you have the time to take her class she grades really easy and is very understanding.

There are group case studies in this class - group of 4 to 5 writing a 1000 word essay on a case pertaining to the topics covered in the module - grading is not the easiest, but your group can re-submit unlimited amount of times to get a 4.0 on the paper. Attendance is required. Class wraps up with a debate, graded easy, debate was very fun.

Dr. Kent is one of the best, if not, the best HPS teacher to have for any HPS course in Lyman Briggs. All the other teachers seem to be nit picky with their grading but Dr. Kent will work with you to succeed and get a 4.0. I will say though her d2l page is very messy and sometimes she does not know what is even on it because she does not make it.
A very solid choice for 326B. The class was very easy and the workload was very manageable. There is a lot of writing in this course, however, the writing was not terribly difficult.
She's a truly kind and understanding professor. I enjoyed the way she structured the class. The work was very doable and the content was captivating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Kent is one of the kindest LB profs you can get. Her class is not hard by any means and she gives awesome feedback on your papers. I highly recommend her as a professor. LB 133 is not the easiest writing class as there is a lot of work. Dr. Kent does not overcomplicate the class. You will not be disappointed.

1 of 4 professors. Lectures are easy to follow, clear, and concise. Exams are fair and of a similar level to the practice exams. He reexplains concepts very distinctly when you ask questions after the lecture. This semester was a bit easier than the last, though that may have been due to experience with the class structure in BMB 461.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 1 of 3 professors. His lectures were better than average, homework is not bad, the textbook can be useful but also goes into a ton of depth, so it can also be confusing, exams are hard but not (usually) unreasonable, and you get a notecard (exam is a bit long for 50 minutes though, so know your stuff!). Review often, and you'll be okay!
I took this class in the Fall of 2024. The class is well structured all the lecturers were good and made getting help in the class extremely easy. Unfortunately, the class is just a hard one.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kevin is a great lecturer, but class structure was poop. There would be 4 exams (no cumulative final) and they pretty much determine your grade. Kevin would explain things clearly and simple, but when the test comes, it will be the opposite. I would say 40% of the test has easy Q's and the rest are hard. Likely will be the lowest grade you will get

He was a good guy and lecturer. Only had his for one exam, but is the course coordinator. His clicker questions and exams are so hard and there is so much content to cover. I like that he writes on the slides and encourages active listening in his lectures. Overall though, the class is hard but helps understand the crazy world of biochemistry.
The course on its own is very hard, I thought he did a great job covering content and made sure people were able to follow. I think he is a great instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The content is a lot to handle and is very difficult to keep up with. That said, Haudek teaches it the best he can. It's a lot of information to get through, but he goes *very* fast, and even then we still go over lecture time by a few minutes every day. No drops and exams are heavily weighted (compared to homework and other assignments).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Lawrence is a tough  grader and his feedback can feel pretty nitpicky and condescending at times. Don't let that discourage you, though! He actually cares a lot about his students. The key is meeting with him outside of class…he's much more approachable in person and genuinely wants to help you understand the material. Be prepared.

This class is easy if you go to class and pay attention. His quizzes and Exams are straight forward but he takes off random points for missing one small detail or if he doesn't like the format. He also dances around your questions and never answers them clearly.
Annoying!!

He is a tough grader, everything must be written in the format that he likes or else points will be ticked off. When you go to ask for help, his feedback isn't always the clearest. Be prepared for there to be a quiz on one unit, but he will teach an entirely new unit first then give you the last 10 minutes of class for the quiz.
Kevin's lectures make me want to fall asleep. He's very invested in his work, but asks unnecessary questions, is not very supportive and does not create a learning atmosphere.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Heavy lecturing and fast paced content. He has poor communication skills. His questions that border on rhetorical are incredibly difficult to answer so much so that only 5% of the class engages with his questions. His lack of regard for his students answers and his belittling mannerisms pose a significant hurdle.
Professor was kind however lectures were boring and hard to stay through the whole time, homework was due sooner than other professors.

Dr. Lawrence is a great professor. There was a ton of content that he had to speed through, but that's not his fault. He is super flexible about meeting and cares about how you do. He is great at explaining the content so that it is easy to understand. As long as you actually pay attention and try, this class is not bad.

This is a naturally difficult course, but Mr. Lawrence does an awesome job of teaching his lectures clearly and gives a lot of help opportunities like office hours. He's incredibly understanding with test makeups. He's also just all around a good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I did eventually drop this class as it was too fast paced for me. Professor Lawrence was super nice though. He was very helpful outside of class and is really understanding when it comes to homework and retakes. I would definitely not mind having him as a teacher again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Math 103 is a very difficult course itself, but prof Lawrence is always down to help and is a very amazing prof who wants to see you succeed!

Kevin is a good professor; this class was just a tad bit difficult. It is a lot of information crammed into one semester. If you have trouble keeping up, take the 2-semester class. Only problem was there was endless HW and there was a quiz every Friday. This course could have been a whole lot worse if I had a bad professor.

Great teacher, and an easy class. However the only thing would be he is very specific for how you draw and write your answers. They have to be in the order he wants and cannot over explain. And the specific storage that it asks for you to use. It's not a blow off class but the material is easy. Study for quizzes and exams and you will be fine.

Really nice guy. Goes through lectures really fast and can sometimes be hard to keep up with. Had to relearn/teach myself a bit of the material because the notes sometimes don't cover all math rules/situations. Quizzes every week. Makes videos that go over every lecture which was nice.

Awful professor and wouldn't recommend to anyone. Most of the time I had to reach it to myself. Very unhelpful when I went to his office hours. The average at least for my class was a 45% the last time I checked. The notes are not helpful when it comes to doing the webwork. He cares more about getting through the notes than if we know it or not.

This professor sometimes can go fast through certain lectures, but overall was a pretty good class. It feels a lot like algebra 2 in high school. Just pay attention and do the homework and it won't be too bad.

He doesn't really lecture at all he just stands and speaks at you. everything i learned in this class i taught to myself. there is a quiz or exam every single week. he does zoom office hours and reviews but they are the most unhelpful thing and just made me feel dumb for not getting it.

Kevin is a great guy who really loves his job. In order to do well in this course you will need to take good notes. There are weekly quizzes, However, they aren't that bad if you study. Overall, this is not a blow-off class and you will need to work hard to pass. All quizzes are closed book and note with no calculator. Kevin is a fair grader!

A very nice and caring professor who also incorporated his humor into class. Be ready to take notes. Provides lots of examples to understand the math. Wants us to do the best we can. Homework was graded for completion and had a quiz once every week/2 weeks. Got grades back quickly and responded timely. Very nice and respectful!

I had Kevin Lawrence for Math 103, and it was such an easy class. He is by far the best math teacher for 103 and made the material very easy to understand. He made himself available outside of class and showed he cared about his students.

I didn't like this class at first but slowly learned to love it. His lectures aren't really lectures, more like rounds of questions that make you think. Forces you to think rather than just take notes all class long. Used geogebra a lot to show concepts, which was new to me. I left the course feeling like I understood what was taught. Got a 4.0!

I was worried about this class as it was the last math class I needed for my program. I'm glad I had Kevin as my instructor. He knew what he was talking about. Sometimes he went off on tangents (that's a calculus joke, at least I learned that much), but overall a good prof. He was willing to meet with me outside of his office hours which was nice.

Had Prof Lawerence for both MTH 201 and 202 this year. Very good professor. Much like my teachers back in China. I had troubles with geometry class but met him in office for help. I am happy to have learned from him.

He was a good prof. Better than the one I had last semester for MTH 201. Made you think, doesn't just give you answers. Also helpful in MLC. He taught high school geometry before, so that was helpful in him knowing what he was teaching. The tests were manageable as long as you did the homework beforehand.

I had him in a different class last semester, but he recently subbed in the math class I am currently taking and it reminded me how much I miss his teaching. He makes you think. He's more interested in why an answer is what it is compared to the right answer. He realizes that we will be teachers and that we need to know this stuff before we teach.

it was my second time taking this course and he much better than the person I had first. He's different because he wants you to know why the math works and in different ways, not just interested in answers. Some in the class didn't like that and just wanted answers. Make sure to staple your homework. LOL.

He was great. I went to his office hours and made appointments a few times and it made everything so clear. He makes sure you understand why the math works, not just that you got the right answer. Made a lot of connections between elementary math and algebra that I was never shown in school. Would definitely take a course with him again.

Seems like a great guy in general lectures are full of interesting information and plenty of listening examples. Very little work outside of class but plenty of reminders for due dates for big projects. Despite the 8 am class time he was always ready to present and had plenty of enthusiasm for his lecture topics. Extremely easy class and fun.

The class is super easy. The class is mostly discussion posts (you don't need to reply to other people, just write the post), some quizzes, two essays, a video presentation, and the final. He gives a ton of supplemental materials that aren't really necessary to pass the class. Attendence is graded, but the class is very easy.

This was the easiest class I had ever taken. I often forgot I even had this class because there's hardly any work for this course; a couple of online quizzes, two essays, and one online presentation. This whole class was basically a grade booster.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far my favorite lecture professor in the college of music. He knows his stuff and is incredibly well read/researched/prepared for every class session. His projects are fun and while it was a difficult class to pass, the class didn't seem difficult for the sake of being difficult and was worth the work. He's also just the nicest guy you'll meet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof is a fraud and it comes across in both his teachings and published papers. Often in lecture he takes important lines straight from assigned articles (that you will have to read after that lecture) and presents them as his own idea. Also assigns elementary-level papers eg. students have to pick their own theme song, a very global concept.
He was fine, helpful at times but passive aggressive at others. Honestly if you show an interest in the class and go to help hours early in the semester/way before a due date hes fine.

I was worried because biology is not my strong suit. I was worried at first about the grading, but the professor does progressive grading and gives a lot of feedback to improve. Overall, I really enjoyed the class and learned a lot.

Dr. McCormick is rude and unprofessional. He gets really passive aggressive when asking questions and it makes me scared to even ask him one. He has biases on groups he likes better as well. Most of this class is based on HW which is graded on accuracy and based on his opinions. Everything is written and in person with no multiple choice.

Dr. Mccormick has to be the most caring and understanding instructor I have ever had as a student. He wants his students to succeed and he also cares about their well-being. We need more professors like him. Your exams will be very heavy but not unfair; if you complete homework and In-class assignments you will do well.

BS161 is a tough class and really difficult the way it was laid out - watch lectures outside of class and do in class assignments with a group- but Dr. M made it really easy to ask for help. He's very approachable and nice.

Dr. McCormick was a good professor, but he had the mentality that "a flipped classroom boosts test scores" mentality, which I didn't like. I feel as if it's a lazy excuse to avoid actual teaching. If you're considering BS 161 (for BS credit) and have the option to choose a different class, I would recommend doing so.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty average guy to be honest. Relatively easy to understand, he puts a lot of trust in his students that they will ask for help if they need it so sometimes he doesn't explain everything completely unless you ask. He's very easy to reach for help outside of class. Not an outstanding professor but well rounded compared to other labs I've taken.

This lab was chaotic in the way that it was laid out but Dr. McCormick did his best to make it clear for us. He would sometimes talk while we were already doing other things which led to feeling a little unsure of what we were doing. The course load wasn't super hard though and it is an easy 4.0, just kind of frustrating to get through.

Professor Khalil is a great guy who seems to care about his students. He always responded to emails fast and when I forgot to do my homework one week, he gave me credit even though it was late. I actually learned a lot from this class and the work was pretty easy (just watching lectures and responding to them).

Professor Khalil is truly wonderful. You can genuinely tell that he cares about his students and is passionate about what he teaches. He makes it easy to succeed in his class, and he's always quick to respond to emails if you're ever confused or need help. Just be sure to pay attention during his lectures and study before the tests.

He is really nice and passionate about what he teaches. I've never rated a professor on here before but he was so lovely I feel the need to for the first (and probably only) time. He's very understanding, engaged and supportive. His lectures are interesting and easy to follow and the workload isn't bad at all. Its very easy to do well in his class.

Prof Khalil is so kind and generous. You can tell he really cares about your success and wants to make the class enjoyable. His lectures are super interesting and he gives great feedback on assignments! The best professor I've had at MSU by far!

Dr. Khalil is such an amazing professor who truly cares about his students. He learned every single one of our names and was super engaging throughout the entire course. I was always so excited to attend this class twice a week. One thing is that the tests in this class are fairly difficult and there is a lot of material covered, studying is KEY!

Dr. Khalil is the best professor that I have had at MSU. He cares a lot about his students and their success. I travel frequently and he was always willing to meet me before hand to help me with the material I would be missing. He also helped me a lot with applying to my Ph.D. program in regards to class and program selection.
Has the best personality and is incredibly kind.

Learnt a great deal about Public Relations. Brought in first-hand knowledge from industry experience,  kept class interesting, and inculcated social media tools such as Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube. Would highly recommend him. He knows his stuff well!
I found him to extremely arrogant. He no longer teaches at our school. I will not miss him.

He is an inspiration from head to toe. Anyone would be blessed to be his student. His teachings are not limited to just a particular class, he supports and guides his students throughout their academic career. I am pretty sure his guidance will help me in professional life as well. The best thing about Dr. Khan, he makes us understand everything
Enjoyed having him in class. Grading was mostly done on time. He went out of the way to help our team on the course project. Highly appreciate his professional attitude and dedication.
Usually available to answer questions. Always interested to talk about his own work. Seems stressed out.
Mr. Khan is our TA for the course and I have always found him to be helpful.  His grading for the assignments and projects is fair.

Professor Khan is a born teacher. His dedication and willingness to help at every step in the course is highly appreciated. He always brought in knowledge from his industry experience which made the course very interesting and beneficial.

Professor Khan was my instructor in the online course that I took this Fall. At first I was not sure if an online course would even be worth my effort and time. I was wrong, Professor Khan and his team made the course very engaging and answered any questions I had without any delay and with great professionalism. A+++ Prof!
Very helpful with the assignments. Did answer questions right away.
He has God gifted talent of teaching!
Very helpful and always available when needed. The guy really cares for his students.
Best TA ever!

Would never take this class again. Worst lecture structure. Walker went in circles and was not organized in lecture. Exams are a foreign language. Tough grading. He constantly makes inappropriate jokes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: confusing lectures, not partial credit, no study guides, unorganized, dismissive, lies about exam averages, impossible.and exam questions don't align with classwork, homework, recitation, or notes!

Lectures were severely chaotic and disjointed, monthly exams were impossible with no multiple choice, no partial credit, no explanation of incorrect answers, and no chance to earn points back. Walker blatantly lied about exam average scores. Walker also said in office hours: students who were performing poorly “weren't worth teaching.”

It was always hard to know what to study. Walker's handouts are very confusing and sometimes even the TAs didn't even know what the answer was. The exams are also different from the textbook and Walker's own handouts. Most questions you couldn't even figure out what he was asking for in each box.

I took CEM 251 back in 2018. Dr. Walker is an incredible professor. I attended his office hours weekly and that really helped. If you put the effort in, you'll succeed in this course. Nothing bad to say about Dr. Walker. I'd recommend taking his course.
Professor walker is a good lecturer despite what others say, if you pay attention in lecture and do his optional handouts you will do fine in this class.

I think his low rating is unwarranted. Mr. Walker is an expert in what he teaches and if you learn through analogy or stories then he will be a great professor. I would understand if his teaching style wasn't for everyone, but lectures are not going to be boring at least. Just attend lectures, study, review: I found outlining the textbook helpful.

He was a pretty terrible lecturer, but grading was quite generous, although you are only graded on like 5 things total. So be sure to do well in all of them. Going to lecture is pretty useless unless you want to participate. Make sure to read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly I found this class to be rather simple, I finished with a 3.0 but never once did I have to put in any effort to achieve that doing the homework was enough and the first exam is all review from gen chem if you just do the homework and do well on one of the exams you should easily get a 3.0

You know in old movies that take place in the dessert with tumbleweeds and half swing doors and cowboys that have toothpicks in their mouth, that is Kevin. He is the most out of pocket person I've ever heard speak. He talks in circles yet thinks he is explain things. One TA was a cocky weasel and the other was the sweetest guy. Exams are impossible

Most people seemed to hate Walker, but he handed out extra credit like candy and made the class very achievable with an 85% cutoff for 4.0. The TAs are also really good for this class and make the content in lecture easy to stomach. He is so funny in class and creates easily rememberable phrases to describe certain mechanisms.

It was without a doubt the worst class I have ever taken. Kevin is an awful teacher. You were only graded on 5 exams and homework. The only kids who passed his class with a 4.0 were chemical engineering majors. He makes very weird sounds and slightly sexual comments about chemistry during class just made me feel weirdly uncomfy. COLD CALLS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easily the most disorganized professor ever. Walker does not have sympathy for poor grades, and does not alter his teaching style to accommodate learners. Curves are not offered, extra credit is minimal, and the exams do not reflect any learned material that is taught. Shame on MSU for hiring the literal worst organic chemistry professor ever.

Lectures are disjointed and did not seem to have a specific goal. Quiz class averages rarely surpassed 40%. Walker never addressed this. Just moved on, not changing his teaching style. Would write mechanisms, but not explain what they were for or even what mechanism it was. Nice as a person, but should not be teaching this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is one of the worst professors at MSU. The chemistry department should be ashamed that he teaches. He has been reported numerous times over the years to no avail. He curses (constantly), proceeds to deviate and go on long tangents, is very difficult to follow in lectures and tries to to be “funny,” by making inappropriate jokes/remarks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most people seemed to dislike Walker, but I felt he was a pretty fair professor. His grading criteria was very fuzzy at first for the biweekly quizzes, but it got better as the semester progressed. He was very funny during lectures, but often acted like you were stupid if you asked questions. Curved the final and gave clear topics to study for it.

Walker is funny prof but his lectures are very unorganized. His office hours are the best resource possible as he can actually explain concepts and come up with problems for you to work on- which preps you for his unique style of quiz questions. He offers a TON of extra credit (around 50 points, aka an entire quiz worth) making it a fairly easy A.

he writes notes on the board but he rarely indicates the mechanism or topic of what he is doing. quizzes were obscenely hard since there was no real structure. no clear learning targets. he is all over the place at all times, no coherent train of thought. he does remember his students and tries to use examples and analogies.

Walker has an interesting teaching style. He often begins to explain a topic and gets off track. Quizzes are hard because we aren't prepared well with what is on them. I've tried to follow him in lecture but its just so hard. Lots of homework (50 problems per week) that you have to use the book to teach yourself. Very difficult class.

Uses chalk and board. My notes were just structures & arrows; no real meaning behind it (which is partially my fault, could of wrote some words). He often skips the arrows and makes it hard how he got to the end. Quizzes are difficult if you don't study b/c it's just blank boxes. Likes students who goes to his office hours and knows them by name.

Walker is a good professor. It's obvious he puts effort into teaching and giving the students what they need to do well. He teaches chemistry though, not mindless problem solving, so be prepared to actually try to understand the material.  He supplies lecture notes and is helpful for any questions you might have after lectures and in office hours.

I'm sure Walker is a decent person outside of the classroom, but his lectures are extremely hard to follow, he treats the class like it's a review course and your entire grade is based off of his impossible quizzes, which he does not prepare students well for. I tried really hard to like him in the beginning but his teaching style is just awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I attended every lecture and all my recitations. I spent time trying to teach myself topics that i did not understand but the exams were VERY tough. Don't recommend unless you are willing to go to every office hour PLUS study 1-2 hours after every lecture.

Im sure professor Walker is a great guy outside of class, however, I couldnt think of a single positive thing to say about the way he runs this course. Let me put it simply, Walker refrained from using D2L the entire semester, only used his words and chalk to explain complicated topics, and was distracted the entirety of the class. I wish you luck

His lectures are very confusing and honestly did not help a lot, but there are quizzes every week that you automatically get 100% on if you just go to class. His exams are very challenging. You will have to take a lot of time out of class to succeed in this course. I highly recommend watching youtube videos and doing the homework to study for exam.

I saw he had horrible reviews and I thought I was smart enough to manage, but nope. He's hands down one of the worst profs at MSU. He acts like this is a review course. My biggest pet peeve is that he hardly ever addresses what he's teaching. For example you could be working on stereoisometry, but he hardly ever actually labels what he is teaching.

Walker is a funny dude, but everything I learned in this class was from his amazing TA. This class was ridiculously hard where only the top 5% of geniuses in the class succeed. Grade is only composed of 4 exams and 6 quizzes. But he did round my grade A LOT at the end of the semester which was nice. Highly suggest another prof tho
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Walker is not the best at lectures and goes off on tangents but does care about his students. Don't take his class if you're not willing to put in hours on your own. Use resources and office hours because lectures move quickly and his notes are jumbled. His exams are hard but if you do all the practice problems multiple times, it's not too bad.
This guy is not organized by any means! and he doesn't know how to articulate his theories or the mechanisms of the reactions! prepare to learn everything on your own.

He needs to be taught how to actually teach a class of 400 kids.Made decent mnemonics. This man made me skip class frequently. Do not sit near the front row unless you want to be called on. He makes you feel dumb. I used to love chemistry, but having him as a teacher made me hate it now. Avoid him at all costs.
"VERY unorganized, makes ZERO sense, scatterbrained. I learned nothing in class. Never looked at my notes once to study. Learned everything from TA's.

First of all, I have a 4.0 GPA, I am a lyman briggs and honors college student. I found Walker to be terrible. The second day of class, he called some girl "Red" who had red hair and a red shirt and at the end of class another girl asked a question and he called her "ginger" after he thought his mic was off. He also blows students off, A LOT.

I ended up 4.0ing this class only because I spent over an hour every day solely studying for this class, teaching myself the material. Dr. Walker's exams are definitely tough and sometimes include things that are not clearly covered in lecture. Exams make up a great percentage of your exam, so if you don't do well on those you will not do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He talks to his students, who don't know chemistry like they've been studying it for as long as he has. He also doesn't teach the overarching concepts in class. His practice exams are wayyy easy compared to the actual exams. He does reviews, but when the questions he reviews are not the same as exam questions, it doesn't help much. AVOID him.

He has a lot of aspects that make up a good professor, but I think he does poorly at connecting with/understanding his students (it also doesn't help that exams are 93% of your grade). If you always pay attention and practice a lot outside of class you should see somewhat decent results. I never went to office hours, but I've heard they help.

Lectures are hard to follow as he constantly goes off on tangents, your grade is determined almost entirely by the insanely difficult exams (which aren't curved at all) and you will likely have to teach yourself the material outside of class. However, due to the way the grading scale works it is entirely possible to bomb every exam and still pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid him. Certified gpa tanker and not a very nice person. Does not answer emails quickly or in full. Exams do not resemble his lecture material or the textbook he assigns. Exams make up 93% percent of the grade. 10+ hrs of studying for each exam did not help my exam scores. Talks down on students, has no sympathy and lectures incoherently.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have such mixed opinions of Dr. Walker. it is evident to see he is very passionate about the material, is very knowledgeable, and does want to see his students succeed. I gave a low rating because he does teach the class as if we already know organic chem. If you aren't willing to put in work, then don't take it. He can't do everything for you.
Mediocre professor. Class is easy, but lectures consist of Walker rambling on and on about nonsense.

I honestly didn't learn anything from the class. Material isn't well explained. Tests and other items are not graded in efficient manner. You will teach yourself the information if you actually want to know the material.

Now that I've had a semester away from Walker, I can speak fairly about him. The class is hard, but he decently prepares you. People love to complain when things aren't an easy A, but if you put in the work & try you can do good (I recommend going to his review sessions before exams - super helpful). Prepared me well for Orgo 2 unlike other profs.

While Dr.Walker tries to make lectures fun and bearable it's just really difficult to learn from him and most of my learning has been from youtube and the textbook. The only grades that are put in are exams and biweekly quizzes. I would strongly recommend choosing a different professor unless you're okay with teaching yourself orgo.

Where do I begin. He is a very off task professor - he starts talking about one thing and next thing I know he has completely shifted to a different topic that has nothing to do with what we're doing. His exams are quite near impossible and your grade is mainly made up of solely exams. STAY AWAY FROM HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor at MSU. Lectures are hard to follow and make little to no sense. You have to study for hours after class to make sense of the material. He gets distracted easily and is not open to questions. Exams are pretty much your only grade and he makes them insanely difficult. I have a 4.0, but walkers class is impossible. STAY AWAY!!

I normally don'r leave reviews but for Professor Walker I have to make en exception. He is by far the worst professor I have ever had. I had to teach myself all of the content, and he crammed two very important topics into one class period. Stay away. If you can't, be ready to spend hours on your own teaching yourself organic chemistry.

His lectures are very hard and confusing to understand. Besides points for the in-class quizzes and going to recitation, exams are the main thing. The exams are nothing like the questions we practice in class and they are very hard.

his lectures are so long and he can't stay on one topic for more than two minutes. he never finishes his thought and is not easy to follow at all. he lectures as if you're already supposed to know the material and does not properly explain anything. exams make or break your whole grade so if you're not doing well on those you have like no EC.

I didn't really learn much in the class. Everything I learned I taught myself. Exams are hard and not from Dr. Walker handwritten notes . He doesn't teach very well. He doesn't answer questions very well either. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT! He isn't a bad prof, just not my cup of tea.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Walker  is a very nice professor and is very passionate about the material; however, CEM 251 is a hard course! You need to dedicate hours each week just to keep up with the material and be ready to read and take notes independently from the textbook as well! Attendance is a must. He is a very knowledge prof who gives lots of extra credit!

I hated him at first, but he grew on me. He is usually entertaining, and makes you work for your grade. Slack off, or don't follow his instructions and you might as well drop. Knows his stuff and will help you. This was the hardest class I ever took, and the one I am most proud to say I got and A in.

They either love him or hate him. I don't understand. Know him from couple of semesters ago. HE'S great to everyone. Knows his stuff. Is helpful. Makes chem fun. But you must study. He can't do everything for you.

Dr. Walker is a very funny guy but definitely knows what he's talking about. His jokes are sooo random but they kinda make sense when relating it to chemistry, so it's funny. CEM 251 is hard course. It is 60% on you and 40% on him. So, practice and go to his or TAs office hours.
Dr. Walker is a decent professor. Not the greatest lecturer. Notes are all hand written and they sometimes get sloppy. Would recommend if you don't like homework and willing to study a lot for tests.

It's definitely a difficult course, but Walker makes the content entertaining and accessible. He's genuinely invested in the success of his students. Use the extra practice problems to your advantage - he's not kidding when he says a lot of those practice problems are similar to exam questions. If you have questions, ask!

He is a great professor and a great guy. Teaching sometimes does not seem to be his best suit. He is unorganized and you will not have an idea what your grade is. If you show up to class and do the work and study a little bit you will pass his class and do pretty well. You have to respect everyone's ideas which I liked.

CEM 251 is a lecture-heavy class, and unfortunately I often found Prof. Walker's lectures to be boring and drawn-out. He is a nice person and a fair, quick grader, but I wish I had been more engaged in his class. CEM 251 is not a hard class, but you really need to know all details in the lecture notes. Anything in them is fair game for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo is hard. IF you put in the time and work. Highly recommend doing all the problems he assigns you for homework because that is what the exam will be like.

He can sometimes go on tangents here and there about what somethings can be used for but overall he is pretty good at giving examples in class and always holds review sessions and encourages his students to come to office hours
He gave extra credit after students asked for it; he has evening review sessions every Tuesday.  I managed to get a 4.0. It is a tough class, but doable.

Professor Walker is a fantastic lecturer, he made use of analysis and comparisons that can help with understanding otherwise vague and new concepts. He's also quite hilarious and would spend time explaining things to you as long as you asked. Go to lectures, take notes, and do every end-of-chapter problem (important) to do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm convinced the last 4 positive comments on here are made by bots or paid for by Professor Walker. I can confidently say he is the worst instructor I've had in my 19 years of living. Avoid at literally all costs if you're not expecting to put hours upon hours upon hours into orgo and still see no results in your grade because of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard class material but nothing much you can do about it. Allows honors option, answers emails fairly quickly. Quizzes and tests are kinda hard but he doesn't try to trick you, answers every question during lecture, lots of opportunities for extra points.
Good class. I was challenged but I learned a lot. Going into this class I thought I was going to hate it but now I actually enjoy organic chemistry.
It's orgo, it's going to be hard. There is lots of studying! All lectures were posted. He's slightly hard to understand but he knows his stuff.

Walker is very passionate about chemistry and prepares his students well for future Chem courses. He uses lots of helpful analogies, and honestly tries to help his students succeed by offering lots of extra credit. Be prepared to study, because the tests are hard and make up the majority of your grade. Think twice before taking the honors option

If professor Walker were to teach the tale of the three little pigs, he'd tell the story backwards and forget to say that the wolf was bad. Absolutely horrendous "teaching style", which involves spending time regurgitating irrelevant information that will never appear on any of his self-made exams. Not there to help you, just to make jokes.
This class has driven me to therapy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Walker's lectures are all over the place and he doesn't explain anything he "teaches" to students. The exams are WAY too unnecessarily hard and nothing related to lecture at all. Averages were failing and he was HAPPY with that and said it was normal for his class, but wouldn't do anything about it. He does not care about his students grades AT ALL
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor. Horribly unorganized lectures/notes. You will not learn a thing unless you read the book and teach yourself. Four exams make up 90% of the overall grade and are 10x more complex than the content he taught. No grade curves at all. I have no positive comments about this class. Don't take his class if you care about grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Walker is a nice person but a horrible professor. Absolutely HORRIBLE. Please, avoid taking his class if you want a good grade in orgo. For the last two exams, the averages were a 58% and he still refuses to curve. Your grade is solely based on exams and the only content material you receive from him to study are his crappy handwritten notes.

VERY DIFFICULT. I don't recommend unless you want to teach yourself. He is very difficult to understand because he is extremely disorganized. Notes are all over the place and often goes off on tangents in the middle of problems. He is a good guy and tries but I do not recommend him as a prof as he is extremely difficult to follow.

Over the semester you have 3 exams & a final and those 4 exams make up 450/500 points total for the class (90% of your grade). His notes are all over the place and make no sense and the only way to learn is khan academy or a tutor. 2nd exam we took, average was a 57% & no curve because 1 person got 100%. Find a diff prof if you want to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He canceled an entire exam the day on hours after it was supposed to take place because he could not figure out how to use the same software we had already successfully tested on. He uses heavy terminology. The only reason I passed was my tutor and the fact that he had to change the grading scale to 74% to get 4.0 since he dropped an entire exam.

Genuinely an awful professor and human being. Calls on people randomly. Will make fun of you during lecture if you leave early. Spends half the class telling unfunny jokes and irrelevant stories. Constantly makes mistakes while teaching and his notes are horrible. Khan Academy does a better job teaching ochem than this guy ever will. Avoid.

Professor Walker does not deserve the amount of hate that he gets. He is very knowledgable. It is just misfortunes of switching to online that became a problem. His grading scale helps you a lot, I 3.5d this class and I didn't deserve it with how little work I put in. He also gives more extra credit than any other chem class!

Everyone is tough on Dr. Walker but he really tries his best to accommodate everyone with exam curves and accessibility. exams long so study! best things are the practice quizzes in class and the end of chapter textbook questions. everyone that complains about Dr. Walker probably wanted their grade handed to them. He's a nice guy and likes to joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: THE ABSOLUTE WORST PROFESSOR AT MSU. he does not teach, he jokes around the entire lecture. he was so behind this semester that he didnt have time to cover 2 ENTIRE CHAPTERS. if you get him as a professor, if he even has a job after this semester (hes been fired before ive heard), drop the class and take it next semester. save yourself the stress

Knows what he is talking about and is able to explain it in many different ways but his lectures are disorganized and he jumps around a lot. Also, the tests are not at all what you would expected and much harder than what you learn. There is no hw in this class your grade is only the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take CEM 251 with walker. I learned more from the TAs/tutors and by teaching myself than he ever taught me. His lectures are hardly worth it. He does not know how to teach effectively and he constantly jumps all over the place. Hes a nice guy, but could use some guidance on how to teach.

Dr. Walker is a very intelligent man; however, he does not understand how to teach his knowledge to those who have never seen organic chemistry before. Choose other professors to learn the material, because he talks more about trying to make students understand him than actually presenting the material to his students in a way that's easy to grasp.

The students' attitudes seem to change year-to-year--guided by social streams. The practice problems look very similar to those on the exam, save those that are concept problems that require you to THINK. Those who do poorly (they are few) in the class seem to think Walker can be a miracle worker and offer the harshest criticisms.

Would not recommend any one to take cem 251 with Dr. Walker. I feel that he assumes his students know what he is talking about when in reality we are all clueless. He poorly explains topics and claims that his practice problems are far more difficult than his exam problems which is completely untrue. If you're not pre-med or pre-vet, run away.
You have to put the work in. You get deja vu after studying practice problems long enough. When you get the test, you realize many of the problems are exactly the same as what you just practiced.

It seems prof walker has changed his ways. I had him for last semester orgo I and he was a good teacher. It gets sticky when he tries to put things into perspective in his own way. Either way the practice homework he posts is 90% the material on the exam.. he even says so. I 4.0 and I just made sure i understood all concepts and problems on the hw.

DO NOT TAKE ORGANIC CHEMISTRY WITH DR. WALKER! He is a terrible teacher, and doesn't seem to care if the students learn the material. He's rather rude and will make you feel dumb if you don't know the answer to questions he asks. His exams are outrageous. This is the worst experience I've had at MSU.

This is by the far the worst teacher on the planet...you can hardly understand anything she says. She makes a somewhat interesting course, DULL & BORING. There is absolutely no point in going to lecture because she takes it DIRECTLY from the book...so just read the book. She will not keep you updated on your grade throughout the entire semester.

Personally, I felt like she made a class that had the potential to be really interesting, incredibly irritating. She takes everything from lectures directly from the book so you don't even need to go to class. It makes it worse that she is REALLY biased about everything she talks about instead of keeping an open mind, which I find very frustrating.

The tests are hard to understand because they're not exactly written in regular English, which ended up hurting my grade.  It's an easy class with not much work, and the professor is very passionate (maybe even too passionate) about what she lectures on.
TERRIBLE. she makes me not wanna come to her class ever. usually i dont, just to protect my mind. horrible teaching skills and almost completely impossible to understand. STAY FAR AWAY.

The course material might have been interesting, but it was guided on statistics pulled directly from the book. Though a nice woman, I felt that a huge burden was put onto the TA. The grammar on the tests was sometimes so jumbled that it was impossible to know what the question was even asking.

Her class is so easy, but don't expect to learn anything. She would assign us to read wikipedia pages for homework and have Pakistani fashion shows... regularly. Again, the class was a breeze, but she's awful.

I actually thought she was kind of fun, mainly because of her accent and because she loved it when people debated in her class. Also, it was really easy. I rarely went to class on tuesdays (exams and stuff were on thursdays) and still got a 3.5 with almost no studying. Really not that bad for a required ISS class.
Probably the worst professor at MSU.. Avoid her!!!

Years later, this woman is my prime example of professors who force you to memorize nonsense to pass the class, and therefore sacrifice your true understanding of the bigger picture. She cares more about useless statistics than she does about concepts one could use in other classes or reality.

DO NOT EVER TAKE ANY OF HER CLASSES. SHE IS HORRIBLE. All we ever talked about was Muslims, Arabs, and Islams. It was an intro to Sociology course. Also, she doesn't put any grades on Angel. It's been a week since I took my final and still haven't received my score back yet. I got my scores from my exam I took yesterday already. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Worst professor I've had while at Michigan State.  She could care less about students, rarely taught unless it was reading definitions directly off her powerpoint, and made a sociology class into a lesson on how all of the white Americans are ruining Muslims' lives.  One upside is that it was an easy class.  Stay away at all costs.

Longest exams ever, and only gives you a limited amount of time which is less than your normal class.  Doesn't know what a valid excuse is for being in the hospital.  Will not post notes to Angel,isn't helpful to any concerns students have. Can't understand her English.

Do not take any of her classes if you can help it.  She is a horrible teacher, doesn't know her own slideshows, and has very poor grammar.  She will often read right from the book-- I can do that at home.  She is also very difficult to understand.  Don't bother going to class, because the tests are completely out of the book.

I came into this class with an open mind, and came out of it pissed off. Not only is she rude, but her tests are ridiculous. She has you read roughly 300 pages per exam just to ask you dates and percentages. She's a pathetic excuse for a teacher (considering she doesn't teach) and i would never recommend this class if you value your sanity.

Seemed culturally knowledgeable at first, later it really _seemed_ like her only interest was preventing overprivileged white people from passing. Asked specific details about population % during specific time periods; ignore her lectures and surf the web. Moved students around (a lot) during exams, which was incredibly distracting and destructive.
hard to understand, shows notes too fast. make sure you read the book! on exams she ask too specific of questions, kinda impossible

This woman complains about how she has been discriminated against for being an Arab Muslim but practices her own form of discrimination. Should you take her class(es), be prepared to bombarded with Islam and nothing else. People outside our class constantly asked with confused faces if it was a religions class, but we only discussed Islam.

I was very pleased with this professor, she is a smart woman and has a lot of life experience to back up her information.  Unfortunately, I noticed that students were somewhat obnoxious in her class, and I think it was for discriminatory reasons or simply their lack of understanding a different culture.  I highly recommend her... if you want to lea

There's no REAL reason to go to this class. She reads from the book - or Wikipedia - every day. She told us videos wouldn't be on exams. Two weeks before the final, she told us they would. She refused to meet anyone about them during office hours or give the names of them.   Take a class taught by someone interested in helping students learn.

This class was HORRIBLE!!! I thought it sounded interesting, but it was boring, and I didn't learn a thing! The tests were ridiculously hard, and the items on the test were not of importance. It seemed like she was just trying to stump us instead of helping us learn. I hated this class, I hope nobody ever takes it again.

Possibly the worst professor I've had at MSU. Got rid of essay exams presumably because she cannot understand big words. Assumes that all students are rich kids who are wasting their parents' money by not coming to class, but I wasted my own money by taking it. Extremely biased toward Muslim/Arab conflicts. Ruined my interest in the subject.

Zaki can barely speak English. Her test questions are structured poorly. Attendance is mandatory, and you fill out a scantron sheet to prove you were there. She once lectured by reading directly off Wikipedia...! How this woman managed to attain a doctorate is a mystery.

Abominable.  At best, she has a tenuous grasp of the English language.  The TA bears the brunt of the teaching work.  Will occasionally lecture directly from such scholarly sources as Wikipedia.  It's nearly impossible for her to generate any kind of enthusiasm for the class.  The tests are easy, but with some obscenely obscure questions from text.

She is by far the worst teacher I have ever had. Even if you study it is useless, she does not curve any of her tests. She makes her TA do all the work and they never answer your e-mails. Good luck trying to get a decent grade. Attendance is mandatory so show up for all the movies/panels. She is wasting everyone's time as a professor. STAY AWAY!!!!
She is good teacher
waste of my time.

ISS330B Lots of reading.  Dr. Zaki has terrible english language skills. Her tests are poorly written. It is possible to pass her class.  Do the reading and attend all 5 required panels and all 5 required movies.

Poor Grasp of the English language (can not understand her). Also, At least when I had the class back in 98, she  had an administrative position and thus did not teach much, which was evident in her performance
will do fine in class if you do all your readings
Don't ever take this class if you don't have to, you will regret it!  I studyed my ass off and I still did horrible exams will kill you literally!

Lecture is completely useless, frustrating, and boring.  There are a lot of outside panels, lectures, conferences, and whatnot that are required to pass.  The exams kick you in the face, no matter how much you study.  This is definitely one of my least favorite classes ever.
Incredibly boring lectures. Really hard tests. Do yourself a favor and don't take this class.
Dont do it! Please no... if you value your GPA you wont take this class... Boring, and long... notes and reading.. thats all.. not really worth your time to go to class...
Her tests are hard.  Try and see if you can get someone else because I studied two days straight for her test and it didn't help that much.  I never knew sociology could be so hard.
Back in 1993(?) gave me an F on a paper for 'too many big words'...I still have the paper and 11 years later haven't forgotten.  One of the all-time worst teachers I've ever had :(
boring.  boring. boring.  whenever i wanted to talk to her, i had to tal to ta's.  plus - i took it at 8am.  bad idea.  you don't have to go really.
Class is a joke, dont bother going, some manditory, panals and movies, her lectures are boring as all hell LOTS of reading

Zaki is a joke, the class isnt too terrible, there are some mandatory Panals and Movies, lectures are a waste of time, but the tests are killer, the material is stuff not even close to lectures, lots of reading tho
one of the worst most unproductive and pointless classes i have had the unfortunate pleasure of taking.
No Comments
she didn't like me intitially...but she still was very helpful
No Comments
No Comments
She is very easy, if you can just get pass the accent. Very intelligent!
Very funny. Would take him again. 4 tests, multiple choice and short answer. HW at least once a week.
Hilarious guy. One of my fav professors so far. He makes his lectures very interesting and cares deeply about the subject.

Doctor Kimbirauskas has been my favorite professor at MSU yet. He expects a lot from his students, and pop quizzes can be assigned, however, he is very accessible and make the topics discussed super interesting. I learned so much from this class and I was only really taking it to complete my ISB credit. Awesome professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. K is the best professor you could have for an 8am lecture. He cares so much about his students and loves it when you engage. His lectures were interesting and you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches.
KimbirGOAT. Need i say more.
Great Guy and Genuinely wants students to succeed, MCQ were confusing at points but just study for the test and you'll be good.

Loved this class! Professor was really engaging and had some funny sotries to share. Even though the class was exam heavy it really isnt hard to get a 4.0 in this class. I did'nt really pay attention in class and studied for maybe two hours for each exam and always got above a 95%. Theres also plenty of extra credit. Only had 2 pop quizzes!!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
The exams are difficult, no study preparation material, only resources include "looking back" at lecture slides. When Dr. K was asked how to improve grade in the class, he said "look back at the slides and THINK ABOUT IT." MCQ format is difficult with options such as A,B,C,D,AB,BC,CA,All of the above. 
Good guy in general, just not a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great professor so if you attend lectures, you grasp the concepts easily. Tests are a huge portion of the grade so you have to prepare for them. Overall, the course was fun even though I'm not that interested in the content. Attendance isn't tracked, but you have to turn in all homework in person, and there are a few surprise quizzes

This professor is so fun and I really enjoyed his class. Attendance isn't mandatory but there are multiple pop quizzes. There is a lot of homework assignments but they are all so easy. Highly recommend his class.
He's a funny professor with interesting lectures. The tests can be a little tough if you don't pay attention, but he offers extra credit questions at the end of every test. Overall would take again

Great teacher! This course mainly focus on the topic for environmental science, but also involves some content for insects. He do cares about the class participation and want to make sure you understand the class materials. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you do need to turn in the hand-written homework during class. Overall a great professor.

He is a great professor, this class is a great course and I learned lots. Only issue I have is with the course there is a lot of terms to memorize and most exams pull stuff from prior units. The material is mostly 8th grader stufff.

He's a great professor with a lot of passion for teaching. This class is super easy if you just dedicate some time to study for the exams. They all had 5 points of extra credit opportunity and were just like his lectures. Occasional pop-quizzes to increase attendance, but attendance isn't mandatory. Overall, probably one of the easier ISB courses.

Attendance isn't like actually taken but you have to turn in homework in class on paper, so you have to go for that. If you try at all you will be fine just pay attention and study the slides before exams. The multiple choice can be tough but if you study you will be good.

Dr.K is so caring and funny and he has really helpful lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory, but sometimes there's a pop quiz. I think it's really important to show up as much as you can anyway. The lectures he gives are pretty much exactly what you're going to see on the exams, and he makes it all very straightforward as long as you pay attention.

Dr. K is such a fun and caring guy, he makes sure that you know everything you need to know before an exam and he offers extra credit on his exams (At least the ones I took). He likes to joke around and be funny and share some of his life experiences and stories. I will very likely be trying to take him again as a professor.

SUPER NICE AND FUNNY GUY. Theres no attendance taken, but you have physical homework to hand in almost every class so you have to go anyway. Only complaint I have is on his exams. The answer chocies sometimes go all the way to G because choices are A, B, C, A&B, A&C, B&C, A&B&C. I got 100% on the written portions, but 60/70% on the multiple choice.

for his exams he gives no study guide. You also have multiple choice and written portions on the exams and if you don't write the exact word he wants, you will fail the question. He also makes his exams too hard for a required class that most people don't have an interest in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was very easy. He's a professor who definitely wants class participation in his lectures and it's unfortunate when no one is willing to answer cause he's not asking for a lot. He does have a big personality and lots of anecdotes. If you pay attention in class you will do well on the exams. Overall chill and I did learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a nice and knowledgeable instructor who cares about attendance and participation. He keeps students on their toes with pop quizzes to encourage showing up, which can help them stay engaged. However, when I asked for help on how to improve after an exam, I didn't get much clear guidance or feedback. Overall, he is a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The adam sandler of MSU
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He was a very engaging lecturer. I wasn't super interested in the course content in general but he made it bearable enough to do well. I didn't study for any exam except the final which is why I 3.5'd but if you put maybe 5 hours into studying each exam (there's 4) its an easy 4.0

Dr. Kimbirauskas was amazing. He was a great teacher and overall great person. He made things in the class interesting, even if you didn't have a interest in the course topics. The tests are a little difficult with their being many options on the tests (A & B, A & B & C). Would definitely recommend taking Dr. K...

Attendance not taken, but you usually have to go to class to turn in a homework assignment anyways. Occasional pop quiz. Lectures are boring but fine. Four exams throughout the semester. None dropped but no final. They are hard with the multiple choice. You will have to do lots of studying. Recommend going to class so that you don't miss anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty chill class, the only annoying thing is the exams. usually 20-30 multiple choice questions and 2-4 short answer. Short answer is usually pretty easy but the multiple choice has options of a, b, c, d, a&b, a&c, a&d, c&d, abc&d. It is extremely annoying and so hard to get the actual question right.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funny teacher with amazing lectures.

Few pop quizzes, easy, sometimes worked with classmates. I was afraid this class would ONLY be about insects (they creep me out), but it really wasn't. Had a few assignments, about one every two weeks, that only take 30-60 mins to do. If you just pay attention and truly absorb the information from class, you'll do great. Prof. K is amazing guy

Dr. K was a very lecture-heavy class but the lectures were entertaining and easy to follow. Make sure you go to class because there are only 5/6 lectures between exams so you can miss a lot of information missing one class. He is a very nice and caring teacher. you will do well in the class if you do all the work.

DO NOT MISS A CLASS. I passed everything but my first exam because I missed it. When your in class, don't take notes and just listen to him, take notes once you're out of class and try to remember everything important after. It will make exams easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at Michigan State by far. Really cares to teach the information and make us apply it; because of this it's important to attend lectures. Extra credit opportunities on exams, super fun and respected guy overall. Literally such an easy 4.0 if you just show up and pay like 50% attention.

This class was very easy, there are only 4 quizzes and most quizzes have some extra credit questions which can help boost your grade. Attendance isn't required but all homework has to be turned in in person, so you'll be attending most days if you want a good grade, there are also a handful of pop quizzes.

Take this professor for your ISB credit, easy class, 4 exams, sometimes homework, and in-class quizzes (though he doesn't tell you until the day of), attendence isn't required but some days he throw in HW or quizzes for a grade/credit. Overall nice professor and is the GOAT of science.

Boring class but he makes it engaging. Attendance technically isn't mandatory, but go anyway. There are pop quizzes and homework that you cant make up. Heads up, the exams are written poorly. They're mainly multiple choice, and sometimes the options go up to G&H. His labs are so much better, would recommend him for those over his lecture.

One of the funniest with full of energetic professors I've had. I find the topic to be kind of boring but he makes the lecture sound fun and easy to understand. Beware of homework, and is part of your final grade so it is important for YOU TO COME TO CLASS. Exams are pretty mediocre but expect to see lots of memorization to do well in class.
Very fun class, he actually cared about learning and was passionate about the class. I expected it to be a blow off but he made me care and I'm grateful for that

This has been my favorite professor so far. I would beware that showing up to class is important because of an occasional pop quiz. But he truly cares about the subject and loves answering your questions. Would 100% take this professor again.

The worst thing about this class is the way that he writes his exams. Almost every single question has an option a,b,c,a&b,a&c, ab&c, etc. Some of the questions go all the way to option i.
He also acts like he is the most caring professor and that he cares about what students need, but gives incredibly difficult exams and is lowkey really annoying.

This professor shows much passion towards what he teaches. He really wants us to actually learn than to just learn for the sake of a grade.
