Chemistry itself is what is the hard part of this course. The professor is great. She wants you to understand the content and goes over how to succeed in the class every day before the lecture. The homework is graded based on effort and is fairly easy and the exams are graded harshly depending on the TA, but overall they're pretty easy.
Very good lecturer! Going to class is really important though and not getting behind
The structure of the lectures and the course as a whole is super followable and well-thought out. She clearly discusses the expectations from the class and as long as you follow that you'll pass!

This class is just unnecessarily hard for being the lowest level chem course available at MSU. It is the definition of a weeder course. Dr. Kijewska is a fine instructor, the course difficulty isn't her fault. The whole chem department needs an overhaul, but she is a fine instructor and friendly to students when they have questions or concerns.

I loved having Dr. Kijewska for CEM 141. Her lectures are thorough and interesting. The learning objectives of each lecture and the required knowledge for each exam are clear. She is caring and very nice.

I had her for both CEM 141 and CEM 142, and she truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. However, the transition from an online setting where I was able to get a 4.0, and then to an in-person setting was very difficult. The multiple choice exams are very difficult and you have to study every little thing if you want to succeed.

Professor Kijewska is a very nice professor to have. She is friendly and easy to talk to. You're required to participate during lectures but it does help keep you engaged. You have two short assignments each week, but you have to study outside of lectures to do well. It is a hard class, but the chem help room is a great resource to use.

Dr. Kijewska was okay to me. Her HAs were more of the problem than she was, but she still wasn't great. I feel like she either over or under explained everything. Quizzes in this class are hard and the graded assignments are even harder.

Favorite professor!! She cares about her students and will constantly check to make sure everyone is on the same page in lectures. That being said, in order to get a good grade you have to put the time in, study, and ask questions. I took Dr. Kijewska for both CEM 141 and 142, and I will miss not being in her class in the future.

The TAs are very hard graders when it comes to the graded assignments. She gives amazing lectures and makes the material interesting and tries to keep everyone engaged. She always checks up on the students and tries her best to make sure that everyone understands the material.

This is a non-bias report. Dr.K is an amazing professor. However, her TAs will butcher the course by being difficult graders. The quizzes are difficult in this course, each question will have 4 or more multiple choice answers being difficult to differentiate since they're similar but a little bit is changed. Graded assignment grading criteria sucks

She is super nice and overall a good teacher, but the TA's are really strict on grading and that was ultimately why I didn't get the grade I wanted. Studying is very important or else you won't get a good grade on the exams.

Lectures presented material clearly, participation is encouraged, and there are plenty of opportunities to ask questions. My biggest frustration with the course was the inconsistent grading of the TAs and the ambiguous grading criteria. Dr. Kijewska is a talented lecturer, however, and was always willing to help.

It's hard to get very personal with her because her classes are so huge but that's not her fault. She explains content very well and clearly. The TA's do the grading, so any issues with that is on them but it was never an issue for me.

The professor is probably one of the best and easiest cem professors you will have. She explains things so easy to understand. However, the only thing holding me back from giving a 5/5 rate is because of the TA's. I'm unaware of which ones, but they are extremely difficult graders, more difficult than the professor. The course would be perfect.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best cem professors Ive ever had. Many find her lecture videos boring. however, her lecture videos are so easily explained to where its almost hard to not learn. Shell do a poll quiz during lectures to see if the class understands, if majority doesnt, she explains it again and better. Take her class, you wont regret it.
Taking this class online sucked. The lectures were long and boring, the material was pretty hard to ynderstand through zoom.

please don't use Chegg in this class or all other classes, I wish someone told me this before I viewed the chegg when a friend ask me to do so during the finals. All the answers for the assignment could be found on the lectures. The prof was very nice and caring when you have questions. And it is not a hard class overall if you watch the lecture.

My lectures were through zoom, but Dr. K is an AMAZING prof and really knows what she's talking about. Lectures are very long, but recordings are available if you need to look back. She takes time to explain things very well and constantly checks to make sure we understand. Homework is graded for participation which was lovely. Quizzes were harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Im not particularly a fan of her lectures. Shell go over a topic really quickly, than will come back later to explain it. It personally made me confused. Theres a lot of homework, but she does offer good extra credit.
Dont miss lectures or fall behind, itll be bad. Overall, wasnt a bad class, but it is a self-taught class, with lots of lecture material and LOTS of reading, but quizzes/GAs are open note/book.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor was really sweet! However, the lecture material did not really match the material that was on the quizzes. Homework was easy as it was for credit, but the Graded Assignments and Quizzes were more difficult. I felt like she didn't really teach much, and I did a lot of self-teaching throughout the semester.

Professor Kijewska's lectures move quick and she was sometimes hard to understand. I liked watching her recorded lectures instead of the live ones. There was about 2 homework assignments/ week, 4 graded assignments, and 3 quizzes including the final. You have to work to understand the material and take good notes because the grading can be tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Switched out of her class after she wrongfully accused me of cheating on an assignment. I talked to her and she refused to look at any proof, wouldnt listen and was simply mean. I switched out of her class and am 4.0 ing the class, take any other prof but her.
Open note tests and quizzes
Her accent was hard to understand at times. Have to attend lectures. Had two quizzes each time, one short answer and the other multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is a queen. Not only is she always is extremely nice and respectful, but also she doesn't give too much homework and makes sure her student get the material through polls.

I truly never thought Id understand chem but this professor made it so clear and easy to understand. I took this course in the summer so it was accelerated, but she made sure that we understood the topic. Quizzes and final are open book/ open note so taking notes during lecture is def what helped me pass.
Amazing prof. Made chemistry easy to understand and made it clear what we needed to know for tests. Very kind and understanding especially during covid times.

I had Dr. Kijewska for CEM 141 in Fall 2020. She was an excellent professor. She explained the material very well and I understood it pretty well, even with her accent. At first, I had trouble with the class because I was a lazy listener during the lectures. But as I adapted to the class, it got better for me. I managed to make it out with a 4.0.

Lectures are kind of boring but have to pay attention and keep up or it gets really confusing. There's assigned readings but I didn't do any, just watched the lectures and got a 3.5 so not too bad. There's 6 MC quizzes and 6 SA quizzes throughout the semester, some of which are pretty tough but you can drop one by doing an EC project.

Lectures were structured well. During the lectures, she would ask questions and would explain why the answer was what it was. The textbook was free and online, so easy to use. Questions asked in test could be directed straight back to material covered in recitation worksheets and the lectures. Definitely attend recitations. They provide extra help.

She's a very sweet and caring professor, I would love to have another class with her! Make sure to complete all hw assignments and go to office hours (very helpful)! Attend the lectures for sure and review learning objectives for quizzes. The extra credit hw's and optional final project boosted my grade a lot at the end.

If you do the homework and watch lectures you will be fine. Attendance isn't recorded and she posts recorded lectures on d2l. There is an optional final project that replaces your lowest quiz score and a few extra credit homework assignments. Do the work and you will be fine!

I was in the hospital on morphine and she wouldn't give me an extension on a quiz that was available for two days. Even if you go to lectures and do the homework, you're not going to be prepared for the tests. Keep in mind I took the class during COVID and I have heard good things about her before. The homework is easy but the tests are super hard.

This class overall was fine. Quizzes are hard even when you pay attention in lectures. Never used the textbook. Professor has an accent, but was very understandable. She is very nice, but doesnt do well explaining material in my opinion because it barely relates to quiz material.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Taken online due to Covid. You have quizzes every few weeks which consists of a short answer portion and a multiple choice. She does have an accent but is easy to understand and follow along with. The final was an optional project which can replace your lowest score. TA's answer a lot of questions and there are lots of office hours for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, she know what she's teaching and how to teach it. Everything she talks about in lecture is on the quiz, so make sure you take notes on what she says aloud and not just the slides. Didn't use textbook much myself. Homework is helpful as well. She keeps students engaged in lecture's which helped me stay focused much of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Go to lecture, download the slides after lecture and watch recorded videos and take notes on what she says (THIS IS KEY). Go to reciation and look at correct answers after in D2L. All the material said and written down help with quizzes. Don't slack on units all of them connect to each other. Great class, very fun to learn. Ask for help!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 1. Lectures are the best material to study. 2. Textbook only supplements lecture material. It wasnt useful to me. But it is free. 3. Take notes. Each unit builds on the next. (Watch out for Unit 4!) 4. Do the HW. Shes really kind. While she may not be able to answer all questions in-depth during class, office hours are always available.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof K is very smart and cares about her students success. Although I wouldn't recommend her to anyone who is an auditory learner. Lots of visual examples in class that didn't help me much and would very quickly explain complex concepts. Her class isn't easy, but college isn't easy. Your grade depends on the exams, be ready to study!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You need to go to lectures to participate in iClicker questions and get credit. The material is presented in a very organized way and if you pay attention in lectures and do the exam reviews, you will do well on exams. Handled the transition to online really well, she wanted everyone to succeed and adjusted properly to do so. Very nice person too!

You can tell she cares about her students and likes to teach the course material. She is very organized and takes her time. She always pauses lecture to ask if there are any questions. The only thing is that you need to go to lecture to get credit for attendance (iclicker questions), but they are beneficial to understanding the material.
I had her for CEM 141. She was great. Homework isn't hard at all, and you don't have to study too much for the tests. Highly reccomend.

I had her for CEM 141 and she was an awesome teacher. I would definitely recommend going to class and paying attention. Homework is basically participation and really quick, and I didn't need to study very much at all. She's very nice and pretty interesting to listen to.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had her for CEM 141 and 142 and absolutely loved her lectures. Her lecture slides are enough to study for the exams. Makes the student's practice problems in the class. I encourage to take part in all the in-class activities. The book is not required. Uses Besocratic which can be frustrating at times but I still think it is worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The class was extremely frustrating. While the professor is clearly smart, I frequently found myself questioning her teaching abilities. Information is constantly thrown so fast at you that it becomes difficult to even remember the overarching topic. Ended up doing well in the class solely through constant hours of studying and a tutor.

This class is one of the worst classes I have taken. Half of the material on the exams was barely even mentioned in lecture. She gave us learning objectives before the exam and a majority of them were never even touched on so I had to teach myself. Do not take this class unless you want to spend 20+ hours studying just to get an average grade.

she may not be the best teacher, but this class is EXTREMELY easy. don't worry about it at all. all you have to do is study learning objectives and the recitation packets before exams and you will get a 4.0.

She is super sweet and an excellent professor. Makes every concept crystal clear, and as long as you pay attention to and study her lecture slides, you will do great on the exams. (Exam 2 was the hardest in my opinion). You also have other grades, which help. Don't skip class; lectures are SO important! Wonderful prof; would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great!

Prof Kijewska is so nice! She does an excellent job explaining the concepts in lecture classes, and does a thorough job. You don't have to attend class (you can skip up to 3 w/out an excuse) but it's not worth skipping. If you come to class, hw, concepts, & everything else will be super easy. would take this prof again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A good teacher. She writes in kind of funny cursive but if you ever ask her a question she will explain the answer clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had a very big class so her style of teaching was only because she had 400 students per lecture, she does a great job and telling you what you need to know, and reviewing key concepts
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You're going to have to study but the book (they give it to you) isn't even worth reading. Lectures won't be super fun but she tells you what you need to know to pass.

She is very smart and very kind. You can tell she just wants the best for her students. If you ask her questions she is always happy to help and is accessible outside lecture. She does have an accent but that shouldn't stop you from taking her class, as she does a very good job explaining difficult concepts. I found 142 to be much easier than 141.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a smart professor and does know what she is talking about, but she just lectures by reading off the slides that she posts after class anyways, but there are clicker questions everyday so you have to go to class and sit through a dry lecture of her lecturing right from slides on the board. Sometimes hard to understand too

I adore Mitch, super nice and funny and made it bearable to come to lecture. The material is hard and moves too quickly, but that's not their fault. Make sure you always do your own homework even in group assignments, because they grade them very harshly. The "practice" assignments are not practice, they're graded like an exam. Overall it was good!

Mitch is great at making lectures engaging and he is INCREDIBLY funny. The course can be pretty difficult but that is of no fault to him, it just has difficult material. He only writes on the board and doesn't use slides so be sure to show up and take notes! The book (which is free and online) is a great reference resource.

Mitch is hilarious, and I really enjoyed his lectures as they were entertaining, but I often didn't take hefty notes on them, as he doesn't use powerpoint slides. The stuff he drew on the whiteboard didn't make a lot of sense to me when I looked over it later, so I'd usually use the book to re-teach myself the content.
He had horrible test questions on every test that all had very similar choices, said he would curve test but never did, and claimed he never said he would curve them. Horrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kleinerman was more interested in being a "friend" versus being a professor. His classes were not well planned and were mainly student lead. Three papers for the course and two still ungraded. Had to push for feedback which is not helpful if you are taking a class to actually learn and grow academically. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND CLASSES WITH HIM

BK is super smart but not in an annoying way. he covers actually important topics that other professors avoid, hes really good at keeping personal bias out of the classroom. Hes also super funny and it makes learning fun and interesting, by far one of my favorite professors!

Kleinerman is ill-informed on almost every topic. There were many instances where someone would ask a question and he would respond, "I really don't know, can anyone else answer that?" He cannot retain control over a class, and has a habit of shutting down discussions before they even begin, which leaves his class feeling awkward and stilted.

Prof Kleiny is my favorite prof of all time. He's quirky and comes off oafish but is extremely smart. He's witty and draws horribly inartistic graphs on the board to help explain his thoughts which makes the class fun. Asking questions always results in interesting and helpful answers. Definitely sets you up to succeed. "Don't sleep on the PDFs"-BK
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: Great professor! I would highly recommend him. The class was so interesting, and he really knows his stuff.
Great prof, lots of fun, although he is a bit quirky (in an endearing way, not an annoying way)
The new BK. He's the man!

Ben was awesome.  I had him for PLS 170 and the class was great, the material was great, and the lectures were even better.  He plays devils advocate on EVERYTHING so you can't take it to heart...  If you didn't enjoy him you probably didn't participate or review the material.
No Comments
does not have good knowledge of PLS, says  Is this clear?  waaaay too many t
incredibly boring, continuous stumbling, not sure what he is talking about.

Had this class as an 8 am but I didn't mind because I enjoyed it so much. I appreciate how she connected with the class and the structure of the course. Class is easy if you put in the effort, and she'll give good feedback to help you get a good grade. I like her quirkiness as well.

Took her for both HST 140 and HST 201 and honestly some of the must fun and interactive classes I've had. 140 was a 8:30 am and I rarely missed a classes because I enjoyed the class. 201 was in a smaller class, and was interactive. the Whole class I feel had fun and Marissa was always helpful on with classwork. Would definitely take a third time

This professor taught the class well and kept helping the entire mass of students until the majority understood the topics. Curves on exams, retakes on in-class quizzes and really funny person.

stories are long and hard to understand. would write 1 1/2 pages per journal, still recieve 0% and asks me to redo everything. stories, quizes, journal due before class (3x week).  3 essays + presenation. will call u out even on zoom. such a harsh grader for a subject that is a uni requirement + not something i will ever go into in the future.

Take this class if you can!!! The professor is so educated in his field and wants to make the lectures engaging and interesting for everyone. Professor Rademaker quickly became one of my favortie professors this semester. He is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about his work and teaching his students. The content is difficult for me to grasp, and the exam questions are sometimes worded weirdly, but if you study well you can pass. There aren't any surprise questions. He's very sweet :)

Kyle is a super nice guy that doesn't give much homework and makes the lectures interesting. He's been one of my favorite professors at MSU.

Dr. Miller was a really nice guy and his lectures were very helpful so I recommend going to class. I really enjoyed Dr. Millers class. This class is extremely hard. I got a 3.5 and this is the only class I didnt get a 4.0 this semester. I genuinely dont think I could have gotten any higher. Dr Miller is overall nice guy who tries to make is lectures enjoyable. Depending on class performance he may also help boost your grade as well(at least when I took him he did). Exams were also worth 80% of our grade.

Dr. Miller is truly an amazing professor. His online course was setup perfectly, and the lectures really prepared you well for the exams. I have a tutor & go to review sessions but exams do not reflect lectures well, hard to do well.

He makes you seem really stupid by saying that every thing is really "simple" or "elementary". He is not very good at answering questions. I spend hours in the library, at the review sessions, and with a private tutor.

dont take dont take dont take. talks about nothing for 75% of the TWO HOUR lab, then gives you 20 minutes to do the assignment you have to finish in class. if you dont finish in class she puts a 0 in the until you turn it in later just to scare you. takes months to grade correctly 4 everything. docks points for nothing on hw (wrong font, typo, etc)

She is very nice and cares, but she talks wayy too much. We almost always had to stay late to finish our labs because she would spend so much time talking so don't schedule a class right after. Overall, she was good, but the only thing I did not like was that she was very nit-picky with assignments.

Hands done one of worst professors I've had at Michigan State so far. She spends almost an hour each class period going over topics that's covered in the prep material. Then she proceeds to spend even more time taking up the class period making the entire class have to finish the in class assignment after the 2 HOUR CLASS is over.

Very easy course, almost an intro to excel and scientific method. Markham is very supportive and will answer any questions and help. Small class size so group projects with table every week with one prep assignment a week too. Very easy course to get college requirements out of the way.

I really loved Mara's class. She made anthropology methods so much more interesting and easy to understand. I learned a lot throughout the semester and actually started enjoying topics I thought would be hard.

Dr. Leichtman has been an amazing mentor. She gives thoughtful and honest feedback that really helps you grow without ever making you feel discouraged. She is incredibly caring, always takes the time to listen, and genuinely wants her students to do well. I have learned so much from her guidance.

Confused by all of these very negative reviews, I found Dr. Leichtman extremely knowledgeable and helpful. I have taken two courses with her now and they have been some of the most helpful courses I have taken. Great feedback on papers, always available to answer questions, I found her courses beneficial.

so cool! if you have any questions in lab she will help lead you on the right path.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson was the best professor to have for LB171! She was always seeking ways to improve and provide her students with the best experience. The exams were a true representation of class material, no curveballs, so that was refreshing. I had a consistent C+ when I took AP Chem, but upon taking this class, I maintained an A the whole semester.

Make sure you understand the concept through the preclass activity before lecture. Her tests are also very fair and we've never seen anything not shown in class. When she grades your exam double check what points you got off  because sometimes her and/or the ULAs accidentally mark you off but she gives you an opportunity to request a regrade!
makes lectures fun and engaging, usually answers questions with another question or tells you to ask groupmates, but other than that is sweet and helpful

The classroom has a flipped learning style, but Dr. K always tries to be available during her many office hour times to help students understand the material. The PCAs are essentially where most of the work happens, so you have to be on top of those to ask meaningful questions during lecture. Her tests are easy and the grading choices are fair.

Dr. Johnson is such an amazing professor, she's great at explaining her lessons during lecture, she is very helpful when going to her office hours, and is very supportive when it comes to trying to learn the material. If you ask her a question during lecture, she may be indirect with an answer, but usually because she wants her students to think.

The class is flipped classroom with the Pre-Class activities being where you'd do most of your learning rather than in lectures. She is really sweet & cares about teaching others, but she always seems to answer questions in a way that does not provide an answer & often messes up her math or explanations, but she usually has the easier exams in 171.
I would recommend her
Best chem professor, great analogies, and very fair

I really wanted to like her but she was so bad at explaining things. Everything I learned I had to teach myself outside of class and with the pre-class assignments. One time in class I asked a question and told her I was confused and she told me that I should be confused and walked away.

Dr. Johnson was a great lab professor and was always guiding us through difficult sections of the lab pretty in-depth. However, the grading was often harsh and the feedback was pretty minimal. If the whole class didnt do well on an assignment, she would allow everyone to re-do it, but the rubrics were still confusing and didnt provide much guidance
I had her for lab, she was very sweet and always willing to answer questions.

Her rubrics are not clear in any way shape or form, and would deduct points based on something that she though you should have included, but wasn't outlined in the rubric. She does give chances to redo assignments, especially if the whole class did poorly though.

The first part of the semester was rough because it was her first time teaching, but she asked for constructive criticism halfway through and really listened to it. The class got much better from there. Pay attention during lectures/recitations, go to the study sessions before exams, and do practice problems. Very group-heavy but she is very fair.

Do not take this professor if you want to learn at all in lecture. Her explanations are confusing and rare. All the learning you will do is on your own. If you ask her a question be prepared to get no answer and a question response

If you did not take AP chem this class will be a struggle for you. Most of the work for this class is done outside of class. I didn't take apchem and I 4.0.

reviews.comment: First year teaching so first month was rocky, however she took peoples feedback and got so much better. Great lectures and were recorded so you can watch them back later. Dr. Johnson was by far the best professor I have had so far. She posts the lecture videos, so lecture isn't mandatory. reviews.comment: This was her first year teaching, and at the start of the semester that was evident. Overall, a very kind, quiet, and apologetic. Always willing to help. I find the other reviews a bit critical given this was her first year teaching. There were mistakes she made along the semester, but she gave us lots of extra credit opportunities to make up for it. Easy to 4.0 and the tests aren't bad, I'm sure she'll be a lot better with time.

Dr Johnson is a very nice person, but her lectures are very confusing, because she has typos in the slides, which often contradict with the material covered. She's really sweet but very confused. It's her first year teaching but she asked for suggestions in the middle of the semester and actually listened and changed. She made many mistakes that confuse the class but she tries.

Dr. Johnson is very kind and always willing to help out. She thoroughly reviews questions and explains things step by step to ensure you comprehend every aspect of the material. I would 100% recommend her to anybody wishing to take chemistry.

reviews.comment: Show up to lecture and secure an A. All exam content is covered through practice problems/mock exams which are just questions derived from previous exams. Easygoing, nice to talk to, and not very difficult at all to pass this class with a 4.0

Dr. Laduca really wants everyone to do well, he is extremely lenient with grading. His exams have questions from the mock exams and practice sets he posts (with answers). Dr. Laduca is very kind and he wants everyone to get a 4.0 so he gives many extra credit opportunities!

Dr. LaDuca is one of the best teachers I've had. He's cares deeply about student success, and I learned an incredible amount of chemistry during his hilarious (and sometimes unhinged) lectures. He gives students the tools needed for success, but beware - you're gonna have to work hard to do really well. Not a cakewalk by any means.

There is a pre class for every class and they are extremely large. The lectures move extremely fast and are too much to comprehend. He contradicts himself every now and then, and his tests are not curved and VERY hard.

LaDuca's lectures were very info-heavy and sometimes he would move through important topics very fast. He did provide extra practice problems if he felt that the class needed it based on in-class iClicker questions. He allows a cheat sheet on exams which was very helpful, and for group exams you can talk with other groups and compare before turn-in

Dr. Laduca is a great professor. He provides lots of practice problems for his exams & posts the answer keys in a timely manner. His exams are difficult but he offers retakes & a 11"x8.5" front-back cheatsheet for each exam. By attending lectures, recitation, asking questions, & completing practice problems, I was able to succeed in the class.

He is a very good teacher that posts a lot of mock exam and exam worthy questions throughout the course. He also likes to crack a few jokes and is always open during office hours if you need any additional help.

He is very caring towards his students and genuinely wants you to succeed. He offers lots of office hours and his exams are very reasonable. He posts mock exams on exam week and they are very similar to the actual exams so as long as you do those, I promise you'll be fine. Expectations are clear, if you do whats expected and go to class you'll 4.0

Dr. LaDuca is a very kind proff. Definitely take him for chem 1 and 2. He prepares you well by incorporating real world situations into his lectures. As long as you go and put in effort you will do well in this class. He always holds office hours and if you ever have any issues just communicate with him.

Ignore all of the bad reviews they are all pure slander and written by lazy people who don't show up to class or don't put in any work to study for the exams. Dr. Laduca is one of the most reasonable and caring professors I have had in my first year at MSU. He regularly hosts office hours, and wants his students to succeed. He is a funny guy too.
Gives female students suspicious deference. Thinks he's the life of the party, not as serious as he should be.

Definitely not the easiest intro to chem class, I knew a lot of people who didn't get the grade they wanted or just didn't pass. Professor LaDuca explains everything that is on each exam in detail and in multiple different ways that makes it easy to understand. He is very accessible outside of class during his office hours or just if you email him.

He cares a lot. If you show up to every lecture you will do well, he does a lot of exam worthy questions in class. He is also extremely funny, easy to pay attention in his class because you do not know what he might say next.

Test are tough, and there is a group section to every exam that is tough if you don't have a good group. He keeps lecture light hearted and the material is learnable if you do the practice problems, which there are a LOT of.

I loved this class, Dr. LaDuca was very funny, incredibly flexible and caring, and also very helpful. 11/10 experience and my favorite quote was “thanks everyone for coming to class today I know it's colder than my ex wife out there” he was so real for that

This class was difficult, and his exams were even harder. They were not like the mock exams or optional problems and the test questions were complicated because you had to figure out what the questions were asking before you figured out the answer to the question. The lectures aren't mandatory, but they are important to understand the concept.

Great professor that makes class entertaining and really makes sure to hammer in the concepts so that the whole class can understand. If not, he recommends several resources from the chemistry department that are available for students. Although attendance is easy to skip, it's imperative to this course in order to really get the material down.

I would take any class he teaches! Amazing professor that goes above and beyond for his students. He always jokes during lectures and plays fail Friday videos to up our spirits. He is a great professor. I highly recommend everyone take him!

The tests for this class were always super hard, but are made by the chem department not him. He tried to make lectures really engaging and funny and really cared about his students. My section did fall behind compared to other sections with the material. Hard class, good professor.
10/10 recommend! He is a great professor who really cares about his students. His exams are very similar to his mock exams and optional practice problems. I would take again he was great.

Hilarious professor and always kept lectures entertaining. Such a nice guy and his tests were very predictable every time, almost the exact same as his mock exams and 'optional' practice problems. Would take this class again if I could. Very understanding and very accessible outside of class for extra help.

Dr. LaDuca is a cool and funny guy. He's great at teaching the material. Although you better be a wiz at chem math because this man loves his chem math. His lecture slides and mock quizzes are almost exactly the same kind of content you will see on the quizzes. Although he seems a bit disorganized, all of the material he provides helps prepare you for the quizzes. Great and funny professor.

He can rush through lectures at times, but he's always willing to clear anything up. STUDY HARD! Chem is tough and short answer Qs on exams suck, so really put the work in if you want an A.

Dr. Laduca is the funniest professor Ive ever had while still being extremely effective at teaching the material. He is so helpful in his office hours, if youre struggling be sure to visit him 1 on 1. His class is quite easy to 4.0 if you study a little bit, Im not sure what others saying hes a tough teacher are talking about.

This is the reason why people say hes difficult and a horrible teacher. You have to take excellent notes. I say notes > mock exams. They are key for a 4.0 in this class.

Overall LaDuca is a nice guy who teaches a hard subject. His class and exams were ridiculously hard, harder than any of the other chemistry profs here and doesnt offer extra credit. Office hours were helpful. I worked really hard though and still 3 pointed (4 pointed all of my other classes). Constant studying for exams. take a different professor.

LaDuca is a Lyman Briggs teacher and this was his first time teaching regular CEM 251. He teaches material fast and doesn't explain things in detail. Prof. Mead was super fun! We took a lot of trips and had classes outside just for the fun of it. Just take her courses, even for fun. Sometimes it can seem like a good amount of work but it is all so worth it and important info that will lead you to finding out more on your own. Her DEI course was great and very informative. LOVE her!!
I loved Prof. Robison! She always let us out early, and the assignments were really interesting! The final is a group project, but it is very easy if you read the rubric.

she is actually the best professor you will ever have in your time at msu. she is quick to get to the point and teaches you well. she doesnt give busy work either. we had one assignment a week and it was pretty simple. easy 4.0 if you at least try.

class can seem intimidating at first but once you get a good understanding of what you are doing its not bad. you do have to get at least 2 textbooks. She is pretty quick at explaining what you are doing. writing assignments are not hard

This has been my favorite class, It is super easy grade, cares more about your learning, uses textbooks (you don't really need to read them, but it is good to have), and gave us a pizza party. Gives more feedback than any other professor. She will read all your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super easy and really nice professor. If you show up, turn your work in on time, say hi to her when you walk through the door its simple A+. Not hard at all if you're a decent student.

Easiest class I've ever taken. Very nice but you truly will learn absolutely nothing. Every assignment was group work and you will get 100 on everything even if you do it wrong. Every class I went to I felt like she was confused as to what she should even be teaching. If you are looking for a class that is a complete joke and an easy A, take this.

Lolo was so much fun and super understanding of your needs. The mid-term was an easy A and so was the class. We were able to swap a final for a group project and that was also easy. All around fun and easy 4.0. Lolo is so sweet and I enjoyed class discussions.
Class is boring and you teach yourself a lot. There is lots of easy group work. The class is a little annoying, but it's easy.

reviews.comment: Super helpful goes through everything in class. Explains concepts well. Im not sure why he is rated so low. I would take this class again with him

Absolutely horrible. Offered no help, was quiet. Anytime I would ask or help his exact words were "just try and keep thinking I can't help you". Genuinely have no idea how he even managed to get the opportunity.
Stay far away.
You have to use two different cameras and your phone and your microphone to show every inch of your room. You still will get confronted and told that you are cheating. It's brutal
Don't bother asking for help. He will just tell u to work harder and that you need to dedicate hours a day including weekends to pass the class

This class is sent from the fiery pits of hell. You are forced to pay for a class that has absolutely zero instruction. You watch pre recorded videos and do countless hours of assignments just for quizzes to ask you to do something you have never practiced. They do not care if you do well and actually prefer if students do poorly.There is zero help

Was a great Professor, only hindered by his students. With a class of over 1200 students on most semesters, his only option is is a flipped lecture model where the student does the majority of the work outside of class and then s reviewed in recitations by TA's. Always very kind and understanding in office hours, where most students didn't go.

this class is horrible. TA's never go over quizzes so if u didn't know what u were doing, u still won't! everyones reviews talking about academic dishonesty and cheating are true. They will accuse u and it is horrible and scary. I hated this class and couldn't wait for it to be over. very tough and the instructors don't care everyone nearly fails.

Accuse you of cheating when they have no proof in class of you doing so. Very strict and will flag your code if it looks somewhat like someone else's. You could get an ADR just by looking around. Would never take this class here again, especially with the way that class is run and it's only taught by TAs and the professor just sits around.

This was such a hard class for being a introductory. If you love yourself, don't take this class. You never see the professor and it's taught by TA's who also don't know what they are doing, it's like they are learning with you. While this class isn't necessarily hard, there is so much work that it makes it near impossible.
Called me the slurs in class
Called me the n word in class
Absolutely the worst professor/class ever. They do not care about you. Accuse you of cheating and treat you terribly

This class was truly the worst part of my entire year. The structure of the class is extremely disorganized. Chances are you'll never meet the professors for actual instruction since they just force teaching assistants to teach the lectures. If you can avoid this class, do it, because it will do wonders for your mental health!
class taught entirely by the ta's you not once see the professor

Not that good of a professor though he is better than the other two CSE instructors, I have never met my professor face to face in person, they let the TA's which are fellow students at MSU teach the course when the professors are much better suited to do so.

if you care about your gpa dont take this class EVER. This class is tought entirely by TA's you will never meet the professors, you will also get accused of cheating very regularly and when you do meet the professors they will treat u like ur worthless!

realistically, this class is a heavy weed-out class for business majors, but genuinely not as bad as I thought. it definitely progresses in difficulty, so if you didnt understand a section, you HAVE to to be able to keep going in the class. you learn quick that you have to make it click yourself, ask A LOT of questions, and stay on top of it.

The professors are overall absent in the class, so you rely really heavily on the TA's. They're helpful. The class is not impossible, but you absolutely have to stay on top of it. missing one lecture sets you back weeks. Gets insanely hard in the last 3 weeks of class. Utilize the lessons, extra practice, and takes notes like your life rides on it.

Professors teach through online videos done outside of the lab, which sucks. They are absent during the lab, so you are relying on the class being run by 2 TAs. The class can be pretty difficult when you are receiving an error but have no clue why it is there. Overall, the class is miserable but required for business students.

This class is TA taught for the labs while the lectures are professor videos from 2-3 years ago. Based on the type of material learned in this class, the professors should be teaching the labs in person while the TA's are there to help. No extra credit either so try and keep up with the labs & quizzes, while also doing well on the exams!

It is comical that TAs run this CSE102 class taken by many first-year business students. While these TA's know how to code they are unequipped to teach students and the professors are unreachable. 
Tyler Lovell seems like a nice guy but he is a terrible teacher and shouldn't work with students even remotely; this course should be completely online.

Take your time and learn the material before moving on to the next section. This class is incredibly difficult but doable. Online or not, you're going to be teaching yourself and I found that this type of class clicks for some people while it is incredibly difficult for others.

Tyler is god awful. This course actually makes me think it was created by the devil. They intentionally make everything way harder for the students. I am a business major yet they want to suck the life out of me in a coding class. The projects and tests are horrendous and they expect so much for a basic intro coding course. Make it make sense.

There are so many students that you will never come in contact with the professors. Taught by TAs. Its a hard class, and they say all the resources are there, but its just an uninviting environment and there always seems to be an issue. This class tested my limits for sure (as it does for a lot of students). Just be prepared.

reviews.comment: CSE 102 is one of the absolute worst classes I have taken. The class is run by TAs, and trying to go to the professor's office hours accomplishes nothing. The exams/quizzes are tough and although they post practice quizzes, THEY ARE ONLY POSTED AFTER THE QUIZZES ARE DUE. Sometimes I question why Tyler is on the MSU payroll.

Ran CSE 102 class very poorly. Class is practically self taught and is one of the hardest courses at MSU. Implemented new programs and grading from last year and as a result the entire course was a complete disaster. I do not recommend taking this course at all unless you have to which most unfortunately do. Professors do better

Prof Lovell's class was the hardest one. I didn't meet the prof, since TAs run this class. Some TAs might be helpful, but only if you're lucky enough. The codes in the videos didn't match what we needed for quizzes, exams, homework, and projects. This class messed up my gpa and might affect getting into the business college.

Never once did I even meet the professor, very unengaged, and seemed like he could care less about CSE 102 as a whole. The class is taught by TAs who don't know what they are doing and won't help. Very exam heavy and the exams are worth 60% of your grade. Also quizzes every 3rd class period. Poorly organized class with a professor who doesn't care.

This class is really hard, but if you keep up with the weekly homework then you should be fine. You will never see the professors, and all of the sections are run by ta's. There are quizzes which are not bad if you've done the homework. Exams are tougher. The projects are the hardest part, but they are only worth 6% of your grade.

The professors are not even there, it depends on how good the ta's are to get help. This class is the absolute worst make sure to take time to pay attention to the labs and videos. Way too much homework and the exams are difficult.

I took cse102 with him and 2 other profs and you do not see them during class at all except for recorded lectures you have to watch outside of class. The first third of the class is pretty easy but after that good luck and I hope you get a TA that gives you help instead saying figure it out yourself. You'll be in the cse helprooms daily in cse102.

reviews.comment: Prof did not teach a well-rounded class. Did not match up with expectations from course description. This is a subpar sociology class.

The class is lecture-heavy, but there isn't much homework. There are quizzes every week and about 11 exams. You do get to drop 3 quizzes and 3 exams. There is also a large research project that takes about the whole semester to do. But it is easy and fun. The professor is fun and has a lot of knowledge on the subject.

reviews.comment: Easy class, no homework just weekly quizzes.
Dr. Thompson is sweet, and her lectures are inspiring and straightforward. Attendence was not mandatory. The exams were harder than I expected, but she allows multiple drops.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: a really great prof! A lot of drops which is really nice, but if you don't want to go to class I would get the book or vise versa. However I will say it is so lecture heavy and I did have to fight my sleep demons more times then I would like LOL. I do wish there were more discussions and more diverse voices and opinions were heard.

The class wasn't hard and the workload is reasonable but it's extremely biased and one sided. Almost everything is taught through a single political lens, and the course often pushes specific societal and feminist solutions without leaving room for other perspectives. It also rarely covers actual women's psychology like biology and cognition.

Dr. Thompson is fantastic, she is so kind, knowledgable and accessible outside of class. You do not necessarily need to go to class, but it certainly helps! If you ever want to talk about something you found interesting pertaining to her course, she is more than willing to chat about it with you because she is so passionate. I would take her again!
Attendence is not mandatory. She does include items from the textbook in her mini exams. Overall, an easy class if you show up.

Ms. Thompson's class was very lecture-heavy. I often felt bored and overwhelmed trying to copy each slide before she moved on. The nearly two-hour lectures were tiring, and the exams every two to three weeks were all memorization-based. The homework was simple—two short quizzes and an assignment every week.

Amazing professor, really cares about the subject and is super easy to talk to about anything. Tons of drops for homework, attendance, and exams. Lectures can be long but making it through them is the only hard part of class.

Dr. Thompson was nice and had interesting stories sometimes but her whole lecture was reading directly off of slides. If you are able to read through textbooks and make quizlets to learn rather than note taking I would recommend this class but it was not enjoyable and I was often stressed about writing everything down as she clicked through slides.

Engaging professor who cares about her students. The lectures are long, but she explains the content clearly and makes it easy to remember. Take good notes and study the homework questions and you'll do well.

It's not hard to pass PSY 101 but it is a hassle to try and get a great grade. She's pretty whimsy and her lectures can be boring if you don't like the content but she knows what she's teaching. Theres attendance interactives locked via password gotten through lecture. About 3 assignments a week pre+post test and then hw and decent deadlines

Lectures are long & attendance does matter, however, the class is very manageable as long as you do not slack off. Not much extra credit. Exams are SO straight-forward and not tricky as she provides study guides. Just memorize key terms and vocabulary and you can easily get 80% on the exams. Lots of homework and quizzes that can EASILY be redone.

Dr. Thompson is a very nice lady that is passionate about her teachings. However, the class is long and boring and hard to engage in. There are a lot of assignments, but they aren't hard. Exams are ok, study and you'll be fine. It is nice before every exam you have the class before off.

I'd say the only bad things about the class were the super long lectures and the study guides. The study guides were just an overview of the notes and were not very helpful. She also curves the tests which is nice, and if you do well you don't have to take the final. Overall, very nice and passionate prof, long and boring class.

She's a very nice Professor and knows what she's talking about. But the way the exams are is too much, there are 4 exams. Not spaced out well, with material not in the study guides she provided. Lots of homework too. You have to come to class and sit there a full 2 hours to receive participation credit.

Thompson is an good prof, not a great one. It is a very lecture heavy class and the lectures are long. She sometimes goes on tangents that will just never help you on any assignment you do for this course. It is somewhat hard to pay attention. With that said, it wasn't like she was a bad prof. She cares about the students and is passionate.

Has very long and boring lectures that take up the whole class period. Get a buddy for the attendance code and you get credit. Grades are off of a point scale so it is easy to get a 4.0. Only need to average a 78% on all of your tests if you do all the other assignments. Ignore the lectures and study the textbook which doesn't take too long to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Thompson is very passionate about her job and it shows. She works hard to make sure everyone understands the subject. The three lowest exams are dropped which helps a lot with grades. Overall the course is interesting.
She's British so if you want to hear that for hours then don't take her.

Good teacher and makes content digestible for students. Clear guidance for students despite the semi-heavy work load. AMAZING grading, very very lenient with drops and will benefit you if you do the work during the Finals Weeks

Prof is nice and knows class content. Really the only issue I had with the layout of this class was the mini exams. The study guides for each were about as long as a regular exam study guide which means there were weeks where it felt like you were prepping for 4 exams in just her class.The questions were often things not on the study guide too.

This was one of my favorite classes this semester. Although attendance was not required, I showed up every single day, as Dr. Thompson was so passionate about what she was teaching. I highly recommend her, as well as this course! I hope I will be able to take another course with her. She was very kind, knowledgable, and understanding. very easy/fun

Dr. Thompson is a great teacher. She gives very interesting lectures. She also has a lot of built in drops for quizzes, exams, discussion posts, and even for the final. I would highly recommend taking her PSY 339 class!

This course offered SONA research experiences for extra credit, along with tests and an optional final, enhancing its flexibility. It included online lectures, Packbacks, and mini quizzes with unlimited attempts, creating a relaxed learning environment. Minimal study was required, making it a fun and interesting class overall.

I loved this course! Extremely easy to understand and genuinely engaging. Exams and assignments make sense even if you don't attend every lecture. Dr. Thompson clearly cares about this field and is very flexible and willing to work with students for deadlines and the like, definitely recommend.

She was very passionate about the subject and I feel like I left the class with a lot more knowledge of the world. She's very caring and interacts with all of her students. She does these things called "mini exams" which are supposed to help with testing anxiety but were overall more inconvenient. Overall I would recommend taking a class with her.
Love love love this professor. Her class is super easy and she is very understanding. By far the best professor at MSU.

I took PSY 101 with her online. The class was very easy to understand and learn about. We had a quiz and one pack back questions due every week. It was one of the stressful least classes I had to worry about over the semester. The one thing I will is that this class has you taking a lot of notes and reading a lot. The textbook was found online.

reviews.comment: Enjoyable class and interesting material. Very easy to do well in this class. I had this class fully online so it was super spread out throughout the week and paced very nicely.
Amazing professor! Took this class online, it was organized great, clear directions for the class. Digestible and helpful class assignments. Do the work and get an A.
Easiest class I have every took. Lectures were actually enjoyable and so many free points were given just for trying in the class. Dr. Thompson is also very sweet.

I took this class asynchronous and it was good overall. There were many lectures to watch each week and you had notes as well. The discussion posts on packback were easy and as long as you pay attention to the lectures, you will do well on the tests.
Took this asynchronous, if you do whats assigned its an easy A. She does a lot of discussion boards to get the class talking, makes the class more fun. Fun and interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took psych this semester and I really enjoyed it. In part because of the professor. Dr. Thompson was an amazing professor who cares about her students. The class is really lecture heavy but it isnt necessarily hard material. We do weekly Packbacks which are easy to get an A on. Overall, great professor and its a easy A if you do the work.

For the most part, if you participate in this class, you're going to get an A. Unlimited attempts on all quizzes, and she drops one of each different type of assignment. I never needed my textbook, though it's a free pdf, and I hardly needed to study either.

I enjoyed his recitations a lot. He has a ton of math knowledge and he is super helpful when you don't understand a concept. He can come off a little frantic when he enters class or gives explainations. But he is super helpful if you just ask.

Lucas Hall was a nice professor, however he was incredibly disorganized. It was his first time teaching the course. His explanations of simple material were abstract and when asked to clarify he wouldn't know how to answer. If you take him, expect to spend a lot of time on YouTube and reading in the textbook as you'll have to mostly teach yourself.

reviews.comment: Very nice! I believe it was his first time running the course, so it was a bit difficult at first. He is very smart, but sometimes hard to understand. All of that aside, he truly has his students in his best interest!
If you ask him a question, he will riddle the answer and make everything unclear. This was my hardest class at MSU so far, and I do not recommend taking this course.

Dr. Lucas is extremely knowledgeable and clearly cares about supporting his students and their learning. He prioritizes methodology and the analytical process in his teaching, in addition to subject matter. The low reviews are just because of his tough grading, but if you are able to write coherently and support an argument you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Does not accept late work under any circumstances even if they're valid. Teaches humanities but is so far into academia that he's lost touch of real life situations.

Professor Lucas is a cool guy, funny (if you like dad jokes). I didn't actually have him for 202, but he was my recitation professor for 201. The average recitation was him briefly mentioning the lecture and/or readings from the previous day, and putting us in small groups to write any questions on the board. Never answered them fully, little lazy.
Does not care about students and will not take the initiative.

His class was a struggle for me. He sets it up where the majority is on questions about the corresponding lecture, which sounds helpful, but he is really terrible at answering questions and ends up making things more confusing. He also refuses to answer some questions if they aren't 'big picture' enough.

This class was geared towards international relations majors, so if you aren't one I would steer clear. Professor Lucas's lectures hardly touched on the lengthy readings and were difficult to understand. The amount of readings, essays, and presentations were insane, even for JMC. Overall, I didn't feel like I learned much for the work I put in.
Professor Lucas allows for most classes to only be about questions on the material presented in the lecture and it is hard to get your questions effectively answered.

Long useless lectures that don't help with class or understanding of materials. You ask him a question and he responds, with a question. Doesn't give useful feedback that actually helps with papers. You need to go to office hours to get a good grade. Went twice and that still wasn't enough. Boring class and caused lots of stress.

Lucas lectures for hours and expects you to understand it all in a second. Don't bother asking questions because when you do, he talks down to you and never gives you an answer. He doesn't return feedback on time to improve your next assignment.

I found his way of lecturing to be very confusing and unclear but that's okay because he's usually not the one lecturing. It's pretty much impossible to 4.0 this class. And although you should go to class to get information for your essays you could fake it without going. Go at the end in case he does a take home final like he did for us.

Knows his stuff & doesn't give ANY exams, so that's good. Instead, you do online quizzes and write essays which he grades in an unclear way that makes it impossible to 4.0 them. Even though attendance is mandatory, going to class is POINTLESS because you write the essays off of different novels/movies instead of the textbook that he lectures about.

Dr. B does not know how to run a class. She's unorganized, and soft spoken with lectures that contain redundant information. You can gain more from just reading the textbook than attending lecture. The exam questions are poorly written and draw straight from the textbook with hyper-specific questions on case studies that aren't covered in class

The class was difficult with many exam questions being trick questions or questions about case studies from the textbook, never mentioned in class. Poor planning, an exam had to be cancelled because she didn't print enough exams. The lectures didn't complement the homework reading and you basically had to memorize both to get good grades.

Course was all Connect assignments, and the lectures felt long as she repeated the homework word for word. Exam based. Hard to memorize for, as the written questions required multiple case studies related to the question. Exam schedule was lined up badly, with the last units exam a week before the cumulative final exam.

She was a very caring professor who clearly enjoyed teaching ecology. She was very caring and helpful. This was however her first semester teaching so some there was inconsistencies here and there, but she always accommodated the best she could. Test heavy class, and tests were fairly tricky. Still highly recommend taking her class.

Dr. Wassink is not everyone's cup of tea, but I thought she was great. She is very easy to talk to and will joke around or just chat with students. Very calming presence. She wants you to do well but the first test will be extremely difficult and she can be a tough grader at times. She seems to prefer lab over lecture greatly, lecture can be boring

reviews.comment: Dr. Wassink is one of the best teachers I've had in college, which is saying something because I had her last year on Zoom when everything was shut down because of COVID. You can tell that she genuinely cares about her students. Class is a lot of work, but she makes it enjoyable. 10/10 would recommend.
Dr Wassink was a new professor, but you could tell she cared about helping her students learn the material. It's a harder class, but certainly doable and I would definitely recommend her!

The in class activities are super vague and are not at all like the 120pt exams. The homework is taking notes on prerecorded lectures and she grades them on how well you engagement is. Exams are graded terribly, barely any partial credit for 15-30 point questions, usually all or none. Would not recommend her to anyone.

LB144 is a lot of work, Dr. Wassink gives you what you need to be successful. You have take very good notes as they are graded on quality. Exams are 120 pts and are pretty challenging (do well on these they make or brake your grade). Her in-class activities are just like the exams, so that is a big help.

Professor Wassink was new this year but she did super well. Her preclass lectures were easy to follow and the in class work really helped later since most of her exam questions were similarly set up. The notes on the lectures took a while but the effort is worth it because they will help so much when studying for exams. Prelabs were also helpful.

reviews.comment: I had an average master score in her class. I take organic chemistry currently and I have a 4.0 currently. She isn't great at building relationships with her students. A lot of people say she's not a good explainer but that is absolutely wrong, she lacks passion in her explanations. an unpassionate professor results in students not learning.

I wish she would explain her lectures better. Extremely tough grader, you could be right on an answer and she'll still find a reason to get you partial credit. reviews.comment: there's plenty of opportunities for extra-help. Sometimes she moves a little too fast but she takes questions and clarifies if you ask. Assignments correlate to the lectures and she's not a super tough grader.

reviews.comment: She is a good teacher, sometimes she explains things in difficult scientific vocabulary but she will do everything she can to help and she is nice.

reviews.comment: Very nice and always willing to help explain to better your understanding. She cares about her students and wants them to learn rather than pass the class. Tough class but if you put in the work you'll do fine.

reviews.comment: Posey is not good at explaining things and does not have control of her classes. I do not recommend taking her class at all.

I took her class as a grad student and really liked it.  Unfortunately, the undergrads all wanted her to bend over backwards and give study guides and extra credit.  They also tried to leave early every day.  If you're a grad student, you will enjoy  her class.  Well organized and she's very knowledgeable.

Very monotonous and indifferent professor. The ways she explains things are either confusing or lack enough detail for the lessons to make sense. Go to an earlier lecture with a better professor if you can. Stay away from this one.

Utter filler, everything she says is nothing and half of the time it seems as if she is purposely trying to throw you off.  I also think she sabotages her PowerPoints so you have to come to class to get the revised copy, way too many convenient corrections that are critical to understanding things.
She talks like a book! Very hard to understand. Though she doesn't mind giving extra help, she is even harder to understand one on one. Notes don't make sense.

She could give a****.. IF you can't do the work, handle the class.  your assed out.. get out of her class!  Prey for someone else to teach it.. if someone esle is teaching.. take early, take it on a weekend.. do what ever you can!
Very hard to follow, she used words that were way beyond our understanding.  She's a very nice person, just a hard to understand prof.
No Comments
The hottest prof I have ever had!!! She is very good looking!!! Bad teacher though!!! I will say I would date her if I was in my 60s. Lynmarie is a niceperson, horrible prof.
the class was really hard, but the prof wasnt bad.  the TA's were better than any professor ive ever had. dont bother buying a book, it has nothing to do with the lecture

Hypnotizing.  I got veeery sleeeeeeepy.  She doesn't have an accent, but don't let that fool you.  It doesn't mean what she says will make sense.  To sum it up, chemistry with Posey is unfun.  And honors is a, um, witch.

Posey speaks nervously, stuttering and adding many ums.  She also likes to use terms that are beyond our level of study.  The labs were out of sync with the lectures, which added to the difficulties of explaining what we observed.  Depend on the book.

My all time greatest professor I had in college.  Of course he was tough on students/grading - but that's what you need!  A good challenge with someone who knows what he is talking about AND is a Dead Head!
great prof, hard and 4 times the work of any other prof in the class
Great professor, always makes class interesting.  This class requires quite a bit of time.
B.A.

Lectures are 4 days a week and every time you go sit in lecture; he just reads off the slides which you will already have yourself. I found that my time was better spent in the help room with the TAs instead of going to lecture, because all of his examples and slides are right from the book, and you will already have it.
