reviews.comment: He seems like a really fun guy but does not explain physics that great. The quizes seem fair if you do the homework and extra problems. There is extra credit but there is a cap. I highly recommend talking with classmates and help each other with the homework. Read the slides on your own and watch youtube videos you should do okay.
Horrible professor. wouldn't recommend to anyone, take the other professors class if possible
He's a great professor! While physics is difficult, you'll do fine in this class if you really pay attention and take iclickers seriously.

He's a nice guy, but all over the place. Lectures are mandatory with iClicker questions but the lectures itself are so vague and he rushes through the slides without explaining anything. When you get the clicker questions wrong, he doesn't explain the concepts and just kind of moves on. Would not recommend physics with Lynch!

Professor Lynch gives rambling, confused lectures that are not conducive to learning. Also, during lecture, he will often have WRONG ANSWERS displayed for the Iclicker questions. This class is really not that difficult, but there is a ton of homework and you will be learning all the content through doing it, not from Professor Lynch.

Although I have never talked to Prof. Lynch one-on-one I can tell he wants his students to be successful in this class; however, classes are terrible and can be very confusing to follow. Often he starts and ends clicker questions which results in you missing points, and he overall brushes over material too quickly. I recommend choosing a diff. prof

I created this account just for this course. Professor Lynch's class is the most frustrating thing I've ever experienced. He reads off his slides and it's impossible to take notes, some of the webwork answers are blatantly wrong and you can't do anything about it, and he is a very snooty old man that get's frustrated with his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible. Don't take PHY183 with Lynch. Trust me.

William Lynch... where do I start... he is the ABSOLUTE worst! He doesn't know what he is doing half of the time, he doesn't know how to teach and his iClicker questions are often wrong during lectures. He also often put the wrong grades in the gradebook. Please do not take PHY183 with this professor. Btw he has a fanny pack.

PHY 183, Lynch has very bad handwriting and takes a lot of time to think about what he's going to say, but he is a great person and extremely entertaining. His class became a lot more enjoyable when speaking to Lynch outside of class. His lectures are a little fast, but he loves questions.

Not 184, but 183. Reads off of slides. Makes it impossible to take notes or do anything in his class. As someone who has never taken a physics class, this was awful. Some people who have taken a physics class before or is good at physics will probably do good in his class. Final exam was nothing like the practice exam.

I think Bill is over-hated, and I understand why some people dislike him so much but for me I never really found him to be problematic. He offers online midterm exams to get extra points that you miss on the in-person midterms following the latter's completion. He doesn't make the class a cakewalk, but never makes it impossible to succeed.

I thought he was alright at the beginning, and honestly, a little funny sometimes. Now I just don't like him. He never sounds like he knows what he is talking about, and takes forever to explain anything.

Last midterm, I had a page of notes and was prepared pretty well for it. There ended up being questions I had NEVER seen before on it. Not good.

Has a fanny pack and some big foam hands. The course material is tough so pay attention in the lectures, a Chegg account definitely helps and a lot of the equations for homework and the tests are in the D2L slides.
Very rude/condescending when students get clicker questions wrong. If you have the option to not take his sections, don't. Worst class I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not good with communication, dont expect him to email back unless its a real emergency
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor reads off lecture slides the entire time with minimal explanations. 

Move very fast through material.

Condescending when the material is misunderstood.

Has fanny pack.

Terrible teacher. If you have to take him, sign up for a chegg account. Does not explain well and expects you to know what he's talking about before being taught. If you ask questions he'll tell you indirectly that your question was dumb or had and obvious answer. Goodluck...

If you want an absolutely terrible experience in physics this is the prof you want. He doesn't teach the material he just expects you to know it. You can't meet him outside of class and is very difficult to reason with. He will not be friendly or easy when something has come up if your life. He still uses LON CAPA which is old and annoying.

If you like professors who have the hardest homework imaginable, is hard to meet outside of class, is really bad at teaching, has the worst handwriting ever, and often forgets what he's doing, then this is the professor for you! He also uses LON CAPA and frequently posts slides that are wrong (don't match his lecture) or incomplete.
This professor goes by lectures fast, dont understand the way he explains material. Only went to class for iclicker points
Better to wait a semester and take another prof.
Horrible.

This guy has no clue how to teach this course. For your own sanity avoid this professor because it is a huge waste of time. I study for hours on end and no matter what I do it doesn't help for the homework OR the tests. Avoid this at all costs.

I loved this professor, he explained things in a way that was easy to understand. It's a hard class but as long as you take notes and actually study you'll be fine. He gives a TON of extra credit so I never really felt like I was going to get anything under a 4.0 in the class.

Overall a good guy and professor, bad course structure. Expect to study more than your friends with other orgo 2 professors. Stay on top of things from day one because grades come mainly from in-person quizzes and exams. Get help early if needed. No major extra credit or cheat sheets like other professors, so it's easy to fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is not a professor, he is a chem lover who cannot teach. If you love chemistry you will get along with him, but if you don't want to study it every single day then be prepared to fail. I have not taken a class from a worse professor. He would drone on and on about topics that he liked, but then put completely different ones on the exam

I don't believe there is a worse chem class than this one. He was frequently going on tangents that don't matter, while barely covering the material we are tested on. Each exam the average was failing. He didn't seem to care about the students learning, instead just  stroking his ego with how well he knows chemistry. You're the professor, teach us.

Great professor and clearly knowledgeable on organic chemistry. It's a hard class, but if you put in the work you'll do fine. All the people saying that the lectures were bad either don't know how to take notes, or they didn't actually attend them.

Professor Maleczka is one of the best professors ive had here at MSU so far. CEM252 is a tough class and you need to be ready to put in the work. His lectures are very in depth and he has very good explanations. It's clear he actually knows what he is talking about, and it shows in his lectures. Overall a great professor and I enjoyed the class.

I thought he was an engaging professor, even if some material covered felt longer than necessary. Lots of bonus points and he adjusts grades after each exam so I found it very easy to get a high grade. He was also very helpful at office hours and adjusted homework assignments to give more attempts than originally allowed.

Terrible professor, the only reason people pass his class is due to dropping the required points. If he was a good professor that would not be needed. Every lecture drags with material that isn't needed, and the quizzes are based off of material barely covered. Worst Chem professor at MSU in my opinion.

When I asked for supplemental materials to try to understand the concepts better in class he told me to google reactions. He isn't a good educator and spends his time drawing on the board instead of giving proper lectures, which left us way behind at the end of the semester having to do a month of materials in a week.
Poor lecturer, spends too much time on chalkboard instead of giving meaningful lectures, weeks behind in the last month of classes.

I didn't align with this prof at all and have to retake this course. The structure of this class sucks with quizzes every week that doesn't align with the homework, I've attended office hours with the only ULA that fit my schedule and felt like I was being looked down on the entire time. Orgo is difficult as it is but this prof made it 5x harder

Dr. Maleczka is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. He is an extremely down to Earth dude and clearly cares very deeply about what he teaches. His enthusiasm and openness to questions creates an amazing environment that has inspired me to attend every lecture he gave. 100/10 professor.

The set up of this class was awful, with the average student failing the exams. Posts lecture slides but instead writes on chalkboard all lecture. Exams and quizzes have unfair questions that are too specific, and homework assignments have little correlation with what is spoken in class. This class is not taught well under him, and we're suffering.

Dr. Shen went on maternity leave so Dr. Maleczka stepped in for the semester. He gave very clear explanations and helped us remember things (like repeated themes in reactions). He didn't design the course (Dr. Shen did) so can't rate on anything other than his lecturing, which I found very useful and clear. He was patient and good with questions.
Dr. Mac is super nice and very chill! The class content is a little hard and there's a lot to take in regarding both the lecture and the lab. Study hard and you'll for sure do well in her class.

dr. mac is AWESOME! ibio328 is SO HARD (especially the lab, lots of memorizing and difficult dissections) but i learned so much incredible knowledge that i WILL utilize in my future as a zoo major. love her teaching style in lecture, lots of great notes and slides!

She's really nice, and very helpful. If you are interested in Zoology or FW however, I wouldn't recommend IBIO200/Animal Biodiversity unless you are looking for a class that will tell you more about your future education. 60% of what we did in class had nothing to do with learning about Animal Biodiversity.

The professor was nice, but the class itself was terrible. I don't understand why the lab is a requirement on top of the lecture. The lab is stupid and so much memorizing of terms for the exams. Avoid taking this class, but sadly for me it was a requirement which was also a joke because never in my career will I utilize anything I learned.
Dr Mac is fantastic. She is understanding and caring. As long as you participate and turn in your assignments, the class is a breeze.

I just want to make it clear that IBIO365 is not intended to be an easy class. You will have to do a lot of studying and majority of it is memorization. But there are a lot of resources to study from. Teresa is an excellent professor and cares for her students. I had a great time in this class and I got a lot from it.

Genetics was a horrible experience. She never responded to my emails and she didn't even teach her own material, in fact, she didn't teach at all. I also want to say the reason I'm submitting this review now is because the one I submitted prior was deleted. Looks like all her bad reviews were, go figure. Take with another professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's by far one of the best professors I've had. Makes helpful commentary as opposed to reading off the slides.  Lab is difficult, but there are plenty of ways to do well, you just have to take the time to study and memorize. Do not procrastinate if you want to succeed. Prof McElhinny creates a welcoming environment for students & is approachable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I have ever taken. It is only grades on quizzes and exams. It is such a difficult course because there is a lot to it, such as memorization. They expect way too much from you, and expect you to be very knowledgable regarding anatomy. You have to dissect a lamprey, shark, bullfrog, and a CAT. It is horrible and miserable

Professor McElhinny gives great study guides with exactly what you need to know for the exam on them. The lab is a lot of memorization, but you can get a lot of extra credit here which is really important in the end. She records lectures and posts them on D2L and attendance is not required for lecture. It does take a bit for them to grade stuff tho
Really sweet lady but the class itself is very difficult. The lab is really cool but also very difficult.

Dr. Mac was wonderful! She was clear about what we had to do and was always there for assistance. Her class wan't overbearing or over-explained. It was very interesting material and I am sad the class is over. It was a lot of group work, but it wasn't bad at all. My group was great.

Dr. Mac is an excellent instructor. Her class is fairly easy, but also pretty interesting. She genuinely cares about student success and is actually passionate about what she teaches, which makes it more engaging to learn.
Dr. Mac is awesome!! This class is very easy and does not have very many assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mac is a very knowledgeable, respectable professor. I absolutely loved taking IBIO 200 with her and hope to have her as a professor again in the future.

Dr. Mcelhinny is one of the most caring professors at MSU. Not only are her lectures super helpful, but she genuinely cares about her students and makes sure they are successful. I recommend her for genetics!

I would 100% recommend anyone to take Dr. McElhinny for genetics. She is very understanding and TRULY cares about how her students do in the class. She is accessible outside of class and always stays after class to answer peoples questions. Genetics as a subject was difficult for me, but she made me want to come to lectures due to her positivity.
I loved this class and her teaching style. You do have to be prepared before lecture though, as her lectures are more discussion based. Not much homework and pretty much everything is group based.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Her lectures are thorough and she makes she people are engaged by having them chime in through the chat to answer questions or ask questions. Shes spends a solid amount of time on each slide and makes sure everyone understands the content before moving on

You don't have to read the book before class but it does help. Her lectures are very thorough and though she may seem direct, she's very knowledgeable and helpful. She specializes in teaching and it shows. Recitations are helpful, do the homework, go to class, and do lots of practice.

Took this class online after the pandemic. Instructors were uncommunicative, unhelpful, and even used YouTube videos as supplemental lectures. Exams were much harder than any homework given and there were no curves, unproductive office hours, and the instructors would often miss individuals appointments made with students. AVOID!!!

Really great teacher. Know basic bio concepts and she will help you learn the rest. Go to recitation (and lecture for clicker points). She can be direct but is always very willing to help. Do all the assignments and go to class and it should be ok.

The biggest turn-off about this class is the workload. Sapling homework, class prep assignments, and recitation pre-class problems. Yes, that's 3 different homework assignments (per week, sometimes). And, clicker questions throughout every lecture. Also, the exams are hard. Dr. Mac's teaching was fine, but the workload was just too dang high.
Mr. Mac made my life so much better after BS 161. I thought everything was going to be awful after I had Dr. Koslowsky for 161, but Dr. Mac and Dr. Roberts were fantastic

Homework due online 3 times a week (some have 50+ questions). She expects you to have the entire chapter read before lecture, you have a clicker quiz on it at the start of class, and then questions throughout the lecture so it's not like you can just leave after the quiz. Her lectures are so hard to pay attention to. Would not recommend at all.

Lots of clicker questions each class. BS 161/171 are the best classes to prepare you for this class. Printing key figures for lecture is helpful but not necessary. Always go to recitation. Give yourself PLENTY of study time before exams (i.e. days in advance). Exams are LONG and you MUST give yourself time to do the short answer ones.

It's pretty sad that her GTA at the time was a better professor than her. You have a quiz at the beginning of every lecture and probably at least 15 clicker questions for participation points during the lecture so she ends up rushing through the lecture. None of the lectures are online and the tests are way harder than what you actually learn.
bad teaching, doesn't make sense, none of the lectures are cohesive, theyre all from 2018. mind you thats 8 years ago. you can tell she cares only about grades and not actually teaching you anything

lecture vids are from 2018 and 2020. homework's are confusing, not cohesive, long. has numerous assignments due on Fridays which are also exam days. lecture content simply doesn't make sense. no flow to lectures whatsoever. chatGPT and youtube have been teaching me everything. also assigned homework and lecture videos during spring break.

Dr.Mcguire is an amazing professor. Her understanding and respect for students is rare and admirable. Yes, the material is difficult, but like the mammal biology course, its memorization. DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS!! I cant stress that enough because they are eerily similar to the exams. Study hard in lab and seek help if needed, she's great!

This class is a lot of content but it is so doable. Do each of the Problem Sets a couple times before you take the exam and you won't struggle. Dr. McGuire is incredibly thoughtful, just be honest with her and she will listen. Very accommodating and kind. Go get help in between quiz attempts!

reviews.comment: the class content is kinda hard — you just watch a lot of online lectures, first exam is pretty much all review. the exams get cheat sheets so not bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. McGuire is very nice and pretty helpful throughout the course, although lectures and modules are very confusing and did not seem to connect together. Exams are pretty difficult even with a cheat sheet and you really need to study and do the problem sets/ hw. Recitations are helpful for getting the problem set done but not much else.

A very kind professor. The class is inherently difficult, but she was very helpful, especially during review sessions. I do wish the rules of the lac operon stuff had been explained better, but that was my only gripe. If you put in the effort, you will 4.0.

Dr. McGuire is super passionate about her field and about sharing experience with students. She's always willing to meet with you or have discussions in class. The class is difficult and a lot of memorization, but she tries to make it straightforward and curve grades when needed. Fascinating material presented by an excited lecturer!

Super kind and amazing! Dr. McGuire is very clearly passionate about reptiles/amphibians and it shows. The lab is a lot of memorizing, but she gives you a word bank for exams. All the lectures are interesting and she makes the class exciting. All lectures are recorded and posted after. She's also super understanding and will accommodate your needs.
Does not care about her students. Don't take online if possible, might have a better chance of her actually responding if she's in person.

reviews.comment: I would just like to say if you are taking IBIO 341 online, get close with your TA. She does not answer emails at all and claims to be available to students. The class is also very test heavy, 70% of your grade. The exams are also on lockdown browser. If you find it hard to learn online in the first place taking this class is not the right option.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So much material to know for only two exams -sometimes felt impossible even when attending and paying attention in class everyday

I took the class mainly online. The class is difficult, but mostly because of how much material there is. Both the teacher and TAs regularly made themselves available for questions. This one just requires some tough work.

I found her lectures so unhelpful that I mainly learned everything from her recorded live sessions. Not writing on the slides in her lectures with so much math/punnet squares/etc was difficult to learn from. First two units were easy but unit 3 was randomly much harder imo. Exams make up 70% of your grade and are lockdown but you get note sheets.

Let me start with how knowledgeable she is in her field. She obviously cares a lot about the topic but does lack when it comes to the students. The grade is determined by 4 exams (70% of your grade), the exams are not open note and lockdown browser. I felt like the practice exams were not adequate study material for content actually on the exam.

I loved Dr. McGuire! She was such a sweet teacher and has so much passion for what she talks about. She is fairly straightforward, and there weren't any curveballs for exams. As long as you study you will be all set and she gives you the option to write a cheat sheet before exams. If you are at all interested in the environment, take her class!
Shes a great prof and its a very easy class. I never went to any classes and did well on exams.

Let me start with something positive, very kind and cares about her students. My issue with her is the complete lack of organization and misinformation in her lectures. She often tries to dumb down concepts that are simple and fails to explain them correctly. Please avoid her, class is passable but made me confused about the easiest of concepts.

Dr McGuire is one of my favorite professors here at Michigan State. I am currently enrolled in her IBIO 341 course and her lectures are amazing. She holds weekly office hours that are super helpful and she explains everything so clearly. She makes genetics SO much better.

Dr. Mcguire is caring and lenient. The lectures were quite long, but she offered recordings so you can watch them sped up later. There were group assignments every week, which really helped with active learning and problem-solving. She made great efforts to provide choices for students, and really care about students' experiences and performances.

Very easy class if you remember the basics of BS161 and some high school biology. Lectures are hard and boring, I skiped most. Did some very easy group work once a week. took around 30 of the 80 minutes alotted. Very exam heavy 60-70% of grade. She was very kind and considerate though.

This is already a very difficult class, but I think Dr. McGuire does a good job teaching it. She's definitely knowledgeable on the topic and you learn A LOT. I wouldn't recommend taking the class if you're not a huge fan of herpetology. You need to pay attention and ask questions in lectures to do well because you cover SO much material.

Professor McGuire was a great person, but she doesn't teach well. Much of the exams were harder than they should've been because material wasn't as deeply delved into as you'd hope it to be. BS162 was not a hard class, but the exams were just hard to study for, when they count for 70% of the overall grade.

Professor McGuire is a very good person but on the teaching aspect is awful. First 6-8 lectures of class are solely on the scientific method and every test we had was pushed back because she taught irrelevant info. Also, exams aren't information based they're more math based and how you interrupt graphs that she goes over for 0.2 secs during lect.
She doesn't present the material clearly and goes on a lot of tangents . Overall pretty easy though but lecture is hard to sit through

Dr. Mcguire is super helpful and it's clear that she cares about her students. I took this class over the summer (2021) and it was accelerated and I had two jobs at the time so I had to put in a lot of work for this class. The class was all lectures and then you go to one recitation taught by one of the TA's to go through a worksheet (done before)

Her lectures are a bit disorganized and hard to follow. She also goes through the material very quickly. She is great at explaining things and gives good feedback. She has a lot of personal experience with the subject which is great but also I feel makes her bias to certain topics and teach them more heavily.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is difficult but the prof and TAs make sure you understand the material. The lectures are well organized and require the use of clickers. There is just enough required homework for you to learn the material and extra problems are offered if you want to further your understanding. There are a few tests but they aren't too difficult.
Super Nice Takes Attendance occasionally with clicker Tests kinda hard Not cumulative final 1 easy group project Dont need to pay attention in lecture
This professor is nice and has an amazing system for making sure you do well on each phase of the project. Do the work and you will do well.

This class is just working on a group project the entire semester, then a presentation at the end of the year for your final. It is pretty easy. She needs a new mic though, with the accent and her breathing into the mic like your homie is yelling into his headset. I would take another section but if this is the only one left you'll be ok.

This professor has a tendency to give you a rubric for your group projects that explains what you will be graded on. When the grade comes back your will realize that she takes away points a lot from things that weren't even mentioned on the rubric. She also does not listen to the students side of the story on things. What she thinks is final.

All quizzes are not based on any lecture slides but rather on what she talks about in class. The problem with this is the lectures are the biggest drag, and numbed minded talking that you will never be able to understand and will only be able to pick apart a few words becuase of the heavy accent. Don't take ADV of 330 with her if u want to pass.
Professor Ma's lectures can be very boring and she can be strict, but if you put effort into her class and show her that you care she is very kind and accommodating to students needs.

Nice but on the teaching side she is a different person. I had her once and she was awesome. 2 semesters later I take her again since I knew I liked her. She was so different. Harsh grader and feedback isn't helpful it just isn't nice. 2 presentations and if she doesn't remember your presentation you'll get a bad grade for not covering everything.

On a power trip and bipolar. Very nice some days then extremely mean others. A really hard grader and assignments are out of 5 points and she will mark you down 2 points for reasons that weren't in rubric or not true. Will call you out and yell if you have laptop open even if you want to take notes. Talks SO fast and mind numbing lectures.

Do not ADV 375 with Prof. Ma if you want to keep your sanity. Grading is outrageously scrutinizing, and does not communicate her expectations well. There are group projects and on each one, we got at least 1-2 points off (graded out of 4 or 5 pts) for things that were not expected of us in the rubric. Lectures are mind numbing. Does not allow tech.
This professor has the most mind-numbing lectures known to man.

She was dismissive and lacked understanding during our interaction. When I asked a clarifying question, she raised her voice and responded with noticeable frustration. Her lectures are often difficult to stay engaged with, and she becomes visibly upset when students arrive late or are unable to attend every class.

Professor Ma is THE BEST professor at MSU. I've taken ADV375 and ADV205 with her and she DEEPLY cares about her students. She encourages everyone to connect with her on LinkedIn at the beginning of the semester and if you show up, pay attention and show respect she will GLADY connect you with internship opportunities or networking connections.
Overall easy class, I took this course online and it had a pretty consistent schedule of work and due dates. Lectures can be a bit boring but not terrible.

This class was insanely easy. The McGraw hill connect was very easy, however, her lectures were extremely boring. All the content was on the online textbook so I could get everything done easily. I wanted to fall asleep in class

she is the most boring person i have ever encountered in my life. Do NOT take this class with her she will screw you over so hard on attendance. It's three days a week and if u miss more than 1 class, be prepared for your grade to tank. The quizzes and homeworks are SO hard for absolutely no reason and she talks SO FAST u can't understand a thing.

Would not recommend this class. Absolutely mind-numbing lectures and this class could've easily been online. The participation is required and holds way too much weight in the class. If you mess up on one assignment be prepared for it to ruin your entire grade cause there's such few assignments and she won't help you at all regarding that.
will screw you over on absences. missed 5 of I think 43 classes and only got a 50% for attendance, basically saying I did not go to around 22 classes. insane.

professor ma was a nice lady and the class was fairly easy. the reason behind the rating was because there is no reason this class should be in person. the class consists of her reading off of slides with info directly out of the textbook which are then posted on D2L. homework/quizzes are hard. VERY strict ab absences. take this class online!!

Professor Medina is great. She understands that being a college student is stressful and doesn't want to add to that. Only weekly quizzes, no midterms or final. Just do your quizzes and show up to class and you will 4.0 it. You get 5 drops for attendance too! Great experience

Medina herself is a very sweet woman, I just could not for the life of me sit through this class. I just wish it was more interactive and easy to engage with. I learned more efficiently about how to conduct research from my ISB lab.

I've taken two classes with Professor Medina and would gladly take another! Her lectures are fast-paced, which I personally like. If you do the readings, you will score well on the weekly quizzes. Attendance is mandatory, but you get 5 freebies before it affects your grade.
The class wasn't too bad, but it could be boring at times, as it's nothing interactive. The class is really easy to pass as you're only graded by attendance and one assignment per week, no exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easiest 4.0 ever. Apparently in previous semesters she had midterms and finals, but not this time. This ISS 300+ level class was graded by online quizzes and attendance, and that's it. Easiest ISS 300+ credit ever. But it's possible she may make midterms/finals in future semesters. Class topic was mildly interesting as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is quirky but knows a lot about Latin America which makes it easy to ask her questions. She really cares about students and will help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Objectively easy course. The lectures are boring but there's no exams, you just need to show up for attendance, and you can skim the powerpoint to get an easy 3.0+. She's very understanding and the absence policy is pretty lenient. Great GPA boost/course to add onto a busy schedule. Would take again!
i personally love this teacher she cares about her students so much and the class that i had her in was really easy it was pls 201.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She really cares about students and made the class interesting, she not only taught about stats but also how to read academic papers which is very useful.

The class was pretty easy 5 classes are excused before points are deducted from attendance points. 20% attendance and 80% assignments/quizzes which are based off of lecture/readings. The only real issue I had with her is she changed the syllabus about 2-3 weeks before the end of the semester which changed the grading scale to make it higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof who really cares about her students! Attendance policy is super lenient, and I found that it wasn't hard to catch up if you missed class. Quizzes were all open-book, open-lecture and open-note (I got a 4.0 just from Ctrl + F searching key terms), and there are no midterms or finals -- your entire grade is 20% attendance, 80% quizzes.

This is one of my favorite professors, im taking another class with her and i am excited. she truly cares about students and makes classes so easy. lenient with absences we had 5 classes we could miss and still get full credit. overall, a good teacher and person.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took the honors section and there was no extra project or anything so it was a super easy H. The class has no exams or projects, only weekly assignments that are 10 questions based on the readings (which you don't even really have to do) and attendance. You can only miss 5 classes but she usually ends class early anyway. Super nice and easy 4.0!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were not too boring, although a bit complicated! No lab, no exams; weekly online quizzes worth 80% of your grade and 20% attendance (you can miss 5 classes). Nice professor that explained things well and easiest 4.0 ever. Would totally take again

Mariana is a great teacher. She is very knowledgeable about Latin America and tries to include current events and relates them to the class topics.
She is kind of quirky but really cares about students.
nice professor and easy class, however attendance was mandatory and we needed to buy a textbook to access homework

I took PLS 160 not 201! Really easy class, only two exams and most your grade is based on weekly homework assignments that are super easy. Do need a textbook for this class, but it can be found online at this time. Overall if you are interested in international relations and you have the option to have her I would 100% recommend.
It is sort of hard to 4.0 this class as her quizzes/exams can be tricky and it is only based on those grades, and her lectures are mandatory.
Mariana was a great prof. She really cares about students and it's an easy 4.0 as long as you do the weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: inability to convey material clearly. If it was not for the TA I had during recitation, whole class would have done poorly. Everything you will learn will be during the recitation. Very nice teacher, but lectures are very dull and material hard to understand ESPECIALLY If you have never coded before.

Professor Medina is kind and cares about her students. This class was easy, and as long as you showed up to recitation, you could get a great grade on every assignment. No final or midterms. Although reading was required, it wasn't necessary to excel in the course. Great professor, and would be happy to take another one of her classes!

Class was super easy as there were no tests, just weekly assignments. The weekly readings aren't necessary to do as she'll go over what you need to know in the lectures. Unless you do the readings, don't skip the lectures. I was lucky as my TA told us the answers for the assignments, but I heard this wasn't the case for all TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this professor if you can! She is very nice and caring! Grades are comprised of weekly assignments that you do in the recitation and attendance, so no exams or anything. The class was super easy, and make sure to go to the recitation! Really nice prof, great at helping with honors credit as well!
Just go to class for the attendance points and GO TO RECITATION!! The class is easy as long as you go to class

You could tell Dr. Medina was very interested in the subject matter, and knew a lot about it, so this made asking her questions or whatnot a lot easier. You're only graded by a few things, but she makes the grading criteria very flexible, and she's a pretty easy grader. Definitely take the honors section if you need an honors credit!

Skip the lectures and go to recitation. Lecture attendance is online clickers, recitation is in person. Helpful TA. No exams or tests, just one easy weekly assignments every week. Don't buy the textbooks cuz there're useless unless you really want to learn about R coding. Should be easy 4.0. Lectures slides are on d2l.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy 4.0 but a little boring. 3 exams each 20% of your final grade, weekly quizzes, attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It was a boring lecture class. Just readings then quiz due at the end of week

There's an attendance QR code for the lecture, but you could always get someone to get your attendance for you. All slides are posted, and all quizzes (weekly, 10-15 questions) and exams (midterm and final, 40-50 questions) are pulled from the posted slides. I mostly did other homework during lecture, but it's an easy 4.0 if you take your time.

10/10 class. Attendance is graded so you have to go to the lecture. However, all the slides for the quizzes are on D2L, you can read them while taking the quiz. Her lectures are kind of boring and she's a bit hard to understand but she's nice and lenient. Don't listen to any bad reviews on her, just do the work and you'll get 100%.
Very lenient with attendance, interesting material, you get any notes you want on all quizzes and exams. Very easy and enjoyable class that gives you a breather in your semester.

She was very accessible outside of class and responded to emails quickly and had a zoom after the first few weeks. I thought the class was easy, but the lectures did not help with the assignments, the recitation was extremely helpful. Easy 4.0 class, just do the assignments and the attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mariana is nice, but it's difficult to follow her lectures as she goes through the slides so fast. Don't bother trying to take notes during lecture, she goes too fast. TAs are very helpful in walking through the weekly assignments and explaining concepts during section. No exams. Just do the weekly assignments and check in for attendance = easy 4.0

Mariana was fine, but above all else almost useless. I learned jack squat from her lectures. Yet, the TAs on the other hand were extremely helpful. Seriously. Skip the lecture and just go to the recitation. This class is only graded on weekly assignments, which were easy for the most part.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was very interesting and she does a great job making connections to help students better understand concepts. There are weekly quizzes that are straight forward from the readings and slides. I wish more people went to class because I can tell it made her sad seeing 5-10 students there every day when there were 200+ students in the class.

There are a lot of interesting and useful concepts taught in this course. Professor Medina's lectures are good and easy to understand. She should start taking attendance since most people in my section almost never came to class. She is very nice and easy to talk to. Good class overall, but better course organization is in order.

The material is easy, however, do not come to class there is no point. I do better on the quizzes when I don't go to her class than when I do. The biggest complaint I have about this class is her having the weekly quizzes due every Friday at 12 PM. Yes, you read that correctly, not AM but 12 in the afternoon for some reason. It makes no sense atall
She takes attendance but you can miss a few classes. She grades the midterm and final super easy. She posts the questions ahead of time and you can ask her anything about them.

This professor lectures at an unreasonable pace. You'll want the slides pulled up. Get ready to write as fast as possible. She is not accommodating to student circumstances and apathetic towards appeals from students. Avoid if possible. Grading is relatively lax but she is ultimately unreachable to students and her lectures are at record-pace.

Overall, she is a good professor. There was a midterm exam and a final exam, every week had a 10 question quiz. There were 3 reading summaries dues before the midterm and 3 due before the final, 1 page each. Everything was open note and mainly the exam and quiz questions were word for word from the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Medina is a really kind person who cares about students, she is very understanding if you have any issues pop up. However if you are a procrastinator be careful because she leaves all the martials open from the semester and you can do them at you leisure.

I don't think that Dr. Medina is the issue, but she is also not the solution. I had her for PLS 201 and that class has made me drop my public policy major. The class is boring, and is mostly programming in R. She is good as far as grading, but the class itself is so unnecessary tedious that its overall not a good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: Material was very easy, lectures were pre recorded and theres a lot of reading material. Nice lady, awful professor. She wont help students if they arent understanding the material she even guided me in the wrong direction. Her quizzes are like guessing games, even if its in the material for why its right shell justify why its wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Tough grader--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is 3 exams and each exam is 22% of the grade. The exams are very very vague - it's very hard to know what she expects you to answer. Yes, she is very nice but we need better grades. She just reads of slides and sometimes it's hard to understand her. Going to class is not worth it at all. I wouldn't recommend taking her but you might like it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: not much to say. the class is pretty boring & she just goes over the material. she drags through the lecture & it is so boring. really hard to stay awake during class. the grading isnt bad, but you will work a lot with database searches through a computer programming app which is kinda hard. overall not a great class but will keep your gpa up.

She is seriously an awesome professor! She is so caring and understanding. As long as you communicate with her about what you need she is very accomodating. Her exams are super easy and so are the assignments. I would 100% recommend her especially for a requied course!

She was an awesome professor and was always willing to help her students. As long as you show up and pay attention to her lectures its an easy A. She has very easy pop quizzes and her exams are straight forward. She does a review before each exam which is extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Mariana Medina was a great prof! Had her class as an 8am which honestly was terrible and i probably would have done better if i took it at a later time because i could never make it to class. Lots of pop quizzes but she posts the slides for her lectures on D2L a few days before class so you know what the Q's are before hand! 4 exams total!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mariana is a gem. I took an 8 am with her and we never stayed past 8:50 for lecture. She also posts the lectures the night before, but there are pop quizzes so if you don't go, you might miss out on a grade. You also aren't graded on a lot in this course, so you should probably go. You also have to read the book and write responses on it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Wahman! You can clearly tell he cares about his class. Lectures were easy to follow, the only negative thing was having to pay for tophat. You are graded on only a few things, but the quizzes are fairly easy if you study and pay attention to the lectures.

Easily one of the best professors at MSU. Don't listen to the bad reviews on him. If you show up and do the work, you will pass just fine. If you get a chance to take a class of Professor Wahman's... DO IT!! He is so understanding and you can tell how much he loves and respects the topics he teaches.
The GOAT
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had him for a class this year and he is amazing. He was so understanding and is fair. He taught well and the exams were not difficult and very straightforward. It is an easier class and should not be hard to get a 4 in. You don't need to go to class and can study on your own. Slides are provided, just memorize and should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 3 quizzes worth 40% of grade, 1 film review worth 20%, final worth 40%. You can drop the final. PowerPoints are all posted ahead of class. Dr. Wahman is very accessible out of class. His lectures are sometimes worded very fancy and his examples are almost never on the test, but he is very knowledgeable.

Professor Wahman is a passionate professor who knows his stuff, but you need to go to class or you will not pass. His quizzes are so hard and I struggle to even know what is going on in his class. This was my first PLS class at MSU and it is exceptionally difficult. The textbook is so painful to read too, and its required. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Generally you'll do fine if you pay attention and come to class pretty regularly. There are only 3 tests and the final, the lowest of which he'll drop, plus a film review. It's pretty easy to get a 4.0 if you put a basic level of effort into the course and absorb the lectures well. Readings definitely help but probably aren't super crucial.

Professor Wahman doesn't give you much room to coast through this class. 5 very strict and clear assignments are all that determine the grade. Since the class is a mix of all grade levels, coming in as a freshman was a little bit more difficult than expected. If you show up and put the work in though, you should be able to do well in this class.

Wish every professor set their classes up like his. Very little to no homework in every one of his courses. Therefore, you are graded mostly by exams, but if you just make sure to go to more classes than you miss and take decent notes, you'll be fine. Attendance not mandatory, which is a huge plus and he's an entertaining lecturer. Would recommend.

There is no reason a student should struggle and have to study 20-25 hours for each test when they've never missed a lecture. That is what I had to do in this course. Mind you I have a 4.0 overall and am in the honors college yet this course was stressful. You are only graded by four things, a film review and three tests. Easily the worst PLS Prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wahman is incredibly knowledgable, engaging, and kind. Classes were very interesting and fast-paced. The multiple choice quizzes sort who did the reading and who didn't, and some questions were very specific. Final exam is two essays, which are both written by hand, but, they are open note. Overall, great guy, great class.

This class is very easy. I didn't do any of the readings and still got a 4.0 with ease. His lectures are great and concise, with some good discussion and plenty of room for questions. The one project was very easy and not graded tough. If you show up to class and take notes you'll 4.0, though attendance is not mandatory.

I had professor Wahman for PLS 392, it was a fantastic lecture to attend. The information in the class is quite easy to comprehend and is structured pretty well. The readings are long, but relavant to the information being taught during the lecture. He was a pretty tough grader especially since there were very few assignments within the class.

Wahman definitely loves what he does but isn't the best at teaching it. He assigns way to much reading that you wont need, the lectures are long and just way to expansive. He has lots of discussions and expects participation. This class was just discussion, what I learned factual could fit on a single page. Tests were easy and few.

He isn't a great online prof, he did occasional zoom meetings that didn't help with learning the material. He doesn't give out study guides and very vague descriptions of what will actually be on the test. If you have in person classes give him a try but he didn't work as an online prof for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture is online and nothing is explained well in or out of class. Complete waste of time and I would have dropped out if it wasn't required for my major. Worst set up possible. he never takes his mask off either so you can't understand anything he says, but then he blames you for talking over him, but no. It is his fault, guys. Don't take this
He is a very bad professor and person in general. Grades too harshly and is rude when you try to ask for help. Don't take his class.

He wears a mask during class which makes his talking very muffled when he speaks, so it is very difficult understanding what he is saying. The class structure wasn't decided by him directly but it makes it hard to succeed in the class.

Mike Wiser has given attitude each time I have raised my hand and asked for help. Not only is he very discouraging, but his class has the worst structure that any class could possibly have. I would also like to add that it is impossible to hear Dr. Wiser even when I am 100% focused.
I truly felt he had the class set up to fail. You get 3-4 different assignments during class to do with your group. Class is a waste of time and money.
"Active learning cycle" is not an excuse to not teach your class

for some reason we have to teach ourselves all of the material outside of lecture and then we go to lecture just to sit in a group and do an abnormally difficult worksheet. Plus he is rarely very nice to a student who has a question or is not understanding the iclicker assignments.

So much work for a 2-credit lab. Knowledgeable about the material, but he aims to correct rather than teach you where you are. If you don't know how to use RStudio, learn immediately. Incredibly strict grading. would not take again

Dr. Wiser is a fine lecturer. Easy to understand and learn from, but don't even try asking questions. He interrupts students and is extremely condescending. I can tell when he grades my assignments because he is out for blood. I hope he knows this is an intro course. DO NOT TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN, I have suffered all semester.

Seems very conceited and snobby, and not very good at lecturing. Unclear about what certain assignments are what, and doesn't respond to emails. Avoid participating in his class, as multiple times this semester I witnessed other students get essentially made fun of by him for wrong answers. If contemplating taking him for honors, don't.

idk why he has such bad reviews. maybe people don't like his stern-ness/attitude. he was very helpful, reached out to me when he didn't have to and graded very fairly. he definitely enjoys biology. attendance is necessary, but you can miss a couple and be fine. only thing i could see is he can be a bit condescending sometimes, but probs needed lol

Truthfully, I don't think your professor matters that much for bio 161. All the classes are ran the exact same and is a flipped classroom. You do group activities in class, and watch the lectures as homework (awful). I pretty much taught all the material to myself, and the only reason I got an A was the help room videos. To get an A, 100% watch.

In his class be prepared to spend 1-2 hours before watching the pre class activities where the recorded lectures are for the day that is not taught by him. There is also in class activities everyday to complete. Overall my biggest issue with this class is that he didn't teach me anything, I did all my learning from google docs and a womans lecture

Dr. Wiser is a overall great professor. Gives good feedback, connects well with his students. One thing about bs 161 is there are video lectures and a pre class activity to complete and then during the class you work on an in class activity after he gives a short lecture. The ULAs and the professor are really helpful when you have questions.

Dr. Wiser is a really nice guy, I always enjoyed and appreciated talking to him! I'm not a bio guy, but he made the lab enjoyable enough for me to not dread it every week. Heard a lot of people complain about his grading, but the rubrics and instructions are very clear, and he gives feedback on why you lost each point.

He was very helpful in class and took the time to get to know students and teach one on one. I went to office hours a few times and they really helped. He's a bit awkward sometimes but has very good intentions and teaching style.

The slowest grader I have ever met on the planet. Also takes off random points for no reason and doesn't tell you how to fix it. Takes weeks to upload the lecture slides to D2L. Answers every question with another question and makes you feel stupid. Not a great prof, but if you do the work and go to class it'll be ok.

The professor himself is interesting to listen to, but the way the course is organized is horrible. There are in-class assignments every day that are extensive. Tests are unfair and graded heavily. I had an A in the class until the final that was completely irrelevant to anything we learned and reviewed. I ended up with a 3.5.

Mike is probably the worst professor I've had during my time at MSU. He is very condescending and provides unclear answers when you ask him questions, he does not respond to emails, and there were multiple times that I had to contact my advisor and the BS department chair. VERY easy course but he makes it far more complicated than it needs to be.

This class was required for me and seeing the ratings for Dr. Wiser intimidated me in the beginning but after reading past ratings I think he has changed the structure of the course a good amount. The topics were pretty straightforward and the exams aligned with the material. The one thing I will say is that the homework is very harshly graded.

If this is the only professor open for BS162, take it the next semester.  He grades hw harshly, takes points off for things on exams that are objectively right, has no sympathy, and is lazy. He takes points off on the exams for 0 reason when the answer is right. This is the first review I have every written on a professor, I felt it was necessary.

He gives no drops, no makeups, and zero sympathy for mistakes. ULAs also take points off for things like a spelling error. His HW questions are ambiguous, and you get marked off if you answer in a way he doesn't agree with. One of my exams I failed, even though objectively I got every question right, but he didn't agree with the explanations.

At first I thought he was great, he talks like hank green and was just a harsh hw grader, but then I submitted a blank homework on accident and it was worth quadruple the amount of any other homework and I asked him even if I had proof the file wasn't changed if I could get SOME credit and he was stern about not changing it and I literally cried

This guy is extremely harsh when it comes to grading home work, doesn't add what you did wrong, and gives you a bad grade. Another thing is the lectures, in lecture you cant even read the board half the time, either its too blurry, or to bright, another thing is he always skips through the slides, whenever you try to take notes he will just skip it

The layout of this class is a lot initially and will be tough to navigate.
My advice is to take the pre-lecture videos extremely slow and draw and understand everything before class. You NEED 1-2 hours of work on the pre-lectures if you want to do well in this class. Attend lecture, learn more. Study the RIQs for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you take BS 161 at MSU the class is structured the same for all of the classes, that's why none of the professors teach in this department. He expects that everyone knows everything about the upcoming lecture BEFORE class time. He said the text book is mandatory and I never bought it and I still passed, I just watched the videos he posted.

This was by far the hardest class I have had to take. You have to teach yourself and come to lecture very prepared. The content learned outside of class is nothing compared to what they actually have you complete in-class. Attendance is mandatory because your in-class assignment is graded for correctness which is shown through i-clicker.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!! He believes that his students do not do well because they should study harder but in reality he just does not teach. You are assigned online lectures that are not in depth and does not relate to the quizzes or exams. Spent hours upon hours on this class and still really struggled.
Terrible class. Quizzes every week that they grade harshly, a lot of inconsistency when grading the 2nd attempt of quizzes.

This class was way harder then it needed to be. The topics were very basic and easy to understand but the exam questions were so hard and confusing. The people who grade the exams and homework are also very picky and take points off for the littlest things. The professor did give a very generous curve cause everyone was doing bad so that was nice.

This was Dr. Mike Wiser's first time teaching this class and you can tell. No textbooks at all so you can't read anything outside of class. The lecture content was easy but when it was time for exams, the content was all of a sudden difficult, and not all what he taught in lectures. He also doesn't seem friendly or nice. I would not recommend him!

Makes content seem very simple in lectures, but then tests on content that has not been taught. Exams are much harder than practice exams and in class activities. There will be questions that you were never taught how to answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He made the course is harder than it needs to be for a 100-level. His homework and in-class assignments are unlike the actual exam content. He gave us useless material at noon the day before an exam like it was helpful. His exams are the majority of the grade. This was his first time teaching the course and he was very unforgiving. So frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unfortunately, "Professor" Wiser will read these reviews and say, "Well if only my students studied harder!". He has an ego that everything is based on his students performance and that he is the best professor. What he fails to realize is that his teaching methods are flawed and in 90% of cases so ineffective that 50-70% of his students fail! Haha

I feel like I was set up to fail. Normally this should be an easy class. This was his first time teaching this course, and he made it so hard. The material itself is easy, but the entire grade is 70% exams. He is a very harsh and picky grader. It doesn't matter if you are good at bio, if you don't do well on exams, you are screwed.

Dr, Wiser is possibly the worst professer I have ever had. He sets you up to fail unless you are the smartest person in the world. The disrespect he has for students is beyond me especially when they try to particpate in class he embarresses them. When asking for help he answers questions with questions and made me feel dumb. Plus tests are hard!

He should not be in a classroom. I strongly believe he should stick to what he knows - his PHD and research. Do not teach a low level class and mess up all of your students mental health. He ruined my love for biology and my love for studying in general. I don't know why MSU let him teach. I wish I dropped out of his course and took it later.

Dr. Wiser is a pleasant person, his lectures aren't the worst, but they're not engaging. The work we do in class does not prepare us for the exams because of the different wording and pressure. The concepts are the same but they make it difficult to understand compared to in class work. You also will need to attend lectures to be able to pass.

Many reviews say that exam questions don't match the material, but I think it's more so that students aren't  prepared properly for the high level questions given. He's pleasant as a person but makes this course too hard for 100Lv class. I wouldn't say you should be scared to take his class but definitely be prepared to study. I give him 2.0 grade.

The beginning everything was going well with the pre-recorded quizzes because they will say what is right or wrong but after that week. The quiz does not give you the answers and every lecture I have no idea what is right or wrong anymore. The RIQ in the first week was 1hr but now is shortened to 30mins and I cant skip the question no more
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Story and his ULA are so kind but MAN they have no clue what is going on. Expecting things to be graded but then they aren't, not knowing how to explain what the rubric requires on the assignments, VERY specific word-by-word grading... unless you're always asking your ULA for their opinion, you're kinda screwed on grading. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've seen a lot of people on here say he is condescending and a terrible professor. I have never once felt he was either of these things. He gives extremely good feedback and is always willing to help. He also tries to make a connection with students and that's not something I see a lot of professors do. Definitely would take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: 100% the worst professor I've ever had. Anything he says in lecture contradicts any lecture videos or anything on the quizzes or exams. He is also very condescending and rude. I 100% will never take a class he teaches again and wish I would have read his reviews prior to enrolling.

Honestly, one of the most condescending people that I have ever met. I had him for BS 172, and I received a 25% on the first lab because my box plots were not the same color. If you can avoid taking him, please do. He expects everyone to understand the RStudio, when I have never coded before in my life.

Dr. Wiser is incredibly smart and understands what he's teaching. The problem is, he can be very disrespectful in class and unavailable outside of class. I had him for lecture and he always seemed to be in a bad mood, especially when iClicker wasn't working right.

I would not recommend taking his class, however, it is not the end of the world.

Dr. Wiser is a bit of a nerd- but he knows what he is doing is excited about it and is good at explaining things. Sometimes he'll talk your ear off but is genuinely a nice guy. The class was pretty rigorous- use every extra credit opportunity even if you think you won't need it.

Where do I start!??! If you're currently picking classes and his name pops up DROP IMMEDIATELY. it is borderline impossible to get above a 80% in any of the assignments he grades. I've unfortunately taken two classes where he was the primary grader and I was torched by him.

Do not take Wiser if you have a choice. I had him for BS172 and BS161. In BS172 specifically he was clueless. He graded post labs, taking off points for the smallest things. He answers questions with questions. He is condescending when you asking him things. He will NEVER respond to your emails, he literally refuses. Overall, DONT TAKE HIS CLASSES!

Dr. Wiser gets a really bad rep. but I honestly did not mind his class. I had him for lab instead of lecture so I know this class is a LOT easier than this lecture class. We had two professors in this class and I think everyone in my lab preferred him over the other professor. Only cons is he is a tough grader and answers questions with a question.

BS 161 is definitely a weed out class. Its meant to be hard. The professor definitely knows what hes talking about  so i ranked him well, but he makes things harder than they need to be. A word of advice: really study for those exams(especially #2) bc you get 3 questions at a time & arent allowed to back track to questions you already answered
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Literally 3 quizzes a week plus reading plus outside lectures. Only do iClicker and group work in class EVERY TIME. Doesn't even lecture or explain to help anyone understand what we're doing. Grades extremely harshly on written questions on exams and didn't tell us what would cause us to lose points until AFTER. Overall, worst prof I've ever had.

Dr. Wiser seems like a good person but he talks a LOT and it gets boring fast. This class is ALL work outside of class, you have a pre-class assignment, pre-class quiz and pre-class lectures to watch before class 2x a week. Then at the end of the week you have to take another quiz. All you do in class is group work which can suck with a bad group.
Such a condescending person who shows no respect to students whatsoever. No help with anything in regards to the e portfolio and expects you to figure it all out with no help.

Such a condescending person who shows no respect to students whatsoever. No help with anything in regards to the e portfolio and expects you to figure it all out with no help. Worst teacher I have ever

Worst professor Ive ever had honestly. Your entire grade relies on the Exams. Iclicker quizzes on zoom are hell too, 15 seconds per questions and are graded for accuracy. Never had a professor give a pre class assignment, pre class quiz, in class assignment, in class quiz, and review quiz on every single class day, so draining. Run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class spring of 2021 but am coming back to write this to warn people to AVOID this professor at all costs. He is the most condescending person I have ever spoken to and I have never seen a more poorly organized class. You could spend 24 hours in a day studying the material he provides and non of it would match the exams.

class is easy work wise but the TA's are so hard on grading and will not anwser your email when you try to reach out to them for any reason. It depends on which TA you have but I wouldn't take this class if your not really strong with writing.

Prof. Myers made me excited to be studying journalism again. Super passionate and engaging classes, very accessible outside of class too. Love Professor Myers, she always made class fun. Super easy class to keep up with and felt pretty moved by a lot of her lectures.

Dr. Myers was amazing, Most of her classes were just wondering what we thought about certain topics, but you didnt have to share your thoughts if you didn't want to. Professor Lee is awesome! She is one of the most helpful professors out there. She also makes class enjoyable as I can tell she really enjoys what she teaches and is honest. She understands that most of the students are beginners in using R, so don't worry if you are learning R for the first time!
