super easy, all the exam answers are online. chat gpt is king
EGR 100 is just generally a bad class, and Dr. Morgan tries her best with what she has. The lectures are generally not interesting with a small quiz at the end.

The class should be an easy 4.0, Morgan will not affect your grade at all as everything is dependent on your TA and your lab group, just do your work and you will be fine. That being said Morgan's lectures are  long, boring, and completely irrelevant to any work we are doing, and she makes you buy an expensive textbook that no one will be reading

Lets get one thing straight the class is not hard. I think most of the ratings are because of the lab, which is a teacher assistant, not Professor Morgan. In lab, you might find yourself in groups that are lazy and uncooperative so you may end up doing most of the work. Anyone rating this professor below a 3 is one of these lazy people.

PICK A GOOD GROUP. The labs are all group-based. Dr. Morgan sucks. The lectures have no value. The labs are where you actually do things. Don't buy the textbook; just use the free trial to do the reading assignments and skip the last 4 or so. But yeah, she is awful.

She's very unavailable and the kectThe class is a weed out class so don't be discourage if you're passionate about your major. It's an easy A when you put the unnecessary amount of work in. Switch your group of its bad and meet people in your lab! There's a lot of busy work for it o be a 2.0 class but use your resources.

Dr. Morgan seemed like a nice person. Although nice, her lectures were very pointless and people only showed up for lecture assignments. The whole course experience depends on if you have a good group or not. You spent way to much time out of class doing homework and assignments for this class being two credits.

From what I can gather, Dr. Morgan is a generally nice person. However, the class is structured very poorly. Overall, it was mostly just a report writing class. The lectures were a mix of vague engineering and physics topics that aren't fully explained, especially the physics. The class wasn't hard, but the textbook is only for homework questions.

she is very rough in grading, and forces the TA's to grade you horribly and harshly. Her office hours are horrible with 2-3 hours a week, and always 5-10 people waiting in line. Be sure to wait for 45 mins to talk to her. And she is very harsh, the course is structured horribly about stuff and not being clear. She also speaks like a robot in class.

Dr. Morgan is a very sweet lady, don't get scared from her low rating. The entire class is based on if you do the work on time. She does make her TA's grade kind of hard on the reports, but it's only to prepare you for the actual reports you'll have to do in the field. They also give you really good feedback so you can improve for future reports.
her class is kind of pointless but easy. pretty much don't understand what she's saying but it doesn't matter because we don't ever use any of the stuff
she is super nice and helped a lot with any questions i had

Very kind and easy to talk to. Although office hours are limited, you can always email your TA with any questions. Overall, it's an easy class if you actually follow the report rubrics and is a pretty fun course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Haven't interacted with the professor much but the class wasn't bad. Depends a lot on if you get a good group, but otherwise it's mostly about following instructions and keeping up with deadlines.

Grade is entirely dependent on your lab group and TA. Lecture is a little boring and usually doesn't relate to lab content. Attendance mandatory as there are lecture assignments. TAs are pretty harsh graders and will give you a 0 for submitting something even one minute late. Also the textbook is crazy expensive for how much you end up using it.

The only thing you need to do to pass the class is focus on the lab. She does lecture assignments but they're pretty trivial. Exams are open note. You don't really gain much from lecture. It's mostly group projects and report writing so its reliant on a good group. I had a good TA which made it a little easier. Keep the lecture assignments.

The grade that you get is largely dependent on the group that you have in lab. But, you do have the option to switch groups after the first project. I don't like the $150 textbook that you have to purchase to do homework. She is pretty decent at Lectures but most of the things are pretty general that we are taught.

Think her average grade is more indicative of the course itself and not her. Experience largely depends on group members and TA. Book costs an insane amount of money for its use case, and lectures are usually pretty boring. She herself is a nice person, course is just repetitive and quite boring.

This is the worst teacher I have ever had in my entire life. Expect to be spoken to as if you are 3 years old. Has two total office hours per week despite a 500 student class size. Therefore, if you show up to office hours expect to wait 30+ minutes for a short conversation that will be her lecturing you about your questions before you finish aski

most work youll have to do for a 2 credit class, lectures are very boring and filled with unnecessary info, course work is mostly busy work and group projects, overall not hard to get a good grade but not a good class

Dr. Morgan is fine. She seems like a robot most of the time during the lectures. The content of her class is important but is very boring. Even though the TAs do the grading, they follow a strict grade scale for each assignment. You will get a 70% on your first paper, the excuse being "It's a tiny portion of your grade." Do the work, you'll be ok.

Dr. Morgan is one of the most soulless people I have ever met in my life. She is very rigid and unaccommodating. If you come to her office hours with questions regarding grading, expect to leave the room with no shreds of sanity left. Her class may not be difficult, but she is certainly difficult to be around...

I earlier gave her a 5 star thinking she was a great professor. I recently got an email saying my honors option was rejected for this class. I LITERALLY PUT IN HOURS OF EFFORT INTO WRITING A 8 PAGE REPORT for honors option and due to some minor error,SHE JUST DECLINED MY ENTIRE REPORT. I mean how could a professor be this tough on an assignment .

I dont know why do some students hate the professor. I agree a lot of content in class can be done in a short amount of time rather than a semester, but professor does teach well and tries to make students learn.. However, her office hours line is really long, it needs to be fixed.

Your grade in this class will be completely dependent on the group that you get, but all other work is extremely easy. My only gripe with Morgan is the $150 textbook which you HAVE to buy in order to do the homework. It's unfortunate that this class is required since its completely unnecessary but she makes the class as easy as possible.

The professor seems great, but lectures can feel boring and pointless. The class heavily depends on the group project, so your experience may vary based on your team. The TA also plays a major role—having a helpful one can really improve the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class is HEAVILY dependent on the group you get. If you get a good group it will be an easy 4.0 with little work. If you get a bad group, like myself, you will have many late nights and the class will be equivalent to a 4 credit course. My group did zero work and it was the most miserable experience I've had in college so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The lectures were useless, and the assignments reminded me of 8th grade math. The lab experience depends solely on the TA. I had Matias Leon-Miquel. He was the best TA and was so kind and helpful during lab and was a pretty lenient grader. Dr. Morgan did nothing. The TA makes it or breaks it. Overall very easy class though.

The lectures and lecture assignments taught me nothing; it was just busy work. She is also not very lenient on changing grades. The class is heavily focused on group projects, and when people in my group didn't submit the work like they said they would, I got zeros, even after going to her office hours, she said she wouldn't change it.

The course itself is very stupid, so I can't put that on the professor, but her lectures are actually very boring and useless when it comes to teaching us content. She is really strict on changing grades and won't give you even 0.01% credit if that meant you would get a 4.0 in the class.

EGR100 is an unorganized class and the lectures and labs are disconnected. The labs have a ton of reports and projects that are often too much. Lectures are to prepare for exams. The class doesn't introduce students to much engineering besides how to write reports and make scatter plots in Excel. Dr. Morgan is kind and accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easy class but the lectures are so boring and not useful. The lecture assignments are so easy. Grading depends on the TA for labs but they are mostly lenient and good with material.
good overall

Class was pretty fun and easy mostly involving a couple of hands on projects and some highschool level math and physics. She's a pretty nice and caring person. $150 for the text book was crazy, another class I'm taking uses the same platform and the text book is $40 with about 10 times more content than this class.

This class is honestly more work than the 2 credits it is, but it is very easy. Make sure to attend lecture as there are lecture assignments you must complete to 4.0. Dr. Morgan is very accessible outside of class. If you ever need help with anything (grading, late assignments, etc.) don't email her, just visit **office hours**.

This class uses a $150 textbook which has content that can be summarized in a YouTube video. The lecture/exam is mostly an arbitrary combination of thermodynamics, physics, chemistry, etc. This class lecture/exams doesn't really serve a purpose for engineers. Labs are useful, as they introduce report writing and collaboration to students.

She is nice and educates you about careers in engineering. all work in this class is very easy. I've seen people on here claim good group members are important to your success in the course, but you could do all the work alone it would just be a more significant time investment than necessary.

She was okay, but the class is just pointless. I don't know why the university forces engineers to take it. You learn quite literally nothing, the lectures are at 8am, and you just talk about random BS and powerpoint/excel. Joke of a class, and Prof. Morgan was just "Okay". HATED the course though

Honestly this course solely depends on your group members and your TA. Also be prepared to spend around 170 for a textbook that is useless. Once again you need immense luck for your teammates and TA to have a good experience.

Yeah, this class wasn't fun, but all engineers have to take it unfortunately. $150 book was useless but required for points. TA was not a good grader. Lecture assignments were easy. Just unit conversions for the most part. Class just annoying rather than difficult. This class should be an easy 4.0 but there were some close calls from bad grading.

Most problems have already been said. Overpriced useless online textbook, big ego, bizarre grading. Keep your lecture assignments (Yes even after they're graded). The lab TA did all the heavy lifting and was very nice. You will not learn anything in this class.
Dr. Morgan gives what are some of the worst lectures at this university. she explains everything badly. also she makes you buy a $150 textbook that she didn't mention a single time.

Genuinely the worst class I've ever had. She seems nice, but had quick, useless lectures that taught us nothing. My lab groups were DESPICABLE- had to do all the work and I didn't know how to ask for help from prof. No lecture content came up in lab at any point. USELESS $130 TEXTBOOK??? GOOD GOD. AND WE HARDLY USED IT. Bad reviews are true.

Hey guys welcome to the 8 AM lecture, let me speed run 30 slides, so you have no idea what I'm talking about. Oh, hey you also have a lecture assignment on said slides, but you only have 10 minutes, good luck! Oh yeah, don't forget to go to that 2 hour lab and jerk each other.

In her lectures, it's fine 35 minutes of her talking and 15 minutes to do an assignment. HER LAB? SUCKS! You do two projects throughout the semester with a team, if you have a teammate that isn't doing any work and you want to leave their name off? The rules for that are very fuzzy. I hated this class, but it is the first step to being an engineer.

I have never seen any professor that tries to "fail' a student as hard as she does.
She's unreasonably strict and seems like love to give students penalty.

Dr. Morgan is kind but inflexible and overly strict. Missing a scatter plot cost me 60 points out of 200, and despite scoring 98/100 on the final, I got a B. Submitting assignments even one minute late results in zero points. The course demands too much for a 100-level class, the $100 e-book feels pointless, and emails often go unanswered.

Not outstanding, but not necessarily an awful professor. You have very little time to take notes in lectures, and the projects are super mundane and not exciting. It's very unclear what the curriculum is supposed to teach or prepare you for. Depending on your TA, you will be graded super heavily or not at all. Try to take the class with a friend.
Everything taught in the lectures is common sense, all of the real work comes from the lab. Textbook is barely used and very expensive. Professor is nice enough but this class is absolutely useless.

Made me buy a 130-dollar textbook to not use it. This sums up the whole class experience, overall, lectures were unorganized and she went extremely fast. Labs vary greatly depending on your TA and group.

She goes out of her way to stop people from doing well and wastes their time. For example, if work was submitted on time in the wrong portal (she teaches first sem freshman mainly), she makes you come to office hours which are at an awkward time and still might not accept the work even though it was submitted on time just at the wrong place.

the professor seems nice, but the material is so unorganized when it's taught. i had no idea what was happening during lecture assignments. even the labs assignments were confusing to understand. the labs are also two hours and you basically just sit there. they need this to at least be a 3 credit course for all the work and group projects.

Dr. Morgan (you MUST call her doctor or else she will not even respond to you) is extremely difficult to reach and very difficult when it comes to communication. The class itself is not hard, however she instructs the TA's to grade VERY difficult, and would not communicate unless you go to her office hours. I pray one day this class isn't required!

Dr. Morgan isn't the greatest professor, but really isn't as bad as her rating makes her out to be. As a person, she's quite nice and respectful especially while answering questions in lecture. As a professor, her lectures seemed kind of unorganized and hard to follow, sometimes giving us only 10ish minutes to do the required lecture assignment.

Professor is unorganized and teaches concepts that are generally common knowledge. Book is expensive for class that is useless. The only part that is useful is working in groups to complete projects. Should be a 3 credit class as many groups are not efficient and require one person to carry the team.
She assigns a very useless textbook which is 130 bucks. Super easy class.

useless lectures that taught us common sense things like unit conversions. didn't learn anything new, everything was something I new from middle school science classes. labs required a ton of work for a 2 credit class. had to buy useless book for homework, which just glazed engineers and didn't teach us anything.

Overall, class is mostly busy work. Your grade will be determined by how lenient your TA is. Had to buy a $150 textbook that was utterly and completely useless for 10% of the grade. Lecture attendance is required. However, Dr. Morgan is very kind and was always friendly in lecture. Great person, boring class. Wish we didn't have to pay for textbook

This class is a joke. Your once a week lectures are spent sitting there having no clue what is going on, until the last 10 minutes when your handed an assignment and told to do it. Your 2 hour long once a week lab is very TA dependent but with no clear rubrics or guidelines you'll have no clue what to do. Don't even bother with office hours.
Lectures were so boring and I learned absolutely nothing. To be fair, that's mainly a pitfall of EGR 100. Just read off of slides that were mainly dimensional analysis.
Not lenient at all.

This class as a whole is the single most useless information dump ever, get ready to learn about microsoft excel and "problem solving" aka doing random projects for no reason. Other than that, Morgan is not a great prof, she goes through the lecture information too quickly and all the lecture assignments are just copying info from previous slides.

This Professor is the reason my Engineering has so many problems in the modern day. She has said, "We have new students" in one of her lectures she is the reason that so many good engineers quit Engineering because she trys to kick the creative, and questioning students out of engineering.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Morgan wasn't as bad as her reputation makes her seem. Her lectures were decent, but the material presented was pretty useless, as was the class as a whole. She also wasn't very available outside of class, as she usually was not able to talk before/after class and her office hours always had a long wait. Not the worst... not the best either.

If you have any questions for Dr. Morgan that do not directly involve lecture content, she tells you to attend her office hours no matter the question. Once you attend her office hours, she is incredibly rigid and makes you get back in line if you have any modifications to be made. Working with Dr. Morgan is extremely difficult.
Dr. Morgan was very nice and caring, but her lectures didn't make any sense. It felt like she just talked about random stuff and it didn't seem to be relevant or relate to anything.

This is not a hard class to get a 4.0 in, but this was also an annoying class to take. The professor is a good person but not the best at her job, she speeds through the slides and there are in-lecture assignments that you have to do. The labs could be easy or hard depending on your group and TA.

Unfortunately this class is required for engineering majors, otherwise I would recommend that nobody take it. Lectures are super fast and basically useless, it's difficult to keep up. She has mandatory graded lecture assignments so you can't skip. Lab is based almost entirely on group projects and varies WILDLY on your TA and group members.

This class is a waste of time. The lectures are very boring and she doesn't do a good job of explaining so you don't really learn anything. At the end of each lecture, there is a lecture assignment, which is most of the time hard as she doesn't explain the topics but rather reads them off a slide show. This was one of my least favorite classes.

One of the most useless classes in MSU. Her lectures were fast paced and boring. Those assignments during the lecture were so easy. The projects are just waste of time regardless of only 2 credits. Wouldn't take this class again.
egr 100 is the most useless class of the curriculum. that two credit class is more painful than anything.

Morgan is not bad herself and her lectures are fine, but a bunch of calculations are thrown at you and you don't really learn anything. Exams are easy as she walks you through it step by step. BUT, I cannot stress this enough please get a good group for lab or this class will be horrible. Please don't feel bad and leave them as it is your grade!

Dr. Morgan's class was a typical first year intro class. It's easy to manage a 4.0 in her class if you provide group effort and have a interest in engineering. The biggest takeaway from her class was learning how to work in groups. Her lecture assignments were my biggest struggle (not too hard though) due to the intensity of the calculations.
easy class, lectures were just really boring and fast paced. there is lowkey no point in showing up to the lectures besides the lecture assignments because the videos she uploads are the same.

Jenahive herself is nice but it's the TA's to be aware. Most of the class is group work and the TA's are very picky on the projects. They don't grade based on the rubric or requirements and take off points for the smallest stuff. The TAs also aren't very clear on what the projects or reports are supposed to have. Midterm and final exam are easy.

She was ok. Good person, but treated kids like they didn't know anything, like kindergartners. Projects graded unnecessarily hard. Most of the grade is based on 2 projects. Lectures were generally unhelpful and did not flow at all.

Class felt absolutely useless for later in life, way too much work outside of class, especially for 2 credits, and a $100+ textbook that is essentially only used for homework problems (that you absolutely have to buy new; can't get secondhand). Only a 2/5 instead of 1/5 because she was easily accessible through email.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Morgans lectures have nothing to do with the Labs and are very unhelpful, even for the lecture assignments. You never know when anything is due and she fails to remind you to keep the assignments even when you have to submit them at the end of the semester. Its almost like Dr.Morgan sets you up to fail.

Dr. Morgan is a nice, helpful woman but her lectures seem pointless. All the consist of are her going over random calculations that seem to have no correlation to anything we do in the lab. The lecture assignments are repetitive, and the midterm was really weird. The lab is fun as long as you get a good project which can be unfair.

Terrible. No late work even by 30 minutes even though they grade 2 weeks later. Some TA's are the harshest graders. I had more work in this 2 CREDIT class than my four credit classes. This class is also completely useless and your grade is based on luck whether you get assigned an easy or a hard project. This being a mandatory eng class is a joke.
I have spent a cumulative 12 hours in her lectures and have not learned a single thing. At least the labs are pretty fun.

You are required to purchase a textbook and complete reading quizzes which ask questions that are utterly useless. You have to resubmit already graded papers a month after they are done getting another grade to "make sure you keep the papers." And the classes talk about things you would learn better in other classes but she goes way to fast.

Will give you lecture assignments to do, then takes them for points, gives them back graded, and then expects us to turn them in again for what? Why what reason? She does things without reason. This woman teaches with rules. She doesn't flinch at students asking for help or needing more time on slides. If it can be avoided avoid

Never accessible for help outside class except during office hours - will never do anything over email. Makes you purchase a $150 textbook for 5 homework assignments. Attendance in lectures are required and there are graded assignments in them. Dr.Morgan along with her TA's are unsympathetic and unhelpful. You will teach yourself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Morgan is one of the most caring profs at MSU. Although the lab projects can get hard, get with a good group and you'll do fine. She also helps you on the graded lecture assignments each class and goes over stuff to help. Theres lots of opportunities to earn credit as long as you complete everything. There are also only two tests for the class.

Dr. Morgan is a good person, but terrible professor. I had more work in 2 credit EGR 100, than the rest of my classes combined. I didn't buy the $115 textbook, got zeros for the reading quizzes, and still got a 4.0. The group work is terrible if your group is bad. Grading is done by TAs. The midterm was a cake walk if you follow her example demos.

She acts like her 2 credit class is the most important thing in the world.  Her level 100 class had more work in it than my level 300 class.  It was boring and taught me nothing and costs $1000 to take.

This course is completely irrelevant, but a requirement for all engineering majors. The lectures are useless, and group projects are tedious and trivial but can be fun if you get a good group. If you don't get a good group, you will not enjoy this class. Dr. Morgan has office hours twice a week and will help if needed, but this should be an easy A.

The course lecture and required $100 textbook are totally unrelated to the lab and exist solely to be mined for final exam material. Expect to do poorly on the exams and lecture assignments if you do not have a solid physics foundation coming into the course. Labs are all group work, which is great if you get a good group, but awful if you do not.

The lecture, reading (which costs $100), and labs are irrelevant. The TAs vary; some could be very harsh, even on a tiny mistake, but others care. The professor herself is really nice, she tries to make everyone understand the concept and does well in this course. She truly cares for her student and provides constructive feedback towards questions.
The group projects were awful and the TA's grade insanely harsh. It's easy to forget to do work for this class so make sure you stay on top of your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course was irrelevant: lectures had nothing to do with labs and most of the work was done in lab. Lectures were mostly spent going over slides and most people couldn't keep up with her and take notes because she went through everything very fast. TA's did most of the teaching throughout the course, and every TA grades differently so beware.

Dr. Morgan's class (specifically EGR 100) is unnecessarily difficult because there is a lot of irrelevant information in her lectures. Basically the entire semester it is unclear what you need to know. However, I think that Dr. Morgan does try to help students when she can.

Professor Morgan puts in zero effort for her students. The class is unnecessarily harder than it needs to be.  The lectures by Professor Morgan is a waste of a hour but you have to stay till the end to complete the lecture assignment that she gives the answer to. It seems they pay her for her PhD title and not actually teaching proficiency.

Dr. Morgan was of minimal help the whole semester, and her lectures were very irrelevant and unhelpful with the labs. I first entered this course with high expectations and quickly became disappointed for many reasons. Also, the required $110 online textbook was completely useless other than needing it for a few 5-minute quizzes the first month.

Dr. Morgan is honestly not a terrible teacher or person, she's just not a good lecture professor. She goes through things thoroughly but it's almost boring and the lecture assignments are somewhat hard. If she was a TA, it would be much better

EGR 100 is a complete waste of time. The lectures were just boring and the only reason I went was because of the assignment. 99% of the work for the class is done in the lab portion and which is taught by the TA. Class is super easy but will ned to do work on the group projects, so pray you to get a good project group. Projects are also super easy.

Lecture is required but has absolutely no relevance to the class. I'm not sure I've ever taken a class and learned nothing before. Lab is enjoyable but make sure you have a good group or else you are in for it.
They grade based off of "creativity", which is an arbitrary and poorly described metric.

EGR100 is a simple class. Most of the work is in lab and if you pick an easy project, you'll be fine. In lectures, however, Dr. Morgan speeds through the notes and students have no time to write anything down. Everyone took pictures of the screen before she clicked to the next slide. Lecture assignments can be hard, so ask around you for help.

The lectures and lab work are very different but they do relate to what you're going to be doing in engineering. Most of your grade is based on lab work, so hopefully you get a competent group. Projects are decently easy the TA's help you out a lot and the prof gives good resources to use on projects and the midterm in d2L. Attendance is graded!!!

Professor Morgan seems to care about the students and was usually really helpful when I visited her during office hours. However her lectures were completely unrelated to the stuff you did in lab and if you don't get a good lab group you'll have a tough time. Some projects are also way easier than others but you have little say in which one you get

DON'T PAY FOR THE ONLINE COURSE BOOK. It is over a hundred dollars and it's five hours to go through all of the work assigned using your free trial. As for the rest of your class, your group will make or break this so make an effort to actually get to know them. The course material is very basic, be ready for a lot of high school science classes.

The lectures were all recorded and posted, but the assignments were difficult as she doesn't go over the material in detail and expects you to have prior knowledge. The bulk of your grade is the lab group projects, which were awful or great depending on if you got a good group. The midterm was easy since she outlined it in lectures.
I like Dr. Morgan, she seems nice. The lectures are fine, nothing amazing about it. I really hate this class though, most engineers won't use the skills taught.

I saw Dr. Morgan twice the whole semester, I had an in person lecture but realized watching it online was easier. This class is stupid at best the projects you do in lab are equivalent to what middle schoolers do. Hope you get a good group because it will be an easy A. Midterm is worth a lot of points but she has videos outlining how to do it.

Morgan doesn't seem awful, but she isn't really the one doing the teaching outside of pre-recorded lecture videos. Your TA is who does most of the class, the projects (a lot of the grade), and the one who grades stuff, most of them mark you down for the smallest of things. If this isn't required for your major don't take it. Hope for a good TA.

You would have a better time by converting your tuition into nickels, filling bags with the nickels, then having people hit you with said bags. If this was my first taste of engineering I would want to change majors. Unfortunately, at least during my time, she was the only one to teach this class.

Interesting course. Heavy group work. Decent amount of work for 2 credits. Hope for a good group cause some of these sorry engineering students won't do anything in these groups and you will have to pick up.

Dr. Morgan, overall, was not the best professor, but not the worst. Had virtually no student interaction besides pre-recorded videos, which were very slow-paced, and the course required a 100 dollar online textbook that was barely used. Class itself was easy for me, though apparently some TAs are extremely tough graders, so watch out for that.

First, you are required to pay 100 dollars for an online textbook that contains graded reading quizzes which have no bearing on anything else in the class. Your grade is VERY dependent on your TA and project group. Dr. Morgan herself seems nice in her videos but it's not like I would know, since almost nobody in the class ever met her.

We never met with her face to face. She was completely asynchronous and basically did nothing besides create very boring and irrelevant lecture videos. The group projects consumed our time primarily. The TAs handled the project grading and project directions alone. Your grade is entirely dependent on having a competent TA. Pr. doesn't do anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Congratulations! You just spend a space in your scheduling learning how to use excel. Sorry if you already know how, that's not MSU's issue. As far as Dr. Morgan goes, where was she? She did the lectures which were boring and irrelevant. She didn't interact with the 2 large projects which make up almost all your grade. Pray for a good TA and group.

The class was super random and the content was not related. Your grade completely depends your TA. I've had friends take this class and do great but I did not do as well because my TA graded so aggressively hard on our group projects that even though I got 100% everything else I still couldn't end with a A and there was nothing I could do about it

She has the teaching assistants do 99% of her work (holding meetings, grading work, etc.) while she sits there and does nothing but assign you busywork. Such a poorly ran course, very lazy professor. And of course she makes you pay $100+ for a textbook you barely use and frankly don't need. Absolute clown professor.

Her asynchronous lectures are awful. Be prepared to teach yourself everything if you don't have a good TA to reach out to. The workload is ridiculous as well; we lost two weeks (scheduling error) to work on our first project, and we're still getting lecture assignments that burn through time and don't actually benefit us. Avoid this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: As an online class you don't really have much contact with her besides office hours. She was helpful whenever I went to office hours, but I mainly went for guidance on an honors option and not the course content. Her lectures and assignments are kind of random compared to the projects but they're okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: .A ton of this class is dependant on your TA, and if you get stuck with one that isn't too great-good luck. The grading is mostly done by TA's and ULA's as well, and is often super inconsistent between classes, especially because grading criteria is super unclear. It is not that hard to get an A, but it is very draining at times.

Dr. Morgan was great. She helped a lot during office hours and always responded to my emails. Her lectures dont go along with the labs but its still helpful. Final is hard if you dont study. The honors essay seems hard since its 10 pages but if you choose a good topic youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lab practical is not very practical but easy if you print out your previous coding solutions. Passable but terrible experience.

I strongly recommend State to replace Dr Nahum with a loaf of bread, as it would be more helpful and occupy less space. Dr Nahum, please reconsider your ways. Or career. Or both!

Harsh grading and hard projects.

Start the homework 2-3 days before. The first 2 projects are doable in 2-3 days. The last one takes 4-5 days. Also, Lab Practical should be a week before Finals.

The first 2 projects were straightforward, but the third caught everyone off guard.

Professor Ohl was intimidating at first, but once I actually reached out to him for assistance, he was extremely helpful when troubleshooting my problems and further understand the content. I personally didn't find the class difficult, but a bunch of my classmates found it challenging. Be sure you understand the content and work thru all activities

Class was taught primarily by TA'S. Felt like I was teaching myself this class which was impossible. The help room was really the only option for help and they give you 5 minutes at a time which is not nearly enough. Cse102 Is the reason I had to switch my major even though it has nothing ti do with my degree.
Impossible to reach does not give any help to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was awful. You are taught entirely by TAs who barley know how to explain stuff, and only come in contact with professors through email. I am one who put a lot of effort into this class and still could not preform well. The content is not well explained, the projects are hard, and the exams are extremely difficult. Worst class ever.

This class is very difficult, the homework isn't mandatory but if you don't do the homework you will not get a good grade. There are a lot of valuable resources outside of the classroom that everyone should take advantage of. People mistake this professor for being "terrible" because the class (CSE 101) is difficult.

Nice guy, always was willing to help out. Unfortunately, course was incredibly difficult and specific for no reason. Incredibly fast at teaching class because he is the course instructor, and not a TA. Would not recommend taking at MSU, you will get PTSD
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is hard for no reason, but it is meant to differentiate business students who are applying to broad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is horrible. The grading scale is ridiculous.  The quizzes have 3 problems and if you miss one you automatically fail the quiz. Don't even get me started on the exams. Kevin wants you to email your ta instead of him for help, but the tas are all students and half the time they are in class or working and can'take answer your questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is incredibly hard for no reason. The class itself has a 44% success rate which is absolutely absurd on the universities part and it really says something about how this class is instructed. Kevin talks down on you and is not understanding at all.  Avoid taking CSE 101 through MSU at all costs, you will not pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I have ever taken. It is unnecessarily hard. Class and notes do not prepare you for meticulously graded HW, quizzes, and exams. Homework takes over three hours, quizzes are very tough, and exams make you want to pull hair out. I am a hardworking student that has a high GPA, but this class surely took its toll.
Terrible Course overall, the grading of exams and quizzes are just horrible

We love Hannah! She is one of those professors who is relatable and willing to joke around, but at the same time, will actually get you learning. She was always helpful and even held extra office hours (optional) with her dog when we asked.
She teaches well and is down to earth, and makes you feel comfortable enough in the class to participate, but keeps it professional! She knows what she is talking about.

Hannah ROCKS!!!!!!!! I absolutely love her teaching style. She relates it to the real world and adds funny videos/gifs/photos/memes into her lectures. Only 3 absences allowed but that is decided by the department and not by her. This is the only class that i ever look forward to going to! And trust me you wont even want to miss class. EASY A!!!!!!!

Prof. Olsen is the bomb. I legit can't even talk about her without tearing up because my experience was so awesome. I would write this in French, because I'm totally fluent now, but you probably wouldn't understand - unless you took her class. For reals though, if you are trying to learn French at the 101-202 level, this is the person to do it with
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Olive is a wonderful professor and is great at teaching immunology content. The course itself is hard, and requires a lot of studying for exams that are not easy and require enough understanding to apply the knowledge. they are open note but that truly will not help you if you don't have a solid understanding first. Difficult but he's great

Dr. Olive knows his stuff and explains content in a digestible way. His office hours are extremely helpful, and so are his in class activities. Exams are in person and open note, as long as they are on paper. The class requires effort but as long as you use the resources Dr. Olive provides and ask for help when you need it, you will be fine.

Dr. Olive knows his stuff and explains difficult content in a digestible way. His office hours are extremely helpful and so are his in class activities. Exams are in person and open note, as long as they are on paper. The class requires effort but if you use the resources Dr. Olive provides and ask for help when you need it, you will be fine.

Dr. Olive is the most passionate professor at MSU. Immunology is a hard class, and his exams are difficult, and you will need to study, but his in class assignments, quizzes, and office hours are very useful. All lectures are online, and the in class time is for an assignment and to ask questions.

He is a passionate professor and he is nice. but his exams are SO complicated and take SO long, even after studying. the MC in the exams is annoying because if you don't select all then you will get 0 points.

Dr. Olive is one of the most passionate and well educated professors I've ever had. He knows his stuff very well and although the content is difficult he does a good job at teaching it over recorded lectures and then in class activities!

While the course content itself is more advanced, Dr. Olive does an amazing job at teaching the material and setting up the students for success. I was extremely nervous doing into the class as I really hated other mmg courses I took, however this one was literally amazing!!! Dr. Olive really knows his stuff and knows how to teach it well!

Exams were take-home, free response and multiple choice. MC on exams can have multiple answers that ALL need to be selected to earn credit. People complained about MC because they did not study enough for the exams, sounds like a them problem. He graded the free resp easily. Be prepared to take 3-4 hours for exams if you did not study.

All multiple choice questions are "select all that apply" and out of 5 answers. If you select one wrong or one too many, you get 0/4 points. I have never had a class that grades exams so ridiculously. He praises the top percent of the class and expects everyone to perform as well as them. It's ridiculous. Does not care about students who struggle.

I would have really enjoyed this course if I didn't thoroughly learn the material and open the exam to find them so difficult. Short answers/creating experiments/multiple answer questions you lose 4 points for if you don't select them all/etc. Open for 24 hours and take SO long. ICA keys weren't posted to review work. Just really disappointing.

Dr. Olson is an incredible professor and lecturer. It is very apparent that he wants students to do well and understand the material. He genuinely loves teaching. He is so excited about the topic which makes lectures interesting. The homework is great practice for exams and overall, the class is very easy to 4.0 even if you just attend lecture.

Dr. Olson is my favorite prof I've had at MSU. I wholeheartedly believe I'd enjoy even my least favorite subjects if he was the professor for them. He's incredibly patient, and doesn't make people feel bad if they speak up in class and get it wrong. Instead he redirects and re-explains. Amazing professor and helped make difficult topics make sense.

This class was very manageable. Homeworks are fairly easy, & you can submit multiple until you get a 100%. With that, one bad test score can hurt you if you slack off. You are only graded by attendance, 3 tests, and 2 homework's (3 total but 1 is dropped.) So be mindful of that. If you study for tests, you should be fine - retakes are offered.

Olson is really passionate about the stuff he lectures about. The material isn't as in-depth as I was expecting, but it's still interesting and ties in modern examples. All the tests have corrections for full credit and all the homework can be resubmitted as much as you want. You do have to come to almost every lecture since attendance is graded.
He does a good job of walking through the content and reviewing it with students. You can tell that he is passionate about the material he presents.
Super nice guy that embodies the welcoming atmosphere and kindness of a rural Midwestern town.

Eric Olson is hands down one of the best professors I've taken at MSU. He is very genuine and incredibly patient and sweet. He was always very concerned if everyone in the class was understanding the material. Exams were very easy if you did the homework and self-explanatory. I wish he could teach the rest of my classes.

Professor Olsen is one of the best professors I've had at MSU. He's passionate about what he's talking about and has a ton to talk about. He does a lot to make sure students pass his class and understand the material. As long as you go to lectures and pay attention, you'll 4.0 the class.

If you have the choice between IBIO 341 or CSS 350 (like me), I'd recommend taking this class with Dr.Olson. The class was online so we were able to use notes on the exams which made them really easy. Class is easy going and I didn't see myself doing to much outside of class. Homework only took about 30 minutes, overall it was a good experience!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Olson seems to be really interested in plant genetics (especially wheat). He always throws in dad jokes and outdated memes. Grading is pretty simple, 4 homework assignments and 4 exams. These are all on google forms (cause he doesn't like D2L) and are open note. Textbook is listed but he says not to get it unless you really want to.

He is a very straightforward professor, and his lectures reflect that. He makes things easy to understand and is quite passionate about his subject matter. He is understanding about sickness and other similar absences, but he can be strict about other matters. Great prof.

Dr. Olson should not be a physiology professor. Our TAs warned us ahead of time that he often teaches things incorrectly and they were right. Exam questions and lectures have been incorrect. His lectures are also INCREDIBLY boring and even listening to recordings on 1.5 speed is painful. Don't go to class, read the book or use online resources.

He is just awful. Everyone says his two units are the hardest. This isn't because of the content, it is because he does not teach well. If you do not attend class, you hardly stand a chance; even then he is hard to understand. The exam averages are all over the place, and the rest of the endless quizzes won't count enough to save your grade.

He teaches the GI and endocrine units, which are rather difficult. He had good lectures, although they could be complex at times. All tested material was fair. The course format is very clear and generally pretty set in stone, and if you're a good student and understand the material the class should be manageable. Traditional lecture class.

He was one of the least understanding professors I've ever had, especially during a pandemic... he worries more about keeping his class average low than he does about if the students learn anything. On top of that, he doesn't understand simple grading math with ended up making or breaking my grade at the end. He should not be the PSL head professor
imo, he taught the hardest sections of PSL 432 (GI physio and Endocrinology).  GI was the hardest, and to be honest, I didn't attend class too often.  Instead, I watched all the lectures online.

Matt is one of the best professors and people in general I've met at MSU. His classes are engaging and applicable, and as an education major his courses prepared me more than any courses technically housed under the College of Ed. After this course, he has continued to check on me and been extremely caring throughout. Can't recommend him enough.

Matt Oney is the best professor I have had over my 5 years here at MSU. He is not only kind and understanding, but he engages his students in every lesson while ensuring they understand. He grades very fairly and is flexible if personal things come up. He truly cares about his students and he creates an amazing atmosphere.

Matt was a great professor. He always made the time fly by with awesome projects, experiments, discussions, and lectures. It's important to document your projects and findings, as they will be useful later in class and life.

Professor Oney is caring for his students and is always checking in on us. He is a good professor and an easy grader. The SAS are uploaded on D2L so attendance is not mandatory however after 2/13 he switched it to a QR code so you had to go to lecture to access it. There are 4 presentations, 2 papers, and very few quizzes but everything is easy.

Professor Oney was one of the most kind and caring professors I have ever had. His class was engaging and incredibly easy with a fair workload. He went out of his way to provide me with accommodations when I had issues with the content within the class, despite me not having university accommodations. I would highly recommend him to any student.

I had Matt Oney for ISB 202. My lectures contained about 180 kids, yet he made it feel like a small classroom. The lectures are super interactive and he makes everybody feel included. The work load in the class is pretty light. You have 2 total papers with one being dropped, also 4 total presentations with one being dropped. Overall love Matt!

Prof. Oney is hilarious, and his lectures are genuinely interesting even if science is not your focus. Only 1 test (final), 2 papers, 4 presentations that you do not have to present in class and that's it.
Attendance is mandatory so if you go the class it is very simple and able to understand the content. I think there's one test all year.
Love Prof. Oney!

Great man. Class was his lectures and then an activity you did with a group that was very easy. Exams were extremely easy, three short answer questions that he prepares you very well for. Overall great class and professor.

I LOVED Prof. Oney. Gives such a welcoming/comforting approach to his course as well as his teaching. He was very understanding, whether it was telling him I couldn't come to class due to personal matters, or asking for further explanation on an assignment, he always responded in a very kind caring manner. Recommend him x10000 for other students.
Attendance wasn't really necessary, but at each lecture we did an activity worth ten points. All the exams were online and very easy. Would take again.

Very chill professor, clearly really educated in biology and connected the lectures to current events. Exams are very straightforward, nothing out of left field. Outlines things very clearly, youll rarely have questions that arent already answered.

Professor Oney is very chill. He wants everyone to do well and is generally accommodating and quick to respond to emails. His ISB 202 class is not tough its just a lot of homework, easy to pass quizzes, and reading outside of the classroom. The class could easily be done all online. During the lectures be ready to work in a group setting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: great. only complaint is the ammount of online assignments. (usually 2 300-500 word asignments a week)

Prof made the class very interesting, and the material was relatively engaging. The assignments due before class weren't overly difficult, and they all prepared me for the exams. While he provides lots of help prior to exams, the exams weren't the easiest and he ended up curving due to low scores throughout the class. He is overall a cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Gabe is the goat. One of the greatest men I've ever met and easily my favorite professor that I've had at MSU so far. I will admit it's a higher workload than a typical ISB class, but if you aren't a bum it's easy. Sit in the front and talk to him! You won't regret it!
Great man, terrible exams. the study guide he provides does not help at all. if you dont listen or pay attention, youre doomed. a lot that he talks about he doesnt put on the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Gabe is probably the best professor I've had at MSU so far. Attendance is tracked through half sheets which are things you write a bit of notes on and turn in, so bring a pencil and paper. There'll be around 3-5 online assignments per week. With the pop quizzes you can talk to your classmates so there's no need to worry about them.

He is an extremely harsh grader, if an assignment is even a minute late he gives you 50% on it. Also he doesn't tell anyone their grades, you have to talk to a TA who also never responds or emails, in person about assignment grades. You don't even get your full grade until the end so there's no way to make up anything.

Gabriel is a really good professor, but the class requires so much homework. Like a lot of busy work. The overall class is pretty good and focus on the importance of our environment. Just be prepared for an hour or 2 of homework before every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gabe is by far one of the best professors I have ever had. He takes the time to learn names and make himself available to anyone who needs help or just wants to hang out during office hours. He has great sense of humor and is genuinely so fun to have as a teacher. I was not excited to take this class, but Gabe made it so much fun and very enjoyable

Gabe's class is very homework heavy, not hard just A LOT of busywork. He spends 20-40 minutes at the beginning of class not really teaching much, just kind of messing around, then gets upset at the end of the semester when the class is behind. He also takes forever to grade things.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hawkins is brand new to JMC/PTCD, but he is a truly great teacher. He really impressed me, and he did not shy away from tough topics, and fairly presented all the reasonable angles in this class, which is a pretty controversial class. I Highly, HIGHLY reccomend taking classes with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite JMC prof I've had thus far, he creates a comfy environment. I used to be so nervous to join discussions, but I was good to share my takes in this class. He gives genuine feedback, and will happily meet with you if you need help. He also lectures with slides instead of just yapping for a straight hour and a half. Pls take him he's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hawkins is a refreshing change in the PTCD lineup. He has moved away from the usual Straussian dogma toward a more critical, historically grounded approach. If you're a Straussian, you may not enjoy the critical readings so much, but there will be ample opportunity to interpret and grapple with the canonical texts. Participating is key!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kinda boring to listen to. Sometimes she doesnt know what she is doing. Shes nice, and makes time to answer questions outside of class.

reviews.comment: Amazing Prof best math teacher I've had in my life. When you don't know or understand something tell her and she will go out of her way to help you understand. The quizzes arnt bad and as long as u do the homework and go to class you'll do great.

Although I do recommend going to class, I have skipped my fair share of times and still consider the tests and quizzes easy peasy. She's super sweet and is willing to answer any questions. And when she notices her students are struggling, she actually tries to find a new way to teach so it makes more sense!

Literally the best professor you will ever get! Dr. Milik is so understanding of how you are a college student with other classes. And it is very rare that a professor cares about your grades but he wants you to pass the class believe it or not! 10/10 would have him as a professor again if I can!

Dr. Milik is one of the best professors that I have ever had. He is extremely educated in the field that he teaches. He genuinely cares about his students' success and is very understanding. Lectures were extremely interesting, and he is very flexible in regards to the topics he covered, I definitely recommend taking a class with him.

He subbed in to teach the class a bit last minute due to a situation at the beginning of the semester, but he adapted well and was an amazing professor. His lectures were very good and connected big ideas with the appropriate small details. He also kept a pretty neutral stance when discussing controversial topics, which is something I appreciate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very rude when you try to contact him with any questions. Impossible to receive any feedback throughout the class, all  you get is short and unclear answers.
SO much extra credit
easy class, go to the class and youll do fine

Ok class, subject was fine, but doing well was difficult.  Took the class online, would NOT recommend that!  Prof yawned through out all his lectures, which made it difficult to concentrate.  Getting feedback and help was very difficult as well.  I imagine he would be a good prof in person, rather than online...

I enjoyed his class for the most part.  Its hard to follow sometimes.  The things you are learning are quite different than what you would except.  He seems on the more liberal side, and that was just fine with me!

Quite possibly the hardest to understand, least organized Political Science Prof. I had during my years at MSU.  He should be allowed to teach nothing higher than PLS200, as 201 was seemingly out of his reach.
Great teacher. His lectures are easy to follow and captivating. He has a slight liberal bias which can be annoying at times, but I'd say it's worth putting up with.
I had her Tuesdays and Thursdays, I had quizzes every Tuesday and exam every Thursday! Quizzes were only 3 questions and exams were 10 questions! READ.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a very interesting person I loved her sociology class you made it really easy to get into the material. Her grading is precise uses clickers for quizzes so you get your grades back faster. Be aware quizzes are every week but if you do the readings you'll be fine. She does have a accent so if that bothers you don't take her. Overall Awesome!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Entering her second semester here at UTRGV,  D.r.  Oum demonstrated her  classroom expectations and standards early on.  Be expected to put to use those fresh-outta-high-school-soften brains to use.  Critical thinking is what you are going to find yourself  doing.  Seriously, just look up her credentials.  Tough on the tests but, fair.  Also funny!

I wouldn't really suggest taking her class. She is a very nice woman but has a strong accent and talks incredibly quiet making it hard to understandhear her. Not very clear on what she wants from you. Three tests, all are 5 short answer and two essays. Decent teacher but I think you could do better.
Worse prof ever! Worse class ever! I 4.0 the class but I would never recommend it-DO NOT take this class. The material is interesting but the professor is terrible!

she is great. she makes you work, which a lot of students had trouble with. she always has time to help students and met with me when i asked her questions. the problem with the course was the other students, not the prof. if you are willing to work, she will help you learn. i learned a LOT about food. TAKE THIS CLASS!

This is by far the worst professor I have had at MSU. I am a 4.0 student ( even in CEM 141) and I will be lucky to 2.5 this class. She is RIDICULOUS. She is Korean and her English usage in her exams is completely wrong and will cause you to get the wrong answer. Do not, DO NOT take this class with her as the professor. I wish I had a warning.

Great professor! Put lots and lots of effort into the lecture videos for each of the design assignments. The lecture videos were very understandable and Dr. Owen gave clear descriptions for the class concepts. CSE 335 is a tough class at times, and takes a lot of time investment, but it is well-organized and very fair to students.

This class and the prof is great, All the projects are fun and you actually do something instead of 232 learning random stuff (edge cases) that will not be applicable at all, but this class it's fun to figure out and the assignments literally take you hand by hand through everything and it's overall just great one of the most well setup CSE classes

Really out of touch and to me it seems like he thinks all CS students want to only so software development which is just wrong and its clear both the classes he teaches here are the 2 weed out classes
Dr. Owen is very out of touch with the CS field as a whole. Needs to reformat this course and care about students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The look on my face when I saw his goofy little cgi studio in his first video is legitimately the hardest i've probably laughed in my entire college experience. That alone sold me on this professor, but the lectures are also very clean and easy to follow, so its a win/win !

Amazingly structured class. Every assignment was nearly perfect and genuinely encourages me to use what was learned here outside in personal projects. The only bad part was Project 1, but that's because of other students not participating, not any fault of the course or the professor.

CSE 335 is a tough class. There is no way to procrastinate in this class and do well. The content isn't impossible, it just takes time to think through. Owen has a really good course structure here and it allows you to do pretty well regardless of your skill level IF you start everything EARLY. I started assignments 2-3 weeks before they were due.

CSE 335 (and 320) are really difficult, but Owen is one of the few professors that actually makes the online format work.  Make sure to participate in the 335 projects as there are huge grading penalties to those who don't.  Look through the common mistakes that Owen posts (the small '+' buttons that open tabs), it will save you a lot of time.

Dr. Owen makes hard classes but you learn a lot in them. Took this class a year ago and I don't remember everything from it, but the things I do remember, I remember very well. Owen can be snarky at times, don't expect him to hold your hand. I've learned more in Owen classes combined than I probably have from most of my other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My favorite CSE professor. Shows that he cares by making his lectures funny but thorough. Would definitely recommend.

Professor Owen is by far the best professor I have had at MSU so far. Yes his classes are difficult, and yes he can be condescending when answering questions. But the only questions he is condescending too are the ones that have already been answered through the lecture videos. Do your work, pay attention, and don't slack off and you will get a 4.0

Dr Owen is an amazing professor. He singlehandedly puts more effort into his courses than any other professor at MSU. He could be nicer on the forums but its very important information that you to understand in order to succeed. I've had the absolute pleasure of speaking with him in person and he's one of the nicest and encouraging teachers Ive had
dr owen is rude and condescending. worst professor i've had at state
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had, changed my view on life, I'm a different person now

You love him or you hate him, but there is no denying that Professor Owen has passion in his teachings and his fun lectures reflect that. His courses are tough and he can be harsh but if you really pay attention and do the work he is one of the most informational professors out there and you can definitely learn a lot. Had him for 320 and 335.

For CSE300 I thought that Dr. Owen was awesome. His lectures were really enjoyable with high production quality and clear effort put into them. The class itself isn't too hard either, just gotta do a few weekly assignments. Not sure how he is for other courses, but for CSE300 he was outstanding,

I learned more from Dr. Owen than any other professor at MSU. The class was brutally difficult but bridged the gap between "toy command line programming" and me feeling like I knew how to build something real with software. He greatly increased my awareness of what makes "good" object oriented code. I went on to take every class I could from him.

While Dr. Owen knows how to teach efficiently, I have seen plenty of times where students ask a question and are told by Owen or one of his TAs that they should switch majors. This is definitely not the attitude a teacher should have.

Hands down the worst professor and class I have ever had. He attempts to come across as funny and nice in his videos, and then constantly disrespects students via his questions forum. After asking a question you will most likely return to a response that not only diminishes you but discourages you from asking future... (1/3)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The way he does this class is simply amazing. I love the two track course structure, and the online videos are different than your normal online class in that you can learn so much from them. I find his humor a little difficult to get used too, but after a minute his somewhat blunt humor is ilarious to me. I will always recommend him for this class

I recommend taking notes on your own time. He posts the lecture slides, but speeds through them in a short amount of time in class. I 4.0 this class, and while not doing great on the exams, there are a lot of other easy 100% to do to ace the class. Quizzes were always online but the exams were challenging. You get a cheat sheet on it, though.

He's a great guy. However, it was tough to take notes because he sped through them. Also, the study guides never aligned with the exams, attendance was mandatory with only one drop, he never responded to emails, he gave pop quizzes, and has an ignorant TA who could never spell my name right in emails.
Every exam he gave had content that was not covered throughout the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: His lectures were absolutely amazing, and he is very responsive to questions. My only gripes with this class were having two exams worth 35% each, and the homeworks were sometimes very proof focused which was difficult and brought down my overall grade a lot. However, I managed to do well. If you put in a lot of hard work into studying, you are ok!

He explains things very well and is always willing to answer questions. He draws good diagrams and graphs. He sometimes gave challenging homework problems but they were good for learning and help was available. Overall great prof.
He gives great lectures, and is very willing to answer questions. He posted notes for the class which were nice to review. Exams were reasonably difficult. Overall, a great professor.

Homework was difficult and graded based on accuracy. 2 big exams worth 35% of your grade each. A bit of an accent but it's manageable. Good notes and very good explanations. Answers questions and stays after for them. Exams were moderately difficult but manageable with good study habits. Overall, he was an absolutely incredible professor.

This is for MTH 314 no MTH 234. This professor goes through learning materials well during lectures by drawing, giving examples, and thorough explanations. At some instances, I found online explanations a bit more clear but overall he is not a bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very good lectures. Explains concepts well and draws pictures well so you understand what's going on. Always open to answering questions during the lecture or afterwards. The class itself is tough though but if you work hard you can get a good grade.
Honestly, he used the Maccombs videos for the online class but he was really quick to reply to your emails. I would take him again I got a low score since I kinda gave up later in.

Good professor, his lectures were very clear. Sometimes had difficulty to understand his accent but we could still understand him at most of the times. His note takings were very helpful to us. The grading may be a bit tough. I ended up with 3.5 for MTH 234 last semester. But as long as you put in much effort, you will get at least 3.5.

His lectures are very clear and make learning enjoyable. He always gives time in lecture to ask questions on the homework or lecture material. Provides notes to class a draws really good pictures to model what is happening in certain problems. He also has a sense of humor which can lead to some funny moments in class.
Hard to understand. Too many filler words-"uhh";"uhm".  (BTW I took mth133, not 234. It doesn't show the option here.) Didn't attend more than 4 lectures all semester. He tries though.

Going into MTH234 as a freshman, I was scared that many of the concepts were going to be difficult. However, professor Paparizos, despite his heavy accent, was very helpful during lectures, and answers student's questions in a very nice and succinct way. He's sometimes also hilarious, and is aware of the shortcomings of the MTH department in MSU.
Professor Paparizos and his notes carried me in Calculus 3. Great professor!!!
Makes custom reviews and uploads notes. Great insructor for this hard class.

MTH 234 - Class was very very tough, but that does not reflect poorly on the professor. He has a strong accent - it can be tough at times to understand, but usually not a problem at all. Lectures are typical, and he will stop to answer any question. He stays after class when people want to ask questions separately. Personable dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Paparizos was a good lecturer and cared a lot about his students. I had to reach out to him a couple times and he was also helpful and responsive. The math department is rough at MSU so he doesn't have a whole lot of control over grading but I think he did a good job at setting up his students to do well.

Only had him as my recitation leader but he did a good job laying out the steps for important math questions. Did a much better job explaining things than my professor, Alex Waldron. Had a 10 min quiz every week during recitation which was usually pretty tough.
there was a lot of opportunities for extra credit. most of the difficulty of this class is just putting in the work to memorize stuff, but she presents the information well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pfeiffer is overall a good Professor for anatomy but not outstanding. She is kind and it is clear that she does care, but the class has many ways in which it could be easily improved. Be prepared to study in ADVANCE 20+ hours for exams, and go to class in order to get extra credit from clicker quizzes. Quizzes are few and far between, no curve.

Definitely the hardest class Ive taken at Michigan State, but she is truly a great professor. Exams require 20 plus hours of studying. She does offer extra credit. Doesnt curve tests. Go to class, study , and take the practice exams.
Dr Pfeiffer is one of my favorite professors. She offers a lot of extra credit and cares about her students. As long as you go to class and study a lot for the exams you'll be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: More then willing to work with you to make sure you get at least a 2. You have to spend time studying and memorizing facts to pass the tests because parts of her tests are fill in the blank.
As long as you put in the time to study and don't treat this as a blow off you will be fine. Better than ANTR 350 but still requires adequate studying.
Study hard and put in the time and it's not so bad. Be prepared for her to throw anything at you for the test.

I genuinely wanted to cry every time I would go to this class because he loves to treat his students like uneducated children. He picks on certain students who challenge his views and is overall rude. Every assignment in this class is an essay, but he doesn't provide a rubric or clear instructions, which leads to multiple points being deducted.
Never take this prof, he pushes his political views and degrades his students. This class would be fine if he were open to other views. 2 hr lecture to hear him rant.

Worst professor I've had at MSU. He spends most of class pushing his political opinions and assigns work that forces students to support his agenda. Little relevant material is covered despite two-hour classes. Attending lectures felt like a complete waste of time. I don't know how he still has a job teaching anybody.

This teacher is the worst professor I've ever had. He only posts topics about his extreme political side, and if he doesn't agree with you on something he will give you a 0. I genuinely don't know how he's still employed at MSU. The content learned in this class is useless and disgusting.

Class is insanely easy, but the lectures are just the prof ranting about his personal views. It's pointless and annoying, as someone who agrees with his views, he makes me want to change my beliefs just so I don't side with him. He's also super condescending to students like we're clueless. Not worth it but also the easiest class I've ever taken.

This professor constantly shares his political views with the class, almost pushing them onto you. He presented multiple opportunities to go to politically charged protests for extra credit. While the class was easy, I would never take his class after the constant tangents about completely irrelevant political topics. Very unclear grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course was nothing but offensive honestly. I feel I learned very little about the actual subject, and more about his political and outside views. Don't even try to email him, he wont respond for weeks with hardly a one sentence response. Ask about a low grade? He doesn't have an answer. Do not take this class with him. If I could drop, I would
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does a good job teaching as he is passionate about the material. Offers a lot of different and cool extra credit opportunities. Get ready to write, since every chapter is graded on one paper that is usually 5-8 pages long and covers many topics. If you can write well, you should do well. He is lenient with deadlines and cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is not a good teacher, the majority of the material that he teaches can be summarized in the readings that he requires before each class. The required readings can also be done half-assed before the class and still get full credit. Make sure you cite and answer the full question for each essay, that is how you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Schauert is very caring to his students and knowledgeable about the subject material. His lectures can be a little boring at times and the essays are long but he's reasonable when it comes to grading if you put in effort. People who struggle don't pay attention in class, listen to what he says and make small mental notes and you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is one of my favorite teachers in college! I was deeply attracted by his teaching style. There is no in person final exam.The semester paper is very simple, you just need to look at the reading material a little. It feels less like a paper and more like a discussion and response. All you have to do is write this assignment and get 4.0.

Not sure why his rating is so low on here :-( Paul is my favorite professor I've had at MSU! His interest in what he teaches makes his lectures easier to follow along with. He posts everything for the course at once so you can read ahead. We have essays every module instead of exams, and a lot of EC opportunities during & at the end of the semester
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: I don't recommend this IAH to anyone who is taking hard classes at the time. There is no real homework but the essays throughout the course are excessive and time-consuming. Lectures are very long and his comments to students sometimes are backhanded. You can tell he is very passionate about what he is teaching but not about his student's success.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Schauert was such a good professor and honesty one of my favorites. I am confused as to why he has so many bad reviews on here because he is so passionate about what he teaches & makes class interesting.I learned the most I have learned in this class over any class here at MSU. He is very understanding & is willing to give extensions.

One the first day of class he told us that if we missed any references in our weekly 1000-1500 word essays it would be an automatic zero with a chance to resubmit for a cap of 70%.Readings were around 8-50 pages long, lectures are boring.He goes on rants that aren't on the essay.Take this class if you really love the history, barely any music.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy
