reviews.comment: He was ok. I went into this class expecting to learn about music but it was more like a U.S. History class that mentioned music. I understand that you need historical context to explore the music, but the music part probably only took up like 10% of the lecture which was super disappointing. The final project was def overkill for a 200 lvl IAH
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. I have never reviewed a professor before but he's so bad, I felt compelled to warn anyone considering his class. It's beyond horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Honestly such an amazing professor. He is super passionate about what he teaches, and if you are into music and music history, you will really enjoy this class. 
There are weekly hw assignments, but they are very easy which he uses as attendance. There are also three big essays that take up most of your grade, but it isn't hard to do well on them.
Class is only graded on 5 Essays through the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Schauert is one of the best professors I've ever had. Super nice, enthusiastic about what he teaches, and genuinely cares about his students. You're graded by only a few things, but they're very straightforward
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had! I was in his class during the tragic event in February 2023, he responded in the most professional yet compassionate way. He genuinely cares about all his students. Exams are just essays that you have the whole unit to work on with very clear grading criteria. Just be open and honest, he will work with you!
This is easily the worst professor I have had at this University, and I am a senior. Take this class with literally anyone else.

Assigns a lot of reading/writings to do. Even though I spend DAYS on my essay and answer my questions with a large paragraph or more and a citation, there is still never enough there to satisfy him, he always wants more answered even if he doesn't ask. Even if you misplace one word he will make a comment about it, we are all human seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Class twice a week with multiple chapters of reading, videos, and a long question for attendance. 
He has so much reading you need to do bi weekly. 

In class he said derogatory terms to say "we don't say these anymore" that were offensive to people in the class. Very uncomfortable & not handled with care.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was amazing! Best Calc prof ever!

Peroux is extremely smart yet very humble and easy to talk to. I never felt judged when I asked a question or come to office hours. What I really love is that he starts every class with a clear review of what we did last lecture, so I never felt lost. He is very caring and you can tell he wants every students to succeed.

By far one of my best professor at MSU! He really explains everything so well, and he is super humble about it. He is so smart but knows how to speak to students who don't want to do math! Highly recommend.

I really enjoy going to his lectures. He goes over everything carefully and always allows us to ask questions. I cannot understand the lecture videos by the others, but Prof. Peroux always make things super clear. Sometimes he goes a bit slowly on some examples, but it helps me really understand what is going on.
He talks super fast and did not really do much explaining. He clearly knows what he is doing but cannot explain it to students learning it for the first time. Seems like a nice person though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing instructor. He was proctoring an exam for my class and handled everything with professionalism and kindness, which really helped me stay focused. I attended his lecture afterward and his explanations were incredibly clear and easy to follow. Highly recommend.

This instructor is genuinely amazing. He's calm, kind, and extremely supportive, and his lecture was one of the clearest I've attended. He explains concepts in a way that actually makes the material click. Strongly recommend.
This is the most caring and thoughtful professor I have had at MSU.
He's great!

Lectures felt like a math TED talk, engaging, clear, and full of insight. Prof. Peroux is smart, thoughtful, and genuinely wants every student to succeed. He brings energy and care to every class. Easily one of the most inspiring instructors I've had.
He made a confusing course make sense. The grading is a mess, but he walked us through it calmly and clearly.

I took Péroux's class thinking it'd be just another credit, but I ended up rethinking my whole relationship to math. He has a way of explaining difficult ideas with elegance and patience. His French accent adds to the charm, he's articulate and thoughtful. I walked out of this class more confident, curious, and inspired than I've ever been in STEM.
He is a very engaging professor and makes everyone feel included! I learned a lot from him and going to lectures! He changed my view of math, I used to hate it
Hes a nice guy but didn't explain things in a very engaging way. I learned most things from the tutors in the Math Learning Center, not from the lectures.

Péroux is super nice and caring. The class is set up in a way that there is a quiz or two every week, but we get 3 shots for each graded objective. The system is set up so that there is a lot of work for us students, but the professor is doing a great job with what is given.

Professor Peroux is an effective and accommodating teacher, but the course content is challenging. Expect weekly quizzes with the material. If you attend class, pay attention, and complete the work, you will pass. Homework and attendance aren't mandatory, but in-class assignments and quizzes are required. Good teacher, bad course. Would take again.
It is at a fast pace during class. Sometimes, it is hard to keep up with what is shown on the board, and sometimes, there would be five minutes left of class, and he would rush through a new lesson.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a god guy overall but him having a French accent doesn't help anyone in the class. People are often confused with what he is saying. Overall he's a good teacher but understanding during lectures can be difficult.

PJ is a genuine and kind instructor who holds his students and their success in his heart. There is a loose structure to the ideas taught but each class is an intellectual stimulation of the current topic. You gain an understanding through the literature, concepts, but most importantly through personal experience, sharing, feedback, and from others

PJ is genuinely the best professor I've ever had. He is so passionate and so kind! I had him for SOC216 but am taking him again for SOC350 because of how awesome he is. I'd recommend this class to everyone!

PJ is incredibly passionate about teaching and is extremely kind. He has been my favorite Professor I have had at MSU so far. I learned so much about social justice and inequality. The class does require a lot of reading, and he is pretty strict about grading. But he is very flexible when it comes to students needing extended deadlines.

I really enjoyed taking Sex and Gender with Dr. Pettis. PJ made the class interesting, engaging, and enjoyable. He was very kind and understanding of all the students' circumstances and made sure everyone felt included. I appreciated the depth of the material we covered and the leniency provided to students who were struggling with the class.

PJ is very kind. My low mark is because for a prof teaching a gender course, he really does not seem to have basic knowledge of trans issues. Also Very disorganized. Changes dates, assignments, etc. It makes the class feel chaotic. I would caution against people taking the course because of it and lack of knowledge about diverse gender identities.

PJ runs a pretty lenient class, but it is quite unorganized. He would change dates and wouldn't to post verbal announcements unless urged to. That being said, if you have a problem, he is quite willing to accommodate if you ask. He assigned a lot of reading, but if you go to class, much of it is covered. Class was only mandatory on group work days.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pettis was one of my first college professors and truly helped me adjust. He's patient when needed but can be strict. Very understanding, kind, and engaging. Lectures are clear and interesting, and there are limited tests/homework. Amazing class!

Professor Pettis is so kind and knowledgeable. He truly cares about his students and their overall success. His classes are meaningful, engaging, and actually relevant to understanding the broader subject. Beyond teaching, he is just really nice to engage with.
Dr. Pettis has been one of the best professors I have ever had at MSU. They truly share so much knowledge and compassion with their students! I would take a class with Dr. Pettis over and over again!

If you're a queer person debating taking this class, take it! Got to participate in so many important dialogues with actual peer reviewed articles and evidence. PJ is a very understanding professor, willing to extend deadlines in extenuating circumstances, checks their email often, and forms connections with students.
The class was long and drawn out by the lectures. The coursework was unorganized, and sometimes, the criteria were unclear.

Genuinely the most caring professor I have had throughout college, he really cares about his students and everyone's perspectives, you can tell! He was so gracious with extra credit, deadlines, and attendance as well as long as you communicate. And all of the lessons were so interesting too. PJ is the coolest and I highly recommend his class!
Class is easy workload wise, but just note attendance is mandatory. I would not take this class again with this professor though.
Super nice guy, easiest class I have taken, highly rec

THE MOST AMAZING PROFESSOR! PJ's class was my absolute favorite. He establishes a personal connection with each student and is incredibly funny. Although his class had some big writing assignments (and quite a bit of reading) I really did learn a lot from his course. He genuinely cares about his students, and it is very easy to achieve an 4.0.

I enjoyed Professor Pettis' class. He was genuinely kind, caring, and made the class enjoyable by encouraging students to actually connect with the material. He also intentionally made every effort possible to make sure the whole class felt included.

Philip Pettis is amazing if you can take his class I definitely suggest doing so. You can tell he truly cares about his students, on more than one occasion I saw him talking to students that were struggling, he was very empathetic and offered to do anything he could to help them out. Also he was very understanding to students needing an extension.

lectures are enjoyable and very engaging. He is very accessible outside of the classroom. However, the foundation of course work is lacking. Lecture, writing, and reading is extremely heavy considering it is a 200 level course. Structure of the course is unorganized as it relates to applying it to quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Pettis is an AMAZING and very caring prof! He is incredibly approachable and has a very warm, kind energy that he expresses to his students. He gives multiple opportunities for extra credit too. The only downside to the course was that it was very writing-heavy with multiple papers, but he was very accommodating in regards to this!

Professor Pettis was absolutely amazing. He was very accommodating to his students and their changing/unpredictable schedules. I took SOC 216 (Sex, Gender, and Sexuality), and highly enjoyed it. He truly cares about his students and their well being. This was an in person class but he gave a zoom option in case of sickness, mental health reasons.
Very, very easy course. Decent lectures. Way too much extra credit available.
Very easy class

Great teacher! This course is lecture heavy and requires a lot of memorization, but all assignment and quizzes are open book, open notes. Attend the lecture and do the homework you will be ok. A lot of extra credit opportunities that can bump up your grade by a huge amount of percentages. Final is only 10%, so don't worry about that.
Honestly, you can look up all the answers to everything if you're just looking for a 4.0.
Che is awesome! His class is very straightforward and all homework and exams are online with multiple attempts. If you can take the in person lecture you should!!
his class is very easy to follow along!

This professor misspoke multiple times in lecture videos but didn't edit them making them hard to follow along with. The amount of readings you are assigned each week with only 5 days to complete is overwhelming. I didn't understand the way things were being taught so I taught myself. He's a kind person, but the class could be structured better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor does not care about the class at all, multiple times in his lecture video he would mess up over and over again but was too lazy to edit the video or restart. This class is basically a completely online class that has a structure so he does not have to Grade anything. The work load is very above average.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Communication is amazing. He always give you ample time and notification when something is due. He is super easy to contact and understanding. One of the best professors I have had while completing my business minor.
He gives extra credit opportunities that are decently easy to do, he also makes a lot of the quizzes use examples from homework so if you do the homework or  extra practice you will be good

The class is well-organized, with a clear syllabus and helpful structure. Quizzes and the final are untimed, and homework allows three attempts. Zoom and in-person support is available. There's one research project, Packback posts, and low-pressure grading. Extra credit and quiz reminders are a plus.
As long as you turn in your assignments and do the work it is more than possible to achieve a good grade in this class. There are lots of extra credit opportunities.

Took the online version, not a hard class. Lectures are monotone and read off slides. You'll need to buy the online textbook to do homework - $85. Also weekly discussion posts. Practice problems are very similar or even identical to the exams. LOTS of extra credit. For me the final didn't end up mattering, its only worth 10%.
Just do the assignments on time and you'll be fine. Do the extra credit opportunities!! Do not skip them

This course was well laid out. The textbook quickly and easily gets your grades in, so you are not left to wonder like many other courses. Peterson was always on top of things too, it was almost impossible to fall behind in the course. Just pay attention to reminders and emails in the course and you will be fine.

The professor was nice and genuine but a bit boring. The course includes conceptual and math questions. Homework had multiple attempts, and quizzes were online, time-flexible, and unproctored. Practice questions and homework closely match quiz questions. He also offers great extra credit opportunities, which I highly recommend doing.

He's a very strict professor when it comes to excuses. The course isn't hard per say, you really have to remember to do the work and set time to learn the materiel. The class is perfectly structured, you are never unsure when something is due. When I had severe mental episode, he made a plan with me to still be able to succeed in the class.

super nice guy and great class structure. totally online and he is reachable and understanding. I had to go to the ER during my semester on the day of a quiz and he was totally understanding about making it up and worked with me to find a good time. would take again 100%
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you have interest in accounting, this is a great class to test the waters. If you don't, avoid it at all costs. I found the online class to be incredibly boring, with anywhere from 3 to 10 lecture videos per week to watch (each 2-20 minutes long). He is VERY monotone. The platform used for hw, quizzes & exams is terrible and often glitches.

Overall, he's a very kind and easy-going professor. He will accommodate things like quizzes or participation points for you if anything happens in your life with no problem. I took the class in person, so participation was required. There were 4 quizzes and then the final exam. I strongly recommend using the practice problems to your advantage.

Not a hard class; however, there is a lot of content and information you need to learn. You get several attempts for homework assignments and quizzes are online with no lockdown browser. Prof. Peterson reads off the slides he makes but still tries to make a personal connection with his students. Overall an ok class with nothing extraordinary.

Posts lecture slides every week, typically 8-12 videos varying from 4-16 minutes. The textbook is very tedious but provides good practice questions that are seen in the quiz and shows a lot of graphs to connect your learning to an image. 1 homework assignment a week and quiz (exams) every 4 weeks. 1 large excel assignment.

I just hate paying for online courses. I only reached out to Che one time to ask a question about a quiz, and it led to him connecting me with one of his associates for a job prospect, which was sweet. The course is hit or miss. Weekly discussions on top of homework. Quizzes and exams require heavy study time unless you cheat. Not an easy 4.0.

Prof Peterson is super accessible, very helpful if you have a question. Will open more office hours if you can't come during his. While confusing in MBC, his syllabus directly states when all due dates are. Homework & quizzes can be a little confusing, but it's open note. It is accounting so it is confusing, but he is a great professor overall.
There is not much guidance given by this professor and the class was overall very confusing.

Gotta pay to do ur HW. L professor. no reason for you to not get 100 on every hw, it's online. quizzes, not too bad my lazy self got like 78s so you can probably do better. Easy W for the credit. simple weekly HW (with the use of "external resources") discussion posts you can do in 30 seconds (shout out to gpt) and 4 quizzes hither and thither.

Due dates are all over the place, the list of assignments blends in with the readings/lectures necessary so its confusing reading it section by section. Overwhelming amounts of stuff on your screen. Do not recommend this class, because it was difficult to maintain this class with many other due dates. Very poor system and way of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He uses Mybussinesscourse for the entire class. Meaning you will have to pay $120 just to be able to do the homework that everyone is just going to cheat on anyway. I took this class as a summer class and I didn't have the option to purchase any options for access besides 6 months for $120. He was cool overall as a prof though.

Terrible organization, had to update syllabus numerous times throughout the semester to make adjustments that should have already been there. Bad at checking his email, some peers reported that he took multiple days to respond and only gave a one word answer. If you have to take ACC 230, try a different professor.

This man is hands down the smartest person I know and my favorite professor of all time. He comes off as a little quiet and awkward at first but his lectures are well structured and well taught, incredibly interesting, and incorporate lots of discussion and participation. He also brings food for us a lot. Grading is very fair.

Professor Warsaw is one of the best CSUS professors I have had.  He is funny and the lecture material is interesting and I looked forward to going to each class.  I would definitely take another class with him.

Warsaw is quite literally the best prof I have had at MSU. Exactly what a college class should be. He cares more about you learning the content than random quizzes. Few assignments, but they do force you to engage and be introspective. Inspiring beyond belief as well as passionate and incredibly knowledgable. Cannot recommend highly enough.
A super funny professor who creates and delivers amazing lectures!!

The course load was very light, there are only assignments due every few weeks right before exams, and the assignments and exams are both easy. The lecture slides are easy to follow, and the professor holds weekly meetings for any questions because this is an asynchronous class.

I am ok with working hard, I always do. I read everything, and there is a lot to read from Professor Phiroz. The real concern I had was that his quizzes were incredibly difficult. Some questions relate to obscure details that don't demonstrate understanding of the course concepts. I would recommend utilizing other methodology to test understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not a hard class only a handful of simulations and homework. 4 exams all reasonable

overall, not a good professor. This class was extremely unnecessary. All the exams could be found on quizlet. And the hw and simulations were pointless. Good luck getting into contact with him if you are experiencing difficulties with assignments, as he does not respond.
Most rad professor, hes cool and understanding. Take this guy if you can

Professor Strong is an amazing professor! He is kind and friendly and cares a lot about his students. There is a lot of reading in the textbook, and he assigns weekly quizzes about each chapter, but it's easy. Before class ends, we usually do a short graded reflection that we have to turn in, so I recommend going to class. 10/10!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The nicest most inspirational professor ever. Take him you will have fun
Dr. Strong is just the best! Anyone taking ISS 215 should definitely take him if you can.
Just the greatest
Very nice guy, attendance is mandatory but class is overall very fun to be in. Assignments are easy and engaging. Hes an amazing teacher and you will learn alot.

He's a really nice professor, and as long as you turn things in on time and pay attention in class, you'll be fine. The things you have to turn aren't difficult at all; it's normally just stuff straight from the book.
Dr. Strong wants his students to succeed. His class was the most fun class ive ever taken. You will learn alot and have fun doing it.

One of the nicest professors. Probably the best at MSU. He really cares about his students and it shows.

 I would take any class with Dr.Strong. Gives resources that you can use for the rest of your life. Highly recommend taking.
This professor clearly enjoys teaching and just wants to make sure you know the information and can apply it towards your future career. Phenomenal instructor. Highly recommend.

Pirouz is top 5 best professors at MSU. His lectures are not mandatory, but they're enjoyable if you do go. He uses Connect for homework assignments and exams. I wish I could take him again for all of classes. He is the best. 10/10.

Such a nice professor with a great sense of humor. The class was easy, with 4 open-note exams taken at home. McGraw Hill assignments for each chapter with plenty of time to complete. There's one group project, and groups are assigned in class by him. Attendance isn't mandatory, and lecture slides are posted online. Take this professor!

One of my favourite professors. Super easy going, also such an interesting guy. Loves to crack dad jokes, and understands that students have a life outside of class. He just asks that you show up and do the work. Would recommend.

MKT 300 is extremely easy and I would recommend it to anyone. There is no homework and only a couple of easy exams throughout the easy semester. At the end you have to write a group paper but it is extremely easy and everyone gets 100% if turned in on time. Take this course if you want an easy A.

Professor Pirouz was great. The workload was reasonable. I would recommend taking this class. 3 exams and 1 group project. Attendance was required at the start of the semester but was eventually dropped.

3 exams, 1 big project. Pirouz is a great person. I did not show up to lecture since september but I 4.0'd. Make sure you stay on top of your group project, all exam answers are in revel book. Not stressful whatsoever. Would 100% take another class taught by this man. 10/10 experience.
Super nice guy, grades very easy, gives lots of time for assignments, open note exams, and tons on extra credit

I'm only 5 weeks into the semester, but so far a pretty big fan of Prof. Pirouz. Go to class, his lectures are a decent summary of the readings, and a lot of it (so far) is information for the group project. 
I'm taking MKT300 because it's required, I'm not really into marketing, but he does a good job of making it accessible and easy.
One of the best if not the best professor I've had yet

Dr. Horner is an excellent professor. To pass this class, all you have to do is listen carefully to instructions. She can come off as extremely intense, but one on one she's a great person. (Participating and expressing your opinion will be beneficial in this course)

Great professor but very intense. She legitimately yelled at a student once for asking a question she said she'd already covered in an earlier class. Stay on her good side, keep up with readings and attendance, and be careful with questions that she might deem "stupid". I learned a lot, but I wouldn't choose to take a class from her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This is for ISS-310. Genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. Probably THE best. Very inspirational and caring. I went to office hours once to check my grade and we ended up talking for an hour. Her class is so fun and I genuinely looked forward to it every Tuesday/Thursday. Such a talented professor. Please take her if you can.
I love this proffesor everyone take this class

She's incredibly intelligent and has fascinating class content, but overall didn't provide helpful feedback or clear grading criteria. Instructions were given, but we rarely seemed to meet her standards. Things improved toward the end, though. Overall, the class experience was chaotic and stressful for many, but the course topics were interesting.

Dr. Horner is an amazing professor. Very authentic and knowledgeable. You can tell she knows her stuff when she lectures, and expects high quality work from her students. Very funny and engaging. Just make sure you come to class prepared, properly cite sources, and use your brain and you'll be just fine.

Dr. Horner is a great professor who truly cares about her students learning and professional development and will challenge and push them. As long as you do the readings, follow assignment instructions, and participate, your grade will be fine.

Gives terrible feedback, doesn't give clear or even good expectations, won't grade anything until the end of the semester, teaches literally nothing herself just makes us read and watch a bunch of things.

At first I was kinda scared of her, but half way through the course I started to realize how funny she is. The class is so easy you just have to show up and turn your work in on time. 100/10 would have her again!

If you attend and participate you are eligible for 85-90%, which is below a 4.0 standard. The only way you can get 100% each week is by saying something "profound" which is completely subjective and not prudent in large classes. The teaching style is chaotic and lazy. She does not teach. She does not provide clear expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Horner is phenomenal. She is extremely intelligent. She is a macro professor, and has the class do an advocacy project. There is a lot of reading but well worth it. Do the work, do it well, and you will do fine. Take the time to have a personal relationship with her. The work seems daunting but it is not if you manage time well.
Pilar Horner is easily the best professor in the program. Not only was she an inspiration but she also taught me the true meaning of critical thought. You wanna pass her class? Use your brain.

Pilar is a hard teacher, but I learned so much! She demands a lot from her students - she pushed me so hard, and I'm so grateful for it. I feel ready for grad school because of this class! Plus, I realized my love for SW policy and it is what I'm pursuing!

Horner is difficult but it was one of my favorite social work classes.  She encourages deeper and better thinking.  Class is mandatory and she doesn't let you out early but it is well worth your time and is interesting. I would recommend her!

Phil was EASILY the best prof I've ever had thus far in my college career. While the course is based off of attending lectures/Tophat questions and 5 exams, it is not challenging as long as you attend class. While some material can feel a bit boring and/or repetitive at times, Phil makes it very easy to stay engaged with his vibrant personality!

Phil does a good job lecturing the material. You're only graded on 5 exams and a participation/attendance TopHat score. Attendance not mandatory but the TopHat questions are graded so it's better to just show up and answer them. It's not hard material to understand, mainly government/capitalism stuff. Can be boring but easy enough to get a 4 or 3.5
Lectures were not bad, he loves when people participate. Tests were not too bad, you just have to get used to the wording. Very fun class though, one of my favorite professors for sure.

Your entire grade is attendance/top hat questions, and exams and there's no in-between and he doesn't give study guides for the exams. The first exam we had was overly wordy, and we asked for a study guide for future exams he gave us a PDF with study TIPS. The class itself isn't bad but I'd change a couple things. Lecture can be a bit boring.

Going into the class I found it very hard, but that's only because usually I rely on the course material rather than the lectures. With this class you HAVE to go to the lectures and the professor makes it really fun and interesting so it's easier to understand the course material. 100% would take a class with this professor.

I hate school and find it generally hard to be engaged during long lectures, but Phil's class was a breath of fresh air. He is the most genuine, funny, and intelligent professor and I am so sad he only teaches this course for undergraduates. You can't miss any classes if you want to really know what is going on but you will want to attend lectures!

Professor DeOrtentiis makes learning so much better, I genuinely have not had a better professor than him. He is up to date with an awareness of his students when it comes to topics talked about in class and is very sensitive and aware of them. Grading-wise, there is no homework so exams and in-class questions have a lot of weight on your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Phil is well articulated, smart, funny, and makes the class pretty enjoyable. I would take another class from him if I could, and the tests are really easy too.

Super funny and really just a cool guy. About as real as a professor can get while still staying a teacher and not a friend. I can't recommend this class enough as you do learn a lot in a fun environment. The only downside is that he uses Tophat and you have to pay for it but other than that really a 10/10 class.

Good professor. Attendance is mandatory and there is no homework which is amazing. The exams are open note but SUPER HARD. Not based off notes or lectures, very hard to get a 4.0. It is a GPA dropper for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 5 exams worth 85% of your grade. No curves on exams and hardly on final grade. Attendance is graded but not required. Very bad at making due dates known and communication isn't his strength. Worst grade I got this semester
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Phil is an awesome professor. He makes lectures interesting, has a great sense of humor, and cares about his students. Highly recommend his class!
Phil was the best. If you have the opportunity to take a class of his, do it.

Phil is a great professor! The class is made up of 5 homework assignments, 5 tests, and participation. Homework has multiple attempts and tests are multiple-choice, open note. The lectures are very engaging and he is a funny guy. He is very understanding. This is a great class.

Good class, kinda interesting but the lectures (which attendance is graded for) can feel like a drag. He is a pretty funny professor tho which makes the lectures bearable. As long as you attend his lectures you should do well in the class. His tests sometimes got a tad tricky but they are entirely open note with the slides online. Overall gr8 prof!

He was an awesome prof. He lectures a lot but it's not super boring. You have to go to class because he uses tophat and it tells him if you're in class. I missed one class and I had a 88 in tophat attendance. A lot of exams, but if you have notes you will get a 4.0 on it. He is awesome and cares!

Phil was the best!! he always made class interested by relating it back to real life, and he was a funny guy, would always crack jokes in class. Take the notes and study, just basically do what he tells you and you will be just fine. Hoping I have him for another class one day

I loved professor DeOrtentiis! I wish I would have him again in another class! His lectures are interesting, and he is constantly making jokes to make sure students are paying attention. He is relatable and his exams are very straight forward!

Phil is such a great professor! There are 5 exams (no final and it is not cumulative) and 5 homework assignments (multiple choice and are included on the exams). His exams are extremely fair and entirely based off of his lectures. His lectures are very interesting and makes the subject easy to grasp. I wish he taught more HRLR classes!
Funny guy, awesome lectures. Good real world knowledge taught in this class.

Phil is hilarious. He doesn't take attendance, but also doesn't post his content. The class is interesting and he does a good job explaining the material. Eighty percent of your grade is exams, but the exams are really easy if you go to class.

Professor Pillai is one of the best professors that I've ever had! He genuinely cares about his student's success and often goes above and beyond to provide excellent feedback. I loved taking this class and I'm deeply grateful for this experience.
Loved having Professor Pillai for Intro to Screenwriting! He taught us a lot and gave meaningful feedback for our scripts. You can tell he cares about his students and their film ideas.
He was clear about what we needed to learn and understand and was very easy to contact if you need to reach him. Lectures could be long and could get lost but it was easy to catch back up.

Professor Pillai is a great instructor! He makes me think more when I am working on my assignments. When I am in trouble, he gives me creative feedbacks and tries to solve it together. His course is very useful and fun!
He was very kind and reachable. Sometimes I would get lost in the lectures but material was easy to catch up on.
An amazing mentor and incredibly intelligent. His enthusiasm is clear and he has really helped me develop as a student of film.
Taking this course gave me an excellent comprehensive understanding of film post-midcentury. Awesome film studies course.

Professor Pillai is an excellent instructor who gives the class time to read materials outside so that they can understand the lecture material and content. I would take a course of his again if I had the opportunity!
HE always uses PowerPoints to teach in class, and posts them on d2l after so we can look back on it later if we need too.
Prof Pillai is very nice and loves to engage with students! He is very knowledgeable. His class is very interesting and enjoyable as long as you are engaging with the material.
Swarnavel deserves a great rating. DS 103 was an easy course because he only grades on 3 tests. All answers were in class and the homework was watching movies.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pillai is amazing! Kind and accessible with meaningful coursework! He always spends extra time after class answering all questions with students. If you attend lectures, you will surely have a good grade. There are a few tests but the answers are clearly laid out for you and he rewards any extra creative energy you give to your answers!

He always gave such great feedback on work, and was very great at encouraging participation even in a fairly low-commitment class. He probably could have engaged more with actually teaching the material but it is a primary independent-work class and he made it very enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I know what the other reveiws say, but I really enjoyed this course. It's easy to get a good grade.The structure is simple; you watch a movie on Tues and go over a powerpoint on Thurs. To some the class might be boring, but I really liked it. Prof Pillai is very kind and open to all sorts of discussion. Just participate and you will have fun!

I absolutely did not like this class. Professor Pillai makes it so difficult to follow along with anything. You watch a movie Tuesday and talk about it Thursday. You are graded on 4 things. 3 exams and the rest is attendance/participation. He says attendance is mandatory but never takes it. He's not a bad guy, just needs to reevaluate the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst class I have ever taken. I don't even know what to say went wrong, because I don't know where to start. Lectures are extremely long yet teach very little material. It is unclear what the course aims to teach. Impossible to follow.

Confusing, doesn't explain how course material is relevant or connected to the course. The class is called Media History, but he fails to make it clear if the class is about the history of media, history as depicted in media or historical media. The worst class I have ever taken.

This professor is a horrible grader I spent hours on my final paper which was 8 pages long by the way. I got a 37/100. She critiques the smallest mistakes and takes off points. I worked so hard in the class and turned in every assignment and this was the grade I got. There is a lot of lectures and videos and extra readings on top of the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very disappointed, there is a 500 word min. discussion post due weekly, along with a 300 word min. reply to classmates, citations/references for both. Additional "journal" writings due weekly along with a timed quiz (20 questions in 25 min.). Way too much writing for a criminology class. Also, only read the chapters, not quizzed on extra materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class was literally read book, write a paper, take an exam.  Every.single.week.  No interaction wit other class mates.  Exams are crazy timed (25 minutes for 20 questions) Last paper and Final Exam count for 30% of your grade. Other than weekly posts to the message board I had no interaction with the professor, all of my items were graded by a TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the better professors that I have taken at MSU. She tends to get a bad rap but I think she is great. I did not do as well in the class as I would have liked but it was my fault not hers. Take her if you want to be in a class where the professor cares about what they are doing.

At first she comes off as tough and mean but she is very likable and it nice.  Class becomes more enjoyable and it is so much fun talking.  She's tough but for a reason and it makes a better student.  I did not even notice her accent.  Great teacher! Take the class, go to class everyday, share your opinions, and read!
More than willing to help if you are responsible and you go to her with questions.
She is strict, annoying and her accent is horrible!
Overall just a great professor. It's obvious she cares about her students and teaching the course. Pay attention and participate and GRM101 will be pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's great! mandatory attendance, but classes are still fun. GRM 101 is pretty basic, so it isn't very hard. She is very nice, an easy grader, and a fun professor. It is cool that she is the only prof who is a native German speaker! would definitely recommend for any class, especially GRM 101
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: From what I know, she's one of the only native speakers in the German dept. She's super sweet and even brought everyone cookies on the last day of class. Although you don't have to go to class, seeing her is definitely worth it. Plus, so long as you do the work, you'll get an A.

Dr. Pirouz could be phenomenal if she was organized. For example: she utilizes 5 different email addresses and is slow to respond (>1 week), for this asynchronous class, she doesn't post the lecture materials, or they are incorrect / the content on the slides is Frankenstein'd from other classes, the homework/book/lectures are all disconnected.

Had Pirouz for MKT300 and 351 (351 last sem. online/asynchronously). It often takes her a long time to email back but if you text her she will reply very quickly. The course load was really reasonable and you can tell she's super interested in marketing. Overall a pretty good prof, 4.0'd and liked both her courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: To pass this class with a 4.0 you need to show up to all the lectures, put effort into the two case write-ups (one of which is the take-home final), and do well on the mid-term exam. Professor Pirouz's turn around time on graded assignments is a bit excessive. You won't know your class grade going into the take-home final with outstanding grades.

Great professor, engaging lectures and interesting topics and stories, I wish he taught more classes. 10 Pop quizzes so go to the lectures, but the quizzes are easy. He makes it easy to understand what questions are going to be on the exams and goes over those topics' multiple times. Overall, a fun and relatively easy class, I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Plaga was an outstanding professor. He truly loves and cares about what he does and in turn so do his students. Not only were the topics covered interesting but the ways he presents them keeps you intrigued, he also included his own experiences with topics as he was the former lutenist in Michigan police.  TAKE HIS COURSE!

Plaga is an amazing professor. His lectures are entertaining and filled with fun stories and his own experiences. Grading is super simple: midterm and final and 11 pop quizzes scattered throughout the course, so it's best to show up to every class so you miss one. Wish he taught more CJ courses!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This professor has been the best I've ever had at MSU, he makes lectures very fun to attend. There are quizzes and exams that make up most of the points, so just make sure you go to class. I wish he taught more courses because like I said I enjoyed having him as an instructor!

The class is pretty entertaining and filled with a ton of notes. Attendance is not required, but he does do pop quizzes, so it's best to attend every lecture. The quizzes are fairly easy since you'll take them right after writing notes for them, and he offers a good amount of extra credit on exams. Grades are rounded up if you do the extra credit.

Grades based on a midterm, a final and 11 pop quizzes done at the end of random lectures during the semester. Attendance isn't required but if you consistently don't go you will miss a lot of pop quizzes (which are very easy). Experienced in the field and directly tells you things which are guaranteed to be included on a test or quiz. Entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Plaga is by far my favorite professor I have had at MSU. You do have to show up for class but it is only twice a week. All of the quizzes are Kahoots and he drops one of them. Many opportunities for extra credit. He is very enthusiastic about teaching and uses real life examples when lecturing. If you can show up, then you will get a 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Good professor, but you have to show up 100% of the time, attendance is required since he does surprise quizzes. Some careful things to remind you about is that his version of extra credit is going to a talk show that costs +$10 and requires a 5-page paper after. If you're even a point away from a grade. He won't give you it or flex.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All you have to do to do well in this class is to just show up. The quizzes were kahoots and the exams were very easy as long as you took notes on what he said in class. The lectures are not available outside of the class so make sure you are connected to other students or take really good notes on what he's saying. Great guy and well connected.

I'll try to be unbiased, but Ken was a real peach. He knew how to teach the content and have a good time. My advice to future students: loosen up and have fun with it (try to stay somewhat professional), he won't bite unless you give him a reason to. It takes a week or two for him to open up, and after that it's the best class for CJ majors IMO.

She tells a lot of stories, which is nice until it takes up time that we could use to learn quiz content. With that being said, you should read some of the textbook, because there is a quiz every class and oftentimes she doesn't even get to the lesson. Overall, she is nice, and she grades easily, just be ready for the class to feel VERY long.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jackie is incredible! She is very understanding and super entertaining during class. I highly recommend.
Nicest and most undertsanding professor ever. Has great lecutures and relates her lessons to her real life experiences. Always brought snacks for the class every morning.
I loved Jackie- she was very accessible, and has a lot of experience so her lectures were so interesting. Very easy class if you put effort in and show up! Recommend her.
Super respectful and will help you when you ask for it!

There is a quiz per week on the required reading from the online textbook but beyond that she is very generous with her grading of the group and solo presentation and interview assignments. There are two massive midterms that are pretty tricky so beware of those. Her lectures are full of personal anecdotes from her and are informative.

The worst. Avoid at all costs, all you get graded by is 3 exams and unless you ace them you cant get a good grade and no other work outside lecture scan QR code. The lab is just lectures there is one mock exam at one of the labs thats 25 points out of the total exam grade. Absolutely worst dosent care about students success one bit.

Pontifex is honestly a pretty good professor when it comes to explaining the material, and I do feel like I actually learned in lecture. However, this class is almost impossible to study for. The exams are 30% what we actually learned in lecture/lab, and the other 70% is material that was never fully covered or not mentioned at all in class.

Lecture isn't mandatory, more helpful to review the slides on my own. Vry exam-heavy, makes it hard to earn a 4.0. USE THE QUIZZER for studying. Pontifex is decent, but some TAs can be hard to follow, and Checks for Understanding are based heavily on the worksheets answers aren't always provided, which can make it frustrating.

His lectures were great I can't lie, BUT the class is all based on exams and the "labs" are just another lecture to your week. He starts the class by saying "ill probably see most of you again next semester" which makes me sad he doesn't care enough to have his students succeed. His exams are half questions from the quizzer and half jibberish.

Content is super interesting. Study it well and there's no reason this class will be too difficult. Pontifex has an ego and not everyone liked him, but I enjoyed his teaching style a lot. He is organized, straight-forward, and uses strategies during lecture to improve our chances of remembering the content (his examples given are always great)

Students should know that Professor Matthew Pontifex really cares about helping students understand the material. His lectures are engaging and he explains concepts clearly, which makes the class easy to follow. If you pay attention and participate, you will learn a lot. He is passionate about what he teaches and creates a positive environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I think that professor Pontifex is very knowledgable in what he teaches. In lecture, he makes specific examples that make the content easier to understand. There is extra credit given in specific lectures. I got a 4.0 without getting above an 88% of a test but I also never missed a lecture or lab. I recommend reading the lecture material!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is pretty good with lecturing and knows what he's talking about but comes across kinda rude. I didn't find the content to be too bad but it's definitely test heavy and would recommend going to lectures to do well. Also has you do a check in for every class for points so those, the labs and the check for understanding quizzes are easy points

Extremely test heavy. If you do not take notes and do the quizzers, you WILL fail. A lot of the questions on the exam will be on the quizzers but there are a good portion of them that are curveballs and are meant to make you think. He does NOT post any of the slides he uses to teach the class and you're left with lecture PDFS that aren't very good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There are people with big egos, and then there's this guy. He enjoys being rude to students, and the exams are completely different from the lectures. Do not ever take his class, he is the worst.

This professor is way too full of him self. We spent multiple lectures talking about osteoporosis and it was one question on the exam. The exams are not what is covered in class and his notes are not easy to follow. Try and take this class with a professor that is less full of himself and his exams are easier.

honestly, you can tell he is full of himself and does not really care. if you have an excuse letter- don't count on anything being excused. lab was just an extension of lecture. do the quizzer but also look over notes heavy for exams. pay good attention

Definitely has his lectures memorized they're so seamless and easy to follow, which was the reason for my good grade. He makes the content interesting with relatable examples which stick in your memory.  He is part of the neuro/psych depts. and uses his knowledge to help his students. A bit egotistical but straightforward. I'd highly recommend!

He begins the first class by saying I will see most you again retaking this class. The class is difficult if you aren't putting in constant effort. He moves very fast through his slides in class and he doesn't upload them so take notes as fast as possible. Don't miss class literally you miss one lecture and its almost impossible to catch up.

Dr. Pontifex is a good professor. I found his lectures engaging and the material interesting. However the structure of the class is not set up for you to succeed. Since the majority of your grade is based off of 3 exams with no drops or extra credit, it makes it especially difficult to 4.0. My pharmacology class gave me more leeway than this.

I took his Kin 240 class as my first Kin classes last semester as a freshman and it was definitely challenging but I really loved his class! His lectures were very interesting and he had a great viewpoint on hard material to help you remember. I overall would say that he is a great professor!

Took KIN 240, do not miss class, you will fail. Lab can be hard depending on who your TA is, most of the time ends up being 2 hours. Pop quiz every lab on material learned, they can be rough. Overall, study a little after every class and you should be good for tests. Use the Quizzer online to study, it helps a ton. Good luck.

I thought that this class was pretty straightforward if you studied the skeleton notes and did the quizzer. The annoying thing about this class was how he never posted the slides or lectures. Also, in the labs, you had to take a quiz right after learning the material. He was a decent professor, but I did think he had some egotistical tendencies.

He was a good professor, but the class is tough. There's no final, so your grade depends heavily on the three exams. Use the quizzer he provides to prepare—it helps. Be ready to study a lot if you want a good grade. Attendance is mandatory and you get points for it.

Professor Pontifex was fine. His lectures were kind of boring at times but it was alr. This class is TEST HEAVY. The quizzes in labs are either easy or hard. ( mostly hard) We get no drops in anything. And the quizzes are what we learned that day.

Professor Pontifex was great. He was incredibly engaging during class. I know everyone says this is the hardest KIN course, and they aren't lying. But it has more to do with his grading criteria than the material itself. As long as you actively take notes, you'll be fine. That's why you should review review review!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pontifex is very smart and knows what he's talking about. If only what was in lecture directly correlated with exam material. There are only 3 exams and he makes a makeshift quizlet to study with, but it always felt like the questions on exams were never in the notes, quizlet, or lecture. I went to every lecture yet never felt prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think that while the course was very test heavy (most of your grade will be your tests) Dr. Pontifex and the TA's were very helpful with the material, and you can easily pass if you show up to class. Dr. Pontifex and the TA's are also really understanding and helpful with RCPD accomodations in my experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Start preparing for exams weeks ahead of time, since they're weighted so heavily. Go to lab to get points from quizzes/participation. Its unfortunate that he does not provide more opportunities to improve your grade, but focus on the important concepts he stresses in class and use the quizzer he provides and you will do well.

The class was interesting and engaging. However, your grade was based off of 3 exams. If you don't do well on the exams it is nearly impossible to get your grade back up. There are quizzes in lab and some are harder than others. There is only 45 points of participation the rest is graded.
Really nice guy, fun to listen to. The quizzes in lab are harder than the exams, exams are manageable if you use the quizzer.

Dr. Pontifex has an interesting personality but his tests are insanely easy. If you go through his makeshift quizlet, 100% of the time they will show up on the tests. His labs are easy but we have quizzes for each lab and some are harder than others. That depends on your TA though. Attendance is recorded and given for points.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pontifex can be perceived as a bad or "arrogant" guy but I think that depends on how you are doing in the class. He does sometimes say some things that makes you be like "uh.. ok?!" but it makes the class sorta entertaining. The class is only graded on 3 exams and lab quizzes, BUT if you do the quizzers and study the skeleton notes you can 4.0

TBH this class needs to be restructured especially new lab instructors. If u utilize the quizzer for the test then u should be able to do really well on the exams. But, our entire grade is based on 3 exams and lab quizzes. The lab quizzes are the hardest part the stuff we learn in labs has nothing to do with the class which can ruin ur grade fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pontifex is definitely arrogant and a little hard to approach with questions, but he knows his stuff. Very nice guy once you work up the courage to ask a question. Your grade is mainly based on 3 exams but if you utilize the online quizzer and review the "skeleton" notes you'll be just fine. 4.0 is achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr.Pontifex is extremely arrogant and conceited, and I am not the only one that thinks this. Not only is the professor awful, but the class itself has awful criteria. Don't get me wrong, the information is useful and interesting, but your entire grade for this class is based off of 3 exams. So get ready to study. One of the hardest classes ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pontifex is arrogant, but he is that way for a reason. He knows the class and teaches it well. This class is difficult, but it is absolutely possible to do well. Go to lecture, go to lab, and utilize the quizzer function in the syllabus. Many of the questions you see in the quizzer will be in the exam. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is based off of 3 exam. The first one is the toughest in my opinion. You typically have labs every week and at the end of lab, you take a quiz. Only one chance for extra credit and its worth 10 pts. Highly recommend doing it. If you don't have to take the class, I would not recommend. As long as you study the notes, you should do well.

Dr. Pontifex is a really cool guy, but the class is hard. All you do every time you have class is get lectured too, and the class is basically graded by the 3 exams you take. He's a great guy, always willing to answer questions. The downside is KIN173 formatting is not good, and you can kiss a 4.0 goodbye off of one bad test.

Prof Pontifex has very engaging lectures and is very passionate about what he is teaching. First test is the hardest, but gets easier after that. He gives three exams, and a few small quizzes. Option for extra credit paper given at the end of the semester. As long as you study and attend lecture, a 4.0 is very attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pontifex was a good prof, his lectures are entertaining to say the least but he practically gives you the notes for every lecture which is really helpful. The class is pretty much based on three or four 100 point exam grades and the rest of the grades are pop quizzes and note checks. Just go to class because you won't do well if you skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is very difficult. If you don't go to class you will be behind. The class is mostly based on 3 one hundred point exams which he does not prepare you for. There are pop quizzes and quizzes due every week. If you aren't constantly paying attention or taking notes throughout every lecture you probably won't do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This prof is extremely arrogant... not saying he doesn't know his stuff, but his cockiness is annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Freshman year I had him and it was fine. watching the lectures and showing up to the recitations is not enough for me personally. I did the skeleton notes and then proceeded to write my own notes so I could break concepts down and learn them. I feel that if you put in the effort and truly strive for an A it is completely achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: In his class, there are really only three exams worth 100 points each and then a 6 point quiz every week. His exams are very hard to prepare for since there is no book and he only posts a 40 min lecture each week. He also gives pop quizzes that are all application-based. One of the pop quizzes we took this week was about statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: At the start he gave off arrogant vibes, but as time passes I've grown to like him more. He's passionate about the content and tries to host engaging lectures. He gives fun examples to connect the material to the real world. Beware that he DOES sometimes give pop quizzes! The first exam was a struggle but by the second I figured it out how to study
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hes a smart guy and knows his stuff, but he can come off as kind of arrogant bc of this. Hes not rude, just a tough teacher and really makes you put the work in to get a good grade and doesnt just hand out 4.0s. I was frustrated at first with this guy but now i know his vibe and how this class works, you just gotta get past the first exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures seem easy at first but he doesn't prepare you for the exams at all, they are all very hard. There are 3 exams, the second one being the easiest in my opinion because I managed to get a B on it. The third final exam the class average was around 63% and I received a 76% which I was proud of. He curved the class grade at the end however.

This was one of the hardest classes I've ever taken, and I'm a Junior. Dr. Pontifex's exams are so hard it's nearly impossible to pass them. The average in the class was a 72. Please do yourself a favor and avoid this class at all costs so it doesn't ruin your GPA you worked so hard for. this class was harder than my Physiology class.

Really wouldn't recommend this course. Only total of 410 points. 300 from tests which are harder than you would expect. The other 110 points come from lab which the TAs do not grade easy on. You must go to class. Tests are confusing and meant to trick you. Labs questions are also confusing.
Honestly horrible professor and does not care about his students. He is also extremely cocky. Very hard and test questions made to trick you. Would never take a class with him ever again.

Good professor who knows what he's talking about. The exams are tough so you need to pay attention to lecture and write down everything HE says. Study hard for the first exam, its harder than you'd expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Listen to every word he says because the little things will become test questions and youre screwed if you dont listen. Most important thing is to study a lot more than you think- especially for the first exam. It was the hardest in my opinion and its hard to come back from bombing one since there arent many grades in the course. Labgo
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Clearly knows his stuff but the class is tougher than I predicted. Tests are nearly 100% application based & notes are all you have to study from. My #1 tip after taking this course would be to study way more than you think and VERY in-depth. Pontifex doesnt answer emails which is frustrating (in my experience)- also important to go to labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: avoid this class at all costs
Very good professor. Makes all lectures fun and interesting. Definitely study hard for the exams though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hilarious, very passionate about teaching and really knows his stuff. Make sure that you go to labs and do as well as you can on those because they affect your grade a lottt. Tests are challenging study more than you think you need to. The TA's are helpful, go see them at office hours before you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Extremely good lectures, if you're interested in KIN. His tests are a little challenging, but it you study outside of class a little you should do just fine. Also, do the labs, they will affect you grade ALOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: make sure you study outside of class a lot. exams are tough

I personally don't like the way that he teaches the class. He goes quickly through the lecture because he wants you to print off his notes and then fill in the blanks, which doesn't work well for me and how I study. Tests are application based and very had if not prepared for. You have to go to class to get the notes unless gotten from a friend.
He knows his stuff, very good about keeping the class interesting and giving examples and stories to remember things.

Absolutely loved him as a professor.  Lectures aren't boring and he keeps you engaged.  Connects to situations you can connect to and cracks a few jokes here and there.  Loved the material as well.  Not hard to 4.0 if you go to class and study.

Prof Pontifex is a pretty cool dude. I was never bored in class. He's clear during lectures and note taking is just simple fill in the blanks. He's young and in touch with todays generation, always manages to slip in a few jokes. Tests were sorta tricky but as long as you have the notes & actually understand the material you'll be fine.

Kin 173 is a pretty easy class to follow along with. Prof Pontifex is a pretty cool dude. I never found his lectures boring, he slides in some jokes every now and then. I thought he was pretty clear in explaining things. Tests can be sorta tricky, but as long as you get the notes & don't cram last minute you'll be fine!

Make sure you get a good TA because it will make or break you from a 3.5 and a 4.0. Class is harder than it needs to be but still easy to 4.0 if you do the work and study. Pontefix is a little arrogant at times too, but who isn't these days?

Pontifex is a great teacher. He does a good job of getting students involved and making class interesting. Rarely bored in lecture. However I felt that the lab was pretty unrelated and my TA was incompetent to put it nicely. The lab reports can be tricky, but if you take your time and follow the write up instructions you can make up for it.

Loved the professor, he knew exactly what he was talking about and make analogies and comparisons to different things to help us understand concepts. He kept the class interesting and I was never bored in class.
Go to class for notes. All easy fill in the blank notes anyway. The labs are pretty new and pointless to me, big waste of time in my opinion.

Many think this class is difficult since he added the lab for it. I did not like taking the lab portion of this class at all. If they kept the course without the lab it wouldn't be so bad. Just a heads up. The first actual lab write up is probably the hardest though.
Need to go to class for notes unless you get them from someone else.

Easy class if you go to class to fill in the notes. Lab reports can be difficult at first but get easier. Make yourself familiar with excel. Do the checks for understanding and you're fine. The last exam is the hardest by far but do well on the others and you shouldn't be to bad.
Amazing professor and pianist. A privilege to learn from him.
I had him for 147. Super great teacher and you can tell he's very passionate about what he does!
Exceptional Piano Pedagogy professor. We read from his book, which was amazing. So caring, so involved. Cannot recommend highly enough!

Such a great class in Pedagogy.  We taught a lot in this class and this was hard, but Dr. Polischuk was supportive and caring.  So even though teaching little kids is scary, at the end of the semester you're not so scared.  Dr. Polischuk is so supportive and knows so much about teaching.  This is such a great class.

Dr. Polischuk has a comprehensive understanding of piano technique, with an uncanny way of relating this information in a lesson.  Basically, you leave a lesson feeling as if you are a significantly better pianist than an hour ago (as long as you put in the work and are open-minded). Polischuk DEMANDS that you practice!
Amazing.  So Caring.
I loved working with Dr. Polischuk in pedagogy class--it was a great experience, and actually teaching children as our major class project is invaluable as a pedagogy student.

Professor Polischuk is an extremely musical and engaging instructor.  His care for his students is paramount, creating an inspiring environment in lessons and studio class.  He provides specific feedback while giving students freedom to make musical and technical choices for themselves.

Fabulous teacher, fabulous course!  Challenging, thought provoking, fun!  He led the class well, and asked us to question the process of teaching, of approaching technical matters, of solving musical questions, thoughtfully.  An excellent, involved, caring, passionate professor, with a course of real value.
An extremely compassionate, helpful and intelligent piano teacher.  His insights into technique are easy to apply.  Take lessons with him if you can!
No Comments
Unbelievable class!  Inspirational professor.
No Comments

Would not recommend. She assigns an overwhelming amount of homework and excessive reading every week. The workload feels unreasonable and hard to keep up with. She's very strict and the class is unnecessarily difficult. It's more stressful than productive, and there's little support or flexibility for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: The instructor had very high expectations, and there was a heavy workload from start to finish. We had extensive reading assignments each week, frequent papers, and multiple group projects that required a lot of coordination outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Disorganized, unhelpful, and difficult to follow. The professor rarely responded to emails and gave no clear feedback. The exams didn't match the material, making it hard to succeed. Would not recommend.
She was very knowledgeable and gave really good advice. She was also very caring towards students and understood if a student needed more time for projects. I highly recommend taking a class with her

She is not a very good explainer at all. She either over-explains things, or doesn't explain them at all. She often seemed rushed. Also you don't even have to do the homework as it is not for a grade. Very quiz and exam graded. Overall would not take her.

Overall Professor Powers is a nice woman and you can tell that she cares, The way she structures her courses as far as quizzes doesn't necessarily set students up for success.  There have been too many occasions where she's rushing through class notes running out of class time. It tends to throw off other students who are trying to keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is fine. Teacher is a little weird and explains weirdly like over explains easy stuff and doesn't explain hard stuff. Gets mad if people don't answer her questions aloud or if you try to leave class. she also speaks to students like they are 5. Overall not bad teacher just annoying

She was the only reason I passed 103A and B. She is a bit aggressive, but only because she wants you to succeed. She always makes sure students know what they need to be doing and her husband is a counselor so she always offers you to talk to him. She makes it clear when the tests and quizzes are. Go to office hours and MLC. You wont pass without.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It is not Professor Powers' fault that MTH103B is formatted in a way that speeds through units during the semester. She tries her best to accommodate students in and out of class, but sometimes, due to the content, it's difficult to get help on specific units. Overall, a helpful and caring professor with a challenging course. Would take again.

This is for MTH103B. Content is much more complex than 103A but the amount of time given to learn new concepts is much shorter. She jumps from concepts to concepts and there will often be times where  you will have to learn and master something within a few days. Good resources for studying but requires a lot more effort than 103A.

Anyone can learn and master the topics. Starts out slow with basic high school concepts and builds upon those (almost everything relates to functions and graphs). Will walk everyone through steps and offer help. Quizzes/exams are short, can be specific in grading criteria at times. Pay attention & attend class you will have a VERY easy time.

You are not graded on homework at all, so if you do wonderful at homework but horrible at quizzes (like myself) then prepare for a hard semester. She teaches at a fast rate, each class meeting covers a new subject, regardless of whether or not you've comprehended the last one. Talking to her/asking her questions is an intimidating experience.
Professor Powers was super nice, def a little odd, but always willing to help! If I paid attention I probably would've eaten the class up (MTH103B), had her for A and B and loved her both semesters.
Super rad lady, who goes out of her way and makes connections with students. Rushes through lessons with little to no explanation. Tries her best to help students.
all around not a good class. you learn a new leason before your quizes and nothing in class is on the exams

Powers is a good prof, but the class moves at such a fast pace its kinda hard to keep up. Very quiz heavy, I don't think the homework was graded at all. All homework and quizzes were online, except for exams and the occasional in-person quiz which we had like four times. Her handwriting is kinda sloppy. Not that hard of a class though

Professor Powers was really nice to everyone, but she's a little weird. The class isn't hard, but you do have to pay attention and put in the work to do well in the class. She stays after class to help you with anything you don't understand, is quick with emails, and posts all lectures online if you miss them or need to really work on them.

Powers was great. As long as you study the material you will do fine. She records all lectures and posts them to study from and go back to if you're confused. She also somehow gets to know every one of her students' names, not sure how. Very nice and easy to approach if you're ever confused or have a quick question about the course. Would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this professor for two semesters and found her teaching style okay, the way she explained the material wasn't always super clear and honestly my friend in the class taught me half of it. The extra blank lessons help, it seems boring but if you do it with a friend it's not bad. The homework isn't graded but the quizzes are.

Honestly one of the rudest teachers I have ever met. Do you have a question after class? Sorry she wont answer it, instead head to her 8:30 am office hours to get it answered. Oh, but it's a really quick question? Too bad. I had an issue with the grading on an exam, brought it to her attention, left in tears. overall pretty bad. teaching is mid.

I really liked her as a person but not as a professor. She explained things in a way that was very confusing and contradicting to what she previously taught. Will not answer questions unless it is during her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is a great class for somebody who is already good at math. She goes incredibly fast so it's really important to take notes. An ok teacher if you really dedicate your time to the class.
Powers is a decent math teacher but she's hard to understand at times because her handwriting is kinda bad. There's better math teachers in the math department.

I took 103a and 103b with her. The class is fast paced but she provides all the lessons as recordings and also materials to practice. She is a very caring professor and will somehow learn everyone's name. Definitely recommend taking her but be prepared to put in work!
Nice teacher who genieunly seemed to care about her students picking up on the material, MSU math grading policy for the course made it easy

Powers is a regimented professor and can be repetitive, but personally that is exactly what I need to succeed in math. The lecture will move quickly if the class participates or she will have long pauses waiting for a response. Webwork is very important for this class, but sometimes the questions won't have an example from class to follow.
