She definitely tries her best but definitely feels more like a high school teacher than a prof. lacks empathy for students and often explains things to the point of confusion.

This professor is nice, she will sometimes over explain things, but try her best to make sure everyone understands, she try to talk and connect with students to see how they are doing in the class. You will need a calculator, she does get upset about those, otherwise is a good teacher.
If you skip class, you won't pass. Does not have a lot of empathy towards students, but honestly I think she is trying her best to be the best she can be.

This class requires effort. She goes through material very quickly, but does provide videos of the lectures and completed notes. Pay attention and do the homework and practice questions and you'll be all good. A lot of material is in this course so she isn't able to slow down much. Be prepared to seek external help if you struggle a lot in math.
she is a terrible teacher. has no empathy for any of her students. is very unfair.

Over explains things to the point of confusion but if you just zone out when you see it coming you're good. If you watch the lectures and do the work, not much at all, you should ace this without a doubt. Even if she does go fast, she explains everything so in depth that you cant miss anything.
She moves way too fast and seems like more than half her class doesn’t know that material, but she doesn’t care. Very nice teacher just not a great one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Powers is the worst professor I have ever had. She doesn't care when we ask her to slow down, and she is impossible to learn from. Everyone I know in this class, is not going to pass. I do all the homework, go to class, study, get tutored, but all the efforts I have put in will not change the fact that she is a horrible professor. Worst professor .

She moves extremely quick and always over explains everything to the point of confusion. Doesn't acknowledge when students ask her to go slow or go back.(DONT take if you have ADHD!!) She will always refer you back to the syllabus for any and everything and that her only answer. Quizzes and exams NEVER match and no opportunity to redo missed work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: only way to do good in thus class, is to do good on all the quiz. she teaches pretty fast but overall she not that bad. sweet lady

She goes through material very quickly. She ignores students when we ask her to slow down, or repeat the info. When we try to ask she just says go to office hours. If we do go to office hours, it's crowded and your questions won't get answered. If the majority of the class did very poorly, she won't give a curve. She also won't review before a test

She definitely is demanding during lectures and goes very quickly so be prepared to pay attention. Print the notes out before you attend lecture that way you can follow along. Basically it is just a review of high school math and what you see on the notes and practice quizzes is what is on the final exam.

Attendance is only mandatory for recitation, going to her lectures made me understand concepts even less than when I arrived. The webwork was way more difficult than what was in lectures and quizzes, but at a similar level to the exams. Highly recommend using the webwork to study for exams as opposed to practice exams and notes bc they're harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not the best professor. Goes through lectures very quickly (do not take Powers if you have ADHD!) and has strange ways of explaining things. Very caring and accessible outside of class but be prepared to teach yourself. Webwork is very difficult and never on the exams. Quizzes are easy but exams are hard.

Took 3 years of algebra in highschool and only got a 2.5 by .98%. I basically taught myself the whole class. Would get 80-95s on practice exams and self assessments then would get 65-75 on exams... only thing that really saved me was having a good TA.

Ive never witnessed a class anything like this. Every lecture did not make any sense and left students confused every time. Even though many kids struggled and had very low grades the professor failed to show that she cared the slightest bit.

If you love math and are good at it this class won't be a problem, however if not, then you have to really work hard for it. Powers always moves really quickly and does not stop for student's question. Her final exams are kinda hard but if you go over the notes, and practice exams you would be fine. Also her handwriting is not the best .
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class sucks! She is a nice lady but she rushes all of her notes and doesnt explain anything throughly. I aced College Algebra in HS but this was terrible. Putting a bunch of students who failed the math placement test in a lecture hall where they cant ask any questions in asinine. Not a very good teacher and not a good system to begin with.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I went to the MLC, very often and failed majority of my exams. Even after I did all of the practice exams. WARNING the practice exam is wayyyy easier than the real exam. I suggest that you look up every concept on YouTube. That's how I ended up passing the class.

Powers herself wasn't awful, she seems like a sweet lady but she sometimes gets upset in the middle of lecture and lashes out. She goes pretty quick so be ready. Also, it's really hard to read her handwriting at times. Most people just skip lecture and get the notes online. Exams are way harder than practice exams, especially exam 2, so beware.
Very sweet, no B.S. kind of professor. easy math class to start college with.
Super clear, sometimes moves quickly. Doesnt have time for questions but is nice as well.

She's alright but she should really get some new pens. Her handwriting isn't the best and she uses markers to write which just makes it worse to read through the projector. Is always shushing the class even when no one is talking. Always starts class a minute before class time. Isn't the greatest but I just needed to get a good grade and I did.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hand writing is horrible- can't read it. Goes very fast. Ended up with a 3.0. She is an average professor.

goes fast on notes & will get through at least 3 or 4 lessons done in lecture, doesnt stop for questions & handwriting is pretty hard to read, so if you go to lectures you have to actually listen to what she says. webwork & quizzes are super easy & your best bet is to stud at least two days before an exam
Lol, terrible teacher.

Powers is an alright teacher, but Math 103 is an awful class. Who thought it'd be a good idea to throw kids who failed the placement exam in a lecture hall where you can't ask questions? Powers goes through notes extremely fast & doesn't care if you understand the material. The quizzes and webwork aren't too bad, but the exams are MUCH harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Powers was a good math teacher! You should go to class, because her lectures are pretty dense and she goes through the material very quickly. The first two tests of the semester were the hardest and the last two were the easiest. The homework is tough and WebWork based. She usually assigns one set of 10 homework problems every week.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's really nice and caring, and even brought us candy before exam week. Even though she goes pretty fast, her lectures are okay and easy to understand. You're given lots of recommended problems to do in the book and actually doing them will help you understand the material on the tests which aren't too hard if you pay attention and go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a great professor, gets things taught efficiently. She refers to the class as "boys and girls" but not really in a condescending way. You'll have a TA to teach your recitation and grade your tests and quizzes. Powers makes some quiet jokes and plays them off, that's really funny if you pay attention.

Granted I'm not the best math student to begin with, but this class wasn't easy. If math isn't your strength be prepared to work hard in this class to get above a 3.0/3.5. Powers isn't very approachable and isn't enthusiastic about answering your questions. She comes to lecture, dictates the notes, and thats that. You'll have to work hard for a 3.5
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She explains things pretty throughly most of the time, but sometimes she goes super fast and then super slow. She is really moody and you never know how she will act. She has yelled at kids for asking questions and is constantly saying "be quiet" when the classroom is silent. Overall a pretty easy class, but she isn't the best.
Explains things in detail

She's overall a really good and in-depth professor. She really assists and go over material with you if you are having trouble with it. Exams are pretty much similar to what you've learned in class, just attend the class and you'll be good.

I'm not a fan of math by any means, but with the right teacher you can do very well. Professor Powers is a good teacher, but I didn't hardly show up to lecture, so I did pretty poorly in her class. Not a good idea to skip, otherwise you'll be scrambling as I did. Great professor, though she is slightly belittling.
Great teacher, she'll go through an specific topic and explain it thoroughly. She'll joke sometimes and try to make math a little less tedious. Overall, she made math interesting and fun.

Attendance isn't mandatory for lecture, but is for recitation. Being a math class, lectures are extremely important. Lessons are put up online and you should print them out before the lecture. You take notes the whole time and she makes the work pretty clear. Easy to 4.0 if you put forth the work. Do the homework problems before quizzes & exams.
Lost of people are quick to judge due to her niceness. If you attend to class and pay attention you'll get an easy A. She's pretty funny and tries to have a stress free class.

The class is hard (coming from a non-math person), 5 credits, 5 days a week. But, Powers is great. She is very clear, makes the best of the huge lecture situation, and obviously cares about her students doing well. She understands math is not easy for everyone and would explain every step of of every problem -  no one was ever confused due to her.

While Mrs. Powers is very good at explaining math, she treats students like they are little kids.  She regularly calls students "boys and girls".  She also tends to baby-talk and she doesn't use the correct terminology all the time.  Exams are a lot harder than the quizzes but there are a lot of help rooms available!

Her lectures were really good, she was very clear and knew how to explain the material. If you listen close enough you will catch an unexpected joke, which always gave me a good laugh. I dont recommend that you ask questions during the lecture though, I have seen her lite a couple kids on fire. But overall really a nice teacher.

Mrs. Powers is a fantastic teacher, this is coming from someone who HATES math with a burning passion. She made it much easier to understand and he explanations are always very clear. She loves what she does and I think that translates into what she brings to class. :)
She was an okay math teacher, very clear but she lectures like she is speaking to small children, which unfortunately people act like in the class.
Great math teacher, best one I've ever had. I did really well and I'm horrible at math.
She knows what she's talking about, but she lectures like she's speaking to small children. If you can handle that, you'll be just fine.
She teaches really fast and when I raised my hand to ask a question she told me to hurry up.
Lectures as if the students are way younger than they are. Didn't really mind though because her explanations are good and I did well in the class.

She's a great teacher. Although she doesn't like talking to students one on one before or after class, she writes her office hours in addition to other important due dates or MLC reviews on the projector each lecture. VERY clear explanations. I'm awful at math, but she made it easy and ...fun?
She knows what shes talking about, but she tends to drone on a bit.
Clearly loves math and knows what she's talking about! One of the best math teachers I've ever had.
Solid. Nice lady. Cares alot about helping her students.
She's awesome! It's so funny and awesome how much passion she has for math. Best math class ever!
She acts like everyone has some sort of learning disability, its almost as bad as when a teacher acts like we're all rocket scientists. Go to class, don't ask questions and you'll do good.

She is the first math teacher I have actually understood! One of the best professors here at MSU. Engaging and relevant lectures, clear homework instructions, and cares about students. Make sure you attend lectures.
so kind and i love her and her classes. she doesnt believe in exams which i agree with. a queen

Her lectures are very engaging and each quiz per week follow with the lecture videos. Its important to do all connect assignments since this course is heavily based on assignments and readings. With no Exams at all!!
Prof Sullivan is such a warmhearted individual. She actually wants us to learn and it is evident through our assignments and her grading procedures. I wish more professors were like her!

Sullivan is by far the best prof at MSU. She cares about her students a lot and she shows it with every class. Not to mention she is very funny and makes the class laugh, which makes lectures fun to attend. Take her if you can!

Amazing professor, gives tons of extra credit and no one grade is going to massively hurt you. Her online lectures are actually well-thought out, the slides are genuinely helpful, and the quizzes directly pull from them. She also actively takes feedback on what activities actually help teach the content, take this class with her if you can!

I am glad to have taken this course, with one of the best professors at Michigan State. Professor Sullivan truly cares about how her students learn from her course setup and asks for input on how to improve and help students receive the most from the course.  I can't recommend her enough. if you can take her course jump on it you won't regret it!
Wants you to succeed, really enjoyed this course.

Professor Sullivan is a great teacher for Marketing 300. She allows the class to be structured how the students want (fully in-person, hybrid, fully online, etc.) and allows us as the student body to choose what we want out of this course. She gives a weekly quiz and discussion posts, but you'll be set as long as you go to class and listen.

Hands down the best professor I've had at MSU. Really interesting lectures (even though it's a boring topic) and a great person who genuinely cares about her students. I wish I had more classes from her. Workload is reasonable, but she won't take any excuses for missed deadlines.

Passionate and down-to-earth professor. Yes, his class is hard, but Ethics in Health Care is extremely relevant and important. I learned so much in this class, and that is why I'm enrolled in university.

I personally really enjoyed having Reese as my professor. This is his first class, so I'll give him the benefit of the doubt. He is extremely intelligent, especially in his field of study. This can make it hard to keep up. The class is really boring, but interesting. The quizzes are a lot, I will say. How am I supposed to get a good grade?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Is new to this so I think that's part of why this class is so hard, I don't think he really knows how to navigate it. Nice guy, but the structure of the class is not great and the quizzes are based on what he perceives from the text...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: There's usually 2 quizzes every week and the questions are made up on his own. 50% of the final grade  is based on two exams, which can be difficult if you don't do well on them... classes are usually boring.
I would say more but the guideline doesn't allow for it, just expect to read every other week, you have to buy the textbooks, and remember the most minute details.

Lectures are extremely long boring and unorganised, he doesn't seem to know the due dates to his assignments, very confusing. Even if the entirety of his lecture wasn't him just loving the sound of his own voice and telling you how much of an intellectual he is, I still could never find anything he "taught" interesting. Performative Final Boss.
Lectures are long and boring. This class is a class that most people take for an IAH requirement so it feels too strict and high stakes to actually learn.

Rachman's main focus is that you know how smart he is; nothing else matters. He can be funny and engaging, and he loves to drop in pop culture references every change he gets, but if you have a funnier narrative, what you get is a teenage boy who wants to forever impress his mommy!

If I could say one thing about him, it would be that he needs to acknowledge that his prerequisite classes are not that interesting to most people that are required to take them. He was also a little unorganized when it came to due dates and it's obvious he likes to hear himself talk. Overall the class was easy, but had lengthy and boring content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Rachman was great, you can tell he loves his job. He got to know students and would often remember things we wrote or talked about. He gives informative yet fun feedback and is quite forgiving in terms of grading. It's a reading heavy class, a new text or parts of a book every week, there are some good films in there too. All around a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took professor Rachman's 221C course and loved every minute of it. Fair warning: there is a lot of assigned reading, most of which are stories and not textbook reading. In this course we were mainly graded on papers and attendance. If you show up and write the papers well you'll have nothing to worry about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Rachman is so smart it's almost unbelievable. Pop culture is such a fun and interesting English class, I would highly recommend it.

Professor Rachman is, to put it simply, the professor you envision having in college. He's funny, caring, and energetic through lectures. He sees potential in his students and gives grace to them when it is needed. I absolutely loved going to every class and hope I can take him again in the future!
Best professor in the English department and it's not even close. He cares so much about his students.

Honestly a really good professor who cares about listening to his students and making sure they are engaging with the material. Most of the class is discussion-based (so do your reading) but Rachman likes to hear himself talk so he'll prompt you on what he wants to hear. Really easy to talk to and accessible outside class. Quizzes are super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: ENG473A Literature and Medicine- Understanding about attendance if you make effort to reach out or participate on Zoom meetings. Talks a lot just for himself but he does say a lot of thought provoking things. Grading is kind of vague and he dates himself sometimes with things he says. Very good with literature analysis and is enthusiastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goated professor who made dense readings understandable. Best professor in the English department.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Rachman is extremely kind and knowledgeable. His class was interesting and the books we read were amazing. I really liked this class. The workload is reasonable and professor Rachman was understanding and worked around deadlines. I would definitely recommend you take this class with professor Rachman.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best profs I've ever had.

This was an online class, so things may be different normally. Prof. Rachman was a good professor. If you read the books and take notes you shouldn't have too many issues on the quizzes once you get used to his style. He did assign a fair number of essays, but wasn't overly harsh grading them. Class was a bit political, but that's college profs.

Dr. Rachman is incredibly smart and assigns interesting readings. His assignments are occasionally difficult, but his grading is reasonable. If you have any issues with the course, I highly recommend speaking with him about it. I found him to be very accommodating and fair.

Rachman was a pretty chill guy. I took ENG 342 Readings in Popular Literary Genres online during the Summer with him and it was a pretty interesting class. His topic is detective books. The readings were pretty interesting and got better as the class went along. The online lectures are a little boring but not too bad. Overall I liked the course.

I've taken multiple classes with Steve. He's extremely supportive and is always willing to give advice. Go to office hours! You need to read the books and articles to do well on quizzes and to be able to participate. Highly recommend. My favorite prof at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Ranchman is too smart too teach. Loves to hear himself talk and I'm convinced he dresses up as Sherlock Holmes on the weekends. Attendance is MANDATORY, i had word during his class and he was super pissed about it. There is a quiz ever week on the books and they're tough, so be prepared to read a lot, or use spark notes lol

His lectures are really hard to take notes off of. I just stopped listening about 2 weeks into the semester because I was getting nothing from it. But attendance is mandatory except for 3 absences so I had to go to class and sit there and work on other stuff.

Overall, Professor Rachman is a decent guy. He likes to hear himself talk, but he knows what he's talking about. He's really interested in popular literature. He assigns a lot of readings, even though it's a 100 level course. The exams are difficult, as every question has answer e.) none of the above and f.) all of the above. Be prepared to work.

Professor Rachman is a superbly intelligent teacher. His study in the class of character and philosophy is incredibly interesting. His assigned readings (though there are a lot) are perect for the topics he wants to explore. His is not a class you want to take for a blowoff, but if you want to work a bit and explore a lot take a class with him!

This professor has no interest in facilitating meaningful discussion.  The second a student makes a statement he connects to in some way, he interrupts and inserts his own take on what that student just said.  He seems to love the sound of his own voice, because he answers his own questions again and again.  Where's the meaningful learning?

this class blows and will continue to blow if  taught by this prof again. this is no reflection on the character of the man, but if i wanted to, i could get by without reading the books for the class since he spends the entirety of his lectures READING THE BOOKS OUT LOUD. really frustrating, but if u need a flashback to forst grade, go for it.
The class and work load suck but Rachman is extremely entertaining and hilarious!
Love the class and Rachman too.  Super nice and helpful.  Let with a little crush and an B, but I had to study to make the grade.

Alot of info in lectures and only shows slides for split second so being an expert note taker is a must. Exams need to be studied for. Attendance is 40% of your grade, however, he gives little assignments that graded strictly which are included in that 40 percent, overall a very philosophical class.
Most confused I've ever been. Very confusing teaching style

Earlier I rated them way higher, I take it back. The entire year they told us that the 4.0 cut off was a 90 turns out it was a 93% they have absolutely no idea how they wanted to run this class because the syllabus changed every few weeks. Such a waste of time class.

This was honestly a really stupid class, with the syllabus changing throughout the year. It became easier to 4.0 but every time a new grade is put in you're stuck at the grade you had before the syllabus change. We have no tests, instead we make our own exams. It is an easy class but a waste of time class.

This professor cared too much about making the class a "safe and happy" atmosphere more then the actual learning of math. they also were so unhelpful with answering questions and graded super harshly. there were no tests tho

Im not going to sit back and say this was a hard class because of content, bc it wasnt. But she is extremely disorganized, which makes it hard. Grades are due tomorrow and I still have several zeros in my gradebook that have not been taken care of after several emails sent, just not a teacher u want. RUN far away. Most disorganized class ive taken.

Most unorganized class I've ever taken. Took 2+ weeks to get any accurate communication bc the professor kept reusing last years D2L posts. Everything is graded with an AI, including the weekly essays, your peer evaluations, and the feedback on your essays evaluations. Yeah, it's as insane as it sounds. Prof doesn't even use an MSU email. BEWARE!

This was one of my worst classes ever, even online. Totally disorganized, lectures, assignments, & essays posted randomly and graded late. Kritik's AI detector was unreliable, and students were penalized for things they couldn't control. Does not respond to emails with concerns. Avoid taking this with Rhodes.

The most unorganized course of all time. Professor never updates grades (MONTHS late). Horrible grade transparency due to extremely unorganized D2L. Poor communication. Minimal effort to teach. Uses Kritik for students to grade each other, so she doesn't have to. Useless class. MSU should be ashamed and embarrassed to offer a class like this one.
Most horribly organized class I have ever been a part of, my high school teachers fresh on the covid shutdown did a better job.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Horrible, politcal & doesn't know what she's doing. Syllabus took more than a month to be updated from last semester. A LOT OF HOMEWORK (reading, quizzes, discussions, Kritik (another discussion website that takes 3 weeks for each module), takes forever to respond, grades based on what AI says, or simply takes all semester TO put in grades. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Genuinely one of the worst class experiences i've had.
unorganized
due dates always wrong
assignment due on thanksgiving. 
all of our discussions were very political. 
if you're a good writer good luck, cuz she uses inaccurate ai detectors to grade and gave me a zero for ai even though i didn't use it, and refused to use own her discretion to grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Most unorganized class I've ever taken. Emails ignored, discussion questions answered weeks late, and we had to pay for Kritik even though no grades were ever posted. Constant due-date mistakes.. even had an assignment due ON THANKSGIVING. Nancy Rhodes should not be teaching. TA was no help either. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Discussion posts are political every single time, due dates do not match the syllabus, organization in general is terrible. You have to use Kritik, where you will grade other students work (and not be paid a professor salary) as well as grade how other students graded your work 😃. Genuinely cannot believe this class is real.

The work is simple: take quizzes, post discussions, and write short essays. The organization and maintenance of it, however, was the absolute bare minimum. Multiple assignments were set with due dates from previous years, grading is not updated until the end of the semester -- and often times incorrect -- and emails were never answered.

Couldn't tell if I was taking a political class or an advertising class. Every discussion post somehow involves politics? Makes you buy an online course so that you can grade other students work and other students can grade yours. She never updates the grade book. By far the worst professor I've ever had avoid at all costs.

This professor was professional and responsive in the online asynchronous CAS 110 class, which included six essays and weekly quizzes. While the content was useful, the class wasn't very engaging. SONA extra credit was offered. More professors are available in spring, but for fall online, this is the only option, which could be improved.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Grades NOTHING, makes you buy a online platform for OTHER STUDENTS to grade your work. She never has to lift a finger, her lectures are old and hours and hours long. Does absolutely nothing to make the course interesting, engaging, or fresh. This was my least favorite course I have ever taken at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: quizzes are worded completely differently from the readings that they're on. I think she does this so that students can't command f and search the readings for the answers but it makes it so confusing to know what part of the reading she's referencing. There are writing assignments almost every week and you have to read other students papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Really great professor, she makes what can be a pretty dull business law course fairly interesting. She almost always lets you out 20-30 minutes early. Her exams are pretty hard and you don't get enough time. Marks down for not attending but doesn't give points for it. Doesn't post slides which sucks. Weekly quizzes but no homework
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Ross is a great teacher. She likes to talk about current events as well which is helpful to be able to understand whats going on in the world if you dont have much legal knowledge. The weekly quizzes are easy enough but I wish there was more time given for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was required for my CJ, I was hesitant at first. Throughout the semester I realized that Prof Ross is a really great Prof. She cares about what she's doing. She is really laid back. All the exams have been online, and she will let you out of class early. The class isn't too hard, just some weekly quizzes.

I have always wanted to go to law school and study corporate law so I found this class to be very informative and captivating. Professor Ross is nice and laid back. Our tests and final were given to us online and the only homework we had was a weekly quiz due Sundays. She is not good at giving a heads up if class is cancelled though (minor detail).

She is such a laid back professor. All of our exams were online. She lets class out like 25-30 minutes early every time. Not much homework, just weekly online quizzes that are not too challenging. She made business law my favorite class this semester. Highly recommended.

Rhonda is AWESOME! She is a great professor and she's pretty funny in class. You need to read the book to do well on exams since she usually gets side tracked in class and she doesn't post the lecture slides. She explains the material really well and has really great examples. I would definitely take GBL 295 again with her.

Not a great instructor and does not teach the coures. The LA's run your learning experience. The course is designed for you to teach yourself the material and have the material learned before stepping into class to apply that knowledge. You get 3 different ones in the span of the semester and they may not always be good
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Richard himself comes off as very disrespectful sometimes. In terms of his class, it relies heavily on self teaching yourself the material, then coming to class to work on problems in a group. You get graded individually on how the whole group performs, and there is 3 group projects that they grade way too harshly. Pray for a good group.

This class is a TA run class! He runs the class in a group work setting where the entire class is working through problems with an assigned group. The TA's are all young and from what I've seen respectful people. The one interaction I had with him he was pretty stingy but the problems he creates for class are normally funny/interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class is quite difficult, but if you study, watch the videos and pay attention you should be fine. TA run, so you don't really interact with Dr. Hallstein, but all the interactions that I HAVE had with him where always positive,

I took PHY 183 and enjoyed the class; it's run great. You interact with the TA's 90% of the time and most of the time they're very helpful. Help room is such a great resource since this class is difficult. However, during every interaction I had with Richard, he was rude and failed to answer any of my questions.
Good professor, you mostly interact with the TA's, who are all very helpful.

The class can be a lot of work and a bit difficult, but the professor was great! He was very welcoming and clear in explanations during office hours and was always ready to help during class if he could, although its usually guided by your ULA. I enjoyed him and would definitely retake his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: PHY 183 is an awesome class. If you show up to class and participate, you are pretty much guaranteed a good score. Richard provides quite a few extra credit opportunities as well. There are weekly home works, 3 group projects, and non cumulative exams. Should be an easy 3.5 or a 4 with a little bit of effort.

This was easily the hardest class I have taken yet at MSU. Hallstein is a good professor and gives out extra credit opportunities, however I did the accelerated version and only took it in 5 weeks and it was EXTREMELY DIFFICULT. The syllabus says 30 hours a week and it did take that if not more. Expect your entire life to be consumed by this class.

I took the P cubed physics which is all group base. I had Richard as one of my TAs with one of my groups. He makes everyone feel not smart and if you do not know something he will point you out for not knowing it. He expects you to know it when he teaches you nothing. He will give you a bad grade if you don't know the answer to questions he asks.

You have to watch the lectures outside of class. You whole grade is based on group work and exams. If you get stuck with a bad group, you will not get a good grade on the group projects. You can't even switch groups. The ULAs grade you and help rooms aren't that helpful.

Take prof Hallstein's physics class! It's a group-based class and there's no lectures or taking notes. The grading scale is very generous with much of the weight being on homework and in-class assignments. And the final isn't cumulative. Not to mention Hallstein is a super nice and caring guy. Also, the help rooms are awesome!

Richard is a great professor and genuinely cares about his students. The grading is super easy as the prof sees participation and learning as more important than straight up tests. If you start homework early you'll be fine, lots of help rooms. The material is difficult, but the professor wants to see you succeed and is always helpful and kind.

While this was an exceptionally difficult course, I took it over half a summer and still got an A+. This professor is fantastic and genuinely wants you to pass, he offers at least 7% extra credit, yes 7 extra percent to your grade for his physics 1 and 2. I often found myself rewatching lectures but that is my only complaint.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Richard for EMP-Cubed. I went into this class dreading E&M and came out absolutely loving, it actually made me want to ULA in the course for next semester. Highly recommend this class if you have the option! Easy 3.5-4.0 for a class that's usually difficult. Exams are a little difficult but only account for 30% of your total grade,

Don't even get me started, man. He literally didn't explain anything, didn't give us any material for outside class, and literally just went over examples without saying why he was doing things or anything. It was all online, so that made it even worse. He literally didn't even care that everyone was failing. It was a total mistake and disaster.

Hallstein's lectures are badly explained and he is unconcerned with whether students actually understand the material. The class average of our second quiz was around 50% and he said that was normal, not accepting any responsibility that we did poorly because he taught poorly. If you ask a question, you will get a half explanation at best.

Terrible professor. Clearly did not for teaching. Often got angry about questions he deemed not worth his time. Puts less effort into teaching than most students will need to put into learning in this class. Gives short, rude answers when emailed. Many people I spoke with hated this prof. I don't know how I'll get through PHY232. Trust me!

Overall I liked the organization of this class, but it was very time consuming. There was no final exam, but rather a final "reflective paper" which was very easy. Quizzes every other week as well as homework every week. I used Chegg a lot and it did seem to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: There's so much EC which helped a lot in that class so definitely do all that and use your *web resources* on the quizzes. No exams just 6 quizzes and one gets dropped. No final exam, just a final paper which is so easy I wrote it in 30 mins and got 100. Lecture videos seem pointless though and I learned nothing

This class was SO easy online. There were no exams or a final exam, instead you did an easy final paper. There were 6 quizzes that were exactly like the quiz prep questions, which was great! Everything is on loncapa so no $ spent. There are bonus questions in the pre-recorded lecture videos. Homework is also super easy! Attendance not required!

Extremely boring class, but taking it over the summer is great since it lets you focus on that subject and you get a years worth of material done in 3 months. Definitely worth it but it's NOT fun. It was one of the hardest classes I have taken at MSU, but the extra credit helped and having a friend (study buddy) in the class with you also helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: TAKE ONLINE PHYSICS WITH HALLSTEIN!! You won't regret your decision. Bonus homework points and correction exams both help boost your grade in the course. Take all practice exams and put them on your cheat sheet, the exams are modeled mostly after those. Also put formulas and how to use them. Make a good cheat sheet and you'll be all set.

The deadlines for the summer online class for homework was insane and I emailed him to make them later since I work 9-5 and they are due at 5. He just emailed me one word: no. Also when asked questions he just said look at the book. Dropped and took it the next semester with a diff professor and did well.

We had an exam on a Tuesday from 9PM-10pm. I had surgery the next afternoon and the corrections were due on Friday. I asked him if i could get an extension because i was on extreme narcotics, very out of it. He said No i will not because it has been open since Tuesday night @10pm and you should not have waited until after your surgery on Wednesday

Here's the thing. Hallstein's good guy. But taking this class? WORST MISTAKE OF MY LIFE. The first 3 exams are pretty straight forward, do the practice exams and you'll be fine. But the final for this class messed us up. His TA should be fired tbh. When asked a qn, he says "check the lecture". Waste of my money & time. Better off avoiding

Took online over the summer, lots of homework that takes a while to complete, I looked at the book 3-4 times, the midterm was only 13 questions but 50pts but there are corrections that help a little, the discussion posts on homework were sometimes helpful but took a long time to get a response most of the time Probably better in person than online
Great professor, work is heavy but not undoable
Professor Hallstein is a very nice and respectful teacher. I had him the physics 170 (lab) and he was very understanding and explained everything if I had problems understanding things.

I had Richard for P-Cubed PHY183 & got to work with him one-on-one. Super nice guy&offers lots of extra credit in P-Cubed. Explains things well & really cares about students &their level of understanding. I would definitely take his class again. If at all possible, take P-Cubed for PHY183 with Hallstein and Irving! Seriously my favorite class ever!

DO NOT TAKE ONLINE. Hardest class I've ever taken. The only helpful thing is the discussion allowed on homework problems. Takes FOREVER to explain problems in videos (and you can't skip ahead or go back). TAs were far more helpful than he was. Almost no equations are given to you on the exams. Homework requires a ridiculous amount of time.
He is one of the best professors I have ever seen.

This guy has probably been one of my favorite professors. The easiness isn't max only because physics material is a bit harder, but he makes it easier to understand. You can tell he's really passionate about physics, and does demonstrations in every class. I'd retake every physics class with him if I could.
Attendance is only mandatory for clicker points. He is super easy! You don't even need to study to pass the class. Just put a little effort in and you could 4.0!

you need to watch all the lectures, i did most of the practice problems and got 90+ on all the exams. they are fully open note, so if you keep up you will be fine. funny guy and made me laugh a few times, i wouldn't listen to the other reviews. it'll take some more time than other classes but its all online so its no problem
everything is on McGraw Hill, he explains it all nicely in the videos. Each assignment is like 5 questions and exams are open book 25 questions

Don't take this class if you're not a great test taker. The final (which he gives NO review for) is worth 25% of your course grade. Also, the other exams are worth another 40% of your grade. Don't count on the Exams being anything like the practice questions either; he purposely formats them completely differently, so you are caught off guard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rimer is not a professor but rather a "face for the course". The lecture videos are outdated, and with only 8 graded assignments, students are expected to learn entirely on their own. There was little support provided, no practice exams, and almost no guidance on the final exam format or content. A required course should not be this unstructured.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a hard class for no reason all application problems of excel and even the vocab problems don't make sense. Exams make up 65% of your grade but as they're MCQ one question wrong tanks your grade. around 2-3 hours of work a week

This class is fully online, so be sure to stay on top of it. HOWEVER, even though I watched every single lecture, did every practice assignment and hand took notes, it was a rough class. You get your lowest exam dropped, but its a 20 question exam worth 225 points so do well. Not my toughest class, but not a breeze either.

This class was honestly not helpful at all, I don't think finance can be taught online. The videos were not enough and we had to teach ourselves excel. Chapter assignments are graded harshly , and exams are difficult and have a lot of rules . Not a very understanding professor , no ec or grade bump. Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures give so many hits for whats on the exams. He goes through each excel model and explains how they work. If someone says he's a bad professor, that student was at harpers too often tbh. Rimer is a great teacher and I would take another one of this classes. I did the assignments the day of each exam and got a 4.0.
Long video lectures with no slides. Exams are tricky and make up most of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I read lots of reviews from this class that freaked me out just make sure to take the exams(he might give you extra credit just for taking the exams)they are open note but proctored so make sure to take good notes from the lectures! When emailing him he responded pretty quickly as well do the class assignments and pre test it will help your grade.

Professor Rimer seems to be a nice guy, but when the exams are only 20-30 questions getting 1 or 2 wrong really hurts your grade. This being my second finance class taken at MSU this class is significantly harder. Just be ready to study alot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's chill and funny and the homework is manageable. I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took FI320 for my business minor. He explains concepts in an easy way to understand and gives lots of examples. The tentative schedule is easy to follow and helpful. Practice problems are optional, but help a lot with assignments. If you read and watch lectures, you're gonna learn the concepts. Would recommend taking this before an ACC class.

He bases your entire grade on 3 exams and 5 assignments. He also forces everyone to buy an expensive textbook that you barely use because he creates videos for every small piece of information, in which the slides he uses are not available due to "people just using the slides instead of watching the lectures." He genuinely cares about his students doing well and will do whatever he can to help you to understand the material.

Edwards is the BEST math teacher/professor I have ever had. He is really good at making the material easier to understand and cares if you are learning the content. Lectures arent mandatory, but I always went because I loved going (mostly because of his dad jokes). He made me develop a new appreciation for math when I have always dreaded it.

I LOVE DR EDWARDS! I had him my first semester of Freshman Year for Calc I and he is the best. He made calc so understandable! Go to his office hours, email him! I highly recommend this class to anyone! The only reason to buy the book is for access to the homework code. I never read a page of it besides review for the tests.

Best math teacher in Lyman Briggs. He is super nice and always have something interesting to add to the lecture, making it not just math based. This was probably the only math class I've ever learned interesting history in along with the math concepts. The class was also very easy if you had already had a calculus class prior.

I typically struggle with math, but he is the best math teacher I have ever had. Something about the way he taught just made so much sense to me, and if it didn't he would always explain. He was a godsend of a teacher, especially since I had no high school calc experience. I 1000% recommend taking this class with Edwards, amazing guy & teacher.
This class is absolutely worth it. He makes Calculus interesting by describing the historical reason for why the topic was created: makes it seem like the stuff you do in the class is worth learning.

Dr. Edwards creates such a pleasant atmosphere within the classroom that all my worries went away and I was immediately set at ease. You can tell he really cares about calculus, and he also usually adds jokes or funny historical stories to lectures. He definitely goes out of his way to make the class interesting, and was very approachable as well.

Dr. Edwards is so good!!! My opinion is you shouldn't ever take any other professor for calculus, especially at Lyman Briggs. Super easy fun class. I usually hate math but I loved this class and he made learning calculus fun! Very engaging and enthusiastic and funny! Lenient grader and has a very cute baby daughter.

Dr. Edwards is really funny and his power points are extremely helpful when studying for exams. He lets you get up to 50% of the points you missed on the exams back which can really help your grade. He gives you review problems before the exam to help get you prepared. He tells funny jokes and is a great professor. Would definitely take again.

Dr. Edwards is a professor who I respect highly, not only for his teaching ability but for his heart and soul. He has so much passion for math and its history, he really takes a (in my opinion) boring class and makes it into an engaging lesson. I would highly recommend taking his class, he is amazing in and outside of lecture. And he bakes cookies.

Dr. Edwards loves the material he teaches, and he wants you to love it too. The WebAssign homework is not very difficult, and exams are almost identical to the reviews. If you do the review problems, go to class regularly, and pay attention in class, you will definitely pass with flying colors.

He is such an awesome professor and I would totally recommend him. He made Calc 1 a breeze which is very hard to do. Don't waist your money on a book, its pointless. I never once used mine. All of the homework is online and fairly easy. He also has fun math stories to share along with math jokes along the way to keep your interest.
He makes the class really fun and his tests are very straightforward. I would definitely take another class with him.

Rob is absolutely amazing and took the whole class out for ice cream after our final exam. As a non-major I never acted a day in my life (and I'm still extremely bad at it) and I still 4.0d. He grades based on the growth and effort you put in, and doesn't dock points if you're extremely anxious.

He is absolutely amazing. He was hard on me in the beginning because of something I missed, but even then I could tell he wasn't being mean, he just wanted me to focus on what was important to me and to work for it. He is a wonderful teacher and everything he says is clear and helpful. I learned more from him than any other teacher this semester.

He was great, not a challanging class and attendence was cool because you had 4 no shows and then he only took 1 point away for every class you missed which isn't much. exams weren't to hard. he was funny and chill, played music which started our mornings good.

Rob was genuinely one of my favorite professors. You can tell that he cares for his students. As long as you complete the work and participate this class is a breeze. I learned a lot in this class about myself and how to deal with stress healthily and made many friendships in this communicative class.

Professor Rob was 100% my favorite professor this year. He genuinely cares about his students and will help guide them through assignments. His classes are very discussion heavy, but the class environment he creates is so welcoming, that it feels like your opinions are welcome and accepted no matter what. I highly recommend his THR 204 class:)
Directing is the best class ever. Don't forget to do the reading though.

Best theatre professor at MSU. I personally don't have any interest in directing but took the class since it's a requirement, and it was way better than I expected. The readings were actually interesting unlike the other classes I've taken, and the way he runs class is super fun and open-ended, so you get to create whatever you want.

Rob is hands down the best professor I've ever had. I'm no longer continuing with theatre, but would take this class again regardless. He gets to know you as an actor and as a person and is 100% supportive of you in everything you do. As long as you show you care and put in work, you will 4.0 the class. Brings out something special in you.
Such an awesome person.

The best teacher in the Theater Dept, hands down. Knows his stuff but will push you harder than any other professor to achieve success. Never cuts corners and can be blunt, but you will get more from his class than any other
Best professor I've ever had.  Has so much professional experience with Theatre that he is the TOP guy to learn from.  Utterly hilarious and I look forward to his class every day.

Dr. Schwab is one of the best professors if you are starting up the Math Major. I took MTH 317H and 327H with him and he gives very good lectures, and focuses a lot on mathematical intuition rather than rigor. If you do well enough in the Homework and Exams, a 4.0 is practically guaranteed. However, I would look for other professors after 327H.
The class structure is near perfection, would take it again 11/10 times

Prof. Schwab is absolutely the best. I had him in my freshman year of college in my first math class (317H). He was so kind and caring and urged me to believe in myself. When I thought I would fail the class, I ended with a 4.0. I did not realise that I actually enjoyed Linear Algebra and Proofs until I took 317H with him!

Brilliant Professor with wonderful lectures. Teaches slowly for students to understand and explains questions clearly. Homework is graded with a focus on improvement rather than completion and perfection. 10/10 would recommend to a peer!

317h is one of the best classes I've ever taken, and Russell is an amazing professor for it. His lectures are amazing, and he goes very in depth and is always willing to answer any questions. While the class is certainly difficult, he makes it feel much easier and fully supports you through your learning. He also provides the textbooks for you!

One of the most understanding and helpful professors I've met. While his lesson plans moves a bit slow (covered up to matrices only in LADR), he takes the time to help students improve proof-writing techniques and etiquette, and focuses half the class on developing intuition for mathematical proofs than on just linear algebra. Highly recommend!
This man is great. He deserves good ratings, especially the chili.
He is obviously very smart and is really attractive. Grading is definitely fair
As a Food Science major this class was very easy. Just pay attention during lecture, and you'll be fine. Dr. Walker is great to talk to and I enjoyed his lectures.

This class wasn't hard as a food science major, but it could be for other majors. The lectures have a lot of material, and a lot of it isn't even tested anyway. Lots of fluff. He does bold what will be tested though. 7 free absences is nice, and attendance isn't a huge chunk of your grade anyway. Tests are all MCQ, but worth a lot, 60% total.

I didn't do well in FSC, but I am not a food science major. The exams were pretty hard for me and even tho I went to every lecture, I still never got above a 60%. A few discussion posts and online quizzes. Online textbook. He was nice, but the lectures weren't very engaging. He just read off the slides word for word.

I enjoyed the class the quizzes are online and exams weren't too difficult if you study a bit. There's a chance for extra credit which I appreciated. Attendance matters but you get some absences so that's nice. I skipped a lot if I showed up everyday it would've been an easy 4.0. If you show up everyday its a piece of cake and you'll learn a lot!

So he barely teaches and just reads off slides. Every lecture is information overload and the exams are very difficult and he barely provides help to students. There is never a study guide or practice exam and he doesn't even give exams back. The grade is a few quizzes and then three massive exams. Would stay very far away.

Dr. Walker is such a kind and passionate professor. This class was 8 weeks and was difficult, but it is very manageable and he is very approachable and responsive. He cares about his students learning.

Dr Walker is an amazing professor! He has lots of past work in the field and is very excited to engage with students. Class was very easy, show up for lectures and glance over the readings. Quizzes online every other week. He is always great to ask questions to after class, he has a very clear passion for food science and his students.

Dr. Walker is an awesome professor with tons of industry experience. The HACCP class is incredibly applicable to any future career in the food industry. The certificate earned at the end of the course is valuable to anyone entering the industry. The final project is tough, but mimics what is done in the food industry, providing real experience.

Professor Bellon is very kind and knowledgeable regarding the class material and surrounding information. For STEM majors, his class may feel slightly reading heavy and you will have to work in groups with peers. His lectures can feel (and often are) quite long, but they are tolerable. Overall, I would reccomend Professor Bellon and this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Overall, a great professor. While this wasn't my favorite class and lectures can run long, the material is often interesting and thought-provoking. The course is reading-heavy but very doable, and key ideas are reviewed in class. He grades generously, offers extensions, and clearly cares about student success, even if a bit repetitive at times.

While he is fun to talk to, there is a heavy workload of things to read before majority of the classes, such as 8 chapters of a book. He also is very strict about talking about class related stuff during group work, felt like I was in high school again. PARTICIPATION is a big deal, and be prepared to read lots of articles

Professor is very talkative and can get super annoying. Very long lectures and talking with no break. He just runs his mouth about the information and none of it sticks because his voice is super annoying. Attendance is mandatory and you can't sign your friends in. Would never take this class or professor if you paid me.

Everyone complaining about reading and writing in this class is just... It's completely doable. The articles and books weren't hard to comprehend, especially considering we discuss the key themes in class before and after we read them. Disliking Dr. Bellon for wanting his students to be actually engaged in class is an interesting take for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: very hard not to do well in this course even if the topics aren't really interesting to you. it can sometimes feel disorganized but not in a way that will make it difficult to finish work. lectures can get wordy and hard to follow but i enjoyed this class nonetheless. Deadlines and expectations are made very clear, overall very easy.

Every class period I sat on my phone after doing his pointless work hoping a car would crash into the building or the fire alarm would go off hoping that just maybe we would be able to leave early. This is the most time consuming class for how unimportant it is. Genuinely makes you feel stupid paying tuition for a class like this
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: You know when someone talks forever even though it could've been said in one sentence? His entire lecture is like that. And it's not even really a lecture. he just divides people into groups to work on a Google document. He yaps for the first ten minutes, then spends the rest of the time wandering around the classroom. Good exercise for him!

This professor was pretty great and you can tell he cares a lot about students actually learning. He is pretty lecture heavy and attendance is required but there is always opportunities to make up assignments / extenstions or make up attendance points missed.

waste of time. long lectures and makes you stay the entire time for attendance. yaps the entire class about useless stuff. doesn't actually teach anything besides how using ai is bad for your brain. dreadful and boring to sit through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!! Take any other iah there is, if this is the only one open, there's a reason why. He talks so much, and he is very boring. There is so much work compared to every other IAH class. Listen to me, do not take this class.

reviews.comment: do not take this class he just yaps the entire time and the work is pointless. make friends because you need a group to work with every class. 4 essays which are annoying but not that hard. mandatory attendance and two hour long podcasts every week. don't take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: everyday i walked to class i wish i got hit by a bus. do not take this class. the only good thing is that i made friends that i could talk to everyday. so much unnecessary  work that takes forever if you actually do it. a total of four essays that are many pages long. easy class but takes too much time for it being mandatory. take any other iah.
