reviews.comment: Lectures were pointless made us read 2 books that were a waste of time. Weekly notebook entries on 3 plus readings a week. Not a super hard class just a lot of busy work for a class that has nothing to do with really any major. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: While this class isn't hard, you should only take it if you love writing and want to submit an entry every week. Attendance is mandatory and you will work in groups every day. He spends a large majority of the class yapping and doesn't really "teach" you anything. I've gotten nothing out of this class. It's a bunch of work and reading for hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Holy yapper of yappers. He makes you stay the whole class time even when everyone seems to be done. He will talk about random subjects to keep you there longer. Every class you need to fill out a paper about an episode guide that itself takes 40 minutes. At the end there is always a group writing assignment. Absolutely horrible to sit through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice enough guy, but the class is extremely droning and repetitive. Likes to talk about personal issues in the world. Nearly every lecture there's a paper and the recitations seem very thrown together and unstructured.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Bellon is nice, but he tends to go off topic during his lectures. If you want to take a class about the dangers of AI, this is the perfect class for you! If not, then I would steer clear. You get 5 skips total, and there is a LOT of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor was nice but the class was a lot of work. It was constant reading and writing/reflecting. Also participation matters in the class and counts towards your grade.

Doctor Bellon was amazing! His enthusiasm about what he teaches in class is inspiring.He gives weekly announcements on D2L of everything that is due that week. He wants his students to succeed and takes his time to proof read and revise our essays. I can say out of all the teachers I had he wants to help because he has a passion for what he does.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Y'all hating just because it was a lot of work, I loved his class. I feel like a learned a lot, the papers were fun for the most part, and his mini-lectures before the group work were consistently appealing. He taught me more about writing than WRA 101 ever did. 

At the very least, this was good weight training for the rest of college.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I would never take this professor again if my life literally depended on it. He assigns an unruly amount of homework. No thought in his head to people having an actual life because he assigns 5+ hours of work a week. what's crazy is he expects his students to care as much about his course when it has nothing to do with our major, WASTE of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bellon is very enthusiastic about what he teaches. There are three books to read and have to create a podcast with like two other people (not that bad). Also the final has you connect all the readings and podcasts you've done. He does grade fairly and on the higher end. It can feel overwhelming but overall it was doable and I had 18 credits.

You could tell that Bellon really cared about what he was teaching.. however, you have to read three very thick, often very difficult to digest books throughout the semester and write some pretty heavy papers. This class consumed a lot of my academic time just reading. I would only take this if you have spare time, like reading and get bored often.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He waste peoples time, All the work is online and he stills requires you to attend classes when you can be doing something else more important

This class is very writing and reading heavy. You are required to read three books which are so boring. The lectures are also pointless and have nothing to do with the books you read, while recitation is only based off the books, I felt like I was taking two different classes. Bellon also won't allow you to see your grade the whole semester.

The class itself wasn't hard, but it was rather boring. Most of the learning is done outside of class, making lecture seem pointless. The material, such as the required books, were boring and often tedious to read. The class itself is extremely writing heavy. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. IAH is suppose to be a social science class, instead he decided to change the topic to biology and technology. I HATE BIOLOGY AND TECHNOLOGY. You have to write multiple papers about science, specifically influenza. I was about to throw up writing them and especially reading the EXTREMLY BORING books ur forced to read

Bellons Iah 206 was not hard, but I see many places for improvement. Such as actually making lecture useful. This is the worst lecture ever and all learning is done out of class, you will only learn on your own. Yet he insists on making sure you showed up to waste your time. also refuses to post grades and makes you email him an essay to see them
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Bellon's IAH 206 course is a mixed bag. I was surprised by how interesting the course material was, and Dr. Bellon's passion for it was a breath of fresh air. Unfortunately, his lectures feel like a waste of time. The lecture activities consist of repetitive group work with no real engagement. 100% of the learning is done outside the lectures.

I had Dr. Bellon for LB322A and he was condescending and didn't act like he cares about us learning, more about showing much he knows about Brave New World... He has no gradebook, so I had to calculate my grade myself. I had pry to find out what was wrong with an essay because he didn't use a rubric and graded it subjectively...

There are 3 readings, where you need to write a short essay on the chapters every week. There are 3 5-page essays and a 10-page final which are exhausting. Bellon has lectures, attendance is mandatory but also has 1 hour-long lectures online (2 a week) which are required for a grade and to be used as evidence for your essays.

This class was not worth it! So hard and so much reading! The midterm and final exam are really really hard and takes so much time. In lecture Bellon does not even teach. You have to get into groups and write on a google doc and that is the study guide. This class was awful. Do not reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Richard Bellon is possibly the worst professor I have ever seen. He refuses to show you your overall grade, rambles on about unimportant information during lectures, provides useless busywork for you to do in groups while at the lectures, chooses the most boring books known to man for his readings, and overall just wastes the time of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a lot of homework for this class but it is not hard. Bellon is easy to work with and responds to emails relatively fast. I would definitely recommend taking IAH 206 especially because it is worth 4 credits and the work could be a lot worse for this class.

Professor Bellon is super nice and funny. Lecture are split with and group work. You read 3 books and write 4 papers. The workload isn't bad and lecture's are fun. If you put the effort in and pay attention to the podcasts it's an easy 4.0! I would definitely want Bellon as a professor again, he is understanding and passionate about the topics.

Overall, Bellon is an amusing, caring teacher in the lectures he makes you group up with people around you and work on an in-class assignment. However, there is a lot of homework outside of class including readings, podcasts, essays each week from the readings, and intense exams that involve writing multiple essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The grading depends on your TA. He is pretty chill and hilarious. There is lots of reading though. You should attend meetings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of reading and videos that need to be watched before class every week. Lectures are mandatory but overall easy if your TA grades generously. However this semester he did not turn grades at the end of the semester and did not notify students or return emails

The class itself I didn't care too much about, it was a required elective and the lectures I didn't find interesting. The professor himself was amazing. He was so nice, so willing to take feedback, and would always work with you if you ran into problems.

A solid prof and a solid class. Do the readings if you want to get more out of his class. Lectures can be long and confusing, and the final involves a lot of memorization- so start making a study guide for it sooner rather than later so you aren't kicking yourself during finals. Go to his office hours and get feeback- he's very helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He can talk lots of stuff on lecture and never give you powerpoints. If you're trying to do well on exams, you need to organize the important historical people and events he mentioned in class. However, I tried so hard on exams and papers, but tough grader only gave me a 3.5 in the end. Their grading rubric is just decorator, they grade with mood.

The final paper, a very significant portion of the grade, could be negatively influenced by not showing improvement from draft to final. Doesn't matter how good the writing was, apparently the 'process' is what really mattered. Final exam was based on lectures that notes were never made available after the lecture, so no review. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You will need incredibly unhealthy amounts of caffiene to stay awake in this class, as it is the most boring lecture I have ever had the misfortune of sitting through. Dr. Bellon will drone on and on about topics that are sometimes not directly related to exam material. He is a tough grader and if you require an IAH class, avoid 206 like the plague
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is extremely hard to pass if you don't go to the lectures, which are very boring!! Weekly "Notebook Entry" assignments (short essays on the required reading), 3 term papers (you can choose 2 of the 3 to write), midterm is painfully hard, final was even worse. If you can avoid this class, please do yourself a favor and choose another IAH!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: By far the worst class I've taken thus far at MSU. Did well on papers (87%+) and managed to 2.5 the class. Anything below an 84% in the class and you're in trouble. Although it is clear he has passion for the subject, his lectures are painfully boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: took this class because it seemed the most interesting of the IAH's. I was wrong. Not interesting at all. A ton of repetitive material which was super annoying. You can tell Bellon is very interested in the topic but doesn't present it in a very interesting way. No electronics what so ever in his class (phones, computers, etc). Doesn't post lecture
Very well-prepared lectures, expectations for class were clear from the beginning.  Pushes students to higher levels of achievement. Only complaint is excessive use of the phrase "sort of".

Discussion was poorly lead and only a few people dominated the discussion and did not give a chance for other people to speak up. Participation is part of the grade! Other than discussion the class wasn't bad i was just uninterested in the topic.
I like his class but he gives out a lot of papers to write which is very stressful.

Best professor ever. Only professor to take the time to learn EVERYONEs name and did review sessions Q&A style till 9pm sometimes before exams. Class was decently difficult but he was a fair grader and let you submit regrades on stuff you didn't like the grading of. 11/10 prof

Amazing professor who is always available and is very engaging and passionate. His class is pretty difficult and the tests he gives are a decent challenge but earning a 4.0 is not too bad because of three test retakes.
Can talk fast at some points during lectures, but overall a very good professor. Cares about his students and wants them to do well.

Dr. Sweeder is a great professor who truly cares about teaching his students. He was super nice and went out of his way to learn everyone's names, which really means a lot in a class with 60+ students. His lectures are great, he is super good at explaining concepts and making sure nobody gets lost. One thing I'd say is that his exams are difficult.

Dr. Sweeder is awesome! So many opportunities to do successful in this course. He does exam retakes, group exams, many easy assignments for points, and even drops your lowest exam grade. It is pretty easy to stay focused during lecture, and he explains the material very well. It honestly is quite hard not to 4.0 the class!

I enjoyed this class. You get to leave whenever all of your work is finished. Be sure to go to class & do the skills modules. There are pre-lab notebooks to do before lab and also pre/post lab quizzes. Dr. Sweeder is AMAZING and he floats around two sections of lab. Great prof and be sure to build a relationship with him! ULA's lead the class.
Dr. Sweeder taught LB 171 very well. He is very approachable and gives out good advice, especially on office hours. A 4.0 in his class is very achievable if you put in the time.
Kind guy. Good prof. As usual for Lyman Briggs, content must be learned BEFORE class, which personally I like, although it makes class harder. Funny.

Sweeder was hands down the best prof I've ever had. He's super funny, takes time to help students, will make alterations to his teaching if needed, and is such a helpful professors. His office hours are a life saver; I went to almost every one. He makes a super hard class very manageable and will be there to help. All around, he's the best!

This man was my absolute saving grace for chemistry. I considered myself hopeless at chem and was ready to take the L, but Dr. Sweeder made it very easy to reach out to him. He was always available for questions. He gives out good study tips for his course and college courses in general. Bro is the dad of the chemistry department at LB.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr.Sweeder this semester and I have to say he was my favorite. The class itself was somewhat difficult, however, his lectures and positive attitude made learning easy. He posted study material online which made me feel very prepared for the exams. Overall, amazing professor! Take his classes if you have the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Sweeder is one in a million. Don't pass up the opportunity to take any class he teaches. He is a great professor who makes sure his students understands the material and will take the time to make sure that is the case. His class may be on the more difficult side, but his positive attitude in class makes up for this fact.

Dr. Sweeder was one of my favorite teachers in the past couple of years. When the class heard that he wasn't teaching the next semester they all were upset and begged him to teach again. The classes are engaging, and he truly cares about the students. When the class did poorly on an exam, he took responsibility.

Dr. Sweeder is such an amazing prof! He does a really good job of explaining concepts in a multitude of ways so that everyone can understand. He also cares that students do well both within chemistry and in life. Awesome prof!

Dr. Sweeder was hands-down one of the best professors I had this past semester. He genuinely cares about his students and will do whatever he can to help you out if you are struggling. If you are taking LB 171, I highly recommend that you take it with him!

Dr. Sweeder gives awesome feedback to you when you have questions. I learned a ton and retained a ton of information from his class. Instead of straight lectures you collab with a group to work through concepts. Tests are not overly hard, but they do make you think. Homework was not crazy either.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class and the material aren't always easy but Dr. Sweeder is funny and will make time to talk about whatever is needed. He is accessible and gives good feedback as well as presenting the material well. Attending lectures is always helpful and use the mastering chemistry to practice for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Sweeder is amazing! The tests can be pretty difficult however, he is always willing to help out and make sure you're understanding everything! He is super sweet and funny and a wonderful prof to have for this class:))
Great professor to have for such a difficult topic. He was always upbeat and made learning a little less dreary. Plus, he gave out candy when you answered questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Sweeder was my saving grace! I had him for LB171L but went to his office for help with regular chem lecture stuff. He is so nice (intimidating at first) and went above and beyond in helping me out. I had never had any chem before LB171 and he is SO good at explaining thing- I honestly could not recommend him more. He's also pretty funny.

Dr. Sweeder was a pretty good professor. He is very smart and can seem intimidating at first, but go to office hours and get to know him because he is very helpful. His tests are hard, but if you study and understand the material FULLY then you will be fine. Know how the "Why?" and "How?" of everything as there are lots of explanations on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ryan Sweeder is a relatively new professor in Michigan States college of Lyman Briggs. He talks quickly and can be intimidating during lecture if you fall behind on the content in his class. This being said, if you attend his office hours you will soon realize how helpful and intellectual he can be. He cares about his students.

This class is difficult because of the amount of material, but he teaches it very well. He is a tough grader and expects an A to represent excellent understanding of the material. He is very kind and always willing to help, but the exams are challenging (yet doable). Wants everyone to do well but really challenges students (in a positive way).

Exams could be challenging but manageable. Lectures were very straightforward at a fast pace. Very accessible outside of class. Office hours were basically a second lecture, if you go to these consistently with a group of friends its like extra study sessions. Would sometimes Zoom me for twenty minutes to explain concepts. Best teacher.

reviews.comment: Really great lab prof. Always explained things and taught me a lot. Really personable guy and I even learned some lecture topics from him. Seems like a great professor.
He is not a very good teacher. He tends to write things on the board and just expect you to know it. If you want a good professor switch into Cass right away!

Dr. Sweeder is a great professor and teaches the material really well. He is super helpful during his office hours. His practice exams are very similar to his actual exams and he normally has a review session before the exam which is really helpful. He also tries to relate the material to whatever is happening lab that week.
Dr. Sweeder made chem easy and interesting. He's a great dude
So attentive to students, very approachable, and tells his students what to expect in terms of exams (his practice exams are great). You will have to STUDY, but it is not AT ALL unreasonable.

He was always sure the class understood what he was talking about before moving on to a new topic, and he was the only Briggs chem professor that used demonstrations in his lectures, which really helped in understanding and visualizing what he was talking about.
Dr. Sweeder is a little more vague than Dr. Laduca, but he's still better than Shay. He's really easy to approach and a solid lecturer, and even can have some humor at times.
Sweeder is the best Lyman Briggs Chem teacher. I have sat in on other lectures and he is the best at making things hard seem simple, and his tests are fair.. you want him!
Easy to understand if you go to class.

Sweeder is the best professor I could ever have! I took him for two semesters because he was so great! So chill and easy to talk to, and if you go to office hours he will know your name, and is extremely willing to help you out. Great letters of rec coming from him!!!
Helpful and funny -- great class and instructor!
really funny in class and easy to learn from
Very clear, fairly easy class if you pay attention (and still pretty easy if you don't).

I've had a very hard time following Sweeder's lectures and notes. Not only that, but he seems to go out of his way to "trick" students on quizzes and tests. Some have great success with Sweeder - I just haven't been able to.
Honestly one of the best professor. He taught what was needed to know and if you go to class and put in the time for the class you should have no troubles.
His class isn't as difficult as Laducas. He is a good professor and is willing to help if you ask for it. Chemistry is still my nemesis but that's my fault.
Sweeder and Laduka are the best briggs chem profs. Sweeder is probably slightly easier than Laduka though. One of my favorite freshman classes
Extremely easy professor. show up and study, you're bound to pass the class. He is available for help, and makes chemistry interesting for you. He also has a great sense of humor

Like everyone said, he is very easy to approach.  He does examples in class (on the board and actual physical examples).  He is very easy to get in contact with if something is wrong.  Pretty easy to do well if you have had chemistry before.  If not, it could tend to be a little harder but not impossible.
He's pretty cool.  Just pay attention and do the homework.  And STUDY!
If you've had experience with chemistry before, he's a decent professor, he tries very hard to show how applicable chemistry is outside of textbook examples, mildly funny in a cynical way as well.
maybe I just don't like chem, but I have never been so confused in my entire life!
very easy to approach
This man needs to learn how to teach! But he is easy to approach, though we think he looks like a giant flamingo.

A great professor. He's also the advisor for all geography students. The class itself has no exams, but does have assignments and group projects. There's also guest presenters such as public, private, and nonprofit sectors; MSU career services; and grad school. GEO 480 is intended for geography majors. Non-majors shouldn't take it.

Grades based on weekly quizzes, lectures were just reading off the slides on D2L, but iClicker gave extra credit for an easy 4.0. super sweet and caring professor, chill guy, but the class is basically self-paced.
iClicker counts for extra credit, easy 4.0

He is very nice, and I found this class to be very easy. It is based on weekly unit quizzes(open note, two attempts), and I got full points easily. He uses iClicker, but it can be done remotely, and he gives extra credit if you answer correctly. Lectures were boring and not helpful, but the content is interesting. Basically self paced.

I took this class as an elective. I learned how to do weather analysis and forecasting because of this course! When criteria or instructions were unclear, he was always available to give clarity. The only thing that would discourage me from taking this course again is the hard labs and quizzes. Other than that, I'm glad I took this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was based on reading assignments and quizzes, and if you didn't do all the reading assignments, you probably won't get higher than a C. The quizzes are open book but still make no sense due to the wording he uses. I went to about 6 classes due to the lectures not being helpful. I can barely tell you anything I learned from that class.

he seems like a nice person, but he just reads from the slides (that don't cover much despite the quantity) and doesn't answer questions. he offers no clarity on topics, very scientific language, and is hard to understand. i passed the class but couldn't tell you what i learned and i actually went to the lectures and did all the work.

reviews.comment: This class was okay and easy but boring and I never actually attended class. Professor Shadbolt was always super nice but I am not sure anyone would want to take this class unless they have to or they have an interest in weather.

Shadbolt's mild temperament and good nature show through his teaching.  He does as much as possible to offer students the benefit of the doubt and allow them to get work done in their own time. I think his class format is unique and very effective for a motivated student, but can be difficult if you're not good at scheduling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Very nice guy. Quizzes are open note and directly from reading and lecture slides. Easy 4.0 ISS, he's the best.

I really enjoyed taking Dr. Shadbolt's class! He gives clear and straightforward lectures and I never thought that I would be interested in reading a textbook until I took his class, because the readings he assigned were very interesting and I learned a lot from this class!

Really cool guy. The textbook content can be confusing, but his lectures helped clarify my understanding. I'm not sure what these other reviews are about, he really knows what he's talking about when it comes to lectures. Yeah, it is a lot of reading, but it really is not that much work outside of that. Definitely worth it, definitely take it.

Fantastic Professor for this class, clearly knows a lot about the material he is teaching (Meteorology), and clearly answers questions when prompted. There are also weekly quizzes with many extra credit opportunities, and no final exam. Overall seems to care about his students, and I am glad to have taken this class.

Graded on 12 quizzes (14 in the semester), and the content is difficult and lengthy. However, for a 4 credit class, it is an easy 3.5-4.0 and not much work. Quizzes were open note, which helped greatly in being successful. Would recommend taking this class as a ISS 300 prereq. After a few quizzes, you begin to understand how they are structured.

reviews.comment: This class was awful. The entire thing was graded on 12 quizzes, which lectures didn't prepare for since he basically rephrased the textbook. Eventually I stopped watching lectures and just studied the textbook and got better grades, that's how bad lectures were. If you want to learn this stuff buy the textbook, it's a better teacher than he is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please do not take this class. You are only graded off of 12 quizzes throughout the whole course. All he does in the lectures is read the slides he provides through D2L, and the content is heavy. If you are not interested in the science/details/statistics behind climate change, this class isn't for you.

By far the worst class I've ever taken. Class is graded on quizzes and nothing else, which is a lazy way to run a class. The lectures don't cover the material on the quiz but just talk through the textbook sections without anything from the professor added, a lazy way to lecture. The bottom line in this class is lack of care and it sucks.

Great professor and advisor, especially for first semester at MSU GEO Dept! Super nice guy and very intelligent. Cares about his students, his profession, and is understanding and thoughtful. Overall a wonderful guy!

Capstone course for geo majors, no exams, 2 group projects, and a few individual assignments that help with career. Replied to emails quickly, accessible outside of class. Most of the class are peers presenting or guest speakers, and the prof talking about upcoming assignments or the book he goes over in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was next to impossible. 4 exams and then participation points based off quizzes. The tests were HARD. Literally sentences out of the book and charts that you had to go back in the book and reference across 3 chapters and 120 pages of content for each exam. In order to do even decent on the exams, I had to outline THE WHOLE BOOK. nice man

Extremely tolerant & patient & respectful. Decent lecturer. Keeps self-promotion of his work to a minimum but it's still very slightly annoying. D2L somewhat poorly organized. Projects take up a LOT of time, beware. Pretty good feedback on projects. Strange attendance policy. Most material probably could be independently learned from Scott McCloud

STA201: Loved this class. LOTS of work depending on how ambitious you are. Show up to class even if you don't have the project done. Chime in during discussions. It's always been a dream of mine to make comics and this class has let me do that. 
Btw you don't need the course pack if you're a digital artist. Ames lettering at most for one assignment

Honestly, it's the participation. As another rating said, if you are even 30 seconds late he will mark you absent. I was 1 minute late once, and I walked in and he had already started lecturing. He doesn't even wait for class to start to take role. The class is also focused heavily on time-management, but it's HIS time management. Not good for all.

He obviously knows what he's talking about, but does so in a way that is accessible and down-to-earth. If you're interested in exploring the comics medium or diving in to improve your work, the comics courses with Ryan Claytor are a great way to go. Workload is a bit demanding, but I've never experienced another class that made me feel so proud!
Great teacher! very fun class and easy to talk to

This professor will mark you late for being a minute off time a class period after he was five minutes tardy himself. He loves to advertise to his students, and will add ads for his own personal benefit to your homework assignments. If you show up loving drawing, you might hate it by the time he's done with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Excellent teacher. Dedicated, respectful, knowledgeable, and well prepared. Makes the extra effort to make lectures interesting.

Ryan is amazing! He pushes us as actors and will take you out of your comfort zone in the best ways possible. There is some mention that this class was to much for people, but if you really care about the work (like you should as an actor) this is a class you will flourish in. Ryan will forever be my top 2 acting professors at MSU!
NOT THR201 but For IAH241E, Easy class, watch a film each week, do a quiz and discussion post. couple papers throughout the semester. Overall, good but he does take some time to grade which sucks

reviews.comment: Ryan is the best acting teach that I have had so far. Ryan keeps us on our feet and makes sure we learn from this class. Obviously we have to memorize and work on scenes with partners or individually, but that just makes sense. Couldn't imagine a better professor for this class. He loves his craft and is dedicated to teaching us the best material.
Ryan is really good at giving feedback and is fun to learn from. Participating in class matters and just make sure that you come in prepared to work!
Worked me to the bone in this class but he was the jumping off point I needed for my confidence to grow as an actor.
Film acting 2 was crazy hard but one of the most worthwhile classes I've taken, he definitely improved like crazy over film acting 1. Definitely grew as an actor.

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst professors Ive had at this university. His classes are a poor use of time management.

I had her for WRA101 and she was amazing. The sweetest human alive and you can tell that she really cares about her students. I would go out of my way to take a class with her again. This class was stress free for me for the entirety of the semester.

I had her for WRA 101 and she was amazing. The sweetest human alive and very understanding. She is very relatable and cares about her students. I would go out of my way to take a class with her again. This class was stress free for me for the entire semester. She tries to make this class as fun as possible.
Super understanding and caring, and you could tell she genuinely loves her students. Made the classroom feel like a safe space and was super helpful on projects.

(For WRA101)
The sweetest professor I've had this far. Cares so much about her students and truly will shape the class depending on us. All group projects that were ok and easy to deal with. Do not worry about this class one bit.
I loved the teacher.. She cares about you... I had her in WRA 101
she really cares about you. I had her in WRA 101. She is the best professor

I felt he was very disrespectful. The most BORING professor at MSU. He encouraged attendance for an 8:00AM class on MONDAYS when literally all he does is have students discuss with each other rather than him do anything to actually teach the class. I had lots of problems with group work. My group submitted a project with little/no communication and took my name off of it. The professor was not helpful, even with all of my evidence for doing some work, and never notified me of anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Schwartz's class. He was a fairly easy grader and he explained the assignments decently. His course is heavy on group work and the assignments seem never ending, but once you get used to it, it's nothing. His class wasn't my favorite but It was enjoyable. Very much an average professor.

Ronald Schwartz wasn't necessarily a bad guy but he is very old fashioned. The course was very misleading and so were the assignments. They had nothing to do with the course and your grade is heavily graded on group work. The work isn't impossible, just a lot. There aren't really quizzes or exams but just a lot of writing and group work. No break.

Unreasonably strict grader for a pre-rec humanities class. Refuses to discuss/appeal grades. Group work is crucial in this class. If you have a poor group or group member he will just send you a list of strategies to work well in teams. Does not respond to emails well. Questionable attitude. Take another course if you want an easy 4.0.

He made this class as painful and annoying as possible for all of his students. Awful at explaining every project/assignment. Always changing his mind last second and he is one of those smug professors who thinks he can do no wrong. Luckily I escaped with a 4, but do not take this course with him. It will be the most painful 4 you've ever received.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take IAH 209 with Ronald Schwartz. Although the class is easy and manageable, he is a tough grader and refuse to talk about grades when you ask him why you got the grade you did. This would've been an easy 4.0 if he wasn't a harsh grader. He also has a questionable attitude.

This class was very easy to take but you do have group projects which was kinda hard due to not having a group not doing work. Attendance is not required but I found it helpful going to class and being able to talk to him one-on-one he explains the projects better than the documents he sends which can be very long.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such an easy class and it was actually fun. I had him for horror cinema. He is a very easy grader.

Professor Schwartz was amazing! His class was about horror cinema so I found it really interesting. He is an easy grader. There are 3 group projects and weekly reflection papers but they are super easy and I think this class was one of my favorites.

All we had to do each week was write a 2-3 page reflection on the assigned readings and he gives everybody a 100%. My course was asynch and so beyond easy. You just have to put it that hour or two of work every week
If I could actually rate this course, it would be a 0.5/5. As long as you write an essay that is 2-3 pages you will probably get an A+.

I love professor Schwartz. I would take every class he teaches if I could! Super understanding, very easy grader and makes class interesting. You can tell he really enjoys his job. I'd recommend him to anyone

He has an attendance policy where each absence after 3 classes drops your grade half a GPA point. I didn't know about this policy until I saw I 2.5'd instead of 4.0'ing.
