Easy homework but tests and quizzes are very tricky with wording

She's an awful lecturer and SO rude, reads off the slides and doesn't care if you understand. If you have any questions she'll respond condescendingly. She brought campus police to class and threatened to have anyone whose talking be arrested. Pick a prof that doesn't require attendance, they all suck at msu and you'll be teaching yourself anyway.

Honestly it's not that hard of a class but she's just an awful professor. She just reads the notes off a word document word for word and just has a monotone and boring voice that puts you to sleep. She also does not care to communicate with students and was rude when I emailed her about one of my homework grades. Overall just a rude and trash prof.

I tend to focus on her accent more than the actual statistics. She is not only rude, but also makes 0 effort to ensure her students understand the material; she just reads off of her slides and expects you to understand. She is good at math, but not communication nor is she good with people. By the end of 1st semester, half of the lecture shows up
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: awful teacher. worse than community college. you'll be teching yourself the entire class.

This professor is the worst. She is extremely boring and monotone, and she just stands there and reads off her slides. The class itself is not that hard as long as you do the problems for the practice exams. As a person she is extremely rude. Each time I have emailed her I have gotten a nasty mean response and she makes her students feel stupid.

I barely went to lecture as she posts them online. I did have to spend a bit more time studying because of this but her lectures were boring and not useful to me. There is an easy "lab" every week that is in the computer lab and basically just playing with stats data. I did not like her teaching style, but this class was not difficult.

Overall good professor. Homework isn't graded so it is up to you to do it on your own in order to stay on track. Many people became lost in the class lessons because they hadn't done any of the homework to review. So do it. Grades are made solely from exams, and the weekly Lab assignment which should be easy points. She did offer EC at the end.

Only stats prof at MSU that doesn't let you use a cheat sheet for exams. Her lectures are the most boring thing I have ever had to sit through, she reads off her notes for an hour and 20 minutes very slowly and monotonously. She only teaches concepts and doesn't go through examples very often.

Super boring, monotone lectures that drone on. She just reads of the projected papers, and only talks about the concepts. The examples in class and on assignments are not similar. She does teach you anything, just reads of the slides and expect you to figure it out. The book is "required", but is never used. Also grading can be very inconsistent.
She's very very boring, but the class is really simple so there's not much to be excited about. She's very kind and respectful and the class was an easy A.

Terrible. The lectures are horrible and her tests are so hard. The final exam review and practice problems were really helpful, probably the only reason I passed it. The subject is difficult itself and between her heavy accent, monotone voice and inability to explain how to solve problems, it's even more so. She's a nice lady, just not a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This professor is incredibly boring and unclear. She drones on all lecture long in a monotone voice, not necessarily going over how to do the problems, but just explaining the concepts. She relies on the TA to teach you in recitation, but forbids them from teaching us the calculator functions. I have had to study more for this class than any prior.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: These lectures are impossible to sit through; she is completely monotone with zero facial expressions and teaches at a speed of -27. She posts the notes filled in the same day after lecture, so you really don't need to go. I only went to recitations and still did well. If you want an easy A, shes the way to go.

AWESOME teacher!! Very helpful. This class was filled with learning lots of practical skills--she explained them very clearly and helped us execute them well on the first try, including blood draws from the jugular. Taught us practical info that will apply to real life. Was always cheerful and upbeat--I always looked forward to her class!

Tied for best college professor ever along with my English professor!!Made even boring subjects interesting and showed us how the topic related to real life.She also made sure to highlight the important sections and didn't fill the lectures with lots of useless info.Tests were very clear and didn't have any extra info than what we learned in class.
Kristi is an excellent teacher. She is very helpful and explains things very thoroughly.

Kristi's probably as close to perfect as you're going to find. She explains things very well, doesn't assign too much work, explains why you need to know what she's teaching, and is extremely helpful if you have problems. She's also very friendly -- she gets to know her students and is on a first-name basis with most of us.

There is one midterm and a final. They are both 100 true/false questions. He tells you that you will not need to know things for the test that he then puts on there. Average for the tests is a 60%. Lectures are super interesting and I learned a lot but Dr. Snider likes to purposely trick you on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Do the homework!!!  The tests are hard because it's not clear what it's on. Many interesting guest speakers, but I didn't feel like I learned a lot.
great teacher, great advisor. he really knows the field, and will answer any questions you have. don't be intimidated, he's really  great guy!

Not a hard teacher if you know how to take notes and pay attention in class. Interesting to listen to, and he knows what he's talking about, though he gives few lectures for this class. Most of the lectures are guest speakers. Highly recommended.
No Comments
class consists of many different lecturers. exams are hard.

Professor Smith seemed kind and accommodating overall, but I always had a weird vibe from her. She tried to unenroll me behind my back and was odd when I emailed about something in her syllabus. Her exams were also harder than I think they should've been but they were doable as long as you studied for a while. I wouldn't take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a person, she's nice. As a professor, her course just isn't interesting. She talks slow with long pauses (a big pet peeve of mine) and doesn't utilize class time wisely. I hated coming to this class, it felt like a waste of my time-- time I could have been using to study for my major-required classes that I actually enjoyed.

I mean it when I say get ready to read A LOT, if you think you've studied enough for a quiz-you probably haven't, go through the material again. Im serious. Tough grader, unorganized syllabus and calls out students from the attendance sheet if no one willingly raises their hand to answer a question. Mainly history, less art.

I would NEVER take a course with her again. Her absence policy is very strict for students, but she has no problem taking personal days for "mental health post election" and because she had to deal with some things in her own personal life. Has also told the class multiple times how she is not of Christian faith not sure how that is relevant at all
Content is mainly in long lectures which make it hard to review. Be prepared to read articles before every class.
Professor Smith's lectures were long and tedious- sometimes rendering it difficult to remain engaged and awake.

I took this in the summer. She was not understanding at all with any life situations and never made exceptions. Just a b in general, you could tell. I do not like professors like this, who think they're better than their students when we pay their bills. Don't take her, she made the class un-enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she has the biggest power trip ever. she literally doesn't care about her students success whatsoever. i don't know why people like this still teach. my therapist has made so much money from my sessions about this foul class.

This is literally the worst class I've ever taken. I would rather take college over again for the rest of eternity than ever take this class again- or any class by this prof. Refuses to help when you ask, gives ZERO instructions and then fails you if you didn't read her mind. Not one good thing to say. My biggest life regret.

took HA253 with her virtually and never again. I've talked to other students and there seems to be a pattern of her dismissing the knowledge of students of color. She presents herself as the ultimate authority on communities she doesn't belong to. I would strongly advise any students against taking a class with her. I have not heard any good things

Genuinely one of the worst lecturers, the whole class is just history and no art. Would have enjoyed if it was art history. Also, uses offensive language when talking about Indigenous communities, would not recommend.

Professor Smith established very few graded activities throughout the year, causing the final to be weighted extremely heavily. Additionally, her slides were outdated, resulting in dull, tedious, and long-lengthened lectures. Moreover, she was unable to structure a simple debate without the help of her students.
Very tough grader. Will make you answer with her opinion or else it is incorrect. Very strict on grading for being a class that is not essential. Do not recommend.

Laura is a horrible professor and I hope she sees this. Its supposed to be an easy class, but she makes it impossible. Too many essays that she grades too harshly, and on top of that shes the most boring person to listen to speak.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of those professors that answers questions with more questions and never actually answers yours which is bad because you either answer with her opinion or you're wrong. Always looking at nude photos and examining how they reflect the patriarchal male gaze, pushing feminism. There is a reason 10 kids dropped during the first week. MEMORIZATION
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst/boring class ever, I don't major in art so she made sure she picked on me and others who looked uninterested or confused. She will nicely insult you and take away points for stupid elementary reasons. A beginner class shouldn't have been so annoying. DONT TAKE UNLESS YOU'RE FAMILIAR WITH THE ARTS!!

Very inconsiderate, As the other comment said she is belittling and has some sort of a power struggle over people. Class format and timeline is unorganized and all over the place. If you can not take her classes, don't.

She is literally the worst person ever. I have no idea why she teaches other than to have some sort of power trip over people. She has the most tedious and unnecessary rules that affect your grade in a big way. you could write a paper with perfect content and if you dont have a verb and adjective in the right place, she deducts points. ridiculous.
Fantastic professor. Friendly, understanding, helpful and FULL of resources if you just ask.

This teacher can't lecture.  She is utterly incomprehensible, and thinks that having us re-write notes (80% of the class work) to turn in will help.  I don't know about you but we did that in high school.  Avoid her!

She is the worst teacher ever at MSU. Nothing is ever outlined so she makes you completely guess out of thin air on how she wants you to write things. Then when you do it, she claims its all wrong and belittles you. She does not like anyone who is not in the art college and will surely make the class horrible for you.
prof smidt is the goat, made an 8:30 class enjoyable

This class was pretty easy and attendance isn't rly require but there are pop quizzes that you have to take in person. The midterms and finals are straightforward, and he provides a study guide which made it easy.

He doesn't go out of his way to make things hard, but the class is pretty lecture-heavy, so take good notes. Attendance isn't mandatory, but pop quizzes are 30% of your final grade, so beware! Also, the grading scale is a bit steep; you need a 94 for a 4.0, 89 for a 3.5, and so forth. Really, showing up for this class is the most important thing!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class isn't super daunting but his class is pop quiz and exam HEAVY. Attendance is technically not mandatory but he does pop quizzes so you have to show up. Does not provide his own bluebooks and makes students bring their own for exams. Lecture heavy course with very little supplemental info. Boring and tries to be funny so class can be awk.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most stressful and least rewarding classes I have ever taken. This class has less than 10 assignments all year, and the first grades come out nearly 75% into the semester. Lectures are long, boring and should just be posted on D2L since its entirely her just reading off the slides anyway. Might not be Prof. Smith but the class is AWFUL!

I enjoyed Dr. Marisa Smith's course - she is one of the best professors I've ever had. I was initially afraid of taking a quantitative research class, but the instructor made it easy to understand.

The classes were interactive and engaging, the assignments were interesting, and she was always eager to help. I highly recommend taking her courses.

Overall, a great professor I enjoyed the class. It is lecture heavy in the aspect of taking notes, but you can find quiz answers in the notes which ensures you'll get a good grade on the quiz. There is a group project which isn't bad but will require some work. Easy class to do well in as long as you try.

She was consistently late to every class including the final, and would rarely ever give notice. She does NOT prepare you for the exams whatsoever, and there are very few materials given, graded by quizzes and exams only.

Professor Smith's class was really great this semester, with a few issues. Classes often start late or are canceled abruptly. AI usage in lectures was unhelpful and seemed to just waste time. The class is quite easy, high grades are easily achieved.

Had her for my first semester of freshman year. Professor Smith was nothing but kind, and the class was very easy. There were times when she would show up late / not show up, which could have been better communicated, but the class itself was easy if you were willing to show up and get the assignments done on time. Overall, very solid
Used AI in creating her course materials and it showed. Would regularly just teach wrong history.

Stacy never shows up to class and cancels 10 minutes before class (sometimes). The class structure is very easy, but Stacy is very unorganized and lecture slides are long. There's no point in showing up to class even when attendance is mandatory.

Do not take this class, it is an easy grade but it is not enjoyable and is extremely long and everything taught is just common sense. She also will cancel right before class time even after most people already arrived to class. She rambles about NOTHING.

Her leftist opinions dominate the class, and she shuts down students who disagree instead of allowing for real discussion. She was often late, rude, and swore regularly while begging for students to treat her with respect in her syllabus. class was easy, but I would recommend taking it with anyone else.

worst professor. she cancels class more then she hold it, which seems fine but its always 10 minutes before class starts, WHILE your sitting in class waiting for her to show up. she also shows up 20 minutes late and shows up with food, while the rest of us have been waiting for her to show up. she only cares about herself and it shows. DONT TAKE.

Overall, this class was not difficult whatsoever, but I would not recommend taking this professor again. She was constantly late to class multiple days wasting our time. On top of that she would cancel class 30 minutes before class multiple times as well while I was already on my way. She thinks she is funny and sometimes makes inappropriate jokes

LOVE Dr Smith! She is funny, interactive, creative, and caring! Lectures were engaging, especially bc she uses similes to connect new vocab to everyday life. We discussed theories of conflict and inequality, which is not a liberal agenda, just the backbone of the field. Assignments are straightforward and routine, and she is beyond understanding :)

I love Dr. Smith so much. She is teaching an inherently political class that align with left-wing ideology, however the point is to learn history. People hate her because they're not interested in learning the content and think she's too woke. She is disorganized which is frustrating for sure — I have however found it manageable if you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I don't get why everyone hates on Dr. Smith. I took ISS 215 & 335 with her. She is definitely left-wing, and her views are clear in her lectures, but regardless, the class is super simple with assignments. Simply just go to class and do the homework, and you will 4.0. Anything less than that is simply a lack of effort, not intelligence.
I do not enjoy this professor

Not gonna lie I really didn't like going to this class, lectures were SO boring and I don't feel like I learned anything. However, it was easy and exams weren't bad. Theres a 5 question quiz and packback discussion post due each week & only a few in class assignments. You get a lot of drops. Prof smith wasnt that bad but ive definitely had better.

The hate is so forced, Dr. Smith is strange, but she's so funny. Easy class, be prepared for weekly quizzes (takes like 5 mins to do), attendance is mandatory, exams are simple and easy, gives you many opportunities to make up your work, and cares about yall. Yes, she's woke, so what? That makes class so much funnier than other classes.

READI! Worst class I've ever
taken. Easy to pass but Dr. Smith
is the most woke leftist teacher
ever, brings her political views into
the classroom. Has said she's
been in a house with spirits? and
requiring IDs to vote oppresses
the poor, and said it "just isn't
true" that some immigrants
commit crimes. There's way
worse beyond these. Save urself.

This professor is very unorganized and all over the place while teaching. If that isn't your learning style, I highly recommend taking a different class. The workload is manageable, but it's full of a lot of busy work. Exams are very easy.
Very tedious class, quizzes every week along with packback discussions, and class was three times of week with iclickers for attendance.

Literally what even happens in this class. Lectures end up being an absolute waste of my time. We debated about if chickens are a good pet for like an hour, when I could have been studying for chemistry. Always confused and information just gets shot at me with no real way of comprehending it!
Dropped the class after 2 sessions. 100% mandatory attendance and if you don't align with her political agenda, she has a problem with you. Very strange woman.

Only gets a 2 bc she's so easy. Lectures were horrible and riddled with her political views. I couldn't stand it. Teach without a bias please. Luckily where her poor lectures lacked, the ease of the class carried. So simple and straightforward. Easy A, just TERRIBLE lectures

Go to the lectures and do the work and you will be fine! The reason I lost credit is because I stopped going to her lectures. But she is passionate and will give you a good education through her course material and other subjects she connects to her lectures. I would take her class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was insanely easy. The only negative is that she cancels class A LOT. Even worse, attendance is mandatory; and many of the times she canceled class, she did it last minuet. She gives tons of extra credit and weekly assignments are super simple. The midterm and final exams could both be retaken if you somehow did poorly on them.
Weird but easy A if you push through.
The class was alright.
Honestly Dr. Smith was very caring and her class material was very easy to learn. Her class is unorganized and her lectures are very boring but it is so easy to 4.0 this class.

Such an easy class but the prof does not come off as smart or organized. Had probably as many classes canceled as actually happened and sometimes 10 min before class. Also one of those people that lovessss the sound of their own voice.

I took this class as a university requirement. The lectures were very engaging. If you show up to class, do your work, communicate with the professor, and take a small interest in what you're doing you should be able to get a decent grade.

Stacy was an easy professor for a blow-off requirement. Her lectures were long but engaging, and she made discussions fun. Some days were movie days, which gave a nice break. I don't get the hate—she clearly cares about her students. We had one online quiz a week, and the 2 exams were online too.

Manageable, but class constantly changed. We went from iClicker (which wasn't set up well) to Google Forms and went weeks sometimes without seeing the prof (cancelled due to multiple reasons). If people left during the lecture, expect to sign your name on a paper to get credit for the in-class assignment. Tricked us to see if we used ai as well.

Stacy lectured right up until the last MINUTE of class and her lectures were beyond boring. We didn't have class for 3.5 weeks at some point in the semester because she kept coming up with random excuses on why she couldn't make it. Her class was very easy, but, the 2 hour lectures made this class miserable.

Attendance mandatory, but also cancelled class last minute for weeks straight. Unorganized with lectures, and didn't learn anything new or beneficial that I'll remember. Often tried to trick students to catch if they used AI without understanding that this is an MSU requirement. Graded by quizzes, attendance, in-class assignments, two exams.

This was the most unorganized and poorly run class I have taken in a long time. Professor Smith constantly cancels class putting us far behind and she rambles about nothing for 2 hours during class time, not getting to the material pertaining to the exams. I consistently left class more confused than when I went in. Find a different professor.

The worst class I have ever taken at MSU, so take at your own risk. She doesn't know what she's teaching because she's changed how she's formatted the course multiple times throughout the semester. She's cancelled more classes than not and always with only a 10 minute max heads up. The assignments are never explained and the ULAs dont answer emails

Bro, she keeps changing the class format she always tries to throw in stuff to catch ChatGPT but people use it cause she can't teach properly, she overdoes the work we need to do, she changes the attendance taking every single week, she always cancels class last minute, i think i had less classes than i went. Material just gets harder
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She has change the way the class format has been ran so so many times. she's canceled more classes than we've actually had. she gives assignments with no directions. when you email any of the teaching team they just don't respond or don't know what's going on either. She's changed attendance many times and the semester is over in two weeks.

It takes her days to respond to emails, a quiz every week, and Pack back every week, and if you miss one, that's ten points you lose. Grading is very strict, she always makes mistakes on her quizzes, and one of her ULAs took 29 days to respond to my email. Very dissapointed

This class has been extremely frustrating for the entire semester. Classes get canceled very often, many times have been less than an hour before the class start time. Lectures are very long and hard to focus on the amount of content. Way too many at-home movie days with worksheets that contain tons of questions that you do not benefit from.

Nonsense is a word would use to describe this class. She's nice enough where outside of teaching I would have no problem. Cancels class quite a bit, but makes up for it in never ending lectures. Things often don't make sense because the format is always changing. I find my self often confused with little to no answers even if I ask. Easy though.

Tbh yes she cancels class all the time and up until today we didn't have in-person class since 5ish weeks ago. But it's so easy. Same assignments every week. If you want an easy A take her. Still don't know what the class is even about honestly but it's a breeze. Nice enough but rambles about irrelevant topics

Super caring, lectures are really interesting. Exams are online and use questions from open-note quizzes given throughout the semester. Sometimes has in class assignments. You'll be fine as long as you go to class and do your homework.

The lectures are somewhat relevant, but most of the quizzes are just based on the book we have to read outside of class. All of the quizzes were open book and online. All exams were online on d2l. She doesn't take attendance, but there's lots of in-class assignments worth points. It's not a heavy load of work, and she does have a sense of humor.

As long as you do the work, and put in some effort you'll get a passing grade. It is super easy to get a 4.0 if you try on everything. She sometimes is late or cancels class last minute, but I really like the vibe she brings to class.
I really enjoyed her writing tier 2 class.

I enjoyed this professor. Even though she sometimes got off topic of the unit it was interesting and funny. Very easy class to pass and only two exams which are also easy. She is organized, all you do every week is one packback and one quiz (which is also easy). Often you have in class assignments so attending class is mandatory but they are easy.
She is ALWAYS late and doesn't end on time. If she cancels class she does it with very little notice. Easy class to pass but she annoys the class so much.

This is my second time taking a class with Professor Smith. The first time, she had an accident and the class was moved online. It was super disorganized, but I figured it was just because of the unexpected accident. In person, the course is just as disorganized. Lectures are unrelated to content. Spends way too much time on irrelevant intro.

Stacy would talk about the most random things during class. If you are looking for an easy class with a nice professor GO FOR THIS ONE! I felt like the work for this class was not hard at all the professor was just talking about random things most of the time. My class had online exams that you did not have to be in person for as well.

This class was very straightforward and easy to pass. However, the instructor was highly disorganized. She was late to nearly every class, her lectures were irrelevant, and she was nearly impossible to communicate with. If you can just tune her out and do all the work, it's a very easy class. I'd recommend finding another instructor if possible.

The class itself is an easy A. The weekly online quizzes are easy and open-book and exams were all online and not on lockdown so you could use your notes. Her lectures were super long, boring, normally off-topic and didn't relate to what we were supposed to be learning about. She was also late to class almost every day and very unorganized.

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS! She's always late to class. Lectures have NOTHING to do with content about 70% of the time and its obvious she puts her slides together last minute. She kept a "class cancelled" sign up too long and punished the students that didn't show up for class even though her syllabus explicitly states she won't do that.

Honestly one of the pettiest professors I have ever had. Gave the whole class extra credit for showing up when there was a sign saying the class was cancelled. Made comments about the shooting during our first class period. If you are taking her be careful on what days you skip, there will be in class assignments randomly throughout the semester.

This course was so disorganized. The professor had many personal issues this semester, but this doesn't excuse how inadequate she was at running the course. Consistently showed up late or not at all and her excuse was that she just forgot. In class assignments every class period that were unrelated and often thought of on the spot.

I had her for this class and ISS 210 this semester and it was one of the worst teaching experiences I have ever had. She was consistently late or absent from both classes. On multiple occasions she simply forgot what times her classes started. On another occasion she cancelled class 20 minutes before it started. Ridiculously unorganized as well.

She was late to class almost ever single day by like 10 to 20 minutes and expect us to just sit there and wait for her. The lectures she teaches during the class has nothing to do with what are on the quizzes which comes from the book. Every class you have to do an in class assignment some take 5 minutes some are watch a 2 hour movies and write.

Most ridiculously unorganized class ever. Wont upload our quizzes due that night tell days later. Always late. Starts almost every class with "so I messed up".  Every time you email her with an issue she either wont respond or tell you to go to some other party about it.  Also took her months to grade our three question assignment.

This was the most unorganized class I have ever taken. Due dates changed all of the time, would randomly drop graded assignments after completion so you would get no credit, schedule was extremely hard to follow with constant changes. Was supposed to just be an elective and became my most challenging course. Stay away!

I was never able to reach the professor outside of class, even though I sent multiple emails. The PackBack assignments due every week were tedious and your entire grade is based on them and the exams.

Professor Smith was fantastic! She was very insightful and taught the class very well and from various viewpoints. The class was well organized but sometimes it got confusing when doing the PackBacks each week. You are only graded on PackBacks and the midterm and final which were both very easy. Do the reading, take notes, and you'll be good.
easy class better professor

Exam questions are pretty much directly from the textbook. As an online class, it was very very easy. Good if you want to do sociology, probably. Kind of disorganized -- just make sure you join a GroupMe and you'll be fine.

I felt that their lessons weren't organized. We'd have to write a discussion post about the book and lecture, but sometimes the lecture wouldn't be posted until late in the week. With this class being all asynchronous, I felt it was too jumbled and sometimes she and the TA were hard to reach when helped was needed.

This class was very easy. The only thing that I didn't like was that the discussion post topics were hidden within her lectures, meaning you had to watch them in order to do the assignment. The answers to the exams and quizzes came straight from the textbook, and the grading criteria on the discussion posts are very fair and lenient.

I am currently taking this in spring 2021, so it is all online. She is very unorganized with uploading. I never know when things are due. She also posts the required content that goes over the quiz late, so it is hard to know what to go over.
Very strict grader and doesnt answer emails about grading issues.

Dr. Smith is the best professor Ive ever had. Do what he says and take his advice and you will do outstanding in this class. The readings are not super important. I never did the readings and did very well. Attendance is not mandatory however you should act like it is because if you don't go you will fail. The tests are what he says in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He made this class challenging, if you have the ability to push yourself academically you will do well and gain a ton of knowledge. If you struggle with ambition or don't have time to dedicate to this class I would advise you find another. There are no assignments, just exams, and you will have to prepare extensively and attend every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Okay, Chrissy Smith grew on me. He started off not being my favorite just because he was a bit hard to read and I couldn't tell if he even liked us, the first exam took all of us by surprise but I love him now. He says everything that is on the exam in class but that does not mean it is on the slides so make sure to attend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wouldn't recommend taking this class unless you absolutely have to. I understand chris wanted to challenge us but he made it far too difficult for a 200 level and this class is mostly only useful for law students which wasn't the case for me or many others.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Solid professor. He gives you the opportunity to challenge yourself, and doing so pays off. Amazing lectures, every lecture was super interesting.

One of the best prof. I've had. So worth it. It is a tough class but nothing he doesn't make doable. He provides good study guides, great lectures, and is a very caring teacher. He is very available for help and makes the content very interesting. Your grade is based on 3 tests and 2 quizzes and you get a notecard for the exams. 100% recommend!
textbook is free and you are provided with a link on d2l. Strict but very smart and lectures were enjoyable. I loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Smith is the best professor I've ever had. His lectures are interesting and he is super knowledgable about what he is teaching. He works hard to make sure students understand the material, and wants them to apply outside of class. While there is no mandatory homework, the case briefs and readings definitely help you do well in the class

He is a very knowledgable person and a great fit for this course. The lectures give every detail you need to pass the course but make sure to take notes (he will mention that many times). The course has no homework but is instead based on quizzes, extra credit quizzes, and the exams. You really will learn a lot in this course because of the prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good prof. however a quite tough class. Does what he can to make sure everyone does good on the exams without making them too easy. Gives a few extra credit pop quizzes. There's a lot of reading and a lot of notetaking but as long as you do the notes and pay attention you should do good. Would take him again, maybe not the class

This professor, although tough, is the best professor i have ever had. He is very wise and engaged in the topics surrounding criminal justice. He offers a lot of opportunities for extra credit and he even gives extra credit on the pop quizzes from time to time. As long as you do the study guides and take notes you will be able to pass the tests
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I LOVE Professor. Smith. He seems like kind of a mean teacher the first class or two because he is very strict on his NO ELECTRONICS rule. But along as you do what he says, and do his case briefs, you'll see that he's a magnificent teacher. He is awesome at explaining the material and cases and will do whatever he can to help his students get it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Has a 0 tolerance electronic policy for all classes- seems harsh at first but is a teacher who cares about how his students performs. Always willing to work with you if you ask. Get ready to read every week for this class. Follows power points for lectures which makes notes much easier

He is a really passionate and experienced professor. If you attend the lectures and are interested in the subject matter you will do pretty well. If you follow his advice and write briefs for all the cases he gives you, you should do really well on the exams.

Dr. Smith is HANDS DOWN one of the best professors at MSU. He is the professor that will challenge you and push you to your limits and beyond, because he really wants to see you succeed. My words of advice for any of his classes: DO THE WORK. Just do what he asks, and you will pass NO problem.
Amazing professor who really cares and knows his stuff! Makes class as interesting as he can and presents all the material. Very, very well organized!
Hands down the single best professor at MSU! Made the subject matter extremely interesting. Smartest person you'll ever meet too.

Dr. Smith is also very knowledgeable!  Hes worked in the field for years and has his law degree. He brings humor to his teaching even though it is a very difficult class. Much reading is required, but is rewarding if done. Lots of court briefs are required and the tests are difficult, but if you put in the time, its well worth your time.

Dr. Smith was a very knowledgeable teacher. You have to really study the court cases, and if you have a great memory, take his class. Consequently, hes a great instructor, and I would highly recommend taking his class; he makes it enjoyable.
No Comments
Great professor!!
The Best Prof. I have ever had.
best and most knowledgable professor i have ever had.
More interested in bragging about his books than teaching.
He likes to talk about his new and upcoming books
No Comments

The professor is great and very accommodating. The class is very participation based and is much more philosophical than the impression I got from the class description. We talk a LOT about art made during covid and how it makes us feel, but not so much about what covid did to us. Just something to keep in mind! Easy A if you're not scared to talk.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of if not my favorite classes and professor ever. This class (IAH 206, not english!) will stick with me for a long time and I'm so happy to have been able to take it. Dr Cho is so understanding and accommodating to her students. A truly wonderful person!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing class! The professor cares so much about all the students. She is very inclusive and kind. Although the lectures are mandatory I always enjoyed going. Professor is very upfront about the amount of work. The workload is not at all heavy and there is rarely every homework. Overall the class is very easy and enjoyable.
A very simple course with very lenient requirements.

Was actually course IAH206 
Dr. Cho is extremely accommodating to all of her students and is very passionate about her topics. You can tell she really loves teaching about the topic and gets very excited. Most of the course is discussion based and only a few small projects towards the end.

Had her for IAH206 on disability culture in film, very engaging and never boring. She values everyone's opinions, creates a safe space, and encourages participation. Attendance is tracked with iClicker. There are two big group projects and a solo case study, all fun and manageable. She's super helpful and accommodating.

I had her for IAH 206 but it wasn't an option on here, I loved this prof! She's very kind and clearly cares about the wellbeing of her students and cares a lot about the material she teaches which keeps the class engaging. For projects she was very open to students interpretations of subject matters and understanding everyones opinions/backgrounds
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: this is for IAH207 and she is AMAZING!!! so kind and caring, and creates a friend like environment with the whole class. no homework, no exams, a few projects that are easy and fun. I cannot recommend this class and professor enough.

For Dr. Cho's first year teaching she NAILED IT. I got put into her IAH class due to an issue with scheduling, but it was well worth it. Her class delved into disability culture and it was all opinion based with in class participation making up 80% of the grade. She valued everyone's thoughts on the subject and was eager to share her passion.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved Soo and this class! Very engaging, I learned a lot and she's just a super nice person overall. Also has good amount of reading which I really enjoyed. Would definitely take again!

I highly recommend Professor Cho. Her class was engaging and interesting. She was accommodating and gave students the opportunity to grow and improve their skills and knowledge of digital humanities. Our class was tight-knit and I looked forward to it every week! Take Professor Cho!

I'm still thinking about this class a year later. The way we were "teamed up" was so chaotic. She separated us vaguely by interest, then just threw us into a group of like 12 ppl to try and find 2-3 ppl to spend the next 10 weeks working with. My group was awful & her grading was merciless. One of two classes I didn't get a 4.0 in my entire career.
Graded us with chatgpt because most of her rubrics were wrong so that was nice. her feedback didn't even follow our assignment sometimes.

Makes grading so difficult for a beginner-level course on grant writing. I have never done grant writing before and have never been graded so hard for something I have never done before. Be prepared to have unfair grading, a lack of care from her, and overall one of the worst experiences in a classroom. She also has an unfair grading scale as well

Such an awesome prof. Very kind and resourceful. I took this class without knowing anything about grant writing, but her lectures were great, and she gave very helpful feedback on assignments, so this wasn't an issue at all. If you have to take an upper-level writing course and this is an option, I'd 10/10 recommend you choose to take one with her.
No comment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Marya is the worst. She talks so much that it is impossible to listen and sit through her 3-hour classes. Only talks about herself and how she has to commute from Detroit. She expects so much from students that it is impossible to get 100%. Her d2L is atrocious, and she is one of the most unorganized people I have ever met. She also cold-calls. BYE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this professor. Waste of my time and money. Additionally, she took forever to grade anything and did not submit final grades until the last second possible. She requires you to break up into groups and write a half sheet of paper on the reading materials. This is a graduate level class not middle school.

I don't think I can say she actively taught. We do homework discussions, followed a "workshop" from fellow students that are better than what she "lectures" on. She talks for the remaining of the class period, often showing long videos (please note: she likes to talk about her work in Detroit, commuting from/living in Detroit, orgs in Detroit).
Horrible communication and response to emails. Took forever to grade papers. Very generous with extra credit and will let some paper redos
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Sosulski is a kind, knowledgeable, and reasonable professor. She gives her students a lot of grace, but needs a lot in return. Class materials are often really disorganized, instructions and expectations are unclear, she's hard to get a hold of outside of class and sometimes forgets to show up to office appointments you schedule with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Overall, she is a very kind professor. However, she does not provide clear instructions or grading criteria, and I found myself constantly digging through course materials to complete projects not explained. She also grades things very slowly, which does not allow much time for corrections to be made and reviewed before submitting the next portion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Sosulski cares about her students and you can tell shes passionate about what she teaches. However, shes probably one of the worst profs Ive ever had. She doesnt teach, her 2.5 hour class is literally all discussion, attendance is worth 25% of your grade, she is the toughest grader ive ever had. Save yourself and ur gpa, avoid her class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Sosulski is amazing. You have to work for it and be prepared to do so. If you are willing to put in the effort, you will get much more out of the class than you put into it. Feedback is critical but definitely constructive and makes me want to delve further into lectures, papers, and class discussions. If you have the chance, take her classes!!

I do not recommend this professor! Her lectures are not helpful and she takes forever to get to the point, she is smart but terrible at communicating what she wants to say. Tons of reading, the reading is the only source of learning since class time with her is useless. The papers she assigns are lots of work and come with unclear instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Syllabus changes without notification. Written assignments were graded on criteria that no one knew about. (like having to use 15 academic resources for a paper) She would grade our papers during class, during break, give papers back weeks later. Homework assignments were high reading and lots of analysis of reading.  Think absent minded professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Sosulski is a very knowledgeable individual with less than adequate teaching. Marya is very passionate about politics and policy but struggles to communicate with students. All assignments are graded during class and she doesn't always inform students as to what she is looking for while grading. Do not take if there are other options.

Professor Sosulski expects a great deal for the amount of disorganization  that she has. Tremendous amounts of busy work which you would expect if you were still 7, but not at a masters level.  Sadly, we spend many class periods sitting around waiting for her to grade papers, sometimes up to an hour.  She is a very nice person, just not a professor

Dr. Sosulski seems very passionate about the subject. However, she is very disorganized, she expects a lot of reading, there are a lot of assignments/unnecessary busy work. She does not explain assignments very well and nobody understands her syllabus. Its way too much. We still have no grades but turned in numerous assignments. Don't take her...

Dr. Sosulski is a VERY ANXIOUS person, and very unorganized as a consequence, it is very hard to know what she is expecting. The syllabus changed FOUR times this semester which made keeping track of when assignments were due a nightmare. She has a lot of knowledge to share, but I suspect she has some personal issues going on.

I am a student that gets good grades and I don't mind taking a few tough classes, but this class was a nightmare. Her grading is unbelievably inconsistent. Our first paper got a terrible average because of how unclear the directions were so she gave us a rewrite. Multiple students got a WORSE grade on the rewrite. She is also very unorganized.

There is a heavy workload in this class, but points are spread across many different assignments so it's possible to still get a good grade even if you don't do everything perfectly.  Expect to read a lot, work hard, and pay attention in class.  Group work required for some assignments.  Personality just OK.

Following the lecture in a large, content-heavy class is challenging. His examples and lecture notes are helpful. He was approachable, answering questions during lectures and working through solutions with me when he walked around. Very responsive via email and office hours, accommodating with deadlines, extensions, and study plans to catch up.
He was easy to understand one-on-one, but harder to follow during class. His explanations in one-on-one settings were really clear.
He goes over material too quickly and doesn't follow the lecture notes.

Does not communicate clearly; super fast and does not care for your understanding of the material; handwriting so bad you cant even understand notes; a majority of students stopped attending after the second lecture and learn through Ryan Maccombs on D2L. Do not recommend this professor under any circumstance.

iClicker was graded based on attendance, but it was not location sensitive. Weekly quizzes, but they were open note and came directly from slides that were posted on D2L. The final exam was also open note and not location sensitive.

Class is TA led and content is based on guest speakers. IClicker is not location sensitive, so can be done anywhere during class time. The content itself is really underwhelming and only a few of the lectures were useful as a prospective biochemistry student.

Super easy (kind of boring, although important lectures). There was one really hard and unrelated homework quiz, but she curved it since everyone did poorly and complained. There are also 5 extra credit opportunities open all semester. Also, the TA is easy to reach and will excuse you if you have an emergency and miss class.
Its an easy class, very boring. just show up and dont forget to take quizzes (open note).

She spends about two lectures on biochemistry topics/life as a biochem major. The rest of the lectures are about different resources from guest speakers. For example - career consulting, resume building, and undergraduate research. Short multiple choice quizzes for homework after every lecture. Quizzes and final were open note.

Very easy class, once a week with one homework assignment. The final is online and you are able to use notes, internet, or anything except other people. Cares a lot about her students and wants them to enjoy the class. I HIGHLY recommend taking this class if you need one extra credit for the semester.

The course is quite helpful. You are introduced to many resources and helpful tips from other professors in the department. Quizzes and the final exam are all open-noted, so it's really easy to ace this class.

The class is mainly an intro to BMB. In each lecture, a different professor showed up. The course is very easy. You just need to do a quiz of 7 multiple choices every week and show up for the last exam, no homework whatsoever. There are lots of extra credit opportunities throughout the course.
favorite professor I have no idea why he has any bad ratings 10/10
He was my favorite professor at MSU. I felt very safe in his classroom and enjoyed going to class everyday! He was understanding and wanted everyone to feel hear. I highly recommend his classes!

Best professor I've had at MSU (COM 320). He's open and understanding, and interested in presenting different ideas. One of the most impactful classes I've had. Not a tough grader, you just have to participate in class & read the rubric. People frustrated with their grades likely just didn't listen or pay enough attention. 10/10 recommend.

This professor WILL dock points if you misalign with his thoughts like you are supposed to read his mind. If this professor asks you to choose one prompt or another, make sure you pick the one HE wants... Overall he is very biased & unethical no matter what you believe. Stay away at all costs.

He's a great and hilarious person, but his grading is really terrible. He loves taking off petty points for the smallest things to the point where it's ridiculous. It's a shame because the class is really enjoyable. But the man is itching to give everyone a 3.5 or less. This is coming from someone on the Dean's list every semester with a 4.0.
Literally so easy. took IAH 206 and barely did any work for a 4 credit class. Would take this class again if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I recommend Dr. Spinner for an easy class (IAH 206 hybrid)!! She was so caring and understanding especially after the shooting. We just had 2 essays total and a few short assignments per week (readings, discussion post) which weren't bad at all. Her lecture videos were only 20-30 mins long and quizzes were basically word for word from the slides.
This class is a great IAH if you still need the requirement. The prof is amazing and makes that class easy to get through during a busy semester. 100% recommend

She's not very online savvy and her lectures can be very long. Although, she is a very nice lady who just wants her students to learn how to write research papers better. She dropped a few assignments when we were cutting it close to the end of the semester, which is nice. My suggestion would be to not take this online 8 AM as you WILL doze off.

It was one of the best classes I've taken so far. Your grade mostly depends on the three major writing assignments, but you will have enough time to complete them well. Professor Spence was caring and her lectures were interesting, her feedback was very helpful. I definitely recommend this prof.

Professor Spence is a very caring professor but, some of her feedback on writing portfolios are sometimes unclear and confusing. She is always willing to answer questions outside of class use that to your advantage!

Professor Spence is a very nice women but she does not stay focused during class. She strays from the class topic frequently, assignments that are made to be done in class become homework due to her not staying on topic. Class is not difficult but is very boring, your typical GEN ED.

This teacher is okay, like she talks a lot about random crap. You will have homework every class period, but it is only graded on participation. The projects are okay, you will present in this class at least once.  Honestly she is nice, just very boring, long class periods, but it's easy and she is an easy grader.

Avoid AT ALL COSTS.She is backhandedly rude when you simply ask ?s(even though I did exactly what sheasked).Instructions make NO sense & when you ask ?s she blames your "inability" to read instruction, when they had absolutely no information on my ?. She does not care if you have anxiety & has no empathy. Rambles for 2 hours & doesn't teach a thing

Professor Spence is a nice lady and is very generous in her grading. If you're looking for an easy prof for WRA101, she's a solid choice. The only downside is that classes are very long and there's not much content in them. They're way too long. But to me, it is outweighed by the fact if you give a good try on writing your papers, you'll get an A.

Unbelievably boring. Goes past the class end time constantly and fails to talk about anything of value. While this class is very easy everything in class could be summed up in a simple email. Most boring professor I have ever had.
Overall one of the best teachers Ive had.

Professor Spence is a little awkward, but she is a really nice little old lady. I learned a lot from her - not just about writing, but life lessons and how to improve myself in general. She might be retiring this year. Come to class! If she sees that you're trying, she's going to give you a good grade.

She's a nice enough lady nothing against her, gives good feedback, but this class should be an online class. In class for 2 hours twice a week and whole thing is a waste of time. Nothing she really says in class helps. She gives good resources and shows some good videos, but those could be easily given through email just like all the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Is a super easy class with a cute old prof. She is the best and as long as you show her some work and that you are interested in what you are writing you will get a 4.0! Go to the meetings

There really is no need for this writing class to be almost 2 hours long. She gives a lot of information but I probably found only about 10-20 mins of it useful. There are 3 big essays and a presentation at the end which I found utterly useless. Show her you work really hard and do you best, also, the feedback she gives,use it to get a better grade
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I never had  a paper longer than 5 pages. Easy 4.0 if you show her you want a good grade. highly advise going to office hours.

Best teacher I've had at Michigan State, she was my first professor as a nervous freshman and she made me feel comfortable and at home in her classroom.  I attended her office hours often, not only to go over my paper topics, but also to connect with her on a personal level which was something I am very happy that I did.  :)
She grades based on effort. Show her you are trying and you will get a A. There is no final and the grade is just based off attendance and papers. Pretty easy class.

She is very kind and friendly, but I can never understand what she is saying. I went to one of her office hours to get clarification on a paper but I only left more confused. She tends to ramble and says very little in a TON of words. Out of the 2 hour lecture, only 15 minutes of it is useful information that will benefit your writing.

Do your work and you will get a good grade. Take the time to go to her office hours; she will tell you what to put in your paper and you'll pretty much get a higher grade. Just do what she asks and you can 4 point the class.

I can't recommend this instructor highly enough. Her open friendliness and charm invites the students into a safe environment where they can laugh and participate with each other, as well as to discuss inpsiring ideas about Creativity.

Creativity is a extremely interesting subject to study, especially if one is incredibly creative, or even aware of the creativeness inside oneself. This is a cool class if one can understand that it is about the philosophy of being creative. Dr. Spence did a great job in helping guide students' though processes
Very bias and she has an annoying laugh.
No Comments
No Comments

The professor herself is great and very kind and nice. But the class will be very difficult if you don't engage with the online materials beforehand. If you can deal with the online stuff, you should be fine. Exams are kinda difficult, especially those listening ones.

You have to teach yourself EVERYTHING before class online and the whole “lecture” is partner participation work. Personally, I'm not a fan. The tests are very hard and the listening portions are super difficult to understand.

Very sweet and kind! I enjoyed her greatly and would definitely take her again. I think her only problem was just the strict attendance, only three unexcused absences, but that is more the people above hers fault. Easy course with not too difficult homework and a fun atmosphere in class.

Speers is a super sweet lady. Lots of homework that is all online, so be ready for that. She is pretty forgiving when it comes to grades which helps. Attendance is strict, make sure if you have to miss you get a doctors note or something that excuses it. Most of the problems in the class aren't her fault and come down from people above her.

The issue with this course isn't this instructor's fault. The french language director believes students can only get a cold three times in a semester and that the flu is an "inexcusable" absence. Frankly, this instructor is kind, hard to understand but tries her best with what she's been given. Do participate, that's the only way you can learn.
Although his lectures sound like he is reading off a powerpoint and it is very monotonous, he's very lenient with deadlines and his quizzes were very easy if you follow his study guides.

I'm taking PLS 372 and really like Jon as a prof, you have to pay attention to what he is saying to do well in the class. The grade is based on quizzes and two papers but as long as you pay attention and do the readings to an extent you can achieve high 90s in this class.
Very much based on how you do on the quizzes. They're not too difficult but can trip you up easily if you didn't do all of the readings. Just make sure you go to class and do most of the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a young professor (early 30s?) and he seems to read off a script while lecturing. He has his main topic bullet points listed on a PowerPoint to record in your notes but you REALLY have to pay attention to his tangents to get the right information. Listening and staying interested in his lectures is difficult because he has a monotone voice.

You have to attend his lectures if you want to understand what's going on. However, he is really lenient on attendance up to a certain point. Definitely pay attention to the connections he emphasizes repeatedly, they mean something. A nice guy overall and he isn't just there to rant and be obnoxious (although he sometimes does go on tangents).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took PLS 170 - I don't know why it does not let me tag that. I loved him as a professor! His lectures are incredibly interesting and it was a class I genuinely enjoyed going to (minus the fact that it was at 9am)! However, make sure you go to class bc you will miss a lot of important info if you don't!

I LOVED this class!! Jon doesn't use powerpoints, which is actually extremely beneficial as he MAKES you listen/engage/take notes. I was super satisfied with this course. The one downside is sometimes you have to ask him to repeat what he says, as he is reading a script of sorts, but I appreciated his teaching style, which he will tell you abt it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, but the class is not organized at all. He just talks about how great AI and Shevron are during lecture. All assignments and exams are open note take home and unproctered so there's no need to pay attention or go to class ever.

He's a nice man but the way his class is set up is messy. Trying to navigate his D2L page is harder than the actual course material. Attendance isn't mandatory which is good because he spends majority of lecture rambling about how magnificent AI is. Exams being online, open book, take home made this class tolerable.

The lectures, textbook (expensive and mandatory), and exams are completed unrelated to each other so much so that it feels like taking 3 separate classes. The exams appear to have been AI-generated, with frequent spelling errors and questions that don't make sense to the point where he is forced to comp them since it's literally blind luck.

The simulation assignments were some of the most frustrating assignments I have ever had the misfortune of doing, exams are absolutely awful and none of the questions on any of them had what we studied, his continual A.I glazing got tiring and overall I would never ever take this course again
This isn't a hard class at all but he is so disorganized and confusing that the class becomes hard.

MSU is number one in the nation for supply chain, but our intro course is terrible. Spink is passionate about SCM, but that does not translate into his aptitude for teaching. Disorganized (D2L is horrible to navigate), grades terribly (everything is a zero, confusing labels, always behind), presentations are cluttered. Needs a full course revamp.
Awful class. Avoid if you can. Lectures were long and boring, and useless. Exams were so hard. Extra credit and open-note exams saved this class. Spink was genuinely awful.

D2L is set up beyond poorly, complete cluster and mess. Exams are 75% of the grade, just an unheard of and rather blasphemous percentage. Expects you to know precise word by word definitions of terms, which are contradictory to what is written in the book and slides. Nice person, but horrible class. Very unfortunate that this is a requirement.

Exams are NOTHING like class or notes. If you don't know the word for word definition of the EVERTHING you will not pass the exams. They are online and open note and that does not help. Sucks that it is a required class.
Unreal......

SCM 304 is by far the worst organized class I have ever taken. Information is scattered everywhere and what shows up on quizzes doesn't match what shows up in lectures. Taking this class is incredibly frusturating! Avoid at all costs!!

Go to lectures + do other homework, keep good notes from the (expensive) readings.
Lecture was him telling us about how he will tell us stuff. 
Said he would "teach us how to use ChatGPT", a model designed to be as user friendly as possible. Filled lectures with him telling us to ask AI instead of teaching us. 
Completely unorganized and rambley.

The other reviews are spot on with the disorganized lectures, but this semester, this class has basically become AI (mainly Copilot) glaze. 80% of the class is either talking about AI or Spink telling us to look things up on AI to "facilitate discussion" instead of doing his job of teaching. It's just promo for his and another prof's new AI class.
Brutal class but has taken steps to make it more barrable

This man's class is impossible to understand. His organization is abysmal and his lectures are worthless. Good luck trying to figure out your grade at the end. Exams made no sense. I made it through but I don't think I really learned anything. Sucks that he's the only one that teaches SCM303.

Professor Spink is a good guy, but this class is so unorganized. I attended the lectures for the first 10 weeks, but honestly they were not very helpful. The book is where I learned everything for this class. The exams are hard, but he let us use our notes which was very helpful to refer to.

This class was so easy I don't know why everyone complains about it. Lectures are not mandatory and the exams are basically just re written homework questions (open note, open book). Never went to class except for a few when he offered extra credit. Smartbooks are a pain tho but it's just busy work and the homework is fine.

Spink is one of the worst professors I have had at MSU. His online material is impossible to navigate. You never know exactly if you are doing good or bad in the course. His lectures are about nothing related to the content and you never know what will be on the exams. I would not recommend him to anyone unless you absolutely have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Spink is sweet, caring, and passionate about teaching. However, the class could benefit from restructuring for better cohesion and accessibility. The D2L is disorganized and hard to navigate. While exams were online, which was convenient, they were tough, and I personally didn't learn much in the class.
This class needs major restructuring. Set aside $100 for the textbook and go to class only on lecture days after each exam to get extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He really cares about his students, but D2L is super unorganized and hard to navigate at times. You do weekly readings, and homework assignments that aren't too difficult. Its just hard to study/stay motivated in this class.
Lectures aren't super informative, but he does care about his students. He's also a fair grader and the class isn't very difficult.

Lectures are repetitive and boring. We had online, open note tests, probably wouldn't have passed without that. He thinks his D2L is organized, but there is so much unnecessary garbage on it. Uses connect, which is organized much better because he can't mess with it. Not a bad guy, willing to accommodate, very out of touch with the students.
