Best professor I've ever had at MSU. Super nice person and teaches you how to succeed in the field.

I loved taking this class with her. She made the class enjoyable and didn't bore you with lectures. She was a great help whether you were asking questions that had to do with the class or questions that were out of class. Definitely recommend taking her as a professor. Probably my favorite professor i've had since Ive been at MSU!!

Prof Wahl has been one of my all time favorite profs. She is so funny and engaging in lectures and really cares about her students. She clearly states when things are due and is there for any help that you may need. The tests are very quick, and she takes the final exam questions straight from the tests (she encourages you to look back on answers)

He always knows how to make the assignments fun and interesting. He doesn't have monologue lectures. He plants seeds of creativity and lets students brainstorm and sprout that creativity. Mostly conceptual than detailed.

Gary is such a kind professor. I took ADV210 with him and it was the easiest class ever. Weekly group projects on concept development, 2 weeks per project, easily accessible outside of class and accommodating. Easy grader, just put in the work!

This is my third course with Gary and he is BY FAR the best, most genuine and caring professor I have had at my time during MSU. Great feedback and is super knowledgeable. He's a great professor but an even better person.
He is one of the most laid back professors I've ever had at MSU. He is extremely flexible with due dates and is really passionate about what he teaches.

HE IS the most understanding and caring human EVER. Most of the class is small assignments that you present. He gives great feedback on what you did well and didn't, so on. He doesn't post in D2L though. PLEASE take him if you can/have to. Great guy and good to have in your life. Attendance is encouraged since that's where assignments are discussed
She is super super helpful when you don't understand something.

Prof. Toby is amazing! She is very patient with new students learning Italian and goes everything that you learn clearly! If you are struggling she gives lots of extra credit options! If you take Italian at MSU I highly recommend having her as your professor!
She is the sweetest ever and great at teaching Italian! So sad I cannot take another one of her classes, but I highly recommend taking her course!!
Jessica Toby is a very good professor, she enjoys teaching Italian and always encourages students to participate.

I switched to Toby after taking a semester with the other lower level Italian instructor. I found Professor Toby to be more understanding and easier to talk to than my previous one. Learning a new language was very daunting to me but she has taken a lot of the pressure off and her class is actually a fun place to be.

She is an amazing professor and is awesome at teaching italian. There was a good amount of homework but it all helped with understanding and was manageable as long as I managed my time well. There were frequent quizzes but nothing bad. Great prof!!

Jessica was wonderful. She made learning Italian seem a lot less daunting. The class was pretty lax, but there was quite a bit of homework, but the homework is very helpful and it's still a reasonable amount given you're learning a language. She's very nice and you can tell she really wants you to succeed. I will be taking her each level with her.
Professor Toby is kind and makes class fun. She has very fair expectations of her students and overall is a very good professor.

Yiying Tong is easily a top tier professor at Michigan State University, East Lansing Campus. very helpful for all students, and has clear grading criteria. I would take him over Borzoo Bonakdarpour every day of the week. Inshallah Yiying.

Content wasn't too hard, the professor makes the exams multiple choice and on D2L in person. Only issue I had was that he was a little too slow for my liking, so I would often just go through the lecture slides at my own pace and tune him out. Other than that, gives great examples and makes it fairly easy to get a 4.0

One of the best professors at MSU! It's evident he is passionate about teaching and wants his students to learn and succeed. The 80 minute lectures sometimes got a bit stale, buts thats the only negative thing I can say about Yiying. Looking forward to taking his higher level CSE courses in the future. He's truly an injective (one-to-one) prof.

Was hesitant to take CSE 260 because I heard the other professor (Borzoo) ran a difficult class. I was relieved when after the first few days I realized prof. Tong was completely different. He had clear lectures, reasonable homework/tests, and was accessible outside of class. He's also the reason I bought a Wii to re-live some childhood nostalgia.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I often find myself struggling to stay awake in lecture. However, he's great at answering questions on piazza and explaining the content if you can get past the monotony of the content. I recommend buying the textbook for extra credit, as it'll give you more practice and more room to make mistakes on other assignments (this class is 60% exams).
Lectures are very long and boring. If you pay for the textbook, you are better off learning from that. Not a bad class, but could be much better.

Great professor. Everything about the class was meant to be difficult, but he taught it in a very intuitive way. Fair grading, and easy to score if you study. Helpful, responds to questions fast and effectively on Piazza. 

Inspirational. Also great at Wii Boxing.

Great professor. Everything about the class was meant to be difficult, but he taught it in a very intuitive way. Fair grading, and easy to score if you study. Helpful, responds to questions fast and effectively on Piaza. Textbook not required but is extra credit. 

Inspirational. Also great at Wii Boxing.

Made discrete math super easy to understand. Grading criteria was extremely clear. Also the recitations playing Wii play motion with Yiying were some of the best class memories I've had at MSU. Will never forget the time he cleared all the levels in Wii sports sword fighting… back to back!!

As an international student and a fellow East Asian, I must say that most Asian professors are not good enough. However, Professor Yiying Tong is an exception. He teaches with true ease and enthusiasm rather than being an extremely self-centered person. Lectures attendable online, exams are strict but fair and reasonable.

Amazing professor, lectures are only twice a week, with optional recitation. You can also join lectures online via zoom. homework is not difficult, and due every other week. He uses piazza to answer questions promptly. Book is not required, but purchasing it allows you to get 5% extra credit. Prof. Tong is also great at Mario Kart & Wii Party!

Had some of the best sleeps of my life in his class, with that said, his lecture is pretty boring with the boring material and his soft and slow tones. Everything else is great though, very smart and caring and he made the class as easy as possible despite the the boring class materials. Easy hw and extra credits, would recommend to anyone.
One of the best professors I've had. Very caring, smart, professor. Would 100% take again.

He is the best professor I have ever had. He made learning exactly how it should have been with this course without overly complicating things. He is also super responsive and understanding. Everybody should definitely take.

260 can be a difficult class, but Professor Tong is very caring and gives good responses on Piazza or in-person. The sample exams correlate pretty well as long as you do some decent studying. He also gives 5% extra credit if you buy the Connect book and do the homeworks. The only "bad" thing is that his lectures are often long and he goes fast.

it can be hard to concentrate during lectures, but the professor is very understanding and is always willing to answer questions. the lecture content comes from the online textbook, which you don't have to buy unless you want to complete it for extra credit. overall, the class is a little difficult, but the professor is willing to help you succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is an excellent professor, and although some students may find his lectures somewhat dull, he is always willing to answer questions and help students who need extra support. He is genuinely interested in his student's success and ensures they have the necessary resources to excel. He is one of the most caring professors in the CSE department.
He is very understanding and responds quickly to emails and piazza posts. He has practice exams and quizzes that are close to the actual exams and quizzes which helps a lot. Overall good professor.

His lectures were difficult to understand, especially with dealing with such complex material, but if you were to self learn and master the material, he has very lenient grading and even though the homework load is a handful, it is good practice for both the exams and practical knowledge. He handled the aftermath of the shooting very well.

The lectures were not great so be ready to self-learn and search for youtube lectures. Otherwise, the class was quite fair. The exams and quizzes were all based on previous material shown in class and nothing was surprising. Quite a bit of optional XC was available up to 5% of the total grade. And the homework is also fair and self-graded.

CSE260 is a foundation building course, and professor Tong succeeds in doing that. Annoyingly the book was on Connect and cost a decent bit of money, but it was solely for extra credit points - speaking of which, you won't need them. Lectures are not the greatest, but he'll respond to queries fast. I suggest reading the slides and self-learning.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As another user said, the professor was overall very solid.  Lectures were really slow and boring, but everything else was pretty good.  Was very fast to respond to questions and did a good job organizing the course and listening to students.  All in all a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is such a nice guy that listens to student feedback and adapts the class, but he sucks at lecturing. But god bless his review videos. That is were you will learn the material, cause in lectures good luck not sleeping.

Dont take this class alongside other demanding classes. Be very intentful and careful with your homeworks. The quizzes and tests will try to trick you, so please study hard. Read the book and the slides for maximum effect. For the tests make an amazing cheat sheet. Good enough cheat sheets wont work. Find someone to work/check stuff over with.

Trashhhh. Troy never has a plan for his lectures and walks in every class asking, "what should we do today?" You tell us!! He is a stranger to his students and does not care to get to know them. I feel like I have learned absolutely nothing in his class and am not prepared in the slightest for the succeeding course. Colossal waste of time.

Not at all accessible outside of class, big ego, a dozen kids in the class, and he didn't learn the names of a single one. He has a lot to teach you and is a very experienced guy with an impressive career, but it doesn't seem like he even wants to be teaching us. The class was very easy, just not really the best teacher.  sad :(
Doesn't care about anything but himself.

Self-centered and forgetful. Shows little to no understanding for students' lives outside of the classroom. Arbitrary assignments that distract you from your final project. Does not take student advice on how to better organize the course or assist projects. His "grades don't matter" approach does not work.

he's very passionate and will definitely help you build a portfolio and improved your skills, in that he's great. however, expects unrealistic out of class commitment (told me and my groupmates to film at 2am bc we couldn't find another time). not understanding about you having a life or having things come up. also doesnt let you finish a sentence.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor! Very down to earth. You will learn AlOT because he makes you work.

He's incredibly kind and his lectures can be very entertaining but if you're hoping for a professor that will actually teach the content, don't choose Nagy. If you are confident in your ability to teach yourself the content then you could get away witha good grade because the only helpful thing he provides are his notes.

Don't take the lecture with him unless you're already really good at physics or else you will just have to teach yourself everything. 
Tests aren't bad though until you figure them out - they're the same as the homework problems, so just write down the homework problems and the equations to solve them on your cheat sheet and you'll be set.

Tibor is a very nice guy, has a passion for physics. In his class, I hardly learned anything and had to teach myself/use ai. He writes beautiful, legible notes which are easy to read and helpful for homeworks/studying, but he doesn't cover this stuff in class nor work out problems. He often goes on rants or talks about history. Not awful, not great

Nagy is the nicest dude ever. You will have to study in your own, but he's very approachable and the physics help room is very useful. If you can do the homework then you will have no trouble with the tests.

genuinely one of the kindest professors ever, so nice and understanding and funny! unfortunately, i did not pick up a single thing in physics. you get one page of notes per exam, and the homework questions are exactly like the exams. unfortunately, i did not understand the homework questions. doesn't really do worked out problems in class

I did not learn a single thing during the lectures, but still had to go because of the iClicker attendance and questions. I had to teach myself outside of class. Also, he would constantly hold us past the end of class with clicker questions, which was very annoying because it made me late for my next class.

He spent more time in class doing things like playing Youtube videos/music, talking about Hungarian politics, and playing Wii Party Globe-trotters. don't take if you need to learn physics, but if you already know everything you will have fun
Best ever teacher would recommend

He doesn't go over the same lecture notes the other professors did. Meaning you either have to read it yourself or just learn fast as he doesn't explain things either. The only good thing are the cheat sheets which you can get with any other professor. Overall I was confused most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He didn't cover the same notes the other professor's used and often started class late. There was also no online option for his class like with the other professors of this course.

Nagy is a genuinely nice guy but its hard to say the class is good with how much time he wastes. Four 50 minute lectures a week but the first 20-30 minutes are various stories and tangents. Was really difficult without a good background in physics. He was very helpful during after lecture questions but I'd prefer a more focused lecture.

Tibor Nagy is funny and nice, but his lectures are 90% stories. Unfortunately, I was not fond of this class at all but I don't think it's his fault, more so the department's. The homeworks are very difficult and the exams are no better. The saving grace for this class was the cheat sheets. I do not recommend lecture-based PHY 183 at all.

Does not teach at all in lessons. Be prepared to struggle through homework and rapidly teach yourself hard physics concepts. The only saving grace in this class is the allowed cheat sheets and corrections. You don't learn physics in this class, you just learn how to copy down and adjust homework problem formulas.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took PHY 191 with him. Labs takes forever to come out so you never really know your performance in the class. Finals weeks now and only 3/7 have been graded so far. With the 3 graded so far they are very tough on you for minor things like units, error bars, and significant figures. No extra credit offered and don't expect your grade until it's due.
Love Tibor but lectures are unimaginably useless, homework is impossible to do, and the exams are the absolute worst thing ever.  Never take a class with this mans name on it.

Do not take this class with Nagy unless you absolutely need to. Lectures have almost nothing to do with the homework and exams, which are very difficult to understand. Class averages on the exams were extremely low - sometimes less than 50%. The best part of this class was knowing that it would soon be over.

took PHY191, but not an option to select. PHY191 is frustrating. You never get grades back and there are no rubrics. Without feedback, it's hard to know if you're completing labs correctly or meeting expectations. With finals next week, you're left unsure of your performance and can't improve. Basically, you get blindsided by your grade. DONT TAKE!

I wish I'd spent lectures watching "The Organic Chemistry Tutor" youtube playlist abt physics, they taught me SOO much better. Half of lecture is him going on irrelevant tangents. Go the the physics help room hosted by TA's, very helpful. You should make a grade calculator on google sheets as soon as possible, and update it regularly.

He doesn't actually teach the material you're expected to learn. I spend, on average, 6-10 hours outside of his mandatory lectures to actually teach myself what's going on. Even then I don't fully understand because physics is a hard subject and it doesn't help when the person you're paying hundreds to teach you just tells stories all class.

Pros:
- Lecture attendance is worth a small portion of your grade
- He gives hints pages for all the homework sets
- He is genuinely a funny person
- Allows corrections for missed exam questions for partial credit
Cons:
- Difficult to understand during lectures
- Exams & HW are difficult
This is a difficult class, and they are putting that on Nagy

His lectures are hardly physics related. They typically start with random YouTube videos, followed by notes that are prewritten and loosely related to the homework. He usually gets thirty minutes into class before stating "okay let's do some physics now." Incredibly unprofessional - stood me up two separate times when trying to make up an exam.
unprofessional

Lectures are mandatory but he ends up just reading the notes that he posts on his own website that make little to no sense. It makes you more confused while you look at them. There is very little resources for help, even using the equations given don't provide the right answer. Very frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Seems like a very sweet man but his lectures have me leaving class even more confused than before. I literally have to teach myself everything because no examples are shown in class.

Professor Nagy is very sweet and loves physics. However, his notes are confusing and in lecture he doesn't really explain anything or work through ANY problems or examples. Even if you go to lecture and read the textbook, you will never be able to figure out the homework. Lecture seemed like a waste of my time. Get ready to teach yourself physics.

A nice professor with a terrible teaching style. Notes lack any sort of explanation for work or units and the prof never explains them. The homework almost never reflects the lecture content and is incredibly difficult. If you actually care about learning physics, avoid prof Nagy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The lectures are terrible, don't even bother watching them, don't expect any worked examples from him either. After you finish reading the textbook and doing the example in the book, don't think for a second that you will be able to do the homework. The homework questions are challenging, but not intellectually challenging, just very very annoying
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class is relatively easy to follow at the start. The material is easy until you start with the thermo and quantum stuff. The professor didn't really do much teaching in lectures, so get ready to do a lot of self-study. The exams were a bit difficult compared to his lectures. Overall, the professor is funny but doesn't teach the material well.

For PHY 215,

I thought he was a funny dude who likes to make lots of jokes in class. The lectures themselves were very hard to follow. Many times during the semester, I felt like I hadn't learned much and resorted to watching Science YouTube videos to learn the material. Awesome person, but would've rather taken it with another professor to learn
I have him for PHY215. He spends too much time in class with dumb unrelated videos that leads to him going over time in class. Find another option
pls dont take it, try to give APs

Class is through Lon Capa, which is NOT D2L, somewhat hard to get used to. TONS of homework which is usually more difficult than the Exams. Tibor likes to show us fun videos, demonstrations, and formulas in class but doesn't really teach much. This made this class VERY difficult on me, because teaching myself is frustrating. He is super sweet tho!

Just a horrible professor. He can't teach, and rarely if ever demonstrates how to use the stuff he "teaches". Learning how to teach yourself is important with this class and while that's not bad on its own, the fact that he puts absolutely no effort into trying to show applications relevant to homework or exam problems makes the class atrocious.

Prof. Nagy is a gem. His class isn't that difficult: notes, reviews, iclicker questions, old exams, etc are provided. His class does require you to actually recall and utilize information rather than just copy and paste it for points, so people tend to have problems with that. This man is a national treasure and Hungary lost out when he moved here.
Prajwal Kurapati
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: one of the worst proffesors in my semester. he doesnt teach in calss and then gives homework like no one's job. he doesnt even teach stuff in class.

Be prepared to teach yourself this entire course, and don't be surprised when studying the "practice exams" that contain material from chapters that aren't even on the exams. Also be prepared to create your own equation sheet for some reason, as there isn't one provided. Good Luck.
Only take 183B online if youre a qualified physics professor yourself, because there is little to no instruction in this course.

Dr. Nagy is definitely passionate about physics, but it doesn't translate well to his teachings. Much of the lectures feel like history lessons, but attendance is highly recommended because of clicker points. HW is 38% of the grade so even if you don't do well on exams the HW has a lot of buffer. There are also test corrections.

Honestly, all of the most recent reviews are very accurate. We just had our second midterm and during both of them so far, 3/4 of the class did not finish and had to submit them how it was. Average exam grades are 66% which he is proud of. I say avoid introductory physics and do like phy221 and 222 instead because I do not think he is reasonable.

Not accessible at all. Says the "ideal" value for exams is 66 percent, which a very bad image, as it should be "ideal" that all students succeed. Only sent out emails, and offered help on a discussion board which is not effective at all when learning a difficult subject.

Tibor Nagy is not helpful. If you ask him a question (via email or the lon capa discussion boards) he will be sassy and condescending. If you ask a question, he does not point you in the right direction. He usually just assumes you cannot read the question yourself and rephrases it as if that helps anyone. Email Stump your questions.

Class was undeniably hard. Don't watch his lectures or ask him questions, you'll just be more confused. Only saving grace is the textbook. Exams are ridiculous. Although on the midterms you get to do corrections to earn some points back which is nice because majority of the time you're on the border of failing.

Nagy is ineffective and unhelpful to students. Avoid asking him questions because he is condescending.  Class was co-taught with Stump (who is arguably even worse). 8+ hours of homework each week sometimes containing impossible questions (that you'll likely see later on the exam). Expect to teach yourself all of the material from a textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I don't doubt that Nagy is a nice guy based off of the ratings, but he can't run an online course. First off there is so much homework, so by the time you even finish it, the exam is the next day. This course claims the exams are like the homework, which is sadly just not true. It is misleading, and Nagy doesn't offer help.

If you are a pre health professional, The duo of professor nagy and professor stump will end it very quick. By far the worst class at this university, and overall can't do their job. Nagy doesn't even have office hours which is absurd. He writes these insanely difficult exams, that he claims are like the homework when they are not.

I have never heard of a professor not having office hours. Does not help at all and the exams that HE WRITES are impossible. way too long HW, and overall takes the cake for being the worst professor at this university. I want to transfer out of MSU because no student should be paying this much for this product.

Class is set up to make you pass. 44%? That's a 1.0. Homework is worth 33% and the questions haven't changed in the last decade, neither has LON-CAPA. Exams can be made up for 30% of what you got wrong. Do all of the CAPA alone- get 0's on exams but do makeups, and you'll pass with a 1.5 minimum. You can't fail if you just do the work every week.

Since 183B is asynchronous, expect to teach the majority of the class to yourself. I didn't find the lectures very helpful, but the notes and homework hints on his website were. The discussion board in the homework is nice too if you are stuck
I loved having him as a professor! So funny and definitely cares about the material and his students
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not the best at lecturing. He writes out the lecture s before hand, projects them up on the screen and just reads off of that. No explaining. I am very good at physics but struggled in this class because you do not learn anything in the lecture. However, you do need to go because you get clicker points that are a huge part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: always makes the lectures interesting and always has short stories about every subject taught in class to make it lively. He gives hints for every homework that basically shows how every problem is done and even gives study slides for the exams that are short and give all necessary info. Will extend HW's if you just ask him to for no reason

TIbor Nagy rocks. He posts hints for nearly every homework problem (which basically just gives you the answer and homework is a huge part of the grade so it's great) and lets you have an 8x11 front and back sheet filled out for exams. The class is difficult, but T Nagy makes it bearable. He also loves to make jokes and is very friendly. 10/10.
Very nice and considerate. Will work with you if you are working hard.

I don't like physics at all but if you have to take this class Tibor is the way to go. You get a full page notecard for each exam and exams are based on homework so you can just copy down homework problems. He also posts step by step hints for the homework. Attendance isn't mandatory and lectures are posted but clicker questions are part of grades.
Physics can be dry, but if you have to take it Nagy is a good choice.
Interesting and engaging professor. Funny and charming in an endearing way. Loved that he had step-by-step instructions for EVERY homework problem. Nagy rules.

Do not take physics unless you absolutely must. Insanely hard, loads of material, not for those not proficient in it. Mandatory attendance and no absences to offset missed clicker points, very difficult exams, 94-100 is a 4.0 instead of 90-100. You do get test corrections and exam cheat sheets, though. Not an awful teacher, just an awful course.
Great professor and excited about teaching. The lectures are all put online so you wouldnt need to go to class except there are clicker questions in class worth points.
Crap professor, doesn't know how to teach. Exams are extremely difficult, the final was impossible.
BRILLIANT!

You have to go to class to get the clicker questions. The class was hard, the book is not needed but it's helpful, tests are mostly like the homework, some problems never seen before were on tests, but that's so you understand the material. He's nice and tries to keep class interesting.

I don't know if the whole department does this, but he puts his notes online and lets you bring a cheat sheet to the exams. Only reason to go to lecture is for the clicker questions. It's not easy material, but he gives so many extra points that it's actually a hard class to completely fail.

I don't feel like I learned much going to class. Lectures weren't terrible because Prof Nagy is interesting to listen to and tells stories, but the amount of physics I took away when leaving class was little to none. This class in general is tough, but taking it with another professor might make it a little easier.
Exams are barely similar to the homework. He is weak at describing the fundamentals of physics and just jumps into the tough stuff.
Hard class but he did a great job in teaching it with some humor. Worthwhile of going to every lecture between the jokes and the information learned.

I took his online class and I would recommend it. The exams are exacty the homework questions with just different numbers so it's easy to know what the exams look like. He also gives a lot of slack in grading giving you 12 tries per problem. Definitely take this class online!
Very nice, helpful and clear.  A very good lecturer and fair teacher.  Take his classes if you can.
Tibor is a funny guy and he knows his stuff.  Though I've only ever had him as a sub, but for many classes in addition to this one

He truly cares about his subject of expertise. But his classes are very heavy, he nonstop lectures throughout the 3hr class but give us a break halfway. But other than that, he's amazing teacher and very experienced in his area.
He overall was a good professor, but the lectures are very long and sometimes boring. But the homework is relatively easy and all the exams are open note.

The course is very textbook and lecture heavy, but he is quite understanding and very fair about his grading. Yes, the class is 3 hours, but he gives you breaks and in-class activities that allow you to interact with your peers rather than just listening to him talk. Content and homework can be challenging, but easier than some education courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: get ready to spend hours with your nose in a book, his homework is weekly, as well as frequent exams (you will have 6+ exams for the semester.) Considering he is an educator, he should know that standing and talking for three hours isn't beneficial in the slightest, he just lectures the entire class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the worst classes I have ever taken. Gary seems to be a nice guy out of class, but no one should lecture for 3 straight hours. It is rare that you encounter an education professor that doesn't understand that standing in front of the room and talking for 3 hours is not beneficial.

He is a very nice person and is very engaging! The class is very lecture heavy, so make sure to show up to class. The tests are open notes, but he grades the homework very hard. Make sure to get both of the textbooks.

Great professor. There's lots of content to cover in this class, so lectures are long, but he makes the content very interesting and gives plenty of examples. He's chill, is always willing to take time to answer questions, and is very clear about his grading.

Gary was super nice and relatable. Exams are frequent and tough, but you have an entire week to do them, they're online, open note. Although the content was hard, he made this class enjoyable and understandable. Would recommend Gary!!
Awesome professor and chill. Long lectures though

Gary was rude and liked to interrupt students when they were asking questions. He lectured for the whole 3 hours but provided worksheets that align with the slides. Exams were frequent and hard but open note and aligned with the lectures as well as the textbook.

Like him because it is the same amount of coursework throughout the semester instead of pushing a lot of work towards the end. Very nice, and will be flexible. Exams are online and you have an entire week to do them.

A big portion of the grade for ISS310 comes from the exams. But you get to take unlimited pretests, so as long as you attended class for the in-class test questions, you should be fine. Homework grading was tough but fair. Professor was helpful and approachable

This class was by fair the easiest class I have taken at MSU. I would say attendance is mandatory because there are 20 in class assignments (4 of which are dropped at the end), but there's no homework outside of class. Exams are vey easy as long as you take the pretests multiple times before the exam. Overall, highly recommend for ISS 300 level.

This class was beyond easy, she gives 20 assignments and 3 exams. The assignments are incredibly easy but have to be done at the end of class, usually in a group so you can't skip. But, she drops your 4 lowest so if you do the first 16 you can skip until finals. She posts pretests for the exams that have the questions word for word, very easy A.
Prof MacHemer is super nice. The class is lecture heavy but she makes it interesting. Shes super understanding and willing to help when you need it
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has practice exams accessible before the test, but her assignments are all random busywork that don't teach you anything about the class content or exams. She also occasionally had us give presentations in front of the the class of 100 on previous assignments without warning us before we showed up that day, which is really out there.

She is so cute and nice! The class is so simple and a easy A

While initially intimidating you will find he is truly a kind man. His class, while demanding, gives you an incredible amount of knowledge. I can easily say I learned more from this class than any other I took at Michigan State. The guy is tough but he is not unfair. You will get what you put into his class and then some. He is great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Out of all my classes at MSU I can confidently say I learned the most from Dr. Rooney's GLG 361 class.

Dr. Rooney is a great teacher, he's very passionate about his field and is truly an expert. Although he can be tough at times, he'd easily one of the best and most caring professors I've ever had at MSU. He makes class fun and often mixes in humor to make class more enjoyable. Would definitely have classes with him again

Tyrone Rooney has to be one of the absolute worst professors I've had in my entire educational career. 4 exams total, never told students what to study or how to be best prepared. Any question you asked, he wouldn't answer it. He'd make you answer it and if you didn't know, he still would leave you hanging. If you have him, FIND ANOTHER PROFESSOR!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Rooney was absolutely the worst professor I've had in my educational career. Had 4 exams in this class total, never once gave us any tips or a guide to study off of. All exams covered material I never saw on the powerpoint. Powerpoint were also very vague and hard to follow. Horrible personality, has no interest in helping students.

Dr. Rooney is a brilliant & well respected expert in his field. He absolutely understands & loves petrology, & his lectures are very interesting. Make no mistake, this class is extremely difficult, the topic is tough, he's a tough grader, & doing well definitely requires some dedication. However, Dr. Rooney is the best & you will feel accomplished
Very rude and condescending to students at field camp. Often calling them insulting names and purposefully tries to mislead students.
Very sarcastic but funny. If you enjoy earth science, this is a great class! The hardest part is the video quizzes but if you listen in class, you will get an A on the exams.

Tests are extremely detailed with things we never went over during lecture, especially for a University Requirement. Offers absolutely no assistance with reviews before exam, literally laughed at our class when we asked for ANY sort of guidance on the final covering 15 chapters. Lectures are extremely dry and powerpoint are unclear. Good luck :-)
Test are stupid hard for an entry level class.  Tests you on details that don't have anything to do with the broader picture.

Natural Hazards and the Environment is an interesting course. Tornados, earthquakes, ect effect everyone, so it's like we all have common ground. Rooney is awesome. He loves his area of study and you can tell. He wants his students to do well.

Enjoyed Professor Maddalena! One thing I'd recommend is to watch Maccomb's! Overall, the exams weren't as hard as our homework, and practice exams, which can be extremely confusing! There is no CURVE which sucks. I agree with the comment below, too many people cheated on the final, and only one got caught, which is kind of draining and unfair.

The lectures are a hit or miss so watch professor Leanord on Youube. Exams are easier than the homework and practice exams(practice exams are NOT like the exams!). She's a sweet teacher and tries her best to help everyone. The final was pretty bad.. multiple choice, but I'm sure great for the many people who cheated on the final.

The practice exams were honestly harder than the exams, and the same with the homework so just prepare yourself on basic integrals and derivatives, and you should be fine. I'd recommend watching professor Leanord's lectures because some of the videos were a hit or miss. Only con I'd have to say is the amount of cheating on the final.

I did fairly well in the course, and the best thing to do is just watch Professor Leonard's videos on YouTube. The video lectures are a hit or miss tbh it, and tbh the class didn't have that many cons. Practice exams were harder than the exams, and the homework. What bothered me is the ammt of cheating on the final exams, though...

Overall, calc II with her was okay. I took it online, and I think I was hoping that the online notes were going to be a lot more organized. It just felt like there was not a lot of explanation of steps, so that was confusing. The final was 26 multiple choice, which is really harsh because of a lack of partial credit. The final is what tanked my 4.0
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Maddalena was an excellent intro to MSU math. She sometimes goes too fast in her lectures, but encourages student intervention and use of her office hours. Its very clear how much she cares and she is a great choice for MTH 133.
For the math department not bad and she seems to care a lot and is passionate about math. However test and quizzes are very difficult,

I took this class online, but she provided different ways to listen to the lectures along with a variety of lecture notes. This class really comes down to how good your TA is because I heard some were good, but mine confused me every time I went to the recitation. She cares and she will help in her office hours. The material is just extremely hard.
Good overall

As Calc 2 course coordinator, she scheduled a test for only two days after spring break, which is just setting everyone up for failure. I (among with many others I presume) spent my break stressing over this test instead of resting and relaxing, which is the entire purpose of a break
p.o.s. prof

Big tip is to just practice, practice, practice. It's about the time. About Dr. Maddalena, she does have an accent but I never found that to be much of an issue. She really wants to make sure we are understanding the material during lectures, making it very evident that she wants questions. Overall, can't complain about the experience.

Good online lectures that were generally clear to understand. She is also very active on Piazza, which is great. But Calc II is hard no matter who you have (and this is coming from someone who switched from in-person to online), so it's going to take a lot of work, time, and tears to understand and excel in the content. Good luck, soldier.

it's calculus, i assume you know what you're walking into, so i won't talk about the difficulty of the course. Do all of the WebWork, it honestly helps a lot. my recitation was graded on completing the worksheet given. My recitation instructor went over our worksheet and did each problem step-by-step, which made the material easier to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Same person as below. Recitation reviews mostly graded on accuracy and effort. Mostly difficult and really unrelated to the homework sometimes. This class is very test heavy and accuracy heavy, not really for effort or completion. There is no homework grade, but do all of the homework. Go to office hours they're VERY WILLING to help.

Never had this professor, but she is the lead professor. DO ALL THE HOMEWORK! Don't fall behind. The class is pretty fast paced, 1 quiz per week, exam every 2-3 weeks, and break week after exam. Difficulty varies, quizzes mostly easy, exams mostly hard. MCQ mostly bad. Final grade was 89.97, but I asked and they were nice and rounded it to 4.0 (90)

didn't have her as my instructor, but was my course coordinator. class wasn't designed well, recitation worksheets were very difficult and unrelated to what we learned in lectures. webwork assessment sets were very tedious and annoying. not a super difficult class, but could be better.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very bad. Video lectures are terrible. There are so many times where she just say the answer without explaining or there are times when she will make you go back to a very old chapter to check the answer and when you go back, it's not even there. Exams are difficult. Webwork hw will also be very difficult with little guide. I have to search gg alot

The class was really difficult for me. Went to office hours every week for help, which did not really work hence by grade. She did give back some points to me when we went over my exam. Maybe because I told her I felt confident about the content, but ended up doing worse than my first exam. She is really nice, I wish I stayed connected with her.

MTH 133 is already a very hard class and HW heavy. Valentina tries her best in lectures but its very hard to follow along. Be ready to work on problems on exams that are 10x harder than HW. Exams are based off of HW. Just take Ryan Macombs lectures and watch the Intro Videos and do HW.

She's very caring towards students and is accessible if you have questions about the material. She tries her best to teach the concepts but it usually falls short and gives you little ability to complete the homework that is then assigned. I never had a clue what was going on and relied heavily on tutors and online lectures to teach me the content.

I found Valentina to be an amazing professor. She records during the lecture and posts it on D2L. She was super accessible outside of class and if you went to her office hours, she would always be personable and make sure you understood the material. Math is hard, so there's not much she can do about that, but I found her to be a great teacher.

Calc 2 is a hard class and Maddalena does a good job at levitating that toughness a little bit. She really cares about her students and their success. I didn't have to study at all for any of the exams and got a 4.0; every topic was memorable.

Used a few of her lectures for the course, but really just used Ryan Maccomb's pre-class videos to learn everything because they are short and concise. Class is not as hard as you think it will be, don't stress and don't fall behind.
a little hard to understand due to her heavy accent but was an easy class to understand as long as you have a strong understanding of calc 1

Very nice, cares a lot, and will take time to explain (in and out of class, as needed). Difficulty is a 3/5 because math is just hard at times; there's nothing she can do about it. (Also, I didn't find her accent to make things too difficult, for what it's worth.)

Valentina was pretty good overall. She's a bit hard to understand because of her accent but if you can get passed that then she makes the class bearable. Defiantly invest time into properly doing the webworm because that is were the exam material comes from.
Professor Maddalena is a very friendly person who deeply cares about the success of her students.
She is super nice and open to adapting her teaching style and explain things to you.

The class is difficult. I never really actually interacted with the professor but the course was not easy. However, if you do the lecture notes and do the homework assigned, you'll be fine. However, keep in mind that this course is most definitely a step up from MTH132.

Professor Maddalena is an amazing professor. Had her for MTH 132 and she did an amazing job giving insight into the provided guided notes as well as extra information outside of the notes to really make sure you understand the content. Really cares about students (and calculus!!) and wants students to succeed. Take her if you have to take MTH132/3.

Amazing professor. She is always willing to help her students and is always available after class. Her lectures were very on par with the Webwork assignments and the exams were easy when you attended her review sessions.

She is very nice. The lectures are not very helpful. She is not the best at time management. She would spend 20 minutes on a simple problem and 5 minutes on a tougher one. The quizzes and exams are not like the lecture or webwork. She means well, but can be confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's not that she's a bad teacher, it's just that her accent and lack of English makes it hard in lectures. Sometimes she lacks vocabulary to explain things thoroughly which is sad because she is clearly smart and knows what she's doing. Majority of time I skipped class and watched online videos because they were easier to understand.

Overall wasn't bad, you have to come in on Friday's because that's when you do group work stuff that's graded but in general as long as you ask questions and come to or watch the online lectures then you should be fine

Dr. Maddalena seems like a nice woman. In lectures, she would try to answer students questions and seemed to genuinely care about us. Her accent can be hard to understand, but she taught well. I skipped lecture often, though because online lectures were accessible on the D2L. She went through notes kind of fast so be ready to take pictures.

I really enjoyed having her, she really seemed to care. I was in a small class and she was eager to get to know everyone. She was willing to answer questions and was good at accepting feedback from students. Attendance was only mandatory for recitation, and the class was easy as long as you do the work. Extra credit is offered for showing work!

I really liked her! It was like a normal math class where you go through the notes during class, then have tests throughout the course. The only downside was that she takes a while to answer students questions during lectures. If you do not do work outside of class (like practice problems) the quizzes might be a bit challenging.

I would say she's the best Calc 2 lecturer. I'd say any bad ratings come from people who wouldn't put effort into the class, because she was always happy to help and answer questions. I went to office hours frequently and she gave me lots of partial credit on exams because she knew I was trying. Very kind and empathetic of the difficult material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Maddalena cares that the students understand the material, but she would take a long time to go over one person's question during lectures. There were helpful videos over the notes and attending office hours helped. The tests were somewhat difficult since there were few questions and the T/F questions seemed to be written to trip students up.

Prof. Maddalena seems to care about her students a lot, but that didn't really carry over to the ease of learning in the class. Lectures often left out important information, and quizzes and exams were really difficult to do well on (although assessments were part of the uniform course structure). This is a high time commitment course

Professor Maddalena is great. Others have said that she is hard to understand but I disagree entirely. She cares about her students, and is great at conveying information. Moreover, her ability to explain concepts in depth is terrific. If asked to go back and explain something Professor Maddalena is never bothered or annoyed. Would take again.

Her lectures confused me more than anything. The youtube videos were the only way I was able to get a good grade in the class. She wants everyone to watch the youtube videos before class, then she will just give an overview of them during the lecture. What's the point of going to lecture if I can learn all the material from the videos?
She is a really nice professor who cares about her students. One of the best teachers I have had in my life and am so glad that I had her!

She was a good professor, at times she was hard to understand, but she made sure all of her students had opportunities to do well. Attendance was not mandatory, however, you are asked to turn in homework at the beginning of class that counts toward quiz points.

Homework is due everyday and quizzes every week. The homework due is over the material you're learning that day in class so you have to basically teach yourself the material. She has a heavy accent but it doesn't affect her teaching much
She is very good at clarifying when you have a question, and tries her best to help her class succeed. English is not her first language, but it in no way inhibits her teaching the material.

She expects the online videos she gives you to do all the teaching, isn't clear on what the homework that needs to be done is (that she expects you to do after watching online videos), and overall I'm not learning the material at all.
She explains the concepts in an understandable way.

She's nice but really should not be teaching. English isn't her first language so it's rly hard for her to explain concepts in a logical way. However there are online lectures that she gives you the link to, and they're literally the only reason i'm passing the class and somewhat understanding the material. It's frustrating trying to understand her

This class was easy, and I learned a lot. I took it online in the fall semester, but you could tell he cares about students and the material. He gives great feedback, and I recommend him if you need to take the 1 credit classes.

One of the nicest professors I've ever met. His actual teaching is also great.I cannot fathom how there's even one bad review here. He cares deeply about his students, and his course is VERY clear/easy on how to get a good grade. There was not too much reading, the videos were the perfect length. Take any of his courses with no fear.

CAS 204, fully async class. Workload is light and assignment criteria is clear. It's set up as a "choose your own adventure" system where you do 3 of 8 assignments that best fit you/your major. From his videos he seems like a caring and understanding professor. No exams or quizzes or anything, just take your time on assignments and you'll get a 4.0

Unless you want to learn absolutely nothing and listen to him ramble about nothing for the entire class period, don't take this class. There are 4 projects the entire semester and the only other grade is in person attendance. Take Jeff or Maral's section of this class if you actually want to get an education worth paying for.

So kind and easy to reach through email. Wants everyone to succeed, and easy to 4.0 if you come to class and watch the lecture videos. She is very knowledgeable and helpful if you have questions. She makes this class run very well and it is not a class I ever worry about. Lockdown exams with no camera too and other assignments boosting your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Go through allllllll of the material, it is a lot, but it will help you because the exams are kind of tough. The exams are pretty similar to the in class assignments

Dr. Hedges is very willing to work with you, and she provides a lot of course materials for you to understand the material. I didn't do too well, but looking back on it, this is only because I was stressed with many other difficult classes. Dr. Hedges gives amazing feedback, make sure to attend class and office hours!!

The flipped classroom style isn't for me, but Prof. Hedges was great. Her assignments are very interesting, and you can attend classes in-person OR online (Zoom). Do the study guides, keep up with assignments, and learn the content well- you will get a 4.0. One tip: Make sure you have a good grasp of the material. Tests are application-heavy.

Dr. Hedges was amazing. This class was super helpful to my learning and it was relatively easy to get a good grade as long as you did the assignments and understood how to do the exams. The class is hybrid which is nice if you can't make it. Be sure to do the in-class assignments and weekly quizzes and you will be able to 4.0 this course.

best professor ive had in all my 3 years. i have never learned as difficult information and actually understood it as quickly as i have in this class due to the way this class is formatted. i got the highest grades on everything without having to study once.

Dr. Hedges is a great professor. She gives opportunities to fix exam grades and it is largely independent based outside of class. She uses class time where we can work together and ask questions on the content. The structure and flexibility is great. She is very clear about the grading policy. Definitely Recommend!

All content was online despite it being an in-person class. If you went to class, you just did an assignment that can be done at home. She stressed how much she was there to help, but when I politely emailed a question, her rude response was off-putting. Basically, she doesn't do anything. Her grading scale is nice and allows you to do well though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: GO TO RECITATION. you will regret it if you dont, as half of the time she gives away exam question answers and is super helpful. Do the in class assignment and the additional practice questions, as they are helpful on exams. However, you have to earn a "strong" score on all exams to 4.0 the class, which is a 32/40 on all of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She does not help her students whatsoever. I have tried to ask questions in class and they never get answered. I have emailed her questions and she does not answer them. She made me feel worse when I told her I was feeling overwhelmed.

Only a few weeks into the course but reasonable, accommodating, and respects privacy/student autonomy. Treats us like adults. Exams online, no lockdown, no invasive tech. Difficult material, but I want to actually learn it when profs have personalities like this and trust in students. Kind, reaches out when she se's missing work, easy to access.

I love the length of the lectures. She is very knowledgeable and easy to talk to and contact even outside of class. I do feel as if her exams were harder than the content if you didn't understand the recitation and I think the exam times are too short. So many opportunities to make up your grade though

Dr. Hedges is super caring and makes a huge effort to get to know her students. I wasn't the biggest fan of how she organized her classes, but I still felt like I got a lot out of the class. I recommend going to her recitations though, if you take her class.

I had Dr. Hedges for both 301 and 302 and I loved her! The grading scale is a little weird but she has made it better and you have the opportunity to do corrections on all the exams. Also DO THE RECITATIONS! I didn't for the first semester and regret it greatly.

I can't speak for previous years but both of my semesters with Dr. Hedges in NEU have been really beneficial. I find the tests to be easier than quizzes but still good assessments of what was taught in lecture. Lectures are asynchronous and online-might not be everyone's strong suit. She was fun, lenient and understanding.

I really enjoyed her class and the way she teaches. Her class is online asynchronous with a once-a-week recitation where students work on a worksheet. She mades an effort to come around and talk to students one on one and did a pretty good job of clearing up any confusion. Her lecture videos are shorter and easy to follow.

Super clear and concise lectures. There are ~9 lectures per week spanning 5 mins to 15 mins so it's not that bad. The quizzes are exactly what was covered in the lecture. Exams are a bit harder I feel because they tend to reach a little further than the lectures but still doable. She does offer practice questions each week that help with the exams

I didn't learn very much about neuroscience after taking this class. It was like really easy. It was kind of a bummer, but I got a good grade out of it so... who cares? The professor was really nice and funny though.

Very nice and definitely knows a lot about the material, but this and NEU301 are not an easy 4.0. I never benefitted from the lectures but other people might. Recitations are absolutely necessary to have a grasp on the material.

She was okay, but her lectures are a bit messy, and the grading scale is ridiculous. Her tests are insanely difficult and barely have anything to do with lectures. Also, you barely have any time on the test, so if you don't know the answer right away, good luck. The extra credit offered is your only chance at a 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very, very easy class, with a very good textbook. Probably the best textbook I've seen. Exams can be kind of tough, but they're all open book and open note, so you can Ctrl+F your way through them a lot of the time. I didn't feel like I learned a lot, but it was still a fun class, and definitely a good introduction to neuroscience.

I enjoyed the format of her lectures, but the lectures weren't very helpful for the exams, so what's the point, ya know? The recitations and bonus assignments helped much more. I was glad that 0.5 was added to your grade at the end if you completed the extra credit every week, but everyone needed that 0.5 because her grading scale is ridiculous.

Dr. Hedges is very nice and tries her best to help students understand the introduction to NEU. The exams can be constricting for time, and sometimes confusingly worded. She allows for exam corrections for 1/2 credit on missed content. With a fantastic method of grading and a good course structure, a good understanding of basic biology is required.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hedges is very kind, and easy to contact outside of class. However, the criticism is within her grading scales for her classes. I understand the objective, but it makes it significantly harder to succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good not great. People leaving 1 star reviews must just not be able to handle the material, because she wasn't that bad and it was very straightforward on what needs to be done to succeed. 5 star reviews also confuse me. Overall pretty good tho.

I love neuro and admittedly did not struggle with the subject matter, but I can only imagine how much more miserable this class would have been if that were not the case. Dr. Hedges is truly terrible when it comes to communicating expectations and does not offer students equal levels of assistance. I would avoid classes with her at all costs.
She is awesome

Dr. Hedges is a great professor. The lecture material is all inclusive and the weekly quizzes are not that hard as they could be. Neuroscience is a difficult topic regardless of the professor. Dr. Hedges challenges you, but if you put effort into understanding the material and be ready for exams - easy 4.0. She gave extra credit & exam corrections
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoy Dr. Hedges, she never fails to make me smile even while taking this class remote. The content is hard, but she lays out the information clearly and provides review questions throughout lectures. It is a hard class but she manages to make it bearable. As long as you study and keep up with lectures you'll do well in the class.

Dr. Hedges presents information in a clear, easy-to-understand manner, but you will need to put in the work on your own to fully comprehend it. She made the online class more enjoyable with weekly discussion boards, and while there is a weekly recitation, quiz, and self-assessment, these help you to understand the material much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Switched my major because of her. Extremely difficult tests. Weekly recitation, quiz, and self assessment. Would not recommend at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bad explanations could teach material better

Neuro is difficult but Dr. Hedges does NOT make it simpler to learn. She is a great person but bad prof. I studied for WEEKS prior to exams and still failed due to trick questions & harsh grading on the short answers. Multiple choice options can range from A to J with some saying "B, E, and F are true" or "Only A and G are true." A nightmare.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Hedges and would recommend her to anyone! She's very funny and straight to the point.

Dont blame the prof for the material. the class is not a walk in the park but it is so interesting and if you put time in to it you realize how well she explains and prepares you. she gives daily extra credit and if the whole class is not doing so hot she gives out even more extra credit. shes cool and just wants people to learn and do well.

Sometimes rude. The type of professor that only cares about a select few students. I always go to office hours but still have a hard time. Goes out of her way to make most questions on her exams and quizzes very difficult. Like others have said, even if you know the material by heart, the wording of her questions is very frustrating.

Exam questions are too difficult, even for someone who visits office hours and completely understands all of the material. This also applies for the weekly quizzes. She definitely needs a reality check and realize that we are undergrads and not phd students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She does not know how to create fair questions for an intro level course. Even if you understand the material, her questions set you up for failure. So many friends of mine spend hours studying for her weekly quiz and still end up confused. Don't let the grade averages fool you. I hope she is either replaced or learns to create fair questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I didn't really like her, he exams are tricky and confusing. she grades really heavy on the short answer questions. shes rude sometimes when answering qts. her quizzes are hard too, their is one every week. I dont recommand her at all. weekly quizzes are 18.5% you can drop 2 only out of 14, exams are 61%. donttakeher. I wish I didn't take her
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I did not really like Dr. Hedges. She tries very hard to be relatable which can be annoying, but her class comics are funny. The way she grades isn't very friendly to bombing an exam. I didn't even fail the first exam but to get a 4.0, I had to get all the rest of the points for the rest of the semester. Her exam questions are also very confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Hedges is ok at teaching I dont fall asleep while I'm in class so that should say something, but her exams are ducking hard she words it in really hard way no matter how much you study eithr you understand it or you're ducked, her study guide is objectives which is annoying. 61% of your grade is exams and barely any extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor. Content can be difficult and although the book is not essential, it's recommended for good reason.

Dr. Hedges is so absolutely incredible I literally don't have enough characters to convey it. Probably the best professor I've had at MSU. She's very new to the university but She. Knows. Her. Stuff. Probably the best hire MSU neuroscience has ever gotten. Exceptional and effective teacher and wonderful human being.

This was Dr. Hedge's first semester teaching here, and I WORSHIP HER. She is super fun in class and loves to incorporate memes into the presentations. She keeps it simple, even when the material is difficult. All the info you need to know is on the slides, so no extra note-taking needed. Much extra credit. DOES NOT BELIEVE IN CUMULATIVE FINAL EXAM!
Did his best to connect with students and make course material engaging. The class was flipped classroom but he walked around helping students. Funny and nice.

He is a very good professor and I would take BS 161 with him because he is very nice and is very clear and easy to understand. He is very interactive with students to make sure he is teaching us well. Take this class with him he is really nice for the poorly designed class that BS 161 is
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The professor was engaging and genuinely seemed to take interest when teaching the class. I did not like the way the class was set up though. The asynchronous lecture prior to class (graded), then in class group assignments(graded), and many quizzes was just a lot. I thought there was too much to be graded on.

A good and easy to understand professor. Only had him for half the semester but could tell he genuinely enjoys teaching and biology. A lot of assignments for this class and the exams can be pretty hard so make sure to ask questions in class.

Dr. Vermaas is a great professor and made BS161 much more bearable. He's a really nice guy and is really helpful when answering questions. The class is really difficult but that's just because of how the course is designed.

He has a cowbell 
5 STAR
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very easy class, yet can be a bit boring. She definitely cares about the subject she's teaching, yet at times it feels like there's no rhyme or reason to the class. She's VERY strict about phones or any distractions so be warned. She's a little condescending at times but mostly a caring person. Most classes are just group discussion.

Gave me condescendingly bad feedback on my presentation for 3 whole minutes in front of the class, but I received a 100% and had done the work for my group. Other group members only received positive feedback (on what I wrote for them). Worst professor experience I've had at MSU in all 3 years here. She rambles lots. Less effort=better she grades.

Do not take this class! She is very strict with any electronics (including computers) and WILL call you out in front of everyone for the smallest stuff. Her lectures don't really make that much sense because she goes on random rants about things and interrupts students during discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy class, easy grader. Class feels like high school (no phones out, must pay attention, participation), this was annoying for a university required class. Her advice was condescending, vague yet overcomplicated, ask lots of questions to fully understand the group project before getting too far in. Don't overcomplicate anything though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had her for IAH 207. She graded everything very easily; I got A's on almost every assignment. She will literally love you if you participate in the discussions, so say anything and she will love it or agree with you.

She approved my article for this presentation assignment and then once I presented, she noticed my article didn't have an author and required me to do the assignment all over again for a different article, after she already approved the other one. Her classes are extremely boring and she is always rambling about something not even related. Easy tho

Dr. Weiss will call you out if you are blatantly not paying attention in class, which honestly I think is fair. She's a great person and her lectures are often interesting if you actually care about what we're learning in class. If you do your work it's such an easy and enjoyable class.
There is a lot of group projects/work, and she doesn't let you use electronics during the class unless she says we can get them out.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. She is rude and constantly called me out in class for odd reasons. Forces you to work in groups and gives horrible instructions for every assignment. She wants you to practically read her mind for half of the criteria. Has a few students in the class that she picks on and a few that she favors. Don't take it!

Very condescending and rude, even when just asking for clarification. It's a simple class and assignments aren't too difficult, but I wish I dropped week 1. The class included a group project and the whole process was just beyond unorganized. If you can, choose another IAH.

Worst class I've ever taken. Professor Weiss is condescending, rude and unorganized. Every lecture felt like torture and every student groans at her assignments. Not a hard class but I would've taken a more difficult class if I knew I would be learning anything. Take any other IAH please.

Professor Weiss is extremely willing to help students achieve success in the class. Grading tends to be pretty lenient, although there's a lot of required reading / watching films outside of class. From what I've heard, one of the better IAH profs here.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class because of her good reviews big mistake. This professor was so infuriating to work w/ directions were never clear, lectures made no since, assigned huge reading before every class and had a whole GROUP project entirely on your own out of class. This class was way too much stress and work for an IAH class but TENDED to grade easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a good prof and very nice. However, her lectures were dragged out and unengaging. Attendance is "mandatory" but you can easily get away with skipping classes if you participate occasionally. The irritating thing about this class was how you had to attend 5 events from the program that she was involved in which had no relation to the class.

Professor Weiss is very caring. Sometimes, she isn't as clear as she could be, but she makes her class very manageable. If you put even a small amount of effort in and submit on time, class is an easy A.

So condescending. So passive-aggressive. Lectures are insufferable, she drags out every concept unnecessarily. Course work is fairly easy but there is just so much for this type of class. Requires a lot of out of class participation for films. Asked her a question about how she prefers I turn in an assignment and she was so difficult to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is one of the best professors I have had at MSU. She is really kind and understanding of everything. There are some events you have to attend on the weekend but other than that and the reading she assigns her class is really easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Weiss is a very kind professor, she isn't strict about grading or attendance. I would recommend showing up to class often though as it can be easy to get lost in some of the content she teaches. She does post everything on D2L though so if you miss a class you have access to everything you missed. Sometimes she doesn't explain things well.
Dr. Weiss was really kind and accommodating when it came to getting assignments in. She really cared about our comprehension of the topics presented. Great professor and an enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She made it clear in the beginning that the she wanted her relationships with students to be more peer based rather than professor/student, which made it easy to reach out. She was the sweetest, but also knew when she was being taken advantage of. Most I had to write in this class was 150 words, and a simple group presentation at the the end.

I had Dr. Weiss for IAH 210, I highly recommend taking the class with her because she is such an amazing teacher and is very passionate about the class. The class content is not super heavy and the work load is very manageable. I loved taking her class so much, I am taking a second level IAH with her next sem.
She is the best professor i have seen. She lets you have your our opinions  and  nurtures them. Her classes are very interactive and she is very good in grading as long as you show good effort.

Rafael was my TA for MTH235, so I went to his weekly recitations. He has a great way of explaining hard, difficult concepts to students learning it for the first time. He would clear up three lectures worth of confusion in one hour. He should be teaching this class
I would say that you will have to teach and learn the work outside and inside of class. And will have to purchase both the apps that we use for class work.

The course itself is hard to keep up on if you do not participate outside of class. Doing the homework and practice quizzes is crucial. Gave multiple opportunities to improve your mastery scores, was clear about the grading, and offered help during classes. Good professor!

The professor is very nice. But the way this class is taught is so strange to me, he just shows us work on how he would solve the equations he puts on the board, there is no interaction between the students and the professor during the class time. At the same time, if you get stuck behind in this class, like I did, you're basically screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Cal online, as long as you do what you need to I PROMISE youll at least get a 2.0. He does Effort grades that is based on your homework, quiz and recitation attendance grades. Even if you get 0 on all exams your effort grade (if you do it all right) will get you the grade you need. Highly recommend if you arnt good at math
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not a bad teacher

Many people say MTH 124 is difficult but I think that if you follow along in the lectures and make sense of the concepts, it is easy to do well in this class. Your grade is made up of the final, WeBWorK (which is basically how you study anyway), recitation attendance and bi-weekly quizzes, and easy online effort assignments. The class is very fair.

Prof. Velivasakis is honestly a good math teacher. First few weeks of class are hard but he can always help if you have questions. There are quizzes likely every week but most of them are based off the homework. Really funny professor. Only downfall is the amount of homework he gives so give yourself time to do it because there's no late work.

Tbh his accent is what made me go to class. He is so funny. There is alot of homework and weekly quizzes but if you keep up with it you will be ok. I ended with a 3.0. Half the class skips lecture but i would definitely recommend going.

The material was taught well but the 6 quizzes throughout the semester (worth 55% of our final grade) would often only be 8 questions, so if you only got 2 wrong that would be a 75%. The final was also only 20 questions so it gave room for little to no error.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is hard if you do not attend the lectures. Recitations are mandatory with 2 skips. Luckily there was a built in "effort grade score" so as long as you went to the recitation and actually tried you were automatically passing the class which was really nice. The TA was eh they were not good at explain the material.
This class was genuinely awful. I failed it. The professor is a nice dude but I genuinely cried when walking to class. All I have to say is good luck. My ta was also so awful and did not care
